supported on the positive side of
$P_{1/2}=\{x_3=a/2\}$ whose class in the lattice
reflection-positive Hilbert space is nonzero.
More precisely, let $\vartheta_c=1/500$,
$z_d=(5d/8+a/2)e_3$, and
$f(x)=(d/8-|x-z_d|)_+$.  For $\mu=1,2,3$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-current-norm}
 \omega_\nu\bigl(J^T(fe_\mu)\Theta_{P_{1/2}}J^T(fe_\mu)\bigr)
       \ge\tfrac14c_B\operatorname{tr}(t^2)
                  \mathcal K_4(f,f\circ\theta)>0.
\end{equation}
The bound is uniform in admitted labels and torus-limit
states.  It also holds on admitted tori with $20d\le\ell$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The two tents form a test pair at scale $d$ and
$\vartheta_c$.  Their centres are $5d/4$ apart and
their support radii are $d/8$.  Also
$\operatorname{Lip}f=1$, $\|f\|_\infty=d/8$, and
$\int f=(\pi/1536)d^3\|f\|_\infty
\ge\vartheta_cd^3\|f\|_\infty$.
For large $K$, every endpoint of a bond with midpoint
in its support is strictly above $P_{1/2}$.

On generators, reflection reverses the ordered edge
and sends $\mathsf j^T(v,v')$ to
$-\mathsf j^{T^*}(\theta v,\theta v')$.
Antilinearity also sends $i$ to $-i$.  After summing
the oriented bonds this gives
\begin{equation}\label{C-402-26}
 \Theta_PJ^T(f)=J^{T^*}(\varrho\bar f\circ\theta),
\end{equation}
where $\varrho$ is the linear reflection.  The positive
form of \cite[Thm. B and Thm. A]{QCDM1} therefore
evaluates the left side of \eqref{eq:qcdm2-current-norm}
by the two-current law at $e=e_\mu$ and
$e'=\varrho e_\mu$; the current means are zero.

On these supports $n=x-y$ has $n_3\ge d$ and
$|n_\perp|\le d/4$, so
\[
 \langle e_\mu,k(n)\varrho e_\mu\rangle
       \ge\frac{15}{17}|n|^{-4}.
\]
Choose $d$ so that $\epsilon_V(g,\vartheta_c;d)<1/4$,
and then $K$ so that the two mesh errors in
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-current-law-error} total at most $1/4$.
The leading term less the error is at least
$(15/17-1/2)c_B\operatorname{tr}(t^2)\mathcal K_4$,
which proves \eqref{eq:qcdm2-current-norm}.
The same supports lie in the positive slab of the
torus when $20d\le\ell$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Joint correlations with the flavour currents}

We now include the currents in the family of scalar fields.
The estimate needed for this purpose is a bound on the
chessboard seminorm of one current. Its conditional mean
vanishes, so the fold of a current depends only on propagators
between distinct reflected cells. Meson sources give an
exponential moment of their squared Hilbert--Schmidt norms.

Write $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{usp}(2N_f)\oplus
\mathfrak{usp}(2N_f)$, acting on $W$ as in
\eqref{C-401-3}, and put
$\|X\|=\max(\|X_+\|,\|X_-\|)$.
For a bond $b=\langle x,y\rangle$, let $H_b$ be the sum
of the hopping terms of the fermion action across $b$.
Define the derivation $\delta_X^y$ by
\[
 \delta_X^y\widehat\Psi(v)=1_{x_v=y}X\widehat\Psi(v),
 \qquad j_b^X=\delta_X^yH_b,\qquad
 J^X(F)=a\sum_{x,\mu}F_\mu(x+ae_\mu/2)
                         j_{\langle x,x+ae_\mu\rangle}^X.
\]
The derivation fixes the links. With our convention for
$\alpha_S$, it is the derivative of
$\alpha_{\exp(-\epsilon X)}$ applied only at $y$.
For Hermitian $T=e_+\otimes t_++e_-\otimes t_-$, put
\[
 X_T=\bigl(\operatorname{diag}(it_+,-i\bar t_+),
           \operatorname{diag}(it_-,-i\bar t_-)\bigr).
\]
Then $J^{X_T}=J^T$ with the normalization in
\eqref{C-402-3}.

Fix a real basis $\mathfrak X$ of $\mathfrak g$ with
$\|X\|\le1$ and put
$\mathcal I^{\rm cur}=\mathcal I^{\rm ext}\sqcup\mathfrak X$.
A current entry $(X,F)$ has insertion norm
$\|F\|_X=\|X\|\sup_x|F(x)|$, where $|F|$ is the
Euclidean norm on $\mathbb R^3$. The other insertion
norms remain those used in \cref{C-401-48}.
The joint truncated function is the cumulant of these
fields. Scalar test functions and vector test functions
at current entries are taken with pairwise disjoint supports.

\begin{lemma}[The currents at a fixed cutoff]\label{C-402-45}
Every $j_b^X$ is even, gauge invariant and supported at
the endpoints of $b$. There are $S\in G$ and a Hermitian
$T$ with real diagonal flavour blocks such that
\[
 J^X(F)=\alpha_SJ^T(F),\qquad \|T\|=\|X\|.
\]
The automorphism $\alpha_S$ preserves each cell algebra
and its chessboard seminorm. In particular the conditional
mean of $J^X(F)$ is zero.

Let $\|Q\|_1$ be the sum of the absolute values of the
coefficients of a Grassmann polynomial in the original
generators. Set
\[
 c_{\rm h}=9/2,\qquad
 c^1_{\rm cur}=32c_{\rm h}N_f(8N_f)^{3/2}.
\]
At every gauge configuration,
\[
 \|J^X(F)\|_1\le c^1_{\rm cur}\|X\|a\sum_b|F(b)|,
 \qquad
 \|\Phi[M](f)\|_1\le6144N_f^2\|M\|a\sum_x|f(x)|.
\]
For quadratic polynomials $Q_1,\ldots,Q_s$,
\[
 |\langle Q_1\cdots Q_s\rangle_U|
       \le m_0^{-s}\prod_i\|Q_i\|_1.
\]
These assertions hold on a torus and on the infinite lattice.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The derivation is linear in $X$, preserves the degree, and
acts only on the generators at $y$. The hopping action is
gauge invariant and the derivation commutes with colour,
so $j_b^X$ is gauge invariant and quadratic. For $X_T$,
the derivation is $i\delta_y^T$; differentiating the two
oriented hopping terms gives $j_b^{X_T}=ij_\mu^T(x)$.

Every element of the Lie algebra of a compact connected
group is conjugate into the Lie algebra of a fixed maximal
torus; see \cite[Thm.~3.6]{Knapp97}. Applied to $G$, this gives $X=S X_TS^{-1}$ with
real diagonal $t_\pm$. Unitarity preserves the norm.
The constant substitution $\alpha_S$ preserves $H_b$.
Conjugating the local derivation therefore gives
$\alpha_Sj_b^{X_T}=j_b^X$. By \cref{C-401-16}, $\alpha_S$
commutes with each reflection and preserves the conditional
Gaussian functional. Thus
\[
 \operatorname{Fold}(\alpha_SQ)
       =\alpha_S\operatorname{Fold}(Q),\qquad
 \|\alpha_SQ\|_{\rm ch}=\|Q\|_{\rm ch}.
\]
The vanishing mean follows from \cref{C-402-24}.

Each component of $\widehat\Psi$ is a generator times
a number of modulus one. The formula for $\phi[M]$ has
$16N_f$ components, so
$\|\phi[M](v)\|_1\le\frac12(16N_f)^2\|M\|$.
There are $48$ chambers at a site. For $J^T(F)$ there are
eight chamber pairs above each bond, with two hopping
blocks of norm at most $a|F(b)|\|T\|c_{\rm h}$ per pair.
An $8N_f$ square matrix has entrywise $\ell^1$ norm at
most $(8N_f)^{3/2}$ times its operator norm.
A unitary symplectic substitution multiplies the
coefficient norm of a quadratic polynomial by at most
$2N_f$, since each of its two rows has $\ell^1$ norm
at most $(2N_f)^{1/2}$. These counts give the stated
constants. Finally expand $Q_1\cdots Q_s$ in monomials.
Its Gaussian mean vanishes unless there are $s$ generators
of each type. Otherwise it is a minor of the covariance;
repeated generators give zero, and Hadamard's inequality
bounds each remaining minor by $\|D_U^{-1}\|^s\le m_0^{-s}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Propagators between reflected cells]\label{C-402-46}
Let $Q$ be a set of sites in a chessboard cell $\square$,
at distance at least $\delta$ from its walls. Let $P_r$
project onto the chambers above its reflected copy $rQ$,
and let $\mathsf N$ be the number of cells. With
$\mathsf G_+=a(D_+[U]+m_0)^{-1}$, put
\[
 N_Q(U)=\sum_{r\ne r'}\|P_{r'}\mathsf G_+P_r\|_2^2,
 \qquad
 \mathscr C_K^\flat(Q;\delta)
      =\max_r\mathscr C_K(rQ;\delta).
\]
Then
\[
 \mathsf E\exp\{N_f\varrho_J^2N_Q/8\}
 \le\exp\{\mathsf N(c_V|\square|
                         +\mathscr C_K^\flat(Q;\delta))\}.
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Choose a subset $A$ of the cells and let $B$ be its
complement. Let $\chi_A,\chi_B$ be the indicators of
the corresponding unions of the reflected sets. Use the
meson source
\[
 J_A=\varrho_J(\chi_Ae_{+-}-\chi_Be_{-+})\otimes1_{N_f}.
\]
Its norm is $\varrho_J$. Since $\mathsf G_-=\mathsf G_+^*$,
Schur complementation and $\det(1+AB)=\det(1+BA)$ give
\[
 \det(1-\mathsf GJ_A)
   =\det(1+\varrho_J^2T_AT_A^*)^{N_f},
 \qquad T_A=\chi_B\mathsf G_+\chi_A.
\]
Here $\mathsf G=aD_U^{-1}$ on the original, undoubled
space. The singular values of $\varrho_JT_A$ are at
most $\varrho_J/\mathsf m\le1/4$. Hence
\[
 \det(1-\mathsf GJ_A)
       \ge\exp\{N_f\varrho_J^2\|T_A\|_2^2/2\}.
\]

The chessboard estimate bounds the partition quotient
at $J_A$ by the product of the cell seminorms of the
one-sided sources $\varrho_J1_{rQ}e_{+-}$ or
$-\varrho_J1_{rQ}e_{-+}$. A relative species phase
rotates either source by any unit complex number, without
changing its seminorm. In \eqref{eq:qcd2-small-cell},
average the logarithmic estimate over that phase.
The local energy is holomorphic on the disc of radius two
and vanishes at zero, so its real part has circle mean zero.
Thus each cell seminorm is at most
$\exp\{c_V|\square|+\mathscr C_K(rQ;\delta)\}$, and
\[
 \mathsf E e^{N_f\varrho_J^2\|T_A\|_2^2/2}
 \le\exp\{\mathsf N(c_V|\square|
                            +\mathscr C_K^\flat(Q;\delta))\}.
\]
Now average over all $2^{\mathsf N}$ choices of $A$.
Every ordered pair of distinct cells is in $A\times B$
with probability $1/4$, so
$\mathop{\rm avg}_A\|T_A\|_2^2=N_Q/4$.
Jensen's inequality at each configuration, followed by
integration in $U$, proves the assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A current in one cell]\label{C-402-47}
Suppose that $F$ vanishes at the midpoint of every bond
whose endpoints are not both in $Q$. Then
\[
 \|J^X(F)\|_{\rm ch}
 \le\frac{2\sqrt2c_{\rm h}\|X\|\|F\|_\infty}{\varrho_J}
        e^{c_V|\square|+\mathscr C_K^\flat(Q;\delta)}.
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
By \cref{C-402-45}, it suffices to treat $J^T(F)$.
Write it as $\bar\psi K\psi$. Its two blocks over a
chamber edge $(v,v')$ above the bond $b$ are
\[
 K(v',v)=iaF_\mu(b)h(v',v)TU(v',v),\qquad
 K(v,v')=-iaF_\mu(b)h(v,v')TU(v,v').
\]
The sum of the norms of the hopping blocks in each row
and each column is at most $c_{\rm h}=3(1+r)=9/2$.
Schur's test gives
$\|K\|\le ak$, $k=c_{\rm h}\|T\|\|F\|_\infty$.
The reflected copies $J_r=\bar\psi K_r\psi$ have
$K_r=P_rK_rP_r$, $\|K_r\|\le ak$, and mean zero at
each configuration. Reflection only conjugates these
blocks by unitary matrices, possibly taking their adjoints.

Let $\mathbb G=D_U^{-1}$ and
$\mathbb G'=\sum_{r\ne r'}P_{r'}\mathbb GP_r$.
The conditional mean $\langle\prod_rJ_r\rangle_U$ is
the coefficient of $\prod_rz_r$ in
$\det(1-\mathbb G\sum_rz_rK_r)$. This coefficient is
unchanged when $\mathbb G$ is replaced by $\mathbb G'$.
Indeed in the logarithmic determinant each square-free
word of degree at least two has distinct neighbouring
cell indices, including its last and first indices.
The degree-one terms vanish by the zero conditional means.
The square-free coefficient of the exponential uses only
these square-free logarithmic coefficients.

Put $A=\mathbb G'\sum_rz_rK_r$.
Its trace is zero. If $\lambda_i$ are its eigenvalues,
\[
 |\det(1-A)|
 =\prod_i|(1-\lambda_i)e^{\lambda_i}|
 \le\exp\{\tfrac12\sum_i|\lambda_i|^2\}
 \le e^{\|A\|_2^2/2}.
\]
The first inequality follows from
$|1-z|^2e^{2\operatorname{Re}z}\le e^{|z|^2}$;
the second follows by triangularizing $A$ unitarily.
On $|z_r|=\rho$, the summands have disjoint columns,
and hence
\[
 \|A\|_2^2
 \le\rho^2a^2k^2\sum_{r\ne r'}
                  \|P_{r'}\mathbb GP_r\|_2^2
 =2N_f\rho^2k^2N_Q.
\]
The last equality uses the two species, their adjoint
relation, and the $N_f$ identical flavour copies.
Cauchy's coefficient estimate gives
\[
 |\langle\prod_rJ_r\rangle_U|
       \le\rho^{-\mathsf N}e^{N_f\rho^2k^2N_Q}.
\]
Choose $\rho=\varrho_J/(2\sqrt2k)$, apply
\cref{C-402-46}, and take the $\mathsf N$th root of
the fold expectation. This proves the cell bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Joint bounds with currents]\label{C-402-48}
Let $n\ge2$, $R,d>0$. Suppose that each test function
is real and Lipschitz, its support lies in a ball of radius
$R$, and the supports are pairwise at distance at least $d$.
For labels in $\mathcal I^{\rm ext}\cup\mathfrak g$,
\[
 |S_n^T(\mathcal X)|
 \le[B_{\rm cur}(R)(1+d^{-1})^{\kappa-1}]^n
                      (n!)^\kappa\prod_i\|f_i\|_{\lambda_i}.
\]
The constant is independent of cutoff and volume, and
the estimate holds in each fixed-cutoff infinite-volume
state. For arbitrary scalar labels $M_i\in\mathscr S$,
include the factor $c(N_f)\|M_i\|$ at that entry.
One may take
\[
 \rho_{\rm cur}=\frac{\varrho_J}{8\sqrt2c_{\rm h}},\quad
 \rho_{\min}^{\rm cur}=\min(\varrho,\rho_{\rm cur}),\quad
 B_{\rm cur}(R)=C_B^{\rm cur}
    \max\{e^{c_V}/\rho_{\min}^{\rm cur},K_{\rm co}\}(1+R)^3,
\]
where $C_B^{\rm cur}$ depends only on the fixed source
and counting constants and
$K_{\rm co}=\max\{162,(165888N_f^2+24c^1_{\rm cur})/m_-\}$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Choose the least $q\ge0$ with $\sqrt3L^{-q}<d$ and
put $\eta=L^{-q}/(16n)$. Then
$\eta^{-1}\le16\sqrt3Ln(1+d^{-1})$.
First suppose $a\le\eta$. For scalar entries use the
hat partition of mesh $\eta$ from \cref{C-401-48}.
For currents use the hat partition of mesh $\eta/2$.
Its supports have side $\eta$; the endpoints of bonds
whose midpoints lie there belong to the concentric cube
of side $2\eta$, because $a\le\eta$.
Each entry has at most
$64(1+R)^3\eta^{-3}$ nonzero pieces.

For each tuple of pieces choose cells of physical side
$L^{-q}$ whose walls are at least $\eta$ from their
cubes. In each direction the forbidden wall positions
number at most $n(4\eta/a+1)<L^{-q}/a$.
The cell diameter is less than $d$, so it contains a
piece of at most one entry. This remains true for a
current piece: a nonzero piece has a bond midpoint in
the support of its original entry.

For a scalar piece use its exponential insertion and
the one-variable counterterm from \cref{C-401-48}.
For a current piece $J_i$, use $1+z_iJ_i$ and radius
\[
 \rho_i=\frac{\varrho_J}{2\sqrt2c_{\rm h}
                                  \|f_i\chi_i\|_{\lambda_i}}.
\]
Let $F(z)$ be the expectation of this product, multiplied
by the exponential of minus the scalar counterterms.
Then $F(0)=1$. Its logarithmic derivative in all variables
is the desired cumulant: the square-free coefficient
uses only the constant and linear terms of each factor,
and the subtracted terms depend on single variables.
On a coordinate face indexed by $A$, the chessboard
inequality and \cref{C-402-47} give
\[
 |F(z)|\le\prod_{i\in A}m_i,\qquad
 m_i=e^{c_V+\mathscr C_\eta}\ \hbox{for scalar pieces},
 \qquad m_i=2e^{c_V+\mathscr C_\eta}\ \hbox{for currents},
\]
where $\mathscr C_\eta$ is the supremum of
$\mathscr C_K(Q;\eta)$ over cubes of side $2\eta$.
For currents this uses the seminorm triangle inequality
$\|1+z_iJ_i\|_{\rm ch}\le1+|z_i|\|J_i\|_{\rm ch}$.
Cauchy's estimate and the partition formula give
\[
 |S_n^T(\hbox{pieces})|
 \le2^nn!\prod_i m_i\rho_i^{-1}
 \le2^nn!e^{n(c_V+\mathscr C_\eta)}
       \prod_i\frac{(1+80M)\eta^{-1}
                            \|f_i\|_{\lambda_i}}
                           {2\rho_{\min}^{\rm cur}}.
\]
At action-density entries the extra $\eta^{-1}$ comes
from differentiating the hats. At current entries,
$2\rho_i^{-1}=\|f_i\chi_i\|_{\lambda_i}/
(2\rho_{\rm cur})$, so the same estimate applies.
The source count used in \cref{C-401-48} gives
$e^{n\mathscr C_\eta}\le C_{\rm ct}^n\eta^{-np/2}$.
After summing the pieces we obtain
\[
 |S_n^T(\mathcal X)|\le
 \left[64(1+80M)C_{\rm ct}
       \frac{e^{c_V}}{\rho_{\min}^{\rm cur}}(1+R)^3\right]^n
       n!\eta^{-n(\kappa-1)}\prod_i\|f_i\|_{\lambda_i}.
\]
Use the bound on $\eta^{-1}$ and $n^n\le e^nn!$.

If $a>\eta$, use the moment estimate in
\cref{C-402-45}, the elementary bound
$|O(f)|\le2a^{-1}\sum_p|f(x(p))|$, and the
moment--cumulant formula. Balls of radius $R$ contain
at most $81a^{-3}(1+R)^3$ plaquette centres,
$27a^{-3}(1+R)^3$ sites and $24a^{-3}(1+R)^3$
bond midpoints. Each insertion is consequently bounded
by $K_{\rm co}a^{-4}(1+R)^3\|f_i\|_{\lambda_i}$
in every product moment. Since
$a^{-1}<16\sqrt3Ln(1+d^{-1})$, this gives
\[
 |S_n^T(\mathcal X)|\le
 [2e^4(16\sqrt3L)^4K_{\rm co}(1+R)^3
       (1+d^{-1})^4]^n(n!)^5\prod_i\|f_i\|_{\lambda_i}.
\]
Take $C_B^{\rm cur}$ to be the larger of
$64(1+80M)C_{\rm ct}(16\sqrt3Le)^{\kappa-1}$ and
$2e^4(16\sqrt3L)^4$. Since $\kappa\ge5$, both regimes
give the stated estimate. Every current is a local
Grassmann polynomial, so its product moments converge
along the tori defining a fixed-cutoff state. This
passes the estimate to those states. Expansion in
\cref{C-401-19} gives arbitrary scalar labels.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Joint limits with currents]\label{C-402-49}
Consider a sequence with cutoff tending to infinity,
either on a fixed torus, on growing tori, or in the
fixed-cutoff infinite-volume states used to define a
volume-first limit. There is a subsequence on which
the parameters converge and every joint truncated
function of orders $n\ge2$ for labels in
$\mathcal I^{\rm cur}$ converges on pairwise disjoint
$C_c^1$ supports. The resulting family $S^{\rm cur}$
obeys \cref{C-402-48}; at fixed labels and fixed current
components it defines a unique distribution of locally
finite order away from the diagonals.

On tuples without currents it is the scalar-bilinear
limit of the same subsequence. In particular, if the
sequence already defines $S^{\rm ext}$, that restriction
is unchanged. Every volume-first joint limit can also
be realized on a sequence of growing tori. These claims
include all $2N_f(4N_f-1)$ scalar bilinears, the action
density, and all currents $J^X$, $X\in\mathfrak g$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Fix disjoint closed supports in bounded balls. The
bound in \cref{C-402-48} gives equicontinuity in the
product of their insertion norms. Use a countable
dense family of $C^1$ scalar and vector functions,
supports in rational finite unions of closed cubes,
and the finite label set $\mathcal I^{\rm cur}$.
A diagonal subsequence gives convergence on this
family and convergence of the parameters in their
compact windows. Equicontinuity gives convergence
on all tuples; multilinearity extends the labels.
The restrictions are the original truncated functions
at every cutoff, proving the compatibility assertion.

For a volume-first sequence enumerate the dense
tuples as $\mathcal X^{(q)}$. At cutoff $K_j$ choose
a side $\ell_j\ge j$ from the torus sequence defining
the state so that its truncated functions differ from
the state values by at most $1/j$ on the first $j$
tuples. Such a side exists because each truncated
function is a polynomial in expectations of local
elements; this includes the currents. Uniform
equicontinuity extends the resulting convergence
from the dense family to every tuple.

For fixed labels and current components, the limiting
multilinear form is continuous in $C^1$ on a product
of bounded open sets with disjoint closures. The
Schwartz kernel theorem gives a unique distribution
of finite order there. Uniqueness makes these
distributions agree on overlaps, so they patch off
the diagonals.
\end{proof}

All constants introduced here are chosen after the
source constants of \cite{QCDM1}. They impose no new
small-coupling requirement. The joint compactness
statement concerns correlations away from coinciding
points; the two-current asymptotic proved above remains
a separate, more precise statement about that subfamily.


\section{Analytic dependence at fixed volume}\label{sec:analytic-labels}

A constant source changes the bare coupling or the bare mass.
This observation connects the source estimates to analytic
dependence on the physical parameters. The partition function
itself need not be bounded as the cutoff is removed. The useful
quantity is the partition function after the same vacuum energy
has been removed from its upper and lower bounds.

Throughout this section the physical torus $T_\ell$ is fixed.
Fix $0<g\le\gamma$ and an allowed side $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$,
and write
\[
 I_g=[g^{-2}+\bar B,\,L(g^{-2}+B_\sharp)-\bar B],
 \qquad W=I_g\times[m_-,m_+].
\]
The constants and the cofinal set $\mathfrak L(g)$ are those of
\cite[Prop. 10.20]{QCDM1}. In particular the estimates in this section
hold for every $K\ge1$ and every $(\mathsf b,\mathsf m)\in W$.
We use the chamber operator with $r=1/2$.

For a source $s=(w,J)$ put
\[
 Z_K[s]=\int e^{-(\mathsf b/a)A(U)+O_K(w)}
       \det\bigl(D[U]+a\mathsf m-a\widehat J\bigr)\,dU,
 \qquad a=L^{-K}.
\]
The determinant includes both internal blocks and all flavours.
Thus $Z_K[0]>0$. The source $w$ is a function on plaquette
centres and $J$ takes values in the complex span of the physical
meson basis $\mathfrak B$. The definitions of $O_K$ and the meson insertions are
those in \cref{sec:qcdm2-setting}. The action-source norm is
$\|w\|_\sharp=\max\{\|w\|_\infty,40M\operatorname{Lip}w\}$.
Let
\[
 \mathcal P=\{(w,J):\|w\|_\sharp\le2\varrho,
                              \ \|J\|_\infty\le2\varrho_J\}.
\]
The radii are independent of $K$ and $\ell$, and
$2\varrho_J\le c_Jm_-$, $c_J\le1/2$.

We first recall precisely the source input. It is the combination
of the local-energy, history and counting estimates of
\cite[Props. 10.6 and 10.14, and the counting estimate
preceding Prop. 10.16]{QCDM1}.
There is a holomorphic energy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-energy-decomposition}
 E_K(s)=E_K(0)+\sum_{j=1}^K\sum_{Y\in\mathcal D_j}e_j(Y;s),
 \qquad Z_K[s]=e^{E_K(s)}W_K[s],
\end{equation}
defined on a neighbourhood of $\mathcal P$. Here $Y$ is a
connected union of blocks of physical side $M\lambda_j$,
$\lambda_j=L^{j-K}$, and $d_j(Y)$ is the block-tree length
used in the construction. For fixed positive constants,
\begin{align}
 |e_j(Y;s)|&\le C_Ee^{-\kappa d_j(Y)},\label{eq:qcdm2-local-energy}\\
 |e_j(Y;s)-e_j(Y;s')|&\le C_Ee^{-\kappa d_j(Y)}
 e^{-\kappa_\sigma\operatorname{dist}(Y,\operatorname{supp}(s-s'))/\lambda_j}.
 \label{eq:qcdm2-energy-tail}
\end{align}
Distances in this section are physical. The geometry gives
$\operatorname{diam}Y\le c_DM\lambda_j(1+d_j(Y))$.
The construction chooses $\kappa$ so that summing
$e^{-\kappa d_j(Y)/2}$ over polymers containing one specified
block costs at most $C_{\rm cnt}$. Finally,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-partition-window}
 |W_K[s]|\le e^{(C+2)\ell^3},\qquad
 W_K[0]\ge e^{-C_P(1+\log X_g)\ell^3},\qquad
 X_g=L(g^{-2}+B_\sharp).
\end{equation}
The conjugation of the source makes $E_K$ real for constant real
coupling and mass shifts. No positivity at complex sources is
used.

\subsection{A zero-free neighbourhood}

Set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-analytic-radii}
 V_\ell=\exp\{[C+2+C_P(1+\log X_g)]\ell^3\},\qquad
 \rho_b=\frac{\varrho}{1+V_\ell},\qquad
 \rho_m=\frac{\varrho_J}{1+V_\ell}.
\end{equation}
Let $W_{\mathbb C}$ be the union, over $(b,m)\in W$, of the
open polydiscs $|b'-b|<\rho_b$, $|m'-m|<\rho_m$.

\begin{proposition}[Complex parameters]\label{C-403-41}
For every $K$, the partition function
$Z_{K,\ell}(b',m')=Z_K[0]$ formed with bare parameters
$b'/a$ and $am'$ has no zero on $W_{\mathbb C}$.
For a real base point $(b,m)\in W$, write
$c=(- (b'-b)1,-(m'-m)1)$ and
$R_K(b',m')=W_K[c]/W_K[0]$, with the energies and partition
functions based at $(b,m)$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-zero-free}
 |R_K-1|\le(1+V_\ell)
 \max\left\{\frac{|b'-b|}{2\varrho},
             \frac{|m'-m|}{2\varrho_J}\right\}<\frac12.
\end{equation}
On this polydisc the pressure has the decomposition
\[
 \ell^{-3}\log Z_{K,\ell}(b',m')
=\ell^{-3}E_K(c)+\ell^{-3}\log W_K[c].
\]
The logarithm is chosen real at the real base point, and
\[
 |\log R_K|\le\log2,\qquad
 \ell^{-3}|\log W_K[c]|
 \le C+2+C_P(1+\log X_g)+\ell^{-3}\log2.
\]
Consequently every sequence of cutoffs has a subsequence on
which $\ell^{-3}\log R_K$ converges locally uniformly on this
polydisc, with all parameter derivatives.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The constant source identity
$Z_{K,\ell}(b',m')=Z_K[c]$ holds before any integration:
the action coefficient becomes $b'/a$, and the matrix in the
determinant becomes $D+am'$. The ratio $R_K$ is holomorphic on
the larger polydisc with radii $2\varrho,2\varrho_J$,
$R_K(b,m)=1$, and $|R_K|\le V_\ell$ by
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-partition-window}.
For a nonzero displacement let $r$ be the maximum in
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-zero-free}. Restrict $R_K-1$ to the complex
line through that displacement, rescaled so that its unit
disc lies in the larger polydisc. Dividing by $1+V_\ell$
gives a function of modulus at most one, vanishing at zero.
The given displacement corresponds to radius $r$ on this
disc. Schwarz's lemma proves
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-zero-free}. Thus $R_K$ has a logarithm with
$|\log R_K|\le\sum_{n\ge1}2^{-n}/n=\log2$.
The remaining bounds follow from the positive real lower
bound and the upper bound in \eqref{eq:qcdm2-partition-window}.
Local boundedness gives a normally convergent subsequence;
Cauchy's formula gives convergence of every derivative.
\end{proof}

For example, if $p+q\ge1$, differentiation at a real base point
gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-integrated-cumulants}
 \left|S^T_{p+q,K}((0,1)^p,(1,1)^q)
       -(-\partial_{b'})^p(-\partial_{m'})^q
          E_K(c(b',m'))\big|_{(b',m')=(b,m)}\right|
 \le p!q!\log2\,\rho_b^{-p}\rho_m^{-q}.
\end{equation}
The RG base point $(b,m)$ is held fixed in this derivative.
Here the second label $1$ in $(1,1)$ is the constant test
function and the first is the identity meson matrix, extended
linearly from the chosen basis. The sign comes from the
constant-source identity. The vacuum term may diverge with
$K$; this estimate concerns its difference from the cumulant.
The radii in \eqref{eq:qcdm2-analytic-radii} depend on the
physical volume. No infinite-volume analyticity follows from
this argument.

\subsection{Supports with empty total intersection}

For closed nonempty sets $S_1,\ldots,S_n\subset T_\ell$ define
\[
 d_\cap(S_1,\ldots,S_n)
 =\min_{x\in T_\ell}\max_i\operatorname{dist}(x,S_i).
\]
Compactness shows that $d_\cap>0$ precisely when
$\bigcap_iS_i=\emptyset$. Pairwise intersections are allowed.
A tuple $X=((\alpha_i,f_i))_{i=1}^n$ is admissible in this
section when $n\ge2$, $\alpha_i\in\{0\}\cup\mathfrak B$,
$f_i$ is smooth, and its supports have
empty total intersection. We write $d_\cap(X)$ for this
distance. As usual $\|f\|_0=\|f\|_\sharp$ and
$\|f\|_\Gamma=\|f\|_\infty$ for $\Gamma\in\mathfrak B$;
these basis matrices have operator norm at most one.

\begin{lemma}[Mixed derivatives of the vacuum energy]\label{C-412-53}
Let $s_*+\sum_i z_is_i\in\mathcal P$ for $|z_i|\le r_i$,
and suppose the supports of $s_i$ have $d_\cap=d>0$.
There is a constant $C_{\rm ov}$, independent of $K$, $\ell$
and the sources, such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-overlap-energy}
 \left|\partial_1\cdots\partial_n
       E_K(s_*+\textstyle\sum_i z_is_i)\big|_{z=0}\right|
 \le 2^{n-1}C_{\rm ov}\ell^3(1+d^{-3})\prod_i r_i^{-1}.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $P_i$ set $z_i=0$. A mixed derivative kills every term
independent of one variable. It can therefore be estimated by
Cauchy's formula applied to $\prod_i(1-P_i)e_j(Y;s_*+s(z))$.
Explicitly, this finite difference is
\[
 \prod_i(1-P_i)e_j(Y;s_*+s(z))
 =\sum_{A\subset\{1,\ldots,n\}}(-1)^{n-|A|}
        e_j\left(Y;s_*+\sum_{i\in A}z_is_i\right).
\]
The operators $1-P_i$ commute. We may therefore choose one
index $i$ separately for each polymer, apply the source-tail
bound to $(1-P_i)e_j$, and bound the other $n-1$
differences by their $2^{n-1}$ terms. This is why empty
total intersection suffices: the source that is distant
from a small polymer need not be the same for every polymer.

Choose $y\in Y$. Some support $S_i$ has
$\operatorname{dist}(y,S_i)\ge d$. If
$\operatorname{diam}Y\ge d/2$, half the polymer weight pays
for this diameter:
\[
 e^{-\kappa d_j(Y)/2}
 \le e^{\kappa/2}e^{-\kappa d/(4c_DM\lambda_j)}.
\]
Otherwise $\operatorname{dist}(Y,S_i)\ge d/2$, and the source
tail supplies $e^{-\kappa_\sigma d/(2\lambda_j)}$.
Set
\[
 \eta=\min\{\kappa/(4c_DM),\kappa_\sigma/2\}.
\]
The derivative of one energy is at most
\[
 2^{n-1}C_Ee^{\kappa/2}\prod_i r_i^{-1}
 e^{-\eta d/\lambda_j}e^{-\kappa d_j(Y)/2}.
\]
Assigning each polymer to one of its blocks and using the
polymer count bounds the sum over $Y$ by this expression
times $C_{\rm cnt}(\ell/(M\lambda_j))^3$.
Finally
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^K\lambda_j^{-3}e^{-\eta d/\lambda_j}
 \le C_\eta(1+d^{-3}).
\]
Indeed, split at $\lambda_j=d$. The coarse part is a geometric
sum bounded by $Cd^{-3}$, and the fine part is bounded by
$Cd^{-3}\sum_{u\ge0}L^{3u}e^{-cL^u}$; when $d\ge1$ only
the latter estimate is needed. Summing the energy decomposition
proves the assertion.
\end{proof}

Let $k_n=\sum_{\pi}(|\pi|-1)!$, with the sum over partitions
of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let
$\varrho_{\min}=\min(\varrho,\varrho_J)$.

\begin{proposition}[Uniform cumulants at complex parameters]\label{C-412-54}
For every admissible tuple $X$ the lattice cumulant
$S^T_{n,K}(b,m;X)$ is holomorphic on $W_{\mathbb C}$, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-overlap-cumulant}
 |S^T_{n,K}(b,m;X)|
 \le\left(\frac n{\varrho_{\min}}\right)^n
 \left[k_n(2V_\ell)^n+
       2^{n-1}C_{\rm ov}\ell^3(1+d_\cap(X)^{-3})\right]
 \prod_i\|f_i\|_{\alpha_i}.
\end{equation}
For all $p,q\ge0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-parameter-insertion}
 (-\partial_b)^p(-\partial_m)^q S^T_{n,K}(X)
 =S^T_{n+p+q,K}(X,(0,1)^p,(1,1)^q).
\end{equation}
The tuple on the right has the same $d_\cap$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Work about a real base point and represent the new parameters
by the constant source $c$ of \cref{C-403-41}. For a zero test
function the assertion follows from multilinearity. Otherwise
choose $r_i=\varrho_{\alpha_i}/(n\|f_i\|_{\alpha_i})$.
The sum of the action-source norms is at most $\varrho$,
and the sum of the meson-source norms is at most $\varrho_J$.
Since $V_\ell\ge1$, the constant displacement has norms
less than $\rho_b\le\varrho/2$ and
$\rho_m\le\varrho_J/2$. In particular
\[
 \left\|c_w+\sum_i z_iw_i\right\|_\sharp
        <\tfrac32\varrho<2\varrho,
 \qquad
 \left\|c_J+\sum_i z_iJ_i\right\|_\infty
        <\tfrac32\varrho_J<2\varrho_J.
\]
Thus the whole Cauchy polydisc stays inside $\mathcal P$.
The triangle inequality gives this source budget even
when the supports overlap.

Set $G(z)=W_K[c+s(z)]/W_K[c]$. The zero-free estimate gives
$G(0)=1$ and $|G(z)|\le2V_\ell$. As germs at zero,
\[
 \log Z_K[c+s(z)]-\log Z_K[c]
 =E_K(c+s(z))-E_K(c)+\log G(z).
\]
The mixed derivative of the last term is
\[
 \sum_\pi(-1)^{|\pi|-1}(|\pi|-1)!
                 \prod_{B\in\pi}\partial^BG(0).
\]
For each block $B$ of a partition, Cauchy's estimate gives
\[
 |\partial^BG(0)|\le2V_\ell\prod_{i\in B}r_i^{-1}.
\]
The product over the blocks contains each inverse radius
once and costs $(2V_\ell)^{|\pi|}\le(2V_\ell)^n$.
Summing the partition coefficients therefore bounds the
mixed logarithmic derivative by
$k_n(2V_\ell)^n\prod_i r_i^{-1}$. This calculation uses
the logarithmic germ at zero; the generating function
may have zeros elsewhere in its source polydisc.
Apply \cref{C-412-53} to the energy and use
$\prod_i r_i^{-1}\le(n/\varrho_{\min})^n
\prod_i\|f_i\|_{\alpha_i}$. This proves
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-overlap-cumulant}.

The finite-dimensional integral is entire in the parameters
and the sources. Its partition function is nonzero at zero
source throughout $W_{\mathbb C}$; local logarithms therefore
give holomorphic cumulants there. Differentiating the
constant-source identity proves
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-parameter-insertion}. Adding an entry supported
on the whole torus adds zero to the maximum defining
$d_\cap$, so it leaves that distance unchanged.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Holomorphic families of continuum correlations]\label{C-412-55}
Every sequence $K_j\to\infty$ has a subsequence for which
$S^T_{n,K_j}(b,m;X)$ converges for every admissible tuple $X$,
locally uniformly in $(b,m)\in W_{\mathbb C}$ and with all
parameter derivatives. Denote the limit by $S_n(b,m;X)$.
It obeys \eqref{eq:qcdm2-overlap-cumulant} and
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-parameter-insertion} with the cutoff removed.
At real parameters its restriction to separated tuples is a
continuum limit of the original lattice model on $T_\ell$.
For each fixed choice of indices it determines a unique
distribution on
\[
 T_\ell^n\setminus\{x_1=\cdots=x_n\}.
\]
This distribution is symmetric and translation invariant,
has the flavour and cubic covariance of the lattice
correlations, and depends holomorphically on the parameters
when tested on admissible tensors.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Choose a countable collection of products whose factors are
finite unions of closed dyadic boxes and have empty total
intersection. On each product choose
countable dense sets of smooth test functions, in the $C^1$
norm for an action-density entry and the uniform norm for a
meson entry. There are finitely many basis indices at each
position. The bound \eqref{eq:qcdm2-overlap-cumulant} and
Montel's theorem, followed by a diagonal selection, give
locally uniform convergence on every tuple in these sets.
Use one enumeration containing all orders $n$, all label
strings, all these support tuples, and their dense test
families. A countable compact exhaustion of $W_{\mathbb C}$
makes the local uniform convergence part of this same
selection. Thus one subsequence works for all these data.

For an arbitrary admissible tuple the supports have
$d=d_\cap(X)>0$. Enlarge them by less than $d/4$ and cover
the enlarged sets by sufficiently fine closed dyadic cubes.
The resulting sets still have $d_\cap\ge d/2$. Approximation
within these sets extends the convergence to $X$ uniformly
on every compact parameter set. To see the uniformity,
write $T_K(f_1,\ldots,f_n)=S^T_{n,K}(b,m;X)$ with fixed
labels and these enlarged supports. The bound gives a
common constant $B$ there. Multilinearity gives
\[
 |T_K(f_1,\ldots,f_n)-T_K(h_1,\ldots,h_n)|
 \le B\sum_{i=1}^n\|f_i-h_i\|_{\alpha_i}
       \prod_{r<i}\|h_r\|_{\alpha_r}
       \prod_{r>i}\|f_r\|_{\alpha_r}.
\]
The approximating functions may be chosen with bounded
norms, so the right-hand side tends to zero uniformly
in $K$ and the parameters. Applying the same estimate
to two cutoffs proves convergence for the arbitrary tuple.

For a compact parameter set, choose slightly larger compact
polydiscs still contained in $W_{\mathbb C}$. Cauchy's
formula on their boundaries gives convergence of every
parameter derivative on the smaller sets. The constant
insertions in \eqref{eq:qcdm2-parameter-insertion} also
belong to the common extraction: adding a whole-torus
support preserves $d_\cap>0$. Hence both sides of the
insertion identity converge to the stated identity.

A point outside the total diagonal has two distinct
coordinates. It therefore has a product neighbourhood with
two disjoint closed factors. On this neighbourhood the
estimate defines a continuous multilinear functional on
smooth functions, hence a distribution. These local
distributions agree on overlaps: products of test functions
are dense, and the same limiting functional gives their
values. A partition of unity glues them uniquely.

Permutation, flavour and cubic identities hold at each cutoff
and pass to the limits. Approximate any torus translation by
lattice translations. Translation is continuous in the
test-function norms, so the uniform bound gives the full
translation identity. At real fixed parameters the same
subsequence defines the stated continuum limit. If parameters
also converge inside $W$, local uniform convergence shows that
the limit is the value of this same holomorphic family at the
limiting parameters.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Mass differentiation]\label{C-412-36}
For every admissible tuple the function $m\mapsto S_n(b,m;X)$
is real analytic on the allowed real interval and
\[
 \partial_m S_n(b,m;X)=-S_{n+1}(b,m;X,(1,1)).
\]
The inserted cumulants are bounded uniformly in the cutoff
at fixed $g$, $\ell$, $n$ and supports. The same holds for
every higher mass derivative and for mixed coupling and mass
derivatives.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Apply the preceding theorem and the insertion identity. The
uniform bound for the inserted tuple uses its unchanged
$d_\cap>0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{rem:qcdm2-total-diagonal}
The theorem fixes correlations on partial diagonals. It does
not fix an extension to the total diagonal. If two
translation-invariant distributional extensions exist, their
difference is supported there. In relative coordinates it is
a finite sum of derivatives of the delta distribution with
constant coefficients. Thus the remaining ambiguity is local;
it cannot be prescribed independently on a proper partial
diagonal.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Mass and Wilson insertions near the other fields}

Assume $N_f\ge2$ and choose a Hermitian flavour matrix $t$
with $\operatorname{tr}t=0$ and $\operatorname{tr}t^2=1$.
Write $\Gamma_t^0=1\otimes t$ and
$\Gamma_t^1=i\tau_1\otimes t$, with the identities on spin
and colour understood. In this subsection $a=L^{-K}$ and
$\nu_K$ is the gauge marginal. All masses are positive and
belong to the compact interval fixed in the construction.

The insertion of a constant mass source differentiates a
correlation function. An insertion supported near either
of the other fields requires a further estimate: separated
correlation bounds do not control it. The fourth Schatten
moment in \cref{C-415-21} supplies this estimate. The
Wilson insertion also differentiates the spatial cutoff;
this accounts for the factor $1+a^{1/2}/e$ below.

Put
\[
 \mathcal W=\Delta_++a\mathsf m,\qquad
 G_+=(\mathcal W+\mathcal B_U)^{-1},\qquad
 G_-=G_+^*,\qquad Y=\tfrac12(G_++G_-),
\]
where $\mathcal B_U^*=-\mathcal B_U$ and
$\mathsf G_\pm=aG_\pm$. For a bounded function $\chi$ define
\[
 \mathcal X_\Gamma(\chi)=\sum_v\chi(x_v)
             \bar\psi(v)\Gamma(\Delta\psi)(v),\qquad
 \mathcal J_\Gamma(\chi)=\sum_v\chi(x_v)
             \bar\psi(v)\Gamma(\mathcal B_U\psi)(v).
\]
Here $\Delta$ and $\mathcal B_U$ act on the full fermion
space; neither expression has a factor $a$. Set
\[
 \begin{split}
 T_K(f,\chi,h)&=S^T_{3,K}((\Gamma_t^1,f),
                         (\Gamma_1^1,\chi),(\Gamma_t^0,h)),\\
 T^X_K(f,\chi,h)&=\kappa_3(\Phi_{\Gamma_t^1}(f),
                    \mathcal X_{\Gamma_1^1}(\chi),\Phi_{\Gamma_t^0}(h)),\\
 T^J_K(f,\chi,h)&=\kappa_3(\Phi_{\Gamma_t^1}(f),
                    \mathcal J_{\Gamma_1^1}(\chi),\Phi_{\Gamma_t^0}(h)),\\
 \Xi_K(f,h)&=S^T_{2,K}((\Gamma_t^1,f),(\Gamma_t^1,h))
                  -S^T_{2,K}((\Gamma_t^0,f),(\Gamma_t^0,h)).
 \end{split}
\]

\begin{lemma}[The insertion identities]
\label{C-412-11}\label{C-412-12}\label{C-412-13}
At every configuration,
\[
 Y=G_-\mathcal WG_+=G_+\mathcal WG_-,\qquad
 Y^{-1}=\mathcal W+\mathcal B_U^*\mathcal W^{-1}\mathcal B_U
                    \ge\mathcal W>0.
\]
On a torus, for real bounded $f,h$,
\[
 \Xi_K(f,h)=4a^2\mathsf E_{\nu_K}\operatorname{Tr}(P_fYP_hY)
           =\mathsf m T_K(f,1,h)+T^X_K(f,1,h).
\]
If $\chi$ has support disjoint from those of $f,h$, then
\[
 T^J_K(f,\chi,h)+T^X_K(f,\chi,h)
                         =-\mathsf m T_K(f,\chi,h).
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The sum of $G_+^{-1}=\mathcal W+\mathcal B_U$ and
$G_-^{-1}=\mathcal W-\mathcal B_U$, multiplied by the
two inverses, gives the identities for $Y$. Multiplication
of $(\mathcal W+\mathcal B_U)\mathcal W^{-1}
(\mathcal W-\mathcal B_U)$ proves the inverse formula.

For bilinears at fixed $U$, the determinant identity gives
\[
 \kappa_n^U(\bar\psi A_1\psi,\ldots,\bar\psi A_n\psi)
 =-\sum_{\text{cyclic orders}}
                    \operatorname{Tr}(A_{i_1}G\cdots A_{i_n}G).
\]
Indeed the coefficient of degree $n$ in
$\log\det(1+GJ)$ has sign $(-1)^{n-1}$, whereas the
generating function uses $e^{-\bar\psi J\psi}$.
The one-point function of $\Phi_{\Gamma_t^0}$ vanishes
because $\operatorname{tr}t=0$; those of
$\Phi_{\Gamma_t^1}$, $\Phi_{\Gamma_1^1}$ and
$\mathcal X_{\Gamma_1^1}$ vanish because $\tau_1$ is
off diagonal in the two propagator blocks.
Thus their two- and three-point cumulants are the gauge
means of the conditional cumulants. Wick's rule gives
\[
 \Xi_K=a^2\mathsf E_{\nu_K}
            \operatorname{Tr}(P_f(G_++G_-)P_h(G_++G_-)),
\]
which is the first formula.

For the insertion identity use $\gamma_4=\tau_1$.
Since $\operatorname{tr}\gamma_4=0$,
\[
 \det(e^{\epsilon\gamma_4}(D_{m_0}+J)e^{\epsilon\gamma_4})
                       =\det(D_{m_0}+J).
\]
The derivative at zero replaces the operator by
$2\gamma_4\mathcal W+\{\gamma_4,J\}$. Differentiation
in the two sources uses
$\{\gamma_4,\Gamma_t^1\}=2i\Gamma_t^0$ and
$\{\gamma_4,\Gamma_t^0\}=-2i\Gamma_t^1$.
It gives the asserted identity because
$i\sum_v\bar\psi\gamma_4\mathcal W\psi
=\mathsf m\Phi_{\Gamma_1^1}(1)+\mathcal X_{\Gamma_1^1}(1)$.
The determinant identity holds before the gauge integral,
so it also proves the identity for the full cumulant.

Finally, contraction of $(D_{m_0}\psi)(v)$ with
$\bar\psi(w)$ gives $\delta_{vw}$. With all other
bilinear insertions away from $v$, the expectation of
$\bar\psi(v)\Gamma(D_{m_0}\psi)(v)$ times their product
is $-\operatorname{tr}\Gamma$ times the expectation of
that product. This factor is independent of $U$.
Its cumulants of order at least two therefore vanish.
Use $D_{m_0}=\mathcal B_U+\Delta+a\mathsf m$ and sum
against $\chi$ to obtain the equation of motion.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Local propagator norms and loops]
\label{C-412-60}
For a set of sites $Q$ and $\varphi\ge0$, put
\[
 n_Q=\|1_Q\mathsf G_+1_Q\|,\qquad
 x_\varphi(h)=a^2\sum_{s=\pm}
                  \operatorname{Tr}(P_\varphi G_sP_{|h|}G_{-s}).
\]
For the chamber hops put
$Q_s=(rt_s/2)^{1/2}(1-R_s)$, $0\le s\le3$, with
$r=1/2$. Define
\[
 \Delta_\chi=\sum_sQ_s^*P_\chi Q_s,\qquad
 E_\chi=\sum_s[P_\chi,Q_s^*]Q_s,\qquad
 x^\Delta_\varphi(h)=a\sum_{s=\pm}
                  \operatorname{Tr}(P_{|h|}G_{-s}\Delta_\varphi G_s).
\]
Write $x_Q=x_{1_Q}$ and $x_Q^\Delta=x_{1_Q}^\Delta$.
These loops are nonnegative and increase with $\varphi$
and $|h|$. Moreover $x_\varphi(h)=2\Pi_U(\varphi,|h|)$.

Choose $e=L^{-n}\le1/13$ and let $y$ run over
$e\mathbb Z^3/\ell\mathbb Z^3$. Set
\[
 c(t)=\begin{cases}\cos^2(\pi t/2),&|t|\le1,\\0,&|t|\ge1,\end{cases}
 \quad
 c^\sharp(t)=\begin{cases}1,&|t|\le2,\\
 \cos^2(\pi(|t|-2)/2),&2\le|t|\le3,\\0,&|t|\ge3.
 \end{cases}
\]
Define $p_y(x)=\prod_\mu c((x_\mu-y_\mu)/e)$,
$\chi_y(x)=\prod_\mu c^\sharp((x_\mu-y_\mu)/e)$,
$f_y=fp_y$, $h_y=hp_y$, and
$Q_y=\{x:|x-y|_\infty\le4e\}$. Differences are periodic.
Then $\sum_yp_y=1$, $\chi_y=1$ on $\operatorname{supp}p_y$,
$\operatorname{Lip}\chi_y\le3/e$, and each site belongs
to at most $9^3$ sets $Q_y$. If $a\le e$, all neighbours
of $\operatorname{supp}\chi_y$ belong to $Q_y$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Bounds for the four rings]
\label{C-412-61}\label{C-412-62}
The conditional cumulant defining $T_K(f,\chi,h)$ is the
sum, over $s=\pm$, of
\[
 a^3\operatorname{Tr}(P_fG_{-s}P_\chi G_sP_hG_s),\qquad
 a^3\operatorname{Tr}(P_fG_{-s}P_hG_{-s}P_\chi G_s).
\]
For $T^X_K$, replace $a^3P_\chi$ by $a^2P_\chi\Delta_+$.
The full cumulants are the gauge means of these sums.

Suppose $f$ is supported in $Q$ and write
$n=n_Q$, $x=x_Q(h)$, $x^\Delta=x_Q^\Delta(h)$.
For $|\xi|\le1$ supported in $Q$, each mass ring is at most
$\frac12\|f\|_\infty nx$ in modulus. If $0\le\chi\le1$
is Lipschitz and every neighbour of its support belongs
to $Q$, each Wilson ring is at most
\[
 \|f\|_\infty\left[n^{1/2}(x^\Delta x)^{1/2}
 +C_{\rm hop}a^{1/2}\operatorname{Lip}\chi
          \{n(x^\Delta x)^{1/2}+n^{1/2}x\}\right],
 \qquad C_{\rm hop}=\sqrt3/2.
\]
Both assertions hold with $f,h$ exchanged. Finally, if
$0\le\widetilde\chi\le1$ vanishes on $\operatorname{supp}h$,
and $\mathrm{sh}$ consists of the sites at distance at
most $3a$ from $\{0<\widetilde\chi<1\}$, then
\[
 x^\Delta_{\widetilde\chi}(h)
       \le C_{\rm en}\operatorname{Lip}\widetilde\chi\,x_{\mathrm{sh}}(h),
 \qquad C_{\rm en}=3.
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The zero conditional one-point functions noted above
remove every proper partition from the third-cumulant
formula. In the two cyclic Wick traces,
$(i\tau_1)^2=-1$ cancels its minus sign and $\tau_1$
exchanges the two propagator blocks. The flavour trace
is $\operatorname{tr}t^2=1$. This gives the four rings,
including their signs and powers of $a$.

For a mass ring insert $1_Q$ beside $P_f,P_\xi$ and
write $P_h=P_{|h|}^{1/2}\operatorname{sgn}(h)P_{|h|}^{1/2}$.
Use the operator norm $n/a$ at the propagator between
$f$ and $\xi$, and Hilbert--Schmidt norms at the other
two propagators. Twice their product is at most $x/a^2$.
This gives $\|f\|_\infty nx/2$ for either cyclic order.

Since the $R_s$ are self-adjoint involutions,
$\Delta_+=\sum_sQ_s^*Q_s$. Thus
$P_\chi\Delta_+=\Delta_\chi+E_\chi$. Only $s=0$
moves the physical site, and $t_0=3$, so the row
$C=([P_\chi,Q_s^*])_s$ satisfies
\[
 \|C\|\le C_{\rm hop}a\operatorname{Lip}\chi,\qquad
 \|E_\chi\|\le\tfrac32a\operatorname{Lip}\chi,
 \qquad \|[P_\chi,\mathcal B_U]\|\le3a\operatorname{Lip}\chi.
\]
Let $q=(P_\chi^{1/2}Q_s)_s$ and $\mathbf Q=(Q_s)_s$.
The identity $G_{-s}\mathcal WG_s=Y$ and
$\Delta_\chi\le\Delta_Q\le\mathcal W$ give
\[
 \|1_QG_{-s}q^*\|^2\le n/a,\qquad
 \|(1_Q\otimes1)\mathbf QG_s1_Q\|^2\le n/a.
\]
The squared Hilbert--Schmidt norms with one energy
factor are at most $x^\Delta/a$; those without it are
at most $x/a^2$. In the part with $q^*q$, H\"older's
inequality gives
$a^2(n/a)^{1/2}(x^\Delta/a)^{1/2}(x/a^2)^{1/2}$.
In the two parts with $C\mathbf Q$ it gives, respectively,
\[
 a^2(n/a)\|C\|(x^\Delta/a)^{1/2}(x/a^2)^{1/2},\qquad
 a^2(n/a)^{1/2}(x/a^2)\|C\|.
\]
These are exactly the three terms in the Wilson bound.
Exchanging $f,h$ exchanges the two cyclic orders.

For the energy estimate let $\psi=G_+\phi$, where
$\phi$ is supported on $\operatorname{supp}h$.
The real part of
$\langle P_{\widetilde\chi}\psi,(\mathcal W+\mathcal B_U)\psi\rangle=0$
is
\[
 \langle\psi,(\Delta_{\widetilde\chi}+a\mathsf mP_{\widetilde\chi})\psi\rangle
 =-\tfrac12\langle\psi,[P_{\widetilde\chi},\mathcal B_U]\psi\rangle
       -\operatorname{Re}\langle\psi,E_{\widetilde\chi}\psi\rangle.
\]
The commutators and the one further hop are supported in
$\mathrm{sh}$. Drop the nonnegative mass term and use
their norm bounds to obtain
$\langle\psi,\Delta_{\widetilde\chi}\psi\rangle
\le3a\operatorname{Lip}\widetilde\chi\|1_{\mathrm{sh}}\psi\|^2$.
The same argument applies to $G_-$.
Sum over $\phi=P_{|h|}^{1/2}e_j$ and multiply by $a$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A second moment for the joining loop]
\label{C-412-63}
Suppose $0\le\varphi_1,\varphi_2\le1$ have supports in
one ball of radius $R'$, separated by $d_1>0$. Then
\[
 \mathsf E_{\nu_K}x_{\varphi_1}(\varphi_2)^2
     \le C_{\rm sm}(g,R',d_1)^2,
 \qquad
 C_{\rm sm}=\frac4{\exp(1)\theta_{\rm jl}}C_{\rm jl}(R',d_1)^{1/2}.
\]
This constant is independent of the side, cutoff and
the labels in their fixed intervals.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Use $x_{\varphi_1}(\varphi_2)=2\Pi_U(\varphi_1,\varphi_2)$
and the $q=2$ case of \cref{C-415-24}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The near-support sums]
\label{C-412-64}
Let $f,h$ be real bounded functions whose supports lie
in one ball of radius $R$ and have distance $d>0$.
Set
\[
 e_0=\min\{d/64,\sigma_0(g)/8\},\qquad
 \epsilon_{\rm nr}(e)=8^4(2R+1)^3 C_{\rm S4}
                         e\ell_g(e)^{p_4},
\]
where $\sigma_0,C_{\rm S4},p_4,\ell_g$ are the constants
and function in \cref{C-415-21}. There is
$C_{\rm nr}=C_{\rm nr}(g,R,d)$, independent of the side,
cutoff and labels, such that for $a\le e\le e_0$,
\[
 \begin{split}
 &\sum_y\sup_{\substack{|\xi|\le1\\\operatorname{supp}\xi\subset Q_y}}
   \bigl(|T_K(f_y,\xi,h)|+|T_K(f,\xi,h_y)|\bigr)
 \le C_{\rm nr}\epsilon_{\rm nr}(e)^{1/4}
                                    \|f\|_\infty\|h\|_\infty,\\
 &\sum_y\bigl(|T^X_K(f_y,\chi_y,h)|+|T^X_K(f,\chi_y,h_y)|\bigr)
 \le C_{\rm nr}(1+a^{1/2}/e)
       \{\epsilon_{\rm nr}(e)^{1/8}+\epsilon_{\rm nr}(e)^{1/4}\}
                                    \|f\|_\infty\|h\|_\infty.
 \end{split}
\]
One may take
\[
 C_{\rm nr}=1458\max\{4,12C_{\rm hop}\}
       \max\{1,(8C_{\rm en}/d)^{1/2}\}
                  C_{\rm sm}(g,3R,d/4).
\]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Consider the pieces of $f$ first and discard zero pieces.
Their number is at most $(2R+1)^3e^{-3}$. Each $Q_y$
has side $8e$, so \cref{C-415-21} gives
\[
 \sum_y\mathsf E_{\nu_K} n_{Q_y}^4\le\epsilon_{\rm nr}(e).
\]
For nonnegative random variables $Z_y$ and $0<p\le1$,
H\"older's inequality on the product of $\nu_K$ and
counting measure yields
\[
 \sum_y\mathsf E(n_{Q_y}^pZ_y)
 \le\left(\sum_y\mathsf E n_{Q_y}^4\right)^{p/4}
                  \left[\mathsf E\left(\sum_yZ_y\right)^2\right]^{1/2}.
\]
Indeed the other exponent is $4/(4-p)\le2$,
$\sum_yZ_y^{4/(4-p)}\le(\sum_yZ_y)^{4/(4-p)}$,
and monotonicity of probability norms gives the display.

The cubes $Q_y$ lie in the $d/4$-neighbourhood $Q'$ of
$\operatorname{supp}f$. Their multiplicity is at most
$729$, hence
\[
 \sum_yx_{Q_y}(h)\le729x_{Q'}(h),\qquad
 \sum_y(x^\Delta_{Q_y}(h)x_{Q_y}(h))^{1/2}
           \le729(x^\Delta_{Q'}(h)x_{Q'}(h))^{1/2}.
\]
Take
$\widetilde\chi=\min\{1,\max\{0,3-8\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{supp}f)/d\}\}$.
It equals one on $Q'$, vanishes beyond distance $3d/8$,
and has Lipschitz constant $8/d$. Since $a\le d/64$,
its shell lies in the $d/2$-neighbourhood $Q''$ of
$\operatorname{supp}f$. The energy inequality gives
\[
 x^\Delta_{Q'}(h)\le(8C_{\rm en}/d)x_{Q''}(h).
\]
Dominate $1_{Q''}$ and $|h|/\|h\|_\infty$ by continuous
functions in $[0,1]$, with supports in a ball of radius
$3R$ separated by $d/4$. For example use the linear
cutoffs $\min\{1,\max\{0,5-8\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{supp}f)/d\}\}$
and $\max\{0,1-8\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{supp}h)/d\}$.
Thus \cref{C-412-63} bounds
$\mathsf E x_{Q''}(h)^2$ by
$C_{\rm sm}^2\|h\|_\infty^2$.

Apply the preceding H\"older estimate with $p=1$ to
the mass rings. For the Wilson rings use $p=1/2$ and
$p=1$, the energy bound and $\operatorname{Lip}\chi_y\le3/e$.
Their four cyclic terms, the multiplicity $729$, and
the identical estimate with $f,h$ exchanged are bounded
by the displayed $C_{\rm nr}$. This proves both assertions.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Recovering the constant insertion]
\label{C-412-65}
Fix an admitted torus and a subsequence along which all
off-diagonal scalar correlations converge to $S$.
For real $C^1$ functions $f,h$ with disjoint supports,
define
\[
 j_e(S;f,h)=\sum_{y,y'}S_3((\Gamma_t^1,f_y),
       (\Gamma_1^1,1-\chi_y-\chi_{y'}),(\Gamma_t^0,h_{y'})).
\]
Then $j_S(f,h)=\lim_{e\downarrow0}j_e(S;f,h)$ exists,
depends only on $S$, and
\[
 \begin{split}
 T_K(f,1,h)&\longrightarrow j_S(f,h),\\
 T^X_K(f,1,h)&\longrightarrow\Xi_S(f,h)-\mathsf m j_S(f,h),\\
 |j_S-j_e(S)|&\le C_{\rm nr}\epsilon_{\rm nr}(e)^{1/4}
                                      \|f\|_\infty\|h\|_\infty.
 \end{split}
\]
This is also the constant insertion in any analytic
family of \cref{C-412-55} extending $S$.

If $W_{e,K}$ is the analogous sum with $T^J_K$ in place
of $S_3$, then for $a\le e^2$,
\[
 |\Xi_K(f,h)+W_{e,K}(f,h)|
 \le(m_++2)C_{\rm nr}
       (\epsilon_{\rm nr}(e)^{1/8}+\epsilon_{\rm nr}(e)^{1/4})
                            \|f\|_\infty\|h\|_\infty.
\]
Consequently the iterated limit, first along the cutoff
subsequence and then as $e\downarrow0$, is zero.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
For fixed $e$, the three supports in every nonzero term
of $j_e$ are separated by at least $e$. Indeed
$\chi_y=1$ on the $e$-neighbourhood of $\operatorname{supp}f_y$;
the cutoffs tied to $f$ and $h$ are disjoint because
$e\le d/64$. Thus every term has a limit determined by $S$.
Split the constant insertion by
$1=\chi_y+\chi_{y'}+(1-\chi_y-\chi_{y'})$ and sum over
$y,y'$. The first estimate of \cref{C-412-64} bounds
the difference between $T_K(f,1,h)$ and the separated
sum uniformly in $K$. It tends to zero with $e$.
This proves the Cauchy property of $j_e$, the claimed
limit and its error. The insertion identity then gives
the Wilson limit. If an analytic family exists, the
constant tuple converges by \cref{C-412-55}; uniqueness
of the preceding limit identifies it with $j_S$.

Apply the equation of motion to the separated middle
insertion. The resulting separated mass and Wilson
terms cancel the corresponding parts of the exact
identity for $\Xi_K$. Only the two near-support sums
remain. If $a\le e^2$, then $1+a^{1/2}/e\le2$;
\cref{C-412-64} gives the last estimate.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{C-412-66}
The near-support estimates require $a\le e$. Their
continuum conclusion takes the cutoff limit before
$e\downarrow0$. They assert neither decay for every
$e>0$ at a fixed lattice spacing nor disappearance of
the Wilson insertion: its limit is the displayed
$\Xi_S-\mathsf m j_S$.
\end{remark}

\section{Positive masses and continuation}\label{sec:qcdm2-mass-continuation}

\subsection{Constants independent of a lower mass bound}

The estimates for a step of the flow use
$0<\mathfrak m_k\le1/2$ and
$\eta_k\ge c_b=b_F(1-L^{-1})/(b_F(1-L^{-1})+1/2)$.
Neither inequality requires a positive lower bound for the
physical mass. A lower mass bound enters when the final
Berezin integral is estimated relative to its Gaussian part.
We record the distinction because the comparison of gauge
observables uses the first group of estimates alone.

\begin{definition}[Constants and weak data]\label{C-416-2}
Use the constants of \cite[Prop. 10.20]{QCDM1}, with the
following choices. Increase the flow bound, at its place
in the order, so that
\[
 B_\sharp\ge(1+L^{-1})(c_{2,\rm loop}+N_fc_2^F)+2.
\]
Use the history mark with dials
\[
 (\mathsf w,c_a,C_{\rm vol},c_{\rm Dep})=(1/2,0,0,c_\star)
 \quad\text{and share }\eth=1/2.
\]
Here $c_\star$ is the positive rate gained on a created cell
at zero loss. The dials lie in the admitted ranges.
Choose $\gamma$ under the original ceilings except
\[
 \gamma^2\le\frac{c_bm_-}{8C_{\mathsf S_1}\bar B_M},
 \qquad\phi(\gamma^{-2})\le c_*(m_-),
 \qquad\gamma\le\gamma(2A_\kappa h_*,5B_s),
\]
and except the ceilings formed at the weight $2A_\kappa h_*$
for the last of these. Retain the ceilings at weight $h_F$
and radii $1,5B_s$. Retain the upper-history and pure-gauge
terminal thresholds for the displayed mark and share.
Impose in addition
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 (28C_w\phi(\gamma^{-2})+24\bar B)\gamma^2&\le r_x,&
 C_w\phi(\gamma^{-2})&\le1,\\
 4C_\rho S_3^\sharp\psi_\sharp(\gamma^{-2})&\le1,&
 3\bar B_M\gamma&\le1.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The function in the third inequality is
$\psi_\sharp(x)=x^{-1/2}(1+\log x)^{9\mathfrak p_0}$.
All constants on the right, and those multiplying these
functions, were chosen before the mass interval. Thus these
conditions admit a positive $\gamma$ independently of that
interval.

A weak datum is
\[
 (g,\ell',K',\mathsf b',\mathsf m'),\qquad
 0<g\le\gamma,\quad \ell'\in\mathfrak L(g),\quad
 \mathsf b'\in I_g,\quad0<\mathsf m'\le1/2.
\]
There is no further lower bound on $\mathsf m'$.
Its bare mass is $L^{-K'}\mathsf m'$, its fine masses are
$\mathfrak m_k=L^{k-K'}\mathsf m'$, and its calibrations
are $\mathsf t_i=L^{K'-i}\mathsf b'$.

For a side $\ell=2L^m$, $\mathsf b_*>0$ and $\mathsf m>0$,
let $\bar n$ be the least nonnegative integer such that
\[
 L^{\bar n}\mathsf b_*\ge\gamma^{-2}+\bar B,\qquad
 L^{-\bar n}\mathsf m\le1/2,\qquad
 m+\bar n\ge m_{\bar g},\quad
 \bar g=(L^{\bar n}\mathsf b_*-\bar B)^{-1/2}.
\]
For $K>\bar n$ the relabelled datum is
\[
 (\bar g,L^{\bar n}\ell,\bar K,\bar{\mathsf b},\bar{\mathsf m})
 =(\bar g,L^{\bar n}\ell,K-\bar n,
                           L^{\bar n}\mathsf b_*,L^{-\bar n}\mathsf m).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[The estimates available at a weak datum]
\label{C-416-6}
At every weak datum the zero-source small-field induction,
the step estimates at weight $h_F$ and radii $1,5B_s$,
the upper bounds on the forward mass correction, the second-order expansion with
its cubic remainder, and the pointed activity estimates
hold with constants independent of a lower mass bound.
So do the history estimates, their upper partition bound,
the unintegrated lower measure bound, the exact determinant
identities, and the step-energy estimate
\[
 |e_j|\le C'_e(1+\log x_{j-1}).
\]
This assertion does not include a lower partition bound
with a constant independent of $\mathsf m'$.

At every $1\le k\le K'$ and real
$x\ge\max\{\gamma^{-2},3\mathsf t_k/4\}$, the small-field
weight with coefficient $L^kx$ satisfies
\[
 \int\mathsf{sf}_k[x]\,dV_k\ge
 \exp\left[-\left(\tfrac92\log x+3\log7
                   +24(B_3^{\rm cr})^2\right)n_k\right].
\]
The coefficient $x_k$ of the flow is in this range.

The integer $\bar n$ of \cref{C-416-2} exists. Its relabelled
datum is weak and has the same bare integral, lattices,
calibrations, tests and history terms through level $\bar K$
as $(K,\ell,\mathsf b_*,\mathsf m)$. For $\bar n\le d<K$,
the block field $\mathcal M^{K-d}U$ is the level $K-d$
field in both descriptions.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Enlarge the auxiliary mass interval to
\[
 [m'_-,m'_+]=[\min\{m_-,\mathsf m'\},
                         \max\{m_+,\mathsf m'\}].
\]
Keep all earlier constants, the radii and $\gamma$ unchanged,
and recompute numbers defined from this interval. The weak
datum is a datum for these parameters. We check which
conditions can fail and which estimates use them.

The constants before the mass interval are unchanged.
The enlarged interval still satisfies $0<m'_-\le m'_+\le1/2$.
Of the later conditions only the three omitted ceilings
and $2\varrho_J\le c_Jm'_-$ can fail. The latter is used
to keep the real part of the fine source mass above half
the bare mass. It has no role at zero sources.
The first omitted ceiling bounds the final mass correction
by a fixed fraction of $m_-$, and bounds
$\log(1/\mathfrak m_k)$ by $\log x_k$ with a constant
fixed from the original interval. All three are used to
expand the final Berezin integral at the enlarged weight
$2A_\kappa h_*$. That final expansion is the only use
of this enlarged weight in the estimates listed here.

We now check the estimates that remain.
The background covariance, averaging and reconstruction
bounds of \cite[\S\S5--6]{QCDM1} are valid for every
$0<m_0\le L^{-K'}/2$; their constants depend on the chamber
operator, $L,b_F$ and the chosen geometric bounds.
The local fermion expansion and the step construction in
\cite[\S7]{QCDM1} are applied at weight $h_F$.
Their Grassmann contractions use the same Gram bounds,
and their mass extraction uses $\eta_k\ge c_b$.
The retained ceilings $\gamma\le\gamma(h_F,1)$ and
$\gamma\le\gamma(h_F,5B_s)$ close these steps. No inverse
of the physical mass enters these bounds.

The explicit second-order terms, their moment extraction,
the identity for their total, and the cubic remainder in
\cite[\S8]{QCDM1} use fine masses in $[0,1]$ and
$\eta_k\ge c_b$. Their constants precede the mass interval.
The geometric sum of the cubic remainders and the telescoping
one-loop increments give the forward window
$|s_k|\le\bar B_M/x_k$ under these same ceilings.
Only the further comparison of this window with $m_-$
would use the first omitted ceiling.

The pointed estimate in \cite[\S9]{QCDM1} takes as
inputs this step, the window $|s_k|\le2\bar B_M/\mathsf t_k$,
and the bound $\|E_{\ge2}^{(i)}\|_i\le
C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{i-1})^2$. Its pointwise constant is
$8M^3C_2$. The leg bounds, cluster counts and mass extraction
used in its proof are all at weight $h_F$; its only mass
denominator is $\eta_k$, already bounded below by $c_b$.
It therefore applies at the weak datum. This verifies in
particular the pointed estimate needed in the history sum;
the unpointed estimate alone would not suffice there.

The history construction, its scalar remainders and its
upper bound in \cite[\S9]{QCDM1} use the preceding bounds
and the fixed history mark. The constants $C_5^F,C_E^F,
C_\flat^F,C_{\rm fs},C'_e$ are formed at weight $h_F$.
The upper-bound threshold for the fixed mark is retained.
The exact Gaussian determinant identity and the degree-zero
part of the history term hold at every positive bare mass.
They give the lower bound as measures before it is weakened
to a scalar lower partition bound. Positivity of history
weights and the displayed step-energy estimate also hold
at every positive bare mass. Thus all the assertions made
in the statement have the same constants after enlarging
the interval.

The estimates deliberately excluded from this argument are
the final Gaussian lower estimate, the constants containing
$\log(1/m_-)$, the coarse-cutoff moment bounds using
$\|(D+m_0)^{-1}\|\le1/m_0$, and the charged decay estimates
whose rates depend on $m_-$. When any of them is used,
its mass-dependent constants must be recomputed. Deleting
the matter terms gives the same zero-source construction
without fermions: the relevant conditions on $N_f$ are
floors on constants free to increase, so the already chosen
constants suffice.

For the small-field integral set $s=x^{-1/2}$. The retained
geometric ceilings give
\[
 s\le\gamma\le\bar\varepsilon/4,\qquad
 s\le2\mathsf t_k^{-1/2}
   \le\frac{A_0(\log\mathsf t_k)^{\mathfrak p_0}
                      \mathsf t_k^{-1/2}}{4B_3^{\rm cr}}.
\]
The ball of radius $s$ about the trivial block field passes
the tests. Its measure is at least $(s^3/7)^{3n_k}$, and
the action in the weight is at most
$24(B_3^{\rm cr})^2s^2xn_k=24(B_3^{\rm cr})^2n_k$.
Multiplying these two bounds gives the stated integral.
For $x=x_k$, the flow gives
$x_k\ge\mathsf t_k-\bar B\ge\gamma^{-2}$ and
$\bar B\le\mathsf t_k/4$, so it applies.

Finally the first two conditions defining $\bar n$ hold
for all sufficiently large integers. In the third condition,
$m_{(L^n\mathsf b_*-\bar B)^{-1/2}}$ grows at most like
$\log n$: the only growing term is
$\log_LR(L^{n+1}\mathsf b_*)$, and
$R(x)\le L(\log x)^{r_c}$. The left side $m+n$ grows
linearly, so $\bar n$ exists.
Its first condition gives $\bar g\le\gamma$ and
$\bar{\mathsf b}=\bar g^{-2}+\bar B\in I_{\bar g}$;
the others give the admitted side and
$0<\bar{\mathsf m}\le1/2$.
The identities
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \ell L^K&=(L^{\bar n}\ell)L^{\bar K},&
 L^K\mathsf b_*&=L^{\bar K}\bar{\mathsf b},\\
 L^{-K}\mathsf m&=L^{-\bar K}\bar{\mathsf m},&
 L^{K-k}\mathsf b_*&=L^{\bar K-k}\bar{\mathsf b}
 \end{aligned}
\]
identify the bare integral and every intermediate lattice
and calibration through level $\bar K$. Tests, cubes,
history weights and block maps are formed from these data;
hence they agree. In particular
$n_k=\ell^3L^{3(K-k)}$, with
$n_{\bar K}=L^{3\bar n}\ell^3$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Every positive mass label}

We can choose the upper bound for $g$ before choosing a
compact positive mass interval. The remaining constants
need not stay bounded as the lower endpoint tends to zero.
The argument replaces the final Gaussian lower estimate
by a determinant inequality valid at every positive bare mass.

\begin{definition}[Constants for all positive masses]
\label{C-412-78}
Choose the constants through $h_F$, the action-source radius
$\varrho$, and
\[
 0<c_J\le\min\{1/2,\varrho_*,r_M/L\}
\]
in their original order. Choose $\gamma\in(0,1/2]$ under
all the original step, history and source ceilings except
the three lower-mass ceilings displayed in
\cref{C-416-2} and their enlarged-weight conditions.
Retain the ceilings at weight $h_F$ and radii $1,5B_s$.
Use the original admissible history mark, with its upper
history threshold. After these choices take any
\[
 0<m_-\le m_+\le1/2,\qquad0<2\varrho_J\le c_Jm_-.
\]
Finally, with $\nu=8N_f$, define
\[
 \begin{split}
 C_P^{(K)}&=\max\left\{\tfrac92,
 C_5^F+3\log7+24(B_3^{\rm cr})^2+1+
                                      \nu\log\frac2{c_bm_-}\right\},\\
 C_P&=C_P^{(K)}+C'_e,\qquad
 C_m^w=\log\left(\frac1{b_F(1-L^{-1})}
                                +\frac{1+\bar B}{4m_-}\right).
 \end{split}
\]
Form all later insertion and compactness constants from
these values. In particular $c_V=C+2+C_P(1+\log X_g)$.
The data and admitted sides are otherwise unchanged.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Order of the choices]\label{C-412-79}
The choices in \cref{C-412-78} exist, with a positive upper
bound for $\gamma$ independent of $[m_-,m_+]$.
All original hypotheses hold except the three omitted
ceilings and the conditions at their enlarged weight.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The dependency check in \cref{C-416-6} identifies all uses
of the lower mass bound in the construction. The source
estimates add $2\varrho_J\le c_Jm_-$; we impose it after
choosing the interval. Their other radii are $\varrho$,
$\varrho_*$ and $r_M$, and the domain condition
$L^{k+1-K}\|J\|_\infty<r_M$.
The source-chain constants and ceilings are formed from
these radii and the constants through $h_F$.
The quantities formed later from $\varrho_J$, $C_P$ and
the mass interval are constants in the resulting estimates;
they impose no new ceiling on $\gamma$.

The original history mark changes only its fixed upper
threshold in the proof of \cref{C-416-6}. This threshold
also precedes the mass interval. Each retained ceiling
has a positive right side independent of that interval
and either bounds $\gamma$ directly or bounds a function
tending to zero with $\gamma$. Their finite conjunction
therefore holds on a nonempty interval $(0,\gamma_w)$.
The interval and $\varrho_J$ can then be chosen as stated.
Finally $C_P,C_m^w$ and every later constant are explicit
functions of earlier choices, so introduce no circularity.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Positivity of the extracted mass]
\label{C-398-37}
At every positive-mass datum and every level $k$ of the
forward flow, $s_k\ge0$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The assertion is immediate for $k=0$. On the history with
no large-field region, put
\[
 v(U)=\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset}(U)e^{-\beta A(U)}
       \prod_{j<k}\theta^{-\nu n_{j+1}}\det\Gamma_j[U].
\]
The block tower has the same adjoint pair of internal
blocks as $D[U]+m_0$. Indeed the real averaging maps
commute with the internal projections, and
\[
 \Gamma_j=\mathbb D_j+\theta q^*q,\qquad
 \mathbb D_{j+1}=\theta-\theta^2q\Gamma_j^{-1}q^*
\]
preserve that form. Positive accretivity at $m_0>0$
makes these matrices invertible. Each $\det\Gamma_j$
is therefore the squared modulus of a nonzero determinant,
so $v\ge0$.

Completing the Gaussian square at each level gives exactly
\[
 \check\tau^F_{h_\emptyset}
   =\mathcal M^k_*
      \left(v(U)e^{-\langle\bar\Psi,\mathbb D_k[U]\Psi\rangle}
                                                               dU\right).
\]
Let $\mathfrak K_\ell(V)$ be the degree-two kernel of
minus the exponent in its RG representation, and let
$\mathfrak Z=\mathcal M^k_*(v\,dU)$. Comparing degrees
zero and two gives the identity of matrix-valued measures
\[
 \mathcal M^k_*(\mathbb D_k[U]v(U)\,dU)
                      =\mathfrak K_\ell(V)\mathfrak Z(dV).
\]
Near $V=1$ the small-field tests pass, the degree-zero
density is continuous and nonzero, and $\mathfrak K_\ell$
is continuous. Thus $\mathfrak Z$ charges every sufficiently
small ball $B_\epsilon$ about $1$, and
\[
 \mathfrak K_\ell(1)=\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}
 \frac{\int_{\{\mathcal M^kU\in B_\epsilon\}}
                              \mathbb D_k[U]v(U)\,dU}
      {\int_{\{\mathcal M^kU\in B_\epsilon\}}v(U)\,dU}.
\]
The three-square identity of \cite[\S8]{QCDM1} gives
\[
 \operatorname{Re}\mathbb D_k[U]
 \ge\frac{\theta_k\mathfrak m_k}{\theta_k+\mathfrak m_k}\,1
\]
at every $U$. A conditional mean with nonnegative weight
preserves this inequality, so it holds for
$\operatorname{Re}\mathfrak K_\ell(1)$.

At the trivial field the free block kernels and background
maps are periodizations of exponentially decaying kernels.
Activities on polymers that fit inside the torus agree
with their infinite-lattice versions. The remaining polymers
have diameter at least the side divided by $2M$, minus
two, so the polymer decay bounds their contribution to
any fixed kernel entry by a quantity tending to zero.
It follows that $\mathfrak K_\ell(1)$ converges entrywise
to an exponentially decaying translation-invariant kernel
$\mathfrak K_\infty$. The lower quadratic-form bound
passes first to finite-support vectors and then to its
Fourier symbol at every momentum.

At zero momentum that symbol is the zeroth moment.
The mass extraction subtracts the zeroth moment of each
activity; their subsequent Gaussian readings preserve its
vanishing, by the exact identity used in the forward flow.
Consequently the zeroth moment is
\[
 \frac{\theta_k\mathfrak m_k}{\theta_k+\mathfrak m_k}
                                     +\eta_k^2s_k.
\]
It is real by conjugation. The lower bound therefore gives
$\eta_k^2s_k\ge0$, and $\eta_k>0$ proves the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The lower partition bound at positive mass]
\label{C-412-80}
Under \cref{C-412-78}, the forward flow and the upper
history estimates retain their original bounds. In particular
\[
 |s_K|\le\bar B_M/x_K\le\bar B_Mg^2,\qquad
 0\le s_K\le(2B_F+1/2)/\mathsf b.
\]
At every level $1\le k\le K$,
\[
 Z_K\ge\exp[E_k-C_P(1+\log x_k)n_k],\qquad
 \nu\log(1/\theta_k+1/\mathfrak m_k)
                         \le\nu(\log x_k+C_m^w).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The step and mass-flow bounds follow from \cref{C-416-6},
whose dependency proof applies to the original mark as
explained in \cref{C-412-79}. The induction still gives
\[
 \left|s_K-\frac{F(K;\mathsf m)}{\mathsf b}\right|
 \le C_s\mathsf b^{-3/2}(1+\log\mathsf b)^{9\mathfrak p_0}.
\]
The retained cubic-remainder ceiling and the calibration
comparison give the stated upper bound
$(2B_F+1/2)/\mathsf b$, as in the proof of the forward
flow. Positivity is \cref{C-398-37}.

The determinant tower gives the degree-zero measure of
the all-small history as the image of
\[
 \mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset}e^{-\beta A}
       \frac{\det(D+m_0)}{\det\mathbb D_k}\,dU.
\]
The exact determinant factorization and accretivity give
the lower measure bound with factor
$(1/\theta_k+1/\mathfrak m_k)^{-\nu n_k}$.
The remaining scalar activity in this term has modulus
at most $C_5^Fn_k$. At $k=K$,
\[
 1/\theta_K+1/\mathsf m\le1/(c_b\mathsf m)
                                            \le1/(c_bm_-).
\]
Integrating the measure bound and using the ball estimate
of \cref{C-416-6} therefore gives
\[
 t^F(h_\emptyset^{(K)})\ge
 \exp\left[E_K-\left(C_5^F+\nu\log\frac1{c_bm_-}
      +\tfrac92\log x_K+3\log7+24(B_3^{\rm cr})^2\right)\ell^3\right].
\]
The definition of $C_P^{(K)}$ bounds this below by
$e^{E_K-C_P^{(K)}(1+\log x_K)\ell^3}$.
All history terms are nonnegative before the comparison,
so $Z_K\ge t^F(h_\emptyset^{(k)})\ge
t^F(h_\emptyset^{(K)})$. The energy increments give
\[
 E_K\ge E_k-C'_e(1+\log x_k)n_k.
\]
Since $n_K\le n_k$ and $\log x_K\le\log x_k$, this proves
the lower partition bound at every $k$.

Finally
\[
 \frac1{\theta_k}\le\frac{x_k}{b_F(1-L^{-1})},\qquad
 \frac1{\mathfrak m_k}
   =\frac{\mathsf t_k}{\mathsf b\mathsf m}
   \le\frac{(1+\bar B)x_k}{4m_-}.
\]
Here $x_k>1$, $\mathsf t_k\le x_k+\bar B$, and
$\mathsf b\ge\gamma^{-2}\ge4$.
Taking the logarithm gives the last inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Source bounds after the change of constants]
\label{C-412-81}
The source construction, the intermediate-level generating
function bounds, their base-source estimates, and the
separated-cumulant estimates hold under \cref{C-412-78}.
Use the same source domains, the new $C_P$ in the lower
partition bound, and $C_m^w$ in the determinant estimate.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The source-chain steps use $\eta_k\ge c_b$,
$L^{k+1-K}\|J\|_\infty<r_M$, and the constants through
$h_F$. On the physical source ball the new choice
$2\varrho_J\le c_Jm_-$ still gives a real part at least
half the bare mass. At the terminal level their Berezin
integral is bounded by the Grassmann norm at $h_F$.
The enlarged-weight Gaussian lower expansion is not used.

The three omitted ceilings entered these source estimates
only through the hypotheses of the common partition bound.
Its upper bound is retained by \cref{C-416-6}; its lower
bound at every intermediate level is \cref{C-412-80}.
The exact history identities and the lower bound as
measures are unchanged. The further estimate of its
determinant factor uses the last inequality of
\cref{C-412-80}, with $C_m^w$. Thus the source-chain,
history and Cauchy arguments in \cite[\S10]{QCDM1} apply
with the stated constants.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Construction at every positive mass]
\label{C-412-82}
For the constants of \cref{C-412-78}, the construction of
the original scalar family holds on every compact interval
$0<m_-\le\mathsf m\le m_+\le1/2$ at the same upper
bound $\gamma$ for the coupling. This includes fixed-torus
and growing-torus subsequential limits, and the construction
which first takes the infinite-volume limit at fixed cutoff.
All symmetry, reflection-positivity, reconstruction and
leading short-distance conclusions for that family remain
valid. The forward mass estimate is
\[
 0\le s_K\le(2B_F+1/2)/\mathsf b,\qquad
 |s_K|\le\bar B_Mg^2,
\]
in addition to the one-loop approximation in
\cref{C-412-80}. The estimates need not be uniform as
$m_-\downarrow0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
We check the inputs of the construction rather than
requiring the mass-dependent smallness ceilings again.
At fixed cutoff the inverse and relative-determinant
arguments require only $m_0>0$; they therefore construct
the same torus-limit gauge states. Their constants may
depend on the chosen compact positive interval.
The local fermion and flow estimates are supplied by
\cref{C-416-6}; the common upper and lower partition
bounds and all source estimates by
\cref{C-412-80,C-412-81}.
The volume-independent cumulant bound has the same form,
with
\[
 B(R)=\max\left\{
  \frac{C_Be^{c_V}(1+R)^3}{\min\{\varrho,\varrho_J\}},
  C'_B(1+N_f/m_-)(1+R)^3\right\}.
\]
The second term is the direct estimate at the finitely
many coarse cutoffs; retaining its $m_-$ dependence is
essential.

Compactness, centered moments, the reflection inequalities,
shrinking-plate bounds and reconstruction then use the
same bounds as in \cite[\S\S12--13]{QCDM1}. The leading
two-point proof uses the same source energy and free
propagator, with constants $C_P$, $\varrho_J$, $m_-$ and
the corresponding image estimate. Those constants and
the resulting short-distance threshold are formed after
$g$; they impose no ceiling on its already chosen upper
bound. This verifies nonvanishing and identification of
the first label as well. The fixed-cutoff infinite-volume
construction and its subsequent continuum extraction use
the same local bounds, so the volume-first theorem follows
at each of the compact positive intervals.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Reaching arbitrary positive labels]
\label{C-412-83}
Fix the constants through $\gamma$ in \cref{C-412-78}.
Every pair $\mathsf b>0$, $\mathsf m>0$ is reached by
scaling from data covered by \cref{C-412-82}, with these
same constants. The chosen mass interval, source radius
and the subsequent estimate constants may depend on the pair.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Choose an integer $z$ so large that
$\mathsf b'=L^z\mathsf b>\gamma^{-2}+4B_\sharp$ and
$0<\mathsf m'=L^{-z}\mathsf m\le1/2$.
Set $g=(\mathsf b'-3B_\sharp)^{-1/2}<\gamma$.
Then $\mathsf b'\in I_g$. Now choose
$0<m_-<\mathsf m'$, $m_+=1/2$, and
$0<2\varrho_J\le c_Jm_-$. These are choices after
$\gamma$, so \cref{C-412-82} applies. The identity of
bare lattice integrals and the dilation of the test
functions are those proved in \cref{C-404-91}.
For fixed tori use the corresponding scaled admitted
sides; for infinite-volume limits choose a cofinal sequence
of such sides. Scaling preserves $\mathsf b\mathsf m$.
\end{proof}

As $m_-\downarrow0$ the denominator constants still grow.
For instance, with $\varrho_J=c_Jm_-/2$,
\[
 C_P=C_P^0+\nu\log(1/m_-),\qquad
 e^{c_V}=e^{C+2+C_P^0(1+\log X_g)}
                       m_-^{-\nu(1+\log X_g)}.
\]
Thus the construction for each positive mass does not give
uniform estimates at mass zero. The signed-mass continuation
uses the different source argument of \cref{C-404-81}.

\subsection{The mass at scale one}

\begin{lemma}[Strict positivity of the zero-mass coefficient]
\label{C-398-36}
For the chamber operator, $F_\infty>0$. More precisely,
$\sigma_{k-1}(k;0)$ has a positive limit $\bar s_1$ and
$F_\infty\ge\bar s_1$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
In the notation of \cref{C-398-40},
$\sigma_{k-1}(k;0)=F(k;0)-F_{<k-1}(k;0)$ tends to
$F^{[0]}-F^{[1]}$. We prove that its lower limit is
strictly positive. Work in level-$k$ units and a
nonzero Bloch fibre $\xi$.
The curvature covariance of the last slice is the
orthogonal projection onto $\mathsf{Fl}_k\ominus\mathsf{Fl}_{k-1}$.
The first square in the nonnegative mass form is
\[
 \theta_k^{-1}\langle|D_kXV_A\chi_c|^2\rangle_c,
                        \qquad X=RD[1]^{-1}.
\]
Gauge covariance gives
$XV_{d\lambda}\chi_c=i(Q'_k\lambda)c$.
Its component along $\gamma_1\gamma_2$ is therefore
gauge invariant. Denote this linear functional of
$F=dA$ by $\Lambda(F)$. Since
$\|D_k^{-1}\|\le\theta_k^{-1}+c_1/|\xi|$, the first
square bounds a positive constant times
\[
 \theta_k^{-1}(\theta_k^{-1}+c_1/|\xi|)^{-2}|\Lambda(F)|^2.
\]
For a Gaussian with projection covariance $P$ and
$F_0\in\operatorname{ran}P$,
$\mathbb E|\Lambda(F)|^2\ge|\Lambda(F_0)|^2/\|F_0\|^2$.
We construct such a test curvature.

Let $Z$ be divergence free at level $k-1$ and put
\[
 B=(dd^*+d^*d)^{-1}(Q^s_{k-1})^*Z.
\]
The commuting identity for $Q^s_{k-1}$ gives $d^*B=0$
and $d^*dB=(Q^s_{k-1})^*Z$. Thus $dB$ is orthogonal
to $\mathsf{Fl}_{k-1}$, and its energy is
$\langle Z,Q^s_{k-1}B\rangle$. It belongs to
$\mathsf{Fl}_k$ precisely when $Q^s_kB$ has zero curl.

Near $\xi_*=(\pi/2,0,0)$ take $Z$ on the two momenta
$\xi'_a=\xi$, $\xi'_b=\xi-2\pi e_1$, with amplitudes
$\varpi_a,\varpi_b\in\mathbb C^3$ in one colour.
There are four linear constraints: the two divergences
and two independent components of the coarse curl.
On their nullspace the energy is positive definite.
The coefficients of the constraints, the energy and
$\Lambda$ are sums of the straight-average, Laplacian,
block-average, vertex and propagator symbols. The
summable majorants in the proof of \cref{C-398-40}
hold uniformly on a ball about $\xi_*$. Termwise,
the averages tend to their sinc symbols, the light
propagator to $(i\gamma\cdot q)^{-1}$, the heavy
components to zero and the light vertex to
$i\gamma\cdot A$. Hence these finite matrices converge
uniformly there. Where the constraint has rank four,
the largest quotient $|\Lambda(dB)|^2/\|dB\|^2$
also converges continuously.

At $\xi_*$ choose $\varpi_\alpha=u_\alpha e_2$.
The divergences vanish. Only momenta
$q=(\xi'_\alpha+2\pi Ll,0,0)$ survive the transverse
Dirichlet factors. Put $x_\alpha=\xi'_\alpha/(2L)$.
In the limit the remaining curl condition and the
functional are
\[
 G_au_a+G_bu_b=0,\qquad \Lambda(dB)=H_au_a+H_bu_b,
\]
where
\[
 G_\alpha=4\sin(\xi'_\alpha/2)\sin x_\alpha
                    \sum_{l\in\mathbb Z}(\xi'_\alpha+2\pi Ll)^{-4},
 \quad
 H_\alpha=4\sin(\xi'_\alpha/2)\sin x_\alpha
                    \sum_{l\in\mathbb Z}(\xi'_\alpha+2\pi Ll)^{-5}.
\]
Differentiation of $\sum_l(x+\pi l)^{-2}=\csc^2x$ gives
\[
 \frac{H_\alpha}{G_\alpha}=\frac{h(x_\alpha)}{2L},
       \qquad h(x)=\cot x\frac{2+\cos^2x}{1+2\cos^2x}.
\]
Take $u_a=G_b$, $u_b=-G_a$. Then
\[
 \Lambda(dB)=\frac{G_aG_b}{2L}(h(\pi/(4L))-h(-3\pi/(4L)))\ne0,
\]
since $G_aG_b\ne0$ and $h$ is odd and positive on
$(0,\pi/2)$. The four constraints have rank four:
the divergences constrain the two first components,
and the other curl equation acts separately on the
third components. Thus the limiting quotient is
positive on a ball about $\xi_*$. Uniform convergence
makes the finite-$k$ quotient bounded below on a
smaller ball for all sufficiently large $k$.
Integration over this ball gives a positive lower
limit for the first square and hence for the slice.
All slices are nonnegative, so $F_\infty\ge\bar s_1>0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Prescribing the mass at scale one]
\label{C-412-84}
Use the constants of \cref{C-412-78} and write
$A=2B_F+1/2$. At every admitted datum,
\[
 m\le m+s_K\le m+A/b,\qquad
 |bs_K-F(K;m)|\le C_sb^{-1/2}(1+\log b)^{9p_0}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 b(m+s_K)\ge\max\{bm,
