\(\varpi(W)<2\varepsilon(L^s\mathsf b)
 \le\varepsilon_{\mathcal W}\alpha_0\le\bar\varepsilon\).
The background in \eqref{eq:qcdm2-restart-density} is therefore
defined.  Moreover
\(L^{t_0^\bullet}\mathsf c_w
   =\beta^\bullet-a_{K^\bullet}^{-1}w\), so its action has the
required physical source normalization.

The zero-source restart is also made on \(\mathbb Z^3\), using
these local formulas without the torus density test.  Its
activities determine its own extracted numbers
\((\hat x_i,\hat s_i,\hat e_i,\hat b_i,\hat\mu_i)\).
In particular
\(\hat x_{t_0^\bullet}=L^s\mathsf b\) and
\(\hat s_{t_0^\bullet}=F^{\mathrm{UV}}/(L^s\mathsf b)\).
At sources, the chain starts at
\(\hat\sigma_{t_0^\bullet}(s)
     =\hat\Sigma_w-F^{\mathrm{UV}}/(L^s\mathsf b)\)
and satisfies
\[
 \hat\sigma_{k+1}(s)(x)=L\hat\sigma_k(s)(x)
 +\hat\nu_{k+1}\bigl(w,-a_{K^\bullet}J,
               (\hat\sigma_i(s))_{t_0^\bullet\le i\le k}\bigr)
                         (y_{k+1}(x))-\hat\mu_{k+1}.
\]
The same construction is made on every allowed torus, with the
same infinite-lattice extraction.  Thus its extracted numbers
are independent of the side.

At level \(t_1^\bullet\), denote its exponent by
\(\hat\Phi_s^\bullet\), its total by \(\hat T^\bullet(z)\), and
its extracted energy by
\[
 \hat c^\bullet(s)=\sum_{t_0^\bullet<j\le t_1^\bullet}
       \left(\hat e_jn_j+\sum_{X\in\mathcal D_j}\hat e_j(X;s)\right).
\]
The contact term is \(\mathfrak c^\bullet(z)
       =c^\bullet(s(z))-\hat c^\bullet(s(z))\).

Let \(\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet\) be the product, read on
\(\mathcal Y\), of all tests and gauge-fixing factors along the
empty history from \(t_0^\bullet\) to \(t_1^\bullet\).
Let \(\mathbb M^\bullet(W;\hat\Sigma_w)\) be the matrix of
the quadratic form
\(L^{-t_0^\bullet}\mathsf S_1(\hat\Sigma_w\psi^{\mathrm{bg}})\), and put
\[
 \hat{\mathbb D}^\bullet(W;s)
 =\mathbb D^\bullet_{t_0^\bullet}
       (\mathsf U^\bullet_{t_0^\bullet}(W);
                      m_0^\bullet-a_{K^\bullet}\hat J)
                 +\mathbb M^\bullet(W;\hat\Sigma_w),
\]
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-cut-start}
 \hat F_z^\bullet(W)=\mathbf1_{\mathsf{Cut}^\bullet_{(t_0)}}(W)
 e^{-\mathsf{wab}^\bullet(\mathsf c_{w_z},W)}
                 \det\hat{\mathbb D}^\bullet(W;s(z)),\qquad
 T^{\mathrm{sf},\bullet}(z)=\int\mathsf k^\bullet\hat F_z^\bullet\,dW.
\end{equation}
An undefined tower in this formula is assigned value zero.
For \(s\ge s_F\), \cref{C-418-11} proves that it is defined
throughout the field cut and that \(\hat F_z^\bullet\) is bounded
and Borel.  The density-test set lies in this field cut, so the
Berezin integral of the starting density is
\(\chi^\bullet_{t_0}(T_\ell)\hat F_z^\bullet\,dW\).
The restarted flow requires \(u\ge u_*\); the field-cut comparison
also requires \(L^u\gamma^{-2}\ge\Theta_\star\).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}\label{C-418-4}
Fix one lattice and suppress \(\bullet\).  Let
\(t_0<t_b\le t_1\).  For \(j\le t_b\), set
\(\hat E^{(j)}=0\) when \(j\le t_0\), and let
\(\Delta^{(j)}\) be \(E^{(j)}-\hat E^{(j)}\) after subtracting
the value of its degree-zero part at the trivial pair.  Use the
same subtraction pointer by pointer.  Let \(d_b(s)\) be the sum
of those subtracted values with the opposite sign, and put
\[
 \hat w_b=L^{-(K-t_b)}(x_{t_b}-\hat x_{t_b}),\qquad
 \delta_{t_b}(s)=s_{t_b}+\sigma_{t_b}(s)
                         -\hat s_{t_b}-\hat\sigma_{t_b}(s).
\]
Then \(\hat w_b\) is real, and the two exponents obey
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-exponent-difference}
 \hat\Phi_s^{(t_b)}-\Phi_s^{(t_b)}
 =d_b(s)+a_K^{-1}A(\hat w_b,\mathsf U)
 +L^{-t_b}\mathsf S_1(\delta_{t_b}(s)\psi^{\mathrm{bg}})
                     -\sum_{j\le t_b}\sum_X\Delta^{(j)}(X;s).
\end{equation}
For \(\lambda\in\mathbb C\), define the Grassmann-valued measure
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-base-density}
 \rho^{(t_b)}_{s,\lambda}(dV)
 =e^{E_{t_b}(s)}\mathsf{Stay}(V)
 e^{\Phi_s^{(t_b)}+\lambda(\hat\Phi_s^{(t_b)}-\Phi_s^{(t_b)})}
                   \mathscr M^{\mathrm{fr}}_{h_\emptyset}(dV).
\end{equation}
At \(\lambda=0\) this is the original term.  At \(\lambda=1\)
it is the restarted term multiplied by
\(e^{E_{t_b}(s)-\hat c_b(s)}\).  Its earlier activities are
\(E^{(j)}-\lambda\Delta^{(j)}\), its source is
\((w+\lambda\hat w_b,J)\), and its mass term uses
\(s_{t_b}+\sigma_{t_b}(s)-\lambda\delta_{t_b}(s)\).

For \(k\ge t_b\), retain the histories
\[
 \mathcal H_k^{(t_b)}
       =\{h\in\mathcal H_k:h|_{t_b}=h_\emptyset^{(t_b)}\}.
\]
Their terms are the images of \eqref{eq:qcdm2-base-density} under
the subsequent weighted kernels and partial Berezin integrals,
with the original extracted numbers.  Thus the terms depend
only on this starting measure.  A density \(g_h[s,\lambda]\)
with respect to \(\mathscr M_h^{\mathrm{fr}}\), when it exists,
is understood coefficient by coefficient.  Any two such densities
agree almost everywhere; their integrals, integrated fibre norms
and total Berezin integrals agree.

The difference families are required to have the following form.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(F\arabic*)]
\item Each pointed term is even, local, jointly gauge invariant,
Borel, holomorphic on the fixed complex domains of regular pairs
and holomorphic in the source.  It is invariant under
\(\mathrm U(N_f)\times\mathrm U(N_f)\) acting jointly on the
fermions and \(J\), by conjugation on the latter.
\item Its scalar part vanishes at the trivial pair and satisfies
the pointed sum rule.
\item On an open source set containing \(\mathcal P\), it is a
free family in the sense of \cref{C-422-3}.  Its fermion terms
are obtained from
\(F_j(s)-\hat F_j(s),G_j-\hat G_j,\mu_j-\hat\mu_j\),
with the corresponding infinite-lattice families at zero source.
Here \(F_j,G_j\) are the terms before extraction, at the source
coordinates and at zero respectively.  The hatted data are zero
for \(j\le t_0\).  All these families are invariant under the
common scalar phase on fermions.  Let their sizes be
\(r_j^\psi(s)\) and \(r_j^0(s)\).
\end{enumerate}
For a pointed family define
\[
 \|G\|^{\mathrm{pt}}_j
 =\sup_\square\sum_{X\supset\square}e^{\kappa d_j(X)}
       \sum_{z\in X}\sup_{\mathsf U}
                  \|G(X;\mathsf U,\cdot;z)\|_{h^{(j)}},
 \qquad
 |G_0|_j=\sup_{X,z}e^{(\kappa+1)d_j(X)}
                  \sup|G_0(X;\cdot;z)|.
\]
The suprema are on the fixed domains of regular complex pairs;
in particular \(|\Delta_0^{(j)}|_j=r_j^0\).
The lag bounds with \(\Lambda>0\) at level \(t_b\) are
\begin{align}
 \sum_{j\le t_b}\omega_{k+1-j}r_j^\psi(s)
       &\le\Lambda^{-1}C_w^{\mathrm s}\phi_k,
       &&t_b\le k\le K,\label{eq:qcdm2-lag-L1}\\
 \sum_{j\le t_b}L^{-(k-j)}|\Delta_0^{(j)}(\cdot;s)|_j
       &\le\Lambda^{-1}E_0^{\mathrm s},
       &&t_b\le k\le K,\label{eq:qcdm2-lag-L2}\\
 \|\delta_{t_b}(s)\|&\le\Lambda^{-1}B_\sigma\phi_{t_b},
       &|\hat w_b|&\le\Lambda^{-1}\varrho.
       \label{eq:qcdm2-lag-L3}
\end{align}
Here \(\omega_j=C_\omega L^{j/4}\) and \(\phi_k=\phi(x_k)\).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}\label{C-418-5}
At zero source insert, in each restarted step
\(t_0\le k<t_1\), the factor
\[
 \mathsf m^\bullet_{k,\lambda}(V)
 =\prod_{b\in\mathfrak X^+_{(k)}}
                (1+\lambda\bar\chi^\bullet_{(k),b}(V)),
\]
where \(\bar\chi^\bullet_{(k),b}\) indicates that the fluctuation
is defined and has modulus at least \(\delta(x_{(k)})/2\).
No mark is inserted after level \(t_1^\bullet\).  Its total is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-marked-total}
 Z_\lambda^\bullet=\int_{\mathcal Y}
  \hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet(W)
  \prod_{t_0\le k<t_1}\mathsf m^\bullet_{k,\lambda}(W_k)
                       \hat F_0^\bullet(W)\,dW.
\end{equation}
This is a polynomial in \(\lambda\),
\(Z_0^\bullet=\hat T^\bullet(0)\), and
\[
 \partial_\lambda Z_\lambda^\bullet|_0
 =\sum_{t_0\le k<t_1}\sum_{b\in\mathfrak X^+_{(k)}}
  \int\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet(W)
       \bar\chi^\bullet_{(k),b}(W_k)\hat F_0^\bullet(W)\,dW.
\]
The integral identities, including the equality at zero, are
proved in \cref{C-418-19}.
\end{definition}

\subsection{Constants and the convergence theorem}

\begin{definition}\label{C-418-6}
Let \(c_\#\) be the largest \(c\in(0,1/8]\) for which
\[
 L^c\le11/10,\qquad
 \sum_{j\ge1}L^{-j(1/4-c)}(1+j)^{\mathfrak p_0}
                  \le\tfrac32 S_{1/4},\qquad
 S_{1/4}=\sum_{j\ge0}L^{-j/4}(1+j)^{\mathfrak p_0}.
\]
It is positive: at \(c=0\) the sum is \(S_{1/4}-1\), and it
is continuous and increasing for \(c<1/4\).  Put
\[
 c_n=\tfrac12c_\#\phi_2(n)=\frac{c_\#}{4(6n+11)},\qquad
 P_n=\frac2{\phi_1(n)}=\frac{40(6n+11)}{c_\#}.
\]
These depend only on \(L,\mathfrak p_0,n\).

The preceding construction constants determine the restart
threshold \(u_*\), the constants \(C_\Lambda,p_\Lambda\) in
the lag estimate, and \(C_D,K_F,s_F\) in the comparison of the
starting operators.  They also determine
\[
 C'_E=\frac{C_{\mathfrak E}C_{\mathrm{cnt}}}{M^3(L^3-1)},
 \quad 0<c_\lambda\le1/8,\quad
 \theta_{\mathrm{dis}}=\tfrac12(c_\star-c_\Theta)>0,
 \quad\theta_{\mathrm{tl}}=\tfrac12\theta_{\mathrm{dis}},
 \quad\kappa_{\mathrm t}=\frac{c_{\mathrm{cl}}}{128M^3}.
\]
For the chamber operator \(\nu=8N_f\) and
\(\nu_\natural=48\nu\).  The number of generators per bare
site uses \(\nu_\natural\); the block Dirac matrices use \(\nu\).
Set
\[
 \mathsf M_{g,\ell}
 =\exp\{[C+2+C_P(1+\log X_g)]\ell^3\}.
\]
The constants \(C,C_P\) are the upper and lower partition
bounds, with the source constants chosen as in \cref{C-418-2}.

At a cutoff \(K\), define the following errors:
\begin{align}
 R^F&=\mathsf M_{g,\ell}
  \exp[-\theta_{\mathrm{dis}}A_0^2
                (\log(\tfrac12L^u\gamma^{-2}))^{2\mathfrak p_0}],
 &\hat R^F&=2eR^F,\label{eq:qcdm2-cutoff-discard}\\
 \Lambda&=C_\Lambda^{-1}(K+1)^{-p_\Lambda}L^{c_\#(s-u)},
 &r_\lambda&=\tfrac12(3L^{1/2})^{-u}c_\lambda\Lambda,
       \label{eq:qcdm2-cutoff-lambda}\\
 \epsilon_{\mathrm{ro}}
 &=\frac{2(4\mathsf M_{g,\ell})^{n+1}+2C'_EN_{[u]}}{r_\lambda},
 \label{eq:qcdm2-cutoff-readout}\\
 \epsilon_{\mathrm{cl}}
 &=4\mathsf K_{\mathrm w}c_\rho^2A_0^2(1+2\varrho\gamma^2)
      \bar{\mathsf y}_{[K]}N_{[s]}K^{1/2}L^{-(K-s)/2}.
       \label{eq:qcdm2-cutoff-classical}
\end{align}
The last bound uses the gauge comparison constants
\(\mathsf K_{\mathrm w},c_\rho\).  For the fermion determinant put
\begin{align}
 \bar\varepsilon_{\mathrm r}&=2c_\rho\varepsilon(L^s\gamma^{-2}),
 &\varepsilon(x)^2&=A_0^2(\log x)^{2\mathfrak p_0}/x,
       \label{eq:qcdm2-cutoff-epsilon}\\
 \delta_F&=K_F\left[L^{-(K-s)}+
   \bar\varepsilon_{\mathrm r}\bigl(N_{[s]}L^{-(K-s)}\bigr)^{1/3}\right],
 &\epsilon_F&=\nu N_{[s]}\frac{8L^s}{\mathsf m_-}\delta_F.
       \label{eq:qcdm2-cutoff-fermion}
\end{align}
Finally define
\begin{align}
 \Lambda_{\mathrm{mk}}
 &=\exp[\kappa_{\mathrm t}A_1^2
                        (\log(L^u\gamma^{-2}))^{2\mathfrak p_0}],
 &\epsilon_{\mathrm{mk}}
 &=2e\mathsf M_{g,\ell}\Lambda_{\mathrm{mk}}^{-1/2},
       \label{eq:qcdm2-cutoff-mark}\\
 \epsilon_{\mathrm{sh}}
 &=2(\epsilon_{\mathrm{mk}}+3sN_{[s]}\hat R^F),
 &C_\psi&=\tfrac32c_\rho^2A_0^2\gamma^2\bar{\mathsf y}_{[s]}
                        +\frac{8\nu C_D}{\mathsf m_-}.
       \label{eq:qcdm2-cutoff-shift}
\end{align}
The last \(C_\psi\) is a bound at this cutoff, distinct from
the fixed activity constant with that name.

For a tuple, write \(\varrho_{\min}=\min\{\varrho,\varrho_J\}\) and
\[
 \hat r_i=\min\{R_i,(4nN_{[s]}C_\psi\|f_i\|_\sharp)^{-1}\},
 \qquad\hat{\mathbb D}=\{z:|z_i|\le\hat r_i\}.
\]
For \(\bullet=\mathrm A,\mathrm B\), set
\[
 s_i^\bullet=
 \begin{cases}
 6\ell^3L^{4K^\bullet}\|f_i\|_\infty,&\alpha_i=0,\\
 2\nu_\natural\ell^3L^{3K^\bullet}\|f_i\|_\infty/\mathsf m_-,
                         &\alpha_i\in\mathfrak B.
 \end{cases}
\]
When \(n\ge2\) and \(\mathsf d>0\), let
\[
 \epsilon_{\mathrm{mx}}=
 2^n C_{\mathscr C}\ell^3L^{3u}
 e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm E}\mathsf dL^u}\prod_i\varrho_i^{-1}.
\]

The proof uses the following conditions on \(K\):
\begin{enumerate}[label=(k\arabic*),start=0]
\item \(1\le u<s<K\).
\item \(L^u\gamma^{-2}\ge\Theta_\star\), \(u\ge u_*\),
\(s\ge s_F\), and \(e^{-c_{\mathrm t}L^u}\le L^{-c_\#(s-u)}\).
\item \(r_\lambda\ge16\mathsf M_{g,\ell}\).
\item \(\hat R^F\le1/40\),
\(\epsilon_{\mathrm{cl}}+\epsilon_F\le1/40\), and
\(\epsilon_{\mathrm{sh}}\le1/40\).
\item \(256\mathsf K_u c_\rho^2A_0^2N_{[s]}L^{-(K-s)}
                    \le\gamma_{\mathrm r}A_1^2\).
\item \(\kappa_{\mathrm E}\mathsf dL^u(L-1)\ge\log(2L^3)\).
\item \(K\ge\max\{K_{\mathrm{tt}}(n),K_{\mathrm{mk}}(g,\ell,n)\}\).
\end{enumerate}
Here \(K_{\mathrm{tt}}\) is the threshold for the top test,
and \(K_{\mathrm{mk}}=\max\{K_{\mathrm{rs}},K_\flat\}\) is
the threshold for the marked restart.  They are obtained in
\cref{C-418-14,C-418-15}; their conditions involve only the
already fixed constants and the displayed quantities at a cutoff.
Thus none of these definitions changes an earlier construction
constant.  Only (k5) depends on \(\mathsf d\).

Let \(K_n(g,\ell)\) be the least integer at least two such that
(k0)--(k4), (k6), and
\(\kappa_{\mathrm E}L^{\phi_1(n)K/2}(L-1)\ge\log(2L^3)\)
hold for every \(K\ge K_n(g,\ell)\).  Set
\[
 \sigma_K=\max\{6\ell^3L^{4(K+1)},
                  2\nu_\natural\ell^3L^{3(K+1)}/\mathsf m_-\},
 \quad
 \hat\varrho_K=\max\left\{
 \frac{2n}{(1-c_\lambda)\varrho_{\min}},4nN_{[s]}C_\psi\right\},
\]
and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-cutoff-total-error}
 \begin{split}
 \mathsf B_n(K)={}&20R^F(4n\sigma_K)^n
 +2\epsilon_{\mathrm{ro}}
       \left(\frac{2n}{(1-c_\lambda)\varrho_{\min}}\right)^n\\
 &+[8(\epsilon_{\mathrm{cl}}+\epsilon_F)
                     +12\epsilon_{\mathrm{sh}}+16\hat R^F]
                                      \hat\varrho_K^n\\
 &+2^{n+2}C_{\mathscr C}\ell^3L^{3u}
 e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm E}L^{\phi_1(n)K/2}}
                                (n/\varrho_{\min})^n,\\
 C_n(g,\ell)={}&\sup_{K\ge K_n(g,\ell)}L^{c_nK}\mathsf B_n(K).
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
The threshold exists and this supremum is finite by
\cref{C-418-23}.  Both are uniform in the labels in \(\mathsf W(g)\).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}\label{C-418-7}
Use the chamber model and constants of \cref{C-418-2}, and write
\(\partial_z^n=\partial_{z_1}\cdots\partial_{z_n}|_{z=0}\).
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item For any \(n\)-tuple and \(K\ge2\) satisfying
(k0)--(k4), (k6),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-adjacent-contact}
 \begin{split}
 &\left|S^T_{n;K+1}(X)-S^T_{n;K}(X)
              -\partial_z^n(\mathfrak c^{\mathrm B}
                                      -\mathfrak c^{\mathrm A})(0)\right|\\
 &\quad\le2\epsilon_{\mathrm{ro}}\prod_iR_i^{-1}
 +[8(\epsilon_{\mathrm{cl}}+\epsilon_F)
                      +12\epsilon_{\mathrm{sh}}+16\hat R^F]
                                      \prod_i\hat r_i^{-1}\\
 &\qquad\quad+10R^F
       \left[\prod_i(4ns_i^{\mathrm A})+\prod_i(4ns_i^{\mathrm B})\right].
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
The suppressed labels are \(\ell,L^K\mathsf b,L^{-K}\mathsf m\)
at cutoff \(K\), and the corresponding labels at cutoff \(K+1\).
\item If \(n\ge2\), the supports are pairwise disjoint, two
are at distance at least \(\mathsf d>0\), and (k5) holds, then
\( |\partial_z^n\mathfrak c^\bullet(0)|\le2\epsilon_{\mathrm{mx}}\).
\item Under the support assumptions in (ii), for
\[
 K\ge P_n\max\{0,\log_L(1/\mathsf d)\}+K_n(g,\ell),
\]
one has
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-adjacent-rate}
 |S^T_{n;K+1}(X)-S^T_{n;K}(X)|
 \le C_n(g,\ell)L^{-c_nK}\prod_i\|f_i\|_\sharp.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
The constants \(c_n,P_n\) depend only on \(L,\mathfrak p_0,n\);
\(K_n,C_n\) also depend on the construction constants, \(g,\ell\).
None depends on the label in \(\mathsf W(g)\), the tuple, or its
separation.  The theorem holds for every \(N_f\ge1\) and every
index in \(\mathcal I\).
\end{theorem}

The proof follows the gauge comparison of
\cite[Thm.~AR]{YMM1}.  First discard histories with a large-field
region before depth \(u\).  On each lattice replace the remaining
total \(T^\bullet\) by its restarted total
\(\hat T^\bullet\), keeping the extracted contact term.
The loss of memory between depths \(s\) and \(u\) controls this
replacement.  Finally compare the two starts on \(\mathcal Y\):
the gauge backgrounds and block Dirac operators are close, and
the failures of the two sets of tests have small total mass.
All logarithmic derivatives are taken after the fermions have
been integrated.  The proof and the summation of its errors appear
after these estimates have been established.

\begin{corollary}\label{C-418-8}
Under the hypotheses of \cref{C-418-7}, let \(n\ge2\) and let
the tuple have pairwise disjoint supports.  Choose
\(\mathsf d>0\) smaller than the distance between two of them.
For integers
\(K'\ge K\ge P_n\max\{0,\log_L(1/\mathsf d)\}+K_n(g,\ell)\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-full-cutoff-tail}
 |S^T_{n;K'}(X)-S^T_{n;K}(X)|
 \le\frac{C_n(g,\ell)}{1-L^{-c_n}}L^{-c_nK}
                                   \prod_i\|f_i\|_\sharp.
\end{equation}
Consequently the full sequence has a limit
\(S_n^{(\ell,\mathsf b,\mathsf m)}(X)\), uniformly for
\((\mathsf b,\mathsf m)\in\mathsf W(g)\), and the limit is
continuous in these labels.  If the labels converge while
\(K\to\infty\), the same sequence converges to the limit at
the limiting label.  On the smooth disjoint-support test space,
this is the unique fixed-torus continuum family at that label
from \cite{QCDM1}; it inherits all the properties proved there.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Sum \eqref{eq:qcdm2-adjacent-rate} over the intervening cutoffs.
The geometric series gives \eqref{eq:qcdm2-full-cutoff-tail},
including its uniformity in the labels.  At a finite cutoff the
normalized integrals are continuous in the positive labels, so
their uniform limit is continuous.  Uniform convergence followed
by continuity proves the assertion for varying labels.  The
subsequential construction of \cite{QCDM1} must agree with this
limit on every test tuple, which proves the last assertion.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Estimates used in the cutoff comparison}

The following estimates separate the comparison into its three tasks:
compare the two starting quadratic forms, control the histories removed
at either end, and propagate the difference between the two flows.
Throughout, the datum, depths, errors and conditions (k0)--(k2) are
those of \cref{C-418-2,C-418-6}. The constants are uniform in the
label \((\mathsf b,\mathsf m)\in\mathsf W(g)\).

\begin{proposition}[The two starting operators]\label{C-418-11}
There are \(C_D,K_F\ge1\) and an integer \(s_F\ge1\), determined
after \(\gamma\) by the construction constants, with
\(L^{s_F}\gamma^{-2}\ge\Theta_\star\), for which the following holds.
Assume (k0) and \(s\ge s_F\). Let \(w\) and \(J\) be Lipschitz on
\(T_\ell\), with \(J\) taking values in the complex span of
\(\mathfrak B\), and
\[
 \|w\|_\sharp<\varrho,\qquad
 \|J\|_\sharp:=\max\{\|J\|_\infty,40M\operatorname{Lip}J\}
                                      <\varrho_J.
\]
The sources are sampled as in \cref{C-418-2}. The operators
\(\hat{\mathbb D}^{\bullet}(W;w,J)\) of \cref{C-418-3} act on
\(\ell^2(\Lambda_{s,\ell})\otimes\mathsf F\), with the inner
product in depth-\(s\) units.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item On \(\mathsf{Cut}^{\bullet}_{(t_0)}\), the operator is
independent of the representative of the minimal orbit, bounded
and Borel in \(W\), and holomorphic in the sources. Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{Re}\hat{\mathbb D}^{\bullet}(W;w,J)
                               \ge\tfrac18L^{-s}\mathsf m.
\]
\item For two sources in the stated domain,
\[
 \|\hat{\mathbb D}^{\bullet}(W;w,J)
       -\hat{\mathbb D}^{\bullet}(W;w',J')\|
 \le C_DL^{-s}\bigl(\|J-J'\|_\infty+\|w-w'\|_\infty\bigr).
\]
\item On the intersection of the two field cuts,
\[
 \|\hat{\mathbb D}^{\mathrm B}(W;w,J)
       -\hat{\mathbb D}^{\mathrm A}(W;w,J)\|
 \le K_F\left[L^{-(K-s)}
   +\bar\varepsilon_{\rm r}
       \min\{(N_{[s]}L^{-(K-s)})^{1/2},1\}\right]
 \le\delta_F.
\]
\item If \(w\) is real and
\(\gamma_4J(x)^\dagger\gamma_4=J(x)\) for every \(x\), then
\(\det\hat{\mathbb D}^{\bullet}(W;w,J)>0\).
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
\Cref{C-420-13} gives the constants and all four assertions.
Its lower bound is \(2L^{-s}\mathsf m/9\), hence implies the
one stated here. The last bound in (c) uses
\(\min\{x^{1/2},1\}\le x^{1/3}\) for \(x\ge0\).
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Discarding large-field histories]\label{C-418-12}
Assume (k0). For either lattice, its original partition
function \(Z^\bullet\) and the total \(T^\bullet\) of
\cref{C-418-3} satisfy
\[
 0\le Z^\bullet-T^\bullet(0)\le R^F Z^\bullet.
\]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Apply \cref{C-421-5} at \(t=t_1^\bullet\).
The calibration is \(L^u\mathsf b\ge L^u\gamma^{-2}\);
\(\mathsf Q_\ell\le\mathsf M_{g,\ell}\) gives precisely
the error \(R^F\). This application is recorded in
\cref{C-421-15}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Comparing the totals at depth \(u\)]\label{C-418-13}
Assume (k0)--(k2), and let \(X\) be any \(n\)-tuple.
The functions \(T^\bullet,\hat T^\bullet,\mathfrak c^\bullet\)
are holomorphic on \(\mathbb Q\), and
\(T^\bullet(0),\hat T^\bullet(0)>0\). Their logarithms near zero
satisfy
\[
 \left|\partial_{z_1}\cdots\partial_{z_n}
  [\log T^\bullet-\log\hat T^\bullet-\mathfrak c^\bullet](0)\right|
 \le\epsilon_{\rm ro}\prod_{i=1}^nR_i^{-1}.
\]
Here \(C'_E\) in \(\epsilon_{\rm ro}\) is determined after
\(\gamma\) by the construction constants.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The holomorphic interpolation and Cauchy estimate are
\cref{C-421-14,C-421-15}; the positive lower bound for the
restarted total is \cref{C-427-9}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Removing the top test]\label{C-418-14}
There is \(K_{\rm tt}(n)\), determined after \(\gamma\) by the
construction constants and \(n\), such that (k0)--(k2) and
\(K\ge K_{\rm tt}(n)\) imply, for either lattice,
\[
 \int_{\mathcal Y}|\mathsf k^\bullet-\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet|
                 \hat F^\bullet_0\,dW
 \le R^F\hat T^\bullet(0)\le\hat R^F\hat T^\bullet(0).
\]
The weights and starting density are those of \cref{C-418-3}
and the comparison of tests.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
This is \cref{C-425-9}. Its depth condition follows from
the definition of \(K_{\rm tt}(n)\); (k1) supplies
\(s\ge s_F\), \(u\ge u_*\), and
\(L^u\gamma^{-2}\ge\Theta_\star\).
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The marked restart]\label{C-418-15}
There is \(K_{\rm mk}(g,\ell,n)\), determined after \(\gamma\)
by the construction constants, \(g,\ell,n\), with the following
property. Assume (k0)--(k2) and \(K\ge K_{\rm mk}(g,\ell,n)\).
The marked restart of \cref{C-418-5} is defined for
\(|\lambda|<2\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{1/2}\) through \(t_1^\bullet\).
At \(t_0^\bullet<k\le t_1^\bullet\), its empty-history term has
the exact measure form of \cref{C-426-6}, with no activity at
a level at most \(t_0^\bullet\), and with
\[
 |\hat x_i(\lambda)-\mathsf t_i|\le\bar B,\qquad
 |\hat s_i(\lambda)|\le\bar B_M/\mathsf t_i,
\]
\[
 \|\hat F_0^{(j)}(\lambda)\|_j
      \le C_w\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1}),\qquad
 \|\hat E_{\ge2}^{(j)}(\lambda)\|_j
      \le C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2 .
\]
These bounds hold for the activities and their pointed terms.
The locality, symmetry, holomorphy, scalar-array and later-level
reading properties are those specified in \cref{C-426-6};
the normalizers use the actual pair
\((\mathsf t_{j-1},\hat x_{j-1}(\lambda))\).
The numbers and families are holomorphic in this disc, real
at real \(\lambda\) with the corresponding conjugation identity
for the families, and equal to the unmarked restart at zero.
Moreover,
\[
 Z^\bullet_{\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{1/2}}
             \le2e\,\mathsf M_{g,\ell}\hat T^\bullet(0).
\]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The construction and its domain are \cref{C-426-9}.
The total is bounded in \cref{C-430-8} by the slightly stronger
quantity \(e\,\mathsf M_{g,\ell}\hat T^\bullet(0)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Source energies and contact terms]\label{C-418-16}
Assume (k0) and \(u\ge u_*\). For
\(t_0^\bullet<j\le t_1^\bullet\) and \(X\in\mathcal D_j\),
the restarted source energy \(\hat e_j(X;\cdot)\) is
holomorphic on \(\mathscr O_{j-1}\), vanishes at zero, and obeys
\[
 |\hat e_j(X;s)|\le C_{\mathfrak E}e^{-\kappa d_j(X)},
\]
\[
 |\hat e_j(X;s)-\hat e_j(X;s')|
 \le C_{\mathfrak E}e^{-\kappa d_j(X)}
  \exp\left[-\frac{\kappa_\sigma
        \operatorname{dist}(X,\operatorname{supp}(s-s'))}{L^j}\right]
 \quad(s,s'\in\mathscr O_{j-1}).
\]
These are the constants of the original source induction.
Let \(n\ge2\), let \(\mathbf s_1,\ldots,\mathbf s_n\) have
pairwise disjoint supports, and suppose the first two supports
have physical distance at least \(\mathsf d>0\). If
\(s(z)=\sum_i z_i\mathbf s_i\in\mathcal P\) for
\(|z_i|\le\varrho_i\), then
\[
 \left|\partial_{z_1}\cdots\partial_{z_n}
                      \hat c^\bullet(s(z))\big|_{z=0}\right|
 \le2^{n-1}\prod_i\varrho_i^{-1}
  (\mathscr C_{t_1^\bullet}-\mathscr C_{t_0^\bullet})
                   (\operatorname{supp}\mathbf s_1;\mathsf d).
\]
The right side is at most the same expression with
\(\mathscr C_{t_1^\bullet}\) in place of the difference, where
\[
 \mathscr C_k(S;\mathsf d)
 =C_{\mathscr C}\sum_{j\le k}
       \#_j^+(S)e^{-\kappa_{\rm E}\mathsf d/\lambda_j}.
\]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Use \cref{C-429-4}(c) for the energies and
\cref{C-429-6} for their mixed derivatives.
The required floor on \(C_{\mathscr C}\) is part of
\cref{C-418-2}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Source histories above a base]\label{C-418-17}
Choose \(0<c_\lambda\le1/8\) as in \cref{C-422-16}, after
\(\gamma\) and from the construction constants, so that
\[
 c_\lambda E_0^{\rm s}\le c_0^\Delta,\qquad
 2\sqrt Lc_\lambda C_w^{\rm s}\le c_\psi^\Delta,
 \qquad c_0^\Delta\le M^{-3}\mathsf B .
\]
Assume (k0), \(u\ge u_*\), and the setting of \cref{C-418-4}
on either lattice. Suppress \(\bullet\) in the level indices.
Let \(t_0<t_b\le t_1\), \(\Lambda_b\ge1\), and suppose
the differences have the format (F1)--(F3) of that definition,
\(d_b(s)=d_b\) is constant on \(\mathcal P\), and
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-lag-L1}--\eqref{eq:qcdm2-lag-L3} hold there
with \(\Lambda=\Lambda_b\). Set
\[
 \rho_b=\tfrac12(3\sqrt L)^{-(K^\bullet-t_b)}
                       c_\lambda\Lambda_b,\qquad
 \mathcal D_b=\{(s,\lambda):s=(w,J)\in\mathcal P,\
       \|w\|_\sharp\le(2-c_\lambda)\varrho,\ |\lambda|\le\rho_b\}.
\]
Then \((w+\lambda\hat w_b,J)\in\mathcal P\) throughout
\(\mathcal D_b\). For the histories and measures of
\cref{C-418-4}, the following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(B\arabic*)]
\item The total Berezin mass is preserved:
\[
 \operatorname{Ber}\rho^{(t_b)}_{s,\lambda}(\mathcal V_{t_b})
 =\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_{K^\bullet}^{(t_b)}}
             \operatorname{Ber}\int g_h[s,\lambda]\,
                                      d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}.
\]
The densities may be chosen as the representatives in
\cref{C-422-14}; coefficient by coefficient they are pointwise
holomorphic on the interior of \(\mathcal D_b\).
They represent the given measures, so their values on the
exceptional null set do not change this identity.
\item At each \(t_b\le k\le K^\bullet\), every history has the
source history identity of \cite[Def.\ 10.11]{QCDM1}, with
the following changes. There are no pieces, generated
boundary terms or edge terms at levels at most \(t_b\), and
no stored layers below \(t_b\). The action weight is
\(\beta_k-a_{K^\bullet}^{-1}(w+\lambda\hat w_b)\).
The mass chain begins at
\(\sigma_{t_b}(s)-\lambda\delta_{t_b}(s)\) and obeys
\(\|\sigma_n^h(s,\lambda)\|\le2B_\sigma\phi_n\).
The early activities are \(E^{(j)}(s)-\lambda\Delta^{(j)}(s)\);
the later ones are the actual step outputs. Their frame sizes
and insertion sizes obey
\[
 \mathsf{sz}^{\natural}_j
       \le\tfrac{64}{51}b^{\rm tot,s}(\gamma),\qquad
 \bar v_j^{\rm s}\le b^{\rm blk,s}(\gamma).
\]
The scalar and fermion layer estimates retain their source
constants. The vacuum term has the form
\[
 -\mathcal E^F_{k,\mathcal S}
  =E_k(s,\lambda)-\sum_{t_b<n\le k}f_n(\mathcal S)
                    +\sum_{t_b<n\le k}g_n(\mathcal S;s,\lambda),
\]
where the \(g_n\) are holomorphic in the interior and
\(|g_n|\le C'_{\mathfrak E}\#_n(\tilde Z_n)\).
The regular-sum estimate retains the source constant \(C_E^F\).
\item The sum of the integrated fibre norms satisfies
\[
 \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_{K^\bullet}^{(t_b)}}
       \int\|g_h[s,\lambda]\|_{h_F}\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}
 \le e^{\operatorname{Re}E_{K^\bullet}(s,\lambda)+(C+2)\ell^3}.
\]
\item For \(t_b\le k\le K^\bullet\),
\[
 E_k(s,\lambda)=E_{t_b}(s)+\lambda d_b
   +\sum_{t_b<j\le k}\left(e_jn_j+
                       \sum_{X\in\mathcal D_j}e_j(X;s,\lambda)\right).
\]
The energies \(e_j(X;\cdot,\cdot)\) are holomorphic in the
interior of \(\mathcal D_b\), equal to \(e_j(X;s)\) at
\(\lambda=0\), and bounded by
\(C_{\mathfrak E}e^{-\kappa d_j(X)}\).
\item For \(t_b<t\le K^\bullet\),
\[
 \sum_{\substack{h\in\mathcal H_{K^\bullet}^{(t_b)}\\
                                      Z_t(h)\ne\varnothing}}
       \int\|g_h[s,\lambda]\|_{h_F}\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}
 \le e^{-\theta_{\rm tl}p_0(g_t)^2}
        e^{\operatorname{Re}E_{K^\bullet}(s,\lambda)+(C+2)\ell^3},
 \qquad \theta_{\rm tl}=\tfrac14(c_\star-c_\Theta).
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Since \(\hat w_b\) is constant, the last lag bound gives
\[
 |\lambda|\,|\hat w_b|
 \le\tfrac12c_\lambda\varrho,\qquad
 \|w+\lambda\hat w_b\|_\sharp<2\varrho.
\]
The statements are \cref{C-422-17}, applying
\cref{C-422-14} to the free differences
\((-\Delta^{(j)},-\delta_{t_b},\hat w_b,d_b)\).
In particular \cref{C-422-11} proves that the early scalar
and fermion excesses fit within the original source bounds.
The measure identity uses the Borel representatives constructed
in \cref{C-424-17,C-424-18,C-424-19}; it requires weighted
almost-everywhere invariance, as proved there.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Histories with a prescribed past]\label{C-418-18}
Assume the constants and geometric hypotheses of
\cref{C-423-1}, including \((\Gamma^{\rm F})\) in
\cref{C-423-8}. Let \(1\le t_b<K\), and let a flow satisfying
all the hypotheses of \cref{C-423-9} be given, with its base
\(t_1\) there replaced by \(t_b\). Thus the pointed families
on the torus and on \(\mathbb Z^3\) have the invariance,
holomorphy, zero cell moment and scalar normalization of
(G1); above \(t_b\) they are the actual step outputs with
the coefficient, mass, scalar and pointed bounds of (G2).
Before \(t_b\) they split as \(R+D\) as in (G3), with
\[
 \Lambda_k^\psi(D)=\sum_{j\le t_b}L^{(k+1-j)/4}
                             \epsilon_j^\psi(D)
          \le\lambda_0C_2\phi(\mathsf t_k)^2,\qquad
 \Lambda_k^0(D)=\sum_{j\le t_b}L^{-(k-j)}\mathsf g_j(D)
          \le\lambda'_0(1+E_0)
\]
for every \(t_b\le k\le K\).
The constants \(\lambda_0,\lambda'_0\in(0,1]\) are chosen
before \(h_F\), and \(C_\Sigma,C'_\Sigma\) after \(\gamma\),
as in \cref{C-423-8}.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item With all later families, coefficients and boundary terms
fixed, each frame member is affine in \(D\). Its linear part
and the differences of the step outputs from those with \(D\)
removed are bounded in the respective step norms by
\[
 \mathfrak d_k(D)=C_\Sigma\Lambda_k^\psi(D)
                              +C'_\Sigma\Lambda_k^0(D).
\]
The outputs, pointed activities and extracted numbers are
holomorphic in the input members.
\item Every \(h\in\mathcal H_k^{[t_b]}\), \(t_b\le k\le K\),
has the history identity and bounds of \cref{C-423-14},
with
\[
 \beta_h=L^{t_b}x_{t_b}
           -\sum_{t_b<j\le k}L^jb_j\varphi_j,\qquad
 E_k=E_{t_b}+\sum_{t_b<j\le k}e_jn_j,\qquad f_n=0\ (n\le t_b).
\]
In particular there is no generated boundary or edge term
at a level at most \(t_b\);
\(\mathsf{sz}_k^\natural\le\varepsilon_\flat\);
and the boundary terms agree for equal excerpts under the
torus condition of \cref{C-423-16}.
The scalar, fermion and integrated bounds of \cref{C-423-13}
hold with
\[
 E_0\longmapsto E_0+\mathfrak d^0,\qquad
 C_{\rm leg}\longmapsto
             C_{\rm leg}+C_{\rm leg}^{\square}\mathfrak d^\psi,
 \qquad
 \mathfrak d^a=\max_{t_b\le k\le K}\Lambda_k^a(D).
\]
Here \(\mathfrak d^0\le\lambda'_0(1+E_0)\) and
\(\mathfrak d^\psi\le\lambda_0C_2\).
The edge mass bound uses \(4\bar B_M/\mathsf t_j\).
The integrated estimate uses \(\operatorname{Re}E_k\);
its action profile can be \(\beta_h\), or the constant
\(L^{t_b}x_{t_b}\), with the action correction of
\cref{C-423-13}. No positivity is asserted for this complex flow.
\item If the flow depends holomorphically on a parameter on a
domain where (G1)--(G3) hold, the frame members, step outputs,
extracted numbers and bounded Borel coefficient functions
are holomorphic there. The real \(x_i\), hence also
\(b_i=L^{-1}x_{i-1}-x_i\), are constant on each connected component.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The hypotheses have been stated in the precise form used by
the induction. The sizes in \cref{C-423-2} take the maximum
over the two lattices and place the supremum over regular
pairs inside the pointer sum. Thus the two displayed sums
are exactly the scalar and fermion lag sums for \(D\).
Joint gauge invariance and translation covariance imply
that the quadratic moment commutes with colour and is
periodic; its zero cell sum is the explicit cancellation
hypothesis in (G1). No additional cancellation is inferred
from a norm bound.

The three conclusions are \cref{C-423-12},
\cref{C-423-13,C-423-14}, and the parameter assertion of
\cref{C-423-14}, respectively.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The restarted total at zero source]\label{C-418-24}
Assume (k0), \(u\ge u_*\), \(s\ge s_F\), and
\(L^u\gamma^{-2}\ge\Theta_\star\). For either lattice,
suppress \(\bullet\) in the level indices.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item The zero-source restart of \cref{C-418-3}, with starting
mass \(F^{\rm UV}/(L^s\mathsf b)\), continues through \(K^\bullet\)
on the torus and on \(\mathbb Z^3\). It extracts its own real
numbers from the infinite-lattice activities, with
\[
 \hat x_j=L^{-1}\hat x_{j-1}-\hat b_j,\qquad
 \hat s_j=L\hat s_{j-1}+\hat\mu_j,\qquad
 \hat E_k=\sum_{t_0<j\le k}\hat e_jn_j.
\]
The exact measure form, coefficient and mass windows, locality,
symmetries and scalar bounds are those of \cref{C-427-4}.
There are no activities at levels at most \(t_0\), and
\[
 \|\hat F_0^{(j)}\|_j\le C_w\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1}),\qquad
 \|\hat E_{\ge2}^{(j)}\|_j\le C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2 .
\]
These bounds also hold pointer by pointer. At the trivial
configuration on \(\mathbb Z^3\), the explicit part is
\(T^{(j)}(\hat y)\), with \(\hat y_i=0\) for \(i<t_0\)
and \(\hat y_i=1/\hat x_i\) for \(i\ge t_0\); its remainder
is bounded by \(C_3\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^3\).
Through \(t_1\) this continuation is the restart already defined.
\item Start each history \(h\in\mathcal H_k^{(t_0)}\)
from \(\hat d_{t_0}^\bullet(0)\), multiplied by the density
test \(\chi_{t_0}^\bullet(T_\ell)\), and apply its later
weights and partial fermion kernels. If \(\hat g_h\) is
its density, then for \(t_0<t\le K^\bullet\),
\[
 \sum_{\substack{h\in\mathcal H_{K^\bullet}^{(t_0)}\\
                                     Z_t(h)\ne\varnothing}}
       \int\|\hat g_h\|_{h_F}\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}
 \le e^{-\theta_{\rm dis}p_0(g_t)^2}
                         e^{\hat E_{K^\bullet}+(C+2)\ell^3}.
\]
\item The starting density \(\hat F_0^\bullet\) is nonnegative,
and
\[
 \hat T^\bullet(0)\ge
          e^{\hat E_{K^\bullet}-C_P(1+\log X_g)\ell^3}.
\]
For \(t_1\le k\le K^\bullet\), each history above \(t_1\)
has total Berezin mass equal to the integral of
\(\hat F_0^\bullet\) against a nonnegative Borel weight
on \(\mathcal Y\) containing \(\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet\).
Here
\[
 \hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet\chi_{t_0}^\bullet(T_\ell)
 =\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet
 =\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet
                  \mathbf1_{\mathsf{Cut}_{(t_0)}^\bullet}.
\]
These masses sum to \(\hat T^\bullet(0)\) at every such
level. In particular this total is at least the mass of
the final empty history.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, for \(t_0<t\le t_1\), the histories above the
start in which a large-field region has occurred by level
\(t\) have combined mass at most
\[
 e^{-\theta_{\rm dis}p_0(g_t)^2}
                    \mathsf M_{g,\ell}\hat T^\bullet(0).
\]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The continuation is \cref{C-427-4}; its history estimate
is \cref{C-427-6}. Positivity and consistency of the
Berezin masses are proved in \cref{C-427-7,C-427-8},
and their lower bound in \cref{C-427-9}.
The support identities follow from \cref{C-427-3}.
To obtain the last estimate, extend the histories to
\(K^\bullet\). Consistency preserves their masses, and
nesting of the large-field regions identifies their
extensions with the histories \(Z_t(h)\ne\varnothing\).
Use (b), followed by (c), and
\(\log\mathsf M_{g,\ell}=(C+2+C_P(1+\log X_g))\ell^3\).
\end{proof}

\subsection{Comparing the totals}

\begin{lemma}\label{C-418-19}
Under (k0), put
\[
 \rho_z^\bullet(U)=e^{-A(\beta^\bullet-a_{K^\bullet}^{-1}w_z,U)}
               \det(D[U]+m_0^\bullet-a_{K^\bullet}\hat J_z).
\]
Then
\[
 T^\bullet(z)=\int\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset}\rho_z^\bullet\,dU,
 \qquad
 Z^\bullet[s(z)]-T^\bullet(z)
       =\int\Bigl(\sum_{h\ne h_\emptyset}\mathfrak w_h\Bigr)
                                            \rho_z^\bullet\,dU.
\]
The weights are nonnegative bounded Borel functions, independent
of the source.  If \(u\ge u_*\) and
\(L^u\gamma^{-2}\ge\Theta_\star\), then
\[
 \hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet\chi^\bullet_{t_0}(T_\ell)
 =\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet
 =\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet\mathbf1_{\mathsf{Cut}^\bullet_{(t_0)}},
 \qquad
 \hat T^\bullet(z)=\int\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet\hat F_z^\bullet\,dW
\]
for \(s(z)\in\mathscr O_{t_1^\bullet}\).  The integrand is
bounded and Borel.  If also \(s\ge s_F\), then
\(\hat F_0^\bullet\ge0\), and the marked total in
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-marked-total} is the total of the marked flow
wherever that flow is defined.  Its polynomial coefficients are
nonnegative, its value at zero is \(\hat T^\bullet(0)\), and its
linear coefficient is the sum in \cref{C-418-5}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The exact history identity of \cite{QCDM1} gives the first two
formulas.  Sources change the density, leaving the tests and
gauge-fixing factors unchanged.

In one step along the empty history, the measure is multiplied
by the tests, the gauge-fixing factor and the fermion kernel,
partially Berezin-integrated, then pushed forward by \(\mathcal M\).
The fermion kernel has total Berezin integral one, and pushforward
preserves total mass.  Repeating these identities leaves precisely
the product \(\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet\) against the Berezin
integral of the starting density.  The first fluctuation test and
the density test at the next level imply the density test at the
starting level, by the test-descent estimate used in the original
step.  Thus \(\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet\) vanishes unless that
starting test passes.  Its support lies in the field cut, as
observed after \eqref{eq:qcdm2-cut-start}.  This proves the
second pair of formulas.

Each test is Borel, each gauge-fixing factor is bounded and Borel,
and the iterated averaging maps are Borel.  The finite product
\(\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet\) has these properties.  The starting
Grassmann density is bounded and Borel by \cref{C-419-11}; its
Berezin integral has the same properties.  This proves the
assertion about the integrand without requiring continuity of
the averaging map.

The argument also applies with the mark factors inserted.
At zero source the starting Dirac determinant is positive by
\cref{C-418-11}; the action is real and nonnegative on the field
cut.  Thus \(\hat F_0^\bullet\ge0\).  Each coefficient of
\(\prod_{k,b}(1+\lambda\bar\chi^\bullet_{(k),b})\) is an
elementary symmetric function of finitely many values in
\(\{0,1\}\).  Integrating it against
\(\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet\hat F_0^\bullet\,dW\) gives a finite
nonnegative coefficient.  The constant and linear coefficients
are the stated ones.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{C-418-20}
Assume (k0) and \(R^F\le1/10\).  On
\(\mathbb D^\bullet=\{z:|z_i|\le(4ns_i^\bullet)^{-1}\}\),
\[
 |\rho_z^\bullet(U)-\rho_0^\bullet(U)|
                    \le(e^{1/2}-1)\rho_0^\bullet(U).
\]
Both \(Z^\bullet[s(z)]\) and \(T^\bullet(z)\) are nonzero there,
and
\[
 |S^T_{n;K^\bullet}(X)-\partial_z^n\log T^\bullet(0)|
                  \le10R^F\prod_i(4ns_i^\bullet).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Suppress \(\bullet\).  Since \(0\le a_p\le2\) and there are
\(3\ell^3L^{3K}\) plaquettes,
\[
 |a_K^{-1}A(w_z,U)|\le6\ell^3L^{4K}\|w_z\|_\infty
                         \le\sum_{\alpha_i=0}|z_i|s_i.
\]
Accretivity gives \(\|(D[U]+m_0)^{-1}\|\le L^K/\mathsf m_-\).
For \(Y=a_K(D[U]+m_0)^{-1}\hat J_z\), the chosen polydisc
gives \(\|Y\|\le1/2\).  The logarithmic series therefore gives
\[
 |\operatorname{tr}\log(1-Y)|
 \le2\nu_\natural\ell^3L^{3K}\|Y\|
                         \le\sum_{\alpha_i\in\mathfrak B}|z_i|s_i.
\]
Each sum is at most \(1/4\), so
\(\rho_z=\rho_0e^a\) with \(|a|\le1/2\).

The nonnegative weights of \cref{C-418-19} and the discarded
history bound \cref{C-418-12} imply
\[
 |Z[s(z)]-Z[0]|\le(e^{1/2}-1)Z[0],\qquad
 |Z[s(z)]-T(z)|\le e^{1/2}R^FZ[0].
\]
Hence \(|Z[s(z)]|\ge(2-e^{1/2})Z[0]\), and
\(q=(Z-T)/Z\) satisfies
\( |q|\le4.7R^F\le1/2\).
Thus \(T=Z(1-q)\ne0\).  The principal logarithm
\(-\log(1-q)\) is bounded by \(10R^F\).  Near zero it differs
from \(\log Z-\log T\) by a constant, and Cauchy's inequality
proves the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{C-418-21}
Assume (k0)--(k4), (k6).  The two restarted totals have no zero
on \(\hat{\mathbb D}\), and their ratio has a holomorphic logarithm
\(\mathsf L\), on a neighbourhood of that polydisc, with
\[
 \sup_{\hat{\mathbb D}}|\mathsf L|
 \le8(\epsilon_{\mathrm{cl}}+\epsilon_F)
                       +12\epsilon_{\mathrm{sh}}+16\hat R^F.
\]
In particular,
\[
 |\partial_z^n(\log\hat T^{\mathrm B}-\log\hat T^{\mathrm A})(0)|
 \le[8(\epsilon_{\mathrm{cl}}+\epsilon_F)
                +12\epsilon_{\mathrm{sh}}+16\hat R^F]
                                      \prod_i\hat r_i^{-1}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
On \(\hat{\mathbb D}\), both source norms are at most one half
of their admitted radii.  Thus \cref{C-418-11} applies along
every segment \(s(tz)\), \(0\le t\le1\).

\emph{Variation in the source.}
On \(\mathsf{Cut}^\bullet_{(t_0)}\), write
\(\hat F_z^\bullet=\hat F_0^\bullet e^{\psi_z^\bullet}\), where
\[
 \psi_z^\bullet(W)=\mathsf{wab}^\bullet(L^sw_z,W)
  +\int_0^1\operatorname{tr}\bigl[
  \hat{\mathbb D}^\bullet(W;s(tz))^{-1}
                  \partial_t\hat{\mathbb D}^\bullet(W;s(tz))\bigr]dt.
\]
The background-action bound is
\[
 |\mathsf{wab}^\bullet(L^sw_z,W)|
 \le\tfrac32c_\rho^2A_0^2\gamma^2\bar{\mathsf y}_{[s]}
                                    N_{[s]}\|w_z\|_\infty.
\]
The operator comparison gives
\[
 \|\hat{\mathbb D}^{-1}\|\le8L^s/\mathsf m_-,\qquad
 \|\partial_t\hat{\mathbb D}\|
       \le C_DL^{-s}(\|J_z\|_\infty+\|w_z\|_\infty).
\]
The matrix dimension is \(\nu N_{[s]}\).  Therefore
\( |\psi_z^\bullet|\le N_{[s]}C_\psi
       \sum_i|z_i|\|f_i\|_\infty\le1/4\).
Both \(\hat F_z^\bullet\) and \(\hat F_0^\bullet\) vanish
off the field cut.

\emph{Comparison on the common support.}
Where both \(\mathsf k^{\mathrm A}\) and \(\mathsf k^{\mathrm B}\)
are positive, they equal the common product of gauge-fixing
factors.  Also
\(\varpi(W)<\varepsilon_{\mathrm r}
 =2c_\rho\varepsilon(L^s\mathsf b)\).
The weighted gauge-action comparison
\cite[Prop.~113.9]{YMM1} applies to
\(\mathsf c_{w_z}=L^s(\mathsf b-w_z)\).  Its Lipschitz norm
is at most \(L^s(\mathsf b+2\varrho)\).  It gives
\[
 |\mathsf{wab}^{\mathrm A}(\mathsf c_{w_z},W)
      -\mathsf{wab}^{\mathrm B}(\mathsf c_{w_z},W)|
 \le\mathsf K_{\mathrm w}L^s(\mathsf b+2\varrho)
       \varepsilon_{\mathrm r}^2N_{[s]}K^{1/2}L^{-(K-s)/2}
 \le\epsilon_{\mathrm{cl}}.
\]
For the determinant use
\(\mathbb D_t=(1-t)\hat{\mathbb D}^{\mathrm A}
                         +t\hat{\mathbb D}^{\mathrm B}\).
By \cref{C-418-11}, its real part is at least
\(L^{-s}\mathsf m/8\), so its inverse has norm at most
\(8L^s/\mathsf m_-\).  Hence
\[
 \det\hat{\mathbb D}^{\mathrm B}
       =\det\hat{\mathbb D}^{\mathrm A}e^{\eta_z},\qquad
 \eta_z=\int_0^1\operatorname{tr}
                 [\mathbb D_t^{-1}(\mathbb D_1-\mathbb D_0)]dt,
 \qquad |\eta_z|\le\epsilon_F.
\]
Thus \(\hat F_z^{\mathrm B}=\hat F_z^{\mathrm A}e^{\xi_z}\)
on the common support, with
\( |\xi_z|\le\epsilon_{\mathrm{cl}}+\epsilon_F\).

\emph{The mass outside the common support.}
The test comparison \cref{C-421-7} gives, in either direction,
\[
 \mathbf1_{\{\mathsf k^\circ=0\}}\mathsf k^\bullet
 \le\sum_{k,b}\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet
                           \bar\chi^\bullet_{(k),b}(W_k)
       +\sum_{k,b}|\mathsf k^\bullet-\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet|.
\]
There are at most \(3sN_{[s]}\) terms.  Integrate against
\(\hat F_0^\bullet\ge0\).  The first sum is
\(\partial_\lambda Z_\lambda^\bullet|_0\).  Nonnegativity of
the polynomial coefficients implies
\[
 \partial_\lambda Z_\lambda^\bullet|_0
 \le\frac{Z_r^\bullet}{r}
 \le\epsilon_{\mathrm{mk}}\hat T^\bullet(0),
 \qquad r=\Lambda_{\mathrm{mk}}^{1/2},
\]
by \cref{C-418-15}.  The top-test estimate \cref{C-418-14}
bounds the second sum by
\(3sN_{[s]}\hat R^F\hat T^\bullet(0)\), and also gives
\(T^{\mathrm{sf},\bullet}(0)
       \ge(1-\hat R^F)\hat T^\bullet(0)\).
Using \(|\psi_z^\bullet|\le1/4\), we conclude that
\[
 \int\mathbf1_{\{\mathsf k^\circ=0\}}\mathsf k^\bullet
                        |\hat F_z^\bullet|\,dW
 \le\epsilon_{\mathrm{sh}}
                  \int\mathsf k^\bullet|\hat F_z^\bullet|\,dW.
\]
Here \(e^{1/2}/(1-\hat R^F)<2\), by (k3).

Lemma~\ref{IV-57-13} now applies, with
\(\epsilon=\epsilon_{\mathrm{cl}}+\epsilon_F\) and
\(\delta=\epsilon_{\mathrm{sh}}\): the weights and
integrands are bounded and Borel, the zero-source integral is
positive by \cref{C-418-13}, and both errors are at most \(1/40\).  It gives
\[
 \left|\frac{T^{\mathrm{sf},\mathrm B}(z)}
                  {T^{\mathrm{sf},\mathrm A}(z)}-1\right|
 \le\epsilon_3:=4(\epsilon_{\mathrm{cl}}+\epsilon_F)
                           +6\epsilon_{\mathrm{sh}}\le1/4,
\]
\[
 |T^{\mathrm{sf},\mathrm A}(z)|
 \ge e^{-1/4}\cos(1/4)T^{\mathrm{sf},\mathrm A}(0)
 \ge\tfrac34T^{\mathrm{sf},\mathrm A}(0).
\]

\emph{Restoring the original restart tests.}
The top-test bound also gives
\[
 |\hat T^\bullet(z)-T^{\mathrm{sf},\bullet}(z)|
             \le e^{1/4}\hat R^F\hat T^\bullet(0).
\]
Writing \(a=T^{\mathrm{sf},\mathrm A}(0)\), the preceding
bounds give \(T^{\mathrm{sf},\mathrm B}(0)\le(1+\epsilon_3)a\)
and \(|T^{\mathrm{sf},\mathrm B}(z)|\ge9a/16\).  Consequently
\[
 \left|\frac{\hat T^{\mathrm A}}{T^{\mathrm{sf},\mathrm A}}-1\right|
       \le2\hat R^F,
 \qquad
 \left|\frac{\hat T^{\mathrm B}}{T^{\mathrm{sf},\mathrm B}}-1\right|
       \le3\hat R^F.
\]
All three ratios lie within distance \(1/4\) of one.
Their principal logarithms therefore define
\[
 \mathsf L=\operatorname{Log}\frac{\hat T^{\mathrm B}}
                                      {T^{\mathrm{sf},\mathrm B}}
 +\operatorname{Log}\frac{T^{\mathrm{sf},\mathrm B}}
                                      {T^{\mathrm{sf},\mathrm A}}
 -\operatorname{Log}\frac{\hat T^{\mathrm A}}
                                      {T^{\mathrm{sf},\mathrm A}}.
\]
The inequality \(|\operatorname{Log}(1+x)|\le4|x|/3\)
gives the stated bound.

For completeness these integrals are holomorphic on
\(\mathbb Q\).  At each field the integrand is holomorphic,
and the source-variation bound above gives the common integrable
majorant
\[
 \mathsf k^\bullet\hat F_0^\bullet
          \exp\{N_{[s]}C_\psi\sum_i2R_i\|f_i\|_\infty\}.
\]
Integration preserves holomorphy.  Nonvanishing and the ratio
bounds on the compact polydisc extend to a neighbourhood of it.
Cauchy's inequality now proves the derivative estimate.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{C-418-22}
Assume (k0), (k1), (k5), \(n\ge2\), and pairwise disjoint
supports, two separated by at least \(\mathsf d>0\).  Then
\( |\partial_z^n\mathfrak c^\bullet(0)|\le2\epsilon_{\mathrm{mx}}\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Relabel the separated supports as the first two.  The original
and restarted source-energy bounds each give
\[
 2^{n-1}\prod_i\varrho_i^{-1}\,
 C_{\mathscr C}\sum_{m\ge u}\ell^3L^{3m}
                               e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm E}\mathsf dL^m}
\]
for the mixed derivative; the restarted bound is
\cref{C-418-16}.  By (k5), each summand is at most half the
preceding one.  Each derivative is therefore bounded by
\(\epsilon_{\mathrm{mx}}\).  Their difference is the derivative
of \(\mathfrak c^\bullet\).
\end{proof}

\subsection{Summing the errors}

\begin{lemma}\label{C-418-23}
The threshold \(K_n(g,\ell)\) and constant \(C_n(g,\ell)\) in
\cref{C-418-6} are finite.  If
\(K\ge P_n\max\{0,\log_L(1/\mathsf d)\}+K_n(g,\ell)\),
then all (k0)--(k6) hold and
\(\mathsf dL^u\ge L^{\phi_1(n)K/2}\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Abbreviate \(\phi_i(n)\) by \(\phi_i\).  We have
\[
 \phi_1K\le u\le\phi_1K+1,\quad
 \phi_2K\le s\le\phi_2K+1,\quad
 \phi_2\le1/34,\quad\phi_1=c_\#\phi_2/10,
 \quad c_n=c_\#\phi_2/2.
\]
Also \(3\le L^{1/2}\), \(\gamma^{-2}\ge2\), and
\(\mathfrak p_0\ge1\).  The factors
\(\bar{\mathsf y}_{[s]}\), \(\bar{\mathsf y}_{[K]}\) grow
at most as powers of \(K\).  From the definition of
\(\varepsilon\),
\[
 \bar\varepsilon_{\mathrm r}
       \le2c_\rho A_0\gamma L^{-s/2}
                          \bar{\mathsf y}_{[s]}^{1/2}.
\]
Both discarded-history and marked-history errors contain
\(\exp[-c(\phi_1K\log L)^{2\mathfrak p_0}]\), which decays
faster than every \(L^{-aK}\).

The depths imply (k0) for large \(K\), and (k1) follows from
\(u,s\to\infty\) and the faster decay of \(e^{-c_{\mathrm t}L^u}\).
For (k2),
\[
 r_\lambda\ge\tfrac12c_\lambda C_\Lambda^{-1}(K+1)^{-p_\Lambda}
                    L^{c_\#s-(1+c_\#)u}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Indeed its exponential rate is
\([1-(1+c_\#)/10]c_\#\phi_2>0\).
The remaining errors satisfy, up to fixed constants,
\[
 \epsilon_{\mathrm{cl}}
       \le K^{1/2}\bar{\mathsf y}_{[K]}L^{(7s-K)/2},
 \qquad
 \epsilon_F\le L^{5s-K}
             +\bar{\mathsf y}_{[s]}^{1/2}L^{(29s-2K)/6}.
\]
They tend to zero since \(7\phi_2<1\), \(5\phi_2<1\),
and \(29\phi_2<2\).  This proves (k3).  Condition (k4) uses
\(N_{[s]}L^{-(K-s)}=\ell^3L^{4s-K}\to0\).
The test and mark thresholds give (k6).  They were defined using
(k0), (k1) and the displayed marked radius, before (k6); thus
there is no circular dependence on \(K_n\).
Finally \(L^{\phi_1K/2}\to\infty\), proving the existence of
\(K_n\).

If \(\mathsf d\ge1\), the asserted separation bound is immediate.
If \(\mathsf d<1\), then \(\phi_1P_n=2\) gives
\(\phi_1K\ge2\log_L(1/\mathsf d)\), and hence
\(\mathsf dL^u\ge L^{\phi_1K/2}\).  The extra condition in
the definition of \(K_n\) now implies (k5).

It remains to bound \(L^{c_nK}\mathsf B_n(K)\).
The first term is bounded because its discarded-history factor
decays faster than the exponential Cauchy cost \(L^{4nK}\).
For the readout term,
\[
 \epsilon_{\mathrm{ro}}
       \le C(K+1)^{p_\Lambda}L^{(4+c_\#)u-c_\#s},
\]
and
\[
 (4+c_\#)u-c_\#s
 \le-\tfrac1{10}(6-c_\#)c_\#\phi_2K+4+c_\#
 \le-c_nK-\tfrac7{80}c_\#\phi_2K+5.
\]
This has a strict exponential margin beyond \(c_n\).

Next \(\hat\varrho_K\le C\ell^3L^{3s}
                         (1+\bar{\mathsf y}_{[s]})\).
The three possible exponential costs from
\((\epsilon_{\mathrm{cl}}+\epsilon_F)\hat\varrho_K^n\)
are therefore
\[
 L^{((6n+7)s-K)/2},\qquad
 L^{(3n+5)s-K},\qquad
 L^{((18n+29)s-2K)/6},
\]
times powers of \(K\).  Their rates of decay in \(K\) are
\[
 \frac{6n+15}{2(12n+22)},\qquad
 \frac{9n+17}{12n+22},\qquad
 \frac{2n+5}{4(6n+11)},
\]
each strictly larger than \(c_n\).  The other terms in the
third line of \eqref{eq:qcdm2-cutoff-total-error} decay faster
than every exponential, even after multiplication by
\(\hat\varrho_K^n\).  The contact term is bounded by a constant
times
\(L^{3\phi_1K+3+c_nK}e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm E}L^{\phi_1K/2}}\),
which is bounded as well.  Finitely many smaller cutoffs cause
no difficulty.  Every bound uses only the stated constants,
\(n,g,\ell\), proving the claimed uniformity.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of \cref{C-418-7}]
For each lattice, \cref{C-418-20} replaces the cumulant by
\(\partial_z^n\log T^\bullet(0)\) with its discarded-history
error.  The readout estimate \cref{C-418-13} gives
\[
 \left|\partial_z^n
       (\log T^\bullet-\log\hat T^\bullet
                                  -\mathfrak c^\bullet)(0)\right|
       \le\epsilon_{\mathrm{ro}}\prod_iR_i^{-1}.
\]
Subtract the two identities and apply \cref{C-418-21} to the
remaining difference of restarted logarithms.  This is
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-adjacent-contact}.  The second assertion is
\cref{C-418-22}.

For the stated threshold, \cref{C-418-23} applies.  The bounds
\[
 R_i^{-1}\le\frac{2n\|f_i\|_\sharp}
                      {(1-c_\lambda)\varrho_{\min}},\quad
 \hat r_i^{-1}\le\hat\varrho_K\|f_i\|_\sharp,\quad
 s_i^\bullet\le\sigma_K\|f_i\|_\sharp,\quad
 \varrho_i^{-1}\le\frac n{\varrho_{\min}}\|f_i\|_\sharp
\]
put the right side, including both contact terms, below
\(\mathsf B_n(K)\prod_i\|f_i\|_\sharp\).
The definition of \(C_n(g,\ell)\) proves
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-adjacent-rate}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Three mass derivatives of the pressure}

This subsection concerns a fixed admitted torus $T_\ell$
and $N_f\ge1$. Use the constants and adjacent-cutoff
comparison of \cref{C-418-2,C-418-7,C-418-8}.
For $W=I_g\times[m_-,m_+]$ put
\begin{equation}\label{C-412-67}
 p_K=\ell^{-3}\log Z_K,\qquad
 y_K=-\partial_m p_K,\qquad
 y_K^{(2)}=-\partial_m^3p_K
       =\ell^{-3}S^T_{3,K}((1,1),(1,1),(1,1)).
\end{equation}
The last identity follows by inserting a constant matrix
source. We shall prove convergence of $y_K^{(2)}$.
The contact energy in the adjacent-cutoff comparison
does not disappear from this derivative. Its third
derivative is the difference of two free determinants,
up to a summable remainder. This is the cancellation
needed below.

\begin{lemma}[The third derivative of the free determinant]
\label{C-412-68}
Let $\nu=8N_f$, $\nu_{\rm c}=48\nu$, and let
$\widehat D(p)$ be the chamber symbol, including flavour
and colour. Define
\[
 \Phi_K^{\rm fr}(m)=\ell^{-3}\partial_m^3
                       \log\det(D[1]+am),\qquad a=L^{-K}.
\]
There are constants $C_{\rm fr},C_{\rm pr}$ independent
of $K,m,\ell$ such that, for every fixed admitted side,
\[
 |\Phi_K^{\rm fr}(m)-\Phi_\infty^{\rm fr}(m)|
                   \le C_{\rm fr}a^{1/2},\qquad 0<m\le1/2,
\]
once $K$ exceeds a fixed symbol threshold. Here
\[
 \begin{split}
 \Phi_\infty^{\rm fr}(m)
 &=2\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^3}\operatorname{tr}\widehat D(p)^{-3}
                                       \frac{dp}{(2\pi)^3}
    +2\nu\ell^{-3}\sum_{k\in\Lambda_\ell^*}
                   \frac{m^3-3m|k|^2}{(m^2+|k|^2)^3},\\
 \Lambda_\ell^*&=(2\pi/\ell)(\mathbb Z+1/2)^3.
 \end{split}
\]
The integral and series converge absolutely. On every
disc $|m'-m|\le m/(2C_{\rm pr})$, with
$m\in[m_-,m_+]$, $\Phi_K^{\rm fr}$ is holomorphic
and bounded by a constant $C_{{\rm fr},1}(\ell,m_+)$
independent of $K$ and $m$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
We give the symbol and summation estimates, since their
cancellation is essential. The free-symbol calculation
in \cite[\S6]{QCDM1} decomposes the chamber space into
the constant chamber vector and its orthogonal complement.
Let $\iota$ be the isometric inclusion of the first space.
The heavy block has real part at least $\lambda_\rho$,
the two couplings are $O(|p|)$, and the light Schur
complement is $m+i\gamma\cdot p+O(|p|^2)$.
Away from $p=0$ the real part has a positive gap.
The Schur formula and the resolvent identity therefore give
\[
 \|(\widehat D(p)+\mu)^{-1}\|
       \le\frac{C_{\rm pr}}{|p|+\mu},\quad 0\le\mu\le1,
\]
and, for $|ak|$ sufficiently small,
\[
 \|(a^{-1}\widehat D(ak)+m)^{-1}
       -\iota(m+i\gamma\cdot k)^{-1}\iota^*\|
                            \le C_{\rm lt}a.
\]
All constants depend only on the chamber operator.
For completeness, the error in the light block is
$O(|p|^2)$ and multiplication by its two inverses costs
$O((|p|+\mu)^{-2})$. Each off-diagonal inverse block
has one additional factor $|p|$ from its coupling;
the heavy-heavy block has a bounded regular part.
These bounds prove the displayed estimates uniformly
in $\mu$. Differentiating the same block formula proves
the corresponding symbol estimates.

In particular, at mass zero,
\[
 \widehat D(p)^{-1}=\iota(i\gamma\cdot p)^{-1}\iota^*+R(p),
 \qquad |\partial^\alpha R(p)|\le C_\alpha|p|^{-|\alpha|}.
\]
The leading trace of the cube vanishes:
$\operatorname{tr}(i\gamma\cdot p)^{-3}=0$.
Thus $F(p)=\operatorname{tr}\widehat D(p)^{-3}$ satisfies
\[
 |\partial^\alpha F(p)|\le C_F|p|^{-2-|\alpha|},
                          \qquad |\alpha|\le2.
\]
This proves integrability at the origin.

Antiperiodic Fourier diagonalization gives, with
$\Lambda_{\ell,a}^*=\Lambda_\ell^*\cap[-\pi/a,\pi/a)^3$,
\[
 \Phi_K^{\rm fr}(m)=2\ell^{-3}\sum_{k\in\Lambda_{\ell,a}^*}
                  \operatorname{tr}(a^{-1}\widehat D(ak)+m)^{-3}.
\]
The midpoint sum for $F$ differs from its integral by
$O(a)$. To check the singular point, integrate the bound
$C_F|p|^{-2}$ on the eight cubes next to zero. Their
total is $O(a)$. On the other cubes Taylor's theorem
and the cancellation of the linear midpoint term give
their volume times $Ca^2\sup|p|^{-4}$; summing radial
shells again gives $O(a)$.

Subtract the mass-zero trace and split the momentum sum
at $R=a^{-1/2}$. Below $R$, the preceding inverse
comparison and the identity for the difference of cubes
bound the difference from the continuum expression by
$C a|k|^{-2}$. Its sum is $O(aR)$, because
$\ell^{-3}\sum_{0<|k|\le R}|k|^{-2}\le CR$.
Above $R$, differentiate the trace cube in the mass:
\[
 \partial_m\operatorname{tr}(a^{-1}\widehat D(ak)+m)^{-3}
              =-3\operatorname{tr}(a^{-1}\widehat D(ak)+m)^{-4}.
\]
The resolvent bound gives $Cm|k|^{-4}$ for the mass
difference. The continuum trace has the same bound,
and its omitted tail is $O(R^{-1})$.
Finally
\[
 \operatorname{tr}(m+i\gamma\cdot k)^{-3}
       =\nu\frac{m^3-3m|k|^2}{(m^2+|k|^2)^3}.
\]
Combining $O(a)$, $O(aR)$ and $O(R^{-1})$ proves the
claimed $a^{1/2}$ rate. The lattice momentum estimates
are uniform in the admitted sides; the antiperiodic
shift removes the zero mode.

For complex $m'$, expand the resolvent about real $m$.
Put $S_\ell=\ell^{-3}\sum_{k\in\Lambda_\ell^*}|k|^{-4}<\infty$.
For $n\ge1$, the resolvent bound gives
\[
 |\partial_m^n\Phi_K^{\rm fr}(m)|
       \le(n+2)!\nu_{\rm c}C_{\rm pr}^{n+3}m^{1-n}S_\ell.
\]
The Taylor series converges for
$|m'-m|<m/C_{\rm pr}$. On the half-radius disc its
tail is bounded using
$\sum_{n\ge1}(n+1)(n+2)2^{-n}=14$.
The zeroth term is bounded by the mass-zero midpoint
sum and $6\nu_{\rm c}C_{\rm pr}^4m_+S_\ell$.
These estimates give the stated $C_{{\rm fr},1}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Constant sources and fermion normalizers]
\label{C-412-69}\label{C-412-70}
At level $j$ let $L_j^F(m')$ be the holomorphic logarithm
of the free fermion fluctuation determinant. It exists on
\[
 |m'-m|<\max\{r_J/\lambda_{j-1},m/2\}.
\]
At the constant source $v_\zeta=(0,\zeta1)$ one has
\[
 \sum_Xe_j(X;v_\zeta)=L_j^F(m-\zeta)-L_j^F(m)
                                      +e_j^{\rm fl}(\zeta),
\]
where
\[
 \ell^{-3}|\partial_\zeta^3e_j^{\rm fl}(0)|
          \le C_{\rm tf}\phi_{j-1},\qquad
 C_{\rm tf}=12C_w^s(Mr_J)^{-3}.
\]
The restarted source energies have the same free
determinant, with a remainder bounded by
$C_{\rm tf}\widehat\phi_{j-1}$.

For $|m'-m|<m/2$, the determinant identity for the tower
on the empty history gives
\[
 \sum_{j\le k}[L_j^F]^{m'}_m
  =[\log\det(D[1]+am')]^{m'}_m
      -[\log\det\mathbb D_k(1;am')]^{m'}_m.
\]
At its terminal level,
\[
 \ell^{-3}|\partial_{m'}^3\log\det\mathbb D_K(1;am')|
                   \le128\nu c_1m^{-4},\qquad |m'-m|\le m/4,
\]
where $c_1=\max\{c_{\rm disc}+1,b_F\}$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
There are two domains for the fluctuation operator.
If $\lambda_{j-1}|m'-m|<r_J$, the source fluctuation
estimate applies, since $L\lambda_{j-1}|m'-m|<r_M$.
If $|m'-m|<m/2$, accretivity forms the entire tower.
The two discs have the same centre; their union is the
displayed disc. The determinant is nonzero and
holomorphic there, and hence has a holomorphic logarithm.

At the trivial pair write $D^{(j)}(X;c)$ for the degree
zero part of the new activity after removing its Gaussian
contribution and the two normalizer logarithms. The
source step in \cite[\S10]{QCDM1} bounds
\[
 \sum_{X\supset\square}e^{\kappa d_j(X)}|D^{(j)}(X;c)|
                      \le C_w^s\phi_{j-1}
\]
when the gauge source is constant: its Lipschitz
contribution vanishes. Assign each $X$ to one of its
cubes. Summing over the $(\ell/(M\lambda_j))^3$ cubes
bounds the sum by this number times $C_w^s\phi_{j-1}$.

The gauge normalizer is unchanged by the source. The
Gaussian contribution depends only on the gauge source,
so is unchanged at $v_\zeta$. The localized fermion
normalizer logarithms sum to
\[
 \int_0^1\operatorname{Tr}
       [\Gamma_{j-1}(t)^{-1}\partial_t\Gamma_{j-1}(t)]\,dt
                 =L_j^F(m-\zeta)-L_j^F(m).
\]
The equality is exact: the segment is inside the
zero-free disc just established, so its logarithm is
continued there. The remaining difference of the two
$D^{(j)}$ sums is holomorphic for $|\zeta|<r_J/\lambda_j$
and bounded by $2C_w^s\phi_{j-1}(\ell/(M\lambda_j))^3$.
Cauchy's third-derivative bound cancels the factor
$\lambda_j^{-3}$ and gives $C_{\rm tf}\ell^3\phi_{j-1}$.
The restarted chain uses the same tower and its
normalizers; its step estimates have $\widehat\phi$ in
place of $\phi$. This proves the restarted assertion.
For a constant gauge source the same decomposition
holds with an additional function of that source alone.
This observation will also be used below.

Iterate the Schur determinant identity. Its factors
$\theta^{-\dim H_j}$ do not depend on $m'$, so their
logarithmic increments cancel and give the tower formula.
On the empty history at level $K$ no field is stored.
Writing $T_K=q_K\cdots q_1$, one has
\[
 \mathbb D_K^{-1}=T_K(D[1]+am')^{-1}T_K^*+\theta_K^{-1},
          \qquad \|T_K\|^2=a.
\]
Thus
\[
 \partial_{m'}\log\det\mathbb D_K
       =a\operatorname{Tr}[\mathbb D_KT_K(D[1]+am')^{-2}T_K^*].
\]
Since $\|\mathbb D_K\|\le c_1$, its dimension is
$\nu\ell^3$, and $\|(D[1]+am')^{-1}\|\le(a\operatorname{Re}m')^{-1}$,
the normalized derivative is at most $4\nu c_1m^{-2}$
on $|m'-m|<m/2$. Two further Cauchy derivatives on
circles of radius $m/4$ give $128\nu c_1m^{-4}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The two free operators at the comparison scale]
\label{C-412-71}
Use the adjacent data $A,B$ and depths
$s=\lceil K/58\rceil$, $u=\lceil c_\#K/580\rceil$.
At the trivial configuration let $D_\zeta^A,D_\zeta^B$
be their common-space operators at depth $s$, with
source $L^{-s}\zeta1$. For $|\zeta|<m/2$,
\[
 \operatorname{Re}D_\zeta^\bullet
                   \ge\tfrac12c_bL^{-s}m,
 \quad \|D_\zeta^B-D_\zeta^A\|\le K_c L^{s-K},
 \quad \det D_\zeta^\bullet
          =\det\mathbb D_{t_0^\bullet}(1;a_{K^\bullet}(m-\zeta)).
\]
Consequently
\[
 \varphi^{\rm bl}(\zeta)=\int_0^1\operatorname{Tr}
 \left[((1-\tau)D_\zeta^A+\tau D_\zeta^B)^{-1}
                     (D_\zeta^B-D_\zeta^A)\right]d\tau
\]
is a holomorphic logarithm of the determinant ratio, and
\[
 \ell^{-3}|\partial_\zeta^3\varphi^{\rm bl}(0)|
       \le C_{\rm dp}L^{5s-K},\qquad
 C_{\rm dp}=96\nu K_cc_b^{-1}m_-^{-4}.
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The identification with the tower is the exact
composition of its averages in \cref{C-420-13}.
At the trivial field this tower exists by accretivity
throughout $|\zeta|<m/2$.
In the Schur form set $\varphi=a_0\mathcal K^{-1}R^*\chi$.
Then
\[
 \langle\chi,D_\zeta^\bullet\chi\rangle
  =a_0\|\chi-R\varphi\|^2+
       \langle\varphi,(D^\xi[1]+L^{-s}(m-\zeta))\varphi\rangle.
\]
Here $a_0\ge a_-$ and $\|R\|\le1$. With
$\mu=L^{-s}m/2$, minimizing
$a_0\|\chi-v\|^2+\mu\|v\|^2$ gives
$a_0\mu/(a_0+\mu)\ge c_b\mu$.
The comparison \cref{C-420-10} applies with zero
curvature and constant source; its gradient contribution
vanishes. It gives the norm difference above.

Every convex interpolation is accretive by the same
floor. Its inverse has norm at most $2L^s/(c_bm)$,
and its dimension is $\nu\ell^3L^{3s}$.
Hence $|\varphi^{\rm bl}|\le
2\nu\ell^3K_cc_b^{-1}m^{-1}L^{5s-K}$.
Differentiating the determinant along $\tau$ identifies
its exponential with the ratio. Cauchy's estimate with
radius $m/2$ gives the stated third derivative.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Cancellation of the contact derivative]
\label{C-412-72}
Let $c^\bullet$ be the contact energy of \cref{C-418-3}.
For all sufficiently large $K$, uniformly on $W$,
\[
 \begin{split}
 \ell^{-3}\partial_\zeta^3c^\bullet[v_\zeta]\big|_0
 &=-\Phi_{K^\bullet}^{\rm fr}(m)
   -\ell^{-3}\partial_\zeta^3\log\det D_\zeta^\bullet\big|_0+r^\bullet,\\
 |r^\bullet|&\le2C_{\rm tf}S_\phi
                         \phi(\tfrac12L^{u+1}\gamma^{-2}),
       \qquad S_\phi=(1-2L^{-1/2})^{-1}.
 \end{split}
\]
In particular
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |(y_{K+1}^{(2)}+\Phi_{K+1}^{\rm fr})
                   -(y_K^{(2)}+\Phi_K^{\rm fr})|
 &\le\ell^{-3}N_f^{9/2}C_3L^{-c_3K}
      +C_{\rm dp}L^{5s-K}\\
 &\quad{}+4C_{\rm tf}S_\phi\phi(\tfrac12L^{u+1}\gamma^{-2}),
 \end{aligned}
 \qquad c_3=c_\#/116.
\]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The original and restarted coefficients satisfy
$x_i,\widehat x_i\ge\tfrac12L^{K^\bullet-i}\gamma^{-2}$.
The constant ceiling on $\gamma$ implies
$\phi(Lx)\le2L^{-1/2}\phi(x)$ for
$x\ge\gamma^{-2}/2$. Indeed the logarithmic factor
in this ratio is at most $e^{1/3}<2$.
It follows that each sum of $\phi_i$ ending at depth
$u+1$ is at most
$S_\phi\phi(\tfrac12L^{u+1}\gamma^{-2})$.

The contact energy is the original energy through
$t_1^\bullet$ less the restarted energy from
$t_0^\bullet$ to $t_1^\bullet$.
Apply \cref{C-412-69}. The terms $L_j^F(m-\zeta)-L_j^F(m)$
cancel for $t_0^\bullet<j\le t_1^\bullet$.
The remaining sum through $t_0^\bullet$ telescopes
by \cref{C-412-70} to the fine free determinant less
the determinant of $D_\zeta^\bullet$.
Its third $\zeta$ derivative is minus the third
$m$ derivative of the fine determinant. The two sums
of fluctuation remainders obey the first displayed
bound by the geometric estimate above.
Subtract the identities for $A,B$ and use
\cref{C-412-71} to control the block determinant ratio.

To apply \cref{C-418-7}, expand the flavour identity
in the fixed orthonormal Hermitian basis:
$1=\sum_j\operatorname{tr}(t_j)t_j$.
There are $N_f^2$ terms and
$\sum_j|\operatorname{tr}t_j|\le N_f^{3/2}$.
The three constant entries are an admissible tuple
for the comparison with contact terms retained.
Its error is at most $C_3L^{-c_3K}$ per basis triple.
Multilinearity therefore costs at most $N_f^{9/2}$.
Divide by $\ell^3$ and combine the three bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A complex neighbourhood independent of the cutoff]
\label{C-412-73}
Let $\rho_b,\rho_m$ be the radii in \cref{C-412-54} and put
\[
 \rho_b^\flat=\rho_b/2,\qquad
 \rho_m^\flat=\min\{\rho_m/2,m_-/(4C_{\rm pr})\}.
\]
Let $W^\flat$ be the union of the open polydiscs of
these radii about $W$. Every $y_K^{(2)}$ is holomorphic
there and bounded by the cutoff-independent number
\[
 C_{\rm pd}=C_{{\rm fr},1}+128\nu c_1m_-^{-4}
 +48C_w^s(LMr_J)^{-3}S_\phi\phi(\tfrac12L\gamma^{-2})
 +\frac{48\log2}{\ell^3\rho_m^3}.
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
About a real centre $(b_0,m_0)$ write $b'=b_0+t$,
$m'=m_0+\zeta$. The zero-free estimate of
\cref{C-412-54} gives
\[
 \log Z_K(b',m')=E_K(-t1,-\zeta1)
                 +\log Z_K^{\rm sub}[0]+\log\psi(t,\zeta),
                      \qquad |\psi-1|\le1/2,
\]
on the original polydisc. Use the principal logarithm
of $\psi$, whose modulus is at most $\log2$.
Its third mass derivative on the smaller polydisc is
at most $48\log2/\rho_m^3$.

For the energy use \cref{C-412-69} with constant gauge
source $-t$. The additional Gaussian term depends
only on $t$, so its mass derivatives vanish.
The fermion normalizer sum telescopes, giving a free
determinant term bounded by $C_{{\rm fr},1}$ and a
terminal term bounded by $128\nu c_1m_-^{-4}$.
The remaining degree-zero sum at level $j$ is bounded
by $C_w^s\phi_{j-1}(\ell/(M\lambda_j))^3$.
The circle of radius $r_J/(2\lambda_{j-1})$ about
$\zeta$ remains in its domain, since
$|\zeta|\le\rho_m/2\le r_J/16$.
Cauchy's estimate gives
$48C_w^s(LMr_J)^{-3}\phi_{j-1}$ after division
by $\ell^3$. Sum by the same geometric estimate.
These four contributions are $C_{\rm pd}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[From a real segment to a half-disc]
\label{C-412-74}
Suppose $f$ is holomorphic on $|z-x_0|<R$, bounded
there by $M$, and bounded by $\varepsilon\le M$ on
a real interval of length $2\delta$, whose centre
lies within $\delta$ of $x_0$, where $0<\delta\le R/8$.
Then, for $|z-x_0|\le R/2$,
\[
 |f(z)|\le M^{1-\omega}\varepsilon^\omega,
                 \qquad \omega=\frac{\log(13/11)}{\log(2R/\delta)}.
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
If $x_1$ is the centre of the segment, use
$J(w)=x_1+\frac\delta2(w+w^{-1})$.
It maps $|w|>1$ onto the complement of the segment.
For $1\le|w|\le\rho_1=(2R-3\delta)/\delta$ its image
is inside $|z-x_1|<R-\delta$, hence inside the original
disc. On the annulus the maximum principle applied to
$\log|f\circ J|$ bounds it by the harmonic interpolation
of $\log\varepsilon$ on $|w|=1$ and $\log M$ on
$|w|=\rho_1$. At a point with $|z-x_0|\le R/2$,
$|J^{-1}(z)|<(R+3\delta)/\delta$. Its harmonic weight
on the inner circle is therefore at least
\[
 \frac{\log((2R-3\delta)/(R+3\delta))}
      {\log((2R-3\delta)/\delta)}
                  \ge\frac{\log(13/11)}{\log(2R/\delta)}.
\]
The same bound on the segment is immediate.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Convergence of the differentiated condensate]
\label{C-412-75}
On every fixed admitted torus, $y_K^{(2)}$ converges
along the full sequence of cutoffs, uniformly on $W$.
More precisely, for $K\ge K_*(g,\ell)$,
\[
 \sup_W|y_{K+1}^{(2)}-y_K^{(2)}|
       \le C(g,\ell)(1+K)^{p_0}L^{-c_yK},\qquad c_y=c_\#/1160.
\]
It also converges on the union of the closed discs of
radius $\rho_b^\flat/2$ about $I_g$, uniformly for
real $m\in[m_-,m_+]$, with all $b$ derivatives on $W$.
If $m_-<m_+$, it converges uniformly on the union
$W^\natural$ of the closed polydiscs of radii
$\rho_b^\flat/2,\rho_m^\flat/2$ about $W$.
Its limit is holomorphic on the interior, and all
parameter derivatives converge on $W$. In particular
\[
 \ell^{-3}S^T_{p+q,K}((1,1)^q,(0,1)^p),\qquad q\ge3,
\]
converges for every $p\ge0$. All these assertions
concern a fixed side; their constants may depend on it.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
By \cref{C-412-68}, the increment of the free term is
at most $2C_{\rm fr}L^{-K/2}$. Add this to
\cref{C-412-72}. Since
\[
 5s-K\le5-53K/58,\qquad u\ge c_\#K/580=2c_yK,
\]
each of its three errors is at most a constant times
$(1+K)^{p_0}L^{-c_yK}$. Their series converges, proving
the real assertion with a tail of the same order.

The increments are bounded by $2C_{\rm pd}$ on
$W^\flat$. Apply \cref{C-412-74} in $b$ with
\[
 \delta_b=\min\{\rho_b^\flat/8,|I_g|/2\},\qquad
 h_b=\frac{\log(13/11)}{\log\max\{16,4\rho_b^\flat/|I_g|\}}.
\]
Choose the real segment inside $I_g$ with centre
nearest the base point. The complex increment is
bounded by $ (2C_{\rm pd})^{1-h_b}\varepsilon_K^{h_b}$,
where $\varepsilon_K$ is the lesser of its real bound
and $2C_{\rm pd}$. This series is summable.

If $m_-<m_+$, repeat in $m$ with
\[
 h_m=\frac{\log(13/11)}
              {\log\max\{16,4\rho_m^\flat/(m_+-m_-)\}}.
\]
The resulting exponent is $h_bh_m>0$. Thus the series
converges uniformly on $W^\natural$, at rate at most
$C(1+K)^{p_0}L^{-h_bh_mc_yK}$. Uniform limits are
holomorphic in the interior. Cauchy's formula on the
half-radius polydiscs gives convergence of each
derivative; its cost is
$p!(q-3)!(2/\rho_b^\flat)^p(2/\rho_m^\flat)^{q-3}$.
The constant-source identity identifies these derivatives
with the stated cumulants.
\end{proof}

The radii and constants in this subsection are formed
after the construction constants, $g$ and $\ell$; they
impose no additional mass-dependent ceiling on $\gamma$.
The theorem proves convergence of the second mass
derivative of $y_K$. It makes no assertion that $y_K$
itself converges without a subtraction.

\subsection{Continuation of cutoff convergence}

\begin{lemma}[Propagation along a thin complex neighbourhood]
\label{C-404-89}
Let $a<p<b$, $0<w\le b-p$, and
$G=\{z:\operatorname{dist}(z,[a,b])<w\}$. The harmonic
measure $\omega$ of $[p,b]$ in $G\setminus[p,b]$ satisfies
\[
 \omega(x)\ge\tfrac15\,3^{-4(p-x)/w}\qquad(a\le x<p).
\]
If $F$ is holomorphic on $G$, $|F|\le M$ there and
$|F|\le m$ on $[p,b]$, then
\[
 |F(x)|\le M^{1-\omega_*}m^{\omega_*}
 \quad(a\le x\le b),\qquad
 \omega_*=\tfrac15\,3^{-4(p-a)/w}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
In the disc $|z-p|<w$, slit along $[p,p+w)$, compare
$\omega$ with the harmonic measure of the slit. After setting
$\zeta=(z-p)/w$ and $s=\sqrt\zeta$, with
$0<\arg s<\pi$, this is the harmonic measure of the
diameter of the upper half-disc. At $\zeta=-\tau^2$,
$0<\tau\le1/\sqrt2$, its value is
\[
 1-\frac2\pi\arctan\frac{2\tau}{1-\tau^2}
 \ge1-\frac2\pi\arccos(1/3)>1/5.
\]
The half-disc formula was computed in \cref{C-404-71}.
The maximum principle gives the same lower bound for $\omega$
on $[p-w/2,p)$. For a centre $y\le p-w/2$, the disc
$|z-y|<w/2$ lies in $G\setminus[p,b]$. Harnack's inequality
gives a factor at worst $1/3$ for a step of length at most
$w/4$. A chain from $p-w/2$ to $x$ has fewer than
$4(p-x)/w$ such steps, proving the displayed lower bound.

Apply the subharmonic maximum principle to
\[
 \log|F|-(1-\omega)\log M-\omega\log m.
\]
Its boundary upper limits are nonpositive, so
$|F|\le M^{1-\omega}m^\omega$ inside. If $m\le M$,
use $\omega\ge\omega_*$ on the real interval to the left
of $p$; if $m>M$, the bound $|F|\le M$ is stronger.
On $[p,b]$ use $|F|\le\min\{m,M\}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Full cutoff convergence at real masses]
\label{C-404-90}
Impose the cutoff-comparison hypotheses of \cref{C-418-2}.
Keep $g,\ell,\mathsf b$ fixed. Let $X$ have pairwise
disjoint real Lipschitz test supports, with two supports
at distance at least $d>0$. Put
\[
 \omega_\ell=\tfrac15\,3^{-3r_J/(2w_\ell)},\qquad
 C_n^w(d)=
 \frac{[2B_n^w(d)e^{n(C+2+A^\sharp)\ell^3}]^{1-\omega_\ell}
                  C_n(g,\ell)^{\omega_\ell}}
      {1-L^{-c_n\omega_\ell}}.
\]
Here $c_n,C_n(g,\ell)$ and $K_n(g,\ell;d)$ are the
cutoff-comparison constants in \cref{C-418-7,C-418-8}.
For $x\in I^\sharp$ and
$K'\ge K\ge\max\{K_\sharp,K_n(g,\ell;d)\}$,
\[
 |S^T_{n,K'}(x;X)-S^T_{n,K}(x;X)|
 \le C_n^w(d)L^{-c_n\omega_\ell K}\prod_i\|f_i\|_\sharp.
\]
The full sequence converges locally uniformly on
$\mathcal O^\sharp$ to a holomorphic function, with all
mass derivatives. It also converges at moving masses
$x_j\to x\in I^\sharp$. The rate is independent of the
mass and coupling within the stated ranges, but depends on
the fixed torus:
\[
 \omega_\ell\ge\tfrac15
 \exp[-\tfrac32(\log3)(r_J/c_w)\ell^3(1+\log\ell)].
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \cref{C-404-82,C-404-83}, the increment
$F_K=S^T_{n,K+1}(\cdot;X)-S^T_{n,K}(\cdot;X)$ is
holomorphic on $\mathcal O^\sharp$ and bounded there by
\[
 2B_n^w(d)e^{n(C+2+A^\sharp)\ell^3}\prod_i\|f_i\|_\sharp.
\]
On the positive interval $I_0$, \cref{C-418-7} bounds
the same increment by
$C_n(g,\ell)L^{-c_nK}\prod_i\|f_i\|_\sharp$.
Apply \cref{C-404-89} with
$a=-r_J/4$, $p=r_J/8$, $b=1/2$ and $w=w_\ell$.
Since $p-a=3r_J/8$, its exponent is $\omega_\ell$.
Summing the resulting geometric estimate proves the displayed
cutoff bound. Zero test functions cause no difficulty by
multilinearity.

The sequence is locally bounded on the connected domain
$\mathcal O^\sharp$ and converges on $I_0$, which has
accumulation points there. Vitali's theorem gives local
uniform convergence throughout the domain. Cauchy's formula
gives convergence of all derivatives, and local uniform
convergence gives the assertion at moving masses.
The final inequality follows from the lower bound for
$w_\ell$ in \cref{C-404-82}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Scaling to any real mass label]
\label{C-404-91}
Let $\mathsf b>0$ and $\mathsf m\in\mathbb R$. Choose an
integer $z$ with
\[
 L^z\ge\max\left\{
 \frac{\gamma^{-2}+4B_\sharp+1}{\mathsf b},
 2|\mathsf m|,\frac{4|\mathsf m|}{r_J}\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathsf b'=L^z\mathsf b,\qquad
 \mathsf m'=L^{-z}\mathsf m,\qquad
 g_z=(\mathsf b'-3B_\sharp)^{-1/2}
\]
satisfy $g_z<\gamma$, $\mathsf b'\in I_{g_z}$ and
$\mathsf m'\in I^\sharp$. The product
$\mathsf b\mathsf m$ is unchanged.
For every $\ell'\in\mathfrak L(g_z)$ such that
$\ell=L^{-z}\ell'$ is an admitted torus side, the model
at $(\ell,K,\mathsf b,\mathsf m)$ is the same finite
lattice integral as the model at
$(\ell',K-z,\mathsf b',\mathsf m')$.
Thus the fixed-torus conclusions above transfer to these
sides. The corresponding growing-torus subsequential
conclusions transfer as well.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The inequalities give $\mathsf m'\le1/2$ if the mass is
positive and $\mathsf m'\ge-r_J/4$ if it is negative.
The zero mass stays zero. Also
$\mathsf b'>\gamma^{-2}+4B_\sharp$, whence
$g_z<\gamma$ and
\[
 \mathsf b'=g_z^{-2}+3B_\sharp
       \in[g_z^{-2}+3B_\sharp,Lg_z^{-2}]\subset I_{g_z}.
\]
The two descriptions have the same number of sites and
the same bare parameters:
\[
 L^{K-z}\mathsf b'=L^K\mathsf b,\qquad
 L^{-(K-z)}\mathsf m'=L^{-K}\mathsf m.
\]
The insertion formulas therefore give the scaling identity
directly. For $f^{[z]}(x)=f(L^{-z}x)$,
\[
 O_{K-z}(f^{[z]})=L^{-z}O_K(f),\qquad
 \Phi_{K-z}(f^{[z]})=L^z\Phi_K(f).
\]
Apply \cref{C-404-86,C-404-88,C-404-90} at the primed
parameters and carry each multilinear form back by these
identities. In the two-point laws $\mathcal K_6$ is unchanged
by this dilation and $\mathcal K_4$ is multiplied by $L^{2z}$,
which gives the original leading coefficients after scaling
back. Growing tori use the uniform bound of
\cref{C-404-85} and the same diagonal extraction.
\end{proof}

The continuation and scaling prove these conclusions for the
mass label $\mathsf m$. They supply no assertion that the
physical spectral mass vanishes when $\mathsf m=0$.
The full cutoff theorem here keeps the torus fixed; its rate
does not give convergence uniformly in growing volume.

\section{Laws of the block fields}\label{sec:qcdm2-block-laws}

Fix $0<g\le\gamma$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$, the physical
torus $T_\ell$ and the compact positive label
rectangle $\mathsf W(g)=\bar I(g)\times[m_-,m_+]$.
Throughout this section we impose the constant choices of
\cref{C-418-2}, including its five additional floors and
ceilings. The block map $\mathcal M$ is the same Borel
gauge-covariant map at every cutoff. At depth $d$ its
configuration space $\mathcal V_{[d]}$ is a finite product
of copies of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ on the lattice of physical
spacing $L^{-d}$ in $T_\ell$.
For $K\ge d$ let
\begin{equation}\label{C-406-60}
 \mu_d^{F,K}=(\mathcal M^{K-d})_*\nu_K.
\end{equation}
The superscript $F$ distinguishes the matter law from the
pure-gauge law used below.

\begin{theorem}[Convergence of the block laws]\label{C-406-68}
At the preceding data there are numbers $\tau_K$, independent
of the labels, such that $\sum_K\tau_K<\infty$ and, for all
sufficiently large $K$,
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(\mu_d^{F,K},\mu_d^{F,K+1})\le\tau_K
       \quad\left(0\le d\le d_K:=\left\lfloor\tfrac14\log_LK\right\rfloor\right),
 \qquad \tau_K\le(8\mathsf M_{g,\ell}+26)K^{-2}.
\]
Here $\operatorname{TV}(P,Q)=\sup_E|P(E)-Q(E)|$.
For each fixed $d$, the full sequence converges in total
variation to a gauge-invariant probability measure $\mu_d^F$,
uniformly on $\mathsf W(g)$, with
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(\mu_d^{F,K},\mu_d^F)
                \le\sum_{j\ge K}\tau_j
\]
once $K$ is sufficiently large and $K\ge L^{4d}$.
