The limit depends continuously on the labels in total
variation and satisfies $\mathcal M_*\mu_{d+1}^F=\mu_d^F$.

On the compact product $\mathcal V_{\rm thr}=\prod_{d\ge0}\mathcal V_{[d]}$
there is exactly one probability measure $\mu_{\rm thr}^F$
whose coordinates through depth $D$ have law
\[
       (V\mapsto(\mathcal M^{D-d}V)_{d\le D})_*\mu_D^F.
\]
It is concentrated on the compatible sequences
$V_d=\mathcal MV_{d+1}$. The laws obtained from cutoff $K$
by using $V_d=\mathcal M^{K-d}U$ for $d\le K$ and any
fixed configurations for $d>K$ converge weakly to
$\mu_{\rm thr}^F$ along the full sequence.
\end{theorem}

The proof compares the measures before taking derivatives
in sources. Its three operations on each lattice are to
discard histories with an early large-field region, change
to the restarted history, and sum the histories above its
base. The two restarted measures can then be compared on
one configuration space. We carry a bounded Borel test
function through each operation; this gives total variation.

\subsection{Normalization and positive measures}

\begin{lemma}\label{C-406-61}
The laws in \eqref{C-406-60} are gauge invariant and satisfy
$\mathcal M_*\mu_{d+1}^{F,K}=\mu_d^{F,K}$ for $K\ge d+1$.
For gauge-invariant probability measures, total variation
can be tested on gauge-invariant Borel functions with values
in $[0,1]$. Borel image maps contract total variation.

The following normalization bounds will be used. Write
$x(f)=\int f\,dx$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $x,y$ are positive measures, $x(1)>0$, and
$0\le(x-y)(f)\le(x-y)(1)\le Rx(1)$ for $0\le f\le1$,
with $R<1$, then $y(1)>0$ and the normalized integrals
differ by at most $R/(1-R)$.
\item If $a,p$ are positive measures, $a(1)>0$, $c\ne0$,
and $|cp(f)-a(f)|\le\varepsilon a(1)$ for all Borel
$|f|\le1$, where $\varepsilon\le1/2$, then $p(1)>0$
and the normalized integrals differ by at most $4\varepsilon$.
\item If $x,y$ are positive measures, $x(1)>0$, and
$|x(f)-y(f)|\le\eta x(1)$ for $|f|\le1$, where $\eta<1$,
then $y(1)>0$ and the normalized integrals differ by at
most $2\eta$.
\end{enumerate}
The first bound also holds on a class of tests containing
$1$ when its displayed inequalities hold on that class.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Lift a gauge transformation at depth $d$ to one constant
on each block of the original lattice. Gauge covariance
of $\mathcal M^{K-d}$ and invariance of the bare density
and Haar measure give gauge invariance of its image.
Composition of the block maps gives consistency.
For a Borel set $E$, average $1_E(V^v)$ over the compact
group of gauge transformations. Fubini gives a Borel
invariant function $f_E\in[0,1]$ with $P(f_E)=P(E)$ and
$Q(f_E)=Q(E)$. Conversely, integration of the level sets
of any $[0,1]$-valued test bounds its integral difference
by total variation. The contraction assertion follows by
taking inverse images of Borel sets.

For (i) put $\delta=x-y$. The numerator of the difference
is $x(f)\delta(1)-\delta(f)x(1)$, of modulus at most
$\delta(1)x(1)$, and $y(1)\ge(1-R)x(1)$.
For (ii), $|cp(1)|\ge(1-\varepsilon)a(1)>0$; subtract
the normalized fractions to get
$2\varepsilon/(1-\varepsilon)\le4\varepsilon$.
For (iii), use $|y(f)|\le y(1)$ when subtracting the
fractions with denominator $x(1)y(1)$. Each of the two
terms is at most $\eta$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The comparison at a growing depth}

Use the two cutoffs $K^{\rm A}=K$, $K^{\rm B}=K+1$.
The depths of the cutoff comparison at $n=1$ are
$s=\lceil K/34\rceil$ and $u=\lceil c_\#K/340\rceil$;
the corresponding levels are $t_0^\bullet=K^\bullet-s$
and $t_1^\bullet=K^\bullet-u$.
The common spaces at these depths are $\mathcal Y$ and
$\mathcal X$. Retain the interpolation radius $r_\lambda$
and the errors $R^F,\varepsilon_{\rm sh},\varepsilon_{\rm cl},
\varepsilon_F$ from \cref{C-418-6} at $n=1$.
For $d'\ge0$ put
\begin{align*}
 N_{[d']}&=\ell^3L^{3d'},\\
 R_{d'}&=\mathsf M_{g,\ell}
     \exp[-\theta_{\rm tl}A_0^2(\log(L^{d'}\gamma^{-2}))^{2\mathfrak p_0}],\\
 e_{d'}&=\frac{\exp[(C+2+C_P(1+\log(L^{d'}X_g+\bar B)))N_{[d']}]}
                   {r_\lambda-1},\\
 \eta_K&=3R^F+2\varepsilon_{\rm sh}
                         +2(\varepsilon_{\rm cl}+\varepsilon_F),\\
 \tau_K&=8R_{d_K}+8e_{d_K}+2\eta_K.
\end{align*}
Take $K$ large enough for the cutoff-comparison estimates,
$r_\lambda\ge16\mathsf M_{g,\ell}\ge16$, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-tv-threshold}
 d_K\le u-1,\qquad 8R_{d_K}\le1,\qquad2e_{d_K}\le1.
\end{equation}
The proof below verifies that these conditions hold
eventually, uniformly in the labels.

\begin{lemma}[Histories above the restart]\label{C-406-62}
For $t_1^\bullet\le k\le K^\bullet$, the interpolation at
zero source satisfies
\[
 \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_k^{(t_1^\bullet)}}
        \int\|g_h[0,\lambda]\|_{h_F}\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}
 \le\exp[\operatorname{Re}E_k(0,\lambda)+(C+2)n_k],
           \qquad |\lambda|\le r_\lambda.
\]
The energy is holomorphic for $|\lambda|<r_\lambda$,
and $E_k(0,0)=E_k$ of the original flow.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Apply the free-past source induction \cref{C-422-14}
at base $t_1^\bullet$, using \cref{C-422-17}.
The difference perturbation has the four lag bounds with
$\Lambda$, by \cref{C-418-10}. At zero source those
bounds hold at radius $c_\lambda\Lambda$, and
$r_\lambda\le R_K/2\le R_k/2$. Thus every point of the
stated closed disc lies in the open induction domain.
Its history estimate, after dropping the nonnegative
mark, gives the displayed bound. The densities are
those of \cref{C-424-22}, which agree almost everywhere
with the induction densities. The energy conclusion is
the holomorphy and zero-parameter clause of that induction.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The restarted term is positive]\label{C-406-63}
Let $\hat\theta^\bullet$ be the restarted term at level
$t_1^\bullet$, and let $\nu_\lambda^\bullet$
be the scalar Berezin integral of the interpolated measure
at that level and zero source. Then
\[
 \operatorname{Ber}\hat\theta^\bullet
    =(\mathcal M^{s-u})_*(\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet\hat F_0^\bullet\,dW),
 \qquad
 \nu_1^\bullet=e^{E_{t_1^\bullet}-\hat c^\bullet(0)}
                         \operatorname{Ber}\hat\theta^\bullet.
\]
These are positive measures and
\[
 \nu_1^\bullet(\mathcal X)
 \ge\tfrac58\exp\left[\operatorname{Re}E_{K^\bullet}(0,1)
                  -C_P(1+\log x_{K^\bullet})\ell^3\right].
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
At a step along the history without large fields the
fermion kernel integrates to one in the new generators.
Consequently its scalar Berezin integral pushes forward
the old scalar measure multiplied by the passing-test
indicator and the gauge-fixing factor. Iterating from
$t_0^\bullet$ to $t_1^\bullet$ and using the common block
map gives the first identity. The initial cutoff indicator
is absorbed in $\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet$, as in
\cref{C-418-19}. Both factors in this density are
nonnegative, and its mass is $\hat T^\bullet(0)>0$.
The interpolation at $\lambda=1$ is exactly the restarted
term times the displayed energy factor. That factor is
positive: both zero-source energies are real. Finally
the lower bound in \cref{C-421-4}(d), with the readout
of \cref{C-421-14}, gives the claimed mass after this
energy factor is included.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Discarding large-field histories]\label{C-406-64}
Let $\varsigma_0=e^{-\beta A}\det(D+m_0)$, $Z=\int\varsigma_0\,dU$,
and $m_t(F)=\int\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset^{(t)}}F\varsigma_0\,dU$.
For gauge-invariant Borel $0\le F\le1$,
\[
 0\le\int F\varsigma_0\,dU-m_t(F)
 \le Z-m_t(1)
 \le\mathsf M_{g,\ell}
 e^{-\theta_{\rm dis}A_0^2(\log\mathsf t_t)^{2\mathfrak p_0}}Z.
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The exact history decomposition holds with the density
$F\varsigma_0$. Its terms are nonnegative and bounded by
the corresponding terms with $F=1$. The histories whose
restriction at level $t$ is not $h_\emptyset^{(t)}$ are
precisely those discarded in \cref{C-421-5}(a). Summing
their masses gives the bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Changing to the restart]\label{C-406-65}
Let $0\le d'\le u-1$, $2e_{d'}\le1$, and
$k=K^\bullet-d'$. The interpolated scalar measure on
$\mathcal V_{[d']}$ along $h'=h_\emptyset^{(k)}$ is
\[
 J_\lambda^\bullet
       =(\mathcal M^k)_*(\mathfrak w_{h'}\varsigma^{0,\lambda}\,dU),
\]
where $\varsigma^{0,\lambda}$ is the free-past density of
\cref{C-424-7}. At $\lambda=0$ this is a positive measure
with
\[
 J_0^\bullet(1)\ge e^{E_k-C_P(1+\log x_k)N_{[d']}}.
\]
At $\lambda=1$ it is the image under $\mathcal M^{u-d'}$
of $\nu_1^\bullet$ times the nonnegative weight of the
steps from $t_1^\bullet$ to $k$. It is positive, and
\[
 \left|\frac{J_1^\bullet(f)}{J_1^\bullet(1)}
          -\frac{J_0^\bullet(f)}{J_0^\bullet(1)}\right|
                      \le4e_{d'}\qquad(|f|\le1).
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The free-past construction \cref{C-424-22} at base
$t_1^\bullet$ gives the same interpolated history terms
as \cref{C-406-62}. Along $h'$ there are no proper or
external bonds below level $k$, no new fluctuation
variable, and all free coordinates are the block field
$\mathcal M^kU$. Their reference measure is Haar measure
on $\mathcal V_k$. This remains true at $k=K^\bullet$.
Consequently the scalar Berezin integral of this history
is the displayed image measure.

At $\lambda=0$, $\varsigma^{0,0}=\varsigma_0$, giving
positivity and the lower mass bound from the partition
estimate of \cite{QCDM1}. Factor the history weight as
\[
 \mathfrak w_{h'}(U)=\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset^{(t_1)}}(U)
                         \mathfrak w_{h'}^\circ(\mathcal M^{t_1}U).
\]
By \cref{C-424-34}, $\mathfrak w_{h'}^\circ$ is a product
of passing-test indicators and gauge-fixing factors.
It is nonnegative. At $\lambda=1$ the image at $t_1$
is $\nu_1^\bullet$, positive by \cref{C-406-63}; hence
$J_1^\bullet$ is positive as claimed.

For bounded Borel $f$, $J_\lambda^\bullet(f)$ is entire
in $\lambda$. Indeed the initial density is entire at
each configuration and uniformly bounded on each compact
parameter set. Dominated convergence and Morera's theorem
justify integration. By \cref{C-406-62},
\[
 H(\lambda)=e^{-E_k(0,\lambda)}J_\lambda^\bullet(f)
 \quad\hbox{satisfies}\quad
 |H(\lambda)|\le e^{(C+2)N_{[d']}},\quad |\lambda|<r_\lambda.
\]
Here the Berezin integral is bounded by the fibre norm
because $h_F\ge1$. Cauchy's estimate on discs centered
on $[0,1]$, with radii increasing to $r_\lambda-1$, gives
\[
 |H(1)-H(0)|\le\frac{e^{(C+2)N_{[d']}}}{r_\lambda-1}.
\]
The lower mass bound and
$x_k\le L^{d'}\mathsf b+\bar B\le L^{d'}X_g+\bar B$
make this at most $e_{d'}e^{-E_k}J_0^\bullet(1)$.
Apply \cref{C-406-61}(ii) to
$a=e^{-E_k}J_0^\bullet$ and
$cp=e^{-E_k(0,1)}J_1^\bullet$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Summing above the restart]\label{C-406-66}
Under the preceding conditions and $8R_{d'}\le1$, put
\[
 Q^\bullet=(\hat T^\bullet(0))^{-1}
       (\mathcal M^{s-d'})_*
               (\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet\hat F_0^\bullet\,dW).
\]
Then for Borel $0\le f\le1$,
\[
 \left|\frac{J_1^\bullet(f)}{J_1^\bullet(1)}-Q^\bullet(f)\right|
                                                      \le2R_{d'}.
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The exact image identity of \cref{C-424-20}, applied at
$\lambda=1$, sums the histories above $t_1^\bullet$ to
$(\mathcal M^{u-d'})_*\nu_1^\bullet$. Each summand is
positive: its weight factors over $\nu_1^\bullet$ as
in the preceding proof. Its mass is preserved by summing
its descendants. Thus removing $h'$ leaves a positive
measure, whose mass is the sum over final histories
having a large-field region at level $k$.
The marked estimate \cref{C-418-17}(B5) bounds this by
\[
 e^{-\theta_{\rm tl}A_0^2(\log(L^{d'}\mathsf b))^{2\mathfrak p_0}}
       e^{\operatorname{Re}E_{K^\bullet}(0,1)+(C+2)\ell^3}.
\]
Divide by the lower bound in \cref{C-406-63}.
The discarded fraction is at most $8R_{d'}/5\le1/5$.
By \cref{C-406-61}(i), normalization changes the integrals
by at most $2R_{d'}$. The normalized full image is
$Q^\bullet$, by the two identities in \cref{C-406-63}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The two restarted densities]\label{C-406-67}
At the cutoff-comparison thresholds,
\[
 \int_{\mathcal Y}
   |\hat{\mathsf k}^{\rm A}\hat F_0^{\rm A}
       -\hat{\mathsf k}^{\rm B}\hat F_0^{\rm B}|\,dW
                    \le\eta_K\hat T^{\rm A}(0).
\]
Consequently $|Q^{\rm A}(f)-Q^{\rm B}(f)|\le2\eta_K$
for $|f|\le1$, at every depth $d'\le s$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Insert the passing-test weights $\mathsf k^\bullet$ and
split the integrand into the two differences
$|\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet-\mathsf k^\bullet|\hat F_0^\bullet$
and the middle difference
$|\mathsf k^{\rm A}\hat F_0^{\rm A}-\mathsf k^{\rm B}\hat F_0^{\rm B}|$.
The first and last integrals are bounded by
$R^F\hat T^\bullet(0)$, by \cref{C-418-14}.
Where both weights are positive, they agree, and the
two densities differ by a factor $e^{\xi_0}$ with
$|\xi_0|\le\varepsilon:=\varepsilon_{\rm cl}+\varepsilon_F\le1/40$.
The corresponding integral is at most
$e^{1/40}(1+R^F)\varepsilon\hat T^{\rm A}(0)$.
Where only one weight is positive, the marked-tail
comparison in the proof of \cref{C-418-21} bounds its
mass by $\varepsilon_{\rm sh}\hat T^\bullet(0)/2$.
This estimate uses the nonnegative coefficients of the
mark polynomial and includes the $3sN_{[s]}$ test terms.

Let $D$ denote the integral to be bounded and
$b=R^F+\varepsilon_{\rm sh}/2<1/50$.
Since $\hat T^{\rm B}(0)\le\hat T^{\rm A}(0)+D$,
\[
 D\le\bigl(2b+e^{1/40}(1+R^F)\varepsilon\bigr)
                      \hat T^{\rm A}(0)+bD.
\]
Thus
$D\le\frac{50}{49}(2R^F+\varepsilon_{\rm sh}+1.04\varepsilon)
\hat T^{\rm A}(0)\le\eta_K\hat T^{\rm A}(0)$.
Both densities live on the same Haar space $\mathcal Y$
and use the same image map to depth $d'$. Apply
\cref{C-406-61}(iii); the cutoff thresholds give $\eta_K<1$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Summation and the compatible law}

\begin{proof}[Proof of \cref{C-406-68}]
Put $d'=d_K$ and first test at this depth. For a gauge-invariant
Borel $f\in[0,1]$, \cref{C-406-64} and
\cref{C-406-61}(i) compare the original law to the normalized
$J_0^\bullet$ with error at most $8R_{d'}/7$.
The next two lemmas give errors $4e_{d'}$ and $2R_{d'}$
in passing to $Q^\bullet$. The two restarted laws differ
by at most $2\eta_K$. Adding the three errors on each
lattice gives
\[
 2(8/7+2)R_{d'}+8e_{d'}+2\eta_K\le\tau_K.
\]
Gauge averaging proves the total-variation bound at
depth $d'$. Composing the test with $\mathcal M^{d'-d}$
proves it at every $d\le d'$.

We verify summability and the existence of the thresholds.
Since $d_K\ge\frac14\log_LK-1$ and $2\mathfrak p_0>1$,
\[
 R_{d_K}\le\mathsf M_{g,\ell}K^{-2}
\]
for all sufficiently large $K$. Moreover
$L^{d_K}\le K^{1/4}$ and $N_{[d_K]}\le\ell^3K^{3/4}$.
The interpolation-radius bound of \cref{C-418-23}, at
$n=1$, has the form
\[
 r_\lambda\ge c(K+1)^{-p_\Lambda}L^{a_1K},\qquad
 a_1=\left(1-\frac{1+c_\#}{10}\right)\frac{c_\#}{34}>0,
\]
where $c>0$ depends only on the fixed data. Hence
\[
 e_{d_K}\le C(K+1)^{p_\Lambda}
 \exp\left[(C+2+C_P(1+\log(K^{1/4}X_g+\bar B)))
                       \ell^3K^{3/4}-a_1K\log L\right].
\]
Its positive exponent is $o(K)$, so this is at most
$K^{-2}$ eventually. The same comparison estimates give
\[
 \begin{split}
 R^F&\le C e^{-cK^{2\mathfrak p_0}},\\
 \varepsilon_{\rm sh}&\le C(1+K L^{3K/34})e^{-cK^{2\mathfrak p_0}},\\
 \varepsilon_{\rm cl}&\le C K^{1/2}(K\log L+\log X_g)^{2\mathfrak p_0}
                                      L^{(7s-K)/2},\\
 \varepsilon_F&\le C\left[L^{5s-K}
           +(s\log L+\log X_g)^{\mathfrak p_0}L^{(29s-2K)/6}\right].
 \end{split}
\]
Here $s\le K/34+1$, so $7s-K\le7-27K/34$,
$5s-K\le5-29K/34$, and $29s-2K\le29-39K/34$.
Each of these four errors is eventually at most $K^{-2}$.
Also $d_K\le u-1$ eventually. This proves
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-tv-threshold}, all required cutoff
thresholds, and $\tau_K\le(8\mathsf M_{g,\ell}+26)K^{-2}$.
Every bound is uniform in the label rectangle.

For fixed $d$, telescope the adjacent-cutoff inequality
from $K$ to $K'>K$, with $K\ge L^{4d}$. Completeness
of the space of finite signed measures in variation norm,
and closedness of its probability measures, give a limit
$\mu_d^F$ and the asserted tail estimate. Gauge invariance
passes to this limit. Borel pushforward contracts total
variation, so consistency passes as well.
At fixed $K$ the normalized bare density is continuous
on the compact product of the label rectangle and the
link space, with positive normalization. It therefore
depends continuously on the labels in $L^1$. Its block
images are continuous in total variation, and their
uniform limit has the same property.

For each $D$, push $\mu_D^F$ to the coordinates through
$D$ by $V\mapsto(\mathcal M^{D-d}V)_{d\le D}$.
Consistency gives a projective family of probability
measures on compact metric spaces. The countable-product
extension theorem supplies its unique Borel probability
measure. Each relation $V_d=\mathcal MV_{d+1}$ is Borel
and has probability one; their countable intersection
does too.
For a continuous cylinder test on coordinates through
$D$, its expectation at cutoff $K\ge D$ is an integral
against $\mu_D^{F,K}$ of a bounded Borel function. Total
variation gives convergence even though the block map
need not be continuous. Continuous cylinder functions
are uniformly dense in the continuous functions on the
compact product, by Stone--Weierstrass. This proves weak
convergence of the cutoff laws and finishes the theorem.
\end{proof}

\section{Recovering parameters from block fields}\label{sec:qcdm2-parameters}

The mean and variance of a background action provide observables that recover the coupling and flavour number. We first establish the pure-gauge comparison, then compute the change caused by the fermion determinant.

\subsection{A background statistic under Wilson's measure}
\label{sec:qcdm2-pure-statistic}

We first establish the pure-gauge estimates used to distinguish
the coupling and flavour number. The statistic is the action
of the background determined by a block field. Its definition
is independent of the label at which the law is evaluated.
This independence will let us differentiate its mean.

Use the pure-gauge constants admitted in
\cite[Def.~10.19 and Prop.~10.20]{QCDM1}, including the
source and tail conditions for the small-field chain in
\cite[Sec.~115]{YMM1}. Fix $\ell=2L^m$ and
$J=[b_-,b_+]$ with
\[
 b_-\ge\gamma^{-2},\qquad MR(b_+)\le L^m.
\]
All constants in this subsection may depend on these data,
but not on $s\in J$, $K$ or $d$. The spaces of block fields
and their averaging map are those of \cref{C-406-60}.
Write $N_d=\ell^3L^{3d}$ and
\[
 O(U)=L^K\sum_pa_p(U),\qquad
 \nu^{\rm W}_{K,s}(dU)=Z_{K,s}^{-1}e^{-sO(U)}dU.
\]
The law of $V_d=\mathcal M^{K-d}U$ is denoted by
$\mu^{\rm W,K}_d[s]$.

\begin{definition}[The background statistic]\label{C-375-7}
Let $d_\natural\ge1$ be the least integer with
$L^{d_\natural}b_-\ge\mathsf t_\natural$, the lower threshold
for the field cuts. For $K>d\ge d_\natural$ put $t=K-d$.
On $\{\varpi(V)<\bar\varepsilon\}$ let $U_t(V)$ be a
background over $V$: a regular critical point of the Wilson
action on $\{U:\mathcal M^tU=V\}$. Backgrounds form one
orbit of the gauge transformations preserving this fibre.
Thus their Wilson actions agree. Define
\begin{align*}
 \operatorname{In}_t[s]
   &=\{V:\varpi(V)<2\varepsilon(L^ds)\},\\
 \operatorname{Cut}_t[s]
   &=\{V:\varpi(V)<\bar\varepsilon,\quad
          L^{2t}\varpi(U_t(V))<c_\rho\varepsilon(L^ds)\},\\
 T_d^K(V)&=O(U_t(V))1_{\operatorname{Cut}_t[b_-]}(V),\\
 X_{K,d,s}&=\mathsf E_{K,s}
       (O-\mathsf E_{K,s}O\mid V_d).
\end{align*}
Here $\varepsilon(x)=A_0x^{-1/2}(\log x)^{\mathfrak p_0}$,
and $\varpi$ is the largest plaquette deviation from the
identity. The product in the definition of $T_d^K$ means
that the function is zero off the cut; no background is
chosen there.
\end{definition}

The background and cut properties used here are those of
\cite[Prop.~52.3 and Lem.~113.10]{YMM1}. In particular the cuts
are open and gauge invariant, the background action is
continuous on its domain, and
\[
 \operatorname{In}_t[s]\subset\operatorname{Cut}_t[s]
                  \subset\operatorname{Cut}_t[b_-].
\]
The last inclusion follows because $\varepsilon$ decreases
on $[\gamma^{-2},\infty)$. Consequently $T_d^K$ is Borel,
gauge invariant and independent of $s$.

\begin{proposition}[Variance of the conditional action]\label{C-375-8}
There are $d_{\rm G}\ge2$, $K_{\rm G}$, $K_T$ and $Q'>0$
such that, for $s\in J$ and $K>d\ge d_{\rm G}$,
\begin{align}
 0\le T_d^K&\le Q'L^{4d},\label{eq:qcdm2-statistic-bound}\\
 \left|\mathsf E_{K,s}X_{K,d,s}^2-3s^{-2}N_d\right|
       &\le K_{\rm G}L^{-d/3}N_d,
       \label{eq:qcdm2-pure-conditional-variance}\\
 \mathsf E_{K,s}|X_{K,d,s}-(T_d^K-c_s)|^2
       &\le K_TL^{-d/3}N_d
       \label{eq:qcdm2-pure-statistic-approximation}
\end{align}
for a real number $c_s=c_s(K,d)$. The bound
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-statistic-bound} holds for every
$K>d\ge d_\natural$.
\end{proposition}

The coefficient $3$ counts the Gaussian directions integrated
at each step. To recover it for the conditional action, we
compare the flow between depths $d$ and $d'$ with flows
started with zero earlier terms. A second comparison, using
three choices of the source in the earlier terms, controls
their contribution in $L^2$.

\subsubsection{Earlier terms on a small background}

Fix $s\in J$ for the moment. At level $t$ write $u=K-t$,
$x_t=L^us$ and
\[
 \epsilon_u^\sharp=\frac{2c_\rho\varepsilon(L^us)}
                              {\varepsilon_{\mathcal W}},
 \quad \Xi_u=\frac{c_A\alpha_0}{M\epsilon_u^\sharp},
 \quad \Xi'_u=\frac{L^{m+u}}{2M}.
\]
The constants $c_A,C_A$ are those of the quadratic bound
for an earlier local term, and $\varepsilon_{\mathcal W}$
is the radius in the background theorem
\cite[Prop.~52.3]{YMM1}. The entropy constants are
$C_{E,p}=2048\sum_{n\ge0}(n+2)^pe^{-n}$.
Set
\begin{align*}
 k_u^\sharp
 &=C_AM^2C_{E,2}(\epsilon_u^\sharp/\alpha_0)^2
        +2C_{E,0}(e^{1-\Xi_u}+e^{3-\Xi'_u}),\\
 m_u^\sharp&=k_u^\sharp\frac L{L-1}E_0N_u.
\end{align*}
These are independent of the source. Uniformly for $s\in J$,
$m_u^\sharp=O((1+u)^{2\mathfrak p_0}L^{-u})N_u$.

\begin{lemma}[Earlier actions at a background]\label{C-375-19}
For $V\in\operatorname{Cut}_t[s]$ and $\Xi_u\ge2$,
an array of earlier families $D^{(i)}$, $1\le i\le t$,
with zero counterterms and empty slot satisfies
\[
 |S[D](U_t(V))|
 \le k_u^\sharp N_u\sum_{i=1}^t
             L^{-(t-i)}\|D^{(i)}\|_{i,\kappa+1}.
\]
In particular the earlier action of the chain is bounded
by $m_u^\sharp$ on the full source disc.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The background theorem at radius $\epsilon_u^\sharp$
puts $U_t(V)$ in its regularity class. At level $i=t-l$
its radius is $\epsilon_u^\sharp L^{-2l}$. In the sum
\[
 S[D](U)=\sum_{i,z}\sum_{X\ni z}
       \bigl(D^{(i)}(X,U,z)-D^{(i)}(X,\mathbf1,z)\bigr),
\]
call $X$ short if
$1+d_i(X)\le\Xi_uL^{2l}$ and
$1+d_i(X)<\Xi'_uL^l-2/M$.
Such a domain does not wrap around the torus. The quadratic
bound \cite[Eq.~(2261) and its proof]{YMM1} gives
\[
 |D^{(i)}(X,U,z)-D^{(i)}(X,\mathbf1,z)|
 \le C_A\|D^{(i)}\|_{i,\kappa+1}e^{-(\kappa+1)d_i(X)}
   (\epsilon_u^\sharp/\alpha_0)^2L^{-4l}M^2(1+d_i(X))^2.
\]
Entropy and the $L^{3l}N_u$ sites give the first term of
$k_u^\sharp L^{-l}N_u\|D^{(i)}\|$.
For the other domains use twice the norm and the entropy
tail at
$D_l=\min\{\Xi_uL^{2l},\Xi'_uL^l-2/M\}-1$.
Since $\Xi_u\ge2$ and $\Xi'_u\ge4$,
\[
 L^{4l}e^{-D_l}\le e^{1-\Xi_u}+e^{3-\Xi'_u}.
\]
This gives the second term. Sum over $i$; the chain has
$\|E^{(i)}\|_{i,\kappa+1}\le E_0$. Finally
$\varepsilon(L^us)^2=O((1+u)^{2\mathfrak p_0}L^{-u})$
and $e^{-x}\le2x^{-2}$ give the asserted decay.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The trivial background]\label{C-375-20}
At the trivial block field the background can be chosen
to be $\mathbf1$. Every weighted Wilson action and every
earlier action $S[D]$ vanish at all backgrounds over it.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The background can be chosen
to be $\mathbf1$: averaging preserves $\mathbf1$, which
minimizes the nonnegative Wilson action on its fibre.
Every other background over it is gauge equivalent to it.
Thus every weighted Wilson action and every earlier action
$S[D]$ vanish there, including arrays with counterterms
and a slot. In the local-term formula each bracket is a
value minus itself.
\end{proof}
We will use this fact when evaluating the scalar
normalization of a step.

\subsubsection{Conditional means and the discarded fields}

Let $\varrho>0$ denote the pure-gauge source radius. In this
subsection the source is the constant $z$, $|z|<2\varrho$.
Let $E^{(i)}[z]$ be the chain families and set
\[
\begin{gathered}
c_t(z)=\sum_{i=1}^t c_i^{\rm step}(z),\\
 \psi_t(z,V)=S[(E^{(i)}[z],0)_{i\le t}](U_t(V)),
 \\
 \varphi_t(z,V)=zO(U_t(V))+\psi_t(z,V)-\psi_t(0,V).
\end{gathered}
\]
The ordinary bound on earlier actions gives
$|\psi_t|\le C_{\rm old}LE_0N_u/(L-1)$; the preceding
lemma improves this to $m_u^\sharp$ when $\Xi_u\ge2$.
We choose $Q'$ large enough that
\[
 Q'\ge\max\left\{\varrho^{-1},\,
 \tfrac32c_\rho^2\ell^3\sup_{u\ge1}\varepsilon(L^us)^2,\,
 \varrho^{-1}C_{\rm old}\tfrac L{L-1}E_0\ell^3\right\},
 \qquad Q''=\max\{2Q',6\ell^3\}.
\]
The field-cut action bound proves
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-statistic-bound}. All these choices can
be made uniformly on $J$.

The discarding estimate \cite[Prop.~115.2]{YMM1} gives
\[
 \rho(u)=Q_\ell L^{3u}e^{-\theta_0u^2},\qquad
 \theta_0=c'A_0^2(\log L)^{2\mathfrak p_0},
\]
where one may take
\[
 Q_\ell=2M^{-3}\ell^3
   \exp[(C^\Sigma_{\rm maj}+2+c_{\rm low}
                              +\tfrac92\log s)\ell^3].
\]
Increase a depth $u_\flat\ge d_\natural$ so that $\rho$
decreases and is at most $1/4$ above it. Put
\begin{align*}
 \omega_q(d)&=\sum_{u\ge d}(u-d+1)L^{4q(u+1)}\rho(u),\\
 \eta(d,d')&=1152\bigl(\omega_3(d)+L^{8d}\rho(d')\bigr),\\
 C_1&=\varrho^{-2}E_0
           \left(C_{E,0}L^{-3}+\tfrac12C_{\rm old}\tfrac L{L-1}\right),\\
 \eta_1(d,d')&=2\rho(d')\bigl(C_1N_d+43Q'^2L^{8d'}\bigr)
                                      +Q''^2\eta(d,d').
\end{align*}
Both $L^{cd}\omega_q(d)$ and
$L^{cd}\rho(\lceil d/3\rceil)$ tend to zero for every fixed $c$.

\begin{lemma}[Two depths of the small-field chain]\label{C-375-21}
For $u_\flat\le d'<d<K$, set $t=K-d$ and $t'=K-d'$.
There are positive probability measures $\tilde\nu$ on
$\operatorname{Cut}_t[s]$ and $\hat\nu$ on
$\operatorname{In}_{t'}[s]$ such that, with
\[
 Y=\partial_z\varphi_t(0,\cdot),\quad
 \tilde Y=Y-\tilde\nu(Y),\quad
 Y_2=\partial_z^2\psi_t(0,\cdot),
\]
extended by zero before centering off their cut,
$\tilde Y$ is real almost everywhere for $\tilde\nu$ and
\begin{align}
 \tilde\nu(\tilde Y^2)
    &=c_{t,t'}''(0)+(\operatorname{Log}\hat J)''(0)
                                      -\tilde\nu(Y_2),
       \label{eq:qcdm2-two-depth-variance}\\
 |(\operatorname{Log}\hat J)''(0)|&\le43Q'^2L^{8d'},\qquad
 \tilde\nu(\tilde Y^2)\le C_1N_d+43Q'^2L^{8d'},
       \label{eq:qcdm2-top-source-bound}\\
 |\mathsf E_{K,s}X_{K,d,s}^2-\tilde\nu(\tilde Y^2)|
       &\le\eta_1(d,d'),
       \label{eq:qcdm2-descent-variance}\\
 \int|X_{K,d,s}-\operatorname{Re}\tilde Y|^2
                                      d\mu^{\rm W,K}_d[s]
       &\le\eta_1(d,d')+Q''^2\eta(d,d').
       \label{eq:qcdm2-descent-square}
\end{align}
Here $\hat J(z)=\hat\nu(e^{\varphi_{t'}(z)})$ and
\[
 c_{t,t'}(z)=\sum_{t<j\le t'}\sum_{X,z'\in X}
                               E^{(j)}[z](X,\mathbf1,z').
\]
The same estimate for the conditional variance at $d=K$
holds with $c_{0,t'}''(0)$ and error
$43Q'^2L^{8d'}+12Q''^2L^{8d}\rho(d')$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The small-field weight $w_j\ge0$ is the product of the
field-cut factors through level $j-1$ and
$1_{\operatorname{In}_j[s]}(\mathcal M^jU)$. For nonnegative
gauge-invariant $F$, the discarding theorem gives
\[
 \int Fw_je^{-sO}\,dU\le\int Fe^{-sO}\,dU,
 \qquad
 0\le Z-\int w_je^{-sO}\,dU\le\rho(K-j)Z.
\]
The weighted mass is positive. Indeed its image at level $j$
has an exponential density on the nonempty open set
$\operatorname{In}_j[s]$. Positivity of the image makes that
density positive almost everywhere on this set.
The normalized unweighted functional is a convex combination
of the normalized weighted functional and a positive
functional of mass one. Thus inserting $w_j$ changes a
bounded mean by at most $2\rho(K-j)\|F\|_\infty$ and a
second cumulant by at most
$6\rho(K-j)\|F_1\|_\infty\|F_2\|_\infty$.

Factor $w_{t'}$ into the factors below $t$ and a Borel
function $H_{t,t'}(\mathcal M^tU)$ of the later block fields.
The latter has no source dependence. The recursion of the
chain \cite[Prop.~114.2]{YMM1} gives the exact identity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-pure-source-image}
 \int G(\mathcal M^tU)w_{t'}e^{-sO+zO}\,dU
 =e^{c_t(z)-c_t(0)}
       \int G(V)e^{\varphi_t(z,V)}\,d\sigma_{t,t'}(V),
\end{equation}
where
\[
 \sigma_{t,t'}=(\mathcal M^t)_*(w_{t'}e^{-sO}dU)
   =e^{c_t(0)}1_{\operatorname{Cut}_t[s]}
                       H_{t,t'}e^{\Phi_t^0}\,dV.
\]
Normalize this measure to obtain $\tilde\nu$; the analogous
image at $t'$ gives $\hat\nu$. The masses coincide and are
positive. The source results
\cite[Lems.~114.5--114.6]{YMM1} give holomorphy on
$|z|<2\varrho$ and
\[
 |c_{t,t'}(z)|\le2E_0C_{E,0}L^{-3}N_d.
\]
The difference $c_{t'}-c_t-c_{t,t'}$ has no source dependence.
At $G=1$, the two readings of the left side of
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-pure-source-image} therefore yield
\[
 \tilde\nu(e^{\varphi_t(z)})
       =e^{c_{t,t'}(z)-c_{t,t'}(0)}\hat J(z).
\]
Differentiating twice proves \eqref{eq:qcdm2-two-depth-variance}.
The first derivative of \eqref{eq:qcdm2-pure-source-image},
tested against the imaginary part of $c_t'(0)+Y$, shows
that this function is real almost everywhere for
$\sigma_{t,t'}$. Hence $\tilde Y$ is real.

The source bound at $t'$ gives $|\varphi_{t'}|\le1/4$ on
$|z|<(8Q'L^{4d'})^{-1}$. Consequently
$|\hat J-1|\le e^{1/4}-1$ and
$|\operatorname{Log}\hat J|<0.3343$ there. Cauchy's inequality
gives $2(0.3343)(8Q'L^{4d'})^2<43Q'^2L^{8d'}$.
Apply Cauchy's inequality also to $c_{t,t'}$ and $\psi_t$
on the disc of radius $2\varrho$ to obtain the second
bound in \eqref{eq:qcdm2-top-source-bound}.

We give the descent argument because the bound
$|O|\le6\ell^3L^{4K}$ alone would not be uniform in $K$.
Write $a=X_{K,d,s}$ and
$Y^{(j)}=\partial_z\varphi_j(0)$, extended by zero off
$\operatorname{Cut}_j[s]$; put $Y^{(0)}=O$ and $w_0=1$.
Cauchy's inequality gives
$|Y^{(j)}|\le Q''L^{4(K-j)}$.
Differentiate \eqref{eq:qcdm2-pure-source-image} at adjacent
levels. Under $w_{i+1}$ the cumulants of $F(V_d)$ with
$Y^{(i)}$ and with $Y^{(i+1)}$ agree. Comparing consecutive
weights and summing gives
\[
 \left|\int Fa\,d\mu^{\rm W,K}_d[s]
      -\operatorname{cum}_{w_j}(F(V_d),Y^{(j)})\right|
 \le\delta_j\|F\|_\infty,
 \quad
 \delta_j=24Q''\sum_{u=K-j}^{K-1}\rho(u)L^{4(u+1)}.
\]
This holds for $j\le t$. At $j=t$, change the weight once
more to $w_{t'}$. The right side is then
$\delta_*\|F\|_\infty$, where
\[
 \delta_*\le24Q''\bigl(\omega_1(d)+\rho(d')L^{4d}\bigr),
\]
and the weighted cumulant is $\tilde\nu(F\tilde Y)$.

For $\lambda\ge8Q''L^{4(K-j)}$, use
$F=1_{\{\pm a>\lambda\}}$. Weighted probabilities are at
most $(1-\rho)^{-1}\le2$ times unweighted probabilities.
Absorbing the cumulant term gives
$\mu^{\rm W,K}_d[s](|a|>\lambda)\le4\delta_j/\lambda$.
The shells
\[
 8Q''L^{4u}<|a|\le8Q''L^{4(u+1)},\qquad d\le u<K,
\]
therefore satisfy
\[
 \int a^2 1_{\{|a|>8Q''L^{4d}\}}\,d\mu^{\rm W,K}_d[s]
                      \le768Q''^2\omega_3(d).
\]
On the complementary set put $F=a1_{\{|a|\le\Lambda\}}$,
$\Lambda=8Q''L^{4d}$, and $x^2=\int F^2d\mu^{\rm W,K}_d[s]$.
Cauchy--Schwarz and the descent give $x^2\le Ax+B_2$, with
\[
 A^2=(1-\rho(d'))^{-1}\tilde\nu(\tilde Y^2),\qquad
 B_2=192Q''^2\bigl(\omega_2(d)+L^{8d}\rho(d')\bigr).
\]
Hence $x^2\le A^2+2B_2$. Since
$2\cdot192+768=1152$ and $(1-\rho)^{-1}\le1+2\rho$,
\[
 \int a^2d\mu^{\rm W,K}_d[s]
 \le(1+2\rho(d'))\tilde\nu(\tilde Y^2)+Q''^2\eta(d,d').
\]
Finally apply the descent to $F=\operatorname{Re}\tilde Y$
and the weight comparison to $F^2$. Expanding
$\int(a-F)^2$ gives
\[
 \int(a-F)^2d\mu^{\rm W,K}_d[s]
 \le2\rho(d')\tilde\nu(\tilde Y^2)+2Q''^2\eta(d,d').
\]
The same expansion bounds the variance from below. Together
with \eqref{eq:qcdm2-top-source-bound} these prove
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-descent-variance}--\eqref{eq:qcdm2-descent-square}.
For $d=K$, compare the variance of $O$ directly under the
original and weighted laws, then use the identity at $t'$.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{The Gaussian count and cancellation of earlier sources}

\begin{lemma}[The constant source at one step]\label{C-375-22}
At level $k$, put $u=K-k$. Let $T_k(z)$ be the scalar
constant of the step started with zero earlier terms,
with its source-independent part removed. It is holomorphic
on $|z|<2\varrho$. The following identity holds on
$|z|<\min\{2\varrho,\sigma_\star s\}$, and its remainder
$r_k$ is holomorphic on the larger disc $|z|<\sigma_\star s$:
\begin{align}
 T_k(z)-T_k(0)
 &=-3(N_u-N_{u-1})\operatorname{Log}(1-z/s)
                                      +r_k(z)-r_k(0),
       \label{eq:qcdm2-gauge-normalizer}\\
 |r_k(z)|&\le C_{E,0}\epsilon_u^FN_{u-1},\qquad
 \epsilon_u^F=K_M^f\left(\delta(L^us)
                +e^{-\gamma_2\mathfrak b(L^us)^2/2}\right),
       \quad |z|<\sigma_\star s.
       \label{eq:qcdm2-gauge-normalizer-error}
\end{align}
For the actual chain,
\[
 |(c_{k+1}^{\rm step})''(0)-3s^{-2}(N_u-N_{u-1})|
       \le C(1+u)^{\mathfrak p_0}L^{-u/2}N_u.
\]
The latter bound is uniform over systems of earlier terms
of size at most $E_0$, holomorphic and local in the source.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The constant source changes the action coefficient from
$x_k=L^us$ to $x=x_k(1-z/s)$; the cut and gauge fixing
remain at $x_k$. The complex-coefficient step is
\cite[Thms.~V--W, Eqs.~(898), (924)]{YMM1}.
Evaluate it at the trivial block
field, where every earlier action vanishes. The Gaussian
normalization has exponent
\[
 \tfrac12 n_{\mathcal O}-\tfrac32\#\mathfrak X^+,
 \qquad n_{\mathcal O}=\#\mathfrak X^+=3(N_u-N_{u-1}).
\]
It is therefore $-3(N_u-N_{u-1})\operatorname{Log}(x/x_k)$.
Equivalently there are $6(N_u-N_{u-1})$ integrated
directions after gauge fixing; this is the dimension count
and logarithm in \cite[Sec.~52.3, Eq.~(910)]{YMM1}.
The one-step estimate on
$|x-x_k|<\sigma_\star x_k$ bounds each remaining local
term by $\epsilon_u^Fe^{-(1+4\beta_s)\kappa d(X)}$.
Entropy and the $N_{u-1}$ sites give
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-gauge-normalizer-error}. The logarithms
agree up to a constant multiple of $2\pi i$, which
disappears on subtracting their values at zero.

For completeness, the effect of earlier terms is
quantitative. The one-step Lipschitz estimate
\cite[Prop.~114.3]{YMM1} bounds the difference of the
output families by
$K^dK_\Lambda\mathsf s_k\sum_{i\le k}L^{-(k-i)}\Delta_i$.
Against the zero start, $\Delta_i\le E_0$ and
\[
 K^dK_\Lambda\mathsf s_k\frac L{L-1}
       \le\frac{13}{72}L^{-u/2}(1+uc_{\log})^{\mathfrak p_0}.
\]
The scalar difference is the sum of this family at the
trivial field; the normalizations agree. Entropy followed
by Cauchy's inequality on $|z|<2\varrho$ bounds its second
derivative by
\[
 \frac{13E_0C_{E,0}}{144\varrho^2L^3}
       N_uL^{-u/2}(1+uc_{\log})^{\mathfrak p_0}.
\]
Cauchy's inequality on $|z|<\sigma_\star s$ bounds the
second derivative of $r_k$ by
$2C_{E,0}\epsilon_u^F(\sigma_\star s)^{-2}N_{u-1}$.
These two bounds prove the assertion, since
$\epsilon_u^F=O((1+u)^{\mathfrak p_0}L^{-u/2})$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Three choices of the earlier source]\label{C-375-23}
In \cref{C-375-21}, suppose also $\Xi_d\ge2$ and write
\[
 \tilde Y=\tilde A+P,\qquad
 \tilde A=O(U_t)-\tilde\nu(O(U_t)),\quad
 P=\partial_z\psi_t(0)-\tilde\nu(\partial_z\psi_t(0)).
\]
Put $v_{\rm cl}=\sum_{k=t}^{t'-1}T_k''(0)$ and
\[
 e_I=\frac{13E_0C_{E,0}}{144\varrho^2L^3}
       \sum_{u=d'+1}^dN_uL^{-u/2}(1+uc_{\log})^{\mathfrak p_0}
          +43Q'^2L^{8d'}+\frac{m_d^\sharp}{2\varrho^2}.
\]
For $\theta=1,0,-1$,
\[
 |\tilde\nu((\tilde A+\theta P)^2)-v_{\rm cl}|\le e_I.
\]
Consequently $\tilde\nu(P^2)\le2e_I$,
$|\tilde\nu(\tilde AP)|\le e_I/2$, and
\[
 \int|X_{K,d,s}-\tilde A|^2d\mu^{\rm W,K}_d[s]
 \le4e_I+8\rho(d')(m_d^\sharp/\varrho)^2
                      +2\eta_1+2Q''^2\eta.
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Run the flow above $t$ with earlier families
$E^{(i)}[\theta z]$, $i\le t$. These are admissible earlier
families: the source disc is invariant under multiplication
by $\theta$, and their norm, locality and holomorphy are
unchanged. All three flows agree at $z=0$. The factor
$H_{t,t'}$ is independent of the source and factors over
the intermediate levels. Applying the flow recursion and
dividing by its positive value at zero therefore gives
\[
 \tilde\nu\left(e^{zO(U_t)+\psi_t(\theta z)-\psi_t(0)}\right)
     =e^{c^\theta_{t,t'}(z)-c^\theta_{t,t'}(0)}\hat J_\theta(z).
\]
The source estimate at $t'$ gives
$|(\operatorname{Log}\hat J_\theta)''(0)|\le43Q'^2L^{8d'}$,
for every $\theta$. Differentiating twice yields
\[
 \tilde\nu((\tilde A+\theta P)^2)
 =(c^\theta_{t,t'})''(0)
      +(\operatorname{Log}\hat J_\theta)''(0)
      -\theta^2\tilde\nu(Y_2).
\]
The preceding one-step comparison bounds the first term's
difference from $v_{\rm cl}$ by the sum in $e_I$.
The earlier-action bound and Cauchy's inequality give
$|\tilde\nu(Y_2)|\le m_d^\sharp/(2\varrho^2)$.
This proves the first assertion. The identities
\[
 P^2=\tfrac12((\tilde A+P)^2+(\tilde A-P)^2)-\tilde A^2,
 \qquad
 4\tilde AP=(\tilde A+P)^2-(\tilde A-P)^2
\]
cancel $v_{\rm cl}$. The centered function $\tilde Y$
is real for the common positive law by \cref{C-375-21}.
Since $\tilde A$ is real, so are $P=\tilde Y-\tilde A$
and $\tilde A+\theta P$. Finally $|P|\le m_d^\sharp/\varrho$.
Changing from the weighted law costs at most
$4\rho(d')\sup|P|^2$; combine this with
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-descent-square} and
$|a+b|^2\le2|a|^2+2|b|^2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of \cref{C-375-8}]
Choose all bounds uniformly over $s\in J$. In the discarding
bound use $b_+$; in the field radii and inverse powers of
$s$ use $b_-$. These choices cover the same cuts and source
discs throughout the interval.

Sum \cref{C-375-22} from $t=K-d$ to $t'=K-d'$. The main
terms telescope to $3s^{-2}(N_d-N_{d'})$. By
\cref{C-375-19,C-375-21}, the difference from
$\mathsf E_{K,s}X_{K,d,s}^2$ is at most
\[
 \frac{m_d^\sharp}{2\varrho^2}+43Q'^2L^{8d'}+\eta_1(d,d')
  +C\sum_{u=d'+1}^d(1+u)^{\mathfrak p_0}L^{-u/2}N_u.
\]
Add $3b_-^{-2}N_{d'}$ and take $d'=\lceil d/3\rceil$.
After division by $N_d$, the endpoint term is
$O(L^{-d/3})$, the earlier-action term is
$O((1+d)^{2\mathfrak p_0}L^{-d})$, the sum is
$O((1+d)^{\mathfrak p_0}L^{-d/2})$, and the discarded terms
decay faster than any fixed power of $L^{-d}$.
This proves \eqref{eq:qcdm2-pure-conditional-variance}.

By \cref{C-375-23}, the conditional action differs in
$L^2$ from the centered background action on
$\operatorname{Cut}_t[s]$ by $O(L^{-d/3})N_d$.
The weighted law at $t$ is carried by
$\operatorname{In}_t[s]$, so discarding gives
\[
 \mu^{\rm W,K}_d[s](\operatorname{In}_t[s]^c)\le\rho(d).
\]
The statistic $T_d^K$ differs from that background action
only in $\operatorname{Cut}_t[b_-]\setminus
\operatorname{Cut}_t[s]$, outside this inner set.
Its additional squared error is at most
$2Q'^2L^{8d}\rho(d)$. This proves
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-pure-statistic-approximation}, with
$c_s=\tilde\nu(O(U_t))$. Increasing $d_{\rm G}$ ensures
$d'\ge u_\flat$ and $\Xi_d\ge2$ throughout.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The pure-gauge block laws}\label{sec:qcdm2-pure-block-laws}

We use the same configuration spaces and Borel averaging
map for the pure-gauge comparison. The estimate below
follows from the comparison of weighted densities in
\cite[Prop.~116.1 and its proof]{YMM1}. We give the passage
to arbitrary Borel tests, which is needed for the statistic
$T_d^K$.

\begin{proposition}[Pure-gauge block laws]\label{C-375-24}
In the setting of \cref{C-375-7}, there are $C_{\rm bf}$
and $K_{\rm bf}$, uniform over $s\in J$, such that, for
$K\ge K_{\rm bf}$ and $0\le d\le\lceil K/1260\rceil$,
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(\mu_d^{\rm W,K+1}[s],\mu_d^{\rm W,K}[s])
      \le C_{\rm bf}\ell^3K^{2\mathfrak p_0+1/2}L^{-K/10}.
\]
Here and below $\operatorname{TV}(\mu,\nu)=\sup_E|\mu(E)-\nu(E)|$.
For each $d$, these laws converge in total variation to
a Borel probability measure $\mu_d^{\rm W}[s]$, uniformly
over $s\in J$, with error at most
\[
 \tau_J(K)=C_{\rm bf}\ell^3
                 \sum_{j\ge K}j^{2\mathfrak p_0+1/2}L^{-j/10}
\]
under the same depth condition. The limits satisfy
$\mathcal M_*\mu_{d+1}^{\rm W}[s]=\mu_d^{\rm W}[s]$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Use the two lattices $(\ell,K)$ and $(\ell,K+1)$, put
$u=\lceil K/1260\rceil$ and $v=\lceil K/9\rceil$, and
take the constant auxiliary test $1$ at zero source in
the comparison of \cite[Sec.~116]{YMM1}. For a bounded
gauge-invariant Borel function $F$ at depth $d\le u$,
replace it by $F\circ\mathcal M^{u-d}$ at depth $u$.
This preserves its supremum bound and gauge invariance.
It therefore suffices to work at $d=u$.

For either lattice let $\Lambda_0$ be the unnormalized
Wilson expectation of $F(V_u)$, $\Lambda_1$ its expectation
with the small-field weight through depth $u$, and
$\Lambda_2$ the expectation obtained by starting at depth
$v$ with zero earlier terms and running to depth $u$.
All three are positive functionals of positive mass.
For $\Lambda_1$ this follows from the history image
identity. For $\Lambda_2$ it follows from the positive
start and positive chart kernels; its final exponential
density is nonzero on the common inner set, an open
set containing the identity.

There are three comparisons. First, discarding gives
$0\le\Lambda_0-\Lambda_1$ and
$(\Lambda_0-\Lambda_1)(1)\le R\Lambda_0(1)$.
For $R\le1/2$, their normalized means differ by at most
$4R\|F\|_\infty$.
Second, the two densities of the chain and the zero
start on the final inner set are
$p_1=e^ce^\Phi$ and $p_2=e^{\hat c}e^{\hat\Phi}$.
The forgetting bound is
$|\Phi-\hat\Phi|\le\epsilon_{\rm fg}\le1/8$.
Since both densities are positive almost everywhere,
\[
 |p_1-\varkappa p_2|
      \le(e^{\epsilon_{\rm fg}}-1)\varkappa p_2,
      \qquad \varkappa=|e^{c-\hat c}|>0.
\]
Normalization cancels $\varkappa$ and costs at most
$5\epsilon_{\rm fg}\|F\|_\infty$.

Third, write the two zero-start functionals on the common
configuration space at depth $v$. With $W_u$ the block
field obtained by averaging $W$ down to depth $u$, they
are integrals of $F(W_u)k^\bullet(W)\hat F^\bullet_0(W)$.
The proof of \cite[Prop.~116.1]{YMM1} gives
\[
 \int|k^A\hat F^A_0-k^B\hat F^B_0|\,dW
      \le(2\epsilon_{\rm cl}+3\epsilon_{\rm sh})\Lambda_2^A(1).
\]
This is an estimate of the densities, so it applies to
bounded Borel $F$. When
$2\epsilon_{\rm cl}+3\epsilon_{\rm sh}\le1/4$,
the normalized means differ by at most
$(8\epsilon_{\rm cl}+12\epsilon_{\rm sh})\|F\|_\infty$.
Combining the five comparisons from the original law
on one lattice through both zero starts to the original
law on the other gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-pure-block-increment}
 |\mu_u^{\rm W,K+1}[s](F)-\mu_u^{\rm W,K}[s](F)|
 \le(8R+12\epsilon_{\rm fg}+8\epsilon_{\rm cl}
                             +12\epsilon_{\rm sh})\|F\|_\infty.
\end{equation}
The normalization estimates just used follow directly
by writing the difference of two ratios: if
$|\Lambda'(F)-\Lambda(F)|\le\epsilon\Lambda(1)\|F\|_\infty$
and $\epsilon\le1/2$, their normalized difference is at
most $4\epsilon\|F\|_\infty$.

The bounds of \cite[Sec.~116, proof of Thm.~AR]{YMM1}
are uniform on $J$. They give
\begin{align*}
 12\epsilon_{\rm fg}
 &\le12C_{\rm old}C_{\rm fg}\tfrac L{L-1}E_0L^4
                                             \ell^3L^{-K/10},\\
 8\epsilon_{\rm cl}
 &\le32K_wc_\rho^2A_0^2(1+2\varrho/b_-)
       (\log(Lb_+))^{2\mathfrak p_0}L^{7/2}
                         \ell^3K^{2\mathfrak p_0+1/2}L^{-K/9}.
\end{align*}
The other two errors decay faster than any exponential
in $K$. Increase a common $K_{\rm bf}$ to ensure all
comparison smallness conditions and to absorb these
errors into the same majorant. This proves the claimed
increment for gauge-invariant tests.

Each block law is gauge invariant. For any Borel set $E$
on its finite product of compact groups, the gauge average
\[
 \bar1_E(V)=\int1_E(V^h)\,dh
\]
is Borel, gauge invariant, between zero and one, and
has the same integral as $1_E$. Applying
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-pure-block-increment} to $\bar1_E$ gives
the estimate for all Borel sets. The increments are
summable uniformly on $J$. Their sum is a finite signed
measure in total variation, so the Cauchy sequence has
a countably additive limit; positivity and mass one
pass to the limit. Summing the increments gives
$\tau_J(K)$. Finally pushforward by a Borel map contracts
total variation. Apply this to the finite-cutoff identity
$\mathcal M_*\mu_{d+1}^{\rm W,K}=\mu_d^{\rm W,K}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The pure-gauge thread law]\label{C-375-25}
There is a unique Borel probability measure
$\mu^{\rm W}_{\rm thr}[s]$ on
$\prod_{d\ge0}\mathcal V_{[d]}$ whose first $d+1$
coordinates have the law
\[
 (V\mapsto(\mathcal M^dV,\ldots,\mathcal MV,V))_*
                                      \mu_d^{\rm W}[s].
\]
It is carried by $V_d=\mathcal MV_{d+1}$ for every $d$.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
The finite-dimensional laws are consistent by
\cref{C-375-24}. Kolmogorov's extension theorem on these
compact metric spaces gives existence and uniqueness.
The graph of $\mathcal M$ is Borel, and each compatibility
identity has probability one. Their countable intersection
therefore has probability one.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Variance of the background statistic with fermions}
\label{sec:qcdm2-matter-statistic}

We now estimate the same statistic under the gauge law with
fermions. The proof groups histories by the first level at
which a large-field region appears. On each remaining
small-field portion, an exponential of $T_d^K$ changes one
running coefficient. Holomorphy controls that change; the
large-field bound makes the sum over portions convergent.

For this subsection take the constants of
\cref{sec:qcdm2-setting}, with the additional history mark
\[
 (\mathsf w,c_a,C_{\rm vol},c_{\rm Dep})
                      =(1/2,0,0,c_\star),\qquad\eth=1/2,
\]
chosen before $\gamma$, and impose the associated ceiling
on $\gamma$ in the partition lower bound of
\cite[Thm.~E]{QCDM1}.
Fix $0<g\le\gamma$, $\ell=2L^m\in\mathfrak L(g)$,
$b\in\bar I(g)$ and $\mathsf m\in[m_-,m_+]$.
In \cref{C-375-7}, one may replace $b_-$ by any
$b_\flat\in[\gamma^{-2},b]$ with $MR(b_\flat)\le L^m$,
and $d_\natural$ by any $n\ge1$ satisfying
$L^nb_\flat\ge\mathsf t_\natural$.
This defines the same $T_d^K$ at that lower label.

\begin{lemma}[Two exponential bounds]\label{C-406-57}
Let $\nu$ be a positive measure of mass at most one and
$X$ a real measurable function. Suppose $s,u_0>0$, $B\ge1$,
$s^2u_0^2\ge2B$, and
\[
 \int e^{\pm uX}d\nu\le e^{u^2s^2/2+B},\qquad0\le u\le u_0.
\]
Then $\int X^2d\nu\le2s^2(B+10)$ and
$(\int X^4d\nu)^{1/2}\le2s^2(B+12)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Markov's inequality, with $u=x/s^2$ when $x\le s^2u_0$
and $u=u_0$ otherwise, gives
\[
 \nu(|X|>x)\le
 \begin{cases}2e^{B-x^2/(2s^2)},&x\le s^2u_0,\\
               2e^{B-u_0x/2},&x>s^2u_0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Also use $\nu(|X|>x)\le1$ below $s\sqrt{2B}$.
Put $w=s^2u_0^2/2\ge B$. Integration of these three bounds
against $2x\,dx$ gives at most $2Bs^2+4s^2+16s^2$.
Against $4x^3\,dx$ it gives at most
\[
 s^4\bigl(4B^2+16(B+1)+8(4B+60)\bigr)
       \le4s^4(B+12)^2.
\]
Here $e^{B-w}\le1$, $we^{B-w}\le B$ and
$u_0^{-2}\le s^2/(2B)$ bound the last integrals.
\end{proof}

We need the density identity at real points of the
coefficient polydiscs, as well as the norm estimates there.
We record why the same step supplies both.

\begin{lemma}[A real change of the running coefficients]\label{C-406-59}
Let $(x_i,s_i)$ be the coefficients and shifts of the
canonical flow at a fixed cutoff. At a level $1\le k<K$
suppose real numbers $(x'_i,s'_i)_{i\le k}$ lie in its
windows and satisfy $|x'_i-x_i|\le(2/3)r_xx_i$.
Use the activities obtained by the steps at these numbers,
with the original fine masses. Let $d_k$ be their standard
level-$k$ density on the density-test set, extended by zero
outside it, with any real scalar normalization $E'$.
Then the next density is
\[
 d_{k+1}=\chi_{k+1}\mathsf I
                    [\operatorname{Ber}_k(\operatorname{Ker}_k d_k)].
\]
It is bounded and Borel and has the standard form with
\[
 x'_{k+1}=L^{-1}x'_k-b'_{k+1},\qquad
 s'_{k+1}=Ls'_k+\mu'_{k+1},\qquad
 E'\longmapsto E'+n_{k+1}e'_{k+1}.
\]
The output activities retain the symmetries, locality,
holomorphy, zero moments and closed norm bounds of the
one-step theorem. The density identity also carries bounded
Borel scalar factors in the bare density. If $d_k$ is the
actual history density obtained from a bare density
$\varsigma e^{-\beta A-S_F}$ with $\varsigma\ge0$, integrating
all remaining Grassmann variables gives its positive history
measure. This positivity assertion uses the history identity
with that bare density.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The history weight at level $k+1$ is the previous weight
times the next density test, the two intermediate tests,
the gauge-fixing factor and the fluctuation test. The
intermediate tests equal one on the support of the next
density and fluctuation tests. The full fermion kernel
acts by a linear Berezin integral; thus any scalar Borel
factor is carried along. The chart image formula gives
the displayed density coordinate by coordinate. Its
coefficients are bounded and Borel on the image domain
and vanish outside the next density-test set. Each full
kernel has Berezin integral one in the variables it
introduces. Integrating the final variables therefore
recovers the history weight times the original scalar
density and fermion determinant.

The given point lies in the coefficient polydiscs of
the holomorphic one-step construction. Indeed
$x_i\le(5/4)\mathsf t_i$, while the shift window gives
$|s'_i|\le2\bar B_M/\mathsf t_i\le(5/2)\bar B_M/x_i
\le A\phi(x_i)$, since $A\ge5\bar B_M$.
The windows and the ceiling $4\bar B\gamma^2\le\sigma_\star$
also give $|x'_i/\mathsf t_i-1|\le\sigma_\star/4$.
At each chart point the scalar part of $d_k$ is the
exponential of the Wilson action at $x'_k$ and the earlier
degree-zero action, times a constant. It is positive and
bounded away from zero on the chart. The remaining
Grassmann-valued factor is bounded and Borel. Hence the
chart formula for that coefficient applies to it.

Rotate the generators by the site factor and shift by the
background. Both substitutions have Berezin Jacobian one.
The quadratic form and the full kernel give the new
quadratic form, the fermion fluctuation Gaussian and its
normalization. The other terms are their values at the
new background plus their variations: the shift gives
the mass vertex; the old activities give the scalar and
positive-degree old vertices; the gauge terms use the
pair $(\mathsf t_k,x'_k)$. The potential remains below
the same cluster threshold on these polydiscs. Extracting
its vacuum, action and mass coefficients therefore gives
exactly $e'_{k+1},b'_{k+1},\mu'_{k+1}$ and the stated
new density.

For the applicability of the history norm, the torus
symmetries must hold also at this point. Translation by
a vector of $LM\mathbb Z^3$ carries the charts, pivot
bonds, site factors, walk expansions, local terms and
filing cells to their translates; the seam map multiplies
each local mass bilinear by $u(x)^2=1$. The coefficients
and masses are scalars independent of the site. Thus
induction from the empty family at level zero gives the
pointed translation covariance on every domain, including
those that wrap around the torus. On nonwrapping domains
the same formulas are the restrictions of the
infinite-lattice activities. The field-independent shares
assigned to wrapping rows are translated with their rows.

Charge conjugation is preserved by the same algebraic
operations. For an isometry, apply the chart image identity
to the two densities at a pair of covariance. After
extracting the local coefficients their quotient is an
exponential of a real scalar, a multiple of the background
action and a multiple of the mass bilinear; each is carried
by the isometry. Starting with the covariant bare density
proves covariance at every later level. The gauge Gaussian
part uses the pointed sum rule at the actual coefficient
$x'_i$, which lies in its disc, so it has the same property.
The extraction makes the quadratic zeroth moment vanish.
The reblocking estimate then applies with this zero moment,
holomorphy and joint gauge invariance. The closed norm
bounds and the degree-zero array bound consequently hold
with the constants of the original step. These are exactly
the inputs used by the history norm bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Variance with fermions]\label{C-406-58}
There are $d_2\ge n$ and $C_v<\infty$, depending on the
fixed constants, $\ell$, $b$ and $n$, such that
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mu^{F,K}_d[b,\mathsf m]}T_d^K
          \le C_vN_d,\qquad K>d\ge d_2.
\]
They are independent of $K$, $d$ and
$\mathsf m\in[m_-,m_+]$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Put $k_0=K-d$ and $\mathcal T=T_d^K(\mathcal M^{k_0}U)$.
Let $m_j(F)$ be the unnormalized integral of $F$ on the
history having no large-field region through level $j$.
This is a positive functional on nonnegative gauge-invariant
Borel functions, and $m_j(1)\le Z$. By \cref{C-406-59},
it is also the total Berezin integral of the corresponding
term with scalar factor $F$.

The density-test set at level $k_0$ lies in
$\operatorname{In}_{k_0}[b_\flat]$. On it
$T_d^K=L^KA(U_{k_0})$. Thus multiplying the bare density
by $e^{-u\mathcal T}$ changes the level-$k_0$ coefficient
from $x_{k_0}$ to $x_{k_0}+v$, $v=uL^d$, and leaves all
earlier activities unchanged.

Continue the flow with this new coefficient. It is
holomorphic for $|v|<\rho_v=r_xx_{k_0}/4$, and induction
gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcdm2-statistic-moved-flow}
 |x_j(v)-x_j|\le\tfrac7{12}r_xx_j,\qquad
 |s_j(v)|\le\bar B_M/x_j,\qquad
 |e_j(v)-e_j|\le C_e^o:=L^3.
\end{equation}
Here are the bounds closing the induction. The gauge and
fermion one-loop parts of $b_j$ depend only on the calibration
and fine mass. The remaining part has size at most
$C_w\phi(x_{j-1})$, so
\[
 |x_j(v)-x_j|
 \le L^{-(j-k_0)}|v|+\frac{2L}{L-1}C_w\phi(\gamma^{-2})
              <\left(\tfrac12+\tfrac1{12}\right)r_xx_j.
\]
We used $x_{k_0}\le2L^{j-k_0}x_j$ and
$26C_w\phi(\gamma^{-2})\le r_x\gamma^{-2}$.
The one-loop mass identity, valid for every nonzero
coefficient sequence, gives
$s_j(v)=G_j(x(v))+\sum_{i\le j}L^{j-i}\rho_i(v)$.
Its slices are nonnegative and
$|x_i(v)|\ge(11/12)x_i$, so
\[
 |G_j(x(v))|\le\frac{24B_F}{11x_j},\qquad
 \sum_{i\le j}L^{j-i}|\rho_i(v)|\le\frac1{4x_j}.
\]
This proves the shift bound. Finally the vacuum coefficient
has the form
\[
 e_j=e_j^{\rm YM,0}+e_j^{F,0}
       -3(L^3-1)\operatorname{Log}(x_{j-1}/\mathsf t_{j-1})
       +\tilde e_j,\qquad
 |\tilde e_j|\le C_w\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1}).
\]
The first two terms are unchanged, and the same remainder
bound holds at $v$. Since
$|x_{j-1}(v)/x_{j-1}-1|\le7/96$,
\[
 |e_j(v)-e_j|
 \le3(L^3-1)\frac7{89}+2C_w\phi(\gamma^{-2})\le L^3.
\]
At each stage \eqref{eq:qcdm2-statistic-moved-flow} lies
strictly within the polydiscs required for the next step.

For real $|v|\le1/2$ the moved coefficients also remain
in the original windows. Indeed $|b_i(v)|\le B_\sharp-1/2$,
and the added jump $v$ at $k_0$ gives
\[
 |x_j(v)-\mathsf t_j|
 \le\tfrac12+(B_\sharp-\tfrac12)\frac L{L-1}
                 =\bar B-\frac1{2(L-1)}<\bar B.
\]
Thus \cref{C-406-59} identifies the iterated density with
the actual weighted history term, rather than only a
formal analytic continuation. All inputs of the history
norm bound have been retained: the closed activity norm,
degree-zero array norm, quadratic zero moment, gauge and
flavour invariance, translation covariance and reality.
Consequently, for $k_0\le t'\le K$,
\[
 m_{t'}(e^{-u\mathcal T})
 \le\exp(E_{t'}(v)+C_E^Fn_{t'}),\qquad |u|L^d\le1/2,
\]
where $E_{t'}(v)=E_{k_0}+\sum_{k_0<j\le t'}n_je_j(v)$.
The positive Wilson action can be discarded in this upper
bound, and the remaining Haar measure has mass one.

Put $d'=K-t'$ and
\begin{align*}
 B_{d'}&=\bigl[1+C_E^F+C_P(1+\log(L^{d'}b+\bar B))\bigr]N_{d'},\\
 f_{t'}(v)&=E_{t'}(v)-E_{t'},\qquad
 c_{t'}=-L^df'_{t'}(0),\\
 C_{\rm cen}&=\frac{8C_e^o}{(L^3-1)r_x}.
\end{align*}
The partition lower bound gives
$Z\ge\exp(E_{t'}-C_P(1+\log x_{t'})n_{t'})$.
On $|v|<\rho_v$,
$|f_{t'}(v)|\le C_e^oN_d/(L^3-1)$ and $f_{t'}(0)=0$.
Moreover $\rho_v\ge r_xL^db/8\ge3/2$. Cauchy's estimates
therefore imply, for $|u|\le u_0=L^{-d}/2$,
\begin{align}
 Z^{-1}m_{t'}(e^{-u(\mathcal T-c_{t'})})
   &\le\exp(u^2\sigma_d^2/2+B_{d'}),
       \label{eq:qcdm2-layer-exponential}\\
 \sigma_d^2&=\frac{256C_e^oN_d}{(L^3-1)r_x^2b^2},
       \notag\\
 |c_{t'}|&\le C_{\rm cen}N_d/b,\qquad
 |c_{t'}-c_K|\le C_{\rm cen}N_{d'}/b.
       \label{eq:qcdm2-layer-centers}
\end{align}
For the last estimate apply Cauchy's inequality to
$f_K-f_{t'}$, whose supremum is at most
$C_e^oN_{d'}/(L^3-1)$. The augmented variance parameter
\[
 \sigma_{d,d'}^2=\sigma_d^2+8L^{2d}B_{d'}
\]
satisfies $\sigma_{d,d'}^2u_0^2\ge2B_{d'}$, as required
in \cref{C-406-57}.

Group all histories into the history with no large fields,
the histories whose first nonempty outcome occurs at
$t'+1$, $k_0\le t'<K$, and those with such an outcome
at or before $k_0$. Write their positive functionals as
$m_K$, $\lambda_{t'}$ and $\lambda_-$, respectively. The
history identity gives
\[
 Z\mathsf E F=m_K(F)+\sum_{t'=k_0}^{K-1}\lambda_{t'}(F)
                         +\lambda_-(F),\qquad
 0\le\lambda_{t'}(F)\le m_{t'}(F)\quad(F\ge0).
\]
A first nonempty outcome creates at least one cell.
The chosen mark is therefore at least
$\frac12c_\star A_0^2(\log(L^{d'-1}b))^{2\mathfrak p_0}$.
The marked history sum and partition lower bound give
\begin{align*}
 \lambda_{t'}(1)/Z&\le\min\{1,R_{d'}\},\qquad
 \lambda_-(1)/Z\le R_{d+1},\\
 R_j&=\exp\left[C_{\rm lf}
          -\tfrac12c_\star A_0^2(\log(L^{j-1}b))^{2\mathfrak p_0}
\right],\\
 C_{\rm lf}&=\bigl[C_{\rm maj}^\dagger+2
                    +C_P(1+\log(b+\bar B))\bigr]\ell^3.
\end{align*}
This estimate bounds the final history masses; it does
not require each intermediate gauge-fixing factor to be
at most one.

Apply \cref{C-406-57} to $Z^{-1}m_{t'}$ and
$\mathcal T-c_{t'}$, using
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-layer-exponential}. At $t'=K$ this gives
\[
 Z^{-1}m_K((\mathcal T-c_K)^2)
                   \le2\sigma_{d,0}^2(B_0+10).
\]
For the other layers, Cauchy--Schwarz, the fourth-moment
bound and \eqref{eq:qcdm2-layer-centers} give
\[
 Z^{-1}\lambda_{t'}((\mathcal T-c_K)^2)
 \le\sqrt8\min\{1,R_{d'}\}^{1/2}
       \left[2\sigma_{d,d'}^2(B_{d'}+12)
                         +C_{\rm cen}^2N_{d'}^2/b^2\right].
\]
Finally $0\le\mathcal T\le(3/8)\ell^3L^{4d}$, so the
last portion is bounded by
\[
 Z^{-1}\lambda_-((\mathcal T-c_K)^2)
 \le\bigl((3/8)\ell^3L^{4d}+C_{\rm cen}N_d/b\bigr)^2R_{d+1}.
\]
Choose $d_2$ so this is at most one for $d\ge d_2$.
All three series
\[
 \sum_{j\ge1}(B_j+12)\sqrt{\min\{1,R_j\}},\quad
 \sum_{j\ge1}N_j^2\sqrt{\min\{1,R_j\}},\quad
 \sum_{j\ge1}B_j(B_j+12)\sqrt{\min\{1,R_j\}}
\]
converge, since $2\mathfrak p_0>1$. Summing the layer
bounds and using $L^{2d}\le N_d$ gives
$\mathsf E(\mathcal T-c_K)^2\le C_vN_d$, and hence the
variance bound. Every constant used above is uniform
over the stated mass interval.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The coefficient determined by the block average}

\begin{definition}[The coefficient $\kappa$]\label{C-416-3}
At bare mass $m_0\in[0,1]$, let $\widehat W_{m_0}$
be the translation-invariant operator on exact curvatures
for which the quadratic term of the negative logarithmic
fermion determinant is
\[
 \tfrac12\sum_{c=1}^3
                     \langle dA^c,\widehat W_{m_0}dA^c\rangle.
\]
Thus $\widehat W_{m_0}=N_f\widehat W_{m_0}^{\rm f}$,
where the one-flavour polarization kernel satisfies
$\Pi=d^*\widehat W_{m_0}^{\rm f}d$.
Let $\Pi_l^{\rm tp}$ be the orthogonal projection onto
the background curvatures of the $l$-fold straight
average, and let $\tau_l$ denote trace per site of
$L^l\mathbb Z^3$. Put
\[
 \kappa(l,\mu)=\frac1{2L^l}
                \tau_l(\Pi_l^{\rm tp}\widehat W_{L^{-l}\mu}),
 \qquad l\ge1,\quad0\le\mu\le L^l.
\]
The curvature slice is
$\mathcal C_{(j+1)}=\Pi_j^{\rm tp}-\Pi_{j+1}^{\rm tp}$.

Here is the limiting coefficient of the block average.
For $s(y)=(e^{iy}-1)/(iy)$, with $s(0)=1$, let
$\hat B(k)$ be the diagonal matrix with entries
\[
 \hat B_\mu(k)=s(k_\mu)\prod_\nu s(k_\nu).
\]
Define also
\[
 P(k)=1-kk^{\mathsf T}/|k|^2,\qquad
 G(p)=(e^{ip_\mu}-1)_\mu.
\]
For $p\in[-\pi,\pi]^3\setminus\{0\}$ and $a=1,2$ set
\[
 M_a(p)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^3}
       \hat B(k_n)P(k_n)\hat B(k_n)^*|k_n|^{-1-a},
 \qquad k_n=p+2\pi n.
\]
Let $J_p:G(p)^\perp\hookrightarrow\mathbb C^3$ be the
inclusion and put
\[
 \operatorname{Del}(p)=J_p(J_p^*M_1(p)J_p)^{-1}J_p^*,
 \qquad
 I_B=\frac12\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^3}
                 \operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{Del}(p)M_2(p))
                                      \frac{d^3p}{(2\pi)^3}.
\]
The following lemma justifies the inverse and integral.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The fermion contribution to the background action]
\label{C-416-4}
Use the constants of \cref{C-416-2}. Fix an admissible
side $\ell=2L^m$, an interval $J=[b_-,b_+]$ as in
\cref{C-375-7}, $\mathsf b_*\in J$ and $\mathsf m>0$.
Let $\mathbb E_K^{\rm F}$ and $\mathbb E_K^{\rm W}$
denote the gauge expectations with and without fermions
at $\beta=L^K\mathsf b_*$, with bare fermion mass
$m_0=L^{-K}\mathsf m$. There are $d_2\ge d_\natural$
and $\mathsf K_{\rm S}<\infty$, depending on these
fixed data but independent of $K,d$, such that
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_K^{\rm F}T_d^K-\mathbb E_K^{\rm W}T_d^K
       +3\mathsf b_*^{-2}\ell^3L^{2d}
                   \kappa(K-d,L^{-d}\mathsf m)\right|
                      \le\mathsf K_{\rm S}L^{7d/4},
 \qquad K>d\ge d_2.
\]
Here $\kappa$ is defined in \cref{C-416-3}, satisfies
$|\kappa(l,\mu)|\le C_{\rm kp}N_f$, and tends jointly
to $N_fI_B/4$ as $l\to\infty,\mu\to0$, with
$0<I_B<\infty$. Consequently, for any $K_0(d)>d$
with $K_0(d)-d\to\infty$,
\[
 \lim_{d\to\infty}\sup_{K\ge K_0(d)}
 \left|L^{-2d}(\mathbb E_K^{\rm F}T_d^K-\mathbb E_K^{\rm W}T_d^K)
                 +\tfrac34\mathsf b_*^{-2}\ell^3N_fI_B\right|=0.
\]
\end{theorem}

The proof is given after \cref{C-416-15}. The scale
$L^{2d}$ is smaller than the order $L^{3d}$ of the
mean itself, but larger than its standard deviation,
which is bounded by a constant times $L^{3d/2}$
by \cref{C-406-58}.
This separation of powers will distinguish the flavour
number from the background gauge field.

\begin{corollary}[Upper and lower bounds for the mean shift]
\label{C-416-5}
In the theorem's setting put
$\kappa_0=\tfrac34\mathsf b_*^{-2}\ell^3N_fI_B$.
There is $\kappa_+<\infty$ such that
\[
 |\mathbb E_K^{\rm F}T_d^K-\mathbb E_K^{\rm W}T_d^K|
                   \le\kappa_+L^{2d}\qquad(K>d\ge d_\natural).
\]
There are $d_3,l_0$ such that
\[
 \mathbb E_K^{\rm W}T_d^K-\mathbb E_K^{\rm F}T_d^K
                    \ge\tfrac14\kappa_0L^{2d}
             \qquad(d\ge d_3,\ K\ge d+l_0).
\]
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
For $d\ge d_2$ use the theorem and the bound on
$\kappa$. For the finitely many smaller depths use
$0\le T_d^K\le\mathsf Q'L^{4d}$ and increase
$\kappa_+$ by at most $\mathsf Q'L^{2d_2}$.
Choose $l_0,\mu_0$ so that
$\kappa(l,\mu)\ge N_fI_B/8$ for
$l\ge l_0$, $0\le\mu\le\mu_0$.
Then choose $d_3\ge d_2$ with
$L^{-d_3}\mathsf m\le\mu_0$ and
$\mathsf K_{\rm S}L^{-d_3/4}\le\kappa_0/4$.
The leading term in the theorem is at least
$\kappa_0L^{2d}/2$, leaving the stated lower bound.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Comparing the two flows}
\label{sec:qcdm2-mean-shift-flow}

We compare the gauge marginal with fermions to Wilson's
measure at the same bare coupling. The histories, tests and
calibrations are the same. The fermions change the running
coefficients and the activities. To find the resulting
change in the mean of $T_d^K$, we insert $e^{\zeta T_d^K}$
and differentiate the vacuum energies produced after the
insertion. The final integral will be estimated by positivity
and convexity.

Use the constants of \cref{C-416-2} and the interval
$J=[b_-,b_+]$ of \cref{C-375-7}. Fix
$\mathsf b_*\in J$ and $\mathsf m>0$, and relabel as in
\cref{C-416-6}. Throughout this subsection put
\[
 t=K-d,\qquad d'=\lceil d/8\rceil,\qquad t'=K-d',
 \qquad N_u=\ell^3L^{3u},\qquad n_k=N_{K-k},
\]
and assume $K>d$ and $d'\ge\max\{\bar n,d_\natural\}$.
The two source radii used below are
\[
 \rho'=\tfrac14r_x\mathsf b_*,\qquad
 \zeta_0=\tfrac12L^{-d}.
\]
The bare densities and expectations are
\[
 \varsigma^{\rm F}=e^{-\beta A}\det(D+m_0),\qquad
 \varsigma^{\rm W}=e^{-\beta A},\qquad
 \mathbb E_K^\sharp F=(Z^\sharp)^{-1}
                         \int F\varsigma^\sharp\,dU,
 \quad \sharp\in\{{\rm F},{\rm W}\},
\]
where $\beta=L^K\mathsf b_*$ and $m_0=L^{-K}\mathsf m$.
All constants in this subsection are independent of $K,d$.
Dependence on $\mathsf m$ will be displayed where it enters.

\begin{lemma}[The flow without fermions]\label{C-416-7}
The small-field step of \cite[\S7]{QCDM1}, with all
fermion terms omitted, defines coefficients and activities
\[
 x_0^{\rm W}=\beta,\qquad
 x_{k+1}^{\rm W}=L^{-1}x_k^{\rm W}-b_{k+1}^{\rm W},
 \qquad E_k^{\rm W}=\sum_{j\le k}e_j^{\rm W}n_j.
\]
Write $b_j^{\rm W}=e_{\mathsf N,j}+b_j^{r,\rm W}$.
At every level of a weak datum,
\[
 |x_k^{\rm W}-\mathsf t_k|\le\bar B,\qquad
 |b_{k+1}^{r,\rm W}|\le C_w\phi(x_k^{\rm W}),\qquad
 \|F_0^{{\rm W},(j)}\|_j\le C_w\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1}).
\]
The degree-zero activities have the bound $E_0$ and the
background variation bound of the step. The term of the
history without large fields is
\[
 e^{E_k^{\rm W}}\mathsf{Stay}(V)
 \exp\left[-L^kx_k^{\rm W}A(\mathsf U_k(V))
       +\sum_{j\le k}\sum_XE_0^{{\rm W},(j)}(X;\mathsf U_k(V))
      \right]\mathscr M^{\rm fr}_{h_\emptyset}(dV).
\]
As measures it lies between
$e^{E_k^{\rm W}\pm C_5^{\rm W}n_k}
\mathsf{sf}_k[x_k^{\rm W}]\,dV_k$, and
$|e_j^{\rm W}|\le C'_{e,\rm W}(1+\log x_{j-1}^{\rm W})$.

These activities and coefficients are holomorphic in the
earlier coefficients on their step polydiscs. The bounds
for the activities and the extracted step numbers hold
at $|x'_i-x_i^{\rm W}|\le(2/3)r_xx_i^{\rm W}$.
There is also a density identity for a restart. Suppose
$G\ge0$ is bounded and Borel on the level-$n_0$ fields,
and its history term has the displayed form at level $n_0$
with coefficient $x''_{n_0}$ and vacuum energy $E''_{n_0}$,
and has a bounded Borel density against $dV_{n_0}$.
Keep the original coefficients below $n_0$ and apply the
same steps thereafter. If
$|x''_k-\mathsf t_k|\le\bar B$ for $n_0\le k\le n_1$,
the history terms of $G(\mathcal M^{n_0}U)e^{-\beta A}$
have this form at every such level, with
\[
 x''_{k+1}=L^{-1}x''_k-b''_{k+1},\qquad
 E''_k=E''_{n_0}+\sum_{n_0\le j<k}e''_{j+1}n_{j+1},
\]
and satisfy the same two measure bounds.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
In the combined step the fermion normalization becomes one,
the mass and positive-degree vertices disappear, and the
remaining integral is the gauge Gaussian integral with the
gauge vertices and the variations of the old scalar terms.
The Gaussian uses $x_k^{\rm W}$; the tests, charts and gauge
fixing use $\mathsf t_k$. This is the gauge step in the
chosen calibration frame. Every estimate for the omitted
vertices is replaced by zero. The proof of the small-field
induction in \cite[\S7]{QCDM1} therefore applies, including
its holomorphic dependence and the scalar array bound.
More explicitly, the new fluctuation family has norm at
most $\tfrac12 C_w\phi(\mathsf t_k)$, and its extracted
coupling has modulus at most $C_b\phi(\mathsf t_k)$.
The inequalities $C_w\ge2\sqrt2C_b$ and
$x_k^{\rm W}\le(1+\bar B\gamma^2)\mathsf t_k$ give the
claimed remainder bound. Moreover
\[
 |e_{\mathsf N,j}|\le(1+L^{-1})c_{2,\rm loop},\qquad
 |b_j^{\rm W}|\le B_\sharp-1,
\]
by \cref{C-416-2}. Summing the coefficient recursion gives
$|x_k^{\rm W}-\mathsf t_k|\le\bar B$.

The scalar array consists of the gauge normalization,
the extracted action term, the Gaussian correction and
the fluctuation family. On the coefficient polydiscs their
polymer bounds are the bounds used for the degree-zero
array in \cite[\S7]{QCDM1}; the closed fermion loops and
the fermion coupling coefficient are absent. These bounds
give $E_0$ at rate $\kappa+1$ and the corresponding
background variation. The lower and upper measure bounds
are then the degree-zero history estimate of
\cite[Thm.~E]{QCDM1} with the determinants omitted. The
vacuum-energy estimate is obtained from the same step.

For the restart, the two window bounds imply
\[
 |x''_i-x_i^{\rm W}|\le2\bar B
       \le\tfrac12r_x\gamma^{-2}
       \le\tfrac23r_xx_i^{\rm W}.
\]
Thus all the required activities are in the preceding
polydiscs and retain their bounds. The history weights
multiply at each step. For every bounded Borel bare
density, the next history term is consequently the image
of the current term times the next tests and gauge-fixing
factor. The chart formula uses its density and its
standard form, so it also applies to the restarted term.
Induction gives the displayed recursion and a bounded
Borel density at each level. Applying the scalar array
bound to this density gives the two measure inequalities.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Discarding histories]\label{C-416-8}
Let $\mathfrak w$ be the weight of the history with no
large-field region through level $t'$. Let $\widetilde\nu^\sharp$
be the normalized image of
$\mathfrak w\varsigma^\sharp\,dU$ under $\mathcal M^t$.
There are constants $C_{\rm dis}^\sharp$, independent of
$K,d$, such that, with
\[
 \rho^\sharp(d')=
 \exp\left[C_{\rm dis}^\sharp-\tfrac12c_\star A_0^2
                                   (d'\log L)^{2\mathfrak p_0}\right],
\]
\[
 0\le Z^\sharp-\int\mathfrak w\varsigma^\sharp\,dU
       \le\rho^\sharp(d')Z^\sharp,
 \qquad
 |\mathbb E_K^\sharp F(V_d)-\widetilde\nu^\sharp(F)|
       \le2\rho^\sharp(d')\|F\|_\infty
\]
for every bounded gauge-invariant Borel $F$. Both the
history at level $t$ and $\widetilde\nu^\sharp$ are
carried by
\[
 \operatorname{In}_t[\mathsf b_*]
 \subset\operatorname{Cut}_t[\mathsf b_*]
 \subset\operatorname{Cut}_t[b_-].
\]
On this set $T_d^K(V)=L^KA(\mathsf U_t(V))$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The weights are nonnegative. A history with a nonempty
large-field region by level $t'$ has a created cell at
some level $j\le t'$. The mark counts this cell, and
$\mathsf t_j\ge L^{d'}$, so its value is at least
$\tfrac12c_\star A_0^2(d'\log L)^{2\mathfrak p_0}$.
Apply the marked history sum at the last level
$\bar K=K-\bar n$. In the fermion model its upper bound
is $\exp[E_{\bar K}+(C+2)n_{\bar K}]$.
The unintegrated lower measure bound and the ball integral
of \cref{C-416-6} give a lower partition bound with
\[
 \begin{split}
 C_{\rm dis}^{\rm F}={}&\Bigl[C+2+C_5^F
 +\nu\log\left(\frac1{b_F(1-L^{-1})}
                           +\frac{L^{\bar n}}{\mathsf m}\right)
 +\tfrac92\log\bigl(L(\bar g^{-2}+B_\sharp)\bigr)\\
 &\hspace{35mm}+3\log7+24(B_3^{\rm cr})^2\Bigr]n_{\bar K}.
 \end{split}
\]
Here $n_{\bar K}=L^{3\bar n}\ell^3$ is independent of $K$.
In the gauge model the marked sum and the partition lower
bound of \cite[Thm.~D]{YMM1}, at the same mark and share,
give
\[
 C_{\rm dis}^{\rm W}=
 (\mathsf C_{\rm maj}+2+C_{\rm st}
                       +\tfrac92\log\bar{\mathsf b})n_{\bar K}.
\]
Taking the quotient proves the lost-mass estimate.

The history identity with the insertion
$F(\mathcal M^tU)$ bounds the lost numerator by
$\rho^\sharp Z^\sharp\|F\|_\infty$. Normalizing the
retained numerator costs the same amount. This gives
the factor two. The argument uses positivity of the
complete history measures, without bounding individual
gauge-fixing factors by one.

The indicator of the history through $t'$ vanishes
unless the history through $t$ passes its tests. Its
block field then has plaquette deviation less than
$2\varepsilon(\mathsf t_t)$, where
$\mathsf t_t=L^d\mathsf b_*$. The cut inclusions in
\cref{C-375-7} prove the carrier assertion and the
identity for $T_d^K$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Inserting the background action]\label{C-416-9}
For $|\zeta|\le\rho'$ keep the coefficients below $t$,
replace $x_t$ by $x_t-\zeta L^d$, keep $s_t$, and
continue the step. Denote the resulting coefficients by
$x'_k,s'_k$ and the extracted numbers by
$b_{k+1}(\zeta),\mu_{k+1}(\zeta),e_{k+1}(\zeta)$.
Restart the gauge flow in the same way at
$x_t^{\rm W}-\zeta L^d$. For $t\le k\le t'$,
\[
 |x'_k-x_k|\le\tfrac23r_xx_k,\qquad
 |s'_k|\le2\bar B_M/\mathsf t_k,\qquad
 |x_k^{\rm W}(\zeta)-x_k^{\rm W}|
                                      \le\tfrac23r_xx_k^{\rm W}.
\]
The coefficients and step energies are holomorphic for
$|\zeta|<\rho'$, continuous on the closed disc, and real
on its real interval. The gauge normalization coefficient
$e_{\mathsf N,j}$ and the fermion one-loop coefficient
$b_j^F$ are constant in $\zeta$. In particular
\[
 x'_k-x_k=-\zeta L^{K-k}
       -\sum_{t<j\le k}L^{-(k-j)}
                            (b_j^r(\zeta)-b_j^r(0)),
 \qquad |b_j^r(\zeta)|\le C_w\phi(x_{j-1}),
\]
and the analogous formula holds without fermions.

For real $|\zeta|\le\zeta_0$, both restarted coupling
windows satisfy $|x_k(\zeta)-\mathsf t_k|\le\bar B-1/2$.
The history terms of
$e^{\zeta T_d^K\circ\mathcal M^t}\varsigma^\sharp$
are precisely these restarted densities. Their vacuum
energies are $E_t^\sharp+
\sum_{t\le j<k}e_{j+1}^\sharp(\zeta)n_{j+1}$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Assume the bounds through level $k$. The data lie in the
step polydiscs of radius one: indeed
\[
 2\bar B_M/\mathsf t_i
 \le2\bar B_M\gamma\mathsf t_i^{-1/2}
 \le\tfrac23\mathsf t_i^{-1/2}\le x_i^{-1/2}.
\]
The step therefore supplies its original constants.
Its normalization coefficient depends only on the level
and $L$, and $b_j^F$ depends only on the fine mass.
Subtracting the recursions gives the displayed formula.
The jump has modulus at most $0.26r_xx_k$, since
$\bar B\le x_k/192$. The remaining sum is at most
\[
 2C_w\phi(x_k)\sum_{j\ge0}L^{-j}
 \le\tfrac{13}{6}C_w\phi(x_k)
 \le\tfrac{13}{168}r_xx_k.
\]
Here $x_{j-1}\ge x_k$ for $j\le k$ and $\phi$ decreases
on the admitted range. Their sum is below
$(2/3)r_xx_k$.

The one-loop mass increments telescope at these complex
coefficients, as in \cite[\S8]{QCDM1}. Writing their
cumulative value as $G_k(x')$ gives
\[
 s'_k=G_k(x')+\sum_{j\le k}L^{k-j}\rho_j,\qquad
 |G_k(x')|\le4B_F/\mathsf t_k,
 \quad |\rho_j|\le C_\rho\phi_\sharp(x_{j-1})^3.
\]
The geometric estimate for the last sum, together with
$x_{j-1}\ge3\mathsf t_{j-1}/4$, bounds it by
$0.4/\mathsf t_k$ under \cref{C-416-2}. Since
$\bar B_M=3B_F+1$, this closes the shift window.
The gauge induction uses the same proof with $s=b^F=0$.
Composition gives holomorphy and reality.

For $|\zeta|\le\zeta_0$ the jump is at most $1/2$ in
each coupling window, and every extracted coupling has
modulus at most $B_\sharp-1$. Thus
\[
 |x'_k-\mathsf t_k|
 \le\tfrac12+(B_\sharp-1)\frac L{L-1}
 \le\bar B-\tfrac12,
\]
and likewise in the gauge flow. At level $t$ the carrier
identity of \cref{C-416-8} gives
\[
 e^{\zeta T_d^K(V)}e^{-L^tx_tA(\mathsf U_t(V))}
       =e^{-L^t(x_t-\zeta L^d)A(\mathsf U_t(V))}.
\]
The activities at this level read the earlier coefficients,
so they are unchanged. The source factor is bounded and
Borel. The step's image-density identity then applies
at every later level by \cref{C-406-59}: it reads the
standard density, its coefficients in the polydiscs,
and the activities with their closed bounds. It does
not require the earlier coefficients to obey the
unperturbed recursion. These bounds hold also on all
comparison tori, as the holomorphic construction is
made on the infinite lattice and its restrictions.
Induction proves the density identity with fermions.
For the gauge density apply the restart clause of
\cref{C-416-7}, with $G=e^{\zeta T_d^K}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The mean and the vacuum energies]\label{C-416-10}
For $\sharp\in\{{\rm F},{\rm W}\}$ put
\[
 c_\sharp(\zeta)=\sum_{t\le k<t'}
                         e_{k+1}^\sharp(\zeta)n_{k+1},\qquad
 f_\sharp(\zeta)=\log\widetilde\nu^\sharp(e^{\zeta T_d^K})
 \quad(\zeta\in\mathbb R).
\]
There is $C_{\rm fc}$ depending only on the fixed
construction constants such that, with
\[
 \begin{split}
 R_{\rm fc}&=C_{\rm fc}(1+d'+|\log\mathsf b_*|
                              +\log_+(1/\mathsf m))N_{d'},\\
 C_{\rm cx}&=L^3+6K_Mc_{\rm cl},\qquad
 \bar S=128C_{\rm cx}N_d/(r_x^2\mathsf b_*^2),
 \end{split}
\]
we have $f_\sharp(0)=0$ and
\[
 f_\sharp(\zeta)\le c_\sharp(\zeta)-c_\sharp(0)+R_{\rm fc}
                       \quad(|\zeta|\le\zeta_0).
\]
The function $c_\sharp$ is holomorphic on $|\zeta|<\rho'$,
with
\[
 |c_\sharp(\zeta)-c_\sharp(0)|\le C_{\rm cx}N_d,
 \qquad |c_\sharp''(\zeta)|\le\bar S
                              \quad(|\zeta|\le\rho'/2).
\]
If $(2R_{\rm fc}/\bar S)^{1/2}\le\zeta_0\le\rho'/2$,
then
\[
 |\widetilde\nu^\sharp(T_d^K)-c_\sharp'(0)|
                              \le(2R_{\rm fc}\bar S)^{1/2}.
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
By \cref{C-416-9}, the mass of the retained tilted
history is its vacuum exponential times a final integral
$I^\sharp(\zeta)$. Thus
\[
 f_\sharp(\zeta)=c_\sharp(\zeta)-c_\sharp(0)
                          +\log\frac{I^\sharp(\zeta)}{I^\sharp(0)}.
\]
In the fermion model the degree-zero history bound gives
$e^{\mathsf{rg}}\mathsf{sf}'_{t'}dV_{t'}$ with
$|\mathsf{rg}|\le C_5^Fn_{t'}$ and
$0\le\mathsf{sf}'_{t'}\le1$, before the remaining
fermion determinant is restored. The exact determinant
identity of \cite[\S9]{QCDM1} gives
$0<\det\mathbb D_{t'}\le\theta_{t'}^{\nu n_{t'}}$,
where $b_F(1-L^{-1})\le\theta_{t'}\le b_F$.
Consequently
\[
 I^{\rm F}(\zeta)\le
              e^{(\nu\log(1+b_F)+C_5^F)n_{t'}}.
\]
At zero source the lower measure bound and the ball
integral in \cref{C-416-6} give
\[
 I^{\rm F}(0)\ge
 \exp\left[-\left(C_5^F+
 \nu\log(1/\theta_{t'}+1/\mathfrak m_{t'})
 +\tfrac92\log x_{t'}+3\log7+24(B_3^{\rm cr})^2\right)n_{t'}\right].
\]
Here $\mathfrak m_{t'}=L^{-d'}\mathsf m$,
$x_{t'}\le\tfrac32L^{d'}\mathsf b_*$ and $n_{t'}=N_{d'}$.
Their logarithms are bounded by a constant times
$1+d'+|\log\mathsf b_*|+\log_+(1/\mathsf m)$.
Without fermions, \cref{C-416-7} gives the same upper
and lower estimates with the determinant terms omitted.
For the lower estimate $x_{t'}^{\rm W}\ge\gamma^{-2}$
and $x_{t'}^{\rm W}\ge3\mathsf t_{t'}/4$, so the ball
integral applies. This proves the first inequality.

The parts of a vacuum energy independent of $\zeta$
cancel in its difference. The Gaussian part is
\[
 g_k(x)=-3(L^3-1)\operatorname{Log}(x/\mathsf t_k).
\]
Its coefficient is half the number of integrated
nongauge directions per level-$(k+1)$ site; see
\cref{C-375-22}. The test contribution has modulus
at most $K_Mc_{\rm cl}$, and the cluster contribution
at most $2K_Mc_{\rm cl}$. Since
$|x'_k/x_k-1|\le1/12$, the difference of the Gaussian
terms is at most $L^3$. Hence
$|e_{k+1}^\sharp(\zeta)-e_{k+1}^\sharp(0)|\le C_{\rm cx}$.
Now $\sum_{t\le k<t'}n_{k+1}\le N_d$, which proves
the holomorphic bound. Cauchy's estimate on discs of
radius $\rho'/2$ gives the stated second-derivative bound.

Finally $f_\sharp$ is smooth and convex because $T_d^K$
is bounded. For $0<h\le\zeta_0$,
$\pm hf_\sharp'(0)\le f_\sharp(\pm h)$. Taylor's
formula for $c_\sharp$ therefore gives
\[
 |f_\sharp'(0)-c_\sharp'(0)|
             \le\tfrac12h\bar S+R_{\rm fc}/h.
\]
Use $h=(2R_{\rm fc}/\bar S)^{1/2}$ and
$f_\sharp'(0)=\widetilde\nu^\sharp(T_d^K)$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The scalar part of the step}
