Its terms of fluctuation orders one and at least three belong to
the potential; its quadratic term belongs to the quadratic origin
and is defined at every real fluctuation.  For $i\ge1$, localise
the term at $p$ by the shift parameters on the polymers containing
$X(p)$, the union of cells required to read that plaquette.  At
$i=0$, take $X(p)$ to be the union of cubes containing a corner of
$p$; there is no shift system.

The mass direction is
\[
 \mathcal V_i^{\mathrm s}[c]
 =-L^{-i}\left[
  \mathsf S_1(c\,\mathsf H_{0,i}(\mathsf U')\widetilde\Psi)
  -\mathsf S_1(c\,\mathsf H_{0,i+1}(\mathsf U)\Psi_{i+1})
                         \right].
\]
Write and localise its legs by the mass-variation rule of the
step.  For an old family $F$ at level $l\le i$, write
$\mathcal V_i^{\mathrm{old}}[F]$ for its variation at
$\lambda B$.
For $F_0$, apply the scalar bracket localisation to the bare array
consisting of $F_0$, pointed equally at its sites, with all other
entries zero.

For $F_{\ge2}$ and $i-l<n_{\mathrm{lag}}$, use the usual
fermionic variation.  At $i-l\ge n_{\mathrm{lag}}$, first use the
long-lag decomposition of \cite[Lem.\ 7.9]{QCDM1},
with the cell moment retained as in
\cref{lem:qcdm2-nonzero-cell-reading}. If $t(\mu)$ is
one of its terms when the shift is multiplied by $\mu$, take
\[
 [t(1)-t(0)](\widetilde\Psi)
 +t(0)(\widetilde\Psi)-t(0)(\mathsf H_i(\mathsf U)\Psi_{i+1}),
 \qquad
 \widetilde\Psi=\mathsf H_i(\mathsf U)\Psi_{i+1}+W .
\]
Then localise each term by the shift parameters.  Keep a cell's
local mass term $\bar\Phi(z_c)m_c\Phi(z_c)$ whole, including on a
torus.  File it at the cube containing $c$, enlarged successively
by the walks of both legs and by the cubes of the finite
differences.  This is the filing estimated in
Lemma~\ref{C-403-46}.

\item
The first response is defined recursively.  Put
$\mathfrak N_0[\mathsf g]=0$ and
\[
 \delta_i[\mathsf g]
 =\mathcal V_i^w[\mathsf g]
  +\mathcal V_i^{\mathrm s}[\lambda^4\mathfrak N_i[\mathsf g]]
  +\sum_{l=1}^i\mathcal V_i^{\mathrm{old}}
                                  [\mathbf P^{(l)}[\mathsf g]],
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathbf P}^{(i+1)}[\mathsf g]
       =D\widetilde E_i[\delta_i[\mathsf g]] .
\]
Let $\mathfrak e_{i+1}[\mathsf g](X)$ be its scalar value at the
trivial configuration.  Read the quadratic kernels at level
$i+1$, and split them by the mass-extraction rule.  If
$\mathsf k_{X,p}$ is a piece, define
\[
 \mathfrak n_{i+1}[\mathsf g](y)
   =[\lambda^4]\left(
       -\mathfrak s_{i+1}^{-1}
          \sum_{X,p}'\operatorname{ord}_0[\mathsf k_{X,p}](y)
                \right).
\]
The prime keeps the pieces of diameter less than one quarter of
the torus side; on $\mathbb Z^3$ it keeps all pieces.  Set
\begin{align*}
 \mathbf P^{(i+1)}[\mathsf g]
   &=\widetilde{\mathbf P}^{(i+1)}[\mathsf g]
      -\mathfrak e_{i+1}[\mathsf g]
      +L^{-(i+1)}
           \mathsf S_1(\lambda^4\mathfrak n_{i+1}[\mathsf g]\,\cdot),\\
 \mathfrak N_{i+1}[\mathsf g](x)
   &=L\mathfrak N_i[\mathsf g](x)
          +\mathfrak n_{i+1}[\mathsf g](y_{i+1}(x)).
\end{align*}
Here $y_{i+1}(x)$ is the site whose block contains $x$.
The added mass term is filed as the forms of the mass-extraction
rule at the coefficients of $\lambda^4$.

We specify its units because the long-lag estimates use their
cell sums.  Let $\mathsf k_X$ be the quadratic kernel of
$\widetilde{\mathbf P}^{(l)}$, let
$a_{X,p}=\operatorname{ord}_0\mathsf k_{X,p}$ and
$a_X=\sum_pa_{X,p}$.  The units are
\[
 \mathsf k_X-\operatorname{diag}a_X
 \quad\hbox{at the cell of }X,\qquad
 \bar\Phi(y)a_{X,p}(y)\Phi(y)
 \quad\hbox{at the cell of }y,
\]
and, for every retained piece,
\[
 P_{z;X,p}
   =-\mathfrak s_l^{-1}L^{-l}
       \mathsf S_1(\lambda^4a^{[4]}_{X,p}(z)1_z\psi^{\mathrm{bg}})
 \quad\hbox{at the cell of }z.
\]
The symmetrised zeroth moment is
$a_X(y)=\frac12\sum_{y'}(\mathsf k_X(y,y')+\mathsf k_X(y',y))$.
Consequently the absolute coefficients used in moving one
diagonal term sum to one.  The units of each polymer have zero
cell sum before the moved terms and forms are included; their
complete cell sum is
\[
 m_c=\sum_{z\in c}\left[
      \sum_{X,p}a_{X,p}(z;\lambda)
      -\mathfrak s_l^{-1}
        \sum_y A_l(y,z)\sum_{X,p}'\lambda^4a^{[4]}_{X,p}(z)
                          \right].
\]
Here $A_l$ is the moment map in the mass-extraction rule.

\item
Omitting
$\mathcal V_i^{\mathrm s}[\lambda^4\mathfrak N_i[\mathsf g]]$
from this recursion defines the reduced system
$\mathbf P^{\mathrm{red}}$, $\mathfrak e^{\mathrm{red}}$ and
$\mathfrak n^{\mathrm{red}}$.  Put
$\mathbf P^{\mathrm{rsp}}=\mathbf P-\mathbf P^{\mathrm{red}}$.
All three depend on the same source direction.

\item
The mixed response is
\begin{align*}
 \widetilde{\mathbf Q}^{(i+1)}[f,h]
   &=D\widetilde E_i\!\left[
        \sum_{l=1}^i\mathcal V_i^{\mathrm{old}}
                                      [\mathbf Q^{(l)}[f,h]]\right]
       +D^2\widetilde E_i[\delta_i[f],\delta_i[h]],\\
 \mathbf Q^{(i+1)}[f,h]
   &=\widetilde{\mathbf Q}^{(i+1)}[f,h]
                         -\mathfrak e_{i+1}[f,h],
\end{align*}
where $\mathfrak e_{i+1}[f,h](X)$ is the scalar value at the
trivial configuration.  Its quadratic units are its polymers,
each at its cell: no diagonal terms are moved.

For $\mathbf P^{\mathrm{rsp}}$, subtract the units of the full
and reduced systems using the same linear kernel splitting.
Thus its units are
$\mathsf k_X^{\mathrm{rsp}}-\operatorname{diag}a_X^{\mathrm{rsp}}$
and the moved terms
$\bar\Phi(y)a_{X,p}^{\mathrm{rsp}}(y)\Phi(y)$.
There are no forms, since
$\mathfrak n_l=\mathfrak n_l^{\mathrm{red}}$ by
Lemma~\ref{C-403-48}.  Its cell sum is therefore
\[
 m_c^{\mathrm{rsp}}
       =\sum_{z\in c}\sum_{X,p}a_{X,p}^{\mathrm{rsp}}(z;\lambda).
\]
Linearity of this filing gives
$\mathcal V_i^{\mathrm{old}}[\mathbf P^{\mathrm{rsp}}]
 =\mathcal V_i^{\mathrm{old}}[\mathbf P]
  -\mathcal V_i^{\mathrm{old}}[\mathbf P^{\mathrm{red}}]$
term by term.
\end{enumerate}
The same definitions apply to the infinite-lattice families whose
fitting parts give the torus families.  A subscript $\infty$
will distinguish these families when necessary.
\end{definition}

\subsection{Derivatives joining different cells}

The transfer between torus sizes also uses source derivatives of
order at most sixteen.  Only derivatives whose sources occupy
different cells require an additional estimate.

\begin{definition}[Sources in the comparison cells]
\label{C-403-43-linking}
On the least torus $T_{\ell_G}$ use the board with cell side
$\ell_G/2=L^{m_{\mathfrak L}(g)}$ and centre
$o\in a_K\mathbb Z^3$ for cell $0$.  Its side in lattice units,
$L^{m_{\mathfrak L}(g)+K}$, is odd and at least three, so its
walls are coordinate lattice mirrors through links.
There are eight cells on $T_{\ell_G}$ and
$N_\ell=8(\ell/\ell_G)^3$ on $T_\ell$.
Let $\theta_c$ reflect cell $0$ to $c$, using one wall reflection
in each differing coordinate.  It is an involution.
The balls
\[
 \mathbb B_*=\overline B(o,1/4),\qquad
 \mathbb B_*^{(c)}=\theta_c\mathbb B_*
\]
in different cells have distance at least
$\ell_G/2-1/2\ge\ell_G/4$.

Let $\mathfrak J$ consist of at most sixteen real source
directions, at most two in a cell.  Those in cell $c$ are
members of a pair $(f_c,h_c)\in\mathfrak T(\mathsf d;\vartheta)$,
with $\mathsf d\ge a_K$.  Each support $S_s$ lies in a closed
ball of radius $\mathsf d$; supports in different cells have
distance at least $\ell_G/4$.  Write $D_{\mathrm x}$ for the
least of these distances, so $\mathsf d\le\ell_G/32<D_{\mathrm x}$.

For $\mathsf J\subset\mathfrak J$, let $\mathsf J^c$ be its part
in cell $c$.  Say that $\mathsf J$ joins cells if at least two
sets $\mathsf J^c$ are nonempty.  Define
\[
 \partial_{\mathsf J}
  =\left.\prod_{s\in\mathsf J}\partial_{z_s}\right|_{z=0},
 \qquad w=\sum_s z_s\mathsf g_s,
\]
and let $\operatorname{Part}(\mathsf J)$ be its partitions into
nonempty sets.
The sizes factor over cells:
\[
 \widehat e_l[\{\mathsf g\}]
       =e_l[\mathsf g]\mathfrak l_l^{4\mathfrak p_0+1},
 \quad
 \widehat e_l[\{f_c,h_c\}]=e_l[f_c,h_c],
 \quad
 \widehat e_l[\emptyset]=1,\qquad
 \widehat e_l[\mathsf J]=\prod_c\widehat e_l[\mathsf J^c].
\]
Put $\kappa_{\mathrm B}=\kappa_{\mathrm s}/8$ and
\[
 w_l^{\mathsf J}(Y)
   =\exp\!\left(\kappa_{\mathrm B}
                \sum_{s\in\mathsf J}\delta_l(Y;S_s)\right).
\]
This is a weight system since
$\#\mathsf J\,\kappa_{\mathrm B}\le2\kappa_{\mathrm s}$.
Use the norm
\[
 \|F\|_{l;\mathsf J}
  =\max\{\|F\|_{l;\{1\};\mathscr S_{\mathsf J}},
          \|F_0\|^{\mathrm{arr}}_{l;\{1\};\mathscr S_{\mathsf J}}\},
\]
and also the weaker norm with one pair for the whole sum:
\[
 \|F\|^{\mathrm{pair}}_{l;\mathsf J}
 =\sup_{Z,P}\sup_{\square\subset Z}
     \sum_{\square\subset Y\subset Z}
        e^{\kappa d_l(Y)}w_l^{\mathsf J}(Y)
                 \|F(Y;P|_Y,\cdot;1)\|_{h^{(l)}} .
\]
Here $Z$ may be the whole torus, and $P$ is a regular complex
pair on $Z$.  Restrictions remain regular pairs, so
$\|F\|^{\mathrm{pair}}_{l;\mathsf J}\le\|F\|_{l;\mathsf J}$.
The corresponding step size is
$\epsilon_{\mathsf J}(\delta)
 =\epsilon_{\mathscr S_{\mathsf J}}(\delta)$ of
Lemma~\ref{C-403-45}, with the weight at level $i+1$.
For one source, or a pair in one cell, this size is bounded by
the size with rate $\kappa_{\mathrm s}$ on its supports.

At $\lambda=1$ let
$D^r\widetilde E_i[\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_r]$, $r\le16$, be the
mixed derivative at zero of
\[
 \widetilde E_i\!\left[
       \mathfrak V_i(1)+\sum_at_a\delta_a^{\mathrm p};
       \mathcal V^{\mathrm q}+\sum_at_a\delta_a^{\mathrm o}
                 \right].
\]
Set $\mathbf R^{(l)}[\{\mathsf g\}]=\mathbf P^{(l)}[\mathsf g]$
and $\mathbf R^{(l)}[\{f_c,h_c\}]=\mathbf Q^{(l)}[f_c,h_c]$.
Use $\delta_i[\{\mathsf g\}]=\delta_i[\mathsf g]$; for
$\#\mathsf J\ge2$, put
\[
 \delta_i[\mathsf J]
   =\sum_{l=1}^i\mathcal V_i^{\mathrm{old}}
                              [\mathbf R^{(l)}[\mathsf J]] .
\]
Thus $\delta_0[\mathsf J]=0$ for these sets.
For $\mathsf J$ joining cells, define recursively
\begin{align*}
 \widetilde{\mathbf R}^{(i+1)}[\mathsf J]
   &=\sum_{\pi\in\operatorname{Part}(\mathsf J)}
          D^{\#\pi}\widetilde E_i[\delta_i[b]:b\in\pi],\\
 \mathbf R^{(i+1)}[\mathsf J]
   &=\widetilde{\mathbf R}^{(i+1)}[\mathsf J]
                                      -\mathfrak e_{i+1}[\mathsf J].
\end{align*}
Only the scalar value at the trivial configuration is removed.
The quadratic units of $\mathbf R$ are its polymers.
Finally set
\[
 \eta_{\mathrm x}
  =\min\{7\kappa_{\mathrm s}/8,\,2c_E/c'\},
 \quad c_E=\log18432,\quad
 c_1=\eta_{\mathrm x}/M,\quad c_{\mathrm x}=c_1/2,\quad
 \varsigma_l^{\mathrm x}=e^{-c_1D_{\mathrm x}/a_l}.
\]
These constants depend only on $\kappa,M,c'$.  Choose them, and
the constants in Lemma~\ref{C-403-61}, after $c_\lambda,\rho$
and before $\gamma_{\mathrm e}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Reading activities at a background]\label{C-403-66}
Use the calibration frame and both admissibility
conditions of the construction.  Let $1\le k\le K$,
$a_k=L^ka_K$, and
\[
 \mathcal S_k=
       \mathcal M^k\{\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset^{(k)}}\ne0\}.
\]
For $V\in\mathcal S_k$ let $\mathsf{Ev}_k(V)$
be its evaluation configurations of
\cref{C-403-65}.
Give the formal background legs of level
$n\le k$ the weights
$h^{(k)}(n)=C_HL^{-(k-n)}h_F$.
Here $C_H$ is the fermion background row
constant.  Write $F\circ\mathsf H(\mathsf U)$
for substitution of
\[
 \Psi_n^{\rm bg}=\mathsf H_{n,k}(\mathsf U)\Psi_k,
 \qquad
 \bar\Psi_n^{\rm bg}
       =\bar\Psi_k\bar{\mathsf H}_{k,n}(\mathsf U).
\]
For $V\in\mathcal S_k$ and
$\mathsf U\in\mathsf{Ev}_k(V)$ the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every level $1\le l\le k$ and
polymer $X\in\mathcal D_l$, the pair of
$\mathsf U$ on $X$ lies in the regular
core at radii $\alpha_0/2,\alpha_1/2$.
These pairs agree under restriction between
levels and polymers.  At every bare plaquette,
\[
 |\partial\mathsf U(p)-1|<\tfrac12\alpha_0L^{-2k},
 \qquad |a_p(\mathsf U)|<\tfrac18\alpha_0^2L^{-4k}.
\]
\item For $n<k$, every row satisfies
\[
 \sum_y\|\mathsf H_{n,k}(\mathsf U)(x,y)\|
       \le\tfrac12C_HL^{-(k-n)}.
\]
The same bound holds for the barred row
maps, and $\mathsf H_{k,k}=1$.  Thus the
weighted row inequality
$h_F\sum_y\|\mathsf H_{n,k}(x,y)\|
\le h^{(k)}(n)/2$ holds also for $n=k$.
\item If $F_p$ is the degree-$p$ part of
$F\in\mathrm{Gr}^{\rm bg}_k(T_\ell)$, then
\[
 \|F\circ\mathsf H(\mathsf U)\|_{h_F}
       \le\sum_p2^{-p}\|F_p\|_{h^{(k)}}.
\]
\item For a family of terms $G(X;q,\cdot;\lambda)$
over polymers at levels $l(X)\le k$,
\[
 \begin{split}
 &\sup_{\lambda\in D}
 \left\|\sum_XG(X;\mathbf p_X^{(l(X))}(\mathsf U),
                     \cdot;\lambda)
                        \circ\mathsf H(\mathsf U)\right\|_{h_F}\\
 &\quad\le
 \sup_{\lambda\in D}\sum_X
       \|G(X;\mathbf p_X^{(l(X))}(\mathsf U),
                     \cdot;\lambda)\|_{h^{(k)}}\\
 &\quad\le\sum_X\sup_{\lambda\in D}\sup_q
                         \|G(X;q,\cdot;\lambda)\|_{h^{(k)}}.
 \end{split}
\]
For a level-$k$ family the middle expression
evaluates all terms at restrictions of one
regular pair $P$ on the torus.
With the source norms of \cref{C-403-43},
if $S$ lies in a closed ball of radius
$r\ge a_K$, it is bounded by
\[
 e^{\kappa/16}C_{\mathcal C}(1+r/a_k)^3
                         \|G\|^{\rm o}_{k;D;S},
\]
and the last expression by the same factor
times $\|G\|_{k;D;S}$.
For two supports $S_f,S_h$ the corresponding
bounds are
$e^{\kappa/8}\mathcal C'_k
\|G\|^{\rm o}_{k;D;S_f,S_h}$
and
$e^{\kappa/8}\mathcal C'_k
\|G\|_{k;D;S_f,S_h}$.
\item For a scalar- or matrix-valued function
$c(x;\lambda)$ on bare sites,
\[
 \begin{split}
 &\sup_{\lambda\in D}
 \|L^{-k}\mathsf S_1
       (c(\cdot;\lambda)\mathsf H_{0,k}(\mathsf U)\Psi_k)
                                                 \|_{h_F}\\
 &\quad\le
 \tfrac14c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2
      \sum_\square\frac1{M^3L^{3k}}
          \sum_{x\in\square}\sup_{\lambda\in D}|c(x;\lambda)|\\
 &\quad\le
 \tfrac14C_{\mathcal C}(1+r/a_k)^3
                    c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2\langle c\rangle_{k;D;S}.
 \end{split}
\]
Here $|\cdot|$ is the operator norm for
matrix values, $c_{\mathsf S}=M^3\nu_P\nu C_H^2$,
and $\nu_P$ is the number of places at a
bare site.
\end{enumerate}
The same assertions hold almost everywhere
on the support of the level-$k$ density
test against the coordinate reference measure.
There the regular radii are $\alpha_0,\alpha_1$
and the plaquette bounds are
$\alpha_0L^{-2k}$ and
$\alpha_0^2L^{-4k}/2$, respectively.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The calibration frame is admitted at every
level.  The background part of its induction
theorem gives nonempty evaluation sets on
$\mathcal S_k$, with pairs in the stated
half-radius cores on every polymer in
$\Lambda_l=T_\ell$.
For a bare plaquette $p$, the union $X(p)$
of the cubes containing its corners is
one, two or four cubes and is an admitted
polymer.  All four bonds lie in its
interior bond set.  The core's plaquette
condition there gives
$|\partial\mathsf U(p)-1|<\alpha_0L^{-2k}/2$.
For $\mathrm{SU}(2)$,
$|a_p(\mathsf U)|=
|\det(\partial\mathsf U(p)-1)|/2$,
giving the action bound.
Restrictions are the restrictions of one
bare field and its level currents, so
have the required consistency.
The almost-everywhere clause of the same
background theorem gives the full-radius
cores outside a Borel null set on the
density-test support.  The argument at
$X(p)$ then gives the stated full-radius
plaquette bounds.

Each evaluation configuration is real.
The ceiling on $\alpha_0$ makes the
plaquette bound at most
$\epsilon_*L^{-2k}$.
There are no lower layers and the mass
satisfies $m_0=L^{-K}\mathsf m\le L^{-K}/2$.
These are the hypotheses of the fermion
background row estimate, which gives
\[
 \sum_y\|\mathsf H_{n,k}(x,y)\|
 \le(1+C_\Sigma L^{3/2})C_H^\circ L^{-(k-n)}
 \le\tfrac12C_HL^{-(k-n)} .
\]
The barred map has the same estimate.
At $n=k$ use $C_H\ge2$.

Give each formal leg weight $h^{(k)}(n)/2$.
The row estimates show that substitution
contracts the exterior-algebra norm into
the norm of weight $h_F$.
That norm is the sum of the norms of
the homogeneous parts, and halving the
weights multiplies the degree-$p$ norm
by $2^{-p}$.  This proves (iii).
Apply it term by term and use the triangle
inequality to obtain (iv).
At level $k$, the torus itself is an
admitted polymer, so its regular pair
restricts to all the pairs in this sum.
The source-weight summation estimate of
\cref{C-403-53} therefore applies both
with the common-pair supremum outside the
sum and with the separate suprema inside.
Its cell count is at most
$C_{\mathcal C}(1+r/a_k)^3$,
since distance to $S$ is at least distance
to any ball containing $S$.

Finally a bare mass monomial at one place
has norm at most
$\nu|c(x)|C_H^2L^{-2k}h_F^2$.
Include $L^{-k}$ and the $\nu_P$ places
at each of the $M^3L^{3k}$ bare sites
in a cell.  This gives
$c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2$ times its cell mean.
Its degree is two, so substitution gains
the factor $1/4$.
The weighted mean in \cref{C-403-43}
bounds this cell mean by
$e^{-\kappa_{\rm s}\delta_k(\square;S)}
\langle c\rangle_{k;D;S}$.
Summing cells and using the same cell
count proves (v).
\end{proof}

\subsection{Constants for the complex field scale}

The field-scale argument uses a larger analytic disc than the
local parameter disc of a single step.  We choose its constants
in an order that leaves the feedback contractions available.

\begin{remark}[Order of the constants]\label{C-403-16}
Retain the order of the constants in the lattice construction.
The following additional choices are made before selecting the
datum.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
With the gauge constants fixed, choose $\mathsf t_\flat$ so
that for every $\mathsf t\ge\mathsf t_\flat$,
\[
 \mathsf t\ge e^{2\mathfrak p_0},\qquad
 \mathsf C_{\mathcal A}\delta(\mathsf t)\le\varepsilon_P,\qquad
 \mathfrak b(\mathsf t)^2\ge M^3,\qquad
 (1+\beta_s)\delta(\mathsf t)\le\mathsf s^\star\alpha_0 .
\]
Here $\delta(\mathsf t)=
A_1\mathsf t^{-1/2}(\log\mathsf t)^{\mathfrak p_0}$,
$\mathfrak b(\mathsf t)=A_1(\log\mathsf t)^{\mathfrak p_0}$,
$\varepsilon_P$ is the vertex radius, and $\mathsf s^\star$
is the admissible scalar-localisation ceiling.
These conditions hold eventually and depend only on constants
chosen before the coupling ceiling.

\item
Choose the source-weight constants before $h_F$:
$\kappa_{\mathrm s}$, $C_{\mathcal C}\ge8M^3$,
$C_{\mathrm{rd}},C_{\mathrm{mo}}\ge1$,
$K_{\mathfrak n}=3c_{\mathsf S}c_b^{-2}C_{\mathrm{mo}}$,
the torus-defect constants, and the sums
$S_{\mathrm{tor}},S_\diamond$ in
Lemmas~\ref{C-403-46}--\ref{C-403-49}.
The direct source constants are
\[
 A_{\mathrm{src}}
 =3\max\{\alpha_0^2,\,
       2^{13}\mathsf c_{\mathrm{os}}\alpha_0C_{\mathrm{cf}}/c_h\}
                 (1+2M^3c_{\mathrm{cl}}/w_*),\qquad
 C_{\mathrm{src}}=3^5C_\Sigma M^3A_{\mathrm{src}}.
\]
The mass-mean constant is $C_{\mathrm{mn}}=37$.
Also choose
\[
 C_{\mathrm{Lip}}=78\pi e\,\kappa_{\mathrm s}^{-4},\qquad
 \Sigma_{\mathrm w}
   =\sum_{u\ge0}L^{2u}q_{u+1}^2
                         e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm s}(L^u-1)},\qquad
 C_{\mathfrak l}
   =\sup_{t\ge1}t^{-7/2}(1+\log t)^{8\mathfrak p_0+2}.
\]
These constants do not depend on $h_F$.

Increase $h_F$ to satisfy, in addition to its previous floors,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:C403-F1}
 3K_\mu^{\mathrm s}K_MC_{\mathrm{rd}}C_{\mathcal C}
       (1+2C_{\mathrm{mo}})S_\diamond\,c'_\psi(h_F)\le\frac14,
 \qquad
 c'_\psi(h)
   =\frac{2A_\kappa\Gamma_F}{h}
      +\frac{(c_h/a_{\mathrm{an}}+C_G)c_{\mathrm{cl}}}
                   {4C_Vh^2}.
\end{equation}
Every factor other than $c'_\psi(h_F)$ is already fixed, and
$c'_\psi(h)\to0$.
Choose $C^+$ from the reduction before the lower mass endpoint.

\item
After the original coupling ceiling $\gamma$, put
\begin{align*}
 C_V^\lambda
   &=(4K_P+c_h\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}K_{\mathrm{old}}/
                           a_{\mathrm{an}})A_12^{\mathfrak p_0+1},\\
 C_F^\lambda
   &=C_Vh_F^2\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}A_12^{\mathfrak p_0+1}
                   +2c'_\psi c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2\bar B_M,\\
 C_\eta
   &=8\bigl[K_M(C_V^\lambda+C_F^\lambda+2)
                         +6Lc_{\mathsf S}h_F^2\bar B_M\bigr].
\end{align*}
Choose $c_\lambda\ge1$ so large that
\begin{gather*}
 c_\lambda\ge4\bar B/r_x,\qquad
 A_12^{\mathfrak p_0+1}c_\lambda^{-1/2}
                                  \le\delta(\mathsf t_\flat),\\
 \beta_\lambda
   :=\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}A_12^{\mathfrak p_0+1}c_\lambda^{-1/2}
       \le\min\{\beta_0/2,\,
                c_{\mathrm{cl}}/(4C_Vh_F^2),\,
                a_{\mathrm{an}}/(3c_h)\},\\
 (C_V^\lambda+C_F^\lambda+C_\eta)c_\lambda^{-1/2}
                                           \le c_{\mathrm{cl}}/4,\\
 2K_M^\bullet(C_V^\lambda+C_F^\lambda+C_\eta+2)
                                        c_\lambda^{-1/2}\le1/2,
\end{gather*}
and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:C403-F2}
 6K_\mu^{\mathrm s}K_MC_{\mathrm{rd}}C_{\mathcal C}
       (1+2C_{\mathrm{mo}})S_\diamond
                         c_h\beta_\lambda/a_{\mathrm{an}}\le1/4 .
\end{equation}
Put $\eta=C_\eta c_\lambda^{-1/2}$ and
$s_\lambda=c_h\beta_\lambda/a_{\mathrm{an}}\le1/3$.
The two inequalities \eqref{eq:C403-F1} and
\eqref{eq:C403-F2} give the contraction factor

\begin{equation}\label{C-403-50}
 C_{\mathrm{fb}}

Choose the constants for sources joining cells after these.
Finally choose $0<\gamma_{\mathrm e}\le\gamma$ below the

\[
 \gamma_{\mathrm e}^{-2}\ge2\mathsf t_\flat,\qquad
 \log\gamma_{\mathrm e}^{-2}\ge\mathsf Y_{\mathrm e},
\]
and, for every $x\ge\gamma_{\mathrm e}^{-2}$,
\[
 x(\log x)^{-2\mathfrak p_0}\ge c_\lambda/\rho^2,\qquad
 C_w\phi(x)\le1/2,\qquad

All three conditions hold eventually.
For the radii used below this gives
\[
 (\rho\bar\lambda_j)^2\ge2,\qquad

 C_{\mathrm{fb}}\bar\lambda_j^{-2}\le1/2 .
\]

\item
After $g$ choose $\ell_G,X_g,\mathsf b_\pm$ and the constants

After $(g,\vartheta)$ choose the response bounds
$A^{\mathrm{red}},A_c,C_{\mathrm{wr}}^{\mathfrak N},
B_f,A_{\mathfrak N},A^{\mathrm{rsp}},
A_{\mathbf P},A'_{\mathbf P},A_{\mathbf Q}$,
then $C_{\mathfrak e,1},C_{\mathfrak e,2},
C_{\mathrm{iii}},C_m^{\mathrm{ii}}$,
the bounds for sources joining cells, and finally
$C_{\mathrm T},\mathsf d_{\mathrm R},C_{\mathrm R},
\epsilon_{\mathrm R}$.
The transfer between sides is chosen at this stage.
The comparison with lattice perturbation theory additionally
depends on the cutoff-window exponent $P>1$ and is chosen
after $(g,\vartheta,P)$.
No constant chosen at an earlier stage depends on a later
choice.
\end{enumerate}
\end{remark}

\subsection{Slab operators for chamber fermions}

The comparison between two torus sizes requires an estimate for
unnormalized integrals. We prove it by writing a folded insertion
as the trace of a power of one positive operator. The operator
depends on the cross-section and the cell, but not on the number
of cells in the direction being shortened.

Work in lattice units with the chamber operator at \(r=1/2\),
\(\beta\ge0\), and \(m_0>0\). Gauge fields are periodic and
fermions antiperiodic on a rectangular torus with even side lengths.
Write
\[
 \Omega(F)=\int dU\int d\bar\psi\,d\psi\,
                  e^{-\beta A-\bar\psi(D[U]+m_0)\psi}F .
\]
The determinant is positive and \(Z=\Omega(1)>0\), by
\cite[Prop.\ 2.1]{QCDM1}. The proof of that proposition uses
unitarity of the nearest-neighbour shifts and the two adjoint
chiral blocks; it applies without change to these rectangular
antiperiodic tori.

Fix a coordinate direction and an odd integer \(\lambda\ge3\).
Cut the torus at parallel planes, separated by \(\lambda\),
that bisect gauge links. A slab contains \(\lambda\) layers of
sites, all chambers at those sites, and the gauge links between
them. Every link, plaquette and chamber hop is either internal
to one slab or crosses exactly one wall. For chamber hops this
uses the fact that only \(s=0\) changes the site.

On each bisected link substitute
\(U_b=V_b'{}^{-1}V_b\), with \(V_b,V'_b\) independent Haar
variables. This substitution preserves the integral and assigns
one half-link variable to each neighbouring slab.
Let \(J_{\rm sl}\) denote integration over the gauge and
Grassmann variables of one model slab, including its half links,
with the exponential of the internal action. A slab element is
an even Grassmann polynomial in these generators with bounded
Borel coefficients in its gauge variables.

The wall contribution to the exponent has the form
\[
 -\beta n_\times+Y+X_F,\qquad
 Y=\frac{\beta}{2}\sum_{\substack{p\ {\rm cut}\\a,b}}
                       A^p_{ab}\Theta(A^p_{ab}),
\]
where \(n_\times\) counts the cut plaquettes and \(A^p\)
is transport along the half boundary of \(p\), including the
half links. For a crossing chamber \(v\), with the normal \(n\)
pointing toward \(v\), put
\(\chi=V_b\psi(v)\), \(\bar\chi=\bar\psi(v)V_b^{-1}\).
Its pair of fermion hops contributes
\[
 \sum_{i,j}\bar\chi_i
             \bigl(t_s+\tfrac12t_s\gamma(n)\bigr)_{ij}
                                      \Theta\bar\chi_j
 +\sum_{i,j}\chi_j
             \bigl(t_s-\tfrac12t_s\gamma(n)\bigr)_{ij}
                                      \Theta\chi_i.
\]
Both matrices have eigenvalues \(t_s/2,3t_s/2\).
These are the half-link and crossing identities in the proof of
\cite[Thm.\ B]{QCDM1}; they are identities at a wall on the
covering lattice, so they apply at every wall of this partition.

Diagonalize the positive matrices and expand the gauge exponential.
Products of terms \(G\Theta G\), with \(G\) homogeneous, have
the same form. The fermion exponential is a finite sum and the
gauge exponential converges uniformly. We obtain
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcd-slab-crossing}
 e^{Y+X_F}=\sum_{\alpha\in I}c_\alpha G_\alpha\Theta G_\alpha,
 \qquad c_\alpha\ge0,\qquad
       \sum_{\alpha\in I}c_\alpha\sup\|G_\alpha\|^2<\infty .
\end{equation}
Here \(I\) is countable, each \(G_\alpha\) is homogeneous, and
the norm is any fixed coefficient norm on the finite-dimensional
Grassmann algebra at the wall. The same family is used at all
walls by translation. It depends on the transverse torus and
the model parameters, not on the number of slabs.

For a slab element \(X\), define a matrix on \(\ell^2(I)\) by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcd-slab-operator}
 \mathfrak Y[X]_{\alpha\alpha'}
 =(c_\alpha c_{\alpha'})^{1/2}
 J_{\rm sl}\bigl((\Theta G_\alpha)^{\rm left}
                         XG_{\alpha'}^{\rm right}\bigr).
\end{equation}
The superscripts specify the two faces of the slab. Let
\(X^\Theta\) be reflection of \(X\) in its middle plane,
with the antilinear reversal of Grassmann products. This middle
plane passes through sites; only reflection invariance, not a
positivity assertion at that plane, is used below.

\begin{lemma}[The slab trace]\label{lem:qcd-slab-trace}
The operator \(\mathfrak Y[X]\) is Hilbert--Schmidt and
\(\mathfrak Y[X^\Theta]=\mathfrak Y[X]^*\).
For an even number \(q\ge2\) of slabs and even slab elements
\(X_1,\ldots,X_q\), the product below is trace class and
\begin{equation}\label{C-387-16}
 \Omega\left(\prod_{t=1}^qX_t\right)
 =e^{-\beta n_\times q}
       \operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\mathfrak Y[X_1]\cdots
                                      \mathfrak Y[X_q]\bigr).
\end{equation}
The operators in this identity do not depend on \(q\).
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Expand \eqref{eq:qcd-slab-crossing} at each wall, with
\(G_{\alpha_t}\) in slab \(t\) and
\(\Theta G_{\alpha_t}\) in slab \(t+1\).
The product of crossing factors can be ordered as
\[
 G_{\alpha_1}
 [\Theta G_{\alpha_1}G_{\alpha_2}]\cdots
 [\Theta G_{\alpha_{q-1}}G_{\alpha_q}]
                                  \Theta G_{\alpha_q}.
\]
The bracket at position \(t\) belongs to slab \(t\).
Moving the last factor to the front costs
\((-1)^{p(\alpha_q)}\), since the preceding product has
the same parity. That last factor is initially in slab \(q+1\).
When expressed in the generators of slab \(1\), the
antiperiodic boundary condition contributes the same sign.
The two signs cancel.

A bracket with unequal boundary parities is odd and integrates
to zero. All other brackets are even, commute, and integrate
separately over the slabs. Allocating half of each \(c_{\alpha_t}\)
to each adjacent slab gives exactly the matrix product in
\eqref{C-387-16}. The scalar factors from the walls give
\(e^{-\beta n_\times q}\).

Reflection in the slab's middle plane exchanges its faces
and preserves its internal action and Haar measure. It sends
the Berezin top monomial to its conjugate with sign \(+1\):
the determinants of the two spin matrices cancel.
Consequently \(J_{\rm sl}(F^\Theta)=\overline{J_{\rm sl}(F)}\).
On entries that can be nonzero the two boundary parities
agree, so the face exchange gives
\(\mathfrak Y[X^\Theta]_{\alpha\alpha'}
 =\overline{\mathfrak Y[X]_{\alpha'\alpha}}\).

The summability in \eqref{eq:qcd-slab-crossing} also justifies
these rearrangements. On the finite-dimensional slab algebra,
integration against the internal weight is a bounded linear
functional. Thus, for a constant depending on the fixed slab
and \(X\),
\[
 |\mathfrak Y[X]_{\alpha\alpha'}|
 \le C_X(c_\alpha c_{\alpha'})^{1/2}
                 \sup\|G_\alpha\|\sup\|G_{\alpha'}\|.
\]
Its squared entries are summable by
\eqref{eq:qcd-slab-crossing}. This proves the Hilbert--Schmidt
assertion. Products of at least two such operators are trace
class. Finite truncations of \(I\) converge in Hilbert--Schmidt
norm; their products converge in trace norm. The absolutely
convergent expansion of the original integral has the same
limit, proving the trace identity.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The unnormalized two-volume inequality}

Let \(\lambda\ge3\) be odd, let
\(\mathsf n_\nu\ge2\) be even integers, and put
\[
 \mathfrak G=\lambda(\mathsf n_1\mathbb Z
                 \times\mathsf n_2\mathbb Z\times\mathsf n_3\mathbb Z),
 \qquad \mathsf N=\mathsf n_1\mathsf n_2\mathsf n_3.
\]
For \(o\in\mathbb Z^3\), the board cells are
\[
 \square_{\mathbf k}
 =\{x:|x_\nu-o_\nu-\lambda\mathbf k_\nu|
                       \le(\lambda-1)/2,\ \nu=1,2,3\},
 \qquad \mathbf k\in\prod_\nu\mathbb Z/\mathsf n_\nu\mathbb Z.
\]
A cell element has generators only at chambers whose sites
belong to that cell, is even, and has bounded Borel coefficients
depending only on links with both endpoints in the cell.
Its mirror copies \(G^{[\mathbf k']}\) are obtained by
reflection at the intervening cell walls and even translations.
Write
\[
 \operatorname{Fold}G=\prod_{\mathbf k'}G^{[\mathbf k']},
 \qquad
 \|G\|_{{\rm ch},\mathsf n}
   =\left(\frac{\Omega_{\mathsf n}(\operatorname{Fold}G)}
                                             {Z_{\mathsf n}}\right)^{1/\mathsf N}.
\]

\begin{proposition}[Two-volume chessboard estimate]\label{C-387-15}
For the chamber model with \(\beta\ge0\), \(m_0>0\), and
antiperiodic fermions, the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(C\arabic*),start=0]
\item Mirror copies are well defined on the even cell algebra,
preserve products, and compose according to their destination cells.
\item Folded integrals are nonnegative, and
\[
 \left|\Omega_{\mathsf n}\left(\prod_{\mathbf k}G_{\mathbf k}\right)\right|
 \le\prod_{\mathbf k}
          \Omega_{\mathsf n}(\operatorname{Fold}G_{\mathbf k})^{1/\mathsf N}.
\]
In particular \(|\langle G\rangle_{\mathsf n}|
\le\|G\|_{{\rm ch},\mathsf n}\) for one cell element.
\item[(C3)] Let another board have the same \(\lambda\) and
cell zero, with even \(2\le\mathsf n'_\nu\le\mathsf n_\nu\).
For one fixed cell element \(G_0\),
\[
 0\le\Omega_{\mathsf n}(\operatorname{Fold}G_0)
 \le
 \Omega_{\mathsf n'}(\operatorname{Fold}G_0)^{
                         \prod_\nu\mathsf n_\nu/\mathsf n'_\nu}.
\]
The physical spacing, \(\beta\), \(m_0\), and the cell element
are the same in the two integrals.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Two parallel reflections compose to a translation up to a
parity sign. Two orthogonal reflections anticommute on a
generator, and translation by a period changes its sign.
All these signs disappear on even elements. This proves
(C0), including independence of the route through the cells.

For (C1), group the cell elements into slabs in direction \(1\),
and denote their products by \(X_t\). Apply
\cref{lem:qcd-slab-trace} and Schatten H\"older:
\[
 \left|\operatorname{Tr}\prod_{t=1}^{\mathsf n_1}
                                    \mathfrak Y[X_t]\right|
 \le\prod_t\|\mathfrak Y[X_t]\|_{\mathsf n_1}.
\]
All operators are Hilbert--Schmidt, hence belong to the
Schatten class of even order \(\mathsf n_1\ge2\).
Writing \(Y=\mathfrak Y[X_t]\), its factor obeys
\[
 \|Y\|_{\mathsf n_1}^{\mathsf n_1}
 =\operatorname{Tr}(Y^*Y)^{\mathsf n_1/2}.
\]
The trace formula identifies this with
\(e^{\beta n_\times\mathsf n_1}\) times the integral
obtained by filling direction \(1\) with \(X_t\) and
\(X_t^\Theta\) alternately. It is nonnegative.
The scalar exponential cancels the one in
\eqref{C-387-16}. Repeat in directions \(2\) and \(3\).
This gives the displayed inequality and nonnegativity
of each fully folded integral.
Taking all but one cell element equal to \(1\) and dividing
by \(Z_{\mathsf n}>0\) gives the normalized assertion.

For (C3), first keep \(\mathsf n_2,\mathsf n_3\) fixed.
Fold \(G_0\) in those two directions within one slab,
and call this slab element \(X\). The fold in direction \(1\)
has alternating slabs \(X,X^\Theta\). Therefore
\[
 \Omega_{\mathsf n}(\operatorname{Fold}G_0)
   =e^{-\beta n_\times\mathsf n_1}
                    \operatorname{Tr}B^{\mathsf n_1/2},
 \qquad B=\mathfrak Y[X]^*\mathfrak Y[X]\ge0.
\]
The operator \(B\) is trace class and independent of
\(\mathsf n_1\). If \(k\ge k'\ge1\) and \(b_i\) are
its eigenvalues, then
\[
 \operatorname{Tr}B^k=\sum_i(b_i^{k'})^{k/k'}
            \le\left(\sum_i b_i^{k'}\right)^{k/k'}.
\]
For completeness, when the sum on the right is positive,
divide by it: the resulting nonnegative numbers sum to
one, and each has its \(k/k'\)-th power at most itself.
When the sum is zero the claim is immediate.
Apply this with \(k=\mathsf n_1/2\),
\(k'=\mathsf n'_1/2\). The scalar exponential has exactly
the same power, so it gives the desired inequality when
only the first side changes. Next shorten the second
side and then the third, using the already shortened
transverse tori. The powers multiply to
\(\prod_\nu\mathsf n_\nu/\mathsf n'_\nu\).
\end{proof}

In physical coordinates the board may have any offset in
\(a_K\mathbb Z^3\). In the side comparison of \cref{C-403-38},
its cell side is \(\ell_G/2\), so
\(\lambda=\ell_G/(2a_K)\) is an odd power of \(L\) and at
least \(3\). The least torus has two cells in each direction;
on \(\ell=2L^m\) the number is
\(2L^{m-m_{\mathfrak L}(g)}\). Both boards therefore satisfy
(C3), with the same cell zero and exponent
\((\ell/\ell_G)^3\). For a bounded real cell function \(Y\),
\[
 \|Y\|_{{\rm ch},\ell}
 \le\|Y\|_{{\rm ch},\ell_G}
 \left(\frac{Z_{\ell_G}^{(\ell/\ell_G)^3}}{Z_\ell}
                                      \right)^{1/N_\ell},
 \qquad N_\ell=8(\ell/\ell_G)^3.
\]
The partition-function ratio is retained here: (C3) compares
unnormalized integrals and does not assert monotonicity of
their normalized ratios.

\subsection{Reduction to the mixed source energies}

At zero source, positivity gives a lower bound for the contribution
with no large-field region.  At a complex source, the history
estimate gives an upper bound for its complement.  We use these
bounds at a level whose remaining volume grows only logarithmically
as the separation decreases.  Averaging over many translates then
removes the volume cost from differentiating the complementary
contribution.

Here are the constants used in this reduction.  Retain the
source-history rate
$c=(c_\star+c_\Theta)/2$, the share $\eth\in(0,1)$ and
$c_\eth=(1-\eth)c$.  Set
\[
 C^+=\max\{C,\mathsf C_{\mathrm{maj}}+\lambda_L\},\quad
 \mathsf C_{\mathrm{maj}}=48L^3C_E^F+C'_\star,\quad
 \lambda_L=(6L^3+1)\log2 .
\]
The constant $C$ is the source-history norm constant, enlarged if
necessary before the mass interval is chosen.  Impose the history
tail threshold
\[
 \log\gamma_{\mathrm e}^{-2}\ge
 \mathsf Y_{\mathrm e}
 =\max\{\mathsf Y_{\mathrm b},2\log(1+\bar B)\},
\]
formed at $(c,\mathsf C_{\mathrm{maj}},
C_\flat^F+C'_{\mathfrak E},\eth)$.  All its parameters precede
$\gamma_{\mathrm e}$ in the choice of constants.

For fixed $g\le\gamma_{\mathrm e}$ write
\[
 \ell_G=\ell_G(g),\qquad X_g=L(g^{-2}+B_\sharp),\qquad
 \mathsf b_-=g^{-2}+\bar B,\qquad
 \mathsf b_+=X_g-\bar B .
\]
Thus $\mathsf b_\pm$ are the ends of the label interval.
With the empty-history lower-bound constant $C_P$, put
\begin{align*}
 c_V^+(m)&=C^++2+C_P(1+\log(X_gL^m)),\\
 \mathsf Q_{K-m}
   &=\exp\{c_V^+(m)\ell_G^3L^{3m}\},\\
 \mathsf Q&=\mathsf Q_K,\qquad
 M_0=\exp\{(C^++2)\ell_G^3\}.
\end{align*}
For $0<\mathsf d\le\mathsf Q^{-8}$ define
\begin{align}
 m_*(\mathsf d)
  &=\max\{m\ge0:
         8c_V^+(m)\ell_G^3L^{3m}\le\log(1/\mathsf d)\},
       \label{eq:C403-reduction-depth}\\
 \omega_{\mathrm r}(\mathsf d)
  &=\min\left\{1,\,
       2M^{-3}\ell_G^3L^{3m_*}
       e^{-c_\eth A_0^2
                (\log(\mathsf b_-L^{m_*}))^{2\mathfrak p_0}}\right\}.
       \label{eq:C403-reduction-tail}
\end{align}
The constants from Lemmas~\ref{C-403-46} and
\ref{C-403-49}--\ref{C-403-53} determine
\begin{align*}
 C_{\mathrm T}
   =\max\bigl\{1,\,
     &(8e^{\kappa/16}A_{\mathbf P}
                   +e^{\kappa/8}A_{\mathbf Q})C_{\mathcal C}
         [1+C_{\mathrm{rd}}C_{\mathcal C}
                         (1+2C_{\mathrm{mo}})S_\diamond]\\
     &+2C_{\mathcal C}A_{\mathfrak N}
                         +81\alpha_0^2/8\bigr\},\\
 \mathsf d_{\mathrm R}
   &=\min\{\mathsf d_0(g,\vartheta),\,1/400,\,
                        e^{-8c_V^+(1)\ell_G^3L^3}\},\\
 C_{\mathrm R}
   &=\max\{C_{\mathfrak e,2}
                  +2C_{\mathrm T}^2(1+C_{\mathfrak l}),\,
       7\cdot24^3\cdot1600M^2\mathsf Q^3
                           \varrho^{-2}\vartheta^{-2}\ell_G^{-3}\},\\
 \epsilon_{\mathrm R}(\mathsf d)
   &=\mathsf b_+^3C_{\mathrm R}
         \sup_{0<\mathsf d'\le\mathsf d}
                     [\omega_{\mathrm r}(\mathsf d')+\mathsf d'] .
\end{align*}
Choose these constants after the source-derivative constants and
before the threshold in the final short-distance theorem.

\begin{lemma}[Reduction to source energies]\label{C-403-30}
Assume the two admissibility conditions for the source flow and
the floor on $h_F$ in \ref{C-403-16}.  Let
$0<\mathsf d\le\mathsf d_{\mathrm R}$ and consider a datum on
$T_{\ell_G}$ with $K>s(\mathsf d)$ and a pair
$(f,h)\in\mathfrak T(\mathsf d;\vartheta)$.  Put
$k=K-m_*(\mathsf d)$.

The function $\epsilon_{\mathrm R}$ is nondecreasing and tends
to zero at zero.  Moreover,
\[
 1\le k\le K-1,\qquad a_k\ge\mathsf d,\qquad
 a_k^{-3}\le\frac{\log(1/\mathsf d)}{128},\qquad
 \mathsf Q_k\le\mathsf d^{-1/8},\qquad
 \mathsf d^{1/4}\log(1/\mathsf d)^{3/2}\le1 .
\]
The following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
Split the full history sum as
$Z[w,0]=\mathsf A_k[w]+\mathsf B_k[w]$, according as
$Z_k(h)=\emptyset$ or $Z_k(h)\ne\emptyset$.
Both terms are entire in the finitely many plaquette values of
$w$.  On the source class $\mathcal P$,
\[
 \mathsf A_k[w]=e^{E_k(w)}\mathsf I_k[w],\qquad
 \mathsf I_k[w]=\operatorname{Ber}
             \int \mathsf g_k e^{\mathsf T_k(w)}\,d\mathscr M_k.
\]
Here $\mathscr M_k$ is the measure for the empty history at level
$k$, and $\mathsf g_k$ is its zero-source density times
$e^{-E_k}$.  At the background $\mathsf U$ of its block field,
\begin{align*}
 \mathsf T_k(w)
   ={}&a_K^{-1}\sum_pw(x(p))a_p(\mathsf U)
       -L^{-k}\mathsf S_1(\sigma_k(w,0)\,\cdot)\\
     &+\sum_{j\le k}\sum_X
       [E^{(j)}(X;\mathsf U,\bar\Psi^{\mathrm{bg}},
                          \Psi^{\mathrm{bg}};(w,0))
        -E^{(j)}(X;\mathsf U,\bar\Psi^{\mathrm{bg}},
                          \Psi^{\mathrm{bg}};0)] .
\end{align*}
This element of $\mathrm{Gr}_k$ is independent of the chosen
member of the minimal orbit.  It is even, vanishes at zero
source, and is holomorphic for $\|w\|_\sharp<4\varrho$.

\item
On $\mathcal P$,
\[
 |e^{-E_K(w)}\mathsf A_k[w]|\le M_0,\qquad
 |e^{-E_K(w)}\mathsf B_k[w]|
                    \le\omega_{\mathrm r}(\mathsf d)M_0.
\]
At zero source,
$e^{-E_K}\mathsf A_k[0]\ge M_0/\mathsf Q$ and
$\mathsf B_k[0]\ge0$.
For disjointly supported complex Lipschitz directions $F,H$,
define
\[
 \mathsf r_1(F)
     =\partial_F\log(1+\mathsf B_k/\mathsf A_k)\big|_0,\qquad
 \mathsf r_2(F,H)
     =\partial_F\partial_H
                        \log(1+\mathsf B_k/\mathsf A_k)\big|_0 .
\]
With $\|F\|_\circ=\|F\|_\sharp/\varrho$,
\[
 |\mathsf r_1(F)|
       \le2\omega_{\mathrm r}\mathsf Q^2\|F\|_\circ,\qquad
 |\mathsf r_2(F,H)|
       \le7\omega_{\mathrm r}\mathsf Q^3
                                   \|F\|_\circ\|H\|_\circ .
\]

\item
Let $\mathcal S_k$ be the actual image set in
Lemma~\ref{C-403-66}.  For an $\mathrm{Gr}_k$-valued function
$F$ on $\mathcal S_k$ for which $\mathsf g_kF$, extended by zero,
is measurable for the completion of $\mathscr M_k$ and has
integrable fibre norm, define
\[
 \langle F\rangle_k
   =\frac{\operatorname{Ber}\int\mathsf g_kF\,d\mathscr M_k}
          {\operatorname{Ber}\int\mathsf g_k\,d\mathscr M_k}.
\]
If $F$ is bounded on $\mathcal S_k$, then
\[
 |\langle F\rangle_k|
      \le\mathsf Q_k\sup_{\mathcal S_k}\|F\|_{h_F}.
\]
For any finite set of Lipschitz directions $F_i$, the functions
$e^{\mathsf T_k(\sum_i z_iF_i)}$ and all their derivatives at
zero belong to this class locally in $z$.  Their integrals are
holomorphic and may be differentiated under the integral.

\item
Writing $\|\cdot\|=\sup_{\mathcal S_k}\|\cdot\|_{h_F}$,
\[
 \|\mathsf T_k[f]\|
    \le C_{\mathrm T}e_k[f]\mathfrak l_k^{4\mathfrak p_0+1},
 \qquad
 \|\mathsf T_k[f,h]\|\le C_{\mathrm T}e_k[f,h].
\]
The first bound also holds for $h$.  All families are evaluated
at one regular pair on the torus before summing them; in
particular, the bounds with one pair outside the polymer sum
are sufficient.

\item
There is a set $\mathcal T$ of
$N\ge(\ell_G/(24\mathsf d))^3$ lattice translations such that
balls of radius $8\mathsf d$ containing the translated pairs
are mutually at distance at least $\mathsf d$.  For every such
set,
\[
 S_2^T((0,f),(0,h))
  =\frac1N\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}
     \left.\partial_{z_1}\partial_{z_2}
       E_K(z_1f^t+z_2h^t)\right|_{z=0}+\mathsf R,
\]
where the arguments of $E_K$ denote the action-source slot and
\[
 |\mathsf R|
  \le C_{\mathrm R}[\omega_{\mathrm r}(\mathsf d)+\mathsf d]
                      \mathsf d\,\mathfrak f
  \le\epsilon_{\mathrm R}(\mathsf d)
                      \mathsf b^{-3}\mathsf d\,\mathfrak f .
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The witness-depth estimate gives
$L^K\mathsf d>4L^3M$, hence
$a_K<\mathsf d/(4L^3M)$.
The defining set in \eqref{eq:C403-reduction-depth} contains
$0,1$, is finite, and contains every fixed integer when
$\mathsf d$ is sufficiently small.  Thus $m_*\ge1$ and
$m_*\to\infty$.  Since $8c_V^+(m)\ell_G^3\ge128$,
\[
 L^{3m_*}\le\frac{\log(1/\mathsf d)}{128}
                 \le\mathsf d^{-3},
 \qquad
 \mathsf Q_k\le\mathsf d^{-1/8}.
\]
It follows that $a_k\ge\mathsf d$ and
$L^{m_*}\le\mathsf d^{-1}<L^K$, so $1\le k\le K-1$.
Also $\mathsf d\le\mathsf Q^{-8}\le e^{-128}$.
For $v\ge128$, $v^{3/2}e^{-v/4}\le1$, which proves the remaining
numerical bound.
If $u=m_*\log L$, the logarithm of the second entry in
\eqref{eq:C403-reduction-tail} is at most
\[
 \log(2M^{-3}\ell_G^3)+3u-c_\eth A_0^2u^{2\mathfrak p_0}.
\]
It tends to $-\infty$ since $2\mathfrak p_0\ge2$.
This proves the asserted properties of $\epsilon_{\mathrm R}$.

The history sum is finite and each term is entire.
Lemma~\ref{C-403-65} identifies $Z_k(h)=\emptyset$ with
restriction to the empty history, and sums all its extensions
back to that history at level $k$.  Its source-dependent
density is therefore the density in (1).  Indeed, the action
source enters linearly, the remaining exponent is even, and
all its terms commute.  Subtracting the zero-source exponent
gives exactly $\mathsf T_k(w)$.

We check that this identity can be evaluated on
$\mathcal S_k$.  Two backgrounds in the minimal orbit differ
by a residual gauge transformation equal to one at the nodes,
including every site of level $k$.  Each plaquette action is
gauge invariant; the tower and its legs transform covariantly;
the activities are jointly gauge invariant; and the mass
coefficient acts trivially on colour.  Thus their values after
reading the legs at level $k$ are the same element of
$\mathrm{Gr}_k$ at both backgrounds.
Every $V\in\mathcal S_k$ has an adapted background by
Lemma~\ref{C-403-66}.  Moreover it passes the level-$k$ density
test: the nonzero empty-history weight contains the factor
$\chi_k(T_{\ell_G})(V)\in\{0,1\}$.
The source flow is holomorphic on $\|w\|_\sharp<4\varrho$ at
the fixed regular-pair radii.  Lemma~\ref{C-403-66} places
these backgrounds in that domain.  This proves (1), including
the claimed holomorphy.

For each top history let $\mathsf g_h[w]$ denote its
unnormalised density.  Berezin integration and $h_F\ge1$ give
\[
 |\mathsf A_k[w]|+|\mathsf B_k[w]|
 \le\sum_h\int\|\mathsf g_h[w]\|_{h_F}
 \le e^{\operatorname{Re}E_K(w)+(C+2)\ell_G^3}
 \le |e^{E_K(w)}|M_0.
\]
For the complementary sum, the history tail estimate at levels
$(K,k)$ gives the more precise bound
\begin{equation}\label{eq:C403-history-tail-application}
 e^{-\operatorname{Re}E_K(w)}
 \sum_{Z_k(h)\ne\emptyset}\int\|\mathsf g_h[w]\|_{h_F}
 \le2M^{-3}\#\mathbb T^{(k)}
          e^{-c_\eth p_0(g_k)^2}
                 \Pi_K(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{maj}}+\lambda_L,c_\eth).
\end{equation}
Its hypotheses hold for the calibration frame: the increments
are zero, the flow bound is $B_\sharp$, and
$\log\mathsf t_K=\log\mathsf b\ge
\log\gamma_{\mathrm e}^{-2}\ge\mathsf Y_{\mathrm e}$.
The required age floor is the chosen floor when $c_a=0$;
when $c_a>0$, it follows from the stronger age floor used for
the source-history sum.  The source pair has parameters
$(c,\mathsf C_{\mathrm{maj}},C_\flat^F+C'_{\mathfrak E})$.
Finally,
\[
 \#\mathbb T^{(k)}=\ell_G^3L^{3m_*},\qquad
 \mathsf t_k\ge\mathsf b_-L^{m_*},\qquad
 \Pi_K(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{maj}}+\lambda_L,c_\eth)\le M_0 .
\]
The last inequality uses the product threshold included in
$\mathsf Y_{\mathrm e}$.  Combining
\eqref{eq:C403-history-tail-application} with the preceding
ordinary norm bound proves the estimate with
$\omega_{\mathrm r}$.
At zero source every history contribution is nonnegative.
The fully empty top history is one of the extensions being
summed, so its lower bound gives
\[
 e^{-E_K}\mathsf A_k[0]
 \ge e^{-C_P(1+\log x_K)\ell_G^3}
 \ge e^{-C_P(1+\log X_g)\ell_G^3}=M_0/\mathsf Q .
\]

For later use we give the derivative estimate explicitly.
The sharp norm of a sum of continuous functions with disjoint
supports is at most the largest sharp norm of its summands
when their coefficients have modulus at most one.
For points in different supports, follow a shortest segment
between them.  The functions vanish at its first exit from
the first support and its last entry into the second.  Their
difference is consequently bounded by the larger Lipschitz
constant times the segment length.  Points in the same
support, or outside all supports, give the same conclusion.
For coefficients of modulus one equality holds.

Set $R_1=\|F\|_\circ^{-1}$ and $R_2=\|H\|_\circ^{-1}$,
omitting a zero direction.  The bidisc $|z_i|\le R_i$ at
$w=z_1F+z_2H$ lies in the interior of $\mathcal P$.
On it put $a=e^{-E_K}\mathsf A_k$ and
$b=e^{-E_K}\mathsf B_k$.  Cauchy's inequalities give
\[
 |a_i|\le M_0/R_i,\quad
 |b_i|\le\omega_{\mathrm r}M_0/R_i,\quad
 |a_{12}|\le M_0/(R_1R_2),\quad
 |b_{12}|\le\omega_{\mathrm r}M_0/(R_1R_2).
\]
At zero, $a_0\ge M_0/\mathsf Q$ and
$0\le b_0\le\omega_{\mathrm r}M_0$.
Differentiate $\log(a+b)-\log a$:
\[
 \mathsf r_1=\frac{a_0b_1-a_1b_0}{a_0(a_0+b_0)}
\]
and
\begin{align*}
 \mathsf r_2={}&
 \frac{b_{12}}{a_0+b_0}
 -\frac{a_{12}b_0}{a_0(a_0+b_0)}
 +a_1a_2\left(\frac1{a_0^2}-\frac1{(a_0+b_0)^2}\right)\\
 &-\frac{a_1b_2+b_1a_2+b_1b_2}{(a_0+b_0)^2}.
\end{align*}
The displayed bounds, $\omega_{\mathrm r}\le1$ and
$\mathsf Q\ge1$ give respectively the constants $2$ and $7$
in (2).

We next justify the quotient and differentiation in (3).
The set $\mathcal S_k$ is the image, under the Borel block
map, of the Borel set where the history weight is nonzero.
It is analytic, hence universally measurable.
The density measure is supported there: every Borel set
disjoint from $\mathcal S_k$ has zero pushforward measure.
Inner regularity then gives zero mass to its complement in
the completed measure.  This argument applies to the norm
measure as well, so extending a function by zero causes no
ambiguity.
At level $k$ the norm and empty-history lower bounds give
\[
 \int\|\mathsf g_k\|_{h_F}\,d\mathscr M_k
       \le e^{(C+2)\#\mathbb T^{(k)}},\qquad
 \operatorname{Ber}\int\mathsf g_k\,d\mathscr M_k
       \ge e^{-C_P(1+\log x_k)\#\mathbb T^{(k)}} .
\]
Since $x_k\le X_gL^{m_*}$, their ratio is at most
$\mathsf Q_k$.  Submultiplicativity of the fibre norm proves
the quotient bound.

For differentiation let
$G(z,V)=\mathsf g_k(V)e^{\mathsf T_k(\sum z_iF_i)(V)}$ on
$\mathcal S_k$ and zero elsewhere.  On a sufficiently small
closed polydisc it is pointwise holomorphic and its norm
integral is uniformly bounded by the source-density estimate.
Apply Cauchy's formula on the boundary of a slightly larger
polydisc.  Tonelli's theorem makes the boundary norm
integral finite, and Fubini's theorem permits its integration
in $V$ first.  The Cauchy integrals therefore give both a
holomorphic integral and its differentiated coefficients.
The same boundary estimate proves integrability of the
derivatives.  No pointwise dominating function in a
neighbourhood of zero is required.

We prove (4) using the exact derivative identities
of Lemma~\ref{C-403-44} at $\lambda=1$:
\begin{align*}
 \mathsf T_k[f]
   &=\mathsf T_k^w[f]
       +\sum_{l\le k}\sum_X\mathbf P^{(l)}[f](X)
       -L^{-k}\mathsf S_1(\mathfrak N_k[f]\,\cdot),\\
 \mathsf T_k[f,h]
   &=\sum_{l\le k}\sum_X\mathbf Q^{(l)}[f,h](X).
\end{align*}
These hold on $\mathcal S_k$ by the density-test check above.
The background row substitution in
Lemma~\ref{C-403-66} has norm at most one.
For any family $G$ read at level $k$ and the pair $P$ of this
background on the torus, it gives
\[
 \left\|\sum_XG(X;P|_X,\cdot)\circ\mathsf H(\mathsf U)\right\|_{h_F}
       \le\sum_X\|G(X;P|_X,\cdot)\|_{h^{(k)}}.
\]
Thus the long-lag estimate, with the pair outside the sum,
applies directly; it need not be replaced by a stronger
termwise supremum.

The support ball contains at most $81(\mathsf d/a_K)^3$
bare plaquette barycentres, and background regularity gives
$|a_p(\mathsf U)|\le\alpha_0^2L^{-4k}/8$.  Hence
\[
 \|\mathsf T_k^w[f]\|
       \le(81\alpha_0^2/8)\|f\|_\infty
                        \mathsf d^3a_k^{-4}
       =(81\alpha_0^2/8)e_k[f].
\]
Lemma~\ref{C-403-51}, followed by the weighted total estimate
in Lemma~\ref{C-403-66}, bounds the old first responses by
\[
 8e^{\kappa/16}C_{\mathcal C}
 [1+C_{\mathrm{rd}}C_{\mathcal C}(1+2C_{\mathrm{mo}})S_\diamond]
 A_{\mathbf P}e_k[f]\mathfrak l_k^{4\mathfrak p_0+1}.
\]
Lemma~\ref{C-403-49} bounds the mass term by
$2C_{\mathcal C}A_{\mathfrak N}
 e_k[f]\mathfrak l_k^{4\mathfrak p_0+1}$.
For the mixed response use Lemma~\ref{C-403-52} and the same
total estimate, with factor $e^{\kappa/8}C_{\mathcal C}$;
the count factor is bounded by $C_{\mathcal C}$ since
$a_k\ge\mathsf d$.  The definition of $C_{\mathrm T}$
now proves (4).

It remains to compare the second derivative of $\log Z$
with that of $E_K$.  For a translated pair, write
\[
 \partial_f\partial_h(\log Z-E_K)
       =-\Delta^{(1)}+\Delta^{(2)}+\mathsf r_2(f,h),
 \qquad
 \Delta^{(1)}
       =\partial_f\partial_h(E_K-E_k),\quad
 \Delta^{(2)}=\partial_f\partial_h\log\mathsf I_k .
\]
Lemma~\ref{C-403-53} and its geometric sum over $j>k$ yield
\[
 |\Delta^{(1)}|
       \le C_{\mathfrak e,2}
                    \mathfrak f\,\mathsf d^{5/2}a_k^{-9/2}.
\]
By (3), evenness and $\mathsf T_k(0)=0$,
\[
 \Delta^{(2)}
 =\langle\mathsf T_k[f,h]
            +\mathsf T_k[f]\mathsf T_k[h]\rangle_k
       -\langle\mathsf T_k[f]\rangle_k
                       \langle\mathsf T_k[h]\rangle_k .
\]
For $a_k\ge\mathsf d$,
\[
 e_k[f]e_k[h]\mathfrak l_k^{8\mathfrak p_0+2}
 =(\mathsf d/a_k)^{7/2}
     (1+\log(a_k/\mathsf d))^{8\mathfrak p_0+2}e_k[f,h]
 \le C_{\mathfrak l}e_k[f,h].
\]
It follows that
\[
 |\Delta^{(2)}|
    \le2\mathsf Q_k^2C_{\mathrm T}^2(1+C_{\mathfrak l})
                                               e_k[f,h].
\]

To bound the averaged $\mathsf r_2$, put
$F_\varepsilon=\sum_t\varepsilon_tf^t$ and
$H_\varepsilon=\sum_t\varepsilon_th^t$ for independent signs
$\varepsilon_t$.  The supports of all the summands, including
the two within each pair, are disjoint.  The sharp norm
observation gives
$\|F_\varepsilon\|_\sharp=\|f\|_\sharp$ and
$\|H_\varepsilon\|_\sharp=\|h\|_\sharp$.
Bilinearity and averaging the signs remove the cross terms:
\[
 \frac1{2^N}\sum_\varepsilon
       \mathsf r_2(F_\varepsilon,H_\varepsilon)
       =\sum_t\mathsf r_2(f^t,h^t).
\]
Consequently, using
$\|f\|_\sharp\le40M\|f\|_\infty/(\vartheta\mathsf d)$,
\[
 \left|\frac1N\sum_t\mathsf r_2(f^t,h^t)\right|
 \le7\cdot24^3\cdot1600M^2\mathsf Q^3
       \varrho^{-2}\vartheta^{-2}\ell_G^{-3}
                    \omega_{\mathrm r}\mathsf d\,\mathfrak f .
\]

Such translations exist.  Set
$\delta=a_K\lceil17\mathsf d/a_K\rceil$ and
$n_\delta=\lfloor\ell_G/\delta\rfloor$.
Then $17\mathsf d\le\delta<18\mathsf d$.
Different points of
$\delta\{0,\ldots,n_\delta-1\}^3$ have torus distance at
least $\delta$: in a differing coordinate the distance is
$\min\{j\delta,\ell_G-j\delta\}\ge\delta$.
The pair lies in a ball of radius $5\mathsf d$ about the
midpoint of its two supporting ball centres, since those
centres have distance at most $8\mathsf d$.
The balls of radius $8\mathsf d$ about their translates
therefore have distance at least $\mathsf d$.
Since $\ell_G\ge2$ and $\mathsf d\le1/400$,
\[
 n_\delta\ge\ell_G/(18\mathsf d)-1
                  \ge\ell_G/(24\mathsf d).
\]

Finally,
\[
 \mathsf Q_k^2e_k[f,h]
 \le\mathfrak f\,\mathsf d^{9/4}
                         \log(1/\mathsf d)^{3/2}
 \le\mathfrak f\,\mathsf d^2 ,
\]
and the same last bound holds for
$\mathfrak f\,\mathsf d^{5/2}a_k^{-9/2}$.
Average the identity for $\log Z-E_K$ over these translations;
translation invariance leaves $S_2^T$ unchanged.
The three preceding estimates give the first remainder bound
in (5).  The second follows from $\mathsf b\le\mathsf b_+$.
All constants are independent of $K,\mathsf b,\mathsf m$,
the position of the pair and the chosen packing.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Reading a nonzero cell moment}

The quadratic cell moment need not vanish during
source differentiation. We record the corresponding
form of the old-activity estimate.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:qcdm2-nonzero-cell-reading}
Let $1\le j\le k$ and $n=k-j$. Let $F$ be an
even family with legs of levels at most $j$,
holomorphic and jointly gauge invariant on the
whole regular pair core, with norm at most
$\epsilon$. If $F$ is a sum of summands, use
the sum of their norms and file each summand
at a cell of its polymer. At the trivial pair,
read its quadratic part in the level-$j$ field
$\Phi$ and write it as units $\beta_u$ filed
at cells $c(u)$, with
\[
 \sum_{u:c(u)=c}\sum_{y,y'}\|\beta_u(y,y')\|
       (1+|y-z_c|_j+|y'-z_c|_j)
                         \le Ch_F^{-2}\epsilon.
\]
Put $m_c=\sum_{u:c(u)=c}\sum_{y,y'}\beta_u(y,y')$.
The units may move diagonal terms from the cell
of a polymer $X$ to the cell of $y$. Require
each such term to be a linear combination of
row and column sums at $y$ of the quadratic
kernels of $F_1(X)$ and $G(X)$, with sum of
coefficient moduli at most two. Here $F=F_1+F_2$,
the families $F_1,G$ have the same structural
properties and norm bounds, and their background
maps may use different fine mass matrices in
the common admitted mass ball.

There is a constant $C_\omega$, independent of
the coupling and $h_F$, such that the local
reading at level $k$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nonzero-cell-reading}
 \|F_{\ge2}\|_{\mathrm{read},k}
  \le C_\omega L^{n/4}\epsilon
                   +C_\omega L^nh_F^2\sup_c\|m_c\|.
\end{equation}
Here the norm is the sum of localized terms
meeting a level-$k$ cube, with weight
$e^{\kappa d_k(Y)}$, followed by the supremum
over cubes. Degree at least four and the
quadratic difference from its transported
trivial-pair value have bound
$C_\omega L^{-n}\epsilon$.
For
\[
 n\ge n_{\rm lag}
 :=\min\{n:2(2A_\kappa C_H)^2L^{-n}\le1\},
\]
the same estimates hold at the final-generator
weight $C_Hh_F$. At smaller lags the background
legs remain formal at their own levels; only
the fluctuation images are expanded in the step.
The quadratic part is bounded whole, without
this subtraction.
The assertions are uniform on the constant
smaller-radius systems and on the shifted
pairs whose amplitude satisfies
$|\mu|c_h\sup|B|\le c_{\rm os}a$, strictly
at lag zero, at pair radius $a$.

On a torus the cell moments are formed piece
by piece with the antiperiodic seam in the
transport. If the family, its moved terms and
its paths are the periodic images of an
infinite-lattice family $F^\infty$ wherever they fit,
assume also that $F^\infty,F_1^\infty,G^\infty$ obey
the same norm and unit bounds. Read them at the
periodic lifts of the fine masses and require
covariance under period translations, with the
antiperiodic seam signs. The same bound then holds
with the moments $m_c^\infty$, which are independent
of the chosen lift. The extra terms are filed on
polymers that wrap around the torus.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The proof of \cite[Lem.\ 7.9]{QCDM1} separates
the higher-degree part, the quadratic variation
with the pair, and the quadratic value at the
trivial pair. Its first two estimates use
holomorphy, gauge invariance and the norm bound;
they do not use the vanishing moment. Thus
only the last step changes.

First note the weights when both stages of a
leg are expanded into their local and walk
terms. At the final weight $C_Hh_F$, a leg
costs at most
$(2A_\kappa C_H)^2L^{-n}$ times its old weight.
At $n\ge n_{\rm lag}$, every leg beyond the
fourth has a spare factor $1/2$. This pays
the polynomial counts in the number of legs.
Four legs and the $L^{3n}$ old cells give
$CL^{-n}\epsilon$. The same two-stage expansion
in the quadratic gauge comparison gives its
$L^{-n}$ bound. Finitely many smaller lags
are bounded by the plain cell count and
absorbed into $C_\omega$.

Split each moved diagonal term into the same
two-walk pieces as the kernel from which it
is formed. Such a piece is supported in the
polymer enlarged by the two walks, and its
site $y$ belongs to that enlarged polymer.
Place it with opposite signs in the original
unit and the unit at the cell of $y$. The
row and column sums obey the same positive
walk bounds as the kernel itself, at either
of the admitted fine masses. In particular,
if $Z_p$ is its enlarged polymer and $m_p$
its constant row-sum contribution,
\[
 \sum_p\|m_p\|_{\rm tr}
               e^{\kappa(d_j(Z_p)-d_j(X))}
 \le CA_\kappa^2h_F^{-2}
                 (\|F(X)\|+\|F_1(X)\|+\|G(X)\|).
\]
The same estimate holds for the absolute
double sum of its kernel. The walk weights
also pay the number of cells from which
a moved piece can reach a fixed cell.

Transport both legs to $z_c$ and write
$\Phi(y)=\Phi(z_c)+[\Phi(y)-\Phi(z_c)]$.
The terms with a difference are exactly
those estimated in \cite[Lem.\ 7.9]{QCDM1}:
the $3/4$ H\"older gain and the first absolute
moment give $C\epsilon L^{-11n/4}$ per old
cell, hence $C\epsilon L^{n/4}$ per new cube.
The terms without a difference now sum to
$\bar\Phi(z_c)m_c\Phi(z_c)$ instead of zero.
Their norm at a cell is at most
$\nu\|m_c\|(C_HL^{-n}h_F)^2$.
There are $L^{3n}$ cells, so their sum has
the second bound in \eqref{eq:nonzero-cell-reading}.
To localize this member, expand its two legs
at level $k$ and file it at the cube of $c$
enlarged successively by their walk polymers.
The weighted walk sums and the counts of
reached cubes cost only fixed factors.

The sum over polymers filed in a cube and
the sum over units filed there differ only
by moved pieces crossing its boundary.
Exponential localization leaves $O(L^{2n})$
such pieces, each with the two-leg factor
$L^{-2n}$. Their bound $C\epsilon$ is absorbed
in the first term. The hull estimate
$d_k(X^{\rm up})\le L^{-n}d_j(X)$ and the
spare old rate pay the path and diameter
factors, as in the cited proof. This also
proves the assertions for summands and for
the larger final-generator weight.

On the torus, nonwrapping pieces and their
lifts have the same constant row sums: the
two seam signs cancel at $z_c$. Hence
$m_c^{\rm tor}-m_c^\infty$ is the sum of
wrapping pieces minus the sum of nonfitting
lifted pieces. Each has
$d_j(Z_p)\ge\ell_j/(2M)-2$. The preceding
walk estimate bounds this difference by
$2C_{\rm wr}h_F^{-2}\epsilon
e^{-\kappa(\ell_j/(2M)-2)}$.
File its pieces at their coarse hulls,
or the torus images of those hulls; these
polymers wrap. Their localized sum is at most
\[
 C\epsilon L^n
  \sum_{d\ge\ell_j/(2M)-2}(1+d)^3
                      e^{-\kappa(1-L^{-n})d}\le C\epsilon,
\]
since $\ell_j/(2M)\ge L^n$.
The small lags are again covered by the
plain count. This proves the torus assertion.
The pair and shift domains are precisely
those in the gauge comparison; reducing
the radii rescales its numerator and its
holomorphic radius by the same factor.
\end{proof}

\subsection{One complex scale for all gauge fluctuations}

We now multiply every gauge fluctuation by the same complex
number $\lambda$.  Fermion fluctuations are left unchanged.
The coupling and mass numbers removed at each step are the
numbers of the original flow.  Their dependence on $\lambda$
is placed in the action and mass term explicitly.  This choice
makes the composition recover the original bare action with
inverse coupling $\beta/\lambda^2$.

Write $\mathsf t_i=L^{-i}\beta=\mathsf b/a_i$ and define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:C403-scaled-coefficients}
 \xi_i(\lambda)=\mathsf t_i+\lambda^2(x_i-\mathsf t_i),
 \qquad
 \tau_i(\lambda)=\xi_i(\lambda)/\mathsf t_i,\qquad
 \bar\lambda_i^2
       =\frac{2x_i}{c_\lambda(\log x_i)^{2\mathfrak p_0}} .
\end{equation}
Let $D_i=\{|\lambda|<\bar\lambda_i\}$.
The action at level $i$ is
$\lambda^{-2}A(L^i\xi_i(\lambda)-\lambda^2a_K^{-1}w,\cdot)$;
the mass term is
$-L^{-i}\mathsf S_1(\lambda^2(s_i+\sigma_i(w,0))\,\cdot)$.
The expression for the action is used through its fluctuation
expansion at $\lambda=0$.

The step keeps the tests and thresholds at $\mathsf t_i$.
Its Gaussian covariance is
$\xi_i(\lambda)^{-1}C_i$, and its quadratic origin is
\[
 \mathcal V^{\mathrm q}
   =-\frac{1-\tau_i(\lambda)}2
       (\mathsf t_i^{1/2}B_i,
                    \widehat{\mathsf G}\mathsf t_i^{1/2}B_i)_1.
\]
Thus the action Hessian has coefficient $\xi_i(\lambda)$,
while the gauge fixing has its calibration coefficient.
The Gaussian normalisation introduces the scalar factor
$\tau_i(\lambda)^{-\dim B_i/2}$.

Use the unscaled vertex functions
$\mathsf v^{\mathrm J}(Y;P,\mathcal A)$ and
$\mathsf v^\natural(Y;P,\mathcal A)$,
$\natural=\mathrm G,\mathrm A$, which do not depend on the
calibration.  For $B=\mathsf t_i^{1/2}B_i$ set
\begin{equation}\label{C-403-42}
\begin{split}
 \mathbb V^{\mathrm J,\lambda}(Y;P,B)
   &=\mathsf v^{\mathrm J}(Y;P,\lambda\mathsf t_i^{-1/2}B),\\
 \mathbb V^{\natural,\lambda}(Y;P,B)
   &=-\mathsf t_i\lambda^{-2}
              \mathsf v^\natural(Y;P,\lambda\mathsf t_i^{-1/2}B),
                  \qquad \natural=\mathrm G,\mathrm A,\\
 \mathcal V^{\mathrm g,\lambda}
   &=\mathbb V^{\mathrm J,\lambda}
        +\mathbb V^{\mathrm G,\lambda}
        +\tau_i(\lambda)\mathbb V^{\mathrm A,\lambda}.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
The quotients extend holomorphically to zero, with value zero,
since the two unscaled functions vanish to order three.
The other vertices are the fermion vertex, the mass variation
and all old-activity variations at
\[
 \mathsf U'(\lambda B)
   =e^{i\mathcal A(\lambda\mathsf t_i^{-1/2}B;\mathsf U)}
                                                        \mathsf U .
\]
At nonzero source also include the linear, quadratic and
higher-order terms of the source weight.  Their sum is the
potential $\mathfrak V_i(\lambda)$, with its quadratic source
term assigned to the quadratic origin.

From the new activity remove the following quantities.
Remove its vacuum energy and source energies at $\lambda$,
including the scalar Gaussian factor
$-\frac12(\dim B_i/n_{i+1})\operatorname{Log}\tau_i(\lambda)$.
Remove the original coupling shift
$b_{i+1}=e_{\mathsf N,i+1}+b^F_{i+1}+b^r_{i+1}$, and the
original source mass shift multiplied by $\lambda^2$.
Everything else remains in the activity.
In particular, the scalar term
$(b^r_{i+1}(\lambda)-b^r_{i+1})\mathsf W_1$ remains.
If $\widehat Z_{i+1}(\lambda)$ is the cell-mean zeroth
moment before removing the local mass term, the moment left
afterwards is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:C403-residual-moment}
 Z_{i+1}(\lambda)
       =\widehat Z_{i+1}(\lambda)
                         -\lambda^2\widehat Z_{i+1}(1).
\end{equation}
Indeed $\widehat Z_{i+1}(1)=-\mathfrak s_{i+1}\mu_{i+1}1$.
These rules imply
\[
 \xi_{i+1}(\lambda)
      =L^{-1}\xi_i(\lambda)-\lambda^2b_{i+1}.
\]

\begin{proposition}[The flow at a common field scale]
\label{C-403-33-flow}
Assume $g\le\gamma_{\mathrm e}$ and the constant choices in
\ref{C-403-16}.  For a datum on the least torus, the preceding
construction has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
At zero source the step from level $i$ is defined on $D_i$.
Its covariance, potentials and activities are holomorphic
there.  The potentials satisfy
$\mathfrak V_i(-\lambda,-B)=\mathfrak V_i(\lambda,B)$;
the integrated activities, their pointed terms, vacuum
energies and field-independent parts are even in $\lambda$.
For every $\lambda_\circ\in[1,\bar\lambda_j)$ there are
\[
 4\varrho=\varepsilon_0(\lambda_\circ)
       \ge\cdots\ge\varepsilon_j(\lambda_\circ)>0
\]
such that steps $1,\ldots,j$ are holomorphic in
$(\lambda,w)$ for
$|\lambda|\le\lambda_\circ$ and
$\|w\|_\sharp<\varepsilon_j(\lambda_\circ)$.
The radii may depend on the datum.
At $\lambda=1$ the construction equals the original source
flow, polymer by polymer and pointer by pointer.
At that value it is also defined for every source in
$\mathcal P$ by the original flow.
At $\lambda=0$ the potential vanishes; the gauge integral
has only its calibration tests and the fermion integral
is Gaussian at the background.

\item
Put $\eta=C_\eta c_\lambda^{-1/2}$ and use the norm with
the supremum over $\lambda$ inside the polymer sum.
For each $1\le i\le j$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:C403-scaled-induction}
 \|E^{(i)}_{\ge2}\|_{i;D_{i-1}}\le\eta/2,\qquad
 \|F^{(i)}_0\|_{i;D_{i-1}}\le1,\qquad
 \|\widehat Z_i(\lambda)\|_{\mathrm{tr}}
                              \le C^\psi_{am}h_F^{-2}\eta .
\end{equation}
The scalar bound also holds in the array norm at rate
$\kappa+1$ and at every pointer.  These bounds hold for
both the torus and infinite-lattice families.
$E^{(i)}_{\ge2}$ and $\widehat Z_i$ vanish at $\lambda=0$.
At every zero-source step,
\[
 \epsilon_V+\epsilon_F\le c_{\mathrm{cl}}/4,\qquad
 \|\mathcal V^{\mathrm q}\|_{\star,\lambda_V}\le5w_*/64 .
\]
The joined integral and its Gaussian normalising factor
have logarithms given by their convergent cluster sums.
Their scalar parts are nonzero, and the normalised step
integral is therefore defined throughout this domain.

\item
For real $0<\lambda\le1$ and real sources in the indicated
range, the steps compose exactly at every block field
passing its density test.  Up to a nonzero scalar independent
of field and source, the level-$j$ form is the composite
chart integral over the calibration boxes for $B_i$,
$i<j$, with each fluctuation entering the chart as
$\lambda B_i$.  Its integrand contains the chart Jacobians
and elimination factors, the gauge fixings with coefficients
$\mathsf t_i/\lambda^2$, and
\[
 e^{-A(\beta/\lambda^2-a_K^{-1}w,U)}
                        T^F_{h_\emptyset}[U](e^{-S_F}).
\]
There is no residual counterterm:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:C403-scaled-telescoping}
 \lambda^{-2}L^i\xi_i(\lambda)
                  +\sum_{l\le i}L^lb_l=\lambda^{-2}\beta .
\end{equation}
At the same bare configuration $U$, with $\theta=b_F$,
\[
 T^F_{h_\emptyset}[U](e^{-S_F})
   =\prod_{i<j}\theta^{-\dim H_{i+1}}\det\Gamma_i[U]\,
               e^{-\langle\bar\Psi_j,\mathbb D_j[U]\Psi_j\rangle}.
\]
Its value at $\Psi_j=0$ is
$\theta_j^{-\dim H_j}\det\mathcal K_j[U;m_0]$;
its Berezin integral over $\Psi_j$ is $\det(D[U]+m_0)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
We first record the scale comparisons.
The windows $|x_i-\mathsf t_i|\le\bar B\le\mathsf t_i/4$
give $x_i\ge x_j\ge x_K\ge g^{-2}$ for $i\le j$.
Since $x(\log x)^{-2\mathfrak p_0}$ increases for
$x\ge e^{2\mathfrak p_0}$, the discs $D_i$ decrease with $i$.
For $1\le l\le i$ and $n=i+1-l$,
\[
 \frac35L^nx_i\le x_{l-1}\le\frac53L^nx_i .
\]
Using $\log x_i\ge18\mathfrak p_0$, we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{eq:C403-radius-ratios}
 \left(\frac{\bar\lambda_i}{\bar\lambda_{l-1}}\right)^2
 \le2L^{-n}(1+n\log L)^{2\mathfrak p_0},
 \qquad
 \left(\frac{\bar\lambda_i}{\bar\lambda_{l-1}}\right)^2
 \le2^{10/9}L^{-8n/9}<1/4 .
\end{equation}
For the second inequality use
$(1+(\log2+n\log L)/(18\mathfrak p_0))^{2\mathfrak p_0}
\le2^{1/9}L^{n/9}$ and $L\ge13$.
The same windows give
\[
 \bar\lambda_i\delta(\mathsf t_i)
 \le A_12^{\mathfrak p_0+1}c_\lambda^{-1/2},\qquad
 \bar\lambda_i^{-2}
       \le c_\lambda(\log x_i)^{2\mathfrak p_0}a_i/\mathsf b .
\]
Thus the fluctuation on the field polydisc satisfies
$\sup|\lambda\mathsf t_i^{-1/2}B|<\beta_\lambda$.

The scaled coefficient stays in the coefficient disc of
the one-step expansion:
\[
 |\xi_i(\lambda)-x_i|
 \le(1+\bar\lambda_i^2)\bar B
 \le2\bar\lambda_i^2\bar B\le r_xx_i.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 |\tau_i(\lambda)-1|
 \le\frac52\bar B/c_\lambda
 \le\frac58r_x
 \le\min\{5\sigma_\star/32,\,5/64\}.
\]
Hence $|\tau_i|\le3/2$, $|\tau_i^{-1}|<2$ and
$|\xi_i|>\mathsf t_i/2$.
The complete and decoupled covariances are the corresponding
calibration covariances multiplied by $\tau_i^{-1}$.
They retain their decay bounds, and
\[
 \|\mathcal V^{\mathrm q}\|_{\star,\lambda_V}
      \le|1-\tau_i|K_{\mathsf G}
      \le5\sigma_\star K_{\mathsf G}/32\le5w_*/64 .
\]
The covariance, the quadratic origin and its Gaussian
cluster sum are holomorphic in the coefficient on this
disc, and therefore even and holomorphic in $\lambda$.
Also $\operatorname{Re}\tau_i>0$, so its scalar logarithm
is defined.

We next establish the vertex bounds on the whole field
polydisc.  This requires the fixed calibration
$\mathsf t_\flat$, rather than extrapolation from the
real-coupling estimate.
Let
\[
 r_\flat=\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}\mathfrak b(\mathsf t_\flat),
 \quad r=\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}\mathfrak b(\mathsf t_i),
 \quad \mu=\lambda(\mathsf t_\flat/\mathsf t_i)^{1/2},
 \quad R_i=\delta(\mathsf t_\flat)/\delta(\mathsf t_i).
\]
Then $r_\flat\le r$, $R_i\ge\bar\lambda_i$, and
$|\mu|r/r_\flat=|\lambda|/R_i<1$.
At $\mathsf t_\flat$ the gauge vertices are holomorphic on
the polydisc of radius $r_\flat$ and satisfy
\[
 |\mathbb V^\natural[\mathsf t_\flat](Y;P,B')|
 \le K_P\delta(\mathsf t_\flat)
          e^{-(\bar\kappa-2)d_i(Y)}Q_Y(B'),
 \qquad
 Q_Y(B')=1+M^{-3}
       \sum_{b\in\mathfrak X^{\circ+}\langle Y\rangle}|B'(b)|^2 .
\]
All vanish at zero; the $\mathrm G,\mathrm A$ vertices
vanish to order three.

For clarity, the Schwarz estimates used to rescale this
bound are
\begin{equation}\label{C-403-72}
\begin{aligned}
 |f(\mu B)|&\le
       \frac{|\mu|r}{r_\flat}KQ_Y(B)
          &&\text{if }f(0)=0,\ |f|\le KQ_Y,\\
 |f(\mu B)|&\le
       \frac{|\mu|r}{r_\flat}K
          &&\text{if }f(0)=0,\ |f|\le K,\\
 |\mu^{-2}f(\mu B)|
    &\le\frac{|\mu|r}{r_\flat}
       K(1+M^3r_\flat^{-2})(Q_Y(B)-1)
          &&\text{if }f=O(B^3),\ |f|\le KQ_Y .
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
For the first two, apply Schwarz's lemma to
$f(\zeta r_\flat B/r)$ on the unit disc.
For the third, let $\rho_B=\max_b|B(b)|$ and
$R=r_\flat/\rho_B$.  The maximum principle for
$\zeta^{-3}f(\zeta B)$ gives
\[
 |\mu^{-2}f(\mu B)|
    \le|\mu|K[R^{-3}+R^{-1}(Q_Y(B)-1)] .
\]
Now use $R^{-1}\le r/r_\flat$ and
$R^{-2}\le M^3r_\flat^{-2}(Q_Y(B)-1)$.
The case $B=0$ follows by continuity.

The unscaled vertex definitions imply
\[
 \mathbb V^{\mathrm J,\lambda}
       =\mathbb V^{\mathrm J}[\mathsf t_\flat](\mu B),\qquad
 \mathbb V^{\natural,\lambda}
       =\mu^{-2}\mathbb V^\natural[\mathsf t_\flat](\mu B).
\]
Since $M^3r_\flat^{-2}\le1/9$, (because
$\mathfrak b(\mathsf t_\flat)^2\ge M^3$ and
$\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}\ge3$), \eqref{C-403-72} gives
\[
 |\mathcal V^{\mathrm g,\lambda}(Y)|
 \le4K_PA_12^{\mathfrak p_0+1}c_\lambda^{-1/2}
             Q_Y(B)e^{-(\kappa+1)d_i(Y)} .
\]
The quotients at $\mu=0$ are jointly holomorphic:
Cauchy's formula for $\zeta^{-2}f(\zeta B)$ proves this
also in the pair variables.  The vertices retain joint
gauge invariance, translation covariance and reality.

The bound $\beta_\lambda\le\beta_0/2$ places the completed
field in the regular complex domain for the fermion tower.
At a step after level $i$, it is of the form $e^{iX}U_1$
with $|X|\le\alpha_1L^{-i}\le\alpha_1^*L^{-(i+1)}$.
For the first step this uses
$2C_{\mathrm{cf}}\beta_0\le
\min\{r_P^\circ,\alpha_1/2\}$; for later steps use
$c_h\beta_0\le\alpha_1/2$.
Thus the fluctuation operators, covariances, background
maps and normalisers are holomorphic with their regular
complex-domain bounds.  The real part of each fluctuation
operator keeps a positive floor.

The variation estimates consequently give
\begin{align*}
 \|\mathcal V^{F,\lambda}\|
       &\le C_Vh_F^2\beta_\lambda,\\
 \|\mathcal V^{\mathrm s,\lambda}\|
       &\le(c_\psi+C_G\beta_\lambda)c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2
                                      |\lambda|^2\|s_i+\sigma_i\|_\infty,\\
 \|\mathcal V_{\ge2}^{\mathrm{old},\lambda}\|
       &\le[c_\psi+(c_h/a_{\mathrm{an}}+C_G)\beta_\lambda]
                                                    \varsigma_i(\lambda),\\
 |\mathcal V_0^{\mathrm{old},\lambda}|
       &\le c_h\beta_\lambda K_{\mathrm{old}}/a_{\mathrm{an}} .
\end{align*}
Here $\varsigma_i$ is the sum of the old fermionic families
read at the step.  We justify the scalar estimate separately.
Its bracket localisation is evaluated at
$(P,\lambda\mathsf t_i^{-1/2}B)$.
The same point lies in the domain at $\mathsf t_\flat$.
The scalar localisation has the same value there, since the
calibration enters its definition only through the domain.
The absolute system remains admissible:
only its radius condition reads the calibration, and that
condition is precisely
$(1+\beta_s)\delta(\mathsf t_\flat)\le
\mathsf s^\star\alpha_0$.
Its other properties are those of the original step.
At $\mathsf t_\flat$ its bound is
\[
 K_\Lambda\frac{(1+\beta_s)\delta(\mathsf t_\flat)}{\alpha_0}
        N_{\mathfrak a,\omega}(\mathfrak f_{\circ,\lambda})
                 e^{-(1-2\delta_{\mathrm w})\kappa d_i(Y)},
 \qquad\omega_n=L^{-(n-1)}.
\]
It vanishes at zero fluctuation.  Apply the second estimate
in \eqref{C-403-72} to obtain
\begin{equation}\label{C-403-70}
 |\mathcal V_0^{\mathrm{old},\lambda}(Y;P,B)|
 \le|\lambda|\frac{c_h\delta(\mathsf t_i)}{a_{\mathrm{an}}}
              K_{\mathrm{old}}
                 e^{-(1-2\delta_{\mathrm w})\kappa d_i(Y)}
 \le\frac{c_h\beta_\lambda}{a_{\mathrm{an}}}
              K_{\mathrm{old}}
                 e^{-(1-2\delta_{\mathrm w})\kappa d_i(Y)} .
\end{equation}
The array bound needed here follows from
\eqref{eq:C403-scaled-induction}: the fixed normaliser
terms and counterterms do not read the coefficient, the
Gaussian term stays in its coefficient disc, and the
fluctuation family has norm at most one.
Joint holomorphy follows from the holomorphy of the
localisation in the field and in the array parameters,
the uniform bound, and composition with
$(\lambda,B)\mapsto(\lambda,\mu B)$.

At zero source the mass window gives
$|\lambda^2s_i|\le2\bar B_M/c_\lambda$.
Therefore
\begin{equation}\label{eq:C403-scaled-potential-sizes}
 \epsilon_V\le C_V^\lambda c_\lambda^{-1/2},\qquad
 \epsilon_F\le C_F^\lambda c_\lambda^{-1/2}
                                      +c'_\psi\varsigma_i(\lambda).
\end{equation}
We now close the induction in (2).
For an old family at level $l\le i$, put $n=i+1-l$.
Its long-lag estimate, with its polymers as units, is
\[
 \varsigma_i(\lambda)
 \le\sum_{l\le i}C_\omega
       [L^{n/4}\|E^{(l)}_{\ge2}(\lambda)\|_l
                  +L^nh_F^2M^3\|Z_l(\lambda)\|_{\mathrm{tr}}].
\]
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:qcdm2-nonzero-cell-reading}
with $j=l$, $k=i+1$, and the original polymer units.
These families are even, holomorphic and gauge invariant
on the whole regular core; the background walk estimates
give the required first absolute moment.
At long lags use its transported-leg decomposition,
including its final-generator weight $C_Hh_F$;
at shorter lags use its direct reading.
No diagonal term is moved in these units, so the
additional row and column conditions are vacuous.
Translation covariance gives the cell sum
$M^3Z_l(\lambda)$.  On the torus the infinite-lattice
cell sum is used and the remainder is included in
$C_\omega$.

The induction hypothesis, evenness, and Schwarz's lemma
in $\lambda^2$ give
\[
 \|E^{(l)}_{\ge2}(\lambda)\|_l
       \le\eta L^{-n}(1+n\log L)^{2\mathfrak p_0}.
\]
Expand $\widehat Z_l=\sum_{m\ge1}z_m\lambda^{2m}$.
Its coefficient bound is
$\|z_m\|_{\mathrm{tr}}\le
C^\psi_{am}h_F^{-2}\eta\bar\lambda_{l-1}^{-2m}$.
The order-two term cancels in
\eqref{eq:C403-residual-moment}.
With $q=(\max\{1,|\lambda|\}/\bar\lambda_{l-1})^2<1/4$,
\[
 \|Z_l(\lambda)\|_{\mathrm{tr}}
 \le2C^\psi_{am}h_F^{-2}\eta\sum_{m\ge2}q^m
 \le12C^\psi_{am}h_F^{-2}\eta
                L^{-2n}(1+n\log L)^{4\mathfrak p_0}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \varsigma_i(\lambda)
 \le(1+12M^3C^\psi_{am})C_\omega S_\omega\eta
 \le3K_\mu C_\omega S_\omega\eta .
\]
Here $K_\mu\ge1+4M^3C^\psi_{am}$.
The original contraction
$2\sqrt2\theta_EC_\omega S_\omega\le1/2$,
with $\theta_E=\sqrt2K_\mu K_Mc'_\psi$, yields
$K_Mc'_\psi\varsigma_i\le3\eta/8$.
Together with \eqref{eq:C403-scaled-potential-sizes}
this proves $\epsilon_V+\epsilon_F\le c_{\mathrm{cl}}/4$.

Apply the holomorphic expansion with two independent
parameters $(\lambda,x')$, where $|x'-x_i|<r_xx_i$.
Replace $\tau_i(\lambda)$ in the action vertex by
$x'/\mathsf t_i$.  All the preceding estimates are uniform
there, since $|x'/\mathsf t_i|<3/2$.
After forming the expansion, evaluate at $x'=\xi_i(\lambda)$,
an interior point of the disc.
The new activity is the logarithm of the joined integral:
the logarithm of the normalised interacting quotient plus
the logarithm of the tests alone.  The latter is scalar.
The Gaussian quadratic-origin cluster sum is kept
separately and restored in the scalar normalisation.
Thus neither the tests nor their Gaussian factor have
been dropped.  The cluster representations give their
nonvanishing scalar parts.

The expansion and the tail ceiling imply
\[
 \|\widetilde E^{(i+1)}_{\ge2}\|_{i+1;D_i}
 \le K_M(C_V^\lambda+C_F^\lambda+1)c_\lambda^{-1/2}
                                               +3\eta/8 .
\]
The removed local mass has norm at most
$6Lc_{\mathsf S}h_F^2\bar B_M/c_\lambda$:
indeed $|\mu_{i+1}|\le3L\bar B_M/x_i$ and
$|\lambda|^2\le2x_i/c_\lambda$.
The definition of $C_\eta$ therefore gives
$\|E^{(i+1)}_{\ge2}\|\le\eta/8+3\eta/8=\eta/2$.
The moment estimate gives
$\|\widehat Z_{i+1}\|_{\mathrm{tr}}
\le C^\psi_{am}h_F^{-2}\eta$.
At $\lambda=0$ the potential is zero.  Only the scalar
test activity remains, so both fermionic quantities vanish.

The scalar and pointed bounds require their own admission
check.  Put
