                                      \le\frac{c_b}{18}\mathfrak m_s,\\
 \operatorname{Lip}_s(\hat s_w)
       &\le\frac{16F^{\rm UV}}{9L^{2s}\mathsf b^2}\operatorname{Lip}(w),\\
 \sup|\hat s_w-\hat s_{w'}|
       &\le\frac{16F^{\rm UV}}{9L^s\mathsf b^2}\sup|w-w'|.
\end{align*}
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
The partial-sum and slice bounds follow from \cref{C-398-40} by
the triangle inequality. Since $32\varrho\le\gamma^{-2}<\mathsf b$
and $\mathsf b\ge2\bar B$, the two denominator bounds follow.
Writing $x_i'=L^{k-i}t_k'+(x_i-t_i)$ gives
\[
 \left|\frac{L^{k-i}}{x_i'}-\frac1{t_k'}\right|
 \le\frac{16\bar B}{3t_k^2}L^{-(k-i)}.
\]
Multiply by the nonnegative $\sigma_i$ and sum over $i<i_0$.
The estimate with $t_k'$ uses $|t_k'|\le5t_k/4$; equivalently,
estimate $|t_k'L^{k-i}/x_i'-1|$ directly by
$4\bar B L^{-(k-i)}/t_k$. At $c=0$ use $x_i\ge t_i/2$.
The estimates for $\hat s_w$ are the same denominator calculation.
Its relative mass bound uses the original admission condition
$\mathsf b\mathsf m\ge8C_{\mathcal S,1}\bar B_{\mathsf M}/c_b$,
$\bar B_{\mathsf M}=3B_F+1$, and $C_{\mathcal S,1}\ge1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Starting the source chain at a later level]\label{C-420-4}
The source-chain estimate of \cite[Lem.\ 10.4]{QCDM1} holds from
any levels $0\le t_*\le t^*\le K$ for which its one-step maps
satisfy the same three hypotheses. More precisely, suppose
\[
 0<\phi_k\le2L^{-1/2}\phi_{k+1},\quad
 \kappa_\sigma\le\tfrac14,\quad
 \kappa_\sigma M\le\tfrac14\kappa L,
\]
and
\[
 B_\sigma\ge4B_0+3C_{\rm var}+8C_{\rm tor}C_{\mathcal L},
 \qquad B_\sigma\ge2C_{\mathcal L}B_\nu.
\]
Let the constant-source reference fields be holomorphic for
$|c|<8\varrho$ and satisfy
$|\sigma_i^c(c)|\le B_0'\phi_i|c|/\varrho$, where
$B_0'\le B_0+C_{\rm var}/4$. Start with
$\sigma_i(x)=\sigma_i^c(w(x))$ for $i\le t_*$ and then use
\[
 \sigma_{k+1}(x)=L\sigma_k(x)
     +\nu_{k+1}(c_k)(y_{k+1}(x))-\mu_{k+1}.
\]
Here $x$ is a bare site and $y_{k+1}(x)$ is its level-$(k+1)$
block centre.
The chain is holomorphic on its source domain, remains inside the
coordinate polydiscs, and obeys
\[
 \|\sigma_k-\sigma_k^c(w)\|
 \le C_{\rm var}\phi_k\Xi_k
       +2C_{\rm tor}C_{\mathcal L}\phi_k
          e^{-c_t\ell/(2\lambda_k)}\|w\|_\infty/\varrho,
 \qquad \|\sigma_k\|\le B_\sigma\phi_k.
\]
The norms, local source variation $\Xi_k$, scale $\lambda_k$,
and constant $c_t$ are those of that source-chain estimate.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
We give the changes to its induction. The initial error is zero
at every level $i\le t_*$. Cauchy's estimate for the reference
function gives, at a local comparison point $x_0$,
\[
 |\sigma_i^c(w(x))-\sigma_i^c(w(x_0))|
 \le2B_0'\phi_i\operatorname{Lip}(w)a_K|x-x_0|/\varrho.
\]
Thus the coordinate difference used in the local one-step estimate
has the same bound as before, including the coordinates preceding
$t_*$. In the induction replace the torus error by
\[
 T_k=2C_{\rm tor}\sum_{j=t_*}^kL^{k-j}\phi_j
       e^{-c_t\ell/(2\lambda_j)}\|w\|_\infty/\varrho.
\]
Its recurrence is the required one, and the geometric scale estimate
in the source-chain proof gives
$T_k\le2C_{\rm tor}C_{\mathcal L}\phi_k
e^{-c_t\ell/(2\lambda_k)}\|w\|_\infty/\varrho$.
The ratio entering the local variation sum is at most
$8/(3\sqrt L)$. The admission of the new coordinate follows from
\[
 4B_0'+2C_{\rm var}+8C_{\rm tor}C_{\mathcal L}\le B_\sigma.
\]
These bounds close the same induction and keep each composition in
the holomorphy domain of its next map.

For the restart, use zero reference fields before $t_0$ and
\[
 \sigma_{t_0}^c(c)
   =\frac{F^{\rm UV}c}{L^s\mathsf b(\mathsf b-c)}.
\]
Its modulus is at most
$(F^{\rm UV}/24)\phi(L^s\mathsf b)|c|/\varrho$.
The restarted one-step hypotheses and the required bound on $B_0'$
are supplied by \cref{C-419-8}; hence the lemma applies from
$t_0$ to $t_1$ when $u\ge u_*$. No map at an earlier level is
needed in this application.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Changing the classical background}

We use the classical comparison in \cite[\S113]{YMM1} in a form
that also records the change of individual links. Its excess bound
pays for the square of this change at every scale. This will allow
the fermion resolvent to be compared in operator norm.

\begin{proposition}[The change of the links]\label{C-420-5}
Let $U'$ be a competitor of admitted radius $e$ at level $t$ in
\cite[Prop.\ 113.5]{YMM1}. Thus
$V'_k=\mathcal M^kU'$ satisfies
$\varpi(V'_k)\le eL^{-2(t-k)}$. Let $\mathcal A_k$ be its
nonpivot fields, $v_k$ its axial gauges, and
\[
 h_k=\tfrac\pi2C_{\rm ax}(1+2B_3)eL^{-2(t-k)},\qquad
 c_{\rm db}=(1+24C_{\rm db}^2)^{1/2},\qquad
 \mathcal E_t=8\gamma_{\rm r}^{-1}\mathsf{exc}_t(U').
\]
The constants and the allowed radius are those of that proposition.
There are backgrounds $\check U_k,\hat U_k$, real bond fields
$B'_k,\mathcal H_k$, and gauges $u_k$ for $0\le k<t$ such that
\[
 (V'_k)^{v_k}=e^{iB'_k}V^{\rm bf}_k(V'_{k+1}),\qquad
 \sup|B'_k|\le2C_{\rm db}h_k,\qquad
 \|B'_k\|\le c_{\rm db}\|\mathcal A_k\|.
\]
For $k\ge1$ put
\[
 m_y^k=\sum_{c'}e^{-\delta_0^{\rm e}d_{\mathbf B}(y,c'_-)}|B'_k(c')|,
\]
where $c'$ runs over positive level-$k$ bonds; put
$m_y^0=\sup|B'_0|$. Then
\[
 \sum_y(m_y^k)^2\le\mathsf S_{\rm e}^2\|B'_k\|^2\quad(k\ge1),
 \qquad \sup_y m_y^k\le
 \min\{\mathsf S_{\rm e}^{1/2}\|B'_k\|,
                         \mathsf S_{\rm e}\sup|B'_k|\}.
\]
The backgrounds belong to
\[
 \check U_k\in\mathcal C(\mathbf B_{k+1},V'_{k+1}),\qquad
 \hat U_k\in\mathcal C(\mathbf B_k,V'_k).
\]
Extend $v_k$ to the bare lattice by the identity away from the
level-$k$ sites and denote this extension by $\tilde v_k$. Then
\[
 \hat U_k^{\tilde v_k}=(e^{i\eta_k\mathcal H_k}\check U_k)^{u_k},
 \qquad |\mathcal H_k(b)|\le B_5^{\rm e}m_{y(b_-)}^k,
 \qquad \sup|\mathcal H_k|\le1/132,
\]
and $|u_k(y)-1|\le4\kappa_6B_5^{\rm e}m_y^k$ at level-$k$
sites. At $k=0$ these choices are
$\hat U_0=U'$, $\check U_0=V^{\rm bf}_0(V'_1)$,
$\mathcal H_0=B'_0$, and $u_0=1$.

Set $\tilde U_k=e^{i\eta_k\mathcal H_k}\check U_k$.
For $k<j\le t$,
\[
 \mathcal M^j\tilde U_k=(V'_j)^{u_k^{-1}},\qquad
 \varpi(\check U_k),\varpi(\tilde U_k)\le B_3e\eta_t^2.
\]
Moreover, $\check U_k$ and $\hat U_{k+1}$ belong to the same
residual gauge orbit, with gauges equal to one on the level-$(k+1)$
lattice. The last $\check U_{t-1}$ belongs to the prescribed
minimal orbit over $V'_t$.

In units of level $t$, write
$a_k(b)=\eta_t^{-1}\eta_k|\mathcal H_k(b)|$ and
$\|a_k\|_2^2=\eta_t^3\sum_ba_k(b)^2$. Then
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{k<t}L^{t-k}\|\mathcal A_k\|^2&\le\mathcal E_t,\\
 \|a_k\|_2&\le\sqrt3 B_5^{\rm e}\mathsf S_{\rm e}c_{\rm db}
                         L^{-(t-k)/2}\|\mathcal A_k\|,\\
 \sum_{k<t}\|a_k\|_2&\le
  \frac{\sqrt3 B_5^{\rm e}\mathsf S_{\rm e}c_{\rm db}}{\sqrt{L^2-1}}
                                      \sqrt{\mathcal E_t},\\
 \sum_{k<t}\sup_y m_y^k&\le
  \frac{\mathsf S_{\rm e}^{1/2}c_{\rm db}}{\sqrt{L-1}}
                                      \sqrt{\mathcal E_t},\\
 \sup_ba_k(b)&\le B_5^{\rm e}
  \min\left\{\mathsf S_{\rm e}^{1/2}c_{\rm db}L^{(t-k)/2}
                         \sqrt{\mathcal E_t},
  \pi\mathsf S_{\rm e}C_{\rm db}C_{\rm ax}(1+2B_3)eL^{-(t-k)}\right\}.
\end{align*}
For the two cutoffs of \cref{C-420-2}, $U'=\mathcal M U^{\rm B}$
is such a competitor, with $e=2B_3\varepsilon_{\rm r}$, and
\[
 \mathcal E_t\le8\gamma_{\rm r}^{-1}\mathsf K_u
                       \varepsilon_{\rm r}^2N_tL^{-t}.
\]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The construction in \cite[Lem.\ 113.6 and its proof]{YMM1} gives
the fields $B'_k$, $\check U_k$, $\hat U_k$, and the displayed
response identity. Its pivot estimate is eq.\ (2136), so the factor
in the $\ell^2$ bound is exactly $c_{\rm db}$. The response bound
uses the exponentially weighted sum in \cite[eq.\ (996)]{YMM1}.
Its row and column sums are at most $\mathsf S_{\rm e}$.
The Schur test gives the sum of squares; the two supremum bounds
follow, respectively, by Cauchy--Schwarz and the row sum.
The same response construction bounds $u_k$ at the top sites.
At $k=0$ the field is $B'_0$ itself, and the admitted radius gives
$\sup|B'_0|\le1/132$.

The average is gauge covariant. Since $v_k=1$ on level $k+1$,
applying $\mathcal M^j$ to the response identity gives
$\mathcal M^j\tilde U_k=(V'_j)^{u_k^{-1}}$ for $j>k$.
The background regularity estimate at level $k+1$ gives
\[
 \varpi(\check U_k)\le
 B_3\varpi(V'_{k+1})\eta_{k+1}^2\le B_3e\eta_t^2.
\]
The same argument at level $k$, followed by gauge invariance of
plaquette size, gives the estimate for $\tilde U_k$. These uses
of the regularity estimate are valid at the admitted radius; its
strict input bound can be decreased to the actual plaquette size.
The uniqueness of the residual minimal orbit, used in the proof
of the cited lemma, gives the orbit identifications. Its residual
gauges are the identity at every later block site.

The competitor estimate in \cite[Prop.\ 113.5]{YMM1} gives the
first sum in the statement. For $k\ge1$ there are three positive
bare bonds per bare site and $\eta_k^{-3}$ sites per pillar. Hence
\[
 \sum_b|\mathcal H_k(b)|^2
 \le3\eta_k^{-3}(B_5^{\rm e}\mathsf S_{\rm e})^2\|B'_k\|^2.
\]
Multiplication by $\eta_t\eta_k^2$ proves the bound for
$\|a_k\|_2$. At $k=0$ use
$\|a_0\|_2^2=\eta_t\|B'_0\|^2$ directly. The two summed
bounds now follow from
\[
 \sum_{k<t}L^{-(t-k)/2}\|\mathcal A_k\|
 \le(L^2-1)^{-1/2}\sqrt{\mathcal E_t},\qquad
 \sum_{k<t}\|\mathcal A_k\|
 \le(L-1)^{-1/2}\sqrt{\mathcal E_t}.
\]
For the supremum, use $a_k\le L^{t-k}B_5^{\rm e}\sup m^k$
and the two bounds for $\sup m^k$.

Finally \cite[Lem.\ 113.8]{YMM1} makes $\mathcal M U^{\rm B}$
an admitted competitor of radius $2B_3\varepsilon_{\rm r}$.
Writing $q=(1+j_t)^2$ in its action comparison gives
\[
 \mathsf{exc}_t(U')\le(q-1)A^{\rm B}
                                      +(A^{\rm B}-A^{\rm A}).
\]
The proof of \cite[Prop.\ 113.9]{YMM1} bounds these two terms by
$5C_{\rm en}B_3^3\varepsilon_{\rm r}^2\eta_tN_t$ and
$(10^4L^4B_3^3+\mathsf K_{\rm up})\varepsilon_{\rm r}^2\eta_tN_t$.
Their sum is $\mathsf K_u\varepsilon_{\rm r}^2\eta_tN_t$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The lattice Sobolev estimate]\label{C-420-6}
On a cubic torus of spacing $\xi\le1$ and side $\ell'\ge1$,
\[
 \|h\|_6\le\|h\|_2+\tfrac23\sum_{\mu=1}^3\|\nabla_\mu h\|_2,
 \qquad
 \|h\|_4\le\|h\|_2+\tfrac12\sum_{\mu=1}^3\|\nabla_\mu h\|_2.
\]
For chamber spinors, the energy seminorm of \cref{C-408-8} satisfies
\[
 \|f\|_4\le\|f\|_2+2\mathcal N(f).
\]
If $U_1(b)=e^{iX(b)}U_2(b)$ and
$a(b)=\xi^{-1}|X(b)|$, with
$\|a\|_2^2=\xi^3\sum_{b>0}a(b)^2$, then
\[
 |\langle\psi,(D^\xi[U_1]-D^\xi[U_2])\varphi\rangle|
 \le c_D\|a\|_2\|\psi\|_4\|\varphi\|_4,
 \qquad c_D=12(1+r)=18.
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
On a periodic lattice line a nonnegative function satisfies
$v\le\ell'^{-1}\int v+\frac12\int|\nabla v|$.
Apply this along each of the three coordinate lines. Cauchy--Schwarz
in the three transverse pairs, followed by the arithmetic-geometric
mean inequality, gives
\[
 \|v\|_{3/2}\le\|v\|_1+\tfrac16\sum_\mu\|\nabla_\mu v\|_1.
\]
For completeness, if $g_\mu$ is the resulting bound independent
of coordinate $\mu$, then
$v^{3/2}\le(g_1g_2g_3)^{1/2}$ and the repeated Cauchy--Schwarz
inequality bounds its integral by
$\prod_\mu(\int g_\mu)^{1/2}$. This is the finite lattice version
of the inequality just used; the powers of the mesh cancel.

Set $v=|h|^4$. The difference of fourth powers is bounded by
$2(a^3+b^3)|a-b|$, so
\[
 \|\nabla_\mu |h|^4\|_1
       \le4\|h\|_6^3\|\nabla_\mu h\|_2,
 \qquad \|h\|_4^4\le\|h\|_2\|h\|_6^3.
\]
Division by $\|h\|_6^3$ proves the $L^6$ bound; the zero case
is immediate. Interpolation with $L^2$ and the concavity of the
power $3/4$ gives the $L^4$ bound.

For a covariant difference, unitarity gives
$|\nabla |\varphi||\le|\nabla^U\varphi|$.
Since the gradient norm includes both orientations,
$\sum_{\mu>0}\|\nabla^U_\mu\varphi\|_2
\le\sqrt{3/2}\|\nabla^U\varphi\|_2$.
Write $f=\iota\varphi+g$. The chamber normalization gives
$\|\iota\varphi\|_4=48^{-1/4}\|\varphi\|_4$, whereas
$\|g\|_4\le\xi^{-3/4}\|g\|_2\le\mathcal N(f)$.
Combining the two estimates proves the claimed chamber bound.

For the last assertion, each positive cubic bond occurs in sixteen
chamber hopping terms. Each term has coefficient at most $3(1+r)$,
and $|e^{iX}-1|\le|X|$. Cauchy--Schwarz in the chamber labels,
then H\"older with exponents $2,4,4$ on the bonds, gives the stated
constant $12(1+r)$, including both hopping directions.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Solutions on the full source disc]\label{C-420-7}
Under the side and curvature hypotheses of \cref{C-408-5},
let $\sup|J|\le m/2+\varrho_S$. Define
\[
 C'_{\mathcal S}=\tfrac65C_{\mathcal S},\qquad
 C'_\nabla=\tfrac65C_\nabla,\qquad
 C_4=C'_{\mathcal S}+2C'_\nabla.
\]
Solutions $f=\mathcal S G$, and solutions for the adjoint, obey
\[
 \|f\|_2\le C'_{\mathcal S}\|G\|_2,\qquad
 \mathcal N(f)\le C'_\nabla\|G\|_2,\qquad
 \|f\|_4\le C_4\|G\|_2.
\]
Consequently $\|\mathsf T\|\le C'_{\mathcal S}$ and
$\|\mathsf D\|\le a_++a_+^2C'_{\mathcal S}$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Split $J=J_a+J_b$ pointwise by radial projection onto the ball
$|J_a|\le m/2$. Then $|J_b|\le\varrho_S=1/(6C_{\mathcal S})$.
The equation $\mathcal K[J_a]f=G+\widehat J_bf$ and the estimates
before enlargement of the source disc give
\[
 \|f\|_2\le C_{\mathcal S}\|G\|_2+\tfrac16\|f\|_2,
 \qquad
 \mathcal N(f)\le C_\nabla(\|G\|_2+\varrho_S\|f\|_2).
\]
These give the factors $6/5$. The $L^4$ bound is
\cref{C-420-6}. The adjoint is conjugate by $\gamma_4$ to the
same operator at $J^\sharp=\gamma_4J^\dagger\gamma_4$; both the
source norm and $\mathcal N$ are unchanged.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Changing the background in the block operator]
\label{C-420-8}
Use the competitor of \cref{C-420-5}. Assume the side in units of
level $t$ is at least $C_{\rm side}$, the source has norm at most
$m/2+\varrho_S$, and
\[
 B_3e\le\min\{\epsilon_S,a_Q\},\qquad
 \pi L^{-1}B_5^{\rm e}\mathsf S_{\rm e}C_{\rm db}C_{\rm ax}
                       (1+2B_3)e\le\sigma_Q.
\]
Here $a_Q,\sigma_Q,C_Q$ are the curvature radius, perturbation
radius, and derivative constant for the holomorphic averages in
\cite[Lem.\ 6.4]{QCDM1}. Put
\begin{align*}
 C_{\rm bg}={}&
 (2C'_{\mathcal S}+2a_+C_{\mathcal S}'{}^2)
 (4\kappa_6+C_QL)B_5^{\rm e}
                 \frac{\mathsf S_{\rm e}^{1/2}c_{\rm db}}{\sqrt{L-1}}\\
 &+c_DC_4^2\frac{\sqrt3B_5^{\rm e}\mathsf S_{\rm e}c_{\rm db}}
                                                         {\sqrt{L^2-1}}.
\end{align*}
For $U''$ in the minimal orbit over $\mathcal M^tU'$, at the same
$a$ and source,
\[
 \|\mathsf T[U']-\mathsf T[U'']\|\le C_{\rm bg}\sqrt{\mathcal E_t},
 \qquad
 \|\mathsf D[U']-\mathsf D[U'']\|\le a^2C_{\rm bg}\sqrt{\mathcal E_t}.
\]
The kernel difference is also bounded by the sum of the two
exponentially decreasing kernel bounds from \cref{C-408-5}.
For the two cutoffs, these hypotheses become
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two-mesh-radius}
 \begin{split}
 2B_3^2\varepsilon_{\rm r}&\le\min\{\epsilon_S,a_Q\},\\
 2\pi L^{-1}B_5^{\rm e}\mathsf S_{\rm e}C_{\rm db}C_{\rm ax}
                (1+2B_3)B_3\varepsilon_{\rm r}&\le\sigma_Q.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
With $\mathsf K_b=a_+^2C_{\rm bg}\sqrt{8\mathsf K_u/\gamma_{\rm r}}$,
the resulting bound for
$\mathsf D^{\rm A}[\mathcal M U^{\rm B}]-\mathsf D^{\rm A}[U^{\rm A}]$
is $\mathsf K_b\varepsilon_{\rm r}\sqrt{N_tL^{-t}}$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Residual gauges equal one on the target lattice, so $\mathsf T$
is constant on each residual orbit. The chain in \cref{C-420-5}
therefore telescopes as
\[
 \mathsf T[U']-\mathsf T[U'']
   =\sum_{k<t}(\mathsf T[\hat U_k]-\mathsf T[\check U_k]).
\]
Fix $k$. All averages above level $k+1$ are common after taking
account of the gauge $u_k$. Write $R_{\rm top}$ for their composite,
$w=u_k|_{\mathbb T^{(k+1)}}$, and
\[
 R'=R_{\rm top}wR_{k+1}(\tilde U_k),\qquad
 R=R_{\rm top}R_{k+1}(\check U_k).
\]
Gauge covariance gives $\mathsf T[\hat U_k]=R'\mathcal S'R'^*$,
where $\mathcal S'$ has bare field $\tilde U_k$ and penalty
$aR'^*R'$. Both averages have norm one. The real averages coincide
with their holomorphic extensions on this regular domain. The
derivative bound for that extension and the estimate on $u_k$ give
\[
 \|R'-R\|\le\rho_k,
 \qquad \rho_k=(4\kappa_6+C_QL)B_5^{\rm e}\sup_y m_y^k.
\]
Indeed the field perturbation at level $k+1$ has norm
$L\sup|\mathcal H_k|$; the second radius condition keeps it in
the permitted disc. The first radius condition gives both the
operator estimates and the regularity required for the averages.

The resolvent identity is
\begin{align*}
 R'\mathcal S'R'^*-R\mathcal SR^*
 ={}&(R'-R)\mathcal S'R'^*+R\mathcal S'(R'-R)^*\\
 &-R\mathcal S'\{D^\xi[\tilde U_k]-D^\xi[\check U_k]
                          +a(R'^*R'-R^*R)\}\mathcal SR^*.
\end{align*}
By \cref{C-420-6,C-420-7}, its norm is at most
\[
 (2C'_{\mathcal S}+2a_+C_{\mathcal S}'{}^2)\rho_k
                                      +c_DC_4^2\|a_k\|_2.
\]
The two sums in \cref{C-420-5} give $C_{\rm bg}$.
The last assertion uses its excess estimate and
$\mathsf D=a-a^2\mathsf T$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[A bound using only the radius]\label{C-420-14}
Under the same hypotheses one also has
\[
 \|\mathsf T[U']-\mathsf T[U'']\|\le C_{\rm bg}^\infty e,
\]
where
\begin{align*}
 C_{\rm bg}^\infty={}&\pi B_5^{\rm e}\mathsf S_{\rm e}C_{\rm db}
 C_{\rm ax}(1+2B_3)\\
 &\times\left[
 \frac{(2C'_{\mathcal S}+2a_+C_{\mathcal S}'{}^2)(4\kappa_6+C_QL)}{L^2-1}
 +\frac{3(1+r)C_{\mathcal S}'{}^2}{L-1}\right].
\end{align*}
Thus the two-cutoff background error is at most
\[
 \varepsilon_{\rm r}
     \min\{\mathsf K_b\sqrt{N_tL^{-t}},\mathsf K_b^\infty\},
 \qquad \mathsf K_b^\infty=2B_3a_+^2C_{\rm bg}^\infty.
\]
It is also bounded by
$\max\{\mathsf K_b,\mathsf K_b^\infty\}\varepsilon_{\rm r}
(N_tL^{-t})^{1/3}$.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
In the same resolvent identity use
$\sup m^k\le\pi\mathsf S_{\rm e}C_{\rm db}C_{\rm ax}
(1+2B_3)eL^{-2(t-k)}$ and the elementary hopping bound
\[
 \|D^\xi[\tilde U_k]-D^\xi[\check U_k]\|
                            \le3(1+r)\sup a_k.
\]
The two geometric sums are $(L^2-1)^{-1}$ and $(L-1)^{-1}$.
Finally $\min\{x^{1/2},1\}\le x^{1/3}$ for $x\ge0$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Changing the bare spacing}

\begin{lemma}[Transport between the two meshes]\label{C-420-9}
Let $|\partial U^{\rm B}(p)-1|\le\alpha(\xi/L)^2$, where
$0\le\alpha\le10^{-4}/(2\pi)$, and put $V=\mathcal M U^{\rm B}$.
Let $Q$ be the normalized first fermion average between the two
bare lattices:
\[
 (Q\varphi)(y)=L^{-3}\sum_{x\in B(y)}q(U^{\rm B};y,x)\varphi(x),
 \qquad (Q^*\psi)(x)=q(U^{\rm B};y,x)^*\psi(y).
\]
Then $QQ^*=1$. Write $T_e^{\rm A},T_e^{\rm B}$ for covariant
translations by $\xi e,(\xi/L)e$ at $V,U^{\rm B}$, and
$\nabla_e^{\rm A}=\xi^{-1}(T_e^{\rm A}-1)$,
$\nabla_e^{\rm B}=L\xi^{-1}(T_e^{\rm B}-1)$.
With $C_1=234$ and $C_{\rm tr}=9C_1$,
\begin{align*}
 \|T_e^{\rm A}Q-Q(T_e^{\rm B})^L\|&\le C_{\rm tr}\alpha\xi^2,\\
 \|((T_e^{\rm B})^n-1)Q^*\psi\|
   &\le2\sqrt{n/L}\,\xi\|\nabla_e^{\rm A}\psi\|
                         +C_{\rm tr}\alpha\xi^2\|\psi\|,
                   &&1\le n\le L,\\
 \|\nabla_e^{\rm A}Q\varphi\|
   &\le\|\nabla_e^{\rm B}\varphi\|
                         +C_{\rm tr}\alpha\xi\|\varphi\|.
\end{align*}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The weighted inner products give the stated adjoint, and the
normalization of the contour means gives
$L^{-3}\sum_xq(y,x)q(y,x)^*=1$.
Fix two neighboring blocks. In their complete axial gauge every
link is a product of at most $2L-2$ conjugated plaquette variables,
so its distance from one is at most $2\alpha\xi^2/L$.
Each contour defining a fermion average has length at most
$3(L-1)/2$. Its transport and its mean $S$ are within
$3\alpha\xi^2$ of one. The normalization satisfies
$n(y)\ge(1-3\alpha\xi^2)^2$; hence
$|q(y,x)-1|\le12\alpha\xi^2$.

The same calculation for the gauge average uses the contour-mean
formula in \cite[eq.\ (37)]{YMM1}. Its contour families have
diameter at most $6\alpha\xi^2$, and their group means lie within
$24\alpha\xi^2$ of their members. Thus those means are within
$27\alpha\xi^2$ of one. The straight transport is within
$2\alpha\xi^2$ of one. Each argument of the logarithm in the
block-average formula is consequently within $58\alpha\xi^2$
of one, and its logarithm has norm at most $116\alpha\xi^2$.
It follows that $|V(y,y+\xi e)-1|\le234\alpha\xi^2$.
All logarithms and contour means used here are in their defining
small-field neighborhoods, since $\alpha\le10^{-4}/(2\pi)$.

The products just compared transform covariantly. Thus any two
such products with the same endpoints differ by at most
$6C_1\alpha\xi^2$ in every gauge. The kernel of the first
operator in the statement is $L^{-3}$ times just such a difference:
\[
 V(y,y+\xi e)q(y+\xi e,x+\xi e)
               -q(y,x)U^{\rm B}(x\longrightarrow x+\xi e).
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz within each block proves its norm bound.

For the second estimate, among the $L^3$ sites of a block,
exactly $nL^2$ cross its boundary after $n$ translations in
direction $e$. At the other sites the difference is a transport
error of size $6C_1\alpha\xi^2|\psi(y)|$.
At the crossing sites it is the sum of a transport error and
$q(y,x)^*\xi\nabla_e^{\rm A}\psi(y)$.
Here $|q|\le2$. The transport errors have combined norm at most
$6\sqrt2C_1\alpha\xi^2\|\psi\|$, while the other term has norm
at most $2\sqrt{n/L}\,\xi\|\nabla_e^{\rm A}\psi\|$.
This proves the estimate with $C_{\rm tr}$.
Finally use
\[
 \nabla_e^{\rm A}Q
  =\xi^{-1}(T_e^{\rm A}Q-Q(T_e^{\rm B})^L)
       +\xi^{-1}Q\sum_{j<L}(T_e^{\rm B})^j(T_e^{\rm B}-1).
\]
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The block operators at two spacings]\label{C-420-10}
Assume $\ell L^s\ge C_{\rm side}$,
$|\partial U^{\rm B}(p)-1|\le\alpha(\xi/L)^2$, and
\[
 0\le\alpha\le\min\{10^{-4}/(2\pi),\epsilon_S/2\},\qquad
 \sup|J'|\le\mathfrak m_s/2+\varrho_F,
 \qquad \varrho_F=\min\{\varrho_S,\lambda_\rho/2\}.
\]
The same Lipschitz function $J'$ is sampled on both bare lattices.
Then
\[
 \|\mathsf D^{\rm B}[U^{\rm B};J']
       -\mathsf D^{\rm A}[\mathcal M U^{\rm B};J']\|
 \le\mathsf K_c\xi(1+\operatorname{Lip}_s(J')),
\]
where
\begin{align*}
 \mathsf K_c&=b_F+2b_F^2C'_{\mathcal S}+b_F^2\mathsf K_T,\\
 \mathsf K_T&=\left[(1+r)(1+3C_{\rm tr})
          +\frac{2c_\flat^2}{\lambda_\rho}(2+\sqrt6C_{\rm tr})\right]
                     (C'_{\mathcal S}+C'_\nabla)^2
                 +(\sqrt3/2+b_F)C_{\mathcal S}'{}^2,\\
 c_\flat^2&=3(1+r)^2.
\end{align*}
These constants require no lower bound on $\mathfrak m_s\ge0$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Set $V=\mathcal M U^{\rm B}$. The curvature averaging estimate
gives $|\partial V-1|\le2\alpha\xi^2$, so \cref{C-420-7}
applies on both lattices.

First eliminate the chamber complement at spacing $\xi'$.
For $T_0=D^{\xi'}[U]+\mathfrak m_s-\widehat J'$, write
\[
 E=\Pi_1T_0\Pi_1,\quad C=\Pi_1T_0\iota,\quad
 B=\iota^*T_0\Pi_1.
\]
The chamber coercivity and the source radius give
$\operatorname{Re}E\ge\lambda_\rho/(2\xi')$.
The off-diagonal bounds are
$\|C\varphi\|\le c_\flat\|\nabla^U\varphi\|$ and
$|\langle\varphi',Bg\rangle|
\le c_\flat\|\nabla^U\varphi'\|\|g\|$.
Consequently the site operator and heavy correction are
\[
 k=D^{{\rm W},\xi'}[U]+\mathfrak m_s-J'-H+aP_R,
 \qquad H=BE^{-1}C,\qquad P_R=(R\iota)^*(R\iota),
\]
and
\[
 |\langle\varphi',H\varphi\rangle|
 \le\frac{2c_\flat^2}{\lambda_\rho}\xi'
                 \|\nabla^U\varphi'\|\|\nabla^U\varphi\|.
\]
Since $R=R\iota\iota^*$, putting $R^{\rm s}=R\iota$ gives
$\mathsf T=R^{\rm s}k^{-1}R^{{\rm s}*}$.
Both $k^{-1}G$ and $(k^{-1})^*G$ have norm at most
$C'_{\mathcal S}\|G\|$ and gradient norm at most
$C'_\nabla\|G\|$, by \cref{C-420-7}.

The composite averages satisfy $R^{\rm s}_{\rm B}=R^{\rm s}_{\rm A}Q$.
Using $QQ^*=1$ gives the exact identity
\[
 \mathsf T^{\rm B}-\mathsf T^{\rm A}
 =R^{\rm s}_{\rm A}k_{\rm A}^{-1}
     (k_{\rm A}Q-Qk_{\rm B})k_{\rm B}^{-1}R^{{\rm s}*}_{\rm B}.
\]
Decompose the middle factor as $E_{\rm W}+E_{\rm M}+E_{\rm P}-E_H$,
corresponding to the Wilson term, source, penalty, and heavy correction.
For unit block spinors it suffices to estimate its pairing with
$\varphi=k_{\rm B}^{-1}R^{{\rm s}*}_{\rm B}\chi$ and
$\varphi'=(k_{\rm A}^{-1})^*R^{{\rm s}*}_{\rm A}\chi'$.

For the Wilson term, with $T=T_e^{\rm B}$ use
\[
 (1-T_e^{\rm A})Q-LQ(1-T)
   =QT^L-T_e^{\rm A}Q
       +Q\sum_{j=1}^{L-1}(T^j-1)(1-T).
\]
Move $T^j-1$ to the first factor in the pairing and apply
\cref{C-420-9} in direction $-e$.
Sum $\sqrt{j/L}\le L$, then sum the six directions. This yields
\begin{align*}
 |\langle\varphi',E_{\rm W}\varphi\rangle|
 \le{}&\tfrac12(1+r)\xi
  \bigl[2\|\nabla^{\rm A}\varphi'\|\|\nabla^{\rm B}\varphi\|
       +\sqrt6C_{\rm tr}\|\varphi'\|\|\nabla^{\rm B}\varphi\|\\
 &\hspace{40mm}+6C_{\rm tr}\|\varphi'\|\|\varphi\|\bigr]\\
 \le{}&(1+r)(1+3C_{\rm tr})\xi
   (\|\varphi'\|+\|\nabla^{\rm A}\varphi'\|)
   (\|\varphi\|+\|\nabla^{\rm B}\varphi\|).
\end{align*}
The source acts on spin and flavour, whereas $q$ acts on colour.
The distance from a block site to its center is at most
$\sqrt3\xi/2$, and $L^{-3}\sum_x|q(y,x)|^2=1$.
Thus blockwise Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \|E_{\rm M}\|\le\tfrac{\sqrt3}2\xi\operatorname{Lip}_s(J').
\]
For the penalty,
\[
 E_{\rm P}=(a^{\rm A}-a^{\rm B})R^{{\rm s}*}_{\rm A}R^{\rm s}_{\rm B},
 \qquad |a^{\rm A}-a^{\rm B}|\le b_F\xi.
\]

The heavy correction at spacing $\xi$ is bounded using the third
transport estimate. At spacing $\xi/L$ use the second estimate
with $n=1$, which gives
\[
 \|\nabla^{\rm B}Q^*\varphi'\|
 \le2\sqrt L\|\nabla^{\rm A}\varphi'\|
             +\sqrt6C_{\rm tr}L\alpha\xi\|\varphi'\|.
\]
Since $1+2L^{-1/2}\le2$, their sum satisfies
\[
 |\langle\varphi',E_H\varphi\rangle|
 \le\frac{2c_\flat^2}{\lambda_\rho}(2+\sqrt6C_{\rm tr})\xi
    (\|\varphi'\|+\|\nabla^{\rm A}\varphi'\|)
    (\|\varphi\|+\|\nabla^{\rm B}\varphi\|).
\]
Together these bounds give
$\|\mathsf T^{\rm B}-\mathsf T^{\rm A}\|
\le\mathsf K_T\xi(1+\operatorname{Lip}_s(J'))$.
Finally expand
\[
 \mathsf D^{\rm B}-\mathsf D^{\rm A}
 =(a^{\rm B}-a^{\rm A})
 -((a^{\rm B})^2-(a^{\rm A})^2)\mathsf T^{\rm B}
 -(a^{\rm A})^2(\mathsf T^{\rm B}-\mathsf T^{\rm A}).
\]
Use $|(a^{\rm B})^2-(a^{\rm A})^2|\le2b_F^2\xi$ and
$\|\mathsf T^{\rm B}\|\le C'_{\mathcal S}$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The classical starts}

\begin{proposition}[Comparison of the starting quadratic forms]\label{C-420-11}
There is $\Theta_F\ge\Theta_\star$ such that
\eqref{eq:two-mesh-radius} holds whenever $L^s\mathsf b\ge\Theta_F$.
Assume this inequality and $\ell L^s\ge C_{\rm side}$ in
\cref{C-420-2}. Take $\varpi(W)<\varepsilon_{\rm r}$,
$\sup|J_s|\le\mathfrak m_s/2$, and $\sup|w|<8\varrho$.
Set
\begin{align*}
 \delta_D&=\mathsf K_c\xi(1+\operatorname{Lip}_s(J_s))
                  +\mathsf K_b\varepsilon_{\rm r}\sqrt{N_{[s]}\xi},\\
 \delta_F&=(1+\sup|\hat s_w|/\varrho_F)\delta_D
                      +\mathsf K_c\xi\operatorname{Lip}_s(\hat s_w),\\
 \mathfrak f_s&=(1-c_b/9)\frac{a_-\mathfrak m_s}{2a_-+\mathfrak m_s},
 \qquad \epsilon_F=\nu N_{[s]}\delta_F/\mathfrak f_s.
\end{align*}
Then the following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] Each $\mathsf D^\bullet_{\rm st}$ is independent of
the representative of its minimal orbit, and
\[
 \operatorname{Re}\mathsf D^\bullet_{\rm st}\ge\mathfrak f_s
       \ge\tfrac49c_b\mathfrak m_s\ge\tfrac14c_b\mathfrak m_s.
\]
If $\mathfrak m_s\le2a_-$, then also
$\mathfrak f_s\ge2\mathfrak m_s/9$.
\item[(ii)] The two ordinary block operators differ by at most
$\delta_D$. For any Lipschitz matrix field $N$ with values in
the complex span of $\mathfrak B$,
\[
 \|\mathsf M^{\rm B}[N]-\mathsf M^{\rm A}[N]\|
 \le\frac{\sup|N|}{\varrho_F}\delta_D
                                  +\mathsf K_c\xi\operatorname{Lip}_s(N).
\]
Thus $\|\mathsf D^{\rm B}_{\rm st}-\mathsf D^{\rm A}_{\rm st}\|
\le\delta_F$. In all these bounds the background term can be
replaced by
\[
 \varepsilon_{\rm r}
 \min\{\mathsf K_b\sqrt{N_{[s]}\xi},\mathsf K_b^\infty\}.
\]
\item[(iii)] If $C,\delta>0$ are the kernel constants from
\cref{C-408-5}, the kernel difference of the starts at $x\ne y$ is bounded by
\[
 \min\{\delta_F,
       2a_+^2C(1+\sup|\hat s_w|/\varrho_F)e^{-\delta d(x,y)}\}.
\]
Its exponentially weighted row and column sums at rate $\delta/4$
are at most
\[
 \delta_F+C_\delta
  \sqrt{2a_+^2C(1+\sup|\hat s_w|/\varrho_F)\delta_F},
 \qquad C_\delta=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^3}e^{-\delta|z|/4}.
\]
The norm $|z|$ is the same one used in the kernel decay of
\cref{C-408-5}.
\item[(iv)] For $P_\tau=(1-\tau)\mathsf D^{\rm A}_{\rm st}
+\tau\mathsf D^{\rm B}_{\rm st}$,
\[
 \varphi_F=\int_0^1\operatorname{tr}
       [P_\tau^{-1}(\mathsf D^{\rm B}_{\rm st}
                         -\mathsf D^{\rm A}_{\rm st})]\,d\tau
\]
obeys $|\varphi_F|\le\epsilon_F$ and
$\det\mathsf D^{\rm B}_{\rm st}/\det\mathsf D^{\rm A}_{\rm st}
=e^{\varphi_F}$.
\item[(v)] If $w$ is real and
$\gamma_4J^\dagger\gamma_4=J$, both determinants are positive.
\item[(vi)] For two sources in the stated ranges set
\[
 \Delta_{\rm src}
  =(1+c_bC'_{\mathcal S}\mathfrak m_s/9)\sup|J'_s-J_s|
       +\frac{16F^{\rm UV}}{9L^s\mathsf b^2}\sup|w'-w|.
\]
On either lattice the starts differ by at most
$b_F^2C_{\mathcal S}'{}^2\Delta_{\rm src}$.
Their determinant logarithms, continued along the straight source
segment, differ by at most
$\nu N_{[s]}b_F^2C_{\mathcal S}'{}^2\Delta_{\rm src}/\mathfrak f_s$.
\item[(vii)] Put $c_w=L^s(\mathsf b-w)$ and
\[
 \widehat F^\bullet
 =e^{-A^{\eta_{t_0^\bullet}}(c_w,U^\bullet)}
                               \det\mathsf D^\bullet_{\rm st}.
\]
Then $\widehat F^{\rm B}=\widehat F^{\rm A}e^{\zeta_F}$, where
\[
 |\zeta_F|\le\mathsf K_w\|c_w\|_{(t_0)}
        \varepsilon_{\rm r}^2N_{[s]}t_0^{1/2}L^{-t_0/2}+\epsilon_F.
\]
The norm and $\mathsf K_w$ are those of the weighted classical
action comparison in \cite[Prop.\ 113.9]{YMM1}.
\item[(viii)] The starts are continuous in $W$ on
$\{\varpi<\varepsilon_{\rm r}\}$, Borel on the field cut, and
holomorphic in the finitely many source values. Uniformly there,
\[
 \|\mathsf D^\bullet_{\rm st}\|
 \le a_++a_+^2C'_{\mathcal S}
                 +a_+^2C_{\mathcal S}'{}^2c_b\mathfrak m_s/18.
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Since $\varepsilon(x)$ decreases to zero, the two positive bounds
in \eqref{eq:two-mesh-radius} hold for all sufficiently large
$x=L^s\mathsf b$. Choose $\Theta_F$ accordingly. The classical
backgrounds then satisfy the hypotheses of
\cref{C-420-8,C-420-10}; their bare curvature coefficient is
$B_3\varepsilon_{\rm r}$. The extra small numerical bound in the
transport lemma is already part of the classical comparison radius,
\cite[eq.\ (2146)]{YMM1}.

For accretivity put $\mu=\mathfrak m_s/2$ and
$\varphi=a\mathcal SR^*\chi$. The defining equation gives
\[
 \langle\chi,\mathsf D\chi\rangle
   =a\|\chi-R\varphi\|^2
        +\langle\varphi,(D^\xi+\mathfrak m_s-\widehat J_s)\varphi\rangle.
\]
Its real part is at least
$a\|\chi-R\varphi\|^2+\mu\|\varphi\|^2$.
Since $\|R\|=1$, minimizing this expression gives
\[
 \operatorname{Re}\langle\chi,\mathsf D\chi\rangle
 \ge\frac{a\mu}{a+\mu}\|\chi\|^2,
 \qquad
 \mu\|\varphi\|^2\le\operatorname{Re}\langle\chi,\mathsf D\chi\rangle.
\]
The same calculation for the adjoint gives this last bound for
$\varphi'=a\mathcal S^*R^*\chi$. Hence
\[
 |\langle\chi,\mathsf M[\hat s_w]\chi\rangle|
 \le\frac{\sup|\hat s_w|}{\mu}
              \operatorname{Re}\langle\chi,\mathsf D\chi\rangle
 \le\frac{c_b}{9}\operatorname{Re}\langle\chi,\mathsf D\chi\rangle.
\]
This proves the displayed floor. Its numerical consequences follow
from the admitted $c_b$ and $\mathfrak m_s\le1$; if
$\mathfrak m_s\le2a_-$, use
$a_-/(2a_-+\mathfrak m_s)\ge1/4$ and $1-c_b/9\ge8/9$.
The residual gauges equal one on the block sites, giving the
independence of the minimal-orbit representative.

For (ii), insert $\mathsf D^{\rm A}[\mathcal M U^{\rm B};J_s]$
between the two operators and apply
\cref{C-420-8,C-420-10}. To differentiate, let $N\ne0$ and use
the disc $|z|<\varrho_F/\sup|N|$ in $J_s-zN$. This entire disc
lies in the extended source domain. The previous comparison there
is bounded by
\[
 \delta_D+\mathsf K_c\xi|z|\operatorname{Lip}_s(N).
\]
Cauchy's estimate on smaller circles, followed by a limit to the
displayed radius, proves the derivative estimate. For $N=0$ it
is immediate. Set $N=\hat s_w$ and add the ordinary comparison.
The alternative background bound is \cref{C-420-14}.

Each kernel also has the exponential bound of \cref{C-408-5}.
The same Cauchy argument gives its derivative bound, proving (iii).
Off the diagonal use
$\min\{\delta_F,Ae^{-\delta d}\}
\le\sqrt{A\delta_F}e^{-\delta d/2}$ and sum after multiplying
by $e^{\delta d/4}$; the diagonal contributes $\delta_F$.

Every $P_\tau$ has real part at least $\mathfrak f_s$, so it is
invertible and $\|P_\tau^{-1}\|\le\mathfrak f_s^{-1}$.
Jacobi's determinant formula proves (iv), including the bound
with dimension $\nu N_{[s]}$.

For real $w$, at $J=0$ the two parity blocks of the starting form
are adjoints. Its determinant is therefore
$|\det D_+|^{2N_f}>0$. If $J^\sharp=J$, the same relation with
$\gamma_4$ makes the determinant real along the path $\tau J$.
The accretive floor prevents a zero, so its sign remains positive.

For (vi), differentiate along the source segment. The resolvent
derivative is $\dot{\mathcal S}=\mathcal S\widehat{\dot J_s}\mathcal S$.
The derivative of $\mathsf M[\hat s_w]$ has three terms: the
derivative of $\hat s_w$, and a resolvent derivative on each side.
Thus \cref{C-420-3,C-420-7} give
\[
 \|\dot{\mathsf D}_{\rm st}\|
 \le b_F^2C_{\mathcal S}'{}^2
 \left[(1+2C'_{\mathcal S}\sup|\hat s_w|)\sup|\dot J_s|
                              +\sup|\dot{\hat s}_w|\right].
\]
Integration gives $\Delta_{\rm src}$. Apply Jacobi's formula and
the same floor along this segment to obtain its logarithmic form.

Part (vii) adds the logarithm in (iv) to the weighted action
difference. The latter is exactly the bound of
\cite[Prop.\ 113.9]{YMM1}, applicable to the same backgrounds,
radius, and complex coefficient $c_w$.

The norm bound in (viii) follows directly from \cref{C-420-7}.
For continuity, fix $W_0$ in the stated open set. Nearby $W$ have
a principal logarithmic coordinate relative to $W_0$. The local
real-background response used in \cite[Lem.\ 113.6]{YMM1} supplies
a continuous representative of the minimal orbit in this coordinate.
Its plaquettes stay inside the curvature domain. The finite
matrices $D^\xi$, $R$, and $\mathcal K^{-1}$ are continuous there.
Independence of the representative then proves continuity of the
displayed start as a function of $W$. The source denominators
$\mathsf b-w$ do not vanish, and all inverses remain in their
source domains, proving holomorphy.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Size of the determinant error]\label{C-420-12}
The constants are chosen in the following order: the averaging
constants, the mass-independent operator constants, the background
comparison constants, and then $\Theta_F$. All are formed after
the original admission constants. None is a new restriction on
their choice; $L^s\mathsf b\ge\Theta_F$ is a restriction on the
restart depth.

For later summation it is useful to expand $\epsilon_F$.
Put $q_s=\mathfrak m_s/\mathfrak f_s$ and
$y_{[s]}=(\log L^s\mathsf b)^{2\mathfrak p_0}$.
Then $q_s\le9/(4c_b)$, and $q_s\le9/2$ if
$\mathfrak m_s\le2a_-$. The estimate above gives
\begin{align*}
 \epsilon_F\le{}&\frac{q_s\nu}{\mathsf m}
 \left(1+\frac{c_b\mathfrak m_s}{18\varrho_F}\right)
 \left[\mathsf K_c\ell^3L^{5s-K}
                (1+L^{-2s}\operatorname{Lip}(J))\right.\\
 &\hspace{36mm}\left.
 +2c_\rho A_0\mathsf K_b(y_{[s]}/\mathsf b)^{1/2}
                      \ell^{9/2}L^{5s-(K-s)/2}\right]\\
 &+\frac{q_s\nu}{\mathsf m}\mathsf K_c\ell^3L^{5s-K}
       \frac{16F^{\rm UV}}{9L^{2s}\mathsf b^2}\operatorname{Lip}(w).
\end{align*}
This identity keeps the dependence on the torus side visible.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Uniform constants for the restart comparison]
\label{C-420-13}
Define
\[
 s_F=\min\{s'\ge1:L^{s'}\gamma^{-2}\ge\Theta_F,
             \ 2L^{s'}\ge C_{\rm side},\ 2a_-L^{s'}\ge\mathsf m_+\},
\]
and
\begin{align*}
 K_F=\max\left\{1,
 \left(1+\frac{c_b\mathsf m_+}{18\varrho_F}\right)
 \max\left\{\mathsf K_c\left(1+\frac{\varrho_J}{40M}\right),
                         \mathsf K_b,\mathsf K_b^\infty\right\}
                   +\frac{\mathsf K_cB_F}{2880M}\right\},\\
 C_D=\max\left\{1,b_F^2C_{\mathcal S}'{}^2
           \max\{1+c_bC'_{\mathcal S}\mathsf m_+/9,B_F/9\}\right\}.
\end{align*}
For the data and depth hypotheses of \cref{C-418-11}, assume
$s\ge s_F$. Let $\|w\|_\sharp,\|w'\|_\sharp<\varrho$ and
$\|J\|_\sharp,\|J'\|_\sharp<\varrho_J$, where
$\|f\|_\sharp=\max\{\|f\|_\infty,40M\operatorname{Lip}(f)\}$.
The starting operator $\hat{\mathbb D}^\bullet$ of
\cref{C-418-3} is exactly $\mathsf D^\bullet_{\rm st}$ above.
It is continuous in $W$, Borel on the field cut, holomorphic in the
sources, constant on the minimal orbit, and
\[
 \operatorname{Re}\hat{\mathbb D}^\bullet\ge\tfrac29L^{-s}\mathsf m,
 \qquad
 \|\hat{\mathbb D}^\bullet\|
 \le b_F+b_F^2C'_{\mathcal S}
                       +b_F^2C_{\mathcal S}'{}^2c_b\mathsf m_+/18.
\]
Furthermore,
\begin{align*}
 \|\hat{\mathbb D}^\bullet(w,J)-\hat{\mathbb D}^\bullet(w',J')\|
  &\le C_DL^{-s}(\|J-J'\|_\infty+\|w-w'\|_\infty),\\
 \|\hat{\mathbb D}^{\rm B}(w,J)-\hat{\mathbb D}^{\rm A}(w,J)\|
  &\le K_F\left[\xi+\bar\varepsilon_{\rm r}
                    \min\{(N_{[s]}\xi)^{1/2},1\}\right],
\end{align*}
where $\bar\varepsilon_{\rm r}=2c_\rho\varepsilon(L^s\gamma^{-2})$.
In particular the second bound is at most
$K_F[\xi+\bar\varepsilon_{\rm r}(N_{[s]}\xi)^{1/3}]$.
For real $w$ and $J^\sharp=J$ its determinant is positive.
These assertions prove \cref{C-418-11}.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
The definition of $s_F$, together with $\mathsf b>\gamma^{-2}$,
$\ell\ge2$, and $\mathsf m\le\mathsf m_+$, gives every depth,
side, and mass condition in \cref{C-420-11}. The field cut is
contained in $\{\varpi<\varepsilon_{\rm r}\}$ by
\cite[Lem.\ 113.10]{YMM1}. Source admission gives
$\varrho_J\le\mathsf m/4$, so $\sup|J_s|<\mathfrak m_s/4$.
These statements hold along the segment between the two sources.

We verify the identification of the quadratic form, including its
mass normalization. Put $k=t_0^\bullet$ and
\[
 n_z=m_0^\bullet-a_{K^\bullet}\widehat J+zL^{-k}\widehat N.
\]
Then $\mathcal K^\bullet[J_s-zN]=L^k\mathcal K_k[n_z]$.
If $R_k$ is the average with plain counting inner products, the
weighted normalization gives $R=L^{-3k/2}R_k$ and
$R^*=L^{3k/2}R_k^*$. Hence
\[
 \mathsf D^\bullet[J_s-zN]=L^k\mathsf D^{(k)}[n_z].
\]
The Schur tower exists near $z=0$ by accretivity of its initial
form and then of each Schur complement. Differentiating one step
gives
\[
 \partial_z\mathbb D_{j+1}
 =b_F^2q\Gamma_j^{-1}(\partial_z\mathbb D_j)\Gamma_j^{-1}q^*.
\]
Iterating, starting from $\partial_z\mathbb D_0=L^{-k}\widehat N$,
proves
\[
 \langle\bar\Psi,\mathsf M^\bullet[N]\Psi\rangle
       =L^{-k}\sum_v\bar\psi^{\rm bg}(v)N(x_v)\psi^{\rm bg}(v).
\]
For $N=\hat s_w$ this is exactly the mass member prescribed in
\cref{C-418-3}. This proves the identification on each lattice.

The first conclusions now follow from \cref{C-420-11}.
For source differences use
$\sup|J_s-J_s'|\le L^{-s}\|J-J'\|_\infty$ and
$16F^{\rm UV}/(9\mathsf b^2)\le B_F/9$, since
$\mathsf b^2>\gamma^{-4}\ge16$.
For the two-cutoff bound use
\[
 \operatorname{Lip}_s(J_s)<\varrho_J/(40M),\qquad
 \operatorname{Lip}_s(\hat s_w)<B_F/(2880M),\qquad
 \varepsilon_{\rm r}\le\bar\varepsilon_{\rm r}.
\]
The middle inequality follows from \cref{C-420-3},
$\operatorname{Lip}(w)<\varrho/(40M)$, and
$\varrho/\mathsf b^2<1/128$. Substitute these estimates into
the alternative bound in \cref{C-420-11}(ii).
Finally $\min\{K_bx^{1/2},K_b^\infty\}
\le\max\{K_b,K_b^\infty\}\min\{x^{1/2},1\}$ and
$\min\{x^{1/2},1\}\le x^{1/3}$.
\end{proof}

\section{Restarting the flow and comparing totals}\label{sec:qcdm2-restart-estimates}

The estimates in this appendix control the dependence on discarded scales. They also compare the scalar totals after the restart, including the errors from large fluctuations and from the final density test.

\subsection{The mass contributed by the discarded scales}

A restart at a fixed block scale must retain the mass generated before
that scale.  The relevant number is the ultraviolet part of the
one-loop mass, rather than its full limiting value.  We first identify
this number and estimate the error in replacing the earlier slices by it.

We use the free operators and the three-square formula of
\cite[\S8]{QCDM1}.  All Gaussian expectations below are per block, with
the normalized trace over constant spinors and the three colour
components included.  Put $h=L^{-k}$ when the units are those of level
$k$.  In the operator formulas below $D[1]$ and $V_A$ are in
these units, while $\nabla_j$ is the unscaled lattice difference.
Write $R=R_k(1)$, $P=R^*R$, and
\[
 \mathcal K(m)=D[1]+m+\theta_kP,
 \qquad \theta_k=\frac{b_F(1-L^{-1})}{1-L^{-k}}.
\]
The linear variation of $D[e^{itA}]$ is $V_A$, and that of
$R_k(e^{itA})^*c$ is $\kappa_1$.  For an arbitrary representative $A$
of its gauge class set
\[
 \zeta(m)=\mathcal K(m)^{-1}
       \bigl(V_A\chi_c-m(1-P)\kappa_1\bigr),
 \qquad \chi_c=R^*c.
\]
In the three-square formula replace $\kappa_1$ by $(1-P)\kappa_1$;
call the resulting form $\Phi_k^{\rm nat}(A;m)$.  It agrees with
$\Phi_k$ in the contour gauge used in \cite[\S8]{QCDM1}.  Its Gaussian
mean is unchanged by a gauge transformation whose averaged gauge
parameter vanishes.  Thus it may be evaluated in the straight-average
gauge.  This replacement concerns the representative of the Gaussian
field; it does not change the one-loop coefficients.

\begin{lemma}[The Gaussian for the earlier slices]\label{C-398-39}
Let $k\ge i_0\ge1$ and $n=k-i_0$.  The sum of the Gaussian curvature
covariances for $i<i_0$ is the covariance of one Gaussian on
$\ker Q^s_{i_0}$ with quadratic form
\[
 |dA|^2+|(1-\widetilde P_{i_0})d^*A|^2.
\]
Here $Q^s_{i_0}$ is the straight bond average and
$\widetilde P_{i_0}$ is the corresponding projection for gauge
parameters.  Denote expectation for this Gaussian by
$\mathbb E_{<i_0}$.  In the units of level $k$ its covariance satisfies
\[
 C_{<i_0}\le\Upsilon_0^{-1}\widehat K^{-1},
 \qquad
 C_{<i_0}\le\frac2{\Upsilon_0}
       (\widehat K+L^{2n}/3)^{-1},
 \qquad \Upsilon_0=(2/\pi)^6,
\]
where $\widehat K$ is the symbol of the scalar lattice Laplacian,
acting on each component.  Moreover,
\[
 \sum_{i<i_0}\sigma_i(k;m)
       =\mathbb E_{<i_0}\Phi_k^{\rm nat}(A;m),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{<i_0}|(1-P)\kappa_1|^2\le C_\kappa L^{-n}.
\]
The constants are independent of $k$ and $i_0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
First we prove the gap created by the constraint.  Set $l=L^{i_0}$
and work temporarily in lattice units.  For one component $a$ of $A$,
the average on a coarse bond issuing from $y$ has the form
$l\sum_z\rho_y(z)a(z)$, where $\rho_y\ge0$, $\sum_z\rho_y(z)=1$,
$\rho_y\le l^{-3}$, and its support is the union $X(y)$ of the two
adjacent blocks.  This union has $2l^3$ sites.  If $\bar a$ is the
ordinary mean on $X(y)$, the constraint gives
\[
 |\bar a|^2
   =\left|\sum_z\rho_y(z)(a(z)-\bar a)\right|^2
   \le l^{-3}\sum_{X(y)}|a-\bar a|^2.
\]
Consequently $\sum_{X(y)}|a|^2\le3\sum_{X(y)}|a-\bar a|^2$.
The Neumann Laplacian on a box of sides $2l,l,l$ has gap
$4\sin^2(\pi/(4l))\ge l^{-2}$.  Each site belongs to two such
boxes, and each edge to at most two.  Summing the box estimate yields
\[
 \|A\|^2\le3L^{2i_0}
       \langle A,(dd^*+d^*d)A\rangle.
\]
After changing units this is the gap $L^{2n}/3$.

For completeness, the Fourier constraint has the same uniformly
bounded correction as the full constrained Gaussian.  A level-$k$
fibre $\xi\in[-\pi,\pi]^3\setminus\{0\}$ splits into the $L^{3n}$ classes
\[
 \xi'=\xi+2\pi p,
 \qquad |p_\nu|\le (L^n-1)/2,
 \qquad q\equiv\xi'\pmod {2\pi L^n}.
\]
In each class the covariance is
\[
 \widehat K^{-1/2}B'\widehat K^{-1/2},\qquad
 B'=(1-\Pi')+
 \frac{|(1-\Pi')w'\rangle\langle(1-\Pi')w'|}
      {|\Pi'w'|^2}.
\]
The three direction constraints give the orthonormal vectors spanning
$\Pi'$, and $w'$ is the normalized site-average vector.  The centered
average symbols give $|\Pi'w'|^2\ge(2/\pi)^6$, exactly as for the
constrained covariance in \cite[\S8]{QCDM1}.  Hence
$0\le B'\le\Upsilon_0^{-1}$.  On the constrained subspace the
quadratic form is at least $\Upsilon_0\widehat K$.  Combining this
with the gap and inverting the forms gives the two asserted covariance
bounds on the infinite lattice.

The orthogonal curvature projections telescope: the sum of the first
$i_0$ slice covariances is the projection associated with $Q^s_{i_0}$.
The Gaussian expectation of a quadratic form is linear in its
covariance.  Gauge invariance of $\Phi_k^{\rm nat}$ therefore gives
the identity for the partial sum.

Finally the variation of the composite fermion average telescopes as
\[
 (1-P)\kappa_1=-i\sum_{j<i_0}n_A^{(j)}\chi_c.
\]
There are no terms with $j\ge i_0$, since $Q^s_jA=0$ there.
Each contour defining $n_A^{(j)}$ has at most $3L$ bonds of level $j$.
A straight-average bond at that level has variance at most $C_QL^j$
in lattice units.  Taking square roots before summing the levels
gives the constant
$6L\sqrt{C_Q}/(\sqrt L-1)$, and hence a mean square bounded by
$C_\kappa L^{i_0}$.  In level-$k$ units this is
$C_\kappa L^{-(k-i_0)}$, as required.
\end{proof}

Define the ultraviolet quadratic form by omitting the block part of
the propagator:
\[
 \Phi_k^{\rm UV}(A)=
 \left\langle h^{-1}\sum_j\frac{\varrho_j}{2}
       |\nabla_j^{(1)}\chi_c-\nabla_j\zeta^{\rm UV}|^2
       \right\rangle_c,
 \qquad \zeta^{\rm UV}=D[1]^{-1}V_A\chi_c.
\]
Its slice means are $\sigma_i^{\rm UV}$, and its mean for the
unconstrained covariance $\widehat K^{-1}$ is $F^{\rm UV}$.
This number is independent of scale: the substitution $q=t/h$ gives
\begin{equation}\label{C-398-14}
 F^{\rm UV}=3\Sigma(r),\qquad
 \Sigma(r)=\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^3}\frac{d^3t}{(2\pi)^3}
 \frac1{k_1(t)}
 \sum_j\frac{\varrho_j}{2}
 \|\widehat\nabla_j^{(1)}(t)
       -\widehat\nabla_j(t)\widehat D(t)^{-1}\widehat V(t)
       \|_{\rm HS}^2,
\end{equation}
where $k_1(t)=\sum_\nu4\sin^2(t_\nu/2)$.  The normalization of the
Hilbert--Schmidt norm is the normalized spin trace above.  The identity
$\operatorname{Re}\widehat D^{-1}\le c_{\rm re}^{-1}$ bounds the
integrand by $C/k_1(t)$; thus the integral is finite in dimension three.

\begin{proposition}[Partial one-loop sums]\label{C-398-40}
There is $B_5<\infty$, depending only on the chamber operator, $r$,
$L$ and $b_F$, with the following properties.  Let
$k\ge1$, $0\le i_0\le k$, $n=k-i_0$, and $m,m'\in[0,1]$,
in level-$k$ units.
Set
\[
 F_{<i_0}(k;m)=\sum_{i<i_0}\sigma_i(k;m),\qquad
 F^{\rm UV}_{<i_0}=\sum_{i<i_0}\sigma_i^{\rm UV}.
\]
Empty sums are zero.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item The coefficients $\sigma_i^{\rm UV}$ are nonnegative and do not
depend on $k>i$, the mass, or $b_F$.  They satisfy
\[
 0\le F^{\rm UV}-F^{\rm UV}_{<i_0}\le B_5L^{-i_0},
 \qquad 0\le\sigma_i^{\rm UV}\le B_5L^{-i}.
\]
\item The partial sum obeys
\begin{align*}
 |F_{<i_0}(k;m)-F^{\rm UV}_{<i_0}|
   &\le B_5L^{-n}(L^{-n}+L^{-k/2}+m),\\
 |F_{<i_0}(k;m)-F^{\rm UV}|
   &\le B_5(L^{-i_0}+3L^{-n}).
\end{align*}
\item Its mass dependence and its comparison at two levels satisfy
\begin{align*}
 |F_{<i_0}(k;m)-F_{<i_0}(k;m')|
   &\le B_5|m-m'|L^{-n},\\
 |F_{<i_0}(k;m)-F_{<i_0}(j;m')|
   &\le6B_5L^{-(j-i_0)}\quad(i_0\le j\le k).
\end{align*}
In particular, for $i<j\le k$,
\begin{align*}
 |\sigma_i(k;m)-\sigma_i^{\rm UV}|
   &\le4LB_5L^{-(k-i)},\\
 0\le\sigma_i(k;m)
   &\le B_5\bigl(L^{-i}+4L^{1-(k-i)}\bigr),\\
 |\sigma_i(k;m)-\sigma_i(j;m')|
   &\le8LB_5L^{-(j-i)}.
\end{align*}
\item At every fixed depth $n$ the limit
\[
 F^{[n]}=\lim_{k\to\infty}F_{<k-n}(k;0)
        =F^{\rm UV}+F^{\rm GW,[n]}
\]
exists, with $0\le F^{\rm GW,[n]}\le B_5L^{-2n}$.  Uniformly in
$i_0,n,m$,
\[
 |F_{<i_0}(k;m)-F^{[n]}|
       \le B_5(L^{-i_0/4}+mL^{-n}).
\]
Define $F_\infty:=F^{[0]}=\lim_{k\to\infty}F(k;0)$.  Then
$F^{[n]}\downarrow F^{\rm UV}$, and
$\bar\sigma_d=F^{[d-1]}-F^{[d]}$ is nonnegative with
$\sum_{d\ge1}\bar\sigma_d=F_\infty-F^{\rm UV}$.  The equal-depth
increments satisfy
\begin{align*}
 |F_{<i_0+1}(k+1;m)-F_{<i_0}(k;m)|
   &\le2B_5(L^{-i_0/4}+mL^{-n}),\\
 |\sigma_{i+1}(k+1;m)-\sigma_i(k;m)|
   &\le4B_5(L^{-i/4}+mL^{1-(k-i)}).
\end{align*}
\item Let $1\le i_0\le k\le K$, let $x_i\ne0$ for $i<i_0$,
and let $t_i=L^{K-i}\mathsf b$, $\tau\ne0$, and
\[
 G_{<i_0,k}(x)=\sum_{i<i_0}\frac{L^{k-i}}{x_i}
                              \sigma_i(k;\mathfrak m_k).
\]
Then
\[
 \left|G_{<i_0,k}(x)
          -\frac{F_{<i_0}(k;\mathfrak m_k)}{\tau t_k}\right|
 \le\frac{F_{<i_0}(k;\mathfrak m_k)}{|\tau|t_k}
       \max_{i<i_0}\frac{|x_i-\tau t_i|}{|x_i|}.
\]
If $\varpi>0$, $|x_i-\tau t_i|\le\bar B$ and
$|x_i|\ge\varpi t_i$, this gives
\[
 |\tau t_kG_{<i_0,k}(x)-F^{\rm UV}|
 \le B_5(L^{-i_0}+3L^{-n})
       +\frac{\bar B F(k;\mathfrak m_k)L^{-(n+1)}}{\varpi t_k}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
We give the estimates in level-$k$ units.  Constants denoted by $C$
depend only on the parameters listed in the statement; their maximum
will determine $B_5$.

The form $\Phi_k^{\rm UV}$ is a nonnegative quadratic form in the
curvature and is invariant under every addition $d\lambda$.  Its
density in lattice units does not depend on $k$.  A slice-$i$ law is
periodic under translations of level $i+1$, so its mean per block is
independent of the later level used to compute it.  The curvature
projections increase with $i_0$.  Hence the partial sums increase and
are bounded by $F^{\rm UV}$.  At $k=i_0$ the constrained covariance
differs from $\widehat K^{-1}$ by at most four terms
\[
 \widehat K^{-1/2}|u\rangle\langle u|\widehat K^{-1/2}
\]
per fibre, where $\|u\|=1$ and each coefficient is bounded by
$\Upsilon_0^{-1}$.  The ultraviolet form per unit of $|A_q|^2$ is
bounded by $Ch$.  Each correction therefore costs at most
\[
 Ch\sum_q\frac{|u_q|^2}{k_q}
       \le Ch\,C|\xi|^{-2}.
\]
Its integral is finite.  This proves (a), including the slice estimate
by subtraction of successive partial sums.

We next record the estimates that use the gap of
\cref{C-398-39}.  In the standard fibre notation let
$g=D[1]^{-1}$, $X=Rg$, and
$D_k=(\theta_k^{-1}+RgR^*)^{-1}$.  Write $v_q$ for the block-average
symbol.  The free symbol bounds give
\[
 \|g_q\|\le C|q|^{-1},\qquad
 \|D_k\|\le\min(C|\xi|,\theta_k),\qquad
 \sum_qv_q^2=1.
\]
The improved covariance implies
\begin{align*}
 \mathbb E_{<i_0}|D_kXV_A\chi_c|^2
 &\le C\|D_k\|^2\sum_q
        \frac{v_q^2}{|q|^2(k_q+L^{2n}/3)}\\
 &\le CL^{-2n}\|D_k\|^2(|\xi|^{-2}+\pi^{-2})
 \le C_1L^{-2n}.
\end{align*}
At zero mass,
\[
 \zeta_0=\mathcal K(0)^{-1}V_A\chi_c
       =gV_A\chi_c-gR^*D_kXV_A\chi_c.
\]
The mean square of its first term is bounded by
\[
 C\int_{\mathbb R^3}
       \frac{d^3q}{|q|^2(c|q|^2+L^{2n}/3)}\le CL^{-n}.
\]
That of the second is at most
$CL^{-2n}\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^3}(|\xi|^{-2}+1)\,d^3\xi$.
Together with the last estimate of \cref{C-398-39}, this proves
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcd2-uv-f-bound}
 \mathbb E_{<i_0}|\zeta_0|^2\le CL^{-n},\qquad
 \mathbb E_{<i_0}|f|^2\le C_fL^{-n},
 \qquad f=\zeta_0+(1-P)\kappa_1.
\end{equation}

The free inverse is uniformly bounded,
$\|\mathcal K(m)^{-1}\|\le C_{\mathcal K}$ for $m\ge0$.
Indeed $\mathcal K(0)$ is accretive and its inverse is bounded by
the free symbol calculation in \cite[\S8]{QCDM1}; multiplication by
$(1+m\mathcal K(0)^{-1})^{-1}$ does not increase this bound.
For $u=\mathcal K(m)^{-1}f$ we have
\[
 h^{-1}\sum_j\frac{\varrho_j}{2}|\nabla_ju|^2
       +\theta_k|Ru|^2+m|u|^2
       =\operatorname{Re}\langle u,f\rangle.
\]
We also need the stronger estimate for the first term alone:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcd2-uv-energy}
 h^{-1}\sum_j\frac{\varrho_j}{2}|\nabla_ju|^2
       \le C_{\rm en}h|f|^2,
 \qquad C_{\rm en}=c_{\rm re}^{-1}(1+b_FC_{\mathcal K})^2.
\end{equation}
To see this, write
$u=(D+m)^{-1}(1-\theta_kP\mathcal K(m)^{-1})f$.
The second factor has norm at most $1+b_FC_{\mathcal K}$, while
$(D+m)^{-1}=D^{-1}(1+mD^{-1})^{-1}$ and the last factor is a
contraction.  The identity
$\operatorname{Re}D^{-1}\le h c_{\rm re}^{-1}$ now gives
\eqref{eq:qcd2-uv-energy}.

The resolvent identity is
\[
 \zeta(m)-\zeta_0=-m\mathcal K(m)^{-1}f.
\]
The first square of $\Phi_k^{\rm nat}$ is consequently at most
$C(L^{-2n}+m^2L^{-n})$ in expectation, and the second is at most
$CmL^{-n}$.  In the third square, the correction to the ultraviolet
vector has expected energy at most
$C(hL^{-2n}+hm^2L^{-n})$, by
\eqref{eq:qcd2-uv-energy}.  For a nonnegative quadratic form $q$,
\[
 |q(v+w)-q(v)|\le q(w)+2\sqrt{q(v)q(w)}.
\]
Applying this inequality and Cauchy--Schwarz to the Gaussian mean
bounds the change in the third square by
$C(h^{1/2}L^{-n}+mh^{1/2}L^{-n/2})$ together with smaller terms.
Since $h^{1/2}L^{-n/2}=L^{-n}L^{-i_0/2}\le L^{-n}$, these bounds
prove the first assertion in (b); its second assertion follows from
(a).

For two masses use instead
\[
 \zeta(m)-\zeta(m')
       =-(m-m')\mathcal K(m)^{-1}f',\qquad
 f'=f-m'\mathcal K(m')^{-1}f.
\]
Equation~\eqref{eq:qcd2-uv-f-bound} bounds the mean square of $f'$
by $CL^{-n}$.  The energy identities, the displayed quadratic-form
inequality, and the Lipschitz dependence of the coefficients
$\theta_k+m$ and $m$ give
$C|m-m'|(L^{-n}+h^{1/2}L^{-n/2})\le2C|m-m'|L^{-n}$.
This proves the first assertion of (c).  Compare each of the two
partial sums with $F^{\rm UV}_{<i_0}$ for the second.  Taking
differences at $i_0=i$ and $i_0=i+1$ then gives its three slice bounds.

It remains to prove the limit at fixed depth; this requires a
quantitative comparison of the free symbols.  The first square at
zero mass has integrand
\[
 3\theta_k^{-1}
       \operatorname{Tr}(D_ky^*B'_hyD_k^*),
 \qquad y=\widehat K^{-1/2}\widehat V^*X^*.
\]
Here $B'_h$ is the direct sum of the brackets in the proof of
\cref{C-398-39}.  At fixed $n$ its classes $\xi'$ are fixed.  In one
class the average symbol is
\[
 v'_q=\prod_\nu
       \frac{\sin(L^{-n}q_\nu/2)}{L^{i_0}\sin(hq_\nu/2)}.
\]
The vectors defining $\Pi'$ and $w'$ are obtained from
$v'_q/(\widehat q_\mu\sqrt{k_q})$ and
$v'_q\widehat q_\mu/\sqrt{k_q}$ by normalization.  Their limits
replace $\widehat q$ by $q$, $k_q$ by $|q|^2$, and the average
symbol by the corresponding sinc product.  Ratios of finite-mesh
and limiting entries are uniformly bounded and differ from $1$ by
at most $C\min(1,h|q|)$; missing fine modes are assigned value zero.

Write $q=\xi'+2\pi L^n l$ and
$u(0)=1$, $u(l)=(2|l|-1)^{-1}$ for $l\ne0$.  The explicit average
symbol gives
\[
 |v'_q|\le\prod_\nu u(l_\nu),\qquad
 h|q|\le\sqrt3\pi L^{-i_0}(2|l|_\infty+1).
\]
The normalized constraint vectors have squares bounded by
$C|v'_q|^2$.  The inequalities
$\min(1,s)^2\le s^{1/2}$ and
\[
 \sum_{l\in\mathbb Z^3}(2|l|_\infty+1)^{1/2}
                         \prod_\nu u(l_\nu)^2<\infty
\]
therefore bound their squared difference from the limiting vectors
by $CL^{-i_0/2}$.  The normalization factors have the same relative
bound: their zero modes dominate their sums up to fixed constants.
Since $|\Pi'w'|^2\ge\Upsilon_0$, this proves
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcd2-uv-bracket-limit}
 \|B'_h-B'_0\|\le CL^{-i_0/4},
\end{equation}
uniformly in $n$ and in the classes.

We spell out the other symbol errors as well.  With
$\widehat\Pi_0$ the light-space projection, the chamber symbols obey
\begin{align*}
 |\iota_0^*g_q\iota_0-g_q^0|
      &\le C\min(1,h|q|)/|q|,\\
 \|(1-\widehat\Pi_0)g_q\|&\le Ch,\\
 |v_q(h)-v_q(0)|&\le C\min(1,h|q|)|v_q(0)|,\\
 |\widehat q-q|&\le C\min(1,h|q|)|q|,\qquad
 |\theta_k-\theta_\infty|\le2b_FL^{-k}.
\end{align*}
The first two follow from the light/heavy block inversion of the
free chamber symbol; the remaining formulas follow from the centered
averages and lattice differences.  The vertex is a trigonometric
polynomial, so it differs from its zero-mesh value by
$C\min(1,h|q|)$; its heavy components are multiplied by a row of
$g_q$ bounded by $Ch$.  These are the same free symbol identities
used to prove the uniform mass bound in \cite[\S8]{QCDM1}.
All sums defining $y$ and $D_k$ can now be compared term by term,
including the modes present only in the limiting sum.  Their
majorant is
\[
 |y_q|^2\le Cv_q^2|q|^{-2}k_q^{-1}.
\]
Using $\min(1,h|q|)\le(h|q|)^{1/4}$ and Cauchy--Schwarz, their
change in the trace is at most
\[
 Ch^{1/4}\|D_k\|^2
       \sum_q(1+|q|^{1/2})|y_q|^2
       \le Ch^{1/4}(|\xi|^{-2}+1).
\]
For the zero mode this follows from
$|y_0|^2\le C|\xi|^{-4}$ and $\|D_k\|\le C|\xi|$; the other
modes have $|q|\ge\pi$ and sum to a bounded function.  The same
majorant bounds $\|D_k\|^2\|y\|^2$.  Combining it with
\eqref{eq:qcd2-uv-bracket-limit} proves convergence of the first
square with error $CL^{-i_0/4}$.  Its limit is nonnegative and at
most $C_1L^{-2n}$ by the earlier gap estimate.

The second square vanishes at zero mass.  The third differs from
$F^{\rm UV}_{<i_0}$ by $CL^{-k/2-n}$.  Part (a) now identifies
the limit as $F^{\rm UV}+F^{\rm GW,[n]}$ and proves the asserted
rate at zero mass.  Part (c) adds $CmL^{-n}$.  For each $k$ the
partial sums decrease with $n$, so the limits do too.  The bound
$F^{\rm GW,[n]}\le CL^{-2n}$ identifies their decreasing limit
as $F^{\rm UV}$ and proves the assertions concerning
$\bar\sigma_d$.  Applying the rate to two successive cutoffs at
equal depth, then subtracting two adjacent partial sums, proves the
last two estimates in (d).  The case $i_0=0$ follows by increasing
$B_5$ to cover the bounded empty-sum cases.

Finally,
\[
 \frac{L^{k-i}}{x_i}-\frac1{\tau t_k}
       =\frac{\tau t_i-x_i}{\tau x_i t_k}.
\]
Multiply by the nonnegative $\sigma_i(k;\mathfrak m_k)$ and sum.
For $i<i_0$, $t_i\ge L^{n+1}t_k$, so the additional hypotheses
in (e) bound the resulting error by
$\bar B F(k;\mathfrak m_k)L^{-(n+1)}/(\varpi|\tau|t_k^2)$.
Part (b) proves the final estimate.  A single maximum of the constants
in these arguments gives $B_5$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Restarting the flow}

We compare the original flow with a flow that starts later and carries
only a prescribed mass correction from the discarded scales.  The
background field and the fermion block operator at the starting level
are retained.  All activities and scalar normalizers generated before
that level are discarded.  The construction below checks that this
modified initial density satisfies the hypotheses needed for each
subsequent step.

\begin{definition}[Restart and mass mismatch]\label{C-419-2}
Fix the datum $(g,\ell,K,\mathsf b,\mathsf m)$ of the construction,
and keep its calibrations and fine masses fixed:
\[
 \mathsf t_k=L^{K-k}\mathsf b,
 \qquad \mathfrak m_k=L^{k-K}\mathsf m.
\]
Choose integers $1\le u<s<K$, and set
\[
 t_0=K-s,\quad t_1=K-u,\quad
 \Lambda_k=L^{-(k-t_0)/2},\quad
 \varepsilon_s=(L^s\mathsf b)^{-1/2}
                         (1+\log(L^s\mathsf b))^{9\mathfrak p_0}.
\]
For $k\ge t_0$ we have
$\phi(\mathsf t_k)\Lambda_k\le\varepsilon_s$ and
$\phi_\sharp(\mathsf t_k)\Lambda_k\le\varepsilon_s$.

A label is $c\in\mathbb C$ with $|c|<8\varrho$.  The ordinary
flow at this label has bare coupling $L^K(\mathsf b-c)$ and
coefficients $x_k(c),s_k(c)$.  The calibrations remain
$\mathsf t_k$.  In particular,
\[
 |x_i(c)-x_i|\le\tfrac23r_xx_i,
 \qquad |x_i(c)-(x_i-L^{K-i}c)|\le4C_w\phi(x_i).
\]

For $|\zeta|\le2B_F+1$, define the restarted density at level $t_0$
by
\begin{align*}
 \hat\tau^{\rm F}_{t_0}(dV)
  ={}&\mathsf{Stay}(V)
       \exp\bigl[-A(L^{t_0}\hat x_{t_0},\mathsf U)
       -\langle\bar\Psi,\mathbb D_{t_0}(\mathsf U)\Psi\rangle
       -L^{-t_0}\hat s_{t_0}\mathsf S_1(\psi^{\rm bg})\bigr]
       \mathscr M^{\rm fr}_{h_\emptyset}(dV),\\
 \hat x_{t_0}={}&L^s(\mathsf b-c),\qquad
 \hat s_{t_0}=\frac{\zeta}{L^s(\mathsf b-c)},\qquad
 \hat E_{t_0}=0.
\end{align*}
The density test $\mathsf{Stay}=\chi_{t_0}(T_\ell)$, background
$\mathsf U=\mathsf U_{t_0}(V)$, fermion tower $\mathbb D_{t_0}$,
and reference measure are those of the original datum.  There is no
activity of any degree at a level $j\le t_0$, and no scalar
normalizer $\mathbf N^{{\rm un},(j)}$, $\mathbf N^{{\rm F},(j)}$,
$\mathbf G^{(j)}$, or $\mathbf c_j$ at these levels.

At later levels apply the usual small-field step and extract its own
local parts:
\[
 \hat x_{k+1}=L^{-1}\hat x_k-\hat b_{k+1},\qquad
 \hat s_{k+1}=L\hat s_k+\hat\mu_{k+1},\qquad
 \hat E_{k+1}=\hat E_k+\hat e_{k+1}n_{k+1}.
\]
The same local formulas define the activities on $\mathbb Z^3$ and
on every admitted torus.  The extracted numbers are read from the
infinite-lattice family and are used on all these tori.  Let
$\hat x_k^\circ$ be the real restarted sequence with label zero and
start $\operatorname{Re}\zeta$.  Set
\[
 \hat y_i=0\quad(i<t_0),\qquad
 \hat y_i=1/\hat x_i\quad(i\ge t_0),\qquad
 \zeta'=\frac{\mathsf b\zeta}{\mathsf b-c},\qquad
 \pi=\zeta'-\mathsf t_{t_1}G_{<t_0,t_1}(x(c)).
\]
The one-loop expressions in $\hat y$ mean their linear extensions
from the reciprocal couplings.  Define
$\hat\rho_j=\hat\mu_j-\mu_j^{\rm1L}(\hat y)$.

For corresponding quantities in the ordinary and restarted flows put
$\delta X=X-\hat X$.  Earlier restarted activities are zero, so
$\delta E^{(j)}=E^{(j)}$ for $j\le t_0$.  Their complete scalar parts
satisfy
\[
 \sup_{X,z}e^{(\kappa+1)d_j(X)}
             \sup|E_0^{(j)}(X;\cdot;z)|\le E_0.
\]
For $j>t_0$ the normalizers depending only on the calibration and
fine mass cancel, and
$\delta E_0^{(j)}=\delta F_0^{(j)}+\delta\mathbf G^{(j)}$.
At the trivial pair on $\mathbb Z^3$ use the second-order
decompositions $E_{\ge2}^{(j)}=T^{(j)}+R^{(j)}$ and their restarted
counterparts; both restarted terms are zero for $j\le t_0$.
\end{definition}

We first isolate the linear operation used to compare activities.
The RG step itself is nonlinear.  Reading previously formed
activities into its potential is linear, provided their cells, paths
and hulls have been fixed by the same rules.

\begin{proposition}[Linear reading of old activities]\label{C-419-3}
Let $0\le k<K$.  Use the matrix-mass ball, pair cores and formal-leg norms of
\cite[\S\S5,7,10]{QCDM1}.  The pair radius is $a=\alpha_0$ at
zero sources and $a_k^{\rm rad}\le a\le\alpha_0$ at sources.
Let $G^{(j)}=G_0^{(j)}+G_{\ge2}^{(j)}$, $1\le j\le k$, satisfy the
following conditions.

The scalar terms are local, holomorphic, strictly gauge invariant,
and have finite array norm
\[
 \|G_0^{(j)}\|_{j,\kappa}
       =\sup_{X,z}e^{\kappa d_j(X)}\sup|G_0^{(j)}(X;\cdot;z)|.
\]
Each term of $G_{\ge2}^{(j)}$ is even, has degree at least two,
is holomorphic on the whole pair core, and is jointly gauge
invariant.  Its cell units have the first-moment bound used in the
old-activity lemma, with bound
$\varepsilon_f(G^{(j)})\ge\|G_{\ge2}^{(j)}\|_{j;a}$ for the sum
of their norms.  The two auxiliary families $F_1$ and $G^\flat$
used to form moved diagonal terms also have norms at most
$\varepsilon_f(G^{(j)})$.  Any moved diagonal terms are formed from the same
fixed row and column sums as in the source construction, and obey
its cell-unit condition at lags at least $n_{\rm lag}$.

At zero sources it suffices that each term is invariant under the
common flavour phase $V_1=V_2=e^{i\alpha}1$.  Then the cell units
are the polymers, no diagonal terms are moved, and
$\varepsilon_f(G^{(j)})$ may be its own activity norm.  On a torus
use a pair $(G^{(j),\rm tor},G^{(j),\infty})$: on polymers which do
not wrap, the first is the part of the second that fits in the torus,
with the same cells and pointers.  The second is covariant under
the torus periods, with the fermionic seam sign.  The norm bounds
both families and $m_c$ denotes the infinite-lattice cell sum.

At sources use the triple consisting of the torus family at the
source, its value at zero source, and the corresponding zero-source
family on $\mathbb Z^3$.  The last two form a pair as above.  File
the terms of $m_c-m_c(0)$ at the hulls of their source-dependent
summands, and use their weighted norm $\|\cdot\|_\natural$.
The number $\varepsilon_f$ bounds the sums of the norms of all
families in this triple.

Let $\mathcal V_k[G]$ be the sum of the old scalar localization and
the old terms with legs in the step potential.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item The maps $G\mapsto\mathcal V_k[G](Y)$ are complex linear.
They commute with absolutely convergent sums, Taylor coefficients
and Schwarz quotients.  Each localized term is holomorphic, jointly
gauge invariant, and vanishes at $(B,\bar W,W)=0$.  It depends on
the fields in its polymer alone.  It depends on the source there
alone as well, except for a cell term filed whole, which also reads
the source through its cell sum.  Filing its summands at their hulls
removes this exception.
\item Put
\[
 \omega_n=C_\omega L^{n/4},\qquad
 c_\psi^{(a)}=c_\psi+
    \mathsf C_{\mathcal A}\frac{\alpha_0}{a}
            \frac{c_h\delta(\mathsf t_k)}{a_{\rm an}}
    +C_G\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}\delta(\mathsf t_k).
\]
Then $c_\psi^{(\alpha_0)}\le c'_\psi$ and
$c_\psi^{(a)}\le9c'_\psi/8$ on the source radii, and
\begin{align*}
 \|\mathcal V_{\ge2}^{\rm old}[G]\|
 &\le c_\psi^{(a)}\sum_{j\le k}
 \left[\omega_{k+1-j}\varepsilon_f(G^{(j)})
 +1_{\{k-j\ge n_{\rm lag}\}}
             C_\omega L^{k-j}h_F^2\sup_c\|m_c(G^{(j)})\|\right],\\
 |\mathcal V_0^{\rm old}[G](Y)|
 &\le K_\Lambda\frac{\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}\delta(\mathsf t_k)}a
       \sum_{j\le k}L^{-(k-j)}\|G_0^{(j)}\|_{j,\kappa}
       e^{-(1-2\delta_{\rm w})\kappa d_k(Y)}.
\end{align*}
At sources replace the cell term inside the first sum by
\[
 L^{k-j}h_F^2\left[
 C_\omega\sup_c\|m_c^\infty(0)\|
       +C_{\rm hl}\sup_c\|m_c-m_c(0)\|_\natural\right].
\]
The zero-source torus discrepancy $m_c(0)-m_c^\infty(0)$ is
included in the first term of the bound.  Thus all cell terms vanish
from the bound when the infinite-lattice quadratic cell sums vanish
and there is no source discrepancy.
\item Suppose a segment of potentials
$\mathcal V^\vartheta=\mathcal V+\vartheta\delta\mathcal V$ satisfies
$\|\mathcal V_0^\vartheta\|\le c_{\rm cl}/2$ and
$\|\mathcal V_\psi^\vartheta\|\le c_{\rm cl}/20$ for
$0\le\vartheta\le1$.  Before extraction of local parts,
\begin{align*}
 \|\delta\widetilde E_{\ge2}(X)\|
 &\le K'_M\left[
 \frac{50}{9}\|\delta\mathcal V_\psi\|
 +40\frac{\sup_\vartheta\|\mathcal V_\psi^\vartheta\|}{c_{\rm cl}}
                         \|\delta\mathcal V_0\|\right]
                         e^{-\kappa_+d_{k+1}(X)},\\
 |\delta\widetilde E_0(X)|
 &\le\frac{50}{9}K'_M
           (\|\delta\mathcal V_0\|+\|\delta\mathcal V_\psi\|)
                         e^{-\kappa_+d_{k+1}(X)}.
\end{align*}
In the activity norm replace $K'_M$ by $K_M=C_EK'_M$.
The same bounds hold for the first variation and, pointer by pointer,
for the pointed terms, except for pointers on bonds of the scalar
system.  Those terms do not change if $\delta\mathcal V_0=0$.
If $\delta\mathcal V_0$ changes only the fourth family of that
system, and its admission bounds obey
$\mathsf n'\le w_*/2$ and
$\mathsf n^{\rm int}+\mathsf n'\le w_*$ at both endpoints, the
scalar pointed bound holds with $K'_M+K^{\rm v}_{\mathbf M}$ in
place of $K'_M$, and $K_M^\bullet=K_M+C_EK^{\rm v}_{\mathbf M}$
in the activity norm.
\item At the trivial pair on $\mathbb Z^3$, let $P_j$ be totals
represented by even local families $F^{(j)}$ with no scalar part,
covariant under cube translations, and with quadratic cell sums zero.
The coefficient linear in the old-family parameter has total
\[
 \left(\mathcal J_k\Bigl[\sum_{j\le k}P_j\Bigr]
       -\sum_{j\le k}P_j\circ(\mathsf H_k,\bar{\mathsf H}_k)
       \right)_{\ge2},
\]
and a representative of norm at most
$K_Mc_\psi\sum_{j\le k}C_7L^{(k+1-j)/4}\|F^{(j)}\|_j$.
It depends linearly on the totals $P_j$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Fix the polymer, the cell at which it is filed, and a local or walk
term in each of its legs.  The reading construction first transports
the legs to the cell centre along fixed paths.  It then subtracts the
value at the trivial pair, splits each leg into its value at the
centre plus its difference from that value, and forms row sums,
column sums and the cell sum of the quadratic kernel.  Each operation
is linear in the kernel.  The trees and paths depend on the polymer
and walks; the maps used along them depend on the pair, but none
depends on the family being read.  Moving diagonal terms uses fixed
linear combinations of the same kernel sums.  Finally localization
uses the walk expansion and finite differences in the shift
parameters, again linearly.  Scalar localization is linear in its
array for the same reason.  This proves linearity at each filed term.

At zero source the common flavour phase eliminates the $\Psi\Psi$
and $\bar\Psi\bar\Psi$ quadratic terms.  The remaining kernel has
the form $\bar\Psi\,g_X\Psi$.  Exponential decay of the background
maps bounds its weighted trace norm by
$C h_F^{-2}\|G^{(j)}(X)\|$.  The first moments about the cell centre
are paid by these exponential weights and by the polymer diameter.
This proves the cell-unit bound with the family's own norm.  At
sources the same calculation applies to each summand of the units
and moved pieces, and the norms add.  Phase invariance and the
core properties are closed linear conditions; they therefore pass
to sums, Taylor coefficients and Schwarz quotients.  Absolute
convergence permits the reading maps to commute with these operations.

On a torus the fitting relation and the filing of wrapping terms
are also linear.  At sources split the cell sum into
\[
 m_c=m_c^\infty(0)
       +(m_c(0)-m_c^\infty(0))+(m_c-m_c(0)).
\]
The first term is filed as on $\mathbb Z^3$, the second piece by
piece on wrapping polymers, and the third at the source hulls.  This
gives the pair and triple versions without changing the argument.
Localization preserves the stated holomorphy and invariance.  A term
vanishes at zero fluctuation because it contains either a fluctuation
leg, a walk vertex that vanishes there, or a difference of two
evaluations which agree there.  These observations also prove the
assertions about local dependence.

For the bounds, at lags below $n_{\rm lag}$ read the family without
expanding its cell sums.  At larger lags the old-activity estimate
gives $\omega_{k+1-j}\varepsilon_f$ and
$C_\omega L^{k-j}h_F^2\|m_c\|$.  The field substitution contributes
$c_\psi$ for terms containing a fluctuation leg, the shift contributes
$\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}(\alpha_0/a)c_h\delta/a_{\rm an}$, and
the walk vertices contribute $C_G\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}\delta$.
A cell sum is formed at the trivial pair and depends on the
fluctuation only through its two legs, so it incurs no additional
shift derivative.  The wrapping discrepancy is exponentially small
in the torus diameter and is included in $C_\omega\varepsilon_f$.
For source-dependent cells the hull count costs $C_{\rm hl}$ times
their weighted norm.  The scalar bracket localization costs
$K_\Lambda\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}\delta/a$ and
$L^{-(k-j)}$ per old level.  This proves (b), with exactly the radii
and constants used in the old-activity and source estimates of
\cite[\S\S7,10]{QCDM1}.

For (c), the polymer expansion is holomorphic on
$\|\mathcal V\|<c_{\rm cl}$ and is bounded there, including the test tail, by
\[ (5/2)K'_Mc_{\rm cl}e^{-\kappa_+d(X)}. \]
Every point of the segment has norm at most $11c_{\rm cl}/20$.
Cauchy's estimate on the remaining radius $9c_{\rm cl}/20$ gives
the coefficient $50/9$.  The part with legs vanishes when
$\mathcal V_\psi=0$.  Schwarz's lemma in a leg ball of radius
$c_{\rm cl}/4$, followed by Cauchy's estimate in a scalar ball of
the same radius, bounds its scalar derivative by
\[
 40K'_M\frac{\|\mathcal V_\psi\|}{c_{\rm cl}}
                         e^{-\kappa_+d(X)}.
\]
Change the leg part and then the scalar part and integrate these
derivative bounds.  Summing polymers costs $C_E$.  The pointed
expansion gives the same estimates term by term.  For scalar bond
pointers divide the segment into two halves.  Convexity preserves
the admission bounds, and the change of the fourth family on each
half is at most $w_*/2$.  The scalar-system Lipschitz estimate gives
the additional $K^{\rm v}_{\mathbf M}$, proving the exception stated
in (c).

At the trivial pair the coefficient linear in the old families is
the first variation of the expansion at zero potential.  Its Berezin
integral is the difference between integrating the old total and
evaluating that total at the background fermions.  This is the
displayed expression in (d).  The zero cell sums remove its relevant
quadratic term; the old-family bound gives its stated norm.
Representatives within any positive error of the total norm may be
used, after which that error tends to zero.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Existence of the restarted flow]\label{C-419-4}
For every label $c$ and every $|\zeta|\le2B_F+1$ the restarted
small-field flow is defined through level $K$, simultaneously on
$\mathbb Z^3$ and on all admitted tori.  It has the same form and
closed activity bounds as the original construction, with constants
$C_w,C_2,C_T,C_3$.  These bounds hold for both torus families and
at every pointer.  The density at each level is bounded and Borel.
The extracted numbers do not depend on the side; on polymers which
do not wrap, the torus family is the fitting part of the
infinite-lattice family, with the same pointers.

Its explicit and remainder terms satisfy
\[
 \hat T^{(j)}=T^{(j)}(\hat y),\qquad
 \|\hat R^{(j)}\|_j\le C_3\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^3,
 \qquad |\hat\rho_j|\le C'_\rho\phi_\sharp(\mathsf t_{j-1})^3,
\]
and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:qcd2-restart-mass}
 \mathsf t_k\hat s_k
   =\zeta'+\sum_{t_0\le i<k}
           \frac{\mathsf t_i}{\hat x_i}\sigma_i(k;\mathfrak m_k)
           +\sum_{t_0<j\le k}\mathsf t_j\hat\rho_j,
 \qquad
 \left|\sum_{t_0<j\le k}\mathsf t_j\hat\rho_j\right|\le\tfrac12.
\end{equation}
The coefficient windows are
\begin{align*}
 |\hat x_k(0)-\mathsf t_k|
     &\le(1-L^{-(k-t_0)})\bar B,\\
 |\hat x_k(c)-\hat x_k^\circ|
     &\le\tfrac5{12}r_x\hat x_k^\circ,\qquad
 |\hat s_k(c)|\le2\bar B_M/\mathsf t_k.
\end{align*}
If $\zeta\in[0,B_F]$ is real and $c=0$, then
\[
 \zeta-\tfrac12\le\mathsf t_k\hat s_k
       \le\zeta+2B_F+\tfrac12,
 \qquad |\hat s_k|\le\bar B_M/\mathsf t_k.
\]
Every subsequent step obeys the original one-step estimates on the
full coefficient polydiscs about $\hat x_k^\circ$.  The outputs are
holomorphic in $c$ and are real when $c$ and $\zeta$ are real.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
We run the induction simultaneously in the label, the start and the
torus side.  This is necessary because the extracted numbers come
from the infinite lattice and the symmetry argument compares all
torus sizes.

At level $t_0$ all activity bounds and fitting relations are empty.
The density test restricts $V$ to an open set of small plaquette
configurations.  Locally on this set the minimizing background has
a continuous representative.  Two representatives differ by a
residual gauge transformation equal to the identity at the level-
$t_0$ sites.  The action, the tower form and the background mass form
take the same values on this orbit: the action is gauge invariant,
and the other two forms are gauge covariant with their boundary
arguments fixed.  Their values are therefore continuous functions
of $V$ on the tested set.  The regular-background inverse estimates
give $\operatorname{Re}\Gamma_{t_0-1}\ge C_D^{-1}$, bounded
background maps and a bounded tower
$\mathbb D_{t_0}=\theta-\theta^2q\Gamma_{t_0-1}^{-1}q^*$.
The Grassmann exponential has finitely many coefficients on a torus,
each bounded because
\[
 |e^{-L^K(\mathsf b-c)A(1,\mathsf U)}|\le1
 \quad\text{and}\quad \operatorname{Re}(\mathsf b-c)>0.
\]
Multiplication by the density-test indicator thus gives a bounded
Borel density.  Flavour transformations, charge conjugation,
complex conjugation and lattice isometries carry these three forms
and the background orbit jointly with their data.  This proves the
covariance required at the initial level, including the tested
configuration pairs used by the step.

We make explicit the parts of the original induction that use its
initial level.  They remain valid with $t_0$ as the initial level:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item Covariance on the tested pairs follows from the covariance of
the initial density and from covariance of the integration kernels.
It extends to complex coefficient polydiscs by holomorphy.
\item The linear symmetry spaces for the activity families are
preserved by the step.  Their initial elements are zero, on
$\mathbb Z^3$ and on every torus; the norm bounds are uniform in
the side.
\item Partial charge conjugation and the conjugation operation
$\sharp$ preserve the activity totals and the real local
coefficients.  Their initial hypotheses are empty, and the initial
action and mass coefficients are real for real $c,\zeta$.
This gives reality at each later level.
\item Nonwrapping torus terms agree with the terms that fit from
$\mathbb Z^3$.  This holds at the empty initial family and is
preserved term by term by localization and the polymer expansion.
\item On the full polydisc
$|x'_i-\hat x_i^\circ|\le r_x\hat x_i^\circ$,
$|s'_i|\le A\phi(\hat x_i^\circ)$, the invariant activity balls are
preserved.  The one-step potential stays below $c_{\rm cl}/2$ at
the real fine mass; this argument uses only the earlier families in
their balls and the coefficient windows, not the original bare
action.
\item There is a common open complex neighbourhood of the fine
mass on which these flows are jointly holomorphic and the potential
is below $3c_{\rm cl}/4$.  At the initial level a change of size
$\varrho_*$ in level-$t_0$ units has size at most $\varrho_*/L$ at
level $t_0-1$.  It lies in the actual mass ball of the regular
background inverse estimate, where
$\operatorname{Re}\Gamma_{t_0-1}\ge(2C_D)^{-1}$ and the background
kernel constants may be doubled.  In particular
$\|\mathbb D_{t_0}\|\le\theta+2\theta^2C_D$ there at real
configurations.  The local estimates are jointly holomorphic in
configuration and fine mass on this ball.  At later levels uniform
Lipschitz bounds on the region with potential below
$3c_{\rm cl}/4$, applied about the real-mass region below
$c_{\rm cl}/2$, give a neighbourhood independent of the side.
No inverse estimate is continued beyond its mass domain.
\item Translation covariance on a torus holds polymer by polymer
and pointer by pointer, including wrapping terms.  It is empty at
level $t_0$, and the fixed shift, path and localization rules commute
with translations by $M\mathbb Z^3$ in the units of each level.
Here $t_0\ge1$ ensures that every restarted step uses these rules.
\end{enumerate}
These seven inductions justify application of the original local
step to the changed initial density.  The step gives a bounded
Borel image density and the stated local form.  They also justify
using its full complex coefficient domains, rather than merely the
real trajectory.

The closed second-order and cubic-remainder induction is unchanged
once its initial mass lies in the sharp window.  At the initial
level,
\[
 |\hat s_{t_0}(c)|
 \le\frac{64}{63}\frac{2B_F+1}{\mathsf t_{t_0}}
 \le\frac{2\bar B_M}{\mathsf t_{t_0}},
\]
since $|c|/\mathsf b<1/64$ and $\bar B_M=3B_F+1$.
The four-variable expansion therefore retains the mass parameter
at weight two, with inverse radius
\[
 r_4^{-1}
   \le\frac{2c'_\psi c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2\bar B_M}
              {c_\diamond\mathsf t_k}
   \le C_r\phi(\mathsf t_k)^2.
\]
Its square has weight four and is included in the cubic remainder.

To identify the explicit part, observe that the second-order
creation at level $j$ is linear in $y_{j-1}=1/x_{j-1}$; Gaussian
