integration, reading at the next level and mass extraction are all
linear.  Thus $T^{(j)}$, $\mu_j^{(2)}$ and the one-loop sum rule are
linear identities in $y$.  They hold on the reciprocal image of a
coupling box with nonempty interior, so they hold for every complex
$y$.  With $\hat y_i=0$ for $i<t_0$ their recursion is exactly the
restarted recursion.  This proves $\hat T^{(j)}=T^{(j)}(\hat y)$.

The bound for these explicit terms can also be checked directly.
Their quadratic zeroth moments vanish after mass extraction and
remain zero at later levels.  The new second-order creation is
bounded by $4C_{\rm sl}C_V^2h_F^4/\mathsf t_k$, since
$|\hat x_k(c)|\ge11\mathsf t_k/24$.  By
\cref{C-419-3}(d), the contribution from earlier explicit terms is
at most
\[
 K_Mc_\psi C_7C_T\frac{h_F^4}{\mathsf t_k}
       \sum_{t_0<j\le k}L^{-3(k+1-j)/4}
 \le K_Mc_\psi C_7S_2^\sharp C_T
                         \frac{h_F^4}{\mathsf t_k}.
\]
Mass extraction costs $K_\mu$.  The choices
$C_T=8K_\mu C_{\rm sl}C_V^2$ and
$K_\mu K_Mc_\psi C_7S_2^\sharp\le1/4$ leave a total at most
$3C_Th_F^4/(4\mathsf t_k)$.  Thus a representative satisfying the
closed bound exists.  The same weighted expansion then gives
$\hat R^{(j)}$ and $\hat\rho_j$ with the asserted bounds.

The mass recursion telescopes:
\[
 \hat s_k=L^{k-t_0}\hat s_{t_0}
      +\sum_{t_0<j\le k}L^{k-j}
        \bigl(G_j(\hat y)-LG_{j-1}(\hat y)+\hat\rho_j\bigr).
\]
Since $G_{t_0}(\hat y)=0$ and
$\mathsf t_kL^{k-i}=\mathsf t_i$, this is
\eqref{eq:qcd2-restart-mass}.  The summable cubic bound gives
$\mathsf t_k C'_\rho S_3^\sharp\phi_\sharp(\mathsf t_k)^3\le1/2$
for its remainder sum.

It remains to verify the windows used in this induction.  At label
zero, $|\hat b_j|\le B_\sharp$ gives
$|\hat x_k-\mathsf t_k|\le(1-L^{-(k-t_0)})\bar B$.
At a complex label compare with the real restart:
\[
 \hat x_k(c)-\hat x_k^\circ
 =-L^{K-k}c-\sum_{t_0<j\le k}L^{-(k-j)}
                         (\hat b_j(c)-\hat b_j^\circ).
\]
The calibration and fermion normalizers cancel from the last
difference.  Its remainder is bounded by
$2C_w\phi(\gamma^{-2})$, so the existing ceilings
$8\varrho\le r_x\mathsf b/8$ and
$26C_w\phi(\gamma^{-2})\gamma^2\le r_x$ give
\[
 |\hat x_k(c)-\hat x_k^\circ|
       \le(1/4+1/6)r_x\hat x_k^\circ.
\]
In particular $|\hat x_k(c)|\ge11\mathsf t_k/24$.
Nonnegativity of the slice coefficients and
$\sum_i\sigma_i\le B_F$ in \eqref{eq:qcd2-restart-mass} give the
claimed real mass interval.  In general they give
\[
 \mathsf t_k|\hat s_k(c)|
  \le\tfrac{64}{63}(2B_F+1)+\tfrac{24}{11}B_F+\tfrac12
  \le6B_F+2=2\bar B_M.
\]
These estimates close the windows at the next level.  They put the
entire flow inside the coefficient polydiscs with $A=5B_s$.
Composition of the holomorphic step maps proves holomorphy in $c$;
the third induction above proves reality.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Loss of memory of the earlier activities}

The earlier mass is relevant and must be retained in the restart.
The other earlier terms are small after sufficiently many further
steps.  We prove this by following the mass, coupling, scalar
activities and activities with legs together.  The cubic remainder
must be compared separately: estimating each of its two values
would lose the decay with the distance from the restart.

\begin{lemma}[Comparison of the cubic remainders]\label{C-419-5}
For $t_0\le k<K$ let $\widetilde R^{(k+1)}$ and
$\widehat{\widetilde R}^{(k+1)}$ be the remainder totals before
mass extraction, at the trivial pair on $\mathbb Z^3$.  Put
\[
 q_k^{\rm old}=
 \frac{\sum_{j\le k}L^{(k+1-j)/4}\|\delta E_{\ge2}^{(j)}\|_j}
      {\sum_{j\le k}L^{(k+1-j)/4}C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2},
 \qquad
 q_k^0=\frac{K_\Lambda\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}}
                 {\alpha_0K_0^\sharp}
             \sum_{j\le k}L^{-(k-j)}\|\delta E_0^{(j)}\|_{j,\kappa}.
\]
Then
\begin{align*}
 \|\widetilde R^{(k+1)}-\widehat{\widetilde R}^{(k+1)}\|_{k+1}
 \le{}&8C_\chi\phi(\mathsf t_k)^3
                      \frac{|\delta x_k|}{r_x\mathsf t_k}
       +K_Mc_\psi\sum_{j\le k}C_7L^{(k+1-j)/4}
                                      \|\delta R^{(j)}\|_j\\
 &+C_{\rm rem}\phi(\mathsf t_k)^3
       \left(q_k^{\rm old}+q_k^0
       +\frac{\mathsf t_k|\delta s_k|}{\bar B_M}
       +\frac{|\delta x_k|}{r_x\mathsf t_k}\right).
\end{align*}
One may take
\begin{align*}
 C_0^{\rm rem}
  &=\frac{27}{4}K_Mc_{\rm cl}C_r^3
               \sum_{w\ge3}(w+1)^2(3/4)^{w-3},\\
 C_1^{\rm rem}
  &=\frac92K_Mc_{\rm cl}C_r^2
               \sum_{N\ge1}(N+1)^3(3/4)^{N-1},\qquad
 C_{\rm rem}=4(C_0^{\rm rem}+C_1^{\rm rem}C_2).
\end{align*}
The difference has the linear symmetries required for mass
extraction, and
\[
 |\delta\rho_{k+1}|
 \le c_b^{-2}C_{am}^{\psi}h_F^{-2}
        \|\widetilde R^{(k+1)}-\widehat{\widetilde R}^{(k+1)}\|,
 \qquad
 \|\delta R^{(k+1)}\|
 \le K_\mu\|\widetilde R^{(k+1)}
                         -\widehat{\widetilde R}^{(k+1)}\|.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Use the four deformation variables of the second-order expansion,
with weights $(1,2,1,2)$.  Before extraction its remainder is the
sum of three terms:
\begin{align*}
 \widetilde R^{(k+1)}={}&
 \left(\sum_Xa_{(2,0,0,0)}(X)-\mathscr A_{k+1}\right)_{\ge2}\\
 &+\left(\mathcal J_k\Bigl[\sum_{j\le k}R^{(j)}\Bigr]
       -\sum_{j\le k}R^{(j)}\circ(\mathsf H_k,\bar{\mathsf H}_k)
       \right)_{\ge2}
       +\sum_{|v|_w\ge3}\left(\sum_Xa_v(X)\right)_{\ge2}.
\end{align*}
The first term depends only on the coupling of the current step.
It is holomorphic on the coupling disc and bounded on its inner
$2/3$ disc by $C_\chi\phi(\mathsf t_k)^3$, after the Gaussian test
tail is included.  The segment joining the two couplings stays
within $5r_xx^\circ/12$ of real centres in the coupling window.
It has a disc of radius at least $r_x\mathsf t_k/8$ inside those
inner discs.  Cauchy's estimate gives the first term in the asserted
bound.  For the second, $\delta R^{(j)}$ has zero quadratic cell
sum, so \cref{C-419-3}(d) gives the displayed old-remainder term.

For the third term compare the potentials on a common polydisc.
Write their differences as
$\Delta\mathcal V^{\rm old}_{\ge2}$,
$\Delta\mathcal V^{\rm old}_0$, and
$\Delta\mathcal V^s$.  By \cref{C-419-3},
\begin{align*}
 \|\Delta\mathcal V^{\rm old}_{\ge2}\|
 &\le c'_\psi\sum_{j\le k}C_7L^{(k+1-j)/4}
                                      \|\delta E_{\ge2}^{(j)}\|_j,\\
 \|\Delta\mathcal V^{\rm old}_0\|
 &\le K_\Lambda\frac{\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}\delta(\mathsf t_k)}{\alpha_0}
                    \sum_{j\le k}L^{-(k-j)}\|\delta E_0^{(j)}\|_{j,\kappa},\\
 \|\Delta\mathcal V^s\|&\le c'_\psi c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2|\delta s_k|.
\end{align*}
The first and third bounds also hold with the fluctuation replaced
by $z_1B$ for $|z_1|\le r_1$.  Indeed the physical fluctuation is
then at most
$r_1\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}\delta\le
\min(c_\diamond/(C_Vh_F^2),\beta_0/2)$.
The shift is at most $a_{\rm an}/4$ and each walk link costs at most
$1/4$.  The shift and walk contributions remain linear in this
fluctuation size and their sum is included in $c'_\psi$.

Choose the ordinary radii $r_1,r_3$ and
\[
 r_2=\frac{c_\diamond}
 {c'_\psi\sum_{j\le k}C_7L^{(k+1-j)/4}C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2},
 \qquad
 r_4=\frac{c_\diamond\mathsf t_k}
                   {2c'_\psi c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2\bar B_M}.
\]
Interpolate independently in the three potential differences, with
radii $R_2,R_3,R_4$ equal to half the corresponding reference bound
divided by the norm of the difference.  A zero difference has
infinite radius.  The preceding estimates give
\[
 R_2^{-1}\le2q_k^{\rm old},\qquad
 R_3^{-1}\le2q_k^0,\qquad
 R_4^{-1}\le\mathsf t_k|\delta s_k|/\bar B_M.
\]
On $|z_1|<r_1$, $|z_i|<2r_i/3$ for $i=2,3,4$, and
$|\vartheta_i|<R_i$, each interpolated bracket is at most $3/2$
times its reference bound.  The polymer expansion is therefore
holomorphic and bounded by $2K_Mc_{\rm cl}$.  Its coefficient of
$z^v$ is bounded by
\[
 M_v=2K_Mc_{\rm cl}(3/2)^{v_2+v_3+v_4}r^{-v}.
\]
The same bound holds when any interpolation parameter is set to
either endpoint $0$ or $1$, since each endpoint is a valid flow.
Change the parameters one at a time.  If $R_i>1$, Schwarz's lemma
costs $2M_v/R_i$; if $R_i\le1$, the bound at the two endpoints
costs $2M_v\le2M_v/R_i$.  Changing the coupling last costs
$4M_v|\delta x_k|/(r_x\mathsf t_k)$ by Cauchy's estimate.

Put $\varepsilon=\phi(\mathsf t_k)$.  The radii satisfy
$r_1^{-1},r_3^{-1}\le C_r\varepsilon$,
$r_2^{-1}\le C_rC_2\varepsilon^2$ and
$r_4^{-1}\le C_r\varepsilon^2$.  If $v_2=0$, group coefficients
by their weight $w\ge3$; there are at most $(w+1)^2$ and their sum
is bounded by $C_0^{\rm rem}\varepsilon^3$.  If $v_2\ge1$, remove
one factor $r_2^{-1}$ and put
$N=v_1+v_2-1+v_3+v_4\ge1$.  There are at most $(N+1)^3$ terms.
The ceilings $C_r\varepsilon\le1/2$ and
$C_r^2C_2\varepsilon\le1$ bound their sum by
$C_1^{\rm rem}C_2\varepsilon^3$.  Combining these coefficient
sums with the three interpolation estimates proves the stated
$C_{\rm rem}$ bound.

Both remainder totals have the same linear symmetries.  The mass
functional is linear, with
$\delta\rho_{k+1}=-\eta_{k+1}^{-2}\mathsf{cf}_m
(\widetilde R^{(k+1)}-\widehat{\widetilde R}^{(k+1)})$.
The mass functional and subtraction bounds of the construction give
the last two estimates.
\end{proof}

The constants in the next result are fixed after the construction
constants, independently of $K,s,u$, and of the mass window chosen
after them.  We record their choices because the proof uses a floor
on $u$, rather than a further bound depending on $K$.

\begin{definition}[Constants for the comparison]\label{C-419-9}
Set
\begin{align*}
 S_{\rm fl}&=\sum_{m\ge0}L^{-m}(1+m\log L)^{\mathfrak p_0},&
 S_{\rm fl}^\sharp&=\sum_{m\ge0}L^{-m/2}(1+m\log L)^{3\mathfrak p_0},\\
 \Theta_L&=\sup_{v\ge0}(1+v)L^{-v/2}(1+v\log L)^{9\mathfrak p_0},&
 \bar\phi_v&=L^{-v/2}(1+v\log L)^{\mathfrak p_0},\\
 \bar\phi_v^\sharp&=L^{-v/2}(1+v\log L)^{3\mathfrak p_0},&
 \bar\phi_v^{(8)}&=L^{-v}(1+v\log L)^{8\mathfrak p_0}.
\end{align*}
For $L^v\ge e^{18\mathfrak p_0}$ these functions decrease to zero,
and bound the corresponding scale functions at every $\mathsf t\ge L^v$.
In the following displays the constants are defined in their order:
\begin{align*}
 C_{\mathbf G}&=9K_{\mathbf G}(2+\sigma_\star/(4r_x)),\\
 C_{\rm nm}&=5r_x^{-1}\bigl[
 2^{\mathfrak p_0+2}(C_w+5\theta_sh_F^2B_s)
       +2C_2+200\,4^{\mathfrak p_0}c_sh_F^2B_s^2\bigr],\\
 C_\psi^0&=C_Vh_F^2\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}A_1
       +2c'_\psi c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2\bar B_M
       +c'_\psi C_\omega S_\omega C_2,\\
 C_{\rm ld}&=40K_\mu K_MC_\psi^0/c_{\rm cl},\\
 C_{\rm dr}&=\frac L{L-1}K_\Lambda\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}A_1\alpha_0^{-1}
       \max\{\sqrt2(2+C_{am}r_\alpha^{-2})K_M^\bullet,C_{\rm ld}\},\\
 C_{\rm fc}&=C_{\rm nm}+C_{\rm dr},\qquad
 C_x^\delta=1+C_{am}r_\alpha^{-2},\qquad
 \beta_\star=\theta_EC_\omega S_\omega\le1/(4\sqrt2),\\
 B_\star&=\bigl(7B_5+6(\bar B+4C_w)B_F\bigr)L^{1/2},\\
 C_I&=2+B_\star+E_0L^{1/2}+C_{\mathbf G},\qquad
 A_{\rm LM}=\max\{C_2,C_w,2C_{\rm fc}C_I\},\\
 C_x&=C_x^\delta A_{\rm LM}S_{\rm fl},\\
 C_{\rm arr}&=\frac{K_\Lambda\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}}{\alpha_0K_0^\sharp}
       \left[\frac{13}{12}(E_0L^{1/2}+C_{\mathbf G})
                         +LS_{\rm fl}A_{\rm LM}\right],\\
 C_{\rm fc}^R&=\frac{8C_\chi+C_{\rm rem}}{r_x}
       +C_{\rm rem}\left[
          \frac{A_{\rm LM}}{C_2}L^{3/4}S_\omega
                     +C_{\rm arr}+1+B_\star\right],\\
 A_R&=\max\{C_3,2K_\mu C_{\rm fc}^R\},\qquad
 C_\rho^\delta=c_b^{-2}C_{am}^{\psi}h_F^{-2}L^{-1}.
\end{align*}
Choose
\begin{align*}
 C_{\rm LM}=\max\{&A_{\rm LM}+A_R+LC_\rho^\delta A_R, C_x,
                       10B_F(\bar B+4C_w),\\
 &2(5B_FC_x+C'_\rho S_3^\sharp+C_\rho^\delta A_R),
   2(5B_FC_x+C_\rho^\delta A_RS_{\rm fl}^\sharp)\},\\
 C_\Pi&=2(5B_F+2)+C_{\rm LM}
                    (1+\Theta_L/(2C'_\rho S_3^\sharp)),\\
 B_\delta&=\bar B+4C_w+C_x(1+C_\Pi),\qquad
 \eta_u=(\bar B+4C_w)L^{-u}+LS_{\rm fl}C_x\bar\phi_u^3.
\end{align*}
For the zero-source comparison take $u_*$ so that
$L^{u_*}\ge e^{18\mathfrak p_0}$ and, for $u\ge u_*$,
\begin{align*}
 (5B_FC_x+C_\rho^\delta A_RS_{\rm fl}^\sharp)\bar\phi_u^\sharp
       &\le\tfrac12,& C_{\rm LM}\bar\phi_u^\sharp&\le1,\\
 16B_\delta&\le r_xL^u,& \bar\phi_u^\sharp&\le1,\quad\eta_u\le1,\\
 C_\psi^0\bar\phi_u&\le c_{\rm cl}/20,&
 C_{\rm ld}K_\Lambda\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}A_1L\bar\phi_u
       &\le\alpha_0\theta_EC_\omega.
\end{align*}
Such a finite floor exists because all the left sides that involve
$\bar\phi_u$ tend to zero.  The source comparison below imposes
further floors on the same $u_*$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Loss of memory at a constant label]\label{C-419-6}
Suppose $u\ge u_*$.  With the notation of \cref{C-419-2}, set
\[
 \Pi_k=2|\pi|+C_{\rm LM}
                [(k-t_0+1)\varepsilon_s+L^{-s}/\mathsf b],
 \qquad
 B'_k=7B_5L^{-(k-t_0)}
                +6(\bar B+4C_w)B_FL^{-(s+1)}/\mathsf b.
\]
For $t_0\le k\le k'\le K$,
\[
 |\mathsf t_{k'}G_{<t_0,k'}(x(c))
       -\mathsf t_kG_{<t_0,k}(x(c))|\le B'_k,
\]
and
\[
 \left|\pi-\frac{\mathsf b}{\mathsf b-c}
         (\zeta-F_{<t_0}(t_1;\mathfrak m_{t_1}))\right|
       \le3(\bar B+4C_w)B_FL^{-(s+1)}/\mathsf b.
\]
At $c=0$ one may replace $7B_5$ by $6B_5$ and the coefficients
$6(\bar B+4C_w)B_F$, $3(\bar B+4C_w)B_F$ by
$4\bar BB_F$, $2\bar BB_F$, respectively.  In particular,
\[
 |\pi(F^{\rm UV};0)|
       \le B_5(L^{-t_0}+3L^{-(s-u)})
                         +2\bar BB_FL^{-(s+1)}/\mathsf b.
\]

For $t_0<k\le t_1$, both torus families obey the following
bounds, including each pointed term:
\begin{align*}
 |\delta x_k|
 &\le(\bar B+4C_w)L^{-(k-t_0)}
       +C_{\rm LM}[\phi(\mathsf t_{k-1})\Lambda_k
                         +\phi(\mathsf t_{k-1})^2\Pi_{k-1}],\\
 \|\delta F_0^{(k)}\|_k
 &\le C_{\rm LM}\phi(\mathsf t_{k-1})
                         [\Lambda_k+\phi(\mathsf t_{k-1})\Pi_{k-1}],\\
 \|\delta E_{\ge2}^{(k)}\|_k, \|\delta T^{(k)}\|_k
 &\le C_{\rm LM}\phi(\mathsf t_{k-1})^2
                         [\Lambda_k+\phi(\mathsf t_{k-1})\Pi_{k-1}],\\
 \|\delta R^{(k)}\|_k, |\delta\rho_k|
 &\le C_{\rm LM}\phi(\mathsf t_{k-1})^3[\Lambda_k+\Pi_{k-1}].
\end{align*}
The coupling difference is at most $r_x\hat x_k^\circ/8$.
The scalar activity bound holds polymer by polymer at rate
$\kappa+1$.  The explicit Gaussian term satisfies
\[
 e^{\kappa_+d_k(X)}|\delta\mathbf G^{(k)}(X;\cdot;z)|
       \le C_{\mathbf G}|\delta x_{k-1}|/\mathsf t_{k-1}.
\]
The scalar and leg bounds remain valid after summing the norms over
all pointers, with the additional factor $8M^3$.

The mass difference has the more precise form
\begin{align*}
 \mathsf t_k\delta s_k
   &=-\pi+
       [\mathsf t_kG_{<t_0,k}(x(c))
        -\mathsf t_{t_1}G_{<t_0,t_1}(x(c))]+r_k,\\
 |r_k|&\le C_{\rm LM}
       [(k-t_0+1)\varepsilon_s+L^{-s}/\mathsf b
                               +\phi_\sharp(\mathsf t_k)|\pi|].
\end{align*}
In particular $\mathsf t_k|\delta s_k|\le\Pi_k+B'_k$, and the
bracket vanishes at $k=t_1$.

Finally the activities discarded at the restart, read at a level
$t_0\le k\le K$, satisfy
\[
 \sum_{j\le t_0}C_7L^{(k-j)/4}\|E_{\ge2}^{(j)}\|_j
       \le C_7C_2S_\omega\phi(\mathsf t_k)^2\Lambda_{k+1}.
\]
For $t_0\le k<K$, their scalar localization on
$Y\in\mathcal D_k$ is at most
\[
 K_\Lambda\frac{\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}\delta(\mathsf t_k)}{\alpha_0}
       \frac L{L-1}E_0L^{-(k-t_0)}
                     e^{-(1-2\delta_{\rm w})\kappa d_k(Y)}.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By \cref{C-398-40}(e), with $\tau=1-c/\mathsf b$,
\[
 \left|\mathsf t_kG_{<t_0,k}(x(c))
       -\frac{\mathsf b}{\mathsf b-c}F_{<t_0}(k;\mathfrak m_k)\right|
       \le3(\bar B+4C_w)B_FL^{-(s+1)}/\mathsf b.
\]
Here $|x_i(c)-\tau\mathsf t_i|\le\bar B+4C_w$,
$|x_i(c)|\ge11\mathsf t_i/24$ and $|\tau|\ge63/64$.
The partial-sum comparison in \cref{C-398-40}(c) proves the first
bound and the estimate for $\pi$.  At label zero the stronger real
coupling window gives the stated smaller constants.  Taking
$\zeta=F^{\rm UV}$ and applying \cref{C-398-40}(b) gives its
last estimate.  Notice that $0\le F^{\rm UV}\le F_\infty\le B_F$,
so this is an allowed restart.

Subtract the mass identities of the two flows.  The exact identity is
\begin{align}
 \mathsf t_k\delta s_k={}&
       [\mathsf t_kG_{<t_0,k}(x(c))-\zeta']
       +\sum_{t_0\le i<k}\sigma_i(k;\mathfrak m_k)\mathsf t_i
                    \left(\frac1{x_i(c)}-\frac1{\hat x_i(c)}\right)
          \notag\\
 &+\sum_{j\le t_0}\mathsf t_j\rho_j(c)
       +\sum_{t_0<j\le k}\mathsf t_j\delta\rho_j.
 \label{eq:qcd2-memory-mass-identity}
\end{align}
The second term is at most
$5B_F\max_{t_0\le i<k}|\delta x_i|/\mathsf t_i$.
The third is at most $C'_\rho S_3^\sharp\varepsilon_s$.
These facts use slice positivity, the coupling windows, and
\[
 \phi(\mathsf t_{k-n})
       \le L^{-n/2}(1+n\log L)^{\mathfrak p_0}\phi(\mathsf t_k),
 \quad
 \phi_\sharp(\mathsf t_{k-n})
       \le L^{-n/2}(1+n\log L)^{3\mathfrak p_0}
                                      \phi_\sharp(\mathsf t_k).
\]

We now derive the one-step inequalities.  Set
\[
 X_j=|\delta x_j|/\mathsf t_j,\quad P_j=\mathsf t_j|\delta s_j|,
 \quad d_j^\psi=\frac{\|\delta E_{\ge2}^{(j)}\|_j}{\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2},
 \quad d_j^0=\frac{\|\delta F_0^{(j)}\|_j}{\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})},
 \quad d_j^R=\frac{\|\delta R^{(j)}\|_j}{\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^3}.
\]
For $j\le t_0$ use $d_j^\psi\le C_2$, $d_j^R\le C_3$ and the
full scalar array bound $E_0$; do not replace that bound by a bound
for the fluctuation family alone.

First change the current coupling and mass while holding the
restarted old families fixed.  On the coefficient polydiscs the
outputs have bounds
$2C_w\phi+2\theta_sh_F^2|s'|$ in degree zero and
$2C_2\phi^2+2c_sh_F^2|s'|^2$ with legs.  The coupling segment is
at distance at least $11r_x\mathsf t_k/48$ from its boundary;
the mass segment is at distance at least
$5B_s\phi(\hat x_k^\circ)/2$.  The definition of $C_{\rm nm}$
therefore bounds the relative changes of both activity degrees and
of the coupling extraction by
$C_{\rm nm}(X_k+\phi(\mathsf t_k)P_k)$.
The explicit term $\mathbf G$ depends only on the coupling, so
Cauchy's estimate on the same segment gives $C_{\mathbf G}X_k$
at rate $\kappa_+$, pointer by pointer.

Next change the old families, keeping the current numbers fixed.
By \cref{C-419-3} the potential is affine on this segment and its
norms are bounded by those at the endpoints.  Its scalar part is
at most $c_{\rm cl}/8$, and its leg part is at most
$C_\psi^0\phi(\mathsf t_k)\le c_{\rm cl}/20$.
The derivative estimates in \cref{C-419-3}(c), after local
extraction, give the following four kernels, with $n=k+1-j$:
\begin{align*}
 K_n^{\psi\psi}=K_n^{\psi0}
       &=\theta_EC_\omega L^{-3n/4}(1+n\log L)^{2\mathfrak p_0},\\
 K_n^{0\psi}&=\theta_EC_\omega L^{-n},\qquad
 K_n^{00}=\theta_EC_\omega L^{-3n/2}(1+n\log L)^{\mathfrak p_0}.
\end{align*}
Each satisfies $\sum_{n\ge1}K_nL^{n/2}\le\beta_\star$.
For the scalar-to-leg kernel the derivative carries the additional
factor $\phi(\mathsf t_k)$, because a scalar potential alone
creates no legs.  The last floor in \cref{C-419-9} absorbs its
constant.  The ordinary scalar contraction uses the construction
ceiling
$\sqrt2L(2+C_{am}r_\alpha^{-2})K_M^\bullet
 K_\Lambda\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}\delta(\gamma^{-2})
 \le\alpha_0\theta_EC_\omega$.
The old scalar arrays and $\delta\mathbf G$ contribute the forcing
\[
 H_k=C_{\rm fc}\left[X_k+\phi(\mathsf t_k)P_k
       +E_0L^{-(k-t_0)}
       +C_{\mathbf G}\max_{t_0\le i<k}X_i\right].
\]
We have proved
\begin{align*}
 d_{k+1}^\psi&\le D_{k+1}^\psi
      :=\sum_{j\le k}K_n^{\psi\psi}d_j^\psi
                  +\sum_{t_0<j\le k}K_n^{0\psi}d_j^0+H_k,\\
 d_{k+1}^0&\le D_{k+1}^0
      :=\sum_{j\le k}K_n^{\psi0}d_j^\psi
                  +\sum_{t_0<j\le k}K_n^{00}d_j^0+H_k,\\
 |\delta x_{k+1}|&\le L^{-1}|\delta x_k|
                    +C_x^\delta\phi(\mathsf t_k)D_{k+1}^0.
\end{align*}
All estimates include the local extraction factors.  They hold for
both torus families, and for each pointer, since the potential and
its first variation have these properties.

For the remainder, \cref{C-419-5} gives
\begin{align*}
 d_{k+1}^R\le D_{k+1}^R
  :={}&\sum_{j\le k}K_n^{RR}d_j^R
       +K_\mu\left[
        \frac{8C_\chi+C_{\rm rem}}{r_x}X_k
        +C_{\rm rem}(q_k^{\rm old}+q_k^0+P_k/\bar B_M)\right],\\
 K_n^{RR}&=K_\mu K_Mc_\psi C_7
                          L^{-5n/4}(1+n\log L)^{3\mathfrak p_0},\\
 \mathsf t_{k+1}|\delta\rho_{k+1}|
       &\le C_\rho^\delta\phi_\sharp(\mathsf t_k)D_{k+1}^R.
\end{align*}
The weighted sum of $K_n^{RR}$ is at most $1/4$ by the
second-order contraction floor of the construction.

We close these inequalities by induction with the bounds
\begin{align*}
 D_j^\psi,D_j^0&\le A_{\rm LM}
                      [\Lambda_j+\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})\Pi_{j-1}],\\
 D_j^R&\le A_R(\Lambda_j+\Pi_{j-1}),\\
 |\delta x_j|&\le(\bar B+4C_w)L^{-(j-t_0)}
       +C_x[\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})\Lambda_j
                         +\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2\Pi_{j-1}],\\
 P_j&\le\Pi_j+B'_j.
\end{align*}
For $j\le t_0$ take $\Pi_{j-1}=0$ and use $\Lambda_j\ge1$.
At $t_0$ the coupling bound follows from its ordinary window, and
the mass bound follows from \eqref{eq:qcd2-memory-mass-identity}
with the later sums empty.

Suppose the induction holds through $k<t_1$.  The bound
$\Pi_j\le C_\Pi$ and $16B_\delta\le r_xL^u$ ensure
$|\delta x_k|\le r_x\hat x_k^\circ/8$, justifying the Cauchy
segments used above.  The scale inequalities imply, for $i\le k$,
\[
 X_i\le\eta_u[\Lambda_{k+1}+\phi(\mathsf t_k)\Pi_k],\qquad
 \phi(\mathsf t_k)P_k
       \le\phi(\mathsf t_k)\Pi_k+B_\star\Lambda_{k+1},
\]
and $E_0L^{-(k-t_0)}\le E_0L^{1/2}\Lambda_{k+1}$.
Each of the four kernel sums is at most
$\beta_\star A_{\rm LM}
[\Lambda_{k+1}+\phi(\mathsf t_k)\Pi_k]$.
Thus the two activity inequalities close because
$2\beta_\star\le1/2$ and $A_{\rm LM}\ge2C_{\rm fc}C_I$.

For the remainder, the same scale sums give
\begin{align*}
 q_k^{\rm old}
  &\le(A_{\rm LM}/C_2)L^{3/4}S_\omega
                   [\Lambda_{k+1}+\phi(\mathsf t_k)\Pi_k],\\
 q_k^0&\le C_{\rm arr}
                   [\Lambda_{k+1}+\phi(\mathsf t_k)\Pi_k].
\end{align*}
For the first inequality, bound the numerator by the induction
hypothesis and keep just its last term in the denominator, which is
at least $C_2L^{-3/4}\phi(\mathsf t_k)^2$.  For the second, split
the scalar sum at $t_0$: the earlier part costs
$(L/(L-1))E_0L^{-(k-t_0)}$; the later fluctuation part costs
$LS_{\rm fl}A_{\rm LM}$ times the indicated rate; the explicit
part costs $(L/(L-1))C_{\mathbf G}\max_iX_i$.
As $L/(L-1)\le13/12$, this is precisely $C_{\rm arr}$.
The remainder inequality now closes with coefficient
$A_R/4+K_\mu C_{\rm fc}^R\le A_R$.

Iterating the coupling recursion and using the newly proved scalar
bound gives a geometric convolution bounded by $S_{\rm fl}$.
This proves its induction bound because
$C_x=C_x^\delta A_{\rm LM}S_{\rm fl}$.

For the mass, return to \eqref{eq:qcd2-memory-mass-identity}.
The later remainder sum is bounded by
\[
 C_\rho^\delta A_R\left[
 L^{-1/2}(k+1-t_0)\varepsilon_s
       +S_{\rm fl}^\sharp\phi_\sharp(\mathsf t_k)\Pi_k\right].
\]
The reciprocal-coupling term is at most
\[
 5B_F(\bar B+4C_w)L^{-s}/\mathsf b
       +5B_FC_x[L^{-1/2}\varepsilon_s
                              +\phi(\mathsf t_k)^4\Pi_k].
\]
The terms containing $\Pi_k$ sum to at most $\Pi_k/2$ by the
first depth condition.  The defining lower bounds on $C_{\rm LM}$
absorb the remaining $\varepsilon_s$ and $L^{-s}/\mathsf b$
terms, yielding $P_{k+1}\le\Pi_{k+1}+B'_{k+1}$.  This closes
the simultaneous induction.

The asserted activity estimates follow, since
$C_{\rm LM}\ge A_{\rm LM},C_x,A_R$.
Use $\delta T=\delta E_{\ge2}-\delta R$ for the explicit part
and the remainder mass functional for $\delta\rho$; the additional
terms in the definition of $C_{\rm LM}$ cover both.
Retaining the signed first bracket of
\eqref{eq:qcd2-memory-mass-identity}, instead of its absolute bound,
gives the stated formula and estimate for $r_k$.

The polymer estimates before extraction have rate $\kappa_+$.
There are at most $8M^3e^{d_k(X)}$ pointers in $X$, and
$\kappa_+-\kappa-1\ge2c_E$ leaves the same summable polymer
factor after their count.  Summing pointers therefore costs
$8M^3$.  For local extraction the constant term is put at each
pointer's cube; the action uses nonnegative pointer weights with
sum one; and the mass bound already sums its cells and places.
The resulting factors are
\[
 \frac{8M^3+1+C_{am}r_\alpha^{-2}}{2+C_{am}r_\alpha^{-2}}
       \le8M^3,
 \qquad
 \frac{8M^3+K_\mu-1}{K_\mu}\le8M^3.
\]
This proves the summed-pointer assertion without replacing it by a
bound for the norm of the signed sum.

Finally sum the closed bounds over $j\le t_0$.  With
$n=k+1-j$, retain $L^{-n/2}\le\Lambda_{k+1}$ and sum the
remaining $L^{-n/4}(1+n\log L)^{2\mathfrak p_0}$ into
$S_\omega$.  For the scalar terms apply \cref{C-419-3}(b) and
sum $\sum_{j\le t_0}L^{-(k-j)}\le(L/(L-1))L^{-(k-t_0)}$.
These are the two final estimates.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Comparison in the presence of sources}

The preceding comparison treats the constant part of a source.  A
varying source also changes the local mass increments and their cell
sums.  We first compare the two flows at the same source coordinates,
then compare their actual source chains.  The second comparison is
needed because equal coordinates do not describe equal physical
sources in the two flows.

\begin{definition}[Source coordinates for the restart]\label{C-419-7}
Let $\zeta$ be real, $|\zeta|\le2B_F+1$, and use the real restarted
sequence $\hat x_i,\hat s_i$.  Write
$\hat\phi_i=\phi(\hat x_i)$ and
\[
 \hat\tau_i(w;a)=40Ma\hat x_i^{1/2}\lambda_i
                         \operatorname{Lip}(w)/\mathsf b.
\]
Hats on the source domains mean that $\phi_i,\tau_i$ are replaced
by $\hat\phi_i,\hat\tau_i$, and that the mass coordinates run only
over $t_0\le i\le k$.  Thus a restarted coordinate is
$\hat{\mathfrak c}=(w,\mathsf n,(\sigma_i)_{t_0\le i\le k})$.
If $\mathfrak c$ is an ordinary coordinate, write
$\mathfrak c^\wedge$ for its restriction to these indices.

For $a_k^{\rm rad}\le a\le\alpha_0$ let $\mathfrak D_k(a)$ be
the intermediate domain
\[
 \|w\|_\infty<6\varrho,\quad
 C_{\rm lin}\tau_k(w;a)<3c_{\rm cl}/32,\quad
 L^{k+1}\|\mathsf n\|<3r_M/2,\quad
 \|\sigma_i\|<3B_\sigma\phi_i/2.
\]
In $\mathfrak D_k$ replace the first two requirements by
$\|w\|_{\sharp,k}<6\varrho$.

At level $t_0$ the source restart is
\begin{align*}
 \hat\tau^{\rm F}_{t_0}[\hat{\mathfrak c}](dV)
 ={}&\mathsf{Stay}(V)
 \exp\bigl[-A(L^{t_0}\hat x_{t_0}-a_K^{-1}w,\mathsf U)
       -\langle\bar\Psi,\mathbb D_{t_0}(\mathsf U)\Psi\rangle\\
 &\hspace{36mm}
       -L^{-t_0}\mathsf S_1((\hat s_{t_0}+\sigma_{t_0})
                                            \psi^{\rm bg})\bigr]
              \mathscr M^{\rm fr}_{h_\emptyset}(dV).
\end{align*}
The tower and background fermions have fine mass matrix
$m_0+\hat{\mathsf n}$, where $\mathsf n=-a_KJ$.  There are no
earlier activities, normalizers, or source energies.  Later format
data use the same source step as the construction, with the real
numbers of the restarted zero-source flow.  At level $i$ its
coupling weight is $L^i\hat x_i-a_K^{-1}w$, its mass member is
$\hat s_i+\sigma_i$, and its old activities are exactly those
generated at levels $t_0<j\le i$.

For a physical source $s=(w,J)$ define
\begin{align*}
 \hat\sigma_{t_0}(s)(x)
   &=\frac{\zeta}{L^s(\mathsf b-w(x))}
                               -\frac{\zeta}{L^s\mathsf b},\\
 \hat\sigma_{k+1}(s)(x)
   &=L\hat\sigma_k(s)(x)
       +\hat\nu_{k+1}(\hat{\mathfrak c}_k(s))(y_{k+1}(x))
       -\hat\mu_{k+1},\\
 \hat{\mathfrak c}_k(s)
   &=(w,-a_KJ,(\hat\sigma_i(s))_{t_0\le i\le k}).
\end{align*}
The occurrence of $L^s$ in the initial value uses the integer
restart depth; the argument $s$ denotes the source.  At a constant
label set
$\hat\sigma_k^{\rm c}(c)=\hat s_k(c)-\hat s_k$ and
$\hat{\mathfrak c}_k^{\rm c}(c)=(c,0,(\hat\sigma_i^{\rm c}(c)))$.
The source energies are
\[
 \hat e_j(X;s)=\hat{\mathfrak E}_j
       (X;\hat{\mathfrak c}_{j-1}(s))
                 -\hat{\mathfrak E}_j(X;0),\qquad
 \hat E_k(s)=\hat E_k+
                   \sum_{t_0<j\le k}\sum_X\hat e_j(X;s).
\]
Here $\hat{\mathfrak E}_j$ includes the value at the trivial pair
of the scalar new activity before extraction and the localized
normalizers and Gaussian term of that step.

At equal coordinates put
$\delta X(\mathfrak c)=X(\mathfrak c)-\hat X(\mathfrak c^\wedge)$;
along the chains put
$\delta^{\rm ch}X(s)=X(\mathfrak c_k(s))
                         -\hat X(\hat{\mathfrak c}_k(s))$.
Also set $d\nu_{k+1}=\nu_{k+1}-\hat\nu_{k+1}\circ\wedge$.
Earlier restarted families are zero in these definitions.

Let $c_{\rm lm}$ be the largest number in $(0,1/12]$ such that
\[
 \sum_{n\ge1}L^{-n(1/4-c_{\rm lm})}(1+n)^{\mathfrak p_0}
       \le\tfrac32S_{1/4},\qquad
 L^{c_{\rm lm}}\left(\tfrac83L^{-1/2}
                            +\tfrac{27}{112}L^{-1}\right)\le\tfrac9{10}.
\]
Such a number exists since both inequalities are strict at zero.
Put
\begin{align*}
 \Lambda_k^{\rm s}&=L^{-c_{\rm lm}(k-t_0)},&
 \Pi_k^\flat&=\Pi_k(\zeta;0),&
 \Pi_k^*&=\sup_{|c|<8\varrho}\Pi_k(\zeta;c),\\
 m_k&=\Lambda_k^{\rm s}+\phi(\mathsf t_{k-1})\Pi_{k-1}^\flat,&
 m_k^*&=\Lambda_k^{\rm s}+\phi(\mathsf t_{k-1})\Pi_{k-1}^*.
\end{align*}
Take both $\Pi$ sequences to be zero before $t_0$.  Finally
$\mathrm{tor}_k=e^{-c_{\rm t}\ell/(2\lambda_k)}$ on the torus
and $\mathrm{tor}_k=0$ on $\mathbb Z^3$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Loss of memory with sources]\label{C-419-8}
After the additional, fixed depth conditions specified below, the
following hold for $u\ge u_*$.  The norms of families with legs
sum the norms of their filed summands.  The statements hold on
every admitted torus; on $\mathbb Z^3$ the assertions about format
data and equal coordinates concern constant coordinate fields.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(S\arabic*)]
\item For $t_0\le k<t_1$ the restarted step exists on
$2\hat{\mathscr D}_k(a)$, simultaneously for
$a_k^{\rm rad}\le a\le\alpha_0$, and has the original source-step
bounds with hats:
\[
 \hat\epsilon_{k+1}^{{\rm s},\psi}(a)
       \le2C_w^{\rm s}\hat\phi_k,
 \qquad
 \hat\epsilon_{k+1}^{{\rm s},0}(a)
       \le2C_w^{\rm s}\hat\phi_k+C'_{\rm lin}\hat\tau_k(w;a).
\]
At $a=\alpha_0$ its full scalar arrays have bound $E_0^{\rm s}$.
The fluctuation scalar families have their stated bounds at rate
$\kappa+1$ pointer by pointer.  At $a=\alpha_0$, the norm of the leg families summed
over pointers is at most $8M^3$ times the displayed size, before and
after extraction.  Its increments obey the original local
holomorphy, Lipschitz and torus-defect estimates with $B_\nu$ and
$C_{\rm tor}$.

The restarted constant chain is holomorphic, real at real labels,
and satisfies
\[
 |\hat\sigma_k^{\rm c}(c)|
       \le\tfrac14 C_{\rm var}\hat\phi_k|c|/\varrho.
\]
For $t_0\le k\le t_1$ its physical source chain is holomorphic on
$\mathscr O_k$, belongs to $\hat{\mathscr D}_k$, and obeys
\[
 \|\hat\sigma_k(s)-\hat\sigma_k^{\rm c}(w(\cdot))\|
       \le C_{\rm var}\hat\phi_k\Xi_k(s)
         +2C_{\rm tor}C_{\mathcal L}\hat\phi_k\mathrm{tor}_k
                                             \|w\|_\infty/\varrho.
\]
It has the original source-locality tail estimates.  The energies
$\hat e_j$, $t_0<j\le t_1$, have the original local holomorphy,
conjugation and weighted bounds.  At constant coordinates on
$\mathbb Z^3$, $\hat\nu_{k+1}(\hat{\mathfrak c}_k^{\rm c}(c))
=\hat\mu_{k+1}(c)1$.

\item For $t_0<k\le t_1$ and
$\mathfrak c\in\mathfrak D_{k-1}(a)$, before and after extraction,
\begin{align*}
 \|\delta E_{\ge2}^{(k)}(\mathfrak c)\|_{k;a}
       &\le A_\psi^\sharp m_k\,2C_w^{\rm s}\phi_{k-1},\\
 \|\delta F_0^{(k)}(\mathfrak c)\|_{k;a}
       &\le m_k\bigl(A_0^{\rm s}\,2C_w^{\rm s}\phi_{k-1}
                                 +4C'_{\rm lin}\tau_{k-1}(w;a)\bigr).
\end{align*}
\item For $t_0\le k<t_1$, the function $d\nu_{k+1}$ is holomorphic on
$\mathfrak D_k$.  For $\mathfrak c\in\mathscr D_k$,
$\mathfrak c'\in\mathfrak D_k$, and every level-$(k+1)$ site $y$,
\begin{align*}
 |d\nu_{k+1}(\mathfrak c)(y)-d\nu_{k+1}(\mathfrak c')(y)|
 &\le2A_\psi^\sharp m_{k+1}B_\nu\phi_{k+1}
                       \|\mathfrak c-\mathfrak c'\|_{k,y},\\
 |d\nu_{k+1}(\mathfrak c)(y)-(\mu_{k+1}-\hat\mu_{k+1})|
 &\le A_\psi^\sharp m_{k+1}B_\nu\phi_{k+1}
                         \quad(\mathfrak c\in\mathfrak D_k).
\end{align*}
\item For $t_0\le k\le t_1$, along a physical source chain with
$s\in\mathscr O_{t_1}$,
\begin{align*}
 \mathsf t_k|\delta^{\rm ch}(s_k+\sigma_k)(x)|
 \le{}&\mathsf t_k|s_k(w(x))-\hat s_k(w(x))|\\
 &+A_D\mathsf t_k\phi_k\Xi_k(s)m_k^*
       +C_\Delta\mathsf t_k\phi_k\mathrm{tor}_k
                                             \|w\|_\infty/\varrho.
\end{align*}
The first term is at most $\Pi_k(\zeta;w(x))+B'_k$.  Moreover,
with $N(s)=\operatorname{Lip}(w)/\varrho+L\|J\|_\infty/r_M$,
\[
 \mathsf t_k\phi_k\Xi_k(s)
 \le c_{\rm th}\mathsf b^{1/2}L^{-(K-k)/2}
                    (1+\log\mathsf t_k)^{\mathfrak p_0}\pi_kN(s).
\]
\item For $s\in\mathscr O_{t_1}$ and $t_0<k\le t_1$, at
$a=a_{k-1}^{\rm rad}$, and also at $a=\alpha_0$ when
$\|w\|_\sharp<4\varrho$,
\begin{align*}
 \|\delta^{\rm ch}E_{\ge2}^{(k)}(s)\|_{k;a}
       &\le A_{\rm ch}(m_k^*+\mathrm{tor}_{k-1})
                                      2C_w^{\rm s}\phi_{k-1},\\
 \|\delta^{\rm ch}F_0^{(k)}(s)\|_{k;a}
       &\le A_{\rm ch}(m_k^*+\mathrm{tor}_{k-1})
              (2C_w^{\rm s}\phi_{k-1}+C'_{\rm lin}\tau_{k-1}(w;a)),\\
 \|\varpi_k(s)-\hat\varpi_k(s)\|
       &\le C_\varpi^\delta\phi_k
                              (\Xi_k(s)m_k^*+\mathrm{tor}_k).
\end{align*}
\item At the fixed pair radius, the scalar bounds in (S2) and
(S5) hold polymer by polymer and pointer by pointer at rate
$\kappa+1$, for $\|w\|_\sharp<6\varrho$ and
$\|w\|_\sharp<4\varrho$, respectively.  The leg bounds hold with
factor $8M^3$ in the norm summed over pointers, before and after
extraction.  At coordinates in $2\mathscr D_{k-1}$ and along the
chains,
\[
 e^{\kappa_+d_k(X)}
       |\mathbf G^{(k)}(X;\cdot;z)-\hat{\mathbf G}^{(k)}(X;\cdot;z)|
       \le C_{\mathbf G}^{\rm s}|\delta x_{k-1}|/\mathsf t_{k-1}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
We give the source induction, the comparison of the two format
data, and finally the comparison of their chains.  The constants
and extra depth floors are specified following the proof.

At the initial level there are no activities or pointed terms, and
the format datum is independent of the pair radius.  The source
step can therefore start simultaneously at all radii.  Its zero-
source data satisfy the bounds of \cref{C-419-4}.  In particular,
for $t_0\le i\le j\le t_1$,
\[
 |\hat x_j-L^{-(j-i)}\hat x_i|\le\bar B,
 \quad (1-L^{-1})\mathsf t_i\le\hat x_i\le(1+L^{-1})\mathsf t_i,
 \quad \hat x_i\ge\gamma^{-2}.
\]
As $\mathsf t_i\hat\phi_i\ge2$, its mass members and extracted
increments satisfy
\[
 |\hat s_i|\le\bar B_M\hat\phi_i,
 \qquad |\hat\mu_i|
       \le4\bar B_M/\mathsf t_i\le3\bar B_M\hat\phi_i.
\]
These are the numerical inputs to the source-step estimates; their
proofs now run from $t_0$ with the hatted scale functions.

The scalar array bound needs the complete zero-source terms, not
only their fluctuation parts.  At coordinate zero the restart is
exactly the flow of \cref{C-419-4}.  Its new scalar activity before
extraction, its value at the trivial pair and its action coefficient
have the original bounds with $\hat s_i$ and $\hat\phi_i$.  The
normalizer families generated after $t_0$ are the ordinary
normalizers at the same calibration and fine mass; there are no
earlier terms to estimate.  The Gaussian terms at the weight obey
the same bounds because
\[
 |\hat v_i|=L^{K-i}\|w\|_\infty/\hat x_i
       \le8\varrho/(\mathsf b-\bar B)
       \le r_v/2,
 \qquad |\hat v_i|\le16\varrho\gamma^2.
\]
The scalar constant created by pointing the Gaussian determinant
has bound
\[ (K_{\mathbf G}\bar B\gamma^2+C_w\phi(\gamma^{-2}))
 e^{-(\kappa+1)d_i(X)}. \]
Its nontrivial polymer part is the
Gaussian term at $\hat x_{i-1}/\mathsf t_{i-1}$, and at a single
cube the additional term is
$-3(L^3-1)\log(\hat x_{i-1}/\mathsf t_{i-1})/2$.
The same two unused shares of $E_0$ cover these terms.  The scalar
admission bounds and the source-radius floor therefore remain
valid, giving $E_0^{\rm s}$ and the pointed scalar bounds.

There is one change in the symmetry proof along a source chain.
The mass recursion gives
\[
 L^{-k}(\hat s_k+\hat\sigma_k(s))
   =L^{-t_0}\hat\Sigma_w^\zeta
      +\sum_{t_0<i\le k}L^{-i}
                  \hat\nu_i(\cdot;\hat{\mathfrak c}_{i-1}(s)),
 \qquad \hat\Sigma_w^\zeta=\frac{\zeta}{L^s(\mathsf b-w)}.
\]
After reading on shell, cancellation with the extracted local
parts leaves precisely the starting mass form with multiplier
$\hat\Sigma_w^\zeta$.  This scalar-valued field is invariant under
flavour transformations and charge conjugation, and complex
conjugation carries it to $\hat\Sigma_{\bar w}^\zeta$.  Thus it
has the same joint source symmetries as the other initial terms.
At each step the transformed logarithm and the logarithm of the
transformed integral differ by a scalar in $2\pi i\mathbb Z$.
It is continuous on the convex source domain and zero at source
zero, by \cref{C-419-4}; hence it vanishes throughout.  This proves
the symmetry and conjugation assertions used for the energies.

At a constant source $c$ the restarted source density at $t_0$
is exactly the density with label $c$.  Their later splittings
therefore agree.  In particular the infinite-lattice increment is
$\hat\mu_{k+1}(c)1$.  Subtracting their mass identities gives
\begin{align*}
 \mathsf t_k\hat\sigma_k^{\rm c}(c)
  ={}&\zeta\left(\frac{\mathsf b}{\mathsf b-c}-1\right)
       +\sum_{t_0\le i<k}\sigma_i(k;\mathfrak m_k)\mathsf t_i
             \left(\frac1{\hat x_i(c)}-\frac1{\hat x_i}\right)\\
 &+\sum_{t_0<j\le k}\mathsf t_j
                            (\hat\rho_j(c)-\hat\rho_j(0)).
\end{align*}
Schwarz's lemma on $|c|<8\varrho$ bounds the coupling-extraction
and cubic-remainder differences.  Slice positivity and the coupling
windows then give
\[
 |\hat\sigma_k^{\rm c}(c)|
 \le\left[\frac9{80}(B_F+1)c_{\rm th}\bar\phi_u
       +\frac12C'_\rho S_3^\sharp\bar\phi_u^{(8)}\right]
                          \hat\phi_k|c|/\varrho.
\]
The extra depth floor makes the bracket at most $C_{\rm var}/4$.
The torus increment differs from this constant infinite-lattice
increment only through wrapping terms; the same torus count as in
the source construction applies, now starting from an empty
family at $t_0$.

The initial chain defect
$\hat\sigma_{t_0}(s)(x)-\hat\sigma_{t_0}^{\rm c}(w(x))$ is zero.
Apply the original local-increment recursion with this initial
value and the bound $C_{\rm var}/4$ just proved.  Its constant
requirements are
\[
 B_\sigma\ge3C_{\rm var}\ge8B_\nu,\quad
 B_\sigma\ge2C_{\mathcal L}B_\nu,\quad
 B_\sigma\ge3C_{\rm var}+8C_{\rm tor}C_{\mathcal L},
\]
all among the original floors.  The chain stays in
$\hat{\mathscr D}_k$ and satisfies (S1).  The initial value reads
$w(x)$ alone, so the source-locality tail proof also starts with
zero defect off the support of a source difference.  The energy
proof uses only these chain bounds, the local step and its
normalizers, giving its stated conclusions for the restarted
energies.

We next compare format data at equal coordinates.  The depth
floor and \cref{C-419-6} give
$|\hat x_i/x_i-1|\le1/64$.  Hence
\[
 \tfrac89\phi_i\le\hat\phi_i\le\tfrac98\phi_i,
 \qquad \tfrac89\tau_i\le\hat\tau_i\le\tfrac98\tau_i,
 \qquad
 \mathfrak D_k(a)^\wedge\subset2\hat{\mathscr D}_k(a).
\]
Also $\mathscr D_k^\wedge\subset(9/8)\hat{\mathscr D}_k$.
Both potentials have scalar norm at most $c_{\rm cl}/2$ and leg
norm at most $(9/8)C_\psi^{\rm s}\phi_k\le c_{\rm cl}/20$.
Convexity preserves these bounds on the interpolation segment.

First vary the current coupling on
$|x'-\hat x_k|\le r_x\hat x_k/2$, holding the other format data
fixed.  The scalar origin depends on $x'$ through
$\tau=x'/\mathsf t_k$; its norm remains below $w_*/2$ because
$|\tau-1|\le3\sigma_\star/4$.  The weighted part depends on
$x'v'=-L^{K-k}w$ and is therefore fixed.  The same is true of the
linear source term; the ordinary gauge vertices are linear in
$x'$ and remain within their original bounds.  The expansion is
thus holomorphic on this whole disc.  The segment from $\hat x_k$
to $x_k$ has distance at least $3r_x\mathsf t_k/16$ from its
boundary.  Cauchy's estimate gives a change at most
$14K_Mc_{\rm cl}X_k/r_x$, before extraction, and
$C_{\mathbf G}^{\rm s}X_k$ for the explicit Gaussian term.

Next vary the families.  For $n=k+1-j$, the four derivatives
from (old leg, old scalar) to (new leg, new scalar), after
extraction, are bounded respectively by
\[
 \frac92\theta_E^{\rm s}(1+c_{\rm cs})\omega_n,\quad
 \frac{15}4K_\mu^{\rm s}\frac{C_\psi^{\rm s}}{c_{\rm cl}}
                        \phi_kL^{-(n-1)},\quad
 C_{\rm dl}^{\rm s}\omega_n,\quad
 \frac{25}{27}L^{-(n-1)}.
\]
These are \cref{C-419-3}(b),(c), the hull count for the cell sums,
and the source-radius floor
$2K_M^\bullet K_\Lambda^{\rm s}\mathsf s_k(a)\le1/6$.
The bounds apply to the maximum of the sums of the norms at the
given coordinates, at zero on the torus, and at zero on
$\mathbb Z^3$.  We keep these three sizes together in the induction.

The remaining differences are forcing terms.  There are five:
the current coupling; the current mass member; earlier mass
members and the coefficients $\mu_i$ of moved cell terms; the
explicit scalar families; and the subtraction at zero source in
the scalar extraction.  The first two are bounded using
\[
 X_k\le C_x^{\rm s}\phi_km_{k+1},\qquad
 |\delta s_k|\le\sqrt2(1+S_{B'})\phi_km_{k+1}.
\]
For the earlier mass terms, the discarded levels have
$|\mu_i|\le3\bar B_M\phi_i$, while the later levels have
$|\delta\mu_i|\le(L+1)\sqrt2(1+S_{B'})\phi_i m_{k+1}$.
Their ordinary reading is summed with $\omega_{k+1-i}$.
The additional cell terms involving $A_i^{\mathsf n}-A_i$ are
summed separately: their lag factor is $L^{k-i}$ and their mass
variation contributes $L^i\|\mathsf n\|/r_M$, so their product
is at most $3/(2L)$ on $\mathfrak D_k(a)$.  These two sums give
$C_{\rm mm}\phi_km_{k+1}$.

The discarded explicit scalar families have array bound
$E_0^{\rm s}$, and the later Gaussian differences have bound
$C_{\mathbf G}^{\rm s}X_{j-1}$.  Their localization on the fixed
radius has size at most $C^\natural\phi_km_{k+1}$.  The zero-source
scalar subtraction has size at most
$(2A_{\rm LM}+C_{\rm LM})\phi(\mathsf t_k)m_{k+1}$ by
\cref{C-419-6}.  Wrapping cell discrepancies are included in the
differences of the zero-source families.  Altogether these terms
cost $C_\psi^{\rm fc}m_{k+1}2C_w^{\rm s}\phi_k$ for the legs and
$C_0^{\rm fc}m_{k+1}2C_w^{\rm s}\phi_k$ for the scalar part.

Induct with the slightly stronger bounds
\begin{align*}
 \|\delta E_{\ge2}^{(j)}\|
  &\le m_j(A_\psi\,2C_w^{\rm s}\phi_{j-1}
                  +A'_\psi\phi_{j-1}C'_{\rm lin}\tau_{j-1}),\\
 \|\delta F_0^{(j)}\|
  &\le m_j(A_0^{\rm s}\,2C_w^{\rm s}\phi_{j-1}
                                      +A_\tau C'_{\rm lin}\tau_{j-1}).
\end{align*}
Before $t_0$ these follow from $m_j\ge1$ and the ordinary source
sizes.  At the next step use
$m_j\le L^{c_{\rm lm}n}m_{k+1}$ and
\[
 \omega_n\phi_{j-1}
       \le C_{\rm pc}L^{-n/4}(1+n)^{\mathfrak p_0}\phi_k,
 \quad \phi_{j-1}\le(2L^{-1/2})^n\phi_k,
 \quad \tau_{j-1}\le\sqrt2L^{-n/2}\tau_k.
\]
The four parts of the induction close with the following
coefficients: the leg $\phi$ part receives at most
$(27/32)A_\psi$ from itself and $A_\psi/32$ from the scalar
part; its forcing is at most $A_\psi/8$.  The leg $\phi\tau$
part receives at most $(7/20+1/2)A'_\psi$.  The scalar $\phi$
part receives at most
\[
 \tfrac7{10}A_0^{\rm s}
       +\tfrac32C_{\rm dl}^{\rm s}C_{\rm pc}S_{1/4}A_\psi
       +C_0^{\rm fc}\le A_0^{\rm s},
\]
and its $\tau$ part at most $3A_\tau/4$.
Here the numerical estimates are
$2L^{c_{\rm lm}-1/2}\le7/10$,
$2L^{c_{\rm lm}-3/2}\le1/18$ and
$\sqrt2L^{-1/2}\le2/5$; the small scalar-to-leg terms are covered
by the additional depth conditions.  Since
$C'_{\rm lin}\tau_k<3K_Mc_{\rm cl}/8$ on $\mathfrak D_k(a)$,
this proves (S2) with $A_\psi^\sharp$.

Mass extraction is a fixed linear rule on the localized kernels.
At equal $\mathsf n$ the pieces, walks and filing cells agree in
the two flows.  Applying that rule to their difference and using
(S2) gives its ordinary increment bound multiplied by
$A_\psi^\sharp m_{k+1}$.  The line from
$\mathfrak c\in\mathscr D_k$ towards
$\mathfrak c'\in\mathfrak D_k$ stays in $\mathfrak D_k$ for the
normalized complex parameter of modulus below $1/2$.
Schwarz's lemma costs the factor two in (S3).  Comparing with zero
gives its second bound.

To compare the chains fix a bare site $x_0$, put $c=w(x_0)$, and
set
\begin{align*}
 \Delta_k(x_0)&=[\sigma_k(s)-\hat\sigma_k(s)](x_0)
                     -[\sigma_k^{\rm c}(c)-\hat\sigma_k^{\rm c}(c)],\\
 g_i(c')&=\sigma_i^{\rm c}(c')-\hat\sigma_i^{\rm c}(c').
\end{align*}
We prove
\[
 |\Delta_k(x_0)|\le A_D\phi_k\Xi_k(s)m_k^*+T_k^\Delta,
 \qquad
 T_k^\Delta=\frac{112}{31}C'_\Delta
       \sum_{j\le k}L^{k-j}\phi_j\mathrm{tor}_j
                                             \|w\|_\infty/\varrho.
\]
The ordinary source-chain estimate gives the initial value because
the restarted chain agrees pointwise with its constant chain at
$t_0$.  It is bounded by the displayed right side since
$A_D\ge C_{\rm var}$ and $2C_{\rm tor}\le C'_\Delta$.

Let $A=\mathfrak c_k(s)^\wedge$ and
$A'=\mathfrak c_k^{\rm c}(c)^\wedge$.  Let $\delta_g$ have entries
$g_i(w(x))$, let $\delta'$ have entries $g_i(c)$, and let
$\delta_\Delta$ have entries $\Delta_i(x)$, in their mass slots.
All other entries are zero.  The difference of increment
differences in the recursion for $\Delta_{k+1}$ is
\begin{align*}
 &d\nu(\mathfrak c_k(s))-d\nu(\mathfrak c_k^{\rm c}(c))\\
 &+\{[\hat\nu(A)-\hat\nu(A-\delta_g)]
                         -[\hat\nu(A')-\hat\nu(A'-\delta_g)]\}\\
 &+[\hat\nu(A'-\delta')-\hat\nu(A'-\delta_g)]
       +[\hat\nu(A-\delta_g)
                       -\hat\nu(A-\delta_g-\delta_\Delta)] .
\end{align*}
The first line is controlled by (S3).  The middle braces are a
mixed difference and must not be bounded as two unrelated first
differences.  The constant-label estimate and Cauchy's estimate
in $c'$ give
\begin{align*}
 \|\delta_g\|_\infty
       &\le4(1+S_{B'})m_{k+1}^*/B_\sigma,\\
 \|\delta_g-\delta'\|_{k,y}
       &\le C_{\rm tl}(1+S_{B'})
                      \Xi_{k+1}(s)m_{k+1}^*/B_\sigma,\\
 \|\delta_\Delta\|_{k,y}
       &\le\tfrac98\max_{t_0\le i\le k}
                              |\Delta_i|/(B_\sigma\phi_i).
\end{align*}
For the smallness needed below, (U7) gives the sharper bound
\[
 \|\delta_g\|_\infty
 \le \frac{4}{B_\sigma}
       \bigl(C_\Pi\bar\phi_u+S_{B'}L^{-u/4}\bigr)
 \le \frac1{16}.
\]
The initial coordinate distance is at most $C_c\Xi_{k+1}(s)$
apart from the torus term.  All the shifted coordinates above
lie in $(19/16)\hat{\mathscr D}_k$, while the actual restarted
chains lie in $\hat{\mathscr D}_k$.

For a localized increment piece bounded by $M_0$, let $T_1$ be its
normalized size in direction $A-A'$ and $T_2\le1/16$ that in
direction $\delta_g$.  If $T_1\le1/16$, the bidisc of radii
$7/(16T_1)$ and $7/(16T_2)$ about $A'$ stays in
$2\hat{\mathscr D}_k$; the mixed Cauchy estimate is at most
$2^{11}M_0T_1T_2$.  If $T_1>1/16$, the two separate Schwarz
estimates in the second direction give the same upper bound.
Summing pieces therefore bounds the braces by
\[
 \tfrac97 C^{\rm mix}B_\nu\phi_{k+1}
       \|\mathfrak c_k(s)-\mathfrak c_k^{\rm c}(c)\|_{k,y}
                          \|\delta_g\|_\infty,
 \qquad C^{\rm mix}=2^{10}.
\]
The last two brackets are bounded by $(9/7)B_\nu\phi_{k+1}$
times their coordinate distances.  This gives the recursion
\[
 |\Delta_{k+1}(x_0)|
 \le\left[
 L^{c_{\rm lm}}\left(\tfrac83L^{-1/2}
                         +\tfrac{27}{112}L^{-1}\right)A_D
           +C_D^{\rm fc}\right]
        \phi_{k+1}\Xi_{k+1}(s)m_{k+1}^*+T_{k+1}^\Delta.
\]
It closes because the bracket is at most $A_D$.
The torus recursion closes with factor $112/31$: its feedback is
at most $81/112$, by $B_\sigma\ge2C_{\mathcal L}B_\nu$.
The torus scale sum gives
$T_k^\Delta\le C_\Delta\phi_k\mathrm{tor}_k\|w\|_\infty/\varrho$.
This proves (S4), including its last estimate by
$\Xi_k(s)\le\lambda_k\pi_kN(s)$.

For (S5), split a family difference along the chains into its
equal-coordinate difference and the change of the restarted
family between the two chain coordinates.  Their normalized mass
distance is at most
\[
 T_k(s)\le
 \frac{4(1+S_{B'})+(9/4)A_D}{B_\sigma}m_k^*
       +\frac{9C_\Delta}{2B_\sigma}\mathrm{tor}_{k-1}.
\]
The first coordinate lies in $(9/8)\hat{\mathscr D}_{k-1}$,
the second in $\hat{\mathscr D}_{k-1}$.  Schwarz's lemma on the
line between them costs at most $(16/7)T_k(s)$ times the source
size.  It applies also to the sum of norms of summands: first
apply it to a finite sum tested against arbitrary norm-one linear
functionals, then take the supremum and the absolutely convergent
limit.  This proves the family bounds with $A_{\rm ch}$.

For the zeroth moment the same kernel $A_k(y,z)$ occurs in both
flows at the trivial pair.  Thus
\[
 \delta^{\rm ch}\varpi_k(y)
 =\sum_zA_k(y,z)
           [\delta^{\rm ch}\nu_k(z)-\delta^{\rm ch}\nu_k(y)]
       +\delta^{\rm ch}r_k(y).
\]
Freeze the constant label at $w(y)$.  The four-bracket estimate
above bounds the spatial variation of the increments by
$C\phi_k\Xi_km_k^*$ times $1+|y-z|_k$, plus the torus term.
The weighted kernel sum is at most $C_A^{\rm m}$.  The change of
the kernel with $\mathsf n$ is at most
$C_A^{\rm n}L^k\|\mathsf n\|/r_M$ in row-sum norm; it acts on
the same increment difference.  The remaining constant-label
increment is bounded by
$2\sqrt2(2L^{1/2}+LS_{B'})\phi_km_k^*$, using
$\delta\mu_k(c)=\delta s_k(c)-L\delta s_{k-1}(c)$.
Finally the two torus remainders cost
$3C_r^{\rm t}\phi_k\mathrm{tor}_k$.  The explicit constant
$C_\varpi^\delta$ below is the sum of these bounds.

The scalar comparison was made polymer by polymer at rate
$\kappa_+$, apart from the zero-source subtraction, which has
rate $\kappa+1$ by \cref{C-419-6}.  The same induction and the
chain Schwarz estimate therefore prove the scalar part of (S6).
For legs, count at most $8M^3e^{d_k(X)}$ pointers before
extraction.  The extra decay pays their count.  Each source mass
piece is pointed wholly at its own cell, and the local subtraction
adds at most $K_\mu^{\rm s}-1$ times the largest pre-extraction
size at the three coordinates used in the induction.  Hence
$8M^3+K_\mu^{\rm s}-1\le8M^3K_\mu^{\rm s}$ gives the same
factor after extraction.  Apply Schwarz's lemma in this summed
norm for the chain comparison.  The same argument for one flow
proves the summed-pointer assertion in (S1).  The earlier coupling
Cauchy estimate proves the last Gaussian bound.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Constants for the source comparison.}
Continue the choices in \cref{C-419-9} in the following order.  Set
\[
 S_{B'}=\bigl(7B_5+6(\bar B+4C_w)B_F\bigr)
       \sup_{v\ge0}L^{-v/4}(1+v\log L)^{\mathfrak p_0}.
\]
Then $\phi(\mathsf t_i)B'_i\le S_{B'}L^{-s/4}$ for $i\ge t_0$.
Define
\begin{align*}
 C_\psi^{\rm s}={}&C_V^{\rm s}h_F^2A_1
       +\tfrac98c'_\psi c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2(\bar B_M+2B_\sigma)
       +\tfrac98c'_\psi C_0^{\rm cs}h_F^2\\
 &+\tfrac94(1+c_{\rm cs})c'_\psi C_{\rm pc}S_{1/4}C_w^{\rm s},\\
 C_{\rm dl}^{\rm s}={}&\tfrac{25}2K_M^\bullet c'_\psi(1+c_{\rm cs}),
 \qquad
 C_{\mathbf G}^{\rm s}=\tfrac{32}3(C_{\mathbf G}^v+2r_x^{-1}),\\
 C_x^{\rm s}={}&\sqrt2[\bar B+4C_w+C_x(LS_{\rm fl}+1)],\\
 C^\natural={}&\tfrac{13\sqrt2}{12}
 K_\Lambda^{\rm s}\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}A_1\alpha_0^{-1}
                   (C_{\mathbf G}^{\rm s}+L^{1/12}E_0^{\rm s}),\\
 C_{\rm mm}={}&\tfrac98(1+c_{\rm cs})c'_\psi c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2
 L^{1/2}C_{\rm pc}S_{1/4}
       [6\bar B_M+3B_\sigma+(L+2)\sqrt2(1+S_{B'})]\\
 &+\tfrac98c'_\psi C_0^{\rm cs}h_F^2
       [L^{1/12}+(L+1)\sqrt2(1+S_{B'})/(3\bar B_M)],\\
 C_\psi^{\rm fc}={}&\frac{K_\mu^{\rm s}K_M^\bullet}{C_w^{\rm s}}
 \left[\frac{7c_{\rm cl}C_x^{\rm s}}{r_x}
       +\frac{25\sqrt2}8c'_\psi c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2(1+S_{B'})
       +3C_{\rm mm}
       +\frac{45}2\frac{C_\psi^{\rm s}}{c_{\rm cl}}C^\natural\right],\\
 C_0^{\rm fc}={}&\frac1{C_w^{\rm s}}
 \left[K_M^\bullet\left(
       \frac{14c_{\rm cl}C_x^{\rm s}}{r_x}
       +\frac{25\sqrt2}4c'_\psi c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2(1+S_{B'})
       +6C_{\rm mm}+6C^\natural\right)
       +\frac{2A_{\rm LM}+C_{\rm LM}}{\sqrt2}\right].
\end{align*}
The term $C_0^{\rm cs}$ includes the separately summed cell
contribution:
\[
 C_0^{\rm cs}
       =\frac{6C_{\rm hl}M^3C_{\rm bg}^{\rm w}\bar B_M}
                       {L(1-2L^{-1/2})}.
\]
Next put
\begin{align*}
 A_\psi&=\max\{1,8C_\psi^{\rm fc},C_0^{\rm fc}\},& A_\tau&=4,\\
 A'_\psi&=16K_\mu^{\rm s}C_\psi^{\rm s}/c_{\rm cl},&
 C_A^{\rm s}&=5C_{\rm dl}^{\rm s}C_{\rm pc}S_{1/4}+4,\\
 A_0^{\rm s}&=\max\{1,
       5C_{\rm dl}^{\rm s}C_{\rm pc}S_{1/4}A_\psi+4C_0^{\rm fc}\},&
 A_\psi^\sharp&=A_\psi+\tfrac3{16}A'_\psi K_Mc_{\rm cl}/C_w^{\rm s}.
\end{align*}
These choices give
$A_0^{\rm s}\le C_A^{\rm s}A_\psi$ and all the closing
inequalities in the four-part induction.

For the chain comparison set $C_c=C_{\rm tl}+41M$,
$C^{\rm mix}=2^{10}$ and
\begin{align*}
 C_D^{\rm fc}={}&2A_\psi^\sharp B_\nu C_c
       +\tfrac97\frac{B_\nu}{B_\sigma}(1+S_{B'})
                             (4C^{\rm mix}C_c+C_{\rm tl}),\\
 A_D={}&\max\{C_{\rm var},10C_D^{\rm fc}\},\\
 C'_\Delta={}&4C_{\rm tor}
       +(1+C_\Pi)\frac{B_\nu}{B_\sigma}
            C_{\rm tor}C_{\mathcal L}
       [4A_\psi^\sharp+\tfrac{72}7C^{\rm mix}(1+S_{B'})/B_\sigma],\\
 C_\Delta={}&4C_{\mathcal L}C'_\Delta,\\
 A_{\rm ch}={}&\max\{A_\psi^\sharp,A_0^{\rm s},4\}
       +\frac{18}{7B_\sigma}
            [4(1+S_{B'})+\tfrac94A_D+\tfrac92C_\Delta].
\end{align*}
For the zeroth-moment comparison take
\begin{align*}
 C_A^{\rm m}&=\nu_PA_\kappa^2C_H^2
       \sup_{d\ge0}(1+c_{\mathcal D}M(1+d))e^{-\kappa d},\\
 S_\alpha&=e^{3\alpha_D}
       \left(\frac{1+e^{-\alpha_D}}{1-e^{-\alpha_D}}\right)^3,\\
 C_A^{\rm n}&=2\nu_PS_\alpha^2C_{\rm bg}(C_H+C_{\rm bg}),
       \qquad C_r^{\rm t}=C+C_A(3\bar B_M+B_\nu).
\end{align*}
Here $C$ is the original bound for the remainder $r_k$ in the
zeroth-moment formula, and $C_A$ its kernel constant.  The first
constant bounds
$\sum_z\|A_k(y,z)\|(1+|y-z|_k)$: its walk pieces have weighted
sum $\nu_PA_\kappa^2C_H^2$, and their polymers contain both
endpoints.  The second bounds the two sums of the exponential
background decay.  Indeed a bare site is within three path units
of the origin of its unit cube, and
$\sum_{v\in\mathbb Z^3}e^{-\alpha_D|v|_1}
=((1+e^{-\alpha_D})/(1-e^{-\alpha_D}))^3$.

To verify the third bound, write the mass dependence of each
kernel product as the change of the first leg times the second,
plus the first unchanged leg times the change of the second.
The background-map difference has kernel bound
$C_{\rm bg}(L^k\|\mathsf n\|/r_M)L^{-k}e^{-\alpha_Dd}$.
Summing one leg over bare places and the other over block sites,
with the factor $L^{-k}$ in the mass form, gives
\[
 \sup_y\sum_z\|(A_k^{\mathsf n}-A_k)(y,z)\|
       \le C_A^{\rm n}L^k\|\mathsf n\|/r_M.
\]
This argument uses $L^k\|\mathsf n\|/r_M<2$ and the two
background decay sums above.  On a torus the sums are bounded by
the corresponding sums over all translates on $\mathbb Z^3$.

With these constants one may take
\begin{align*}
 C_\varpi^\delta={}&C_A^{\rm m}
       (2C_D^{\rm fc}+A_D+8C'_\Delta+2C_\Delta+20C_{\rm tor})\\
 &+C_A^{\rm n}
       (2C_D^{\rm fc}+A_D+6L^{1/2}+6LS_{B'}
                         +8C'_\Delta+2C_\Delta+18C_{\rm tor})
       +3C_r^{\rm t}.
\end{align*}

Enlarge the depth floor $u_*$ in \cref{C-419-9} so that the
following four further conditions hold for every $u\ge u_*$:
\begin{align*}
 \tfrac98c_{\rm th}C_\psi^{\rm s}\bar\phi_u
       &\le c_{\rm cl}/20,\\
 \tfrac9{80}(B_F+1)c_{\rm th}\bar\phi_u
       +\tfrac12C'_\rho S_3^\sharp\bar\phi_u^{(8)}
       &\le C_{\rm var}/4,\\
 3K_\mu^{\rm s}(C_\psi^{\rm s}/c_{\rm cl})
                         c_{\rm th}C_A^{\rm s}\bar\phi_u
       &\le1/32,\\
 10C_{\rm dl}^{\rm s}C_{\rm pc}S_{1/4}
       K_\mu^{\rm s}(C_\psi^{\rm s}/c_{\rm cl})c_{\rm th}\bar\phi_u
       &\le1,\\
 4(C_\Pi\bar\phi_u+S_{B'}L^{-u/4})&\le B_\sigma/16.
\end{align*}
The first line admits the potential interpolation; the second
bounds the restarted constant chain; the next two close the
scalar-to-leg estimates; and the last keeps the translated chain
coordinates inside $(19/16)\hat{\mathscr D}_k$.  All constants on
their left have already been fixed, so this enlargement is finite
and independent of $K$, the side, and the source.

\subsection{Differences along the source chains}

We record the estimates in the norms used to add differences to an
RG flow.  For a family with legs, its norm is the sum of the norms
of its filed summands.  The pointed norm sums these further over
the pointers of each polymer.  For scalar families use
\[
 |G_0|_j=\sup_{X,z}e^{(\kappa+1)d_j(X)}\sup|G_0(X;\cdot;z)|.
\]
All pair radii in this subsection are the fixed radii
$\alpha_0,\alpha_1$.

\begin{corollary}[Differences along the source chains]\label{C-419-10}
Let $u\ge u_*$, $\zeta\in\mathbb R$, $|\zeta|\le2B_F+1$, and
$s=(w,J)\in\mathscr O_{t_1}$ with $\|w\|_\sharp<4\varrho$.
Use the restart of \cref{C-419-7}.  Let
\[
 \delta^{\rm ch}E^{(j)}(s)
 =E^{(j)}(\cdot;\mathfrak c_{j-1}(s))
       -\hat E^{(j)}(\cdot;\hat{\mathfrak c}_{j-1}(s)),
\]
where the second term is zero for $j\le t_0$.  Let
$r_j^\psi(s)$ be the largest of the following four quantities:
the norm of $\delta^{\rm ch}E_{\ge2}^{(j)}(s)$; the norms of the
zero-source difference on the torus and on $\mathbb Z^3$; and
$c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2|\mu_j-\hat\mu_j|$, with
$\hat\mu_j=0$ for $j\le t_0$.

The constants in \cref{C-419-9} may be supplemented by
\begin{align*}
 A_r={}&\max\left\{2C_w^{\rm s}A_{\rm ch},
 4\sqrt2L^{1/2}(2L^{1/2}+LS_{B'})c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2\right\},\\
 A_r^{\rm ch}={}&\max\{2C_w^{\rm s},
                6L^{1/2}c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2\bar B_M\}.
\end{align*}
Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item For $t_0<j\le t_1$,
\begin{align*}
 \|\delta^{\rm ch}E_{\ge2}^{(j)}(s)\|_j
   &\le2C_w^{\rm s}A_{\rm ch}
                     (m_j^*+\mathrm{tor}_{j-1})\phi_{j-1},\\
 \|\delta^{\rm ch}E_{\ge2}^{(j)}(s)\|_j^{\rm pt}
   &\le16M^3C_w^{\rm s}A_{\rm ch}
                     (m_j^*+\mathrm{tor}_{j-1})\phi_{j-1},\\
 r_j^\psi(s)&\le A_r(m_j^*+\mathrm{tor}_{j-1})\phi_{j-1}.
\end{align*}
\item At these levels the calibration and fine-mass normalizers
are identical in the two flows.  Consequently
\[
 \delta^{\rm ch}E_0^{(j)}(s)
   =\delta^{\rm ch}F_0^{(j)}(s)
                  +\mathbf G^{(j)}-\hat{\mathbf G}^{(j)}
\]
and
\begin{align*}
 |\delta^{\rm ch}E_0^{(j)}(s)|_j
 \le{}& A_{\rm ch}(m_j^*+\mathrm{tor}_{j-1})
        (2C_w^{\rm s}+8\alpha_0\varrho C'_{\rm lin})\phi_{j-1}\\
 &+C_{\mathbf G}^{\rm s}C_x^{\rm s}m_j\phi_{j-1}.
\end{align*}
Subtracting the value at the trivial pair multiplies this bound
by at most two.
\item For $j\le t_0$ the difference is the ordinary activity and
\[
 \|E_{\ge2}^{(j)}\|_j\le2C_w^{\rm s}\phi_{j-1},\qquad
 \|E_{\ge2}^{(j)}\|_j^{\rm pt}
                  \le16M^3C_w^{\rm s}\phi_{j-1},\qquad
 r_j^\psi(s)\le A_r^{\rm ch}\phi_{j-1}.
\]
Moreover $|E_0^{(j)}|_j\le E_0^{\rm s}$; subtracting its value
at the trivial pair gives the bound $2E_0^{\rm s}$.
\item For $t_0<j\le t_1$, the rates satisfy
\[
 m_j\le m_j^*
     =L^{-c_{\rm lm}(j-t_0)}
                    +\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})\Pi_{j-1}^*,
 \qquad c_{\rm lm}\ge c_\#,
\]
where $\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})\le\bar\phi_u$ and
\[
 \Pi_{j-1}^*=2\sup_{|c|<8\varrho}|\pi(\zeta;c)|
                +C_{\rm LM}[(j-t_0)\varepsilon_s+L^{-s}/\mathsf b].
\]
For the ultraviolet start,
\begin{align*}
 \sup_{|c|<8\varrho}|\pi(F^{\rm UV};c)|
 \le{}&\frac{64}{63}B_5
                       (L^{-t_0}+3L^{-(s-u)})\\
 &+3(\bar B+4C_w)B_FL^{-(s+1)}/\mathsf b.
\end{align*}
For $j\le k\le t_1$,
$m_j^*\le L^{c_{\rm lm}(k-j)}m_k^*$.
On every admitted torus and for $j\le t_1$,
$\mathrm{tor}_j\le e^{-c_{\rm t}L^{u+1}}$; on
$\mathbb Z^3$ it vanishes.
\end{enumerate}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Part (a)'s first estimate is \cref{C-419-8}(S5) at
$a=\alpha_0$; the second is (S6).  The difference is formed
summand by summand, with the same cells and pointers, because
the filing and extraction rules are linear.  The two zero-source
norms are at most $2C_w^{\rm s}A_\psi^\sharp m_j\phi_{j-1}$
by (S2), and $A_\psi^\sharp\le A_{\rm ch}$.

For the remaining entry of $r_j^\psi$, use
\[
 \mu_j-\hat\mu_j=\delta s_j-L\delta s_{j-1}.
\]
The mass bound of \cref{C-419-6}, including its initial-level
bound, gives
$\mathsf t_i|\delta s_i|\le\Pi_i^\flat+B_i'$.
Since $\mathsf t_{j-1}=L\mathsf t_j$, $\Pi_i^\flat$ grows
and $B_i'$ decreases,
\[
 |\mu_j-\hat\mu_j|
                \le2(\Pi_j^\flat+B_{j-1}')/\mathsf t_j.
\]
Now $1/\mathsf t_j\le\phi(\mathsf t_j)^2$,
\[
 \phi(\mathsf t_j)\Pi_j^\flat
     \le2L^{1/2}\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})\Pi_{j-1}^\flat,
 \qquad
 \phi(\mathsf t_j)B_{j-1}'
     \le L^{1/2}S_{B'}L^{-s/4}
     \le LS_{B'}\Lambda_j^{\rm s}.
\]
Here $\Pi_j^\flat\le2\Pi_{j-1}^\flat$ follows from
$\Pi_{j-1}^\flat\ge C_{\rm LM}\varepsilon_s$, while
$j-t_0\le s$ and $c_{\rm lm}\le1/12$ give the last inequality.
Finally $\phi(\mathsf t_j)\le\sqrt2\phi_j$ and
$\phi_j\le2L^{1/2}\phi_{j-1}$.  Combining these inequalities
gives
\[
 c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2|\mu_j-\hat\mu_j|
 \le4\sqrt2L^{1/2}(2L^{1/2}+LS_{B'})c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2
                                  m_j\phi_{j-1},
\]
as required.

For (b), the scalar part is
$F_0^{(j)}+\mathbf N^{{\rm un},(j)}+
\mathbf N^{{\rm F},(j)}-\mathbf c_j+\mathbf G^{(j)}$.
The calibration and fine mass determine
$\mathbf N^{{\rm un},(j)}$ and $\mathbf c_j$;
$\mathbf N^{{\rm F},(j)}$ depends on the fine mass matrix
$m_0-a_K\hat J$, which the two chains share.  These three
terms cancel.  Apply (S5) and (S6), using
$\tau_{j-1}(w;\alpha_0)\le8\alpha_0\varrho\phi_{j-1}$,
and then the estimates
\[
 |\mathbf G^{(j)}-\hat{\mathbf G}^{(j)}|_j
        \le C_{\mathbf G}^{\rm s}X_{j-1},\qquad
 X_{j-1}\le C_x^{\rm s}\phi_{j-1}m_j
\]
from the proof of \cref{C-419-8}.  Evaluation at the trivial
pair is bounded by the same supremum.

For (c), the restarted family is absent.  The ordinary source
step bounds its summand norms by $2C_w^{\rm s}\phi_{j-1}$.
The pointed count multiplies this by $8M^3$.  The same bound
holds at zero sources on both lattices, while
\[
 c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2|\mu_j|
 \le3c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2\bar B_M\phi_j^2
 \le6L^{1/2}c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2\bar B_M\phi_{j-1}.
\]
We used $|\mu_j|\le3\bar B_M/x_j$,
$x_j^{-1}\le\phi_j^2$, and $\phi_j\le1$.
The scalar bound is the scalar-source estimate of
\cite[\S11]{QCDM1}, applied at
$\mathfrak c_{j-1}(s)\in\mathscr D_{j-1}(\alpha_0)$.

For (d), $\Pi^\flat\le\Pi^*$ and the choice of
$c_{\rm lm}$ gives $c_{\rm lm}\ge c_\#$.  Also
$\mathsf t_{j-1}\ge L^u$, so
$\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})\le\bar\phi_u$.  To estimate the initial
mismatch, use the formula in \cref{C-419-6}(A),
$|\mathsf b/(\mathsf b-c)|\le64/63$, and
\[
 |F^{\rm UV}-F_{<t_0}(t_1;\mathfrak m_{t_1})|
           \le B_5(L^{-t_0}+3L^{-(s-u)}),
\]
which is \cref{C-398-40}(b) with $i_0=t_0$, $k=t_1$.
The geometric part of $m_j^*$ changes by
$L^{c_{\rm lm}(k-j)}$ between levels $j$ and $k$; its floor
increases with the level, since $\phi$ decreases on
$[L^u,\infty)$ and $\Pi^*$ increases.  This proves the
comparison of rates.  Finally
$\ell/\lambda_j=\ell L^{K-j}\ge\ell L^u\ge2L^{u+1}$,
since an admitted side is at least $2L$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The restart used for two cutoffs}

The abstract restart now gives the concrete measure to which the
two cutoff constructions will be compared.  Its initial mass
retains the ultraviolet part of the mass renormalization.

\begin{lemma}[The comparison restart]\label{C-419-11}
Use the data of \cref{C-418-2}, the condition \textup{(k0)}, and
$u\ge u_*$.  For either datum $\bullet\in\{\mathrm A,\mathrm B\}$
write $t_0=t_0^\bullet$, $t_1=t_1^\bullet$ and set
$\zeta=F^{\rm UV}\in[0,B_F]$.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item At a source $s=(w,J)$ with $\|w\|_\infty<8\varrho$,
\[
 \hat x_{t_0}=L^s\mathsf b,\qquad
 \hat s_{t_0}+\hat\sigma_{t_0}(s)
       =\frac{F^{\rm UV}}{L^s(\mathsf b-w)}=:\hat\Sigma_w.
\]
Put $\mathsf c_w=L^s(\mathsf b-w)$, and let
$W\in\mathcal Y=\mathcal V_{t_0}$.  Define the weighted
background action by
\[
 \mathsf{wab}(\mathsf c,W)
       =A^{\eta_{t_0}}(\mathsf c,\mathsf U_{t_0}(W)).
\]
The level-$t_0$ term of the restart is
\begin{align*}
 \chi_{t_0}(T_\ell)(W)\exp\bigl[&-\mathsf{wab}(\mathsf c_w,W)
 -\langle\bar\Psi,
     \mathbb D_{t_0}(\mathsf U_{t_0}(W);m_0-a_K\hat J)\Psi\rangle\\
 &-L^{-t_0}\mathsf S_1(\hat\Sigma_w\psi^{\rm bg})\bigr]\,dW.
\end{align*}
Here $dW$ is product Haar probability measure.  No activities,
numbers or normalizers of levels $\le t_0$ occur.  This is the
initial density $\hat d_{t_0}(s)$ of \cref{C-418-3}, restricted
by the density test $\chi_{t_0}(T_\ell)$.

For $s\in\mathscr O_{t_0}$ its density is a bounded Borel
function on $\mathcal Y$ with values in
$\mathrm{Gr}_{t_0}^{\rm ev}$.  It is zero off the open set
$\mathcal V_{t_0}^\chi$ of configurations passing the test and
continuous on that set.  At each such $W$, all three terms of
the exponent have one value on the minimal orbit
$\mathcal C(\mathbf B_{t_0},W)$.
\item The subsequent steps along $h_\emptyset$ use the
calibrations, tests, backgrounds, reference measures and tower
of the original datum.  Their real numbers
$(\hat x_i,\hat s_i,\hat e_i,\hat b_i,\hat\mu_i)$ are read from
the new zero-source activity on $\mathbb Z^3$ at each step.
The chain is the hatted chain of \cref{C-419-7}; the increments
use $\hat\mu_{k+1}=\hat\nu_{k+1}(0)$.  The extracted number is
\[
 \hat E_k(s)=\sum_{t_0<j\le k}
       \left(\hat e_jn_j+\sum_{X\in\mathcal D_j}\hat e_j(X;s)\right).
\]
Thus $\hat E_k(s)=\hat c_k(s)$ in \cref{C-418-9}, and at
$k=t_1$ it is $\hat c^\bullet(s)$ in \cref{C-418-3}.
\item At zero sources the same local start and steps define the
restart on the torus and on $\mathbb Z^3$ of spacing $a_K$.
Its extracted numbers do not depend on $\ell$.  On every
polymer which does not wrap, the torus activity is the part of
the infinite-lattice activity which fits, with the same pointers
under the local chart.  Both families satisfy the symmetry,
locality, holomorphy and norm assertions of
\cref{C-419-4} and \cref{C-419-8}(S1), in their respective norms.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
At $c=0$ the definitions give
$\hat s_{t_0}=F^{\rm UV}/(L^s\mathsf b)$ and
$\hat\sigma_{t_0}(s)=\hat\Sigma_w-\hat s_{t_0}$.  Also
\[
 L^{t_0}\hat x_{t_0}-a_K^{-1}w
       =L^K(\mathsf b-w)=L^{t_0}\mathsf c_w.
\]
The weighted background action is linear in its weight, read at
the barycentres of the bare plaquettes, and
$A^{\eta_{t_0}}=L^{t_0}A$.  Hence the action in
\cref{C-419-7} is $\mathsf{wab}(\mathsf c_w,W)$.
The history $h_\emptyset$ has no stored fluctuations; its free
coordinates are precisely the level-$t_0$ configurations.
Its free measure is therefore product Haar probability measure.
The definition of the source restart now gives the displayed
density and absence of earlier members.

We check its measurability and bounds, since later integral
identities use this actual density.  The tested-field lemma and
the background construction used in \cref{C-419-4} give, near
every $W_0\in\mathcal V_{t_0}^\chi$, a continuous representative
\[
 \Upsilon(W)=U^\circ_{\mathbf B_{t_0}}(W)
                      \in\mathcal C(\mathbf B_{t_0},W).
\]
The latter set is one orbit of the residual gauge group, whose
elements are the identity at the level-$t_0$ sites.  The weighted
action is constant on this orbit, also for complex weights.
Both the fine mass matrix $m_0-a_K\hat J$ and the scalar field
$\hat\Sigma_w$ commute with gauge transformations.  Covariance
of the tower and background maps therefore makes their two
quadratic forms constant on the same orbit: the action on the
external level-$t_0$ generators is trivial.  All three forms
can consequently be evaluated at $\Upsilon(W)$.

The regularity and source bounds needed for these forms hold
on their stated domains.  Indeed every minimizing background
over a tested $W$ satisfies
\[
 |\partial U(p)-1|<\alpha_0L^{-2t_0}
                  \le\epsilon_*L^{-2(t_0+1)},
\]
because $\alpha_0\le\epsilon_*L^{-2}$.  Thus it satisfies
$(\mathrm{Reg}_{t_0})[\epsilon_*]$ on $h_\emptyset$.
For $s\in\mathscr O_{t_0}$ and $\mathsf n=-a_KJ$,
\[
 L^{t_0+1}\|\mathsf n\|<r_M,
 \qquad
 \sup_x\|L^{t_0-K}J(x)\|
            <r_M/L\le\varrho_*\le\varrho_\sharp.
\]
The matrix-source tower estimate in \cite[\S7]{QCDM1} now
applies at $j=t_0$, $k=t_0+1\le K$.  Its matrix-source
span condition is part of the definition of $J$.  It gives
$\|\mathbb D_{t_0}\|\le3\mathsf c_{\rm tw}$ and holomorphy
of its entries.  The corresponding background-map estimate
applies as well: regularity and the source bound at $t_0-1$
follow from the displayed ones, with an additional factor
$L^{-1}$.  It gives the uniform kernel bounds and holomorphy
of those maps.  Their compositions with $\Upsilon$ are thus
continuous and bounded on the tested set.

Moreover $\|w\|_\infty<4\varrho$ there and
$64\varrho\le r_x\gamma^{-2}<\mathsf b$, whence
\[
 \operatorname{Re}\mathsf c_w>0,\qquad
 |e^{-\mathsf{wab}(\mathsf c_w,W)}|\le1,\qquad
 |\hat\Sigma_w|\le\frac{B_F}{L^s(\mathsf b-4\varrho)}.
\]
The second inequality uses the nonnegative plaquette action.
On the finite torus the Grassmann exponential is a polynomial
in finitely many generators.  Its coefficients are bounded
continuous functions on $\mathcal V_{t_0}^\chi$.  Extending
them by zero gives the claimed bounded Borel density.

For (b), \cref{C-419-4} gives the restart's real extracted
numbers at $c=0$.  Extraction reads the new infinite-lattice
activity and depends on neither the torus nor the coupling
weight.  The source step uses these numbers; its local mass
increment at the zero coordinate is $\hat\mu_{k+1}$.
The source-dependent extracted scalar is
\[
 \hat e_j(X;s)=
 \hat{\mathfrak E}_j(X;\hat{\mathfrak c}_{j-1}(s))
                   -\hat{\mathfrak E}_j(X;0).
\]
Summing it and the zero-source terms $\hat e_jn_j$, with
$\hat E_{t_0}=0$, gives precisely the number in the statement.

For (c), the step acts on the pair of infinite-lattice and
torus families, preserving agreement on polymers which do not
wrap and carrying pointers by the same chart.  Both starts use
the same local formulas and have no activity.  Induction on
the level proves the assertion, including the independence of
the extracted numbers from $\ell$.
At zero sources the hatted chain is zero, since its initial
value is zero and $\hat\nu_{k+1}(0)=\hat\mu_{k+1}$.
The source restart at this coordinate is therefore the
zero-source restart on each lattice, with identical source
energies (all zero).  The bounds of \cref{C-419-8}(S1) apply
on both lattices, including the scalar and pointed bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The restarted flow]\label{C-418-9}
Let the two-cutoff data satisfy \textup{(k0)} and $u\ge u_*$.
For either datum, let $t_0\le k\le t_1$ and
$s=(w,J)\in\mathscr O_k$.  The restart with initial mass
$F^{\rm UV}/[L^s(\mathsf b-w)]$ exists up to level $k$.
Its term along $h_\emptyset$ is the exact image of the tested
start in \cref{C-419-11} under the steps $t_0+1,\ldots,k$.
It has a bounded Borel density and the usual RG form, with
\begin{gather*}
 \text{coupling weight }L^k\hat x_k-a_K^{-1}w,
 \qquad \text{tower mass }m_0-a_K\hat J,\\
 \text{mass term }-L^{-k}\mathsf S_1
                    ((\hat s_k+\hat\sigma_k(s))\psi^{\rm bg}),\\
 \text{activities }\hat E^{(j)}(X;\cdot;s),\quad t_0<j\le k,
 \qquad
 \hat c_k(s)=\sum_{t_0<j\le k}
       \left(\hat e_jn_j+\sum_{X\in\mathcal D_j}\hat e_j(X;s)\right).
\end{gather*}
The activities have the locality, covariance, holomorphy and
source extraction properties of the original construction.
Their scalar parts contain no source-dependent constant.
The zeroth moment at a level-$j$ site $y$ is
\[
 \hat\varpi_j(s)(y)
 =\sum_z A_j(y,z)
    [\hat\nu_j(z;\hat{\mathfrak c}_{j-1}(s))
       -\hat\nu_j(y;\hat{\mathfrak c}_{j-1}(s))]
                  +\hat r_j(y),
\]
and
$\|\hat\varpi_j(s)\|\le
C_\varpi\hat\phi_j(\Xi_j(s)+\mathrm{tor}_j)$.
All extracted numbers are real, and
\[
 \hat x_i>1,\qquad |\hat x_i-\mathsf t_i|\le\bar B,
 \qquad |\hat s_i|\le2\bar B_M/\mathsf t_i.
\]

At $t_0<j\le k$ the activities and their pointed terms obey
\begin{align*}
 \|\hat E_{\ge2}^{(j)}\|_{j;a_k^{\rm rad}}
       &\le2C_w^{\rm s}\hat\phi_{j-1},\\
 \|\hat F_0^{(j)}\|_{j;a_k^{\rm rad}}
       &\le2C_w^{\rm s}\hat\phi_{j-1}
                   +C'_{\rm lin}\hat\tau_{j-1}(w;a_k^{\rm rad}).
\end{align*}
For $\|w\|_\sharp<4\varrho$ both are at most
$2(C_w^{\rm s}+4\alpha_0\varrho C'_{\rm lin})\hat\phi_{j-1}$
at the fixed pair radii.  At these sources the full scalar
parts have bound $E_0^{\rm s}$, pointer by pointer at rate
$\kappa+1$.  The chain belongs to $\hat{\mathscr D}_k$ and
$\|\hat\sigma_k(s)\|<B_\sigma\hat\phi_k$.

The activities, chain and source energies are holomorphic on
$\mathscr O_k$.  At zero source they agree with the zero-source
restart.  The latter is defined on both lattices, with
side-independent extracted numbers and the torus agreement of
\cref{C-419-11}(c).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By \cref{C-419-11} this is the source restart of
\cref{C-419-7} with $\zeta=F^{\rm UV}\in[0,B_F]$.
We may therefore apply \cref{C-419-8}.  For $t_0\le j<k$,
$s\in\mathscr O_k\subset\mathscr O_j$, and its restarted
coordinates belong to
$\hat{\mathscr D}_j\subset2\hat{\mathscr D}_j(a_j^{\rm rad})$.
Thus (S1) forms each step with the original source-step
constants.  The step extracts the local mass
$-L^{-(j+1)}\mathsf S_1(\hat\nu_{j+1}\,\cdot)$, the coupling
shift $\hat b_{j+1}a_p$, and the scalar
$\hat e_{j+1}n_{j+1}+\sum_X\hat e_{j+1}(X;s)$.
The identities
\[
 \hat s_{j+1}+\hat\sigma_{j+1}(s)
   =L(\hat s_j+\hat\sigma_j(s))
                        +\hat\nu_{j+1}(\hat{\mathfrak c}_j(s)),
 \qquad
 \hat x_{j+1}=L^{-1}\hat x_j-\hat b_{j+1}
\]
give the displayed form by induction.

This induction is an identity of densities.  If $\hat g_j(s)$
is the density at level $j$, the next one is
\[
 \chi_{j+1}(T_\ell)\,
       \mathsf I[\operatorname{Ber}_j(\operatorname{Ker}_j
                                                  \hat g_j(s))].
\]
The tested chart identity and its image-density assertion
preserve bounded Borel densities.  Apply that assertion
coefficient by coefficient; Berezin integration is a finite sum.
The start has this property by \cref{C-419-11}(a), proving
the exact-image assertion at every level.

At each step the new scalar's source-dependent value at the
trivial pair is extracted.  The only remaining constant is
the zero-source torus correction
\[
 \hat{\mathfrak f}_k
   =\sum_{t_0<j\le k}
       \left(\sum_{X\in\mathcal D_j}
                    \hat{\mathfrak E}_j(X;0)-\hat e_jn_j\right),
\]
which depends on neither fields nor sources; it is zero on
$\mathbb Z^3$.  Source-dependent action coefficients and first
moments stay in the activities.  The usual piecewise mass
extraction consequently gives the displayed zeroth-moment
formula.

Its bound uses only estimates already proved for the restart.
The increments have the local bounds with $B_\nu$, the
constant-chain comparison and the torus defect with
$C_{\rm tor}$, all by (S1).  The physical chain obeys the
same bound with $C_{\rm var}$.  For the constant chain,
\[
 |\hat\sigma_i^{\rm c}(c)|
       \le\tfrac14 C_{\rm var}\hat\phi_i|c|/\varrho
       \le\tfrac14 B_\sigma\hat\phi_i|c|/\varrho,
\]
which supplies the Cauchy estimate in the zeroth-moment
argument of \cite[\S11]{QCDM1}.
Also $|\hat\mu_j|\le3\bar B_M\hat\phi_j$ and the zero-source
torus remainder is at most
$C_{\rm mt}\hat\phi_je^{-2c_{\rm t}\ell/\lambda_j}$.
The omitted polymers are bounded by the (S1) family estimates.
These are precisely the inputs to that argument, so it gives
$C_\varpi\hat\phi_j(\Xi_j+\mathrm{tor}_j)$ with the original
constant.

For the norms at level $k$, note that
$a_{j-1}^{\rm rad}\le a_k^{\rm rad}\le\alpha_0$ and
\[
 C_{\rm lin}\hat\tau_{j-1}(w;a_k^{\rm rad})
 \le\tfrac98\sqrt2L^{-1/2}C_{\rm lin}
                                  \tau_k(w;a_k^{\rm rad})
 <c_{\rm cl}/16.
\]
Thus $\hat{\mathfrak c}_{j-1}(s)$ lies in
$2\hat{\mathscr D}_{j-1}(a_k^{\rm rad})$, and (S1) gives
both displayed bounds.  If $\|w\|_\sharp<4\varrho$, the
coordinate also lies in
$2\hat{\mathscr D}_{j-1}(\alpha_0)$ and
\[
 \hat\tau_{j-1}(w;\alpha_0)
       <8\alpha_0\varrho\hat x_{j-1}^{-1/2}
       \le8\alpha_0\varrho\hat\phi_{j-1}.
\]
Here $40M\operatorname{Lip}w<4\varrho$ and
$\hat x_{j-1}\lambda_{j-1}/\mathsf b\le2$.
This proves the fixed-radius assertions, including the scalar
bound of (S1).

Reality and the windows for $\hat x_i,\hat s_i$ follow from
\cref{C-419-4}(c),(d) at $c=0$ and the real start
$F^{\rm UV}\in[0,B_F]$.  In particular
\[
 \hat x_i\ge\mathsf t_i-\bar B
       \ge(1-L^{-1})\gamma^{-2}>1,
\]
using $\mathsf t_i\ge\mathsf b>\gamma^{-2}\ge L\bar B$
and $\gamma^{-2}\ge4$.
Finally, the source activities and energies are holomorphic
in the coordinates, and the chain is holomorphic on
$\mathscr O_k$, so their compositions are holomorphic there.
The chain vanishes at $s=0$ and its source energies vanish
there.  \Cref{C-419-11}(c) supplies the two-lattice assertions.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Sizes of the differences}

We will add the difference between the ordinary and restarted
flows as an earlier activity.  Besides decay with the distance
from the restart, this requires the precise extraction rule,
the pointed scalar normalization, and estimates summed with
the weights used by later steps.  We verify these in turn.

\begin{definition}[The comparison at a base level]\label{C-428-2}
Use the two-cutoff data with \textup{(k0)}, $u\ge u_*$, and
\[
 e^{-c_{\rm t}L^u}\le L^{-c_\#(s-u)}.
\]
Fix either datum, write its cutoff as $K$, and put
$t_0=K-s$, $t_1=K-u$.  A base level satisfies
$t_0<t_b\le t_1$.  The hatted flow is the restart of
\cref{C-418-9}, with $\hat x_{t_0}=L^s\mathsf b$ and
$\zeta=F^{\rm UV}$.  Its earlier members are zero.
Use the source set
\[
 S_b=\{s=(w,J)\in\mathscr O_{t_1}:\|w\|_\sharp<4\varrho\}.
\]

At level $j$, let $F_j(s)$ and $G_j$ denote the parts with
legs of the new torus activity \emph{before extraction}, at
$\mathfrak c_{j-1}(s)$ and at zero coordinates.  Let
$\tilde G_j^\infty$ be the corresponding zero-source family
on $\mathbb Z^3$, and write
\[
 \mu_j=\mu_j[\tilde G_j^\infty]
\]
for the linear mass extraction functional.  Adding the cube
members $l_\square$ at this number gives $G_j^\infty$.
Hats denote the same objects for the restart, and all five
hatted objects are zero for $j\le t_0$.  Set
\[
 D_j(s)=\max\{\|F_j(s)-\hat F_j(s)\|_j,
               \|G_j-\hat G_j\|_j,
               \|\tilde G_j^\infty-\hat{\tilde G}_j^\infty\|_j\}.
\]
These are the fixed-radius norms on each family's lattice.
Let $\Delta^{(j)}$ be the difference of the activities along
the two source chains, with the scalar value at the trivial
pair subtracted pointer by pointer, as in \cref{C-418-4}.
Use its sizes $r_j^\psi,r_j^0$ from \cref{C-422-3}.

In the estimates of \cref{C-419-6,C-419-7} set
$\Pi_k(c)=\Pi_k(F^{\rm UV};c)$ and define
\[
 X_k=|x_k-\hat x_k|/\mathsf t_k,\qquad
 f_k=\phi(\mathsf t_k)\Pi_k^*+\mathrm{tor}_k
                      \quad(t_0\le k\le t_1),
 \qquad f_k=0\quad(k<t_0).
\]
Thus for $t_0<j\le t_1$,
$m_j^*+\mathrm{tor}_{j-1}=L^{-c_{\rm lm}(j-t_0)}+f_{j-1}$.
\end{definition}
