\begin{definition}[Constants for the difference bounds]\label{C-428-3}
Form the following constants after $\gamma$, in the displayed
order.  They impose no new condition on previously fixed
constants and depend on neither a datum nor a base level:
\begin{align*}
 K_r&=K_\mu^{\rm s}+2(K_\mu-1),\\
 C_\pi&=\tfrac{64}{63}(4B_5+4\bar BB_F)
                          +3(\bar B+4C_w)B_F,\\
 \Theta_\gamma&=\gamma\sup_{v\ge0}(v+1)L^{-v/4}
                (1+v\log L+\log\gamma^{-2})^{9\mathfrak p_0},\\
 C_\Pi^\circ&=2C_\pi+C_{\rm LM}(\Theta_\gamma+1),
 & C_{\rm flo}&=\tfrac12 C_\Pi^\circ+1,\\
 C_{\rm dist}&=\frac{3(1+S_{B'})+\frac94A_D+\frac92C_\Delta}{B_\sigma},
 & A'_{\rm ch}&=A_\psi^\sharp+\tfrac92C_{\rm dist},\\
 C_\Lambda^\psi&=2C_{\rm pc}S_{1/4}
           [\tfrac32K_r+K_rA'_{\rm ch}(\tfrac32+C_{\rm flo})],\\
 C_\Lambda^0&=\tfrac{13}6+\frac1{E_0^{\rm s}}
       \left\{\tfrac98A_{\rm ch}
         (2C_w^{\rm s}+8\alpha_0\varrho C'_{\rm lin})
                         (\tfrac98+\tfrac{13}{12}C_{\rm flo})\right.\\
 &\hspace{25mm}\left.
       +2C_{\mathbf G}^{\rm s}
         [\tfrac98(L(\bar B+4C_w)+L^{1/2}C_{\rm LM})
                  +\tfrac{13}{12}C_{\rm LM}C_{\rm flo}]\right\},\\
 C_\Lambda^\sigma&=
  \frac{\frac98(C_{\rm flo}+S_{B'})+2A_D(1+C_{\rm flo})+2C_\Delta}
       {B_\sigma},\\
 C_\Lambda^w&=\frac{\bar B+4C_w+C_{\rm LM}(1+C_{\rm flo})}{\varrho},\\
 C_\Lambda&=\max\{1,C_\Lambda^\psi,C_\Lambda^0,
                                  C_\Lambda^\sigma,C_\Lambda^w\},
 &p_\Lambda&=0.
\end{align*}
Here $K_\mu^{\rm s}=K_\mu+
\eta_{\min}^{-2}c_{\mathsf S}M^{-3}C_{\rm pw}$ is the
source extraction factor.  The supremum defining
$\Theta_\gamma$ is finite by exponential decay in $v$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Depths and domains]\label{C-428-4}
In the setting of \cref{C-428-2}:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item $t_0\ge s$, $t_b-t_0\le s-u$, and
$k-t_0+1\le s$ for $t_0\le k\le t_1$.
\item $0<c_\#<1/12$ and $c_\#\le c_{\rm lm}$.
\item $\ell\ge2L$ and, for $k\le t_1$,
$\mathrm{tor}_k\le e^{-c_{\rm t}L^u}
                         \le L^{-c_\#(s-u)}$.
\item $12\mathsf t_i/13\le x_i\le14\mathsf t_i/13$ for
$i\le K$, and the same inequalities hold for $\hat x_i$
where it is defined.  Also
$\phi(\mathsf t_i)\le1/2$, $\mathsf t_i^{-1}\le
\phi(\mathsf t_i)^2$, and $\phi(\mathsf t_i)$ increases with
$i$.  Any two of $\phi(\mathsf t_i),\phi_i,\hat\phi_i$
have ratio at most $9/8$, and
\[
 1/(\mathsf t_i\hat\phi_i)
                     \le(14/13)^{1/2}\phi(\mathsf t_i).
\]
\item $S_b$ is open and
$\mathcal P\subset S_b\subset\mathscr O_{t_1}
\subset\mathscr O_k$ for $k\le t_1$.  On $S_b$,
\[
 \Xi_k(s)<2,\quad
 \tau_k(w;\alpha_0)\le8\alpha_0\varrho\phi_k,\quad
 \|\sigma_k(s)\|\le B_\sigma\phi_k.
\]
The ordinary chain lies in
$\mathfrak D_k(\alpha_0)\cap2\mathscr D_k(\alpha_0)$;
the restarted chain lies in
$\hat{\mathscr D}_k\cap2\hat{\mathscr D}_k(\alpha_0)$
for $t_0\le k<t_1$.
\item For $t_0\le i\le j\le t_1$,
\[
 m_i^*\le L^{c_{\rm lm}(j-i)}m_j^*,\qquad
 \Xi_i(s)m_i^*\le\Xi_j(s)m_j^*\quad(s\in\mathscr O_j).
\]
The quantities $\Pi_k(c),\Pi_k^*,
\phi(\mathsf t_k)\Pi_k^*,\mathrm{tor}_k,f_k$ increase with $k$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For the smaller cutoff, $s=\lceil K/[2(6n+11)]\rceil$,
with $1/[2(6n+11)]\le1/34$.  Condition (k0) gives
$s>u\ge1$, hence $s\ge2$, $K\ge35$, and
\[
 K-s\ge33K/34-1\ge K/34+1\ge s.
\]
For the other datum $t_0$ is larger by one.  The remaining
depth inequalities follow from $t_1-t_0=s-u$.

By the choice of $c_\#$, $L^{c_\#}\le11/10$.
Since $L\ge13$, $c_\#<1/12$.  Its weighted-series condition
is the first condition defining $c_{\rm lm}$.  The other
condition holds because
\[
 \tfrac83L^{-1/2}+\tfrac{27}{112}L^{-1}<0.76
 \quad(L\ge13),\qquad (11/10)0.76<9/10.
\]
Both expressions increase with the exponent, and
$c_{\rm lm}$ was chosen maximal.  Therefore
$c_\#\le c_{\rm lm}$.
An admitted side is $2L^m$ with $m\ge1$; for $k\le t_1$,
$\lambda_k\le L^{-u}$.  These give (c).

The coupling windows, $\mathsf t_i\ge\mathsf b>
\gamma^{-2}\ge L\bar B$, and $L\ge13$ give (d)'s first
bounds.  The fixed coupling ceilings make $\phi$ decreasing
on $[\gamma^{-2},\infty)$, with value at most $1/2$ there.
For $x,y\in[12\mathsf t/13,14\mathsf t/13]$,
\[
 \frac{\phi(x)}{\phi(y)}
 \le(7/6)^{1/2}
        \left(1+\frac{\log(7/6)}{18\mathfrak p_0}\right)^{\mathfrak p_0}
 \le(7/6)^{1/2+1/18}<9/8.
\]
The last bound in (d) follows directly from
$\hat x_i\le14\mathsf t_i/13$ and
$(1+\log\hat x_i)^{-\mathfrak p_0}\le1$.

All defining inequalities of $S_b$ are strict and continuous.
On $\mathcal P$, $\|w\|_\sharp<2\varrho$ and
$\mathcal P\subset\mathscr O_K$.  The source-domain
inclusions thus give the first assertions of (e).
The ordinary chain obeys
\[
 C_{\rm lin}\tau_k(w;\alpha_0)<c_{\rm cl}/16,
 \qquad L^{k+1}\|\mathsf n\|<r_M,
 \qquad\|\sigma_i(s)\|\le B_\sigma\phi_i,
\]
which are inside both specified coordinate domains.
The restarted domains follow from
\cref{C-419-8}(S1) and \cref{C-418-9}.

Finally the floor in $m_i^*$ increases with $i$, whereas
its geometric term changes by exactly
$L^{c_{\rm lm}(j-i)}$.  Since the source domains give
$L^{j-i}\Xi_i\le(4/3)^{j-i}\Xi_j$,
\[
 \Xi_im_i^*\le
      ((4/3)L^{c_{\rm lm}-1})^{j-i}\Xi_jm_j^*
      \le\Xi_jm_j^*.
\]
The last inequality uses $c_{\rm lm}\le1/12$ and $L\ge13$.
The other monotonicity statements follow from the formulas
for $\Pi$, $\phi(\mathsf t_k)$, and $\lambda_k$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The mismatch floor]\label{C-428-5}
For $t_0\le k\le t_1$ and $|c|<8\varrho$,
\[
 \Pi_k(c)\le C_\Pi^\circ L^{-c_\#(s-u)},\qquad
 f_k\le C_{\rm flo}L^{-c_\#(s-u)}
                 \le C_{\rm flo}L^{-c_\#(t_b-t_0)}.
\]
For $t_0\le k\le K$,
$\phi(\mathsf t_k)B_k'\le S_{B'}L^{-s/4}$, where
\[
 L^{-s/4}\le L^{-c_{\rm lm}(j-t_0)}\quad(t_0\le j\le t_1),
 \qquad L^{-s/4}\le L^{-c_\#(s-u)}.
\]
For $t_0<k\le t_1$,
\[
 |x_k-\hat x_k|
 \le(\bar B+4C_w)L^{-(k-t_0)}
           +C_{\rm LM}(L^{-(k-t_0)/2}+f_{k-1}).
\]
The same right-hand side bounds $X_k$ also at $k=t_0$.
For $t_0\le k\le t_1$ and $|c|<4\varrho$,
\[
 \mathsf t_k|s_k(c)-\hat s_k(c)|\le\Pi_k^*+B_k'.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The mismatch formula of \cref{C-419-6}(A) at zero label
gives
\begin{align*}
 |\pi(F^{\rm UV};0)-(F^{\rm UV}
                 -F_{<t_0}(t_1;\mathfrak m_{t_1}))|
       &\le2\bar BB_FL^{-(s+1)}/\mathsf b,\\
 |\pi(F^{\rm UV};0)|
       &\le B_5(L^{-t_0}+3L^{-(s-u)})
                   +2\bar BB_FL^{-(s+1)}/\mathsf b.
\end{align*}
It follows that the partial-sum mismatch is at most the first
term on the latter right-hand side plus
$4\bar BB_FL^{-(s+1)}/\mathsf b$.
At any label, $|\mathsf b/(\mathsf b-c)|\le64/63$,
$L^{-t_0}\le L^{-(s-u)}$, and
$L^{-(s+1)}/\mathsf b\le L^{-(s-u)}$.  The same mismatch
formula therefore yields
$|\pi(F^{\rm UV};c)|\le C_\pi L^{-(s-u)}$.

The function $x^{-1/2}(1+\log x)^{9\mathfrak p_0}$
decreases for $x\ge e^{18\mathfrak p_0}$.  Thus
\[
 \varepsilon_s\le\gamma L^{-s/2}
           (1+s\log L+\log\gamma^{-2})^{9\mathfrak p_0},
 \qquad
 (k-t_0+1)\varepsilon_s\le\Theta_\gamma L^{-s/4}.
\]
Insert these bounds in the definition of $\Pi_k$.  Since
$c_\#\le1/8$, all its decays are bounded by
$L^{-c_\#(s-u)}$.  Taking the supremum in $c$, multiplying
by $\phi(\mathsf t_k)\le1/2$ and adding the torus bound of
\cref{C-428-4} proves the assertions about $\Pi_k$ and $f_k$.

For the bound on $B_k'$, write $m=k-t_0\le s$, so
$\mathsf t_k=L^{s-m}\mathsf b$.  Then
\begin{align*}
 \phi(\mathsf t_k)L^{-m}
   &\le\tfrac12L^{-(s+m)/2}
                         (1+(s-m)\log L)^{\mathfrak p_0}\\
   &\le\tfrac12L^{-s/4}L^{-(s-m)/4}
                         (1+(s-m)\log L)^{\mathfrak p_0},\\
 \phi(\mathsf t_k)L^{-(s+1)}/\mathsf b&\le\tfrac12L^{-s}.
\end{align*}
The definition of $B_k'$ and $S_{B'}$ gives the claim.
The two comparisons of decay rates use
$c_{\rm lm}(j-t_0)\le s/12$ and $c_\#(s-u)\le s/8$.

The coupling bound is \cref{C-419-6}(B1), with
$\phi(\mathsf t_{k-1})\le1/2$ and
$\phi(\mathsf t_{k-1})^2\Pi_{k-1}^\flat\le f_{k-1}$.
Since $\mathsf t_k\ge1$ it also bounds $X_k$.
At $k=t_0$, $X_{t_0}\le\bar B$ directly from the windows.
For the mass bound apply \cref{C-419-8}(S4) to the constant
source $(c,0)\in\mathscr O_{t_1}$: its first term is exactly
the displayed constant-label mass difference.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Extraction and the form of the differences}

\begin{lemma}[Boundedness of the extraction rule]\label{C-428-6}
Let $1\le j\le K$.  Suppose that the data $(F,G,\nu)$ obey
the free-family rule (f2) of \cref{C-422-3}, at the fine mass
matrix of a source in $\mathscr O_{j-1}$.  Let
$\tilde G^\infty$ be an even infinite-lattice family of
degrees at least two and finite norm.  Assume (f3) for the
family $G^\infty$ obtained by adding its cube members
$l_\square$ at $\nu=\mu_j[\tilde G^\infty]$.
If $\Delta_{\ge2}$ is formed from these data by (f2), then
\[
 c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2|\nu|
                   \le(K_\mu-1)\|\tilde G^\infty\|_j,
 \qquad
 r^\psi(\Delta)\le K_r
       \max\{\|F\|_j,\|G\|_j,\|\tilde G^\infty\|_j\}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The functional $\mu_j[E]$ is $-\eta_j^{-2}$ times the
normalized trace of the cell average of the row sums of the
degree-two kernel of $E$ at the trivial configuration.
Condition (f3) gives translation covariance of
$\tilde G^\infty$ and invariance under the common flavour
phase.  The latter excludes the $\Psi\Psi$ and
$\bar\Psi\bar\Psi$ parts, since their phases are
$e^{2i\alpha}$ and $e^{-2i\alpha}$.  The row-sum estimate
used in the mass extraction of \cite[\S9]{QCDM1} therefore
applies: these two properties are its only symmetry inputs.
It bounds the normalized trace by
$C_{am}^\psi(8N_fh_F^2)^{-1}\|E\|_j$.
Since $\eta_j^2\ge c_b^2$ and
$K_\mu=1+c_{\mathsf S}C_{am}^\psi c_b^{-2}/(8N_f)$,
this proves the first inequality.

The extraction rule is
\[
 \Delta_{\ge2}(Z)=F(Z)
       +\sum_{(X,p):Z_p=Z}\sum_zP_{z;X,p}
       +1_{\{Z=\square\}}
                    \left(l_\square+\sum_{z\in\square}P_z^\nu\right),
\]
where
\[
 P_{z;X,p}=-\mathfrak s_j^{-1}a_{X,p}(z)L^{-j}
                                \mathsf S_1(1_z\psi^{\rm bg}),
 \qquad
 a_{X,p}=\operatorname{ord}_0 k_{X,p}(F)
                       -\operatorname{ord}_0 k_{X,p}(G).
\]
A form supported on the block of one site $z$ has norm
\[
 \|L^{-j}\mathsf S_1(N1_z\psi^{\rm bg})\|
                         \le c_{\mathsf S}M^{-3}h_F^2\|N\|.
\]
This is the cube estimate with $\nu_PL^{3j}$ places in
place of $\nu_PM^3L^{3j}$; the same background bound holds
at the admitted fine mass matrix.

For clarity, the piece count also applies to the present
data, without assuming that they are an RG output.  For any
even element $E(X)$ its degree-two coefficients satisfy
\[
 \sum_{n,n',x,x'}h^{(j)}(n)h^{(j)}(n')
       \|g_X^{nn'}(x,x')\|_{\rm tr}\le\|E(X)\|.
\]
Each homogeneous part has norm at most that of $E(X)$.
The two localized legs use the same walks for $F$ and $G$,
with the original $A_\kappa,C_H$ bounds: at a source in
$\mathscr O_{j-1}$,
$L^j\|\mathsf n\|=L\lambda_{j-1}\|J\|_\infty<r_M$.
The walk counts $C_{\rm wk}$ and $3C_{\rm wk}$ therefore give
\begin{align*}
 \sum_p\sum_y\|a_{X,p}(y)\|
                e^{\kappa(d_j(Z_p)-d_j(X))}
 &\le CA_\kappa^2h_F^{-2}(\|F(X)\|+\|G(X)\|),\\
 \sum_{Z_p\supset\square}\sum_z\|a_{X,p}(z)\|
                e^{\kappa d_j(Z_p)}
 &\le C_{\rm pw}h_F^{-2}\max\{\|F\|_j,\|G\|_j\}.
\end{align*}
The factor two is included in $C_{\rm pw}$.  Combining this
with $\mathfrak s_j^{-1}\le\eta_{\min}^{-2}$ bounds the
piece forms by
$(K_\mu^{\rm s}-K_\mu)\max\{\|F\|_j,\|G\|_j\}$.

The cube member has
$\|l_\square\|\le c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2|\nu|$.
Each $P_z^\nu$ is the difference of two one-block forms,
at $\mathsf n$ and zero; summing over the cube gives
$\sum_{z\in\square}\|P_z^\nu\|
\le2c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2|\nu|$.
A single cube has weight one.  Thus the sum of the summand
norms of $\Delta_{\ge2}$ is at most
\[
 \|F\|_j+(K_\mu^{\rm s}-K_\mu)
           \max\{\|F\|_j,\|G\|_j\}
                  +3c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2|\nu|.
\]
The first inequality of the lemma makes this at most $K_r$
times the stated maximum, since
$1+K_\mu^{\rm s}-K_\mu+3(K_\mu-1)=K_r$.
The other three entries in $r^\psi$ are bounded respectively
by $K_\mu$, $K_\mu$, and $K_\mu-1$ times the same maximum.
All are at most $K_r$ times it.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The differences are admissible free families]\label{C-428-7}
For $s\in S_b$ and $j\le t_b$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item Every pointed term $\Delta^{(j)}(X;\cdot;s;z)$ is even,
jointly gauge invariant, local in $X$, Borel in the pair, and
holomorphic on the regular complex pairs of radii
$\alpha_0,\alpha_1$.  It is holomorphic in $s\in S_b$.
It is invariant under $\mathrm U(N_f)\times\mathrm U(N_f)$
acting jointly on the fields and sources:
\[
 V=e_+\otimes V_1+e_-\otimes V_2,\qquad
 (w,J,\Psi_n^{\rm bg},\bar\Psi_n^{\rm bg})
 \longmapsto
 (w,VJV^{-1},V\Psi_n^{\rm bg},\bar\Psi_n^{\rm bg}V^{-1}).
\]
In particular the common phase fixes each source and leaves
the pointed term invariant.  Its scalar part vanishes at the
trivial pair and obeys the pointed sum rule.
\item It is a free family in the sense of \cref{C-422-3}.
Its part with legs is formed by (f2) from
\[
 (F_j(s)-\hat F_j(s),G_j-\hat G_j,\mu_j-\hat\mu_j),
\]
with (f3) for $G_j^\infty-\hat G_j^\infty$.  Moreover
\[
 \mu_j-\hat\mu_j
       =\mu_j[\tilde G_j^\infty-\hat{\tilde G}_j^\infty].
\]
For $j\le t_0$ these are simply the ordinary flow's data.
\item The scalar removed from the differences obeys
$d_b(s)=d_b(0)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Both ordinary and restarted activities are evaluated inside
their fixed-radius coordinate domains by \cref{C-428-4}(e).
The source step and \cref{C-419-8}(S1) give the stated
properties for the unpointed activities.  We check the
pointed terms, as their scalar normalization is needed below.

For the terms pointed at a fermion place $p$, the insertion
of an element $F=\sum_nF_n$ is
\[
 F_p=\sum_{n\ge1}n^{-1}\mathsf N_pF_n.
\]
It preserves degree, vanishes unless $p$ carries a leg, and
commutes with every linear change of the fibre at each
place.  In particular it commutes with gauge transformations
and with the joint flavour operation on the coordinates.
The pointed output is the integral over $t\in[0,1]$ of the
$\vartheta$ derivative at zero of the expansion with leg
potential $t\mathcal V_\psi+\vartheta(\mathcal V_\psi)_p$.
For complex $|t|<9/8$, $|\vartheta|<1$ the potential bound is
\[
 \varepsilon_{\rm V}+\varepsilon_\natural
                         \le49c_{\rm cl}/64<c_{\rm cl}.
\]
Thus the expansion is holomorphic in these variables,
the coordinates and the pair.  Gauge covariance follows
from the expansion's gauge identity.  For flavour, each
Gaussian and Berezin integral in the series is unchanged
under the contragredient unitary pair $V,V^{-1}$, which
preserves the fibre norms and maps each cube to itself.
It also conjugates the tower and the potential, term by
term, at the transformed coordinates.  The two absolutely
convergent series therefore correspond term by term.
Differentiation and integration preserve both identities.
The output depends only on the potential pieces and
localized covariances within $X$; if $p\notin X$ its
$\vartheta$ derivative is zero.  This proves locality and
both invariances for the place-pointed terms.

The remaining pointed terms have the same properties for
explicit reasons.  The bond terms and gauge normalizers
are local, separately gauge invariant scalar terms of the
step.  Their earlier scalar inputs are flavour invariant
by induction.  A diagonal block $N_p(X,\mathsf U)$ of a
closed fermion loop is a sum of traces of walk products
within $X$, at the fine mass matrix.  Gauge transformations
conjugate every walk and average, and commute with that
matrix.  At the diagonal place $p$ their trace is unchanged.
The subtracted trivial-field term is independent of the
configuration.  Flavour conjugates these operators by $V$,
so also preserves their traces, numbers per site and
wrapping shares.

The extracted cube forms and $P_{z;X,p}$ are forms
$\bar\psi^{\rm bg}N\psi^{\rm bg}$ with colour-scalar
matrices.  Under flavour their matrices become $VNV^{-1}$,
because the degree-two kernels and background maps have
that covariance.  They are consequently jointly invariant.
The pointed action members are
\[
 -L^jb_j\upsilon_z(\mathsf p)a_{\mathsf p}(\mathsf U),\qquad
 a_{\mathsf p}(\mathsf U)=1-\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}
                                         \partial\mathsf U(\mathsf p).
\]
Their polymer contains the four bonds of $\mathsf p$;
$\upsilon_z(\mathsf p)$ is one quarter the number of its
corners in the block of $z$ and sums to one over $z$.
These scalar terms are local, holomorphic, gauge invariant,
source independent and zero at the trivial pair.  The same
argument uses $\hat b_j$ in the restart.

Every listed term is holomorphic in the source coordinates:
the step output and its pointed variations by the admitted
expansion, and the loop blocks, piece coefficients and
cube forms by holomorphy of the tower and background maps
on the fine-mass domain.  Composing with the two holomorphic
chains proves holomorphy on $S_b$.  The pair dependence is
holomorphic, hence continuous and Borel.

The source set is invariant under $J\mapsto VJV^{-1}$:
the values remain in the specified matrix span and their
operator norm is unchanged.  The chain transforms in the
same way, by induction on its increments; the restarted
initial mass is scalar at each site.  Thus joint coordinate
invariance becomes joint source invariance on the chain.
For the common phase $V=e^{i\alpha}1$, $J$ itself is fixed.
Taking differences and subtracting the scalar values at the
trivial pair preserves all these linear identities and the
pointed sum rule.  This proves (a) and the scalar part of (b).

For the part with legs, both flows use the rule (f2).
The ordinary input is $(F_j(s),G_j,\mu_j)$ and the
restarted input is its hatted counterpart.  All these
families are invariant under the common phase.  At zero
coordinates the forms $P_{z;X,p}$ and $P_z^\nu$ vanish,
since $a_{X,p}=0$ and $\mathsf n=0$.  Thus the
infinite-lattice family after extraction is precisely
$\tilde G_j^\infty$ plus its cube terms $l_\square$.
It is translation covariant summand by summand, and its
torus part which does not wrap is the part which fits.

Its cell sums vanish as matrices.  Indeed the zero-source
family lies in the linear symmetry space preserved by
extraction; its cell sum is
$M^3\mathsf{cf}_m\,1$, and extracting
$\mu_j[\tilde G_j^\infty]$ makes $\mathsf{cf}_m=0$.
The same conclusion holds for the restart by the verified
symmetry-space induction in \cref{C-419-4}, with its own
mass functional and extracted number.  Thus both satisfy
(f3), including matrix cancellation rather than only
cancellation of a trace.

Their pieces, walks, trees, paths, cells and hulls are the
same: these choices are independent of the activity and
the pair, and the two flows share the tower and background
maps at the fine mass matrix $m_0-a_K\hat J$ and at zero
source.  The extraction rule and the functional $\mu_j$
are linear with these choices fixed.  Taking differences
therefore gives exactly the data in (b).  All conditions
of (f3), including the matrix cell cancellation, are
closed linear conditions and pass to the difference.
For $j\le t_0$ the hatted family is zero.  The resulting
data and family are holomorphic in $s$ by the preceding
coordinate argument.

Finally the scalar values at the trivial pair at level
$j$ sum to
$\sum_X\mathfrak E_j(X;0)-e_jn_j$ for the ordinary flow,
and to its hatted counterpart for the restart.  Neither
depends on the source.  The finite sum defining $d_b(s)$
is therefore $d_b(0)$, proving (c).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Differences before extraction]\label{C-428-8}
For $t_0<j\le t_1$ and $s\in S_b$,
\begin{align*}
 \|G_j-\hat G_j\|_j,
 \|\tilde G_j^\infty-\hat{\tilde G}_j^\infty\|_j
       &\le2C_w^{\rm s}A_\psi^\sharp m_j\phi_{j-1},\\
 \|F_j(s)-\hat F_j(s)\|_j
       &\le2C_w^{\rm s}A'_{\rm ch}
                           (m_j^*+\mathrm{tor}_{j-1})\phi_{j-1}.
\end{align*}
In particular,
\[
 D_j(s)\le2C_w^{\rm s}A'_{\rm ch}
            (L^{-c_{\rm lm}(j-t_0)}+f_{j-1})\phi_{j-1}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
At zero coordinates, (S2) of \cref{C-419-8} applies on
both lattices and before extraction, giving the first
two estimates.  At the physical chains, put
$\mathfrak c=\mathfrak c_{j-1}(s)$ and
$\hat{\mathfrak c}=\hat{\mathfrak c}_{j-1}(s)$, and split
\begin{align*}
 F_j(s)-\hat F_j(s)
 ={}&[\tilde E_{\ge2}^{(j)}(\mathfrak c)
          -\hat{\tilde E}_{\ge2}^{(j)}(\mathfrak c^\wedge)]\\
 &+[\hat{\tilde E}_{\ge2}^{(j)}(\mathfrak c^\wedge)
          -\hat{\tilde E}_{\ge2}^{(j)}(\hat{\mathfrak c})].
\end{align*}
The first bracket is the equal-coordinate difference.
Since $\mathfrak c\in\mathfrak D_{j-1}(\alpha_0)$,
(S2) bounds it by $2C_w^{\rm s}A_\psi^\sharp m_j\phi_{j-1}$.

The second bracket changes only the mass coordinates.
Set
\[
 T=\max_{t_0\le i<j}
       \frac{\|\sigma_i(s)-\hat\sigma_i(s)\|}{B_\sigma\hat\phi_i}.
\]
At a bare site $x$, write this difference as the change
of the total mass $s_i+\sigma_i(s)(x)$ minus $s_i-\hat s_i$.
By (S4) and \cref{C-428-5}, its magnitude is at most
\[
 2(\Pi_i^*+B_i')/\mathsf t_i
      +A_D\phi_i\Xi_i(s)m_i^*
      +C_\Delta\phi_i\mathrm{tor}_i\|w\|_\infty/\varrho.
\]
Divide by $B_\sigma\hat\phi_i$.  Use
\cref{C-428-4,C-428-5}, in particular
\begin{gather*}
 \phi(\mathsf t_i)\Pi_i^*\le m_j^*,
 \quad\phi(\mathsf t_i)B_i'\le S_{B'}m_j^*,
 \quad\Xi_i(s)m_i^*\le2m_j^*,\\
 \phi_i/\hat\phi_i\le9/8,
 \quad 2(14/13)^{1/2}<3,
 \quad\|w\|_\infty<4\varrho.
\end{gather*}
This gives
\[
 T\le\frac{3(1+S_{B'})+\frac94A_D}{B_\sigma}m_j^*
       +\frac{9C_\Delta}{2B_\sigma}\mathrm{tor}_{j-1}
       \le C_{\rm dist}(m_j^*+\mathrm{tor}_{j-1}).
\]

If $T=0$ the second bracket vanishes.  For $T>0$, the
function
\[
 f(z)=\hat{\tilde E}_{\ge2}^{(j)}
                (\hat{\mathfrak c}+z(\mathfrak c^\wedge
                                           -\hat{\mathfrak c}))
\]
is holomorphic for $|z|<1/T$.  Its mass coordinates have
norm less than $2B_\sigma\hat\phi_i$ there, while $w$ and
$\mathsf n$ are unchanged.  The domain is thus contained
in $2\hat{\mathscr D}_{j-1}(\alpha_0)$, and (S1) gives
$\|f(z)\|_j\le2C_w^{\rm s}\hat\phi_{j-1}$.
For $T\le1/2$, Cauchy's formula on $1<r<1/T$ gives
\[
 \|f(1)-f(0)\|_j
 \le\frac{2C_w^{\rm s}\hat\phi_{j-1}}{r-1}
 \longrightarrow\frac{T}{1-T}\,2C_w^{\rm s}\hat\phi_{j-1}
 \le2T\,2C_w^{\rm s}\hat\phi_{j-1}.
\]
If $T>1/2$, both endpoints still belong to that coordinate
domain, because
$\|\sigma_i(s)\|\le(9/8)B_\sigma\hat\phi_i$.
Their separate bounds give at most
$4T\,2C_w^{\rm s}\hat\phi_{j-1}$.
In both cases $\hat\phi_{j-1}\le(9/8)\phi_{j-1}$ bounds
the second bracket by
$(9/2)T\,2C_w^{\rm s}\phi_{j-1}$.
Adding the first bracket gives the result with
$A'_{\rm ch}=A_\psi^\sharp+(9/2)C_{\rm dist}$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Summing the differences over levels}

\begin{proposition}[The sizes at each level]\label{C-428-9}
Let $t_0<t_b\le t_1$ and $s=(w,J)\in\mathcal P$.
For $j\le t_0$,
\[
 r_j^\psi(s)\le2K_rC_w^{\rm s}\phi_{j-1},\qquad
 r_j^0(s)\le2E_0^{\rm s}.
\]
For $t_0<j\le t_b$,
\begin{align*}
 c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2|\mu_j-\hat\mu_j|
   &\le(K_\mu-1)A_\psi^\sharp m_j\,2C_w^{\rm s}\phi_{j-1},\\
 r_j^\psi(s)&\le K_rA'_{\rm ch}
    (L^{-c_{\rm lm}(j-t_0)}+f_{j-1})\,2C_w^{\rm s}\phi_{j-1},\\
 r_j^0(s)&\le\tfrac98A_{\rm ch}
    (2C_w^{\rm s}+8\alpha_0\varrho C'_{\rm lin})
    (L^{-c_{\rm lm}(j-t_0)}+f_{j-1})
                             +2C_{\mathbf G}^{\rm s}X_{j-1}.
\end{align*}
The remaining mass field and coupling weight at the base obey
\[
 \|\delta_{t_b}(s)\|\le C_\Lambda^\sigma B_\sigma
                  L^{-c_\#(t_b-t_0)}\phi_{t_b},\qquad
 |\hat w_b|\le C_\Lambda^w\varrho L^{-c_\#(t_b-t_0)}.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For $j\le t_0$ the restarted family is zero.  Each of
$F_j(s),G_j,\tilde G_j^\infty$ is a summand of an ordinary
activity after extraction.  The ordinary source estimates
bound the sums of their norms by
$(2C_w^{\rm s}-C_w)\phi_{j-1}\le2C_w^{\rm s}\phi_{j-1}$.
Apply \cref{C-428-6} to these data.  The scalar norm is
bounded by $E_0^{\rm s}$ before subtracting the trivial
value and by $2E_0^{\rm s}$ after that subtraction.

For $j>t_0$, \cref{C-428-7} identifies the data as
differences and \cref{C-428-6} gives
\[
 c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2|\mu_j-\hat\mu_j|
 \le(K_\mu-1)
          \|\tilde G_j^\infty-\hat{\tilde G}_j^\infty\|_j,
 \qquad r_j^\psi\le K_rD_j.
\]
\Cref{C-428-8} proves the two corresponding estimates.

For the scalar terms, the gauge normalizers and
$\mathbf c_j$ depend on the common calibration and are
their values at zero source.  The fermion loop normalizers
use the common tower at $m_0-a_K\hat J$; their constant
wrapping shares are those of zero source.  Both flows use
the same pointing rule.  These terms therefore agree
pointer by pointer, as in \cref{C-419-10}(b).
There are also numbers $d(X,z)$ attached to the ratio
$x_{j-1}/\mathsf t_{j-1}$, and hatted numbers attached to
$\hat x_{j-1}/\mathsf t_{j-1}$.  Their difference is
independent of the fields and source, so disappears when
the trivial value is subtracted.
Only $\delta^{\rm ch}F_0^{(j)}$ and
$\mathbf G^{(j)}-\hat{\mathbf G}^{(j)}$ remain.  Before
the subtraction their pointed scalar bounds are
\begin{gather*}
 A_{\rm ch}(m_j^*+\mathrm{tor}_{j-1})
      (2C_w^{\rm s}+8\alpha_0\varrho C'_{\rm lin})\phi_{j-1},\\
 C_{\mathbf G}^{\rm s}X_{j-1}.
\end{gather*}
The latter holds at rate $\kappa_+\ge\kappa+1$.
Subtracting the trivial value doubles these bounds.
Since $2\phi_{j-1}\le(9/4)\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})\le9/8$,
this is the estimate for $r_j^0$.

At the base, (S4) gives at each bare site
\[
 |\delta_{t_b}(s)(x)|
 \le\frac{\Pi_{t_b}^*+B_{t_b}'}{\mathsf t_{t_b}}
   +A_D\phi_{t_b}\Xi_{t_b}(s)m_{t_b}^*
   +C_\Delta\phi_{t_b}\mathrm{tor}_{t_b}
                                     \frac{\|w\|_\infty}{\varrho}.
\]
The first term is at most
$\frac98(C_{\rm flo}+S_{B'})
L^{-c_\#(s-u)}\phi_{t_b}$ by
\cref{C-428-4,C-428-5}.  On $\mathcal P$,
$\Xi_{t_b}<2$ and $\|w\|_\infty<2\varrho$.
Use
\[
 m_{t_b}^*\le L^{-c_\#(t_b-t_0)}
                  +C_{\rm flo}L^{-c_\#(s-u)},
 \qquad\mathrm{tor}_{t_b}\le L^{-c_\#(s-u)}.
\]
The three terms add to the claimed bound with
$C_\Lambda^\sigma$.
Finally
$\hat w_b=L^{-(K-t_b)}(x_{t_b}-\hat x_{t_b})$.
The coupling estimate of \cref{C-428-5}, the floor bound,
and $L^{-(K-t_b)}\le1$ give
\[
 |\hat w_b|\le
 [\bar B+4C_w+C_{\rm LM}(1+C_{\rm flo})]
                               L^{-c_\#(t_b-t_0)},
\]
which is the stated result.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The lag sums]\label{C-428-10}
Let $\Lambda_b^{-1}=C_\Lambda L^{-c_\#(t_b-t_0)}$.
For $s\in\mathcal P$ and $t_b\le k\le K$,
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{j\le t_b}\omega_{k+1-j}r_j^\psi(s)
   &\le C_\Lambda^\psi C_w^{\rm s}
                         L^{-c_\#(t_b-t_0)}\phi_k
    \le\Lambda_b^{-1}C_w^{\rm s}\phi_k,\tag{L1}\\
 \sum_{j\le t_b}L^{-(k-j)}r_j^0(s)
   &\le\sum_{j\le t_b}L^{-(t_b-j)}r_j^0(s)
    \le C_\Lambda^0E_0^{\rm s}L^{-c_\#(t_b-t_0)}
    \le\Lambda_b^{-1}E_0^{\rm s},\tag{L2}\\
 \|\delta_{t_b}(s)\|&\le\Lambda_b^{-1}B_\sigma\phi_{t_b},
 \qquad |\hat w_b|\le\Lambda_b^{-1}\varrho.\tag{L3}
\end{align*}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For $n=k+1-j$ the power-counting inequality is
\[
 \omega_n\phi_{j-1}
      \le C_{\rm pc}L^{-n/4}(1+n)^{\mathfrak p_0}\phi_k.
\]
The definition of $c_\#$ gives, for every $N\ge1$,
\[
 \sum_{n\ge N}L^{-n/4}(1+n)^{\mathfrak p_0}
   \le L^{-c_\#N}
          \sum_{n\ge1}L^{-n(1/4-c_\#)}(1+n)^{\mathfrak p_0}
   \le\tfrac32S_{1/4}L^{-c_\#N}.
\]
For $j\le t_0$, $n\ge k+1-t_0>t_b-t_0$, so these
levels contribute at most
\[
 2K_rC_w^{\rm s}C_{\rm pc}\tfrac32S_{1/4}
                          L^{-c_\#(t_b-t_0)}\phi_k.
\]
For $t_0<j\le t_b$, the geometric term satisfies
\[
 L^{-c_{\rm lm}(j-t_0)}
      \le L^{-c_\#(k+1-t_0)}L^{c_\# n}.
\]
Its convolution is therefore at most
$\frac32 S_{1/4}C_{\rm pc}
L^{-c_\#(t_b-t_0)}\phi_k$ before the factor
$2K_rA'_{\rm ch}C_w^{\rm s}$.
The floor is at most
$C_{\rm flo}L^{-c_\#(t_b-t_0)}$, and its convolution
uses the unmodified sum $S_{1/4}$.  Adding these three
contributions gives exactly $C_\Lambda^\psi$ and (L1).

For (L2), the first inequality follows from $k\ge t_b$.
The levels $j\le t_0$ contribute at most
\[
 2E_0^{\rm s}\frac L{L-1}L^{-(t_b-t_0)}
           \le\tfrac{13}6E_0^{\rm s}L^{-c_\#(t_b-t_0)}.
\]
For the later levels, \cref{C-428-5} gives
\[
 X_{j-1}\le[L(\bar B+4C_w)+L^{1/2}C_{\rm LM}]
                       L^{-c_\#(j-t_0)}
       +C_{\rm LM}C_{\rm flo}L^{-c_\#(t_b-t_0)}.
\]
This includes $j-1=t_0$.  The geometric and constant
parts are summed using
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{t_0<j\le t_b}L^{-(t_b-j)}L^{-c_\#(j-t_0)}
       &\le\tfrac98L^{-c_\#(t_b-t_0)},\\
 \sum_{t_0<j\le t_b}L^{-(t_b-j)}&\le\tfrac{13}{12}.
\end{align*}
Indeed $L^{1-c_\#}\ge13^{11/12}\ge9$.
Substitution into the scalar bound of \cref{C-428-9}
gives the braces in $C_\Lambda^0$.  Adding the earlier
levels proves (L2).  Part (L3) is the last assertion of
\cref{C-428-9}, since the four constants are bounded by
$C_\Lambda$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Loss of memory as an admissible perturbation]
\label{C-418-10}
In the two-cutoff setting, assume \textup{(k0)}, $u\ge u_*$
and $e^{-c_{\rm t}L^u}\le L^{-c_\#(s-u)}$.
At every base level $t_0<t_b\le t_1$, the differences
$\Delta^{(j)}$, $j\le t_b$, satisfy the format conditions
of \cref{C-418-4}, with the free-family data of
\cref{C-428-2}.  Their removed scalar $d_b(s)$ is constant
on $\mathcal P$, and their lag sums hold with
\[
 \Lambda_b^{-1}=C_\Lambda L^{-c_\#(t_b-t_0)}.
\]
Thus one may take $p_\Lambda=0$.  At the base $t_1$,
\[
 \Lambda_{t_1}=C_\Lambda^{-1}L^{c_\#(s-u)}=\Lambda,
\]
with $\Lambda$ as in \cref{C-418-6}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
\Cref{C-428-7} gives the pointed format and the free-family
data on the open set $S_b\supset\mathcal P$, as well as
$d_b(s)=d_b(0)$.  The joint flavour map preserves the
interior of $\mathcal P$: it preserves its defining norms,
is linear and continuous, and has the continuous inverse
with $V^{-1}$.  This verifies the precise source-domain
clause in the format.  \Cref{C-428-10} gives the three
lag sums with the sizes of these actual data.  Finally
$t_1-t_0=s-u$ in either datum and $p_\Lambda=0$, so the
base value is exactly the displayed $\Lambda$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Continuing the restart to the last level}

The zero-source restart can be continued beyond $t_1$ to
level $K$.  We need this continuation for two reasons: its
last-level integral gives a positive lower bound for the
normalizing total, and its histories bound the error from
leaving the small-field region after the restart.

\begin{definition}[Histories above the restart]\label{C-427-2}
Use the model and constants of \cref{C-418-2}, including the
two conditions on the gauge tests in the construction.
Let $0<g\le\gamma$, $\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)$ and
$(\mathsf b,\mathsf m)\in\mathsf W(g)$; assume (k0).
For either cutoff write $1\le u<s<K$, $t_0=K-s$,
$t_1=K-u$, $\mathsf t_i=L^{K-i}\mathsf b$,
$\beta=L^K\mathsf b$, and $m_0=L^{-K}\mathsf m$.
All gauge data and the fermion tower are those of this
datum.  Put $\mathcal Y=\mathcal V_{t_0}$, with product
Haar probability measure $dW$, and
$W_k=\mathcal M^{k-t_0}W$.
Write $\mathcal V_k^\chi=\{\chi_k(T_\ell)=1\}$.

The start is
\[
 \hat\tau_{t_0}(dW)=\chi_{t_0}(T_\ell)(W)
 \exp[-\beta A(\mathsf U)
       -\langle\bar\Psi,\mathbb D_{t_0}(\mathsf U)\Psi\rangle
       -L^{-t_0}\hat s_{t_0}\mathsf S_1(\psi^{\rm bg})]\,dW,
\]
where $\mathsf U=\mathsf U_{t_0}(W)$,
$\hat s_{t_0}=F^{\rm UV}/\mathsf t_{t_0}$ and
$\psi^{\rm bg}=\mathcal H_{h_\emptyset}\Psi$.
It has $\hat x_{t_0}=\mathsf t_{t_0}$, $\hat E_{t_0}=0$,
and no activity, normalizer or number of a level $\le t_0$.
Let $\hat{\mathbb D}(W)$ be the quadratic form in its
Grassmann exponent, and put
\[
 \hat F(W)=e^{-\beta A(\mathsf U)}\det\hat{\mathbb D}(W),
 \qquad \hat\nu=\chi_{t_0}(T_\ell)\hat F\,dW.
\]

Let $\hat\tau_k$ be the restarted small-field term at
level $k$, with numbers $\hat x_i,\hat s_i,
\hat e_i,\hat b_i,\hat\mu_i$ and
$\hat E_k=\sum_{t_0<j\le k}\hat e_jn_j$.
If $\mathbf1_j$ is the indicator that all tests pass in
the step from level $j$ and $\mathfrak G_j\ge0$ its
gauge-fixing factor, set
\[
 \hat{\mathsf k}^{(k)}(W)
       =\prod_{t_0\le j<k}(\mathbf1_j\mathfrak G_j)(W_j).
\]
The histories above the restart are
$\mathcal H_k^{(t_0)}=
\{h\in\mathcal H_k:h|_{t_0}=h_\emptyset^{(t_0)}\}$.
Their terms are the images of $\hat\tau_{t_0}$ under
their subsequent weights, partial kernels and partial
Berezin integrals.  Denote their densities against
$\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}$ by $\hat{\mathsf g}_h$, and their
fully Berezin-integrated masses by $\hat t(h)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[The start and the field cut]\label{C-427-3}
Every $W\in\mathcal V_{t_0}^\chi$ has
\[
 \varpi(W)<2\varepsilon(\mathsf t_{t_0})
              \le\varepsilon_{\mathcal W}\alpha_0\le\bar\varepsilon.
\]
Its background exists, and
$\mathsf{wab}(L^s\mathsf b,W)=\beta A(\mathsf U_{t_0}(W))$.
Consequently the zero-source start of \cref{C-418-3} is
$\hat\tau_{t_0}$.  If $L^u\mathsf b\ge\Theta_\star$, the
two-lattice gauge comparison is admitted and
\[
 \mathcal V_{t_0}^\chi\subset\mathsf{In}_{t_0}
                           \subset\mathsf{Cut}_{(t_0)}.
\]
The same action identity holds on the field cut.
Moreover
\[
 \mathbf1_{t_0}\chi_{t_0}(T_\ell)=\mathbf1_{t_0},
 \qquad
 \mathbf1_{t_0}1_{\mathsf{Cut}_{(t_0)}}=\mathbf1_{t_0}
                       \quad(L^u\mathsf b\ge\Theta_\star).
\]
These identities also hold with the weight
$\hat{\mathsf k}^{(t_1)}=\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet$ in place
of $\mathbf1_{t_0}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The tested-field estimate, applied at level $t_0-1$, gives
the displayed plaquette bound.  The lattice is large at
that level: (k0) has $K^{\mathrm A}\ge3$, and the two
lattices of the gauge comparison are large at levels
$K^{\mathrm A}-1$ and $K^{\mathrm A}$ respectively.
Their calibrated frames therefore admit the minimizing
background at $t_0$.  The weighted action is
$A^{\eta_{t_0}}(\mathsf c,U)=L^{t_0}\sum_p\mathsf c(p)a_p(U)$,
constant on the minimal orbit.  At
$\mathsf c=L^s\mathsf b$ it is $\beta A(U)$.
This also identifies the tested start, including its
fine mass, mass member, tower and Haar measure.

When $L^u\mathsf b\ge\Theta_\star$, the gauge comparison
with top level $t_1$ gives its inner set
$\mathsf{In}_{t_0}=\{\varpi<2\varepsilon(\mathsf t_{t_0})\}$
and its inclusion in the field cut.  This proves the
assertion about the cut and the action there.
The first small-field step contains the tests
\[
 \chi_{t_0+1}(T_\ell)(\mathcal MW),
       \mathsf q_{t_0}^0(W),
       \mathsf q_{t_0+1}(W),
       \chi_{\mathsf t_{t_0}}^{\rm sf}(W),
\]
where $\mathsf q_{t_0}^0=1$ since $t_0\ge1$.
The density-test descent property of these calibrated
tests gives $\chi_{t_0}(T_\ell)(W)=1$ whenever this
product is one.  The thresholds satisfy the descent
conditions because the construction imposes, with
\(\varepsilon_\gamma=A_0\gamma
                  (\log\gamma^{-2})^{\mathfrak p_0}\),
\[
 \varepsilon_\gamma\le
        \min\{\bar\varepsilon/2,\varepsilon_\flat\},
 \qquad C_{\rm reg}\varepsilon_\gamma\le
        \min\{\varepsilon_{\rm v},
               L^{-2}c_2^{\rm SO},L^{-2}\bar\varepsilon/2\}.
\]
The remaining strip-comparison and density-descent
bounds are precisely \cite[eqs. (1008), (1011),
(1025), (1030), Props. 53.7 and 53.13]{YMM1};
their uniform admission is checked in
\cite[proof of Lem. 82.5]{YMM1}.
Since \(\varepsilon(\mathsf t_j)\le\varepsilon_\gamma\)
and the calibrated geometry is admitted at every step,
these bounds apply to the present frames. This proves the first
indicator identity; the inclusion just proved gives the
second.  The product weight contains this first-step
indicator, so has the same identities.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The zero-source continuation]\label{C-427-4}
The restart is defined to level $K$, on the given torus,
every admitted torus with the same other data, and
$\mathbb Z^3$.  Its activities satisfy the original
locality, symmetry, holomorphy and scalar-array conditions,
and the closed bounds
\[
 \|\hat F_0^{(j)}\|_j\le C_w\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1}),\qquad
 \|\hat E_{\ge2}^{(j)}\|_j\le C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2,
 \qquad
 \|\hat R^{(j)}\|_j\le C_3\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^3.
\]
The first two hold also for each pointed term, on both
lattices.  The explicit part on $\mathbb Z^3$ is
$\hat T^{(j)}=T^{(j)}(\hat y)$, with
$\hat y_i=0$ for $i<t_0$ and $\hat y_i=1/\hat x_i$ later.
The extracted numbers are real, read from that
infinite-lattice family, and independent of the side and
weight.  They obey
\[
 \hat x_i=L^{-1}\hat x_{i-1}-\hat b_i,\qquad
 \hat s_i=L\hat s_{i-1}+\hat\mu_i,\qquad
 \hat E_i=\hat E_{i-1}+\hat e_in_i,
\]
and
\begin{gather*}
 |\hat x_k-\mathsf t_k|\le(1-L^{-(k-t_0)})\bar B,\qquad
 F^{\rm UV}-\tfrac12\le\mathsf t_k\hat s_k
                      \le F^{\rm UV}+2B_F+\tfrac12,\\
 |\hat s_k|\le\bar B_M/\mathsf t_k,\qquad
 \hat x_k\ge g^{-2}\ge\gamma^{-2},\qquad
 \hat x_k\ge\tfrac78\mathsf t_k,\qquad \hat x_K\le X_g.
\end{gather*}
Every step is the admitted zero-source RG step, including
its invariant symmetry space.  The density of
$\hat\tau_k$ is bounded Borel, zero off
$\mathcal V_k^\chi$, and is the RG expression on that
set, with no member of a level $\le t_0$.
If $u\ge u_*$, this continuation agrees through $t_1$
with the zero-source flow of \cref{C-418-9}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Apply \cref{C-419-4} at $c=0$ and
$\zeta=F^{\rm UV}\in[0,B_F]$.  That proposition forms
the zero-source restart to $K$ and verifies the
original-step applicability from the new base.  It gives
the displayed norms, decomposition, recursions and the
first two windows.  The zero-source symmetry space gives
matrix cell cancellation on $\mathbb Z^3$, so the
old-activity estimates hold there as on a torus.
For a scalar-array bound on a given infinite-lattice
polymer, choose a sufficiently large admitted torus into
which it fits.  The local chart preserves the scalar
values, pointers, norms and polymer sizes, and the
torus estimate uses the same constant $E_0$.
Thus it gives the infinite-lattice scalar bound.

The term has a bounded Borel density at the base by
\cref{C-419-11}; each tested step preserves that property
and supplies its stated expression on
$\mathcal V_k^\chi$.  Its numbers are the linear
extraction functionals on the infinite-lattice activity,
which here coincide with the original extraction rules
because its totals have the required symmetries.

The first coupling window and
$\mathsf b\ge g^{-2}+\bar B$ imply $\hat x_k\ge g^{-2}$.
The ceiling $4\bar B\gamma^2\le\sigma_\star\le1/2$
gives $\bar B\le\mathsf t_k/8$, hence the $7/8$ bound.
At the last level $\mathsf b\le X_g-\bar B$, proving
$\hat x_K\le X_g$.
Finally the source restart's chain is zero at zero
source: its initial value is zero and
$\hat\nu_{k+1}(0)=\hat\mu_{k+1}$.  Its source energies
then vanish and its steps are the same zero-source
steps with the same numbers.  Induction identifies the
two flows through $t_1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Admission above the empty earlier family]\label{C-427-5}
Set $E^{(j)}=0$ for $j\le t_0$ and
$E^{(j)}=\hat E^{(j)}$ later.  With the restarted numbers,
these form a flow with free earlier activities as in
\cref{C-418-18}, at base $t_0$, with
$R^{(j)}=D^{(j)}=0$ for $j\le t_0$.
All earlier-family error parameters are zero.
For $j>t_0$, on both lattices,
\begin{gather*}
 \sup_\square\sum_{X\supset\square}e^{\kappa d_j(X)}
     \sup_{\mathsf U}\sum_{z\in X}
             \|\hat E_{\ge2}^{(j)}(X;\mathsf U,\cdot;z)\|_{h^{(j)}}
                  \le C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2,\\
 \|\hat E_{\ge2}^{(j)}\|_j^{\rm pt}
                  \le C_2^{\rm pt}\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2,\qquad
 C_2^{\rm pt}=8M^3C_2.
\end{gather*}
The exact terms in \cref{C-418-18} are the restarted
terms here, with scalar $\hat E_k$ and action coefficient
$\beta_h=\beta-\sum_{t_0<j\le k}L^j\hat b_j\varphi_j$.
Its action bounds also hold with $\beta$ itself.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The zero family satisfies all earlier-family conditions,
and both lag sums are zero.  For the later families,
\cref{C-427-4} gives the required symmetries, localization,
holomorphy, matrix cell cancellation and torus agreement.
The scalar parts contain no action multiple and, on
$\mathbb Z^3$, no constant; their torus constants are
field independent.  These are the first free-flow
conditions.

We verify the norm summed over pointers.  At a fixed
pair the shares
$n^{-1}\sum_{\mathsf z_j(p)=z}\mathsf N_p$ of a monomial
with $n\ge2$ legs lie in $[0,1]$ and sum to one over $z$.
Taking the infimum over representations in the fibre
norm gives
\[
 \sum_z\left\|\sum_{\mathsf z_j(p)=z}F_p\right\|\le\|F\|.
\]
The expansion majorant is nonnegative and multilinear
in the vertex norms, and the pointed term is the
average of the terms with one leg vertex replaced by
its insertion.  Thus these sums pass under the gauge
majorant integral, Berezin contractions and Cauchy
integrals of the expansion.  They obey the same
coefficient bounds as the whole expansion.  The
vanishing coefficients in the deformation vanish
pointer by pointer.  The remaining mass coefficient
is at most $K_\mu^{-1}c_sh_F^2|\hat s_{j-1}|^2$.
Mass extraction adds forms on disjoint site blocks;
their norms sum to at most
$c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2|\hat\mu_j|$.  Extraction therefore
multiplies the bounds by at most $K_\mu$, giving
\[
 \tfrac12C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2
 +c_sh_F^2|\hat s_{j-1}|^2
 +\theta_E\sum_{t_0<i<j}\omega_{j-i}
                                   \|\hat E_{\ge2}^{(i)}\|_i.
\]
The closed bounds and mass window make this at most
$(1/2+1/4+1/(4\sqrt2))C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2$,
which proves the first displayed estimate.
For the separate supremum at each pointer, apply the
pointed-output estimate of \cite{QCDM1}
at the actual step.  Its step-admission hypothesis is
\cref{C-427-4}; the mass is the original datum's fine
mass, $|\hat s_{j-1}|\le\bar B_M/\mathsf t_{j-1}$,
and all earlier leg activities have the closed $C_2$
bound.  The estimate is therefore $C_2^{\rm pt}$.

The remaining number bounds also hold:
$|\hat b_i|\le B_\sharp$,
\[
 |\hat\mu_i|\le2\bar B_M/\mathsf t_i
                   \le3\bar B_M/\hat x_i,\qquad
 |\hat e_i|\le C'_e(1+\log\hat x_{i-1}).
\]
The latter follows by comparing the extracted scalar
with the free gauge and block-fermion vacuum numbers,
using $|\hat x_{i-1}-\mathsf t_{i-1}|\le\bar B$.
Thus all the free-flow hypotheses hold, including
the pointed and scalar bounds and the fixed
$(\Gamma^{\rm F})$ potential ceilings.
Its base density is exactly $\hat\tau_{t_0}$, so
its terms and extracted scalar are those here.
Finally $L^{t_0}\hat x_{t_0}=\beta$, giving the stated
action coefficients and the bound with $\beta$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[History bounds after the restart]\label{C-427-6}
Let $C_5^{\rm F},C_E^{\rm F},C_\flat^{\rm F}$ be the
zero-source history constants of the construction, and
set $\mathsf C_{\rm maj}^\dagger=48L^3C_E^{\rm F}+C'_\star$,
$\theta_{\rm dis}=(c_\star-c_\Theta)/2$.
The restarted histories have the exact history form
and bounds of \cref{C-418-18}, with the original
constants, $\hat E_k$ in place of $E_k$ and
$\hat f_n=0$ for $n\le t_0$.  Their vacuum numbers obey
\[
 |\hat f_n(\mathcal S)|\le C_\flat^{\rm F}
             (1+\log\mathsf t_{n-1})\#_n(Z_n(\mathcal S)^\sim),
\]
and
\begin{align*}
 e^{-\hat E_k+\sum_n\operatorname{Re}\hat f_n(\mathcal S)}
  \int\|\hat{\mathsf g}_h\|_{h_F}\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}
 \le{}&\exp[\mathsf C_{\rm maj}^\dagger(n_k+\Sigma_Z(h))]\\
 &\cdot\prod_{t=1}^k
       e^{-c_\star p_0(g_t)^2\mathsf n_t^{\rm cr}(h)}.
\end{align*}
For every $t_0<t\le K$,
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_K^{(t_0)}:Z_t(h)\ne\emptyset}
       \int\|\hat{\mathsf g}_h\|_{h_F}\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}
   &\le e^{-\theta_{\rm dis}p_0(g_t)^2}
                       e^{\hat E_K+(C+2)\ell^3},\\
 \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_K^{(t_0)}}
       \int\|\hat{\mathsf g}_h\|_{h_F}\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}
   &\le e^{\hat E_K+(C+2)\ell^3}.
\end{align*}
Here $Z_t(h)\ne\emptyset$ means that a large-field
region has occurred by level $t$; such a history has
a created cell at some level $t_0<t'\le t$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Apply \cref{C-418-18} using \cref{C-427-5}.  All
earlier-family errors vanish, so the constants retain
their zero-source values.  The initial coupling
correction is also zero.  This gives the form, vacuum
bound and integral majorant.

Extend the normalized integral majorant by zero to
histories outside $\mathcal H_K^{(t_0)}$, and call it
$f(h)$.  Put $\mathsf e(\mathcal S)=-\sum_n
\operatorname{Re}\hat f_n(\mathcal S)$ when
$Z_{t_0}(\mathcal S)=\emptyset$, and zero otherwise.
Thus $fe^{\mathsf e}$ is the history integral multiplied
by $e^{-\hat E_K}$ on the retained histories.
The equivalence $Z_{t_0}(h)=\emptyset
\Longleftrightarrow h|_{t_0}=h_\emptyset^{(t_0)}$
ensures this extension respects the history labels.
Define
\[
 f'(h)=f(h)\exp\left[
       \theta_{\rm dis}\sum_{t'=1}^K
                       p_0(g_{t'})^2\mathsf n_{t'}^{\rm cr}(h)\right].
\]
Its decay rate is
$c=c_\star-\theta_{\rm dis}=(c_\star+c_\Theta)/2$.
The calibrated history-summation theorem applies at
this rate, with deposit $c$, weight share $c_\Theta/c<1$
and the already imposed thresholds
$\log\gamma^{-2}\ge\mathsf Y_{\rm f1}$ or
$\mathsf Y_{\rm f2}$ according to $c_a=0$ or $c_a>0$.
The required floors are those used for the original
history sum.  Its majorant and label constants are
at least the ones above (the source constants and
$C'_{\mathfrak E}$ only enlarge them).  Consequently
\[
 \sum_h f'(h)e^{\mathsf e(\mathcal S(h))}e^{\Theta'(h)}
       \le\Pi_K(C,c'')\le e^{(C+2)\ell^3},\qquad
 c''=\tfrac12(1-\eth)(c_\star-c_\Theta),\quad\Theta'\ge0.
\]
This is the same calibrated history sum proved in
\cite[\S14]{QCDM1}; its inputs have just been checked
for the restarted families.  Since $f\le f'$, it gives
the second estimate.  If $Z_t(h)\ne\emptyset$, some
cell was created at $t_0<t'\le t$ and
$p_0(g_{t'})^2\ge p_0(g_t)^2$.
Thus $f'(h)\ge e^{\theta_{\rm dis}p_0(g_t)^2}f(h)$
on this set.  The same sum gives the first estimate.
Nesting of the large-field regions proves the last
interpretation.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Positivity and a lower bound for the restarted total}

\begin{lemma}[The Gaussian at the start]\label{C-427-7}
For a bare configuration $U$, put
$\mathfrak a=\mathfrak a_{t_0}$, $R=R_{t_0}(U)$,
$\mathcal K=\mathcal K_{t_0}[U;m_0]$, and
$\mathbb D_{t_0}=L^{t_0}\mathsf D^{(t_0)}[U;m_0]$.
Define
\[
 \hat{\mathbb M}=\hat s_{t_0}\mathfrak a^2R\mathcal K^{-2}R^*,
 \qquad \hat{\mathbb D}=\mathbb D_{t_0}+\hat{\mathbb M},
 \qquad \epsilon_{\rm st}=\frac{F^{\rm UV}}{\mathsf b\mathsf m}.
\]
The mass form in the start is
$L^{-t_0}\hat s_{t_0}\mathsf S_1(\psi^{\rm bg})
=\langle\bar\Psi,\hat{\mathbb M}\Psi\rangle$ and
\[
 |\langle\chi,\hat{\mathbb M}\chi\rangle|
   \le\epsilon_{\rm st}\operatorname{Re}
                         \langle\chi,\mathbb D_{t_0}\chi\rangle,
 \qquad \epsilon_{\rm st}\le c_b/24.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \operatorname{Re}\hat{\mathbb D}
 \ge(1-\epsilon_{\rm st})
       \frac{\theta_{t_0}\mathfrak m_{t_0}}
            {\theta_{t_0}+\mathfrak m_{t_0}}>0.
\]

Starting with $\hat{\mathbb D}_{t_0}=\hat{\mathbb D}$ and
$N_{t_0}=1$, define, for $t_0\le j<K$,
\begin{gather*}
 \hat\Gamma_j=\hat{\mathbb D}_j+\theta q^*q,\qquad
 \hat{\mathbb D}_{j+1}=\theta-\theta^2q\hat\Gamma_j^{-1}q^*,\\
 N_{j+1}=N_j\theta^{-\nu n_{j+1}}\det\hat\Gamma_j,\qquad
 \theta=b_F,\quad q=q_{j+1}(W_j),\quad W_j=\mathcal M^jU.
\end{gather*}
All these operators are defined and accretive, and
\[
 \hat{\mathbb D}_j^{-1}
  =\theta^{-1}\sum_{0\le i<j-t_0}L^{-i}
                          +Q_j\hat{\mathbb D}^{-1}Q_j^*,\qquad
 Q_j=q_j\cdots q_{t_0+1},\quad Q_jQ_j^*=L^{-(j-t_0)}.
\]
At the last level,
\[
 \operatorname{Re}\hat{\mathbb D}_K
       \ge(1-\epsilon_{\rm st})c_b\mathsf m
       \ge\tfrac{23}{24}c_b\mathsf m
       \ge\tfrac12c_b\mathsf m_-.
\]
Every singular value has the same lower bound.

The one-step Gaussian identity is
\[
 \operatorname{Ber}_j\left(\operatorname{Ker}_j(W_j)N_j
       e^{-\langle\bar\Psi_j,\hat{\mathbb D}_j\Psi_j\rangle}\right)
  =N_{j+1}
       e^{-\langle\bar\Psi_{j+1},\hat{\mathbb D}_{j+1}\Psi_{j+1}\rangle},
\]
and $N_j\det\hat{\mathbb D}_j=\det\hat{\mathbb D}$.
The two chiral blocks remain adjoints, so
\[
 \det\hat{\mathbb D}_j=|\det\hat{\mathbb D}_{j,+}|^{2N_f}>0,\qquad
 \det\hat\Gamma_j=|\det\hat\Gamma_{j,+}|^{2N_f}>0,\qquad N_j>0.
\]
In particular
$\det\hat{\mathbb D}\ge
N_K(\tfrac12c_b\mathsf m_-)^{\nu\ell^3}$.
At a tested background this is the Gaussian of the start;
it is constant on its minimal orbit.  The measure
$\hat\nu$ of \cref{C-427-2} is finite and positive, with
bounded Borel, gauge-invariant density, strictly positive
on $\mathcal V_{t_0}^\chi$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Differentiate the original zero-source tower with respect
to $m_0$, keeping $U$ fixed.  Since
$\partial_{m_0}\mathbb D_0=1$ and
\[
 \partial_{m_0}\mathbb D_{j+1}
   =\theta^2q\Gamma_j^{-1}
                   (\partial_{m_0}\mathbb D_j)\Gamma_j^{-1}q^*,
\]
iteration through the background maps gives
$\langle\bar\Psi,\partial_{m_0}\mathbb D_{t_0}\Psi\rangle
=\mathsf S_1(\psi^{\rm bg})$.
The closed formula
$\mathbb D_{t_0}=L^{t_0}(\mathfrak a-
\mathfrak a^2R\mathcal K^{-1}R^*)$ then proves the
mass identity.

For its relative bound set
$w=\mathcal K^{-1}R^*\chi$,
$\varphi=\mathfrak aw$, and $v=\chi-\mathfrak aRw$.
Then $R^*v=(D[U]+m_0)w$, and
\[
 \langle\chi,\mathsf D^{(t_0)}\chi\rangle
   =\mathfrak a|v|^2+
             \mathfrak a^2\langle w,(D[U]+m_0)w\rangle.
\]
Accretivity of $D[U]$ gives
$\operatorname{Re}\langle\chi,\mathbb D_{t_0}\chi\rangle
\ge\mathfrak m_{t_0}|\varphi|^2$.
Apply the same calculation with $\mathcal K^*$ and
$\varphi'=\mathfrak a(\mathcal K^*)^{-1}R^*\chi$;
the adjoint quadratic form has the same real part.
Since
$\langle\chi,\hat{\mathbb M}\chi\rangle
=\hat s_{t_0}\langle\varphi',\varphi\rangle$,
the desired bound follows by Cauchy--Schwarz.
Here $\hat s_{t_0}/\mathfrak m_{t_0}
=F^{\rm UV}/(\mathsf b\mathsf m)$.
The original positive-mass coupling ceiling gives
$\mathsf b\mathsf m\ge8C_{\mathsf S_1}\bar B_M/c_b$,
and $F^{\rm UV}\le B_F<\bar B_M/3$, with
$C_{\mathsf S_1}\ge1$.  Thus
$\epsilon_{\rm st}\le c_b/24$.
The original block-Dirac floor
$\operatorname{Re}\mathbb D_{t_0}\ge
\theta_{t_0}\mathfrak m_{t_0}/
(\theta_{t_0}+\mathfrak m_{t_0})$ proves the floor for
$\hat{\mathbb D}$.

Let this floor be $c>0$ and write
$P_j=\theta^{-1}\sum_{0\le i<j-t_0}L^{-i}$.
If $\operatorname{Re}\hat{\mathbb D}_j>0$, then
$\hat\Gamma_j$ is invertible and the matrix inversion
identity gives
\[
 \hat{\mathbb D}_{j+1}^{-1}
       =\theta^{-1}+q\hat{\mathbb D}_j^{-1}q^*.
\]
Since $qq^*=L^{-1}$, this proves the stated inverse
formula by induction.  It also preserves a quantitative
floor.  Set $g=\hat{\mathbb D}_{j+1}^{-1}f$ and
$y=\hat{\mathbb D}^{-1}Q_{j+1}^*f$.  Then
\[
 \operatorname{Re}\langle g,\hat{\mathbb D}_{j+1}g\rangle
        \ge P_{j+1}|f|^2+c|y|^2,\qquad
 |g|^2\le(P_{j+1}+L^{-(j+1-t_0)}/c)
                         (P_{j+1}|f|^2+c|y|^2).
\]
Hence
$\operatorname{Re}\hat{\mathbb D}_{j+1}
\ge(P_{j+1}+L^{-(j+1-t_0)}/c)^{-1}$.
At $K$, put $a_-=b_F(1-L^{-1})$.
Since $\theta_{t_0}\ge a_-$,
\[
 P_K+L^{-s}/c
 \le(1-\epsilon_{\rm st})^{-1}(a_-^{-1}+\mathsf m^{-1})
 \le[(1-\epsilon_{\rm st})c_b\mathsf m]^{-1}.
\]
The last inequality uses
$c_b=a_-/(a_-+1/2)$ and $\mathsf m\le1/2$.
This proves the last-level floor, and its singular-value
version follows from
$|\hat{\mathbb D}_Kg|\,|g|\ge
\operatorname{Re}\langle g,\hat{\mathbb D}_Kg\rangle$.

Completing the square in the kernel with
$\Psi_j=\hat\Gamma_j^{-1}\theta q^*\Psi_{j+1}+\Xi$
and the corresponding barred substitution gives the
Gaussian identity.  Berezin translation invariance and
the kernel factor $\theta^{-\nu n_{j+1}}$ give exactly
$N_{j+1}$.  Integrating the next-level generators uses
the kernel normalization one and gives
$N_j\det\hat{\mathbb D}_j=N_{j+1}\det\hat{\mathbb D}_{j+1}$.

The projections $e_\pm$ commute with the averages,
the isometry to the chamber fields and all real scalar
coefficients.  The two blocks of $D[U]$ are adjoints,
and $R^*R,q^*q$ are self-adjoint.  Thus the same
adjoint relation holds for $\mathcal K$,
$\mathbb D_{t_0}$ and $\hat{\mathbb M}$, and is preserved
by the recursion.  Invertibility makes the displayed
determinants strictly positive, and hence $N_j>0$.
The last determinant bound follows in dimension
$\nu n_K=\nu\ell^3$.

Two backgrounds in the minimal orbit over $W$ differ
by a gauge transformation equal to one at level
$t_0$.  Covariance of $D$ and $R$ therefore leaves
$\hat{\mathbb D}$ unchanged.  A gauge transformation
of $W$ lifts to the bare blocks and conjugates this
operator, leaving its determinant and Wilson action
unchanged.  Finally $\hat\nu$ is the Berezin integral
of the bounded Borel start density from
\cref{C-427-4}; the positivity just proved gives all
remaining assertions.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Positive masses and consistency]\label{C-427-8}
With the operators of \cref{C-427-7}, evaluated at
$\mathsf U_{t_0}(W)$, the small-field term is
\[
 \hat\tau_k=(\mathcal M^{k-t_0})_*
 \left[\hat{\mathsf k}^{(k)}\chi_{t_0}(T_\ell)
 e^{-\beta A(\mathsf U)}N_k
 e^{-\langle\bar\Psi_k,\hat{\mathbb D}_k\Psi_k\rangle}\,dW\right].
\]
The integrand is zero off $\mathcal V_{t_0}^\chi$.
Its Berezin integral and its degree-zero part are
finite positive measures; the former is
$(\mathcal M^{k-t_0})_*(\hat{\mathsf k}^{(k)}\hat\nu)$.
At $K$ the Berezin integral is at least
$(\frac12c_b\mathsf m_-)^{\nu\ell^3}$ times the
degree-zero part, as measures.

For each $h\in\mathcal H_k^{(t_0)}$ there is a bounded
Borel weight $\mathfrak w_{h/t_0}\ge0$ on $\mathcal Y$
such that, pointwise on bare configurations,
\[
 \mathfrak w_h(U)=\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset^{(t_0)}}(U)
                      \mathfrak w_{h/t_0}(\mathcal M^{t_0}U),\qquad
 \hat t(h)=\int_{\mathcal Y}\mathfrak w_{h/t_0}\,d\hat\nu\ge0.
\]
In particular
$\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset^{(k)}/t_0}=\hat{\mathsf k}^{(k)}$.
There is a bounded Borel nonnegative gauge-invariant
bare density $\hat\varsigma$ such that every fully
Berezin-integrated restarted term is the ordinary gauge
history term at that density.  Consequently, for
$t_0\le k<k'\le K$ and $h\in\mathcal H_k^{(t_0)}$,
\[
 \sum_{h'|_k=h}\hat t(h')=\hat t(h),\qquad
 \hat t(h_\emptyset^{(k)})\ge\hat t(h_\emptyset^{(K)}).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The first identity follows by induction from the
Gaussian identity of \cref{C-427-7}.  The maps,
weights and kernel entries are Borel.  The operator
recursion uses finitely many rational operations with
nonvanishing determinants, so its entries are Borel
as well.  Multiplying a pushforward by a function of
the output multiplies its original measure by that
function composed with the map.  This observation
commutes the next step through the displayed image.
The identity $N_k\det\hat{\mathbb D}_k
=\det\hat{\mathbb D}$ then gives the Berezin integral.
Positivity of $N_k$ and the determinants gives both
positive measures; the final determinant floor gives
their stated comparison.

For a history above $t_0$, all earlier regions are
the torus.  Thus its later determining sets contain
no bonds from levels below $t_0$.  The test property
(T5) makes each later outcome indicator a function
only of $W_j$, $j\ge t_0$; it is Borel by (T2).
The gauge-fixing factors read the same block fields
and are bounded Borel.  Their product defines
$\mathfrak w_{h/t_0}$ at every $W$ and gives the
pointwise factorization.

We construct a bare density to justify consistency
for these new terms.  Let
$\varsigma_0=e^{-\beta A}\det(D+m_0)$, and let
$\rho\,dW$ be the ordinary small-field image
$(\mathcal M^{t_0})_*
(\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset^{(t_0)}}\varsigma_0\,dU)$.
Its density is bounded Borel and nonnegative almost
everywhere.  It is invariant under block gauge
transformations as a measure: their constant-on-block
lifts preserve the original density, Haar measure,
tests and gauge-fixing factors.  Haar averaging gives
\[
 \bar\rho(W)=\int\rho(W^v)\,dv,\qquad
 \bar\rho=\rho\quad\hbox{almost everywhere},
\]
with $\bar\rho$ bounded Borel and pointwise invariant.

The original intermediate-level lower bound supplies
$\rho\ge c_1\mathsf{sf}_{t_0}$ almost everywhere, where
\[
 c_1=\exp\left[E_{t_0}-
       \left(C_5^{\rm F}+\nu\log(\theta_{t_0}^{-1}
                              +\mathfrak m_{t_0}^{-1})\right)n_{t_0}\right]>0.
\]
On the tested set, $0\le a_p\le2$ gives
$\mathsf{sf}_{t_0}\ge c_2
:=e^{-2L^{t_0}x_{t_0}N_{\rm p}}>0$.
Thus $\bar\rho\ge c_1c_2\chi_{t_0}(T_\ell)$ almost
everywhere.  Define
\[
 r(W)=\frac{\chi_{t_0}(T_\ell)(W)\hat F(W)}{\bar\rho(W)}
 \quad\hbox{if }\chi_{t_0}(T_\ell)=1, \bar\rho\ge c_1c_2,
 \qquad r=0\quad\hbox{otherwise}.
\]
This is bounded Borel, nonnegative and pointwise
gauge invariant, with $r\rho=\chi_{t_0}\hat F$ almost
everywhere.  Therefore
\[
 \hat\varsigma(U)=\varsigma_0(U)r(\mathcal M^{t_0}U)
\]
is a bounded Borel nonnegative density invariant under
every bare gauge transformation.  The factorization
gives, for every retained history,
\[
 \int\mathfrak w_h\hat\varsigma\,dU
       =\int\mathfrak w_{h/t_0}r\rho\,dW
       =\int\mathfrak w_{h/t_0}\,d\hat\nu.
\]
The same identity with any bounded Borel test at
$\mathcal M^{t_0}U$ identifies the image measures.

It remains to identify the terms on each history's
coordinates, since total masses alone do not prove
their consistency.  Write $\xi_h$ for those Borel
partial coordinates.  The domain contains the support
of $\mathfrak w_h$.  At a successor history,
\[
 \xi_{(h,\mathsf o)}=\Sigma_{(h,\mathsf o)}\circ\xi_h,\qquad
 \mathfrak w_{(h,\mathsf o)}
       =\mathfrak w_h(\mathsf f_{(h,\mathsf o)}\circ\xi_h),
\]
on the respective domains, with bounded Borel
$\mathsf f_{(h,\mathsf o)}\ge0$.
These are the coordinate and weight identities of
\cref{C-423-4}.  The partial fermion kernel integrates
to one in its new generators, and later kernels do
not change stored generators.  Hence full Berezin
integration of the step sends a scalar measure
$\nu_h$ to
$(\Sigma_{(h,\mathsf o)})_*(\mathsf f_{(h,\mathsf o)}\nu_h)$.
At the base, $\nu_h$ is the image of $\hat\nu$ under
the one-to-one Borel coordinate chart.  Induction and
composition of partial pushforwards therefore give
\[
 \nu_h=(\xi_h)_*(\mathfrak w_h\hat\varsigma\,dU).
\]
At a successor the factor $1_{\operatorname{dom}\xi_h}$
can be omitted because the new weight vanishes off
that domain.  This establishes the asserted
identification as positive measures and their masses.

The calibrated gauge history consistency theorem now
applies to the bounded Borel gauge-invariant density
$\hat\varsigma$.  Its test assumptions (T1)--(T4),(T6)
are those of the construction, and its threshold
condition follows from
$\varepsilon(\mathsf t_j)\le\varepsilon(\gamma^{-2})
\le\varepsilon_\flat$.
Its pushforward keeps total mass, giving
$\sum_{h'|_k=h}\hat t(h')=\hat t(h)$.
Every extension remains above $t_0$.  For the empty
history the sum includes the final empty history,
and all masses are nonnegative.  This proves the
last inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[A lower bound for the restarted total]\label{C-427-9}
Put
\[
 \hat{\mathsf{sf}}_K(V)=\chi_K(T_\ell)(V)
            e^{-L^K\hat x_KA(\mathsf U_K(V))}
\]
on $\mathcal V_K^\chi$, and zero elsewhere.  This is
a Borel function with values in $[0,1]$.  As measures,
\[
 \operatorname{Ber}\hat\tau_K
   \ge(\tfrac12c_b\mathsf m_-)^{\nu\ell^3}
          e^{\hat E_K-C_5^{\rm F}\ell^3}
                               \hat{\mathsf{sf}}_K\,dV.
\]
For $t_0\le k\le K$,
\begin{align*}
 \hat t(h_\emptyset^{(k)})
 &\ge\hat t(h_\emptyset^{(K)})\\
 &\ge e^{\hat E_K-C_P^{(K)}(1+\log\hat x_K)\ell^3}
  \ge e^{\hat E_K-C_P(1+\log X_g)\ell^3},
\end{align*}
where $C_P^{(K)}$ and $C_P$ are the original
last-level and partition lower-bound constants.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The degree-zero part of the RG expression for
$\hat\tau_K$ has density
\[
 d(V)=e^{\hat E_K}\hat{\mathsf{sf}}_K(V)
                                  e^{\hat{\mathsf{rg}}_K(V)}.
\]
For the empty final history all regions are the
torus, all profiles are one, and the boundary sum is
empty.  The regular scalar sum includes the trivial
values of the activities.  The history estimate of
\cref{C-427-6} therefore gives
$|\hat{\mathsf{rg}}_K|\le C_5^{\rm F}\ell^3$ on
the support of that history's weight.

We pass this bound to the density as a measure.
Its degree-zero measure $\mu$ is positive and is
bounded above by
$(\frac12c_b\mathsf m_-)^{-\nu\ell^3}
\operatorname{Ber}\hat\tau_K$ by \cref{C-427-8}.
The latter is the block image of
$\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset^{(K)}}\hat\varsigma\,dU$.
Thus $\mu$ vanishes on any Borel set containing no
block image of a point where that weight times the
density is positive.  The Borel set
\[
 B=\{V\in\mathcal V_K^\chi:
     |d(V)|<e^{\hat E_K-C_5^{\rm F}\ell^3}
                                    \hat{\mathsf{sf}}_K(V)\}
\]
contains no such image, by the regular-sum bound.
Hence $\mu(B)=0$.  But $d\ge0$ almost everywhere
because $\mu$ is positive, and $d\ne0$ everywhere
on the tested set.  Therefore $B$ is Haar-null.
It follows that
$\mu\ge e^{\hat E_K-C_5^{\rm F}\ell^3}
\hat{\mathsf{sf}}_K\,dV$.  Combining this with the
determinant comparison proves the first inequality.

The tested set is open and its background action is
continuous.  Indeed the fixed ceilings give
\[
 \varepsilon(\mathsf t_K)\le\varepsilon_\flat,\qquad
 2\varepsilon(\mathsf t_K)
       \le\varepsilon_{\mathcal W}\alpha_0\le\bar\varepsilon,
\]
the conditions for the tested-field background
construction.  This proves the Borel assertion.
For its integral use the final block ball of radius
$r_b=\hat x_K^{-1/2}$.  The bounds
$\hat x_K\ge\gamma^{-2}$,
$\hat x_K\ge3\mathsf t_K/4$ and the fixed ceilings
$\gamma\le\bar\varepsilon/4$,
$A_0(\log\gamma^{-2})^{\mathfrak p_0}\ge8B_3^{\rm cr}$
give
\[
 0<r_b\le\tfrac14
   \min\{\bar\varepsilon,
      A_0(\log\mathsf t_K)^{\mathfrak p_0}
                        \mathsf t_K^{-1/2}/B_3^{\rm cr}\}.
\]
Thus the original final-block ball estimate applies:
all density tests pass there,
$L^K\hat x_KA(\mathsf U_K(V))
\le24(B_3^{\rm cr})^2\ell^3$, and its Haar volume
is at least $(\hat x_K^{-3/2}/7)^{3\ell^3}$.
Consequently
\[
 \int\hat{\mathsf{sf}}_K\,dV
 \ge\exp[-(\tfrac92\log\hat x_K+3\log7
                                  +24(B_3^{\rm cr})^2)\ell^3].
\]
Taking total masses in the measure inequality proves
the lower bound with
\[
 C_P^{(K)}=\max\{\tfrac92, C_5^{\rm F}+3\log7
       +24(B_3^{\rm cr})^2+1+\nu\log(2/(c_b\mathsf m_-))\}.
\]
Finally $C_P\ge C_P^{(K)}$, $\hat x_K\le X_g$, and
\cref{C-427-8} supplies the comparison with earlier
empty histories.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{The restarted total at the comparison depth.}
Under $u\ge u_*$, $s\ge s_F$ and
$L^u\gamma^{-2}\ge\Theta_\star$, these results give
\cref{C-418-24}.  Indeed \cref{C-427-4} continues the
zero-source restart to $K$, and \cref{C-427-6} bounds
its histories.  On the initial field cut,
\[
 \hat F_0^\bullet
       =1_{\mathsf{Cut}_{(t_0)}}
          e^{-\beta A(\mathsf U_{t_0})}\det\hat{\mathbb D}
       \ge0.
\]
It equals $\hat F$ on the tested set.  Any history
above $t_1$ contains the first small-field step, whose
weight enforces both the density test and this cut
by \cref{C-427-3}.  Therefore its mass is
\[
 \hat t(h)=\int\mathfrak w_{h/t_0}\hat F_0^\bullet\,dW\ge0.
\]
The masses at every later level sum to
$\hat T^\bullet(0)=\hat t(h_\emptyset^{(t_1)})$ by
\cref{C-427-8}, and \cref{C-427-9} bounds this total
below by $e^{\hat E_K-C_P(1+\log X_g)\ell^3}$.

For $t_0<t\le t_1$, at any intermediate level the
masses of histories having a large-field region by
level $t$ are at most their sum at $K$: each history
is the sum of its extensions, the regions are nested,
and all masses are nonnegative.  Full Berezin
integration is bounded by the fibre norm since
$h_F\ge1$.  Hence \cref{C-427-6} and the lower bound
give the relative estimate
\[
 e^{-\theta_{\rm dis}p_0(g_t)^2}
 e^{(C+2+C_P(1+\log X_g))\ell^3}\hat T^\bullet(0)
   =e^{-\theta_{\rm dis}p_0(g_t)^2}
                    \mathsf M_{g,\ell}\hat T^\bullet(0).
\]

\subsection{Source energies and separated supports}

We next estimate the scalar energies removed between the restart and
the comparison level.  Their dependence on a source is local up to
an exponentially decreasing tail.  This gives a small mixed derivative
when two source supports are separated.

\begin{definition}[Energies after the restart]\label{C-429-2}
Use the data of \cref{C-418-2}, assume (k0) and $u\ge u_*$,
and choose either cutoff.  Write $t_0=K-s$ and $t_1=K-u$.
Distances below are in the units of the bare lattice; a physical
distance $\mathsf d$ is $\mathsf dL^K$ in these units.
The support of a source includes its sites and its plaquette barycentres.
For $t_0<j\le t_1$, define
\[
 \hat e_j(X;s)=
 \hat{\mathfrak E}_j(X;\hat{\mathfrak c}_{j-1}(s))
 -\hat{\mathfrak E}_j(X;0).
\]
Here $\hat{\mathfrak E}_j$ is the scalar energy of the restart
of \cref{C-419-7}, with $\zeta=F^{\rm UV}$, at a free coordinate
of level $j-1$.  The domains and chains are those of
\cref{C-419-7,C-419-8}.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Identification at source coordinates]\label{C-429-3}
The flow of \cref{C-418-3}(2) is the restart of
\cref{C-419-7} with $\zeta=F^{\rm UV}$ and label zero.
The identification includes its activities, increments, source
chains and scalar energies.  At the initial level,
\[
 \hat s_{t_0}+\hat\sigma_{t_0}(s)
 =\hat\Sigma_w,\qquad
 \hat\Sigma_w(x)=\frac{F^{\rm UV}}{L^s(\mathsf b-w(x))}.
\]
The identification holds on the source window
$\|w\|_\infty<8\varrho$ and
$L\lambda_{t_0}\|J\|_\infty<2r_M$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
This is the identification in \cref{C-419-11}, on the larger
source window stated there.  Indeed, the action is read at the same
weight, the tower at the same fine mass matrix, and the mass member
at $\hat\Sigma_w$.  Neither start contains earlier activities or
normalizing factors.  The density test and product Haar measure
are identical.  The inequalities
$0\le F^{\rm UV}\le B_F$, $|\mathsf b-w|\ge\mathsf b/2$ and
$L^{t_0+1}\|\mathsf n\|_\infty<2r_M$
put these expressions in the domains used in that proof.
Equality on each minimal orbit gives equality of the bounded
Borel densities, including at fields for which the density test
vanishes.  Induction under the same one-step map proves all the
claimed identifications.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Locality of restarted source energies]\label{C-429-4}
Let $t_0<j\le t_1$ and $X\in\mathcal D_j$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)]
The step from level $j-1$ is defined on
$2\hat{\mathscr D}_{j-1}(a^{\rm rad}_{j-1})$, which contains
$2\hat{\mathscr D}_{j-1}$.
The function $\hat{\mathfrak E}_j(X;\cdot)$ is holomorphic
there.  It reads $w$ and $\sigma_i$ on $X$; it reads
$\mathsf n$ on $X$ and along the walks of the background maps.
Those walks use cubes of side $M_w$ in their level units and
carry the factor $e^{-1/2}$ per step.  On
$2\hat{\mathscr D}_{j-1}$,
\[
 |\hat{\mathfrak E}_j(X;\hat{\mathfrak c})
       -\hat{\mathfrak E}_j(X;0)|
 \le C_{\mathfrak E}e^{-\kappa d_j(X)}.
\]
\item[(b)]
The map $s\mapsto\hat{\mathfrak c}_k(s)$ is holomorphic from
$\mathscr O_k$ into $\hat{\mathscr D}_k$, and
$\hat{\mathfrak c}_k(0)=0$.  For $t_0\le i\le k\le t_1$,
\[
 |\hat\sigma_i(s)(x)-\hat\sigma_i(s')(x)|
 \le C_{\rm t}\hat\phi_i
 \exp\left[-\frac{\kappa_\sigma
  \operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{supp}(s-s'))}{L^i}\right].
\]
At $i=t_0$ the two values agree whenever
$x\notin\operatorname{supp}(s-s')$.
\item[(c)]
The function $\hat e_j(X;\cdot)$ is holomorphic on
$\mathscr O_{j-1}$, vanishes at zero, and satisfies
\[
 |\hat e_j(X;s)|\le C_{\mathfrak E}e^{-\kappa d_j(X)}.
\]
For $s,s'\in\mathscr O_{j-1}$,
\[
 |\hat e_j(X;s)-\hat e_j(X;s')|
 \le C_{\mathfrak E}e^{-\kappa d_j(X)}
 \exp\left[-\frac{\kappa_\sigma
  \operatorname{dist}(X,\operatorname{supp}(s-s'))}{L^j}\right].
\]
\end{enumerate}
All constants are the constants of the original source induction.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By \cref{C-419-8}(S1), the step at every free coordinate is the
restarted step.  By \cref{C-429-3}, its restriction to a source
chain is the actual restarted flow.  Thus
$\hat e_j(X;s)$ is the composition of a holomorphic function
on the coordinate domain of level $j-1$ with the chain on
$\mathscr O_{j-1}$.  We verify the estimates and the two places
in the symmetry proof that depend on the initial level.

Summing the mass recursion from $t_0$ gives
\[
 L^{-k}\bigl(\hat s_k+\hat\sigma_k(s)\bigr)
 =L^{-t_0}\hat\Sigma_w
   +\sum_{t_0<i\le k}L^{-i}
      \hat\nu_i(\cdot;\hat{\mathfrak c}_{i-1}(s)).
\]
Consequently, when the potential is read on shell, every local
part extracted at a level $i>t_0$ cancels its copy in the mass
term.  The term left from the initial level is
\[
 -L^{-t_0}\mathsf S_1(\hat\Sigma_w\,\cdot\,)
 =-L^{-t_0}\sum_v\hat\Sigma_w(x_v)
       \bar\psi^{\rm bg}(v)\psi^{\rm bg}(v).
\]
Its coefficient is scalar and reads only $w(x_v)$.  Charge
conjugation therefore preserves it exactly as it preserves
the bare mass term.  Antilinear conjugation replaces its
coefficient by its conjugate; since $F^{\rm UV}$ and
$\mathsf b$ are real, this is the coefficient at
$s^\star=(\bar w,\gamma_4J^\dagger\gamma_4)$.

The bases of the symmetry inductions are now at $t_0$.
There is no activity at that level.  The exponent consists
of the action at its source weight, the tower at its fine
mass matrix, the Gaussian form at its critical point, and
the displayed mass term.  The first three transform jointly
with their source entries, as in the original step; the
last transforms as just checked.  At a tested covariance
pair $V,\mathsf tV$, the lattice isometry $\mathsf t$ maps
the minimal orbit above $V$ onto that above $\mathsf tV$.
The two backgrounds are therefore related by a residual
gauge transformation.  At constant matrix entries the
entries commute with that transformation; the tower and
mass matrices transform by
\[
 (\mathsf n,\sigma_{t_0})\longmapsto
 (S_{\mathsf t}\mathsf nS_{\mathsf t}^{-1},
  S_{\mathsf t}\sigma_{t_0}S_{\mathsf t}^{-1}).
\]
The constant-weight action is invariant.  The initial
densities consequently have the required covariance on
tested pairs.  The one-step map reads only such pairs,
up to gauge transformations, so the same induction proves
the symmetry statements at all subsequent levels.  These
are precisely the covariance and conjugation properties
needed by the local extraction.

We next check its quantitative domain.  The restarted
couplings satisfy
\[
 \hat x_k\ge\gamma^{-2},\qquad
 \tfrac12\hat x_k\le\mathsf t_k\le2\hat x_k,\qquad
 \hat x_k\le2L^{K-k}\mathsf b.
\]
The original ceilings
\[
 4C_w^{\rm s}\phi(\gamma^{-2}/2)\le K_Mc_{\rm cl},
 \qquad
 64c_{\rm th}c_\pi C_{\rm lin}C_{\rm rad}A_1\varrho
       (1+\log(2\gamma^{-2}))^{\mathfrak p_0}\gamma^2
       \le c_{\rm cl}
\]
give
$2C_w^{\rm s}\hat\phi_k\le K_Mc_{\rm cl}/2$ and
$C_{\rm lin}\hat\tau_k(w;a^{\rm rad}_k)\le c_{\rm cl}/8$
on $\|w\|_{\sharp,k}<8\varrho$.  Hence
$\hat{\mathscr D}_k\subset
\hat{\mathscr D}_k(a^{\rm rad}_k)$, also after doubling,
and $C'_{\rm lin}\hat\tau_k\le K_Mc_{\rm cl}/2$.
The recursion and the ceiling
$\gamma^{-2}\ge\max\{L\bar B,(2L)^{3\mathfrak p_0}\}$
give
\[
 \hat\phi_{i-1}\le2L^{-1/2}\hat\phi_i.
\]
Indeed, the square-root ratio contributes at most
$\sqrt2L^{-1/2}$ and the logarithmic ratio at most
$e^{1/3}$, with $\sqrt2e^{1/3}<2$.
Also
$|\hat x_k-L^{-(k-i)}\hat x_i|\le\bar B$ and
$\hat x_i\le2L^{k-i}\hat x_k$.
These are the coupling comparisons used in the original
source estimates, with the same constants.

For completeness, the tail induction starts with an
exactly local function:
$\hat\sigma_{t_0}(s)$ depends on $w(x)$ alone.
If $a_i(t)$ denotes the supremum of the difference of
two $\hat\sigma_i$ whose source difference is at distance
at least $tL^i$, then
$a_{t_0}(t)=0$ for $t>0$ and
$a_{t_0}(0)\le2B_\sigma\hat\phi_{t_0}
\le C_{\rm t}\hat\phi_{t_0}$.
The recursion for the local extraction closes with the
same three inequalities as before:
\[
 Lq_\phi e^{-\kappa_\sigma(L-1)t_\flat}\le\tfrac14,\qquad
 (C_{\rm loc}+2e^{2\kappa_\sigma})B_\nu\le C_{\rm t}/4,
 \qquad e^{2\kappa_\sigma}B_\nu/B_\sigma\le\tfrac12.
\]
This proves (b), together with the holomorphic chain
construction of \cref{C-419-8}.

The scalar energy has three parts: the degree-zero part
of the new activity after Gaussian integration, the
localized normalizers, and the Gaussian contribution at
the weight.  For the first part the bound used in the
original source induction is
\[
 2\|D\|+\|D_0\|+M^3|\widetilde e|+\|\mathcal L_0\|
 \le2C_w^{\rm s}\hat\phi_k+
       C'_{\rm lin}\hat\tau_k.
\]
It is at most $K_Mc_{\rm cl}$ on the doubled domain.
The gauge normalizer has no source-coordinate dependence.
The localized fermion normalizer is given by the same
walk expansion as before; it is holomorphic for
$L^j\|\mathsf n\|_\infty<2r_M$ and its difference is
bounded by
$2C_N^{\mathsf n}N_fr_Me^{-(\kappa+1)d_j(X)}$.
For the Gaussian part, each pointed term is bounded by
\[
 C_{\mathbf G}^v(\bar B+16\varrho)\gamma^2
 e^{-\kappa_+d_j(X)}
 \le e^{-\kappa_+d_j(X)}.
\]
There are at most $8M^3e^{d_j(X)}$ pointers, so its
difference is at most $16M^3e^{-\kappa d_j(X)}$.
The original definition of $C_{\mathfrak E}$ bounds
these three contributions.  This proves (a).

Finally let $S=\operatorname{supp}(s-s')$.
If $X$ meets $S$, the same bound applies to the difference.
Otherwise $w$ and $\mathsf n$ agree on $X$, and so do
the initial mass entries.  Regard all later $\sigma_i$
as one collection, with the normalized supremum norm.
Apply Schwarz's lemma along the single coordinate line
joining its two values in the doubled domain.
This bounds the total change by (b), with
\[
 e^{-\kappa_\sigma\operatorname{dist}(X,S)/L^i}
 \le e^{-\kappa_\sigma\operatorname{dist}(X,S)/L^j}.
\]
A change of $\mathsf n$ outside $X$ requires a background
walk to reach $S$.  Split its factor $e^{-1/2}$ per step
equally between summing the walk and paying for this
distance.  The latter gives
$e^{-\operatorname{dist}(X,S)/(12\sqrt3M_wL^j)}$,
which is at most the required tail because
$\kappa_\sigma\le1/(24M_w)$.
The existing factor $2\max\{1,C_{\rm t}/B_\sigma\}$ in
$C_{\mathfrak E}$ bounds the two source values and the
chain change.  This proves (c).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Mixed derivatives of a local family]\label{C-429-5}
Let $1\le j\le K$, $n\ge2$, and let
$\mathbf s_1,\ldots,\mathbf s_n$ have pairwise disjoint
supports.  Suppose the first two supports are at physical
distance at least $\mathsf d>0$ and
$s(z)=\sum_i z_i\mathbf s_i\in\mathcal P$ for
$|z_i|\le\varrho_i$.
For $X\in\mathcal D_j$, let $f(X;s(z))$ be holomorphic
near this closed polydisc and suppose that
\[
 |f(X;s(z))-f(X;s(z'))|
 \le C'e^{-\kappa d_j(X)}
 e^{-\kappa_\sigma
    \operatorname{dist}(X,\operatorname{supp}(s(z)-s(z')))/L^j}.
\]
Then
\[
 \sum_{X\in\mathcal D_j}
  |\partial^{[n]}f(X;s(z))|
 \le2^{n-1}\prod_i\varrho_i^{-1}\,
 C'C_{\mathscr C}^{\natural}\,
 \#_j^+(\operatorname{supp}\mathbf s_1)
 e^{-\kappa_{\rm E}\mathsf d/\lambda_j},
\]
where the derivative is evaluated at $z=0$,
\[
 \kappa_{\rm E}=
 \min\{\kappa_\sigma/8,\kappa/(4c_{\mathcal D}M)\},
 \quad
 C_{\mathscr C}^{\natural}
 =e^{\kappa/2}C_{\rm cnt}
       \sum_{t\ge0}(2t+3)^3e^{-\kappa_\sigma Mt/2}.
\]
In particular the hypotheses hold for a family holomorphic
on $\mathscr O_{j-1}$ with the displayed source tail there.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The last assertion includes holomorphy near the closed
polydisc.  Indeed, on $\mathcal P$ we have
$\|w\|_\sharp<2\varrho$ and
$\|J\|_\infty\le2\varrho_J\le r_J/2$.
Linearity in $z$ shows that on
$|z_i|<3\varrho_i/2$ these bounds become
$3\varrho$ and $3r_J/4$.  Since
$\|w\|_{\sharp,j-1}\le\|w\|_\sharp$ and
$\lambda_{j-1}\le1$, the larger polydisc is in
$\mathscr O_{j-1}$.

Write $F_X(z)=f(X;s(z))$ and let $\mathsf P_i$ set
$z_i=0$.  Inclusion and exclusion gives
$\partial^{[n]}F_X=
\partial^{[n]}\prod_i(1-\mathsf P_i)F_X$.
Cauchy's estimate therefore gives
\[
 |\partial^{[n]}F_X|
 \le2^{n-1}\prod_i\varrho_i^{-1}
      \min_i\sup|(1-\mathsf P_i)F_X|.
\]
For $S_i=\operatorname{supp}\mathbf s_i$ and
$a_i=\operatorname{dist}(X,S_i)$, the tail assumption,
using $i=1,2$, bounds this by
\[
 2^{n-1}\prod_i\varrho_i^{-1}C'
 e^{-\kappa d_j(X)}
 e^{-\kappa_\sigma\max\{a_1,a_2\}/L^j}.
\]
In bare lattice units,
$\mathsf dL^K\le a_1+\operatorname{diam}X+a_2$.
Also
$\operatorname{diam}X\le
c_{\mathcal D}ML^j(1+d_j(X))$.
If $\operatorname{diam}X\ge\mathsf dL^K/2$, half
the polymer decay gives
$e^{\kappa/2}e^{-\kappa_{\rm E}\mathsf d/\lambda_j}$.
Otherwise $\max(a_1,a_2)>\mathsf dL^K/4$ and half
the source tail gives that factor.  In both cases,
\[
 e^{-\kappa d_j(X)}
 e^{-\kappa_\sigma\max(a_1,a_2)/L^j}
 \le e^{\kappa/2}
 e^{-\kappa_{\rm E}\mathsf d/\lambda_j}
 e^{-\kappa d_j(X)/2}
 e^{-\kappa_\sigma a_1/(2L^j)}.
\]
Assign $X$ to a level-$j$ cube in $X$ nearest $S_1$.
The polymer sum at any assigned cube is at most
$C_{\rm cnt}$.  There are at most
$(2t+3)^3\#_j^+(S_1)$ cubes at distance between
$tML^j$ and $(t+1)ML^j$ from $S_1$.
Summing the last display proves the stated bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Contact terms after the restart]\label{C-429-6}
Under the hypotheses on sources and radii in
\cref{C-429-5}, for $t_0<j\le t_1$,
\[
 \sum_{X\in\mathcal D_j}
 |\partial^{[n]}\hat e_j(X;s(z))|
 \le2^{n-1}\prod_i\varrho_i^{-1}
 C_{\mathfrak E}C_{\mathscr C}^{\natural}
 \#_j^+(\operatorname{supp}\mathbf s_1)
 e^{-\kappa_{\rm E}\mathsf d/\lambda_j}.
\]
Choose $C_{\mathscr C}\ge
C_{\mathfrak E}C_{\mathscr C}^{\natural}$.
Then the scalar removed between $t_0$ and $t_1$ satisfies
\[
 |\partial^{[n]}\hat c^\bullet(s(z))|
 \le2^{n-1}\prod_i\varrho_i^{-1}
 (\mathscr C_{t_1}-\mathscr C_{t_0})
       (\operatorname{supp}\mathbf s_1;\mathsf d)
 \le2^{n-1}\prod_i\varrho_i^{-1}
 \mathscr C_{t_1}(\operatorname{supp}\mathbf s_1;\mathsf d).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Apply \cref{C-429-5} to the functions in
\cref{C-429-4}(c).  The identity
\[
 \hat c^\bullet(s)=
 \sum_{t_0<j\le t_1}
   \left(\hat e_jn_j+
     \sum_{X\in\mathcal D_j}\hat e_j(X;s)\right)
\]
is a finite sum of holomorphic functions on the torus.
The numbers $\hat e_jn_j$ have zero mixed derivative.
Sum the first bound and use
\[
 \mathscr C_k(S;\mathsf d)
 =C_{\mathscr C}\sum_{j\le k}
       \#_j^+(S)e^{-\kappa_{\rm E}\mathsf d/\lambda_j}.
\]
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Choice of the contact constant.}\label{C-429-8}
The new constant $C_{\mathscr C}^{\natural}$ is fixed
after $\kappa_\sigma$, from $\kappa,\kappa_\sigma,M$ and
$C_{\rm cnt}$.  The floor
$C_{\mathscr C}\ge C_{\mathfrak E}C_{\mathscr C}^{\natural}$
is imposed at the original choice of
$C_{\mathscr C}=27C_{\mathscr C}^0$, after $h_F$ and
$C_{\mathfrak E}$ and before the mass interval.
It creates no circular dependence: no preceding constant
depends on $C_{\mathscr C}$ and no ceiling bounds it above.
The original proof of the separated-source estimate is
the proof of \cref{C-429-5} applied to the unrestarted
energies, so it remains valid with this larger constant.
The other uses are upper bounds by nonnegative multiples
of $\mathscr C$.  In the overlap estimate the apparent
denominator is paired with $C'_{\mathscr C}$:
$C'_{\mathscr C}/C_{\mathscr C}$ bounds the same
geometric sum independently of $C_{\mathscr C}$.
Thus $C'_{\mathscr C}$ and all other dependent constants
are formed afterwards at the enlarged value.
