The preceding propositions prove the source-energy and
contact-term assertions of \cref{C-418-16}, including
holomorphy on $\mathscr O_{j-1}$ and the difference of
counts $\mathscr C_{t_1}-\mathscr C_{t_0}$.

\subsection{Comparing two integration weights}

The weights in the two restart integrals can have different supports.
The following lemma separates the error on their common support from
the mass lost at its boundary.

\begin{lemma}\label{IV-57-13}
Let \(\nu\) be a finite measure on \(Y\), and let
\(k^{\mathrm A},k^{\mathrm B}\) be bounded nonnegative measurable
functions.  Let \(D\subset\mathbb C^n\) contain zero.  For
\(\bullet=\mathrm A,\mathrm B\), suppose that \(F_z^\bullet\)
is bounded and measurable for every \(z\in D\).  Assume that
\(0\le\epsilon,\delta\le1/8\) and that the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item On \(\{k^\bullet>0\}\),
\(F_0^\bullet\ge0\) and
\(F_z^\bullet=F_0^\bullet e^{\psi_z^\bullet}\), where
\(|\psi_z^\bullet|\le1/4\).
\item On the common support,
\(k^{\mathrm A}=k^{\mathrm B}\) and
\(F_z^{\mathrm B}=F_z^{\mathrm A}e^{\xi_z}\), where
\(|\xi_z|\le\epsilon\).
\item For either choice of \(\bullet\), with \(\circ\) the other,
\[
 \int k^\bullet\mathbf1_{\{k^\circ=0\}}|F_z^\bullet|\,d\nu
 \le\delta\int k^\bullet|F_z^\bullet|\,d\nu.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Put \(T^\bullet(z)=\int k^\bullet F_z^\bullet\,d\nu\), and
assume \(T^{\mathrm A}(0)>0\).  Then
\begin{equation}\label{IV-57-14}
 \begin{split}
 \int|k^{\mathrm A}F_z^{\mathrm A}-k^{\mathrm B}F_z^{\mathrm B}|\,d\nu
 &\le e^{1/4}(2\epsilon+3\delta)T^{\mathrm A}(0),\\
 |T^{\mathrm A}(z)|&\ge e^{-1/4}\cos(1/4)T^{\mathrm A}(0),\\
 \left|\frac{T^{\mathrm B}(z)}{T^{\mathrm A}(z)}-1\right|
 &\le4\epsilon+6\delta.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
At \(z=0\), the first bound holds with the factor \(e^{1/4}\)
replaced by one.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write \(q_z=e^{1/4}\) for \(z\ne0\), and \(q_0=1\).
Positivity at zero and (i) give
\(\int k^\bullet|F_z^\bullet|\,d\nu\le q_zT^\bullet(0)\).
Split the difference of the two integrands over the common support
and the two sets on which just one weight is positive.  Conditions
(ii) and (iii) yield
\begin{equation}\label{IV-57-16}
 \int|k^{\mathrm A}F_z^{\mathrm A}-k^{\mathrm B}F_z^{\mathrm B}|\,d\nu
 \le q_z\bigl[(e^\epsilon-1+\delta)T^{\mathrm A}(0)
                          +\delta T^{\mathrm B}(0)\bigr].
\end{equation}
At zero, the same decomposition and positivity give
\[
 T^{\mathrm B}(0)\le e^\epsilon T^{\mathrm A}(0)
                         +\delta T^{\mathrm B}(0).
\]
Thus \(T^{\mathrm B}(0)\le e^{1/8}(1-1/8)^{-1}
T^{\mathrm A}(0)\le2T^{\mathrm A}(0)\).  Inserting this and
\(e^\epsilon-1\le2\epsilon\) into \eqref{IV-57-16} proves
the first bound, including its improvement at zero.

On \(\{k^{\mathrm A}>0\}\), condition (i) also gives
\(\operatorname{Re}F_z^{\mathrm A}\ge
e^{-1/4}\cos(1/4)F_0^{\mathrm A}\).  Integration proves the
second bound.  Divide the first by this lower bound and use
\(e^{1/2}/\cos(1/4)<2\) to obtain the third.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Transferring fluctuation tails between weights}

The comparison uses the weight of the history with no large-field
region, whereas the change of variables uses the small-field weight.
The following observation transfers tail bounds between them.  Its
error is the total mass of discarded histories.

\begin{proposition}[Comparison of the two weights]\label{C-429-7}
Use the data of \cref{C-429-2} and assume
$L^u\gamma^{-2}\ge\Theta_\star$.
Use the notation of \cref{C-421-2}, and put
\[
 V_k=\mathcal M^kU,\qquad
 N_{\rm bd}=\sum_{k=t_0}^{t_1-1}\#\mathfrak X_k^+.
\]
Let $\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}$ be the weight of the small-field
chain up to level $t_1$, at the calibration
$x_j=L^{K-j}\mathsf b$, and set
\[
 \mathfrak w^\chi(U)=
 \chi_{t_1}(T_\ell)(V_{t_1})\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}(U).
\]
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)]
The two weights are nonnegative bounded Borel functions,
\[
 \mathfrak w_\emptyset\le\mathfrak w^\chi
 \le\mathfrak w^{\rm sf},
\]
and all three agree wherever $\mathfrak w_\emptyset\ne0$.
For every nonnegative gauge-invariant bounded Borel $F$,
\[
 \int F\mathfrak w_\emptyset\varsigma_0\,dU
 \le\int F\mathfrak w^\chi\varsigma_0\,dU
 \le\int F\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}\varsigma_0\,dU
 \le\int F\varsigma_0\,dU.
\]
In particular,
$T(0)\le\int\mathfrak w^\chi\varsigma_0
\le\int\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}\varsigma_0\le Z$.
\item[(b)]
Let $\mathfrak w'$ be any Borel weight satisfying
$\mathfrak w'\ge\mathfrak w_\emptyset$ and
$\int\mathfrak w'\varsigma_0\,dU\le Z$.
For every Borel $F$ with values in $[0,1]$,
\[
 \int F\mathfrak w'\varsigma_0\,dU
 \le\int F\mathfrak w_\emptyset\varsigma_0\,dU
       +Z-T(0)
 \le\int F\mathfrak w_\emptyset\varsigma_0\,dU
       +\mathsf R_{t_1}^{\rm F}Z.
\]
This applies to both weights in (a).
\item[(c)]
For the uniform mark with parameter $r>0$,
\[
 \sum_{k=t_0}^{t_1-1}\sum_{b\in\mathfrak X_k^+}
 \int\mathfrak w_\emptyset
       \bar\chi_{k,b}(V_k)\varsigma_0\,dU
 \le\frac{T_0(r)-T(0)}r,
 \qquad
 \int\mathfrak w_\emptyset\mathbf1_{\{N\ge1\}}
       \varsigma_0\,dU
 \le\frac{T_0(r)-T(0)}r.
\]
With $\mathfrak w'$ as in (b), the corresponding bounds are
\[
 \begin{split}
 \sum_{k,b}\int\mathfrak w'\bar\chi_{k,b}(V_k)
       \varsigma_0\,dU
 &\le\frac{T_0(r)-T(0)}r
          +N_{\rm bd}\mathsf R_{t_1}^{\rm F}Z,\\
 \int\mathfrak w'\mathbf1_{\{N\ge1\}}\varsigma_0\,dU
 &\le\frac{T_0(r)-T(0)}r
          +\mathsf R_{t_1}^{\rm F}Z.
 \end{split}
\]
Moreover $N_{\rm bd}\le4N_{[s]}$.
\end{enumerate}
Here $r$ is the mark parameter, independently of the
Wilson parameter fixed in the model.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The depth assumption gives the small-field and one-weight
settings on both lattices: apply the gauge comparison
admission at cutoff $K^{\rm A}$ with
$t_*=K^{\rm A}-u$.  Since $1\le u<s<K^{\rm A}$ and
$\mathsf b\ge\gamma^{-2}$, we have
$1\le t_*\le K^{\rm A}-1$ and
$L^u\mathsf b\ge\Theta_\star$.
The resulting top levels are $t_1^{\rm A}$ and
$t_1^{\rm A}+1=t_1^{\rm B}$.
The calibrations are the original
$x_j=L^{K-j}\mathsf b=\mathsf t_j$ and $x_0=\beta$.
Thus the bare gauge density in the weight comparison is
$e^{-\beta A}$, and its history weight is exactly
$\mathfrak w_\emptyset$.

The gauge weight comparison gives a bounded nonnegative
Borel $\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}$ with
$\mathfrak w_\emptyset\le\mathfrak w^{\rm sf}$ and
equality on $\{\mathfrak w_\emptyset\ne0\}$.
The density test is Borel and $\mathcal M^{t_1}$ is Borel.
The last step of this history factors as
\[
 \mathfrak w_\emptyset(U)=
 \mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset^{(t_1-1)}}(U)
 \chi_{t_1}(T_\ell)(V_{t_1})
 \mathsf q^0_{t_1-1}(V_{t_1-1})
 \mathsf q_{t_1}(V_{t_1-1})
 \mathfrak G_{t_1-1}[x_{t_1-1}](V_{t_1-1})
 \chi^{\rm sf}_{x_{t_1-1}}(V_{t_1-1}).
\]
It follows that $\chi_{t_1}(T_\ell)=1$ wherever
$\mathfrak w_\emptyset\ne0$; this proves the pointwise
statements in (a).

To apply the gauge integral inequality, replace its
test function by
$\widetilde F(U)=F(U)\det(D[U]+m_0)$.
This is nonnegative, bounded and Borel.  Boundedness
follows from the uniform finite-dimensional bound on
$D[U]$, and the determinant is polynomial in the link
entries.  Gauge covariance
$D[U^\theta]=\theta D[U]\theta^{-1}$
makes $\widetilde F$ gauge invariant.  The gauge inequality
therefore gives the final inequality of (a), because
$e^{-\beta A}\det(D+m_0)=\varsigma_0$.
The other inequalities follow pointwise.

For (b), positivity gives
\[
 \int F(\mathfrak w'-\mathfrak w_\emptyset)
        \varsigma_0\,dU
 \le\int(\mathfrak w'-\mathfrak w_\emptyset)
        \varsigma_0\,dU
 \le Z-T(0).
\]
The last inequality in (b) is
\cref{C-421-5}(a) at $t=t_1$.  Gauge invariance of $F$
is not needed in this step.

Finally the uniform mark is
$\mathsf{Mk}_r=(1+r)^N\ge1+rN$, with integer $N\ge0$.
Integrate this inequality against the positive measure
$\mathfrak w_\emptyset\varsigma_0\,dU$.  Since
$N=\sum_{k,b}\bar\chi_{k,b}(V_k)$ and
$\mathbf1_{\{N\ge1\}}\le N$, it proves the first two
bounds in (c).  Each $\bar\chi_{k,b}\circ\mathcal M^k$
is a Borel indicator; consequently $N$ and
$\mathbf1_{\{N\ge1\}}$ are Borel.  Applying (b) to these
indicators proves the bounds for $\mathfrak w'$.
There are at most $3n_k$ positively oriented bonds at
level $k$, so
\[
 N_{\rm bd}\le
 3\ell^3\sum_{k=t_0}^{t_1-1}L^{3(K-k)}
 \le3\ell^3L^{3s}\sum_{i\ge0}L^{-3i}
 \le4\ell^3L^{3s}=4N_{[s]}.
\]
\end{proof}

\subsection{Comparing the logarithms of scalar totals}

The difference estimates permit interpolation between the original
flow and its restart on a large complex disc.  An upper bound on that
disc, together with a positive lower bound at the original flow,
controls the difference of their logarithms.  The radius of the disc
will supply the small factor.

\begin{definition}[Scalar totals and fluctuation marks]\label{C-421-2}
Fix a datum $(g,\ell,K,\mathsf b,\mathsf m)$ and
$1\le u<s<K$, and put
\[
 t_0=K-s,\quad t_1=K-u,\quad
 N_{[d]}=\ell^3L^{3d},\quad
 \mathsf y_{[d]}=(\log(L^d\mathsf b))^{2\mathfrak p_0}.
\]
The calibration is $\mathsf t_k=L^{K-k}\mathsf b$,
$n_k=\ell^3L^{3(K-k)}$, and the creation deposit is
$p_0(g_k)^2=A_0^2(\log\mathsf t_k)^{2\mathfrak p_0}$.
Let $h_\emptyset^{(k)}$ be the history without large-field
regions and
$\mathfrak w_\emptyset=\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset^{(t_1)}}$.

For a tuple $X=((\alpha_i,f_i))_{i\le n}$, $n\ge1$,
with real Lipschitz $f_i$ and no support restriction,
let $s(z)=(w_z,J_z)=\sum_i z_i\mathbf s_i$ be its source.
Define
\[
 \begin{split}
 \varsigma_z(U)&=
 e^{-A(\beta-a_K^{-1}w_z,U)}
       \det(D[U]+m_0-a_K\hat J_z),\\
 Z(z)&=\int\varsigma_z\,dU,\qquad
 T(z)=\int\mathfrak w_\emptyset\varsigma_z\,dU,\qquad
 c(z)=E_{t_1}(s(z)).
 \end{split}
\]
The last expression is used where $s(z)\in\mathscr O_{t_1}$.
Write $Z=Z(0)$ and
$\varsigma_0=e^{-\beta A}\det(D+m_0)\ge0$.
The crude source sizes are
\[
 \mathsf s_i=
 \begin{cases}
 6\ell^3L^{4K}\|f_i\|_\infty,&\alpha_i=0,\\
 \nu\,\#\mathsf R\,a_Km_0^{-1}\|f_i\|_\infty,
                  &\alpha_i\in\mathfrak B,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad \nu=8N_f.
\]

When the one-weight gauge setting holds up to $t_1$, let
$\mathfrak X_k^+$ be the positively oriented non-pivot
bonds at level $k$, and set
\[
 \bar\chi_{k,b}
   =\mathbf1_{\{|\mathcal A_k^\diamond(b)|
                       \ge\delta(\mathsf t_k)/2\}},
 \qquad t_0\le k<t_1.
\]
These are Borel indicators.  The setting holds for both
cutoffs under (k0), (k1).  Put
\[
 \begin{split}
 \mathsf{Mk}_\lambda(U)&=
 \prod_{k=t_0}^{t_1-1}\prod_{b\in\mathfrak X_k^+}
  (1+\lambda_k\bar\chi_{k,b}(\mathcal M^kU)),\\
 N(U)&=\sum_{k=t_0}^{t_1-1}\sum_{b\in\mathfrak X_k^+}
                  \bar\chi_{k,b}(\mathcal M^kU),\\
 T_0(\lambda)&=\int\mathfrak w_\emptyset
                   \mathsf{Mk}_\lambda\varsigma_0\,dU.
 \end{split}
\]
For a scalar $\lambda$ all level parameters are equal,
so that $\mathsf{Mk}_\lambda=(1+\lambda)^N$ and
$T_0(0)=T(0)$.

For $k<K$ write $a_k=\mathfrak b(\mathsf t_k)/2$;
this $a_k$ is the mark threshold, while $a_K=L^{-K}$
remains the lattice spacing.  With $w_*=c_{\rm cl}$, set
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \kappa_{\rm mk}&=\frac{w_*}{32M^3},&
 \mathsf r_k&=\kappa_{\rm mk}a_k^2-\pi,&
 \epsilon_k^{\rm mk}(\lambda)&=
       \frac{w_*}{32}\frac{|\lambda|}{e^{\mathsf r_k}-1},\\
 \Lambda_{\rm mk}&=
 \exp\left[\frac{\kappa_{\rm mk}A_1^2}{4}
                    \mathsf y_{[u]}\right],&
 \theta_{\rm dis}&=\tfrac12(c_\star-c_\Theta)>0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The expression for $\epsilon_k^{\rm mk}$ requires
$\mathsf r_k>0$.
For $t_0\le k<t_1$,
$e^{\mathsf r_k}\ge e^{-\pi}\Lambda_{\rm mk}$.
Finally,
\[
 \mathsf Q_\ell=
 e^{[C+2+C_P(1+\log x_K)]\ell^3}
 \le\mathsf M_{g,\ell}
 :=e^{[C+2+C_P(1+\log X_g)]\ell^3},
 \qquad
 \mathsf R_t^{\rm F}
 =\mathsf Q_\ell e^{-\theta_{\rm dis}p_0(g_t)^2}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Two values of a holomorphic family]\label{C-421-3}
Let $n\ge1$, $R_i>0$, $\mathsf Q\ge1$ and
$\rho\ge1+8\mathsf Q$.  Put
\[
 \theta=\frac1{4(\mathsf Q+1)},\quad
 \mathbb D_\rho=\{|\tau-1|<\rho\},\quad
 \mathbb P(R)=\{|z_i|<R_i\}.
\]
Suppose $H$ is holomorphic on
$\mathbb D_\rho\times\mathbb P(R)$,
$H(1,0)>0$, and $|H|\le\mathsf QH(1,0)$ there.
Then on $|\tau-1|\le1$, $|z_i|\le\theta R_i$,
\[
 \left|\frac{H(\tau,z)}{H(1,0)}-1\right|\le\tfrac38.
\]
In particular $H$ has no zero there, and
\[
 \left|\frac{H(1,z)}{H(0,z)}-1\right|
 \le\frac{8\mathsf Q}{5(\rho-1)}\le\tfrac15.
\]
For continuous logarithms on this polydisc,
\[
 \left|\partial^{[n]}[
      \log H(1,\cdot)-\log H(0,\cdot)](0)\right|
 \le\frac{(4(\mathsf Q+1))^{n+1}}{2(\rho-1)}
                       \prod_iR_i^{-1}.
\]
If $H(0,0)$ is real, then
$H(0,0)\ge5H(1,0)/8$.
Moreover, if $G$ is holomorphic on the same domain and
$|G(\tau,z)-a-b\tau|\le B$, then
\[
 |\partial^{[n]}[G(1,\cdot)-G(0,\cdot)](0)|
 \le B(\rho-1)^{-1}\prod_iR_i^{-1}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Normalize $h=H/H(1,0)$.  Cauchy's estimate in $\tau$
on discs of radius approaching $\rho-1$ gives
$|\partial_\tau h|\le\mathsf Q/(\rho-1)$ for
$|\tau-1|\le1$.  Thus
$|h(\tau,z)-h(1,z)|\le1/8$.
For $|z_i|\le\theta R_i$, Schwarz's lemma applied to
$h(1,\zeta z/\theta)-1$ gives
$|h(1,z)-1|\le(\mathsf Q+1)\theta=1/4$.
This proves the first estimate.  The difference
$h(1,z)-h(0,z)$ is at most $\mathsf Q/(\rho-1)$ and
$|h(0,z)|\ge5/8$, proving the quotient estimate.
The principal logarithm of that quotient is bounded by
$2\mathsf Q/(\rho-1)$, since
$|\operatorname{Log}(1+w)|\le5|w|/4$ for $|w|\le1/5$.
Cauchy's estimate on the source polydisc gives the
claimed mixed derivative.  Changing continuous branches
adds a constant and does not affect it.  The real
lower bound follows from the first estimate.
For the last assertion apply the same $\tau$ estimate
to $G-a-b\tau$, integrate from zero to one, and apply
Cauchy's estimate in $z$; $n\ge1$ removes the constant $b$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Readout at depth $u$]\label{C-421-4}
Use \cref{C-421-2}.  Suppose $s(z)\in\mathcal P$ on
$\mathbb P(R)$, $\rho\ge1+8\mathsf Q_\ell$,
and $\hat c$ is holomorphic there.
Let $I,E_>$ be holomorphic on
$\mathbb D_\rho\times\mathbb P(R)$ and suppose
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 I(1,z)=e^{-c(z)}T(z),\qquad
 E_>(1,0)=E_K-E_{t_1},\\
 |I(\tau,z)|\le
 e^{\operatorname{Re}E_>(\tau,z)+(C+2)\ell^3},
 \qquad |E_>(\tau,z)-a-b\tau|\le B.
 \end{gathered}
\]
Set $\hat T(z)=e^{\hat c(z)}I(0,z)$ and
$\theta_\ell=1/[4(\mathsf Q_\ell+1)]$.
Then
\[
 I(1,0)e^{-E_>(1,0)}
 \ge e^{-C_P(1+\log x_K)\ell^3}>0.
\]
For $|z_i|\le\theta_\ell R_i$, $T$ and $\hat T$
are nonzero and
\[
 \left|
 \frac{T(z)e^{-c(z)-E_>(1,z)}}
      {\hat T(z)e^{-\hat c(z)-E_>(0,z)}}-1
 \right|\le\frac{8\mathsf Q_\ell}{5(\rho-1)}.
\]
Their continuous logarithms satisfy
\[
 \left|\partial^{[n]}
 [\log T-\log\hat T-(c-\hat c)](0)\right|
 \le\left[\tfrac12(4(\mathsf Q_\ell+1))^{n+1}+B\right]
          (\rho-1)^{-1}\prod_iR_i^{-1}.
\]
Also
\[
 |\hat T(0)|\ge\tfrac58
 e^{\operatorname{Re}(\hat c(0)+E_>(0,0))
                         -C_P(1+\log x_K)\ell^3}.
\]
If $\hat c(0)+E_>(0,0)$ and $\hat T(0)$ are real,
the last estimate holds without absolute values.
One may replace $\mathsf Q_\ell$ by
$\mathsf M_{g,\ell}$ throughout the radii and bounds.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
At every level the threshold is at most
$\varepsilon_\flat$, because
$\mathsf t_j\ge\gamma^{-2}$ and the initial ceiling
gives $\varepsilon(\gamma^{-2})\le\varepsilon_\flat$.
Thus history consistency applies between $t_1$ and $K$.
The determinant density is nonnegative and gauge invariant,
and all history weights are nonnegative.  Hence
\[
 T(0)=
 \sum_{h|_{t_1}=h_\emptyset^{(t_1)}}t^{\rm F}(h)
 \ge t^{\rm F}(h_\emptyset^{(K)})
 \ge e^{E_K-C_P(1+\log x_K)\ell^3}.
\]
The last inequality is the positive last-level estimate
of the original construction.  Since $c(0)=E_{t_1}$,
it proves the first assertion.
Now $H=Ie^{-E_>}$ satisfies the hypotheses of
\cref{C-421-3} with $\mathsf Q=\mathsf Q_\ell$.
Its quotient gives the asserted quotient; the difference
of logarithms of $I$ is the sum of that for $H$ and
the difference of $E_>$.  Apply both derivative estimates
of the lemma.  Finally
$\hat T(0)=e^{\hat c(0)+E_>(0,0)}H(0,0)$ gives the
last estimate and its real version.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The interpolated scalar family]\label{C-421-14}
Assume (k0)--(k2) for either cutoff and the source tuple
of \cref{C-418-2}(5).  At base $t_b=t_1$, use the
interpolated measure $\rho^{(t_1)}_{s,\lambda}$
of \cref{C-418-4} and the continued energies of
\cref{C-418-17}, with $\Lambda_b=\Lambda$.
Define, for $\lambda=1-\tau$,
\[
 \begin{split}
 I(\tau,z)&=e^{-E_{t_1}(s(z))}
       \operatorname{Ber}\rho^{(t_1)}_{s(z),1-\tau}
                                   (\mathcal V_{t_1}),\\
 E_>(\tau,z)&=E_K(s(z),1-\tau)-E_{t_1}(s(z)),\\
 \rho&=r_\lambda,\qquad
 a=E_K-E_{t_1}+d_b,\qquad b=-d_b,\\
 B&=C'_EN_{[u]},\qquad
 C'_E=\frac{C_{\mathfrak E}C_{\rm cnt}}{M^3(L^3-1)}.
 \end{split}
\]
Here $d_b$ is independent of $s$, and all generators are
integrated in the Berezin integral.
These functions satisfy \cref{C-421-4} on
$\mathbb D_\rho\times\mathbb P(2R)$.
Its function $\hat T$ is the actual restarted total
$\hat T^\bullet$, with
$\hat c(z)=\hat c^\bullet(s(z))$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The conditions in (k1) give $u\ge u_*$,
$e^{-c_{\rm t}L^u}\le L^{-c_\#(s-u)}$, and
$s\ge s_F$.  Thus \cref{C-418-9,C-418-10} apply.
The lag sums at $t_1$ hold with $\Lambda$.
By (k2), $r_\lambda\ge16\mathsf M_{g,\ell}\ge16$
and
$\Lambda=2(3L^{1/2})^ur_\lambda/c_\lambda\ge32$.
The perturbations therefore satisfy
\cref{C-418-17}, whose parameter radius is
$\rho_b=\tfrac12(3L^{1/2})^{-u}c_\lambda\Lambda
=r_\lambda$.

On $\mathbb P(2R)$ the source bounds are
$\|w_z\|_\sharp<(1-c_\lambda)\varrho$ and
$\|J_z\|_\infty<(1-c_\lambda)\varrho_J$.
Consequently $(s(z),1-\tau)\in\mathcal D_b$ for
$|\tau-1|\le r_\lambda$, and lies in its interior
for strict inequality.  More explicitly, the open set
\[
 \|w\|_\sharp<(2-c_\lambda)\varrho,\qquad
 \|J\|_\infty<2\varrho_J,\qquad |\lambda|<\rho_b
\]
lies in $\mathcal D_b$ and contains these points.
The shift in the source above the base also stays in
the permitted region, because (L3) gives
\[
 \|\lambda\hat w_b\|_\sharp
 \le r_\lambda\Lambda^{-1}\varrho
 =\tfrac12(3L^{1/2})^{-u}c_\lambda\varrho
 <c_\lambda\varrho.
\]

We spell out holomorphy of the integral because its
density need only be Borel in the field.
The exact history identity gives
\[
 e^{E_{t_1}(s(z))}I(\tau,z)
 =\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_K^{(t_1)}}
     \int\operatorname{Ber}g_h[s(z),1-\tau]\,
                                  d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}.
\]
There are finitely many histories.  Replace each density
by the pointwise holomorphic Borel representative
$\mathsf g_h$ of \cref{C-422-14}.
The two representatives agree almost everywhere,
coefficient by coefficient, since they represent the
same measure; their integrals and integrated fibre
norms therefore agree.  On the open domain just described,
each coefficient of $\mathsf g_h$ is holomorphic in
$(s,\lambda)$ at every field point.
Its integral in absolute value is bounded by
\[
 \exp[\operatorname{Re}E_K(s(z),1-\tau)+(C+2)\ell^3],
\]
using $|\operatorname{Ber}F|\le\|F\|_{h_F}$ and
\cref{C-418-17}(B3).  This is locally bounded in
$(\tau,z)$ by (B4).  On a closed polydisc about any
parameter point, Cauchy's formula on the distinguished
boundary and Tonelli's theorem give an integrable
majorant on the polydisc with half its radii.
The integrands are jointly Borel, since they are Borel
in the field and continuous in the parameters.
Integration consequently preserves holomorphy.
This proves that $I$ is holomorphic.

The energy identity is
\[
 E_>(\tau,z)=(1-\tau)d_b+
 \sum_{t_1<j\le K}\left(
       e_jn_j+\sum_{X\in\mathcal D_j}
                  e_j(X;s(z),1-\tau)\right).
\]
It proves holomorphy of $E_>$.
The source energies of the restart prove holomorphy
of $\hat c$ by \cref{C-429-4}.
At $\lambda=0$ the measure is the original term, giving
$I(1,z)=e^{-c(z)}T(z)$.
At $\lambda=1$ it is
$e^{E_{t_1}(s)-\hat c^\bullet(s)}$ times the restarted
term, giving $I(0,z)=e^{-\hat c(z)}\hat T^\bullet(z)$.

The history bound gives
$|I|\le e^{\operatorname{Re}E_>+(C+2)\ell^3}$.
At $(\tau,z)=(1,0)$ the source energies vanish, so
$E_>(1,0)=E_K-E_{t_1}$.
Finally,
\[
 \begin{split}
 |E_>-a-b\tau|
 &\le C_{\mathfrak E}\sum_{t_1<j\le K}
                 \sum_{X\in\mathcal D_j}e^{-\kappa d_j(X)}\\
 &\le C_{\mathfrak E}C_{\rm cnt}M^{-3}
                    \sum_{t_1<j\le K}n_j\\
 &=C_{\mathfrak E}C_{\rm cnt}M^{-3}\ell^3
                    \frac{L^{3u}-1}{L^3-1}
 \le C'_EN_{[u]}.
 \end{split}
\]
Here each polymer is assigned to a cube it contains;
there are at most $n_j/M^3$ cubes.
Since $\rho=r_\lambda\ge16\mathsf M_{g,\ell}
\ge1+8\mathsf Q_\ell$, all hypotheses of
\cref{C-421-4} are verified.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Discarding histories and summing contact terms}

\begin{proposition}[Discarding early large-field regions]\label{C-421-5}
For $1\le t\le K$, put
$T_t(z)=\int\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset^{(t)}}\varsigma_z\,dU$.
Then
\[
 Z-T_t(0)=
 \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_K:\,Z_t(h)\ne\varnothing}t^{\rm F}(h),
 \qquad
 0\le Z-T_t(0)\le\mathsf R_t^{\rm F}Z.
\]
For every source tuple of \cref{C-421-2}, with no
restriction on its supports, set
$\sigma(z)=\sum_i|z_i|\mathsf s_i$.  Then
\[
 |Z(z)-T_t(z)|
 \le e^{\sigma(z)}(Z-T_t(0))
 \le e^{\sigma(z)}\mathsf R_t^{\rm F}Z.
\]
If $\mathsf R_t^{\rm F}\le1/8$, then $T_t$ has no
zero on $\{4n\mathsf s_i|z_i|\le1\text{ for all }i\}$,
and
\[
 \left|S^T_{n;K,\ell,\beta,m_0}(X)
       -\partial^{[n]}\log T_t(0)\right|
 \le3\mathsf R_t^{\rm F}\prod_i(4n\mathsf s_i).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
History consistency gives
$T_t(0)=\sum_{h|_t=h_\emptyset^{(t)}}t^{\rm F}(h)$.
At $t=K$ this is the single term
$t^{\rm F}(h_\emptyset^{(K)})$.
The remaining histories are exactly those with
$Z_t(h)\ne\varnothing$.  Positivity of their scalar
measures proves the identity and its lower bound.

We retain part of the creation deposit before summing.
For $\mathcal S=\mathcal S(h)$, the original construction
gives the pair
\[
 f(h)=e^{-E_K+\sum_n\operatorname{Re}f_n(\mathcal S)}
       \int\|\mathsf g_h\|\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr},
 \qquad
 \mathsf e(\mathcal S)=-\sum_n\operatorname{Re}f_n(\mathcal S)
\]
at the rate $c_\star$ and the fixed majorant and label
constants.  Put
$c=c_\star-\theta_{\rm dis}
=(c_\star+c_\Theta)/2$ and
\[
 f'(h)=f(h)\exp\left[
 \theta_{\rm dis}\sum_{t'=1}^K
          p_0(g_{t'})^2\mathsf n_{t'}^{\rm cr}(h)\right].
\]
Each created cell now has rate $c$ instead of $c_\star$,
so $(f',\mathsf e)$ is an admissible pair at rate $c$.
The enlarged majorant and label constants used in the
source construction weaken its inequalities and remain
admissible.

Use the history mark with deposit dials
$(\mathsf w',c'_{\rm Dep})=(c_\Theta/c,c)$.
Then $\mathsf w'<1$, including when $c_\Theta=0$.
The thresholds at rate $c$ are among the original
ceilings on $\gamma$; in the calibration frame,
$y_K=\log\mathsf b\ge\log\gamma^{-2}$ meets them.
The history sum gives
\[
 \sum_h f'(h)e^{\mathsf e(\mathcal S(h))}e^{\Theta'(h)}
 \le\Pi_K(C,c'')\le e^{(C+2)\ell^3},
 \qquad
 c''=\tfrac12(1-\eth)(c_\star-c_\Theta)>0.
\]
The constant $C$ contains the enlarged majorant and,
when $c_a>0$, the additional
$(6L^3+1)\log2$ required by that sum.
If $Z_t(h)\ne\varnothing$, at least one cell was
created at a level $t'\le t$.  Since
$p_0(g_{t'})^2\ge p_0(g_t)^2$ and $\Theta'\ge0$,
\[
 \sum_{Z_t(h)\ne\varnothing}e^{-E_K}
        \int\|\mathsf g_h\|\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}
 \le e^{-\theta_{\rm dis}p_0(g_t)^2+(C+2)\ell^3}.
\]
Use
$t^{\rm F}(h)\le\int\|\mathsf g_h\|\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}$
and
$Z\ge e^{E_K-C_P(1+\log x_K)\ell^3}$
to obtain the first upper bound.

The same exact history identity holds with the complex
density $\varsigma_z$: it is bounded, Borel and gauge
invariant.  Since $m_0>0$,
$\varsigma_z=\varsigma_0G_z$, where
\[
 G_z(U)=e^{\mathcal O(w_z)(U)}
          \det(1-\mathsf X_z(U)),\qquad
 \mathsf X_z=a_K(D[U]+m_0)^{-1}\hat J_z.
\]
The action term is at most
$\sum_{\alpha_i=0}|z_i|\mathsf s_i$ in modulus.
Accretivity gives $\|(D+m_0)^{-1}\|\le m_0^{-1}$;
the trace norm of $\mathsf X_z$ is consequently at
most $\sum_{\alpha_i\ne0}|z_i|\mathsf s_i$.
Its eigenvalues have total absolute value at most
this trace norm.  Expanding the product
$\det(1-\mathsf X_z)$ therefore yields
\[
 |G_z|\le e^{\sigma(z)},\qquad
 |G_z-1|\le e^{\sigma(z)}-1.
\]
Integration against the nonnegative history weights
proves the source bound.

On the indicated closed set $\sigma(z)\le1/4$, so
$|Z(z)|\ge(2-e^{1/4})Z$.
Thus
\[
 q(z)=\frac{Z(z)-T_t(z)}{Z(z)}
 \quad\text{satisfies}\quad
 |q|\le1.8\mathsf R_t^{\rm F}\le0.225.
\]
It follows that $T_t=Z(1-q)$ is nonzero and
$|\operatorname{Log}(1-q)|\le3\mathsf R_t^{\rm F}$.
Cauchy's estimate on the polydisc
$|z_i|\le(4n\mathsf s_i)^{-1}$ gives the mixed
derivative bound.  If some $\mathsf s_i=0$, then
$f_i=0$ and both mixed derivatives and the right
side vanish, so no radius need be assigned to that variable.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Summing the contact energies]\label{C-421-6}
Let $n\ge2$ and use the separated sources and radii
of \cref{C-429-5}.  Suppose
\[
 \kappa_{\rm E}\mathsf dL^u(L-1)\ge3\log L+\log2.
 \tag{Sep}
\]
Then
\[
 |\partial^{[n]}E_{t_1}(s(z))|
 \le2^nC_{\mathscr C}M^{-3}N_{[u]}
     e^{-\kappa_{\rm E}\mathsf dL^u}\prod_i\varrho_i^{-1}.
\]
More generally let $\mathcal J\subset\{1,\ldots,t_1\}$
and let $f_j(X;s(z))$ be holomorphic near the closed
source polydisc, with source tails as in
\cref{C-429-5} at constant $C'C_{\mathfrak E}$.
Then, at each level,
\[
 \sum_X|\partial^{[n]}f_j(X;s(z))|
 \le2^{n-1}\prod_i\varrho_i^{-1}
 C'C_{\mathscr C}\#_j^+(\operatorname{supp}\mathbf s_1)
                  e^{-\kappa_{\rm E}\mathsf d/\lambda_j}.
\]
Its sum $\hat c=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\sum_Xf_j$ satisfies
\[
 |\partial^{[n]}\hat c|
 \le2^{n-1}C'\mathscr C_{t_1}
       (\operatorname{supp}\mathbf s_1;\mathsf d)
       \prod_i\varrho_i^{-1}
 \le2^nC'C_{\mathscr C}M^{-3}N_{[u]}
       e^{-\kappa_{\rm E}\mathsf dL^u}\prod_i\varrho_i^{-1}.
\]
In particular the difference $c-\hat c$ between the
original and restarted scalar energies has this last
bound with $C'$ replaced by $2$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The level estimate is \cref{C-429-5}, using
$C_{\mathfrak E}C_{\mathscr C}^{\natural}\le C_{\mathscr C}$.
It applies to the original source energies and, by
\cref{C-429-4}, to the restarted energies, with $C'=1$.
For every support $S$,
$\#_j^+(S)\le n_j/M^3$.
Write $j=t_1-m$.  Then
$n_j=N_{[u]}L^{3m}$,
$\mathsf d/\lambda_j=\mathsf dL^{u+m}$, and
$L^m-1\ge m(L-1)$.  Therefore
\[
 \mathscr C_{t_1}(S;\mathsf d)
 \le C_{\mathscr C}M^{-3}N_{[u]}
 e^{-\kappa_{\rm E}\mathsf dL^u}
 \sum_{m\ge0}
 \left(L^3e^{-\kappa_{\rm E}\mathsf dL^u(L-1)}\right)^m
 \le2C_{\mathscr C}M^{-3}N_{[u]}
          e^{-\kappa_{\rm E}\mathsf dL^u}.
\]
This proves all assertions.  The usual choice
$\varrho_i=\varrho_{\alpha_i}/(n\|f_i\|_{\alpha_i})$
is admissible: it gives $\|w_z\|_\sharp\le\varrho$
and $\|J_z\|_\infty\le\varrho_J$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Adding a fluctuation mark to one step}

The mark is a bounded Borel function of the real fluctuation.
We first estimate it on a large torus of complex parameters.
The individual terms of the expansion are polynomials in those
parameters, so the maximum principle extends the estimate across
the entire polydisc, including the value zero.

\begin{lemma}[The additional origin in the expansion]\label{C-421-8}
Consider an admitted step from $k$ to $k+1$, at radius $a$,
with potential size
$\varepsilon_{\rm V}+\varepsilon_\natural\le c_{\rm cl}$,
and assume $\mathsf r_k>0$.
For $b\in\mathfrak X_k^+$ put
\[
 \chi_b(B)=\mathbf1_{\{\mathsf t_k|B(b)|^2\ge a_k^2\}},
 \qquad
 \mathcal V_\zeta^{\rm mk}(Y;B)
 =\sum_{\square(b)=Y}(\operatorname{Log}\zeta_b)\chi_b(B).
\]
Here $\square(b)$ is the union of the fine cubes containing
an endpoint of $b$.  It is a polymer of size zero, and
both endpoints lie in its interior bond set.
Initially $\zeta_b\ne0$ and $\operatorname{Log}$ is the
principal logarithm.
Adjoin $\mathcal V_\zeta^{\rm mk}$ to the three origins
of the step, and write its new expansion as
$\widetilde E_{\varpi,\zeta}(X)$.
The original expansion is $\widetilde E_\varpi(X)$; put
$\Delta_{\varpi,\zeta}^{\rm mk}
=\widetilde E_{\varpi,\zeta}-\widetilde E_\varpi$.
Let
\[
 \mathbb T_k=\{|\zeta_b|=e^{\mathsf r_k}\},\qquad
 \mathbb P_k=\{|\zeta_b|\le e^{\mathsf r_k}\}.
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)]
$\|\mathcal V_\zeta^{\rm mk}\|_{\star,\lambda_V}
\le M^3a_k^{-2}\max_b|\operatorname{Log}\zeta_b|$.
On $\mathbb T_k$ it is at most $w_*/32$, and
\[
 \log\mathsf E_k\left[
      e^{\mathcal V_\varpi}\prod_b\zeta_b^{\chi_b}\right]
 =\sum_X\widetilde E_{\varpi,\zeta}(X),
 \qquad \zeta^\chi=1+(\zeta-1)\chi.
\]
\item[(b)]
Each polymer term at a Mayer index is a polynomial of
degree at most one in each $\zeta_b$.  A refined cluster
term with $m$ polymers has degree at most $m$ in each
variable.  Their coefficients are holomorphic in
$\varpi$ and in the pair of radius $a$.
The refined series converges absolutely and uniformly
on $\mathbb P_k$, defining both expansions there.
They are holomorphic in the interior and continuous
on the closed polydisc, jointly with the other
parameters.  The identity in (a) holds throughout
$\mathbb P_k$, with a nonzero integral.
\item[(c)]
On $\mathbb P_k$,
\[
 \|\Delta_{\varpi,\zeta}^{\rm mk}(X)\|
 \le\tfrac1{32}w_*K_\Pi e^{-\kappa_+d_{k+1}(X)}.
\]
If $\zeta_b=1+\lambda_b$ and
$\|\lambda\|_\infty\le e^{\mathsf r_k}-1$, then
\[
 \|\Delta_{\varpi,\zeta}^{\rm mk}(X)\|
 \le K_\Pi\epsilon_k^{\rm mk}(\|\lambda\|_\infty)
                           e^{-\kappa_+d_{k+1}(X)}.
\]
\item[(d)]
The difference is even and local in the pair on $X$,
and reads only $\zeta_b$ with $\square(b)^\sharp\subset X$.
It is jointly gauge invariant if the original potential
is so member by member.  The construction commutes
with each linear symmetry carrying cubes to cubes
and satisfying $\zeta_{(\mathsf gb)^+}=\zeta_b$,
and with $B\mapsto-B$.  At real $\zeta$ the mark is real.
\item[(e)]
If $\|\lambda\|_\infty\le(e^{\mathsf r_k}-1)/2$, define
\[
 \Delta^{\rm mk}(X;b)=
 \int_0^1\lambda_b\,
 \partial_{\lambda_b}
       \widetilde E_{\varpi,\mathbf1+t\lambda}(X)\,dt.
\]
These terms sum to $\Delta_{\varpi,\mathbf1+\lambda}^{\rm mk}(X)$
and vanish unless $\square(b)^\sharp\subset X$.
For any complex weights $|\mathsf a_b|\le1$,
\[
 \left\|\sum_b\mathsf a_b\Delta^{\rm mk}(X;b)\right\|
 \le2K_\Pi\epsilon_k^{\rm mk}(\|\lambda\|_\infty)
                         e^{-\kappa_+d_{k+1}(X)}.
\]
They retain locality, evenness, holomorphy and joint
gauge invariance; a symmetry carries the pointer $b$
to $(\mathsf gb)^+$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
On $\{\chi_b=1\}$,
$1\le\mathsf t_k|B(b)|^2/a_k^2$.  Thus
\[
 |\mathcal V_\zeta^{\rm mk}(Y;B)|
 \le\frac{M^3}{a_k^2}\max_b|\operatorname{Log}\zeta_b|
 \left(1+M^{-3}
     \sum_{b'\in\mathfrak X^{\circ+}\langle Y\rangle}
                     \mathsf t_k|B(b')|^2\right).
\]
Since $d_k(Y)=0$, this is the required norm at every
rate.  On $\mathbb T_k$,
$|\operatorname{Log}\zeta_b|
\le\mathsf r_k+\pi=\kappa_{\rm mk}a_k^2$ and
$M^3\kappa_{\rm mk}=w_*/32$.
The expansion admits four origins with these sizes.
It requires only Borel dependence on the real
fluctuation, so the indicator causes no change in its
hypotheses.  Exponentiating and multiplying over $Y$
gives exactly $\prod_b\zeta_b^{\chi_b}$, proving (a).

A Mayer vertex of the mark contributes
\[
 \prod_{\square(b)=Y}
        (1+(\zeta_b-1)\chi_b)-1
 =\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subset\{b:\square(b)=Y\}}
              \prod_{b\in S}(\zeta_b-1)\chi_b.
\]
In a single polymer term each vertex occurs once.
The decoupled measures and tests do not read $\zeta$.
The term is therefore of degree at most one in each
$\zeta_b$, with holomorphic coefficients furnished by
the original parameter-dependent integral.
Clusters may repeat or overlap polymers, so their
degree can be as large as their number of polymers.
On $\mathbb T_k$ each polymer term is bounded by its
usual positive majorant, formed with mark size $w_*/32$.
The maximum principle for a polynomial extends this
same bound to $\mathbb P_k$.  The convergent majorant
series then proves absolute uniform convergence,
holomorphy and continuity there.  On a finite torus
the entire integral in (a) is a polynomial in the
finitely many $\zeta_b$.  It agrees with the exponential
of the convergent series on the distinguished boundary;
Cauchy's formula extends the equality to the polydisc.
The exponential never vanishes, including at $\zeta_b=0$,
where the factor is $1-\chi_b$.  This proves (b).

Subtracting the unmarked expansion leaves precisely
the clusters meeting a marked vertex.  The marked
majorant has size
\[
 K_E\eta^{\mathfrak m},\qquad
 \eta^{\mathfrak m}\le
 (L+2)^3S_{\rm s}e^{4\lambda_1}w_0^{-1}\frac{w_*}{32},
 \qquad
 K_E(L+2)^3S_{\rm s}e^{4\lambda_1}/w_0=K_\Pi.
\]
This proves the first bound of (c), first on the
boundary and then term by term inside.
For $\lambda\ne0$ apply Schwarz's lemma to
$\xi\mapsto\Delta_{\varpi,\mathbf1+\xi\lambda/
                                    \|\lambda\|_\infty}^{\rm mk}(X)$
on $|\xi|<e^{\mathsf r_k}-1$.
It vanishes at zero, and its boundary bound is the
first bound of (c).  The case $\lambda=0$ is immediate.

Locality follows from the regions of the marked
vertices.  The mark reads $|B(b)|$ and no pair.
Gauge transformations act by orthogonal adjoint maps
on $B(b)$, so they preserve it.
Likewise a linear symmetry acts by
$B((\mathsf gb)^+)=O_bB(b)$, with $O_b$ orthogonal,
and carries $\square(b)$ to $\square((\mathsf gb)^+)$.
The expansion intertwines these transformations on
$\mathbb T_k$, term by term.
The resulting identities are polynomial identities
in finitely many $\zeta_b$, and hence hold everywhere:
their coefficients are Fourier coefficients of their
restriction to $\mathbb T_k$.  Uniform convergence
carries the identities to the sums and their
derivatives.  This proves (d).

For $t\in[0,1]$, $|\xi|\le1$ and $|\mathsf a_b|\le1$,
the family $\mathbf1+t\lambda+\xi(\mathsf a_b\lambda_b)_b$
lies in $\mathbb P_k$.  By (c), its difference from
the unmarked expansion is at most
$2K_\Pi\epsilon_k^{\rm mk}(\|\lambda\|_\infty)
e^{-\kappa_+d_{k+1}(X)}$.
Cauchy's estimate in $\xi$ and integration in $t$
give the weighted bound in (e).
The fundamental theorem of calculus gives the sum
rule.  Locality and the symmetries commute with these
derivatives and integrals, proving the remaining claims.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[One marked step]\label{C-421-9}
Let $h\ge h_F$, $\gamma\le\gamma(h,5B_s)$,
$\mathsf r_k>0$, and
$|\lambda|\le(e^{\mathsf r_k}-1)/2$.
Take a point of the open step domain at weight $h$
and the fine mass of the datum.  Assume its potential
has size at most $c_{\rm cl}$ and its earlier families
are covariant under $M\mathbb Z^3$.
Insert the uniform factor $\prod_b(1+\lambda\chi_b)$.
The resulting step is defined on both the torus and
the infinite lattice.  Its new activity before local
extraction is $\widetilde E^{(k+1)}+\Delta_\lambda^{\rm mk}$;
all terms outside the expansion are unchanged.

Point the difference at level-$k+1$ sites by
\[
 \Delta^{\rm mk}(X;z)=
       \sum_bh_z(x_b)\Delta^{\rm mk}(X;b),
\]
where $h_z(x_b)$ is the mean of the tent at the two
endpoints of $b$.  Then the pointed terms vanish
unless $z\in X$, sum to $\Delta_\lambda^{\rm mk}$, and
\[
 \|\Delta_\lambda^{\rm mk}\|_{k+1}
 \le C_EK_\Pi\epsilon_k^{\rm mk}(\lambda),\qquad
 \sup_z\|\Delta^{\rm mk}(\cdot;z)\|_{k+1}
 \le2C_EK_\Pi\epsilon_k^{\rm mk}(\lambda),
 \qquad C_E=4096.
\]
The changes in the three extracted numbers satisfy
\[
 \begin{split}
 |\delta e|&\le M^{-3}C_EK_\Pi\epsilon_k^{\rm mk}(\lambda),\\
 |\delta b|&\le C_{am}r_\alpha^{-2}C_EK_\Pi
                                      \epsilon_k^{\rm mk}(\lambda),\\
 |\delta\mu|&\le
 c_b^{-2}C_{am}^\psi(\nu h^2)^{-1}C_EK_\Pi
                                      \epsilon_k^{\rm mk}(\lambda).
 \end{split}
\]
After extraction the changes in both new families,
including their pointed norms, are at most
$K_{\rm D}\epsilon_k^{\rm mk}(\lambda)$, where
\[
 K_{\rm D}=2C_EK_\Pi
                  \max\{2+C_{am}r_\alpha^{-2},K_\mu\}.
\]
All objects are holomorphic in the parameters.  They
retain locality, parity, gauge and flavour invariance,
and translation covariance.  On the infinite lattice
the extracted families have zero scalar mean per cell,
zero action coefficient, and zero normalized trace of
the cell mean of their degree-two zeroth moment.

For real $\lambda$, if the input numbers and the totals
of the input activities are real on tested background
pairs of a torus, the new total before extraction is
real there.  If the same input numbers and infinite
lattice families occur on arbitrarily large admissible
tori, with real data and uniform bounds, the extracted
numbers are real as well.  Extraction then preserves
reality on each such torus.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Apply \cref{C-421-8} at the uniform
$\zeta=\mathbf1+\lambda$.
The mark enters only the joined fluctuation integral.
It does not enter the operators, normalizers, calibration
prefactor, power of the relative coupling or
$\mathbf G_\tau$ outside that integral.
The tents satisfy $0\le h_z\le1$ and
$\sum_zh_z(x_b)=1$.
If $h_z(x_b)\ne0$, an endpoint $y$ of $b$ has
$|y-z|_\infty<1$ in level-$k+1$ units.
In level-$k$ units this is less than $L\le M$;
thus $z\in\square(b)^\sim\subset\square(b)^\sharp$.
The support and sum rule follow, and the weighted
bound in \cref{C-421-8}(e) gives the pointed estimate.
Summing over polymers uses
\[
 \sup_\square\sum_{X\supset\square}
          e^{-(\kappa_+-\kappa)d_{k+1}(X)}\le C_E,
\]
the same count on either lattice.

On a polymer fitting into an admitted torus, all four
origins agree with their infinite lattice versions
under the chart.  Their terms agree on $\mathbb T_k$,
and hence as polynomials in the marked bond variables.
They therefore agree throughout the polydisc,
including after differentiating and pointing.
This defines the infinite lattice activity independently
of the fitting torus.
The same local bounds and polymer count apply there.

The extracted numbers are the three continuous linear
functionals of the infinite lattice activity.
The scalar value per site costs $M^{-3}$, because
each cube has $M^3$ sites.  The action functional
has norm at most $C_{am}r_\alpha^{-2}$.
The mass functional is
$-(\nu\eta_{k+1}^2)^{-1}$ times the trace of the cell
mean of the zeroth moment; $|\eta_{k+1}|\ge c_b$,
and $\nu^{-1}$ times the absolute trace of the cell
mean is bounded by
$C_{am}^\psi(\nu h^2)^{-1}$ times the activity norm.
This proves the three estimates.
Local extraction is linear and multiplies the pointed
norm by at most $2+C_{am}r_\alpha^{-2}$ in degree
zero and $K_\mu$ in positive degree, proving the
post-extraction bound.
Each extraction functional equals one on its own local
term and zero on the other two: the action vanishes
at the trivial field, a constant has zero second
derivative, and
$L^{-(k+1)}\mathsf S_1(\psi^{\rm bg})$
has zeroth moment $\eta_{k+1}^2\,1$.
This proves the three normalizations.

We give the reality argument because boundedness alone
does not supply it.  Write
$\dagger=\alpha_{(i,-i)}\sharp$.
Flavour invariance of the earlier terms makes their
totals $\sharp$-invariant on the tested pairs.
The potential at a real pair and real fluctuation is
therefore fixed by $\sharp$.
For $0\le q\le1$, multiply this potential by $q$ and
replace the mark by $\mathbf1+q\lambda$.
These parameters stay in the admitted domains.
Let $\mathcal L(q)$ be the total expansion and
$\Xi(q)$ its exponential, the marked Gaussian integral.
Conjugation commutes with both integrations and the
exponential of even elements, so
$e^{\mathcal L(q)^\sharp}=e^{\mathcal L(q)}$.
Their difference is a scalar in $2\pi i\mathbb Z$.
It varies continuously with $q$ and is zero at $q=0$,
where the pure Gaussian logarithm is real.
It is consequently zero at $q=1$.
The terms outside the expansion are real scalars.
Flavour invariance converts $\sharp$-invariance into
$\dagger$-invariance, and gauge transformations preserve it.

It remains to check the numbers read on the infinite
lattice.  On a torus of side $N$ in level-$k+1$ units,
the terms on nonwrapping polymers agree with their
lifts.  Their pointing agrees too: the torus tents
are periodizations, and at most one lift of a pointer
contributes to a fitting polymer, contained in a
cuboid of side less than $N/2$.
The remaining polymers have
$d_{k+1}\ge N/(2M)-2$.
Their bounds, including pointed bounds, are uniform
in $N$: the expansion and mark decay at $\kappa_+$;
the gauge normalizer and closed loops decay at
$\kappa+1$; and
\[
 |\mathbf G_\tau(X,P,z)|
 \le K_{\mathbf G}\sigma_\star
                  e^{-(\kappa+1)d_{k+1}(X)}.
\]
The field-independent per-site terms occupy size-zero
polymers and do not contribute to these tails when
$N>4M$.
Thus the coefficients at fixed fermion places, pointed
totals, and the scalar second-derivative kernels
converge to the infinite lattice ones.
For the last assertion the scalar terms are strictly
gauge invariant and have the same local bounds, so
the usual linear-response kernel limit applies.

The scalar mean per site on each torus is real.
Its limit is the cell mean on the infinite lattice,
by $M\mathbb Z^3$ covariance and uniform tail bounds;
thus $e_{k+1}+\delta e$ is real.
The second-derivative kernels are real on every torus
near the trivial field and hence in the limit.
Their second moments use real weights, so
$b_{k+1}+\delta b$ is real.
For the degree-two kernel, conjugation gives
\[
 \mathsf k(y,y')=\gamma_4\mathsf k(y',y)^\dagger\gamma_4.
\]
Its row sums over a cell converge absolutely.
Translation covariance and the decomposition
$y'=y''+v$, $y''\in c$, $v\in M\mathbb Z^3$, give
\[
 \sum_{y\in c}\sum_{y'}\operatorname{tr}\mathsf k(y',y)
 =\sum_{y''\in c}\sum_{y\in c}\sum_v
          \operatorname{tr}\mathsf k(y'',y-v)
 =\sum_{y''\in c}\sum_{y'}
          \operatorname{tr}\mathsf k(y'',y').
\]
The first and last expressions are conjugates.
Their value is real, and $\eta_{k+1}$ is real;
therefore $\mu_{k+1}+\delta\mu$ is real.
Subtracting the resulting real local terms preserves
reality on every tested torus.  All other symmetries
and holomorphy follow from \cref{C-421-8} and linear
extraction.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Iterating marked steps}

On the chart of an admitted step, the Borel indicator in
\cref{C-421-2} is the indicator $\chi_b$ of
\cref{C-421-8}.  Indeed, a block field passing the step
tests passes the density test, so its plaquette size is
less than $2\varepsilon(\mathsf t_{k+1})$.
It lies in the inner ball and hence in the field cut.
The inverse fluctuation coordinate there satisfies
$\mathcal A_k^\diamond(b)=B(b)$.
Since $\mathfrak b(\mathsf t)\mathsf t^{-1/2}
=\delta(\mathsf t)$, this gives
\[
 \bar\chi_{k,b}(V_W(B))
 =\mathbf1_{\{\mathsf t_k|B(b)|^2\ge a_k^2\}}.
\]
Thus the marked expansion represents the actual Borel
mark under the history map.

\begin{proposition}[The marked flow]\label{C-421-10}
Use \cref{C-421-2} at $h=h_F$, $A=5B_s$, and put
\[
 \begin{split}
 C_{\rm Lip}=\max\{&
 2+2\sqrt2\theta_sh^2A/C_w,\,
 2+4c_sh^2A^2/C_2,\,
 2+8(C_w+\theta_sh^2A)/r_x,\,
 L+6(C_\mu+c_sA^2)/A\},\\
 C_{\rm mk}=\max\{&
 K_{\rm D}/(2C_w),\,K_{\rm D}/(2C_2),\,
 2C_{am}r_\alpha^{-2}C_EK_\Pi/r_x,\,
 3c_b^{-2}C_{am}^\psi C_EK_\Pi/(\nu h^2A)\},\\
 C_{e,{\rm Lip}}&=3L^3r_x+2M^{-3}K_M(c_{\rm cl}+1),\\
 \bar\theta_{\rm mk}(r)&=
 C_{\rm Lip}^{\,s}(s-u)C_{\rm mk}
       \frac{w_*}{16}e^\pi L^s\mathsf b\,
                         \frac r{\Lambda_{\rm mk}}.
 \end{split}
\]
Suppose $r>0$ satisfies
\[
 e^{-\pi}\Lambda_{\rm mk}\ge2,\qquad
 2r\le e^{-\pi}\Lambda_{\rm mk}-1,\qquad
 \bar\theta_{\rm mk}(r)\le\tfrac12.
 \tag{Mk1--2}
\]
For $|\lambda|\le r$, start from the original flow
through $t_0$, insert the uniform mark in the steps
$t_0\le k<t_1$, and continue without marks from
$t_1$ to $K$.  At each step extract its own three
numbers and update
\[
 x_{k+1}(\lambda)=L^{-1}x_k(\lambda)-b_{k+1}(\lambda),
 \qquad
 s_{k+1}(\lambda)=Ls_k(\lambda)+\mu_{k+1}(\lambda).
\]
This constructs the flow through $K$ in the open
step domain.  The families lie in the spaces
$\mathfrak F_j$, including all linear symmetries and
the full zero degree-two moment.
At a marked level the old part uses its original
pointing and $\Delta^{\rm mk}$ uses the tents of
\cref{C-421-9}.
All numbers, energies and families are holomorphic
for $|\lambda|<r$ and continuous on the closed disc.
For real $\lambda$ the numbers and energies are real;
conjugation carries the families at $\lambda$ to
those at $\bar\lambda$.

With $\bar\theta=\bar\theta_{\rm mk}(|\lambda|)$,
for all $i,j\le K$,
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 |x_i(\lambda)-x_i|\le\tfrac12r_xx_i\bar\theta,\qquad
 |s_i(\lambda)-s_i|\le\tfrac13A\phi(x_i)\bar\theta,\\
 \|F_0^{(j)}(\lambda)-F_0^{(j)}\|_j
       \le2C_w\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})\bar\theta,\qquad
 \|E_{\ge2}^{(j)}(\lambda)-E_{\ge2}^{(j)}\|_j
       \le2C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2\bar\theta.
 \end{gathered}
\]
The bounds include pointed terms and both lattice
families at each level.
The history with no large-field region, for the density
$\mathsf{Mk}^{(<k)}_\lambda e^{-\beta A-S_F}\,dU$,
has the usual level-$k$ formula with these numbers
and families, as an identity of measures.
At $t_1$ its Berezin integral is $T_0(\lambda)$.
Finally
\[
 |E_K(\lambda)-E_K|
 \le N_{[s]}s\left[
 C_{e,{\rm Lip}}\bar\theta+
 M^{-3}C_EK_\Pi\frac{w_*}{16}e^\pi
                              \frac{|\lambda|}{\Lambda_{\rm mk}}
                         \right].
\]
In particular this difference is at most one if
the last right side at $|\lambda|=r$ is at most one;
call this additional condition \textup{(Mk3)}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Let $P_k^0$ be the original point at level $k$.
For a point $P$ with primed coordinates, define
\[
 \theta_k(P)=
 \max_{i,j\le k}\max\left\{
 \frac{|x_i'-x_i|}{r_xx_i/2},
 \frac{|s_i'-s_i|}{A\phi(x_i)/3},
 \frac{\|F_0'^{(j)}-F_0^{(j)}\|_j}
                 {2C_w\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})},
 \frac{\|E_{\ge2}'^{(j)}-E_{\ge2}^{(j)}\|_j}
                 {2C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2}
 \right\}.
\]
On a torus include both families in this maximum.
Let $\Omega_k$ consist of points with $\theta_k<1$
whose families lie in $\mathfrak F_j$, with the
prescribed remaining scalar terms at their coefficients.
Since
$|s_i|\le\bar B_M/x_i\le\bar B_M\phi(x_i)$ and
$3\bar B_M/2\le A$, this set lies inside the open
step domain:
$|x_i'-x_i|<r_xx_i$ and $|s_i'|<A\phi(x_i)$.
The potential there has size less than $c_{\rm cl}/2$.

The coupling windows give
$\phi(x_k)\le\sqrt2\phi(\mathsf t_k)$,
$\phi(\mathsf t_k)\le1/2$, and $\phi(x_k)<1$.
The output bounds on $\Omega_k$ are
\[
 \begin{split}
 \|F_0^{(k+1)}\|&\le
       (2C_w+2\sqrt2\theta_sh^2A)\phi(\mathsf t_k),\\
 \|E_{\ge2}^{(k+1)}\|&\le
       (2C_2+4c_sh^2A^2)\phi(\mathsf t_k)^2,\\
 |b_{k+1}-e_{\mathsf N,k+1}-b_{k+1}^{F}|
       &\le2(C_w+\theta_sh^2A)\phi(x_k),\\
 |\mu_{k+1}|&\le(C_\mu+c_sA^2)\phi(x_k).
 \end{split}
\]
The fixed numbers in the third line do not read $P$.
The variable scalar contribution per site,
$\widetilde e_{k+1}$, is bounded by
$M^{-3}K_M(c_{\rm cl}+1)$.
The full scalar number is
\[
 e_{k+1}=e_{k+1}^{\rm YM,0}+e_{k+1}^{\rm F,0}
       -3(L^3-1)\operatorname{Log}(x_k'/\mathsf t_k)
       +\widetilde e_{k+1}.
\]
For $P\in\Omega_k$ with $\theta_k(P)=\theta$,
the line $P_k^0+\xi(P-P_k^0)/\theta$, $|\xi|<1$,
lies in $\Omega_k$, because its family constraints
are linear.  Schwarz's lemma bounds the change of
an output bounded by $S$ on that line by $2S\theta$.
For family norms this is applied to coefficients
and bounded linear combinations before taking
their suprema.

At a marked level, \cref{C-421-9} adds a perturbation
with
\[
 \epsilon_k^{\rm mk}(\lambda)
 \le\frac{w_*}{16}e^\pi
              \frac{|\lambda|}{\Lambda_{\rm mk}}.
\]
At unmarked levels put $\epsilon_k=0$.
The four scaled output distances are bounded respectively by
\[
 \begin{split}
 &(2+2\sqrt2\theta_sh^2A/C_w)\theta_k
           +K_{\rm D}\epsilon_k/(2C_w\phi(\mathsf t_k)),\\
 &(2+4c_sh^2A^2/C_2)\theta_k
           +K_{\rm D}\epsilon_k/(2C_2\phi(\mathsf t_k)^2),\\
 &(2+8(C_w+\theta_sh^2A)/r_x)\theta_k
           +2C_{am}r_\alpha^{-2}C_EK_\Pi\epsilon_k/(r_xx_{k+1}),\\
 &(L+6(C_\mu+c_sA^2)/A)\theta_k
           +3c_b^{-2}C_{am}^\psi C_EK_\Pi\epsilon_k/
                                      (\nu h^2A\phi(\mathsf t_k)).
 \end{split}
\]
For the coefficient line we used $L^{-1}x_k\le2x_{k+1}$
and $x_{k+1}\ge1\ge\phi(x_k)$.
For the mass line we used
$x_{k+1}\le\min\{x_k,\mathsf t_k\}$ and monotonicity
of $\phi$.  Both follow from the original coupling
windows and their ceilings on $\gamma$.
Since $\phi(\mathsf t)^{-1}\le\phi(\mathsf t)^{-2}
\le\mathsf t$ and $\mathsf t_k\le L^s\mathsf b$,
\[
 \theta_{k+1}\le C_{\rm Lip}\theta_k
                         +C_{\rm mk}\mathsf t_k\epsilon_k.
\]
Starting at $\theta_{t_0}=0$, this yields
\[
 \theta_{k+1}\le
 \sum_{j=t_0}^{\min\{k,t_1-1\}}
       C_{\rm Lip}^{\,k-j}C_{\rm mk}\mathsf t_j\epsilon_j
 \le\bar\theta_{\rm mk}(|\lambda|)\le\tfrac12.
\]
It also gives holomorphy and continuity at each step.

We must verify the constraints defining
$\mathfrak F_{k+1}$ before applying the next step.
First run this verification at real $\lambda$,
simultaneously on the infinite lattice and all
admissible tori obtained by changing the side.
The one-weight setting is available on those tori:
its only side requirement is $L\ell'\ge C_LM$,
which follows from their admissibility; its remaining
conditions involve the fixed cutoff, label and
$\mathsf t_{t_1}=L^u\mathsf b$.
All estimates just proved are uniform in the side.
Thus the hypotheses for the reality conclusion of
\cref{C-421-9} hold simultaneously.

The internal symmetries act by maps $\alpha_S$ that
fix scalar coefficient functions.  Inductively they
fix the potential and commute with both Gaussian
integrations.  For any marked bond parameters in
the polydisc, let $\mathcal L_\zeta$ be the total
expansion and $\Xi_\zeta=e^{\mathcal L_\zeta}$.
Then $e^{\alpha_S\mathcal L_\zeta}=e^{\mathcal L_\zeta}$.
Their difference is a scalar in $2\pi i\mathbb Z$,
but $\alpha_S$ fixes scalar parts; hence the
difference is zero.  This proves invariance of
the totals.  For the pointed totals of the original
step, the insertion formula
\[
 \int_0^1
 \mathsf E_k[\dot{\mathcal V}_z e^{\mathfrak V_t}]
                  \mathsf E_k[e^{\mathfrak V_t}]^{-1}\,dt
\]
has invariant numerator and denominator.
For the additional pointed terms, differentiate
$\alpha_S\mathcal L_\zeta=\mathcal L_\zeta$ in
$\zeta_b$ and use the bond pointing and tents.
Thus the pointed totals are invariant as well.

The real logarithm argument in \cref{C-421-9} works
for every real family $\zeta$ in the polydisc:
use the path $\mathbf1+q(\zeta-\mathbf1)$ while
scaling the potential by $q\in[0,1]$.
Consequently real derivatives in $\zeta_b$ are
$\sharp$-invariant, and so are the new pointed
totals.  The numbers extracted on the infinite
lattice are real by the torus limit argument there.
At a tested covariance pair, the density at
$\mathsf gV$ is the image of that at $V$.
The chart substitution $B=\mathsf OB_1$ preserves
the uniform mark, since it permutes the non-pivot
bonds and preserves $|B(b)|$.
Thus covariance of the new density follows.
The scalar ambiguity between its two logarithms
is zero, because both scalar parts are real at
the tested pairs.  This proves covariance on shell.

On nonwrapping polymers all terms and pointers
agree with their lifts.  The torus tents are
periodizations, with at most one contributing lift
for a fitting polymer.  Uniform decay controls
the remaining terms.  Passing to increasing
admissible tori therefore gives the same linear
symmetries for the infinite lattice totals and
pointed totals at the required pairs.
These symmetries make the degree-two zeroth moment
a scalar matrix, constant from cell to cell.
The mass extraction has already removed its
normalized trace, so the whole zeroth moment is
zero.  Likewise the action coefficient is the
invariant coefficient and the scalar extraction
removes the trivial-field value.
This verifies all family-space constraints at
real $\lambda$.

Every remaining constraint is a closed complex-linear
condition on the families.  Its value is holomorphic
in $\lambda$ and vanishes on the real interval,
so it vanishes on the disc and by continuity on
its boundary.  The same continuation proves the
complex-linear symmetry identities.
For conjugation use that
$\lambda\mapsto(\Upsilon_{\bar\lambda})^\dagger$
is holomorphic whenever $\Upsilon_\lambda$ is;
the equality on real $\lambda$ gives
$\Upsilon_\lambda^\dagger=\Upsilon_{\bar\lambda}$.
This also applies to the infinite lattice coefficients,
pointed totals, cell means and second-derivative
kernels, which are continuous linear functions
in the family norms.  The prescribed scalar remainder
does not obstruct this assertion: only
$\mathbf G^{(k+1)}$ depends on the coefficient;
its pointed terms vanish at the trivial field,
and its total vanishes near that field on every
torus by the sum rule.  Holomorphy extends the
sum rule to complex $\lambda$, and the uniform
kernel limit makes its infinite lattice second
derivative zero.  The other remainder terms are
independent of $\lambda$.

We finish by checking the identity of measures.
Suppose the level-$k$ density has the stated form
$d_k[P_k(\lambda)]$ on the density-test set, and
is zero elsewhere.  It is bounded and Borel.
Multiply by
$m_k=\prod_b(1+\lambda\bar\chi_{k,b})$ for $k<t_1$
and by $m_k=1$ afterwards.
The exact image map is linear in this density,
and applies coefficient by coefficient to
$\operatorname{Ber}_k(\operatorname{Ker}_km_kd_k)$.
On its chart the preceding identity for
$\bar\chi_{k,b}$ gives the marked Gaussian integral.
The completed square, background substitutions
and localization sum rules are unchanged.
They are algebraic identities at complex as well
as real coefficients.  The complex action parameter
satisfies
$|x_k(\lambda)/\mathsf t_k-1|<\sigma_\star$,
so its real part is positive and the Gaussian
change of variables applies.
The marked expansion and subsequent extraction
give exactly $d_{k+1}[P_{k+1}(\lambda)]$.
This proves the measure identity by induction.
At $t_1$, integration over all fermion generators
gives $\det(D[U]+m_0)$ at each bare field and the
image preserves total mass.  The total is therefore
$T_0(\lambda)$.

There are $s$ possible changed scalar increments
above $t_0$, each with $n_{k+1}\le N_{[s]}$.
The logarithmic coupling term changes by at most
$3L^3r_x\theta_k$, because
$|\operatorname{Log}(x_k(\lambda)/x_k)|
\le r_x\theta_k$.
The expansion value changes by at most
$2M^{-3}K_M(c_{\rm cl}+1)\theta_k$.
At marked levels add
$M^{-3}C_EK_\Pi\epsilon_k^{\rm mk}(\lambda)$.
Summing gives the final energy bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Admissible initial flows]\label{C-421-11}
The proof also applies to a flow started at $t_0$.
What it requires is its bounded Borel density there;
the same open step domains and bounds around its
reference points; the coupling windows and
$|s_i|\le\bar B_M/x_i$; the family-space and
translation conditions on its earlier activities;
and the following real-data properties on all
admissible tori, with common numbers and infinite
lattice families and uniform bounds.
The initial numbers, energies and fine masses must
be real; the earlier activity totals must be
invariant under the internal symmetries and
$\sharp$ at their tested pairs; and the initial
density must be covariant at tested covariance
pairs.  The proof uses the bare density only to
identify its final scalar integral with $T_0$.
For another start, replace $T_0$ by the Berezin
integral of its marked term at $t_1$.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[A mark bounds fluctuation tails]\label{C-421-12}
For every $r>0$, the two integrals of fluctuation
indicators in \cref{C-429-7}(c) are bounded by
$(T_0(r)-T(0))/r$.
Under \textup{(Mk1)--(Mk3)}, put
\[
 \mathfrak u(r)=
 T_0(r)e^{-E_K(r)-(C+2)\ell^3}.
\]
Then
$T_0(r)\le e\,\mathfrak u(r)\mathsf Q_\ell T(0)$,
so each tail is at most
$e\,\mathfrak u(r)\mathsf Q_\ell r^{-1}T(0)$.
The changes under a weight $\mathfrak w'$ are those
in \cref{C-429-7}(b),(c).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The first assertion is Bernoulli's inequality as
proved in \cref{C-429-7}.  At real $r>0$ the marked
density is nonnegative, $E_K(r)$ is real, and
$E_K(r)\le E_K+1$.
Combine its defining identity with
$T(0)\ge e^{E_K-C_P(1+\log x_K)\ell^3}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Support of the difference of weights]\label{C-421-7}
In the two-lattice gauge setting, assume
$1\le u<s<K$, $L^u\mathsf b\ge\Theta_\star$ and
\[
 256\mathsf K_uc_\rho^2A_0^2N_{[s]}L^{-(K-s)}
 \le\gamma_{\rm r}A_1^2.
 \tag{k4}
\]
For $(\bullet,\circ)=(\mathrm A,\mathrm B)$ or
$(\mathrm B,\mathrm A)$ and any Borel $0\le\varphi\le1$
on the common base configuration space,
\[
 \mathbf1_{\{\mathsf k^\circ(W)=0\}}
       \varphi(W)\mathsf k^\bullet(W)
 \le\sum_{k=t_0}^{t_1-1}\sum_{b\in\mathfrak X_{(k)}^+}
       \varphi(W)\mathsf k^\bullet(W)
                         \bar\chi_{(k),b}^\bullet(W_k).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The two weights consist solely of the gauge tests,
field cuts, inner balls, gauge-fixing factors and
fluctuation coordinates at the calibrations.
The gauge comparison says that failure of the other
weight, when one is nonzero, forces at least one
moderate fluctuation.  Its applicability at the present
depths uses only the following bounds.
The inequalities $1\le t_0<t_1\le K-1$ give the
permitted levels; $L^u\mathsf b\ge\Theta_\star$
gives the two-weight and one-weight settings and
all calibrations needed by the background comparison;
and for $k\ge t_0$,
$N_k\le N_{[s]}$ and $L^{-k}\le L^{-(K-s)}$,
so (k4) gives its error bound at every such level.
The particular fractional choices of the depths
are not used by that argument.
The resulting pointwise inequality, multiplied
by the nonnegative $\varphi$, is the claim.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Constants and large-cutoff conditions.}\label{C-421-13}
The constants of the marked step and flow are formed
after the constants in their displayed formulas.
In particular $K_{\rm D}$ follows $K_\mu$, and
$C_{\rm Lip},C_{\rm mk},C_{e,{\rm Lip}}$ follow
$h_F,A,C_w,\theta_s,C_2,c_s,C_\mu,r_x$ and precede
$\gamma$.  The $C_{\rm Lip}$ here is the constant
of the four scaled output distances, independently
of the Lipschitz constant for free averaging kernels.
These definitions impose no new ceiling on an
earlier constant.

For later use, if $u\ge\varphi_1K$ with
$\varphi_1>0$, $s\le K$, $\mathsf b\le\bar{\mathsf b}$,
and $r=\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{1/2}$, then
$\mathsf R_{t_1}^{\rm F}\le1/8$ and
\textup{(Mk1)--(Mk3)} hold for sufficiently large $K$.
Indeed,
$\mathsf y_{[u]}\ge(\varphi_1K\log L)^{2\mathfrak p_0}$,
where $2\mathfrak p_0\ge2$.
The logarithms of the left sides in \textup{(Mk2)},
\textup{(Mk3)} and of $\mathsf R_{t_1}^{\rm F}$
are bounded, up to a fixed $\log\mathsf Q_\ell$, by
\[
 K(\log C_{\rm Lip}+4\log L)+2\log K+3\log\ell
 +\log(\bar{\mathsf b}C'')
 -\min\{\kappa_{\rm mk}A_1^2/8,\theta_{\rm dis}A_0^2\}
                   (\varphi_1K\log L)^{2\mathfrak p_0}.
\]
This tends to $-\infty$, and \textup{(Mk1)} follows
from $\Lambda_{\rm mk}\to\infty$.
Also $L^u\mathsf b\ge\Theta_\star$ for large $K$.
For the adjacent cutoff $K+1$ one can use
$\varphi_1=\phi_1(n)/2$ and $\bar{\mathsf b}=X_g$,
so one threshold works for both lattices.

\paragraph{The two comparison estimates.}\label{C-421-15}
At $t=t_1^\bullet$, \cref{C-421-5} gives
\[
 0\le Z^\bullet-T^\bullet(0)\le R^F Z^\bullet,
\]
because both calibrations at that level are
$L^u\mathsf b\ge L^u\gamma^{-2}$ and
$\mathsf Q_\ell\le\mathsf M_{g,\ell}$.
This is \cref{C-418-12}.

Under (k0)--(k2), \cref{C-421-14} applies
\cref{C-421-4} at radii $2R_i$ and gives
\[
 \left|\partial_z^n[
 \log T^\bullet-\log\hat T^\bullet-\mathfrak c^\bullet](0)
 \right|
 \le\left[\tfrac12(4(\mathsf Q_\ell+1))^{n+1}
               +C'_EN_{[u]}\right]
        (r_\lambda-1)^{-1}\prod_i(2R_i)^{-1}.
\]
The original total is entire in the sources.
The interpolation gives holomorphy of
$\hat T^\bullet$ and $\mathfrak c^\bullet$ on
$\mathbb Q=\mathbb P(2R)$.
The lower bound in \cref{C-421-4} gives $T^\bullet(0)>0$,
while \cref{C-418-24} gives
$\hat T^\bullet(0)\ge
 e^{\hat E_{K^\bullet}-C_P(1+\log X_g)\ell^3}>0$.
Since
$\mathsf Q_\ell+1\le2\mathsf M_{g,\ell}$ and
$(r_\lambda-1)^{-1}\le2/r_\lambda$,
the displayed bound is at most
\[
 \left[2(4\mathsf M_{g,\ell})^{n+1}
              +C'_EN_{[u]}\right]
 r_\lambda^{-1}\prod_iR_i^{-1}
 \le\epsilon_{\rm ro}\prod_iR_i^{-1}.
\]
This proves \cref{C-418-13}.
For $n\ge2$, \cref{C-421-6}, with
$C'=1$ for each flow, also gives under (Sep)
\[
 |\partial_z^n\mathfrak c^\bullet|
 \le2^{n+1}C_{\mathscr C}M^{-3}N_{[u]}
       e^{-\kappa_{\rm E}\mathsf dL^u}
       \prod_i\varrho_i^{-1}
 \le2\epsilon_{\rm mx}.
\]

\subsection{Marks in the restarted flow}

We apply the marked-step construction to the zero-source restart.
The required margins are verified below; in particular the
restart is an admissible centre for the open-domain estimates.

\begin{definition}[Parameters for the marked restart]\label{C-426-2}
Use the two-cutoff data under (k0), (k1).
All cutoff thresholds in this subsection refer to
$K^{\rm A}$, from which $s,u$ are chosen.
Within either lattice write $K=K^\bullet$,
$t_0=K-s$, $t_1=K-u$.
Let $\hat P_k$ be the zero-source restart of
\cref{C-419-4,C-427-4}, starting with
\[
 \hat x_{t_0}=L^s\mathsf b,\qquad
 \hat s_{t_0}=F^{\rm UV}/(L^s\mathsf b),\qquad
 \hat E_{t_0}=0,
\]
and no earlier activity.  Use $h=h_F$, $A=5B_s$
and the constants of \cref{C-421-10}.
The mark at a level $t_0\le k<t_1$ is
\[
 \mathsf m_{k,\lambda}(V)
   =\prod_{b\in\mathfrak X_k^+}
                       (1+\lambda\bar\chi_{k,b}(V)).
\]
It is bounded and Borel in $V$ and polynomial in
$\lambda$.  Its chart expression is the mark
of \cref{C-421-8}.

Hereafter $\Lambda_{\rm mk}$ uses $\gamma^{-2}$:
\[
 \Lambda_{\rm mk}
  =\exp[\kappa_{\rm t}A_1^2
                (\log(L^u\gamma^{-2}))^{2\mathfrak p_0}],
 \qquad \kappa_{\rm t}=w_*/(128M^3).
\]
It is no larger than its value with
$\mathsf b$ in place of $\gamma^{-2}$.
Set
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 K_{\rm D}^{\rm arr}
    =K_\Pi(2+(M^{-3}+C_{am}r_\alpha^{-2})C_E),\\
 C_{\rm win}=\max\{32,A,2K_{\rm D}^{\rm arr}/C_{\rm mk}\},
 \quad q_2=\tfrac34+\tfrac1{4\sqrt2},
 \quad \sigma_*=\tfrac{23}{11}B_F+\tfrac12,\\
 \bar\theta_{\rm rs}(r)=
 C_{\rm Lip}^{\,s}(s-u)C_{\rm mk}\frac{w_*}{16}e^\pi
                         L^s\mathsf b\,r/\Lambda_{\rm mk},\\
 r_{\rm rs}=2\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{1/2},\qquad
 \theta_{{\rm rs},K^{\rm A}}
 =2C_{\rm Lip}^{\,s}sC_{\rm mk}
      \frac{w_*}{16}e^\pi L^sX_g\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{-1/2}.
 \end{gathered}
\]
Thus $\bar\theta_{\rm rs}(r_{\rm rs})
\le\theta_{{\rm rs},K^{\rm A}}$ for both lattices.
For a radius $r>0$ consider
\[
 \begin{array}{ll}
 \textup{(Mr1)}&
 e^{-\pi}\Lambda_{\rm mk}\ge2,\quad
                  2r\le e^{-\pi}\Lambda_{\rm mk}-1,\\
 \textup{(Mr2)}&\bar\theta_{\rm rs}(r)\le\tfrac12,\\
 \textup{(Mr3)}&
 N_{[s]}s\left[C_{e,{\rm Lip}}\bar\theta_{\rm rs}(r)
 +M^{-3}C_EK_\Pi\frac{w_*}{16}e^\pi r/\Lambda_{\rm mk}
                  \right]\le1,\\
 \textup{(Mr4)}&
 C_{\rm win}L^s\mathsf b\,\bar\theta_{\rm rs}(r)\le1.
 \end{array}
\]
Condition (Mr4) implies (Mr2) and
$\bar\theta_{\rm rs}(r)\le1/32$.
Under (Mr1),
\[
 \epsilon_k^{\rm mk}(\lambda)
 \le\frac{w_*}{16}e^\pi\frac{|\lambda|}{\Lambda_{\rm mk}}
 \le\frac{\bar\theta_{\rm rs}(|\lambda|)}
                         {C_{\rm mk}L^s\mathsf b}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Smaller mark conditions for the scalar total]\label{C-430-2}
Put
$c_{\rm room}=3/4+1/(4\sqrt2)$,
$C_{\rm arr}=K_{\rm D}^{\rm arr}$ and
\[
 \epsilon_\flat=\frac{w_*}{16}e^\pi\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 \bar\theta_\flat=C_{\rm Lip}^{\,s}(s-u)C_{\rm mk}
                                      L^sX_g\epsilon_\flat.
\]
The conditions for the scalar total are
\[
 \begin{array}{ll}
 \textup{(m1)}&\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{1/2}\ge3e^\pi,\\
 \textup{(m2)}&
 \bar\theta_\flat\le1/32,\quad
 r_xL^sX_g\bar\theta_\flat\le\bar B,\quad
 AL^sX_g\bar\theta_\flat\le3\bar B_M,\\
 \textup{(m3)}&
 N_{[s]}s[C_{e,{\rm Lip}}\bar\theta_\flat
                 +M^{-3}C_EK_\Pi\epsilon_\flat]\le1,\\
 \textup{(m4)}&C_{\rm arr}\epsilon_\flat\le1.
 \end{array}
\]
Let $K_\flat(g,\ell,n)$ be the least integer from
which on (k0), (k1) and (m1)--(m4) hold at every
$K^{\rm A}$.  It exists: $\log\Lambda_{\rm mk}$
is bounded below by a positive multiple of
$(K^{\rm A})^{2\mathfrak p_0}$, while the logarithms
of all other factors are $O(K^{\rm A}+\log K^{\rm A})$.
This threshold is chosen after $\gamma$ and depends
only on the constants, $g,\ell,n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[The marked expansion after a restart]\label{C-426-3}
The conclusions of \cref{C-421-8} hold at every
admitted restarted step, with the same constants,
on the torus and on the infinite lattice.
The infinite lattice construction intertwines
$M\mathbb Z^3$ translations, and on fitting polymers
the torus terms and bond-pointed terms agree with
their infinite lattice lifts.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The fourth origin reads the same calibration,
threshold and real fluctuation as in
\cref{C-421-8}; its bound uses no activity before
the current step.  Thus that proof applies.
For the additional chart assertion, a chart
preserves orientations, non-pivot bonds and
$\square(b)$ and carries the fluctuation by
$B(b)\mapsto B(\mathsf ib)$ with equal values.
It therefore carries the fourth origin together
with the other three on every polymer whose
enlargement is contained in the given polymer.
The expansion intertwines these charts on the
distinguished boundary, and polynomial continuation
extends this to the full polydisc and its derivatives.
For a translation by $M\mathbb Z^3$ in level-$k+1$
units, place the polymer and its translate in one
admitted torus and apply the same argument there.
This proves independence of the fitting torus,
translation covariance and the pointed assertions.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[A marked restarted step]\label{C-426-4}
At a point of the restarted open step domain with
potential size at most $c_{\rm cl}$, translation
covariant earlier families, and
$|\lambda|\le(e^{\mathsf r_k}-1)/2$,
all bounds of \cref{C-421-9} hold.
In addition the scalar change after extraction has
the array bound
\[
 \sup_{X,z}e^{(\kappa+1)d_{k+1}(X)}
             \sup|\Delta F_0(X;\cdot;z)|
 \le K_{\rm D}^{\rm arr}\epsilon_k^{\rm mk}(\lambda).
\]
The construction is holomorphic on
$|\lambda|<e^{\mathsf r_k}-1$.
If the earlier totals are invariant under all
$\alpha_S$, the new totals and pointed totals
are invariant as well.
For real data on all admitted tori, with potential
size at most $3c_{\rm cl}/4$, the reality and
infinite lattice conclusions of \cref{C-421-9}
hold for totals and positive-degree pointed totals.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Apply \cref{C-426-3} and the extraction proof of
\cref{C-421-9}.  It uses only the current open-domain
point and the linear extraction functionals, available
at the restart by \cref{C-419-4}.
For the array bound, the degree-zero pointed
difference before extraction is bounded by
$2K_\Pi\epsilon_k^{\rm mk}e^{-(\kappa+1)d_{k+1}}$.
The scalar subtraction has size
$M^{-3}C_EK_\Pi\epsilon_k^{\rm mk}$ on size-zero
polymers.  The action subtraction has size at most
$C_{am}r_\alpha^{-2}C_EK_\Pi\epsilon_k^{\rm mk}$,
also on size-zero polymers, since the pointed
weight member is at most $6M^3\alpha_0^2\le1$.
Their sum is the stated constant.
The bond derivative formula is holomorphic on the
larger disc: for $t\in[0,1]$,
$\mathbf1+t\lambda$ stays inside the polydisc.
The invariance and reality proofs in
\cref{C-421-9,C-421-10} use exactly the asserted
earlier-total symmetries.  For the real logarithm
path, the potential-size bound $3c_{\rm cl}/4$
permits complex scaling by $|q|<4/3$, containing
the real path $[0,1]$.  Differentiating at real
bond parameters proves reality of the pointed
totals.  Uniform local decay and the fitting-chart
identity then give the same infinite lattice
limits and real extraction numbers as in
\cref{C-421-9}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Margins around the zero-source restart]\label{C-426-5}
The restart is defined through $K$, with real
numbers and the symmetries, family spaces and
bounded Borel densities of \cref{C-419-4}.
For $t_0<j\le K$ and $t_0\le i\le K$,
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 |\hat b_j|\le B_\sharp-\tfrac12,\qquad
 |\hat x_i-\mathsf t_i|
       \le(1-L^{-(i-t_0)})\bar B,\qquad
 \tfrac{11}{12}\mathsf t_i\le\hat x_i
                  \le\tfrac{13}{12}\mathsf t_i,\\
 -\tfrac12\le\mathsf t_i\hat s_i\le\sigma_*,
 \qquad
 \hat x_i|\hat s_i|\le\bar B_M,\qquad
 |\hat s_i|\le\tfrac23A\phi(\hat x_i),\\
 \|\hat F_0^{(j)}\|_j
       \le q_2C_w\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1}),\qquad
 \|\hat E_{\ge2}^{(j)}\|_j
       \le q_2C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2.
 \end{gathered}
\]
The family estimates include each pointer and both
lattice families.  In particular
$\hat x_i\ge g^{-2}\ge\gamma^{-2}$.

At level $k$, let $\mathscr D_k$ consist of the
admitted families with
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 |x_i'-\hat x_i|\le r_x\hat x_i,\qquad
 |s_i'|\le A\phi(\hat x_i),\\
 \|F_0'^{(j)}-\hat F_0^{(j)}\|_j
       \le2C_w\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1}),\qquad
 \|E_{\ge2}'^{(j)}-\hat E_{\ge2}^{(j)}\|_j
       \le2C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2,
 \end{gathered}
\]
and the prescribed remaining scalar terms.
The step is holomorphic on this domain and its
potential has size less than $c_{\rm cl}/2$.
Its outputs satisfy
\[
 \begin{split}
 \|F_0^{(k+1)}\|&\le
       2C_w\phi(\mathsf t_k)+2\theta_sh^2|s_k'|,\\
 \|E_{\ge2}^{(k+1)}\|&\le
       2C_2\phi(\mathsf t_k)^2+2c_sh^2|s_k'|^2,\\
 |b_{k+1}-e_{\mathsf N,k+1}-b_{k+1}^{F}|
       &\le2C_w\phi(\hat x_k)+2\theta_sh^2|s_k'|,\\
 |\mu_{k+1}|&\le C_\mu\phi(\hat x_k)+c_s|s_k'|^2.
 \end{split}
\]
The scalar expansion value is bounded by
$M^{-3}K_M(c_{\rm cl}+1)$ per site.
The full scalar activity after extraction has
array bound $E_0-1/2$ at rate $\kappa+1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Since $0\le F^{\rm UV}\le B_F$, \cref{C-419-4}
constructs the flow with its real-data and symmetry
properties.  The internal symmetry induction also
starts at $t_0$: there is no earlier activity, the
action is scalar, the doubled tower operator has
the required symplectic symmetry, and the initial
mass term is a constant multiple of the invariant
$\mathsf S_1(\psi^{\rm bg})$.

The step bound gives
\[
 |\hat b_j|
 \le(1+L^{-1})(c_{2,{\rm loop}}+N_fc_2^F)
                       +C_w\phi(\hat x_{j-1}).
\]
The last term is at most $1/2$ by its original
small-coupling ceiling; the floor on $B_\sharp$
therefore gives $B_\sharp-1/2$.
Summing the coefficient recursion from
$\hat x_{t_0}=\mathsf t_{t_0}$ gives the stated
geometric bound.  Since
$\mathsf t_i\ge g^{-2}+\bar B$ and
$\gamma^{-2}\ge12\bar B$, it implies the lower
bound and the $11/12$, $13/12$ comparison.
This is an induction: the bound at the previous
level supplies the bound for the next increment.

The mass formula of \cref{C-419-4} is
\[
 \mathsf t_i\hat s_i=
 F^{\rm UV}+
 \sum_{t_0\le i'<i}
     \frac{\mathsf t_{i'}}{\hat x_{i'}}
                   \sigma_{i'}(i;\mathfrak m_i)
 +\sum_{t_0<j\le i}\mathsf t_j\hat\rho_j,
 \qquad
 \left|\sum_{t_0<j\le i}\mathsf t_j\hat\rho_j\right|
 \le\tfrac12.
\]
The slices are nonnegative and sum to at most $B_F$,
and $\mathsf t_{i'}/\hat x_{i'}\le12/11$.
This gives the interval with upper endpoint $\sigma_*$.
Consequently
$\hat x_i|\hat s_i|
\le(13/12)\sigma_*\le3B_F+1=\bar B_M$.
Use $\phi(x)\ge x^{-1}$ and $3\bar B_M/2\le A$
for the last mass bound.
In the activity recursion the direct term costs
$1/2$ of the closed bound, the mass contribution
at most $1/4$, and the lag sum at most
$\theta_EC_\omega S_\omega\le1/(4\sqrt2)$.
The two mass ceilings used here are
$8\theta_sh^2\bar B_M\gamma\le C_w$ and
$16c_sh^2\bar B_M^2\gamma^2\le C_2$.
Their sum gives $q_2$.

The open-domain extension in \cref{C-419-4}
is exactly $\mathscr D_k$.  Its family balls have
sizes at most three times the closed bounds.
Each of the four potential contributions is
less than $c_{\rm cl}/8$ there.
The displayed output estimates keep the mass
contribution separate, as in that extension.
For the scalar arrays,
$|x_k'-\mathsf t_k|
\le(2r_x+\bar B\gamma^2)\mathsf t_k$ and
$|s_k'|\le\sqrt2A\phi(\mathsf t_k)$.
The array estimate therefore gives
\[
 E_{\mathbf N}+C_{\mathsf n}
 +C(C_N+M^3)N_f
 +C(1+L^{-1})(c_{2,{\rm loop}}+N_fc_2^F)
 +CK_{\mathbf G}(\bar B\gamma^2+2r_x)+1.
\]
The original floor on $E_0$ contains these fixed
terms, the additional action-extraction term,
$CK_{\mathbf G}$ and $2$.
With $CK_{\mathbf G}\bar B\gamma\le1$,
$2r_x\le1$ and $\gamma\le1/2$, the displayed
bound is at most $E_0-1+\gamma\le E_0-1/2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The marked restart]\label{C-426-6}
Under (Mr1), (Mr2), start at the same
$\hat d_{t_0}^\bullet(0)$, insert
$\mathsf m_{k,\lambda}$ for $t_0\le k<t_1$,
and continue without marks through $K$.
For $|\lambda|\le r$ this defines a flow whose
points lie in $\mathscr D_k$, whose densities are
bounded Borel functions and whose families belong
to $\mathfrak F_j$.  Its exact measure formula
contains only the levels $j>t_0$.
It agrees up to $t_1$ with the marked restart
of \cref{C-418-5}.
The numbers and families are holomorphic for
$|\lambda|<r$, continuous on the boundary, real
at real $\lambda$, and at zero equal to the
unmarked restart.
All symmetry and pointing conclusions of
\cref{C-421-10} hold.

The four distance estimates of \cref{C-421-10}
hold with hatted reference values and
$\bar\theta=\bar\theta_{\rm rs}(|\lambda|)$.
At every $k\le K$,
\[
 |\hat E_k(\lambda)-\hat E_k|
 \le N_{[s]}s\left[
 C_{e,{\rm Lip}}\bar\theta+
 M^{-3}C_EK_\Pi\frac{w_*}{16}e^\pi
                         \frac{|\lambda|}{\Lambda_{\rm mk}}
                         \right],
\]
which is at most one under (Mr3).
Under (Mr4) one has in addition
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 |\hat b_j(\lambda)|<B_\sharp,\qquad
 |\hat x_i(\lambda)-\mathsf t_i|
       \le(1-L^{-(i-t_0)})\bar B,\\
 \operatorname{Re}\hat x_i(\lambda)\ge g^{-2}>1,
 \qquad |\hat x_K(\lambda)|\le X_g,\qquad
 |\hat s_i(\lambda)|
       \le\frac{12\bar B_M}{13\mathsf t_i}
       \le\frac{\bar B_M}{|\hat x_i(\lambda)|},\\
 \|\hat F_0^{(j)}(\lambda)\|_j
       \le C_w\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1}),\qquad
 \|\hat E_{\ge2}^{(j)}(\lambda)\|_j
       \le C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2.
 \end{gathered}
\]
The scalar array bound is $E_0$.
At a later level $k'\ge j$, the fermion terms
assigned to a cube have total norm at most
$C_\omega L^{(k'-j)/4}C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Use the four scaled distances of
\cref{C-421-10}, with hatted centres and indices
starting at $t_0$.
The initial distance is zero.
By \cref{C-426-5}, its open unit ball lies in
$\mathscr D_k$; its proof supplies all four output
bounds and the mass margin used in the marked-flow
argument.  In particular
$L^{-1}\hat x_k\le2\hat x_{k+1}$,
$\phi(\hat x_k)\le\phi(\hat x_{k+1})$, and
$\phi(\mathsf t_k)\le\phi(\hat x_{k+1})$.
Thus the same four normalized inequalities give
\[
 \theta_{k+1}\le C_{\rm Lip}\theta_k+
                       C_{\rm mk}\mathsf t_k\epsilon_k,
 \qquad
 \theta_k\le\bar\theta_{\rm rs}(|\lambda|)\le\tfrac12.
\]
Here $\epsilon_k=\epsilon_k^{\rm mk}(\lambda)$
below $t_1$ and zero afterwards.
The construction is simultaneous on all admitted
tori, with common infinite lattice families:
the start and all constants are independent of
the side, and (k0), (k1) admit the one-weight
setting on each of them.

We check the remaining restart hypotheses of
\cref{C-421-11}.  The initial density is bounded
and Borel by \cref{C-419-11}; its action, tower
and scalar mass term are real and invariant under
the internal symmetries.  There are no earlier
activities.  Its density transforms at tested
covariance pairs by the minimal-orbit argument
of \cref{C-419-4}.
The open-domain and size hypotheses are precisely
\cref{C-426-5}.  The marked step is
\cref{C-426-4}, with potential size below
$c_{\rm cl}/2<3c_{\rm cl}/4$.
Accordingly the symmetry proof in
\cref{C-421-10} applies in its stated order:
internal symmetries of totals and pointed totals,
real logarithm and covariance on shell,
uniform torus limits, scalar degree-two moment,
and its removal by mass extraction.
Analytic continuation gives the closed linear
conditions at complex $\lambda$.
This verifies membership in $\mathfrak F_j$
before the next step.

The density induction also applies:
the same completed square and background
substitutions rewrite the complex exponent;
the coefficient remains within
$(2r_x+\bar B\gamma^2)\mathsf t_k
\le3\sigma_\star\mathsf t_k/4$
of the calibration, so the Gaussian chart formula
has positive real relative coefficient.
Multiplication by the bounded Borel mark precedes
the linear image map; its chart expression is
the marked Gaussian integral.
Extraction rearranges the exponent and gives the
next bounded Borel density, zero off its test set.
This proves the exact measure identity and its
identification with \cref{C-418-5}.
The scalar-energy proof in \cref{C-421-10}
uses at most $s$ increments of size at most
$N_{[s]}$ and gives the displayed estimate.

For the additional conclusions let (Mr4) hold,
so $\bar\theta\le1/32$.
Put $D_i=\hat x_i(\lambda)-\hat x_i$.
Then
\[
 |D_i|\le\tfrac{13}{24}r_xL^s\mathsf b\,\bar\theta
 \le\tfrac{13}{24}\cdot\tfrac18\cdot\tfrac1{32}
 <\tfrac1{400}.
\]
Hence
$|\hat b_j(\lambda)-\hat b_j|
=|L^{-1}D_{j-1}-D_j|<1/200$.
The unmarked increment has margin $1/2$, proving
$|\hat b_j(\lambda)|<B_\sharp$.
Summing its recursion proves the coefficient window.
For the mass, $\phi(\hat x_i)\le1/2$ and
$A\bar\theta\le\mathsf t_i^{-1}$ give
\[
 |\hat s_i(\lambda)|
 \le(\sigma_*+1/6)\mathsf t_i^{-1}
 =(\tfrac{23}{11}B_F+\tfrac23)\mathsf t_i^{-1}
 \le\tfrac{12}{13}\bar B_M\mathsf t_i^{-1}.
\]
Together with $|\hat x_i(\lambda)|
\le13\mathsf t_i/12$, this proves the mass window.
The family bounds follow from
$q_2+2\bar\theta\le q_2+1/16<1$.

The local family conditions include property (N)
and vanishing matrix cell sums on the infinite
lattice.  On a torus their wrapping remainder is
included in $C_\omega$.
The earlier-family readout lemma therefore gives
the claimed $L^{(k'-j)/4}$ bound.
For the scalar arrays, the unmarked step at a
point of $\mathscr D_k$ has size at most $E_0-1/2$.
The marked change is at most
\[
 K_{\rm D}^{\rm arr}\epsilon_k
 \le\frac{C_{\rm win}\bar\theta}{2L^s\mathsf b}
 \le\frac1{2(L^s\mathsf b)^2}\le\tfrac12.
\]
This proves the array bound $E_0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A uniform radius for the marked restart]\label{C-426-7}
Let $K_{\rm rs}(g,\ell,n)$ be the least integer from
which on, at every $K^{\rm A}$,
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 e^{-\pi}\Lambda_{\rm mk}
                       \ge4\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{1/2}+1,\\
 C_{\rm win}L^sX_g\theta_{{\rm rs},K^{\rm A}}\le1,\\
 N_{[s]}s\left[
 C_{e,{\rm Lip}}\theta_{{\rm rs},K^{\rm A}}
 +2M^{-3}C_EK_\Pi\frac{w_*}{16}e^\pi
                          \Lambda_{\rm mk}^{-1/2}\right]\le1.
 \end{gathered}
\]
It exists and depends only on the constants,
$g,\ell,n$.  At such cutoffs satisfying (k0),
$r_{\rm rs}=2\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{1/2}$ satisfies
(Mr1)--(Mr4), for both lattices and every allowed label.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Substitute $r=r_{\rm rs}$ and use
$\mathsf b\le X_g$ and
$\bar\theta_{\rm rs}(r_{\rm rs})
\le\theta_{{\rm rs},K^{\rm A}}$.
The first condition gives (Mr1), the second (Mr4)
and hence (Mr2), and the third (Mr3).
For existence,
$\log\Lambda_{\rm mk}\ge c(K^{\rm A})^2$ for large
$K^{\rm A}$, where
$c=\kappa_{\rm t}A_1^2(\phi_1(n)\log L)^2>0$.
Also
\[
 \theta_{{\rm rs},K^{\rm A}}
 \le2C_{\rm mk}\frac{w_*}{16}e^\pi X_g
       K^{\rm A}(LC_{\rm Lip})^{K^{\rm A}}
