                                \Lambda_{\rm mk}^{-1/2}.
\]
The last two left sides are therefore bounded by
$ae^{bK^{\rm A}}\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{-1/2}$, with
$b=2+4\log L+\log C_{\rm Lip}$.
They tend to zero, and the first condition holds
once $\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{1/2}\ge5e^\pi$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Continuing the marked restart to the last level}

The estimate of the marked total uses all histories above
$t_1$.  We first continue the marked small-field flow
to $K$, retaining the bounds needed for the history
expansion.

\begin{lemma}[Room in the restarted bounds]\label{C-430-3}
Under (k0), (k1), the zero-source restart satisfies
\[
 |\hat s_i|\le\bar B_M/\mathsf t_i
 \le\sqrt2\gamma\bar B_M\phi(\hat x_i)
 \le\tfrac23A\phi(\hat x_i),\qquad t_0\le i\le K.
\]
For $t_0<j\le K$,
\[
 \|\hat F_0^{(j)}\|_j
       \le c_{\rm room}C_w\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1}),\qquad
 \|\hat E_{\ge2}^{(j)}\|_j
       \le c_{\rm room}C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2 .
\]
These bounds hold for the families, their pointed terms,
and both torus families at each level.  The second
also holds for the sum over any set of pointers of
each polymer.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The start has $\zeta=F^{\rm UV}\in[0,B_F]$:
\cref{C-398-40} gives
$0\le F^{\rm UV}\le\lim_k F(k;0)\le B_F$.
Thus \cref{C-419-4} gives
$|\hat s_i|\le\bar B_M/\mathsf t_i$ and
$|\hat x_i-\mathsf t_i|\le\bar B$.
Since $\mathsf t_i\ge\gamma^{-2}\ge12\bar B$,
\[
 \tfrac12\mathsf t_i\le\hat x_i\le2\mathsf t_i,\qquad
 \mathsf t_i^{-1}
 \le\gamma\mathsf t_i^{-1/2}
 \le\sqrt2\gamma\phi(\hat x_i).
\]
The first assertion follows from
$\sqrt2\gamma\le1$ and $3\bar B_M/2\le A$.
Also $\mathsf t_i^{-1}\le\gamma\phi(\mathsf t_i)$.

There are no activities at levels at most $t_0$.
Use the activity recursions with the inductive bounds
stated in the lemma.  The mass contributions obey
\[
 \theta_sh_F^2|\hat s_j|
     \le\tfrac18 C_w\phi(\mathsf t_j),\qquad
 c_sh_F^2|\hat s_j|^2
     \le\tfrac1{16}C_2\phi(\mathsf t_j)^2,
\]
by the chosen ceilings on $\gamma$.
For $m=j+1-i$ the contributions of level $i$ gain
\[
 L^{-m/2}(1+m\log L)^{\mathfrak p_0},
 \qquad
 L^{-m}(1+m\log L)^{2\mathfrak p_0},
\]
respectively.  Since
$2\sqrt2\theta_EC_\omega S_\omega\le1/2$,
the lag sums are bounded by $1/(4\sqrt2)$ times
the corresponding closed size.  Therefore
\[
 \begin{split}
 \epsilon_{j+1}
 &\le\left(\tfrac12+\tfrac18+\tfrac1{4\sqrt2}\right)
                         C_w\phi(\mathsf t_j),\\
 \epsilon^\psi_{j+1}
 &\le\left(\tfrac12+\tfrac1{16}+\tfrac1{4\sqrt2}\right)
                         C_2\phi(\mathsf t_j)^2.
 \end{split}
\]
Both coefficients are at most $c_{\rm room}$.
This starts at $j=t_0$, where the lag sums are empty.

For a set $S$ of output pointers, replace the insertion
at one pointer by the sum of all insertions sent to
$S$.  It multiplies each monomial of the fermion
potential by a number in $[0,1]$, and hence has norm
at most that of the potential.  It preserves parity
in the fluctuation, factorization and colour invariance.
On a one-cube domain its extracted mass term is a
part of the entire mass term, so extraction has the
same factor $K_\mu$.  The majorant is monotone in
the vertex norms polymer by polymer.  Thus the same
recursion bounds these sums, even when $S$ varies
with the polymer.  This proves the last assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The mark on each polymer]\label{C-430-4}
At a translation covariant point of the restarted
open step domain, with potential size at most
$c_{\rm cl}$, let $\mathsf r_k>0$ and
$|\lambda|\le(e^{\mathsf r_k}-1)/2$.
The difference before extraction between the marked
and unmarked new activities satisfies
\[
 \|\Delta^{\rm mk}_\lambda(X)\|_{h^{(k+1)}}
 \le K_\Pi\epsilon_k^{\rm mk}(\lambda)
                         e^{-\kappa_+d_{k+1}(X)},\qquad
 \epsilon_k^{\rm mk}(\lambda)
       =\frac{w_*}{32}\frac{|\lambda|}{e^{\mathsf r_k}-1}.
\]
The assertion holds at every regular complex pair
at the fixed radii, on the torus and on $\mathbb Z^3$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For completeness, the estimate before pointing uses
only one application of Schwarz's lemma.
On the distinguished boundary
$|\zeta_b|=e^{\mathsf r_k}$, the fourth origin is
\[
 \mathcal V^{\rm mk}_\zeta(Y;B)
  =\sum_{b:\,\square(b)=Y}(\operatorname{Log}\zeta_b)
           \mathbf1_{\{\mathsf t_k|B(b)|^2\ge a_k^2\}}.
\]
Because
$\mathbf1_{\{\mathsf t_k|B(b)|^2\ge a_k^2\}}
\le\mathsf t_k|B(b)|^2/a_k^2$ and
$\mathsf r_k+\pi=\kappa_{\rm mk}a_k^2$,
its input norm is at most $M^3\kappa_{\rm mk}=w_*/32$.
The refined terms meeting this origin, counted with
multiplicity, have total norm at most
$K_\Pi(w_*/32)e^{-\kappa_+d_{k+1}(X)}$.
The terms avoiding it are exactly those of the
unmarked expansion.

As proved in \cref{C-421-8,C-426-3}, the Mayer terms
are polynomials in the $\zeta_b$.  Their majorants
extend to the closed polydisc
$|\zeta_b|\le e^{\mathsf r_k}$ by the maximum
principle, applied after a norm-one linear
functional.  Uniform convergence then extends the
refined sum and the displayed bound to that
polydisc.  The Gaussian part subtracted from the
whole integral is independent of $\zeta$.
Consequently $\Delta^{\rm mk}_\lambda(X)$ is
holomorphic for $|\lambda|<e^{\mathsf r_k}-1$,
vanishes at zero, and is bounded by that majorant.
Schwarz's lemma gives the assertion.  Fitting
charts give the same expansion on $\mathbb Z^3$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The marked restart through the last level]\label{C-430-5}
Assume (k0), (k1), and $K^{\rm A}\ge K_\flat(g,\ell,n)$.
For either lattice, start at $t_0$ with the zero-source
restart, insert the uniform mark for $t_0\le k<t_1$,
and use unmarked steps for $t_1\le k<K$.
At each step extract its own numbers and use
\[
 x_{k+1}(\lambda)=L^{-1}x_k(\lambda)-b_{k+1}(\lambda),
 \qquad
 s_{k+1}(\lambda)=Ls_k(\lambda)+\mu_{k+1}(\lambda).
\]
Point $\Delta^{\rm mk}_\lambda$ by the tents and
the remaining activity by the ordinary step rule.
Put
\[
 E_k(\lambda)=\sum_{t_0<j\le k}e_j(\lambda)n_j,\qquad
 \bar\theta(\lambda)=
            \bar\theta_\flat|\lambda|\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{-1/2},
 \quad
 \epsilon(\lambda)=
            \epsilon_\flat|\lambda|\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{-1/2}.
\]
For $|\lambda|\le\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{1/2}$ this
construction has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Each step lies in the open domain about the
zero-source restart at the fixed fine mass.
The families lie in $\mathfrak F_j$; fitting
polymers on every admitted torus are the lifts of
the same families on $\mathbb Z^3$.
The image of the start along the history with no
large-field region has the level-$k$ form with
these numbers and activities, as an identity of
measures.  There are no activities at levels
at most $t_0$.  Through $t_1$ this image is the
marked restart of \cref{C-418-5}.
\item The numbers, energies and families are
holomorphic in the open disc and continuous on
its closure.  The numbers and energies are real
for real $\lambda$, with the corresponding
conjugation identities for the families.
At zero they equal the unmarked restart.
\item For $t_0\le i\le K$, $t_0<j\le K$,
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 |x_i(\lambda)-\hat x_i|
       \le\tfrac12r_x\hat x_i\bar\theta(\lambda),\qquad
 |s_i(\lambda)-\hat s_i|
       \le\tfrac13A\phi(\hat x_i)\bar\theta(\lambda),\\
 \|F_0^{(j)}(\lambda)-\hat F_0^{(j)}\|_j
       \le2C_w\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})\bar\theta(\lambda),\\
 \|E_{\ge2}^{(j)}(\lambda)-\hat E_{\ge2}^{(j)}\|_j
       \le2C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2\bar\theta(\lambda).
 \end{gathered}
\]
These include the pointed bounds and both torus
families.
\item The activity sizes are at most
$C_w\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})$ and
$C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2$, respectively.
The parts with fermion legs have the later-level
reading bound with zero cell sum on $\mathbb Z^3$.
The scalar arrays have bound $E_0$ at rate
$\kappa+1$, pointer by pointer; at $j>t_1$
they have bound $E_0-1$.
Moreover
\[
 |x_i(\lambda)-\mathsf t_i|\le\bar B,\qquad
 |s_i(\lambda)|\le2\bar B_M/\mathsf t_i.
\]
At real $\lambda$ the real coefficient windows hold.
\item
\[
 |E_K(\lambda)-\hat E_K|
 \le N_{[s]}s\bigl[
       C_{e,{\rm Lip}}\bar\theta(\lambda)
           +M^{-3}C_EK_\Pi\epsilon(\lambda)\bigr]\le1.
\]
\item For real $\lambda$, $|b_j(\lambda)|<B_\sharp$.
For $t_1<j\le K$,
\[
 |\mu_j(\lambda)|\le3\bar B_M/x_j(\lambda),\qquad
 |e_j(\lambda)|\le C'_e(1+\log x_{j-1}(\lambda)).
\]
At these levels the sum over any set of pointers
of each polymer has fermion norm at most
$C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2$, and
\[
 \|E_{\ge2}^{(j)}(\lambda)\|^{\rm pt}_j
      \le8M^3C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2.
\]
The last norm sums the norms at the individual
pointers, each with its own supremum over pairs.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
We give the changes needed to run the marked-flow
proof from $t_0$ and to obtain the later history bounds.
First, for $t_0\le k<t_1$,
\[
 e^{\mathsf r_k}\ge e^{-\pi}\Lambda_{\rm mk}
 \ge3\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{1/2}
 \ge2\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{1/2}+1 .
\]
Thus the mark is admitted and
\[
 \epsilon_k^{\rm mk}(\lambda)
 \le\frac{w_*}{16}e^\pi
                   \frac{|\lambda|}{\Lambda_{\rm mk}}
 =\epsilon(\lambda).
\]

Define $\theta_k(P)$ by the four scaled distances
in the proof of \cref{C-421-10}, centred now at
$\hat P_k$, with indices $i\ge t_0$, $j>t_0$.
Let $\Omega_k$ consist of points with $\theta_k<1$
whose families belong to $\mathfrak F_j$ and whose
remaining scalar terms are the prescribed functions
of the coefficients.  By \cref{C-430-3},
$|\hat s_i|\le2A\phi(\hat x_i)/3$.
Hence $\Omega_k$ lies inside the restarted open
domain, with potential size below $c_{\rm cl}$.
On it the step outputs satisfy
\[
 \begin{split}
 \|F_0^{(k+1)}\|_{k+1}
   &\le(2C_w+2\sqrt2\theta_sh_F^2A)\phi(\mathsf t_k),\\
 \|E_{\ge2}^{(k+1)}\|_{k+1}
   &\le(2C_2+4c_sh_F^2A^2)\phi(\mathsf t_k)^2,\\
 |b_{k+1}-e_{\mathsf N,k+1}-b^F_{k+1}|
   &\le2(C_w+\theta_sh_F^2A)\phi(\hat x_k),\\
 |\mu_{k+1}|
   &\le(C_\mu+c_sA^2)\phi(\hat x_k).
 \end{split}
\]
The subtracted terms in the third line do not read
the point.  The variable part of the vacuum
number is
\[
 -3(L^3-1)\operatorname{Log}(x'_k/\mathsf t_k)
       +\widetilde e_{k+1},\qquad
 |\widetilde e_{k+1}|\le M^{-3}K_M(c_{\rm cl}+1).
\]
On the complex line from $\hat P_k$ to $P$,
Schwarz's lemma bounds the difference of an output
bounded by $S$ by $2S\theta_k(P)$.
The mark adds the extraction differences of
\cref{C-426-4,C-430-4}.
Using
$L^{-1}\hat x_k\le2\hat x_{k+1}$,
$\phi(\hat x_k)\le\phi(\hat x_{k+1})$ and
$\phi(\mathsf t_k)^{-2}\le\mathsf t_k$,
the four normalized bounds therefore give
\[
 \theta_{k+1}\le C_{\rm Lip}\theta_k
                     +C_{\rm mk}\mathsf t_k\epsilon_k,
 \qquad
 \epsilon_k=
 \begin{cases}
  \epsilon_k^{\rm mk}(\lambda),&k<t_1,\\
  0,&k\ge t_1.
 \end{cases}
\]
Since $\theta_{t_0}=0$,
\[
 \theta_{k+1}
 \le\sum_{j=t_0}^{\min(k,t_1-1)}
        C_{\rm Lip}^{\,k-j}C_{\rm mk}\mathsf t_j\epsilon_j
 \le C_{\rm Lip}^{\,s}(s-u)C_{\rm mk}
                         L^sX_g\epsilon(\lambda)
 =\bar\theta(\lambda)\le1/32.
\]

The induction must also retain the conditions defining
$\mathfrak F_j$.  The proof of \cref{C-421-10}
applies with the following verifications.
The initial density has no activities and intertwines
the isometries, flavour action and conjugations.
At each marked step, \cref{C-426-3,C-426-4}
give the same four-origin expansion and tent
pointing; after $t_1$ use its value at the trivial
mark.  The scalar mark is fixed by all $\alpha_S$.
The pointed totals are real linear combinations of
the derivatives in the bond parameters of the
total logarithm, so they inherit these symmetries.
For real $\lambda$, fix the logarithm along
\[
 \rho\longmapsto
  \bigl(\rho\mathcal V,\,
          \mathbf1+\rho(\zeta-\mathbf1)\bigr),
                \qquad 0\le\rho\le1.
\]
If the potential size is $\sigma<c_{\rm cl}$,
the first coordinate has the required holomorphic
neighbourhood $|\rho|\sigma<c_{\rm cl}$; the second
stays in the interior of the mark polydisc.
The integral is fixed by $\sharp$.  The difference
between its logarithm and its image under $\sharp$
is a continuous scalar in $2\pi i\mathbb Z$,
zero at $\rho=0$, hence zero throughout.
This includes negative $1+\lambda$.
Real difference quotients give the same conclusion
for the pointed derivatives.

The uniform mark is preserved by the change of
fluctuation variables for each lattice isometry:
non-pivot bonds are permuted and their norms are
unchanged.  This proves covariance on shell.
The bounds above are uniform in the torus side;
fitting-chart identities and the exponential tails
therefore give the infinite lattice symmetries and
real extraction numbers, exactly as in
\cref{C-421-9,C-421-10}.
The degree-two cell moment is a scalar matrix;
the extracted mass cancels it, while the action
and vacuum extractions have the required invariant
forms.  Thus the families satisfy all the defining
linear conditions for real $\lambda$.
Those conditions extend to complex $\lambda$ by
the identity theorem and to the boundary by
continuity.  This closes the induction in
$\Omega_k$ and proves the first three assertions
apart from the measure identity.

For that identity the argument in
\cref{C-421-10} requires the level-$k$ form,
families in $\mathfrak F_j$, the prescribed scalar
terms, an admitted Gaussian coefficient, and the
expansion identity at the actual mark.  The first
conditions have just been checked, and
\[
 |x_k(\lambda)/\mathsf t_k-1|
 < r_x+\bar B\gamma^2\le2r_x\le\sigma_\star/2.
\]
The last is \cref{C-426-3} at a marked step and
the ordinary expansion otherwise.
The start is a bounded Borel density of the
asserted form.  The chart identity for the
integrand, followed by the partial Berezin
integral, therefore proves the measure identity
inductively.  Through $t_1$ its tests and Borel
marks are precisely those of \cref{C-418-5}.

The sizes follow from \cref{C-430-3} and
$c_{\rm room}+2\bar\theta_\flat\le1$.
Membership in $\mathfrak F_j$ gives zero cell
sums and the later-level reading estimate; the
wrapping cell remainder is included in $C_\omega$.
For scalar arrays, the ordinary step on these
balls has bound
\[
 E_{\mathbf N}+C_{\mathsf n}
 +C(C_N+M^3)N_f
 +C(1+L^{-1})(c_{2,{\rm loop}}+N_fc_2^F)
 +CK_{\mathbf G}(\bar B\gamma^2+2r_x)+1
 \le E_0-1.
\]
Here $\bar B\gamma^2+2r_x<1$, and the last term
bounds the fluctuation family by the stipulated
ceiling.  At a marked step the additional array
bound is $C_{\rm arr}\epsilon(\lambda)\le1$;
after $t_1$ there is no such term.
The coefficient window follows from
\[
 |x_i(\lambda)-\mathsf t_i|
 \le r_x\mathsf t_i\bar\theta_\flat
       +(1-L^{-(i-t_0)})\bar B\le\bar B,
\]
since $\mathsf t_iL^{i-t_0}\le L^sX_g$ and (m2).
The same condition gives
$|s_i(\lambda)|\le\bar B_M/\mathsf t_i+
A\bar\theta_\flat/3\le2\bar B_M/\mathsf t_i$.

The vacuum number changes by at most
$C_{e,{\rm Lip}}\theta_k+
M^{-3}C_EK_\Pi\epsilon_k$:
use
$|\operatorname{Log}(x_k(\lambda)/\hat x_k)|
\le r_x\theta_k$
and the Schwarz bound on $\widetilde e_{k+1}$.
There are $s$ terms and $n_{k+1}\le N_{[s]}$.
Condition (m3) gives the energy assertion.

It remains to verify the bounds for later histories.
At real $\lambda$ the ordinary increment differs
from $\hat b_{k+1}$ by at most
$2\sqrt2\bar\theta(\lambda)$.
The mark adds at most
$r_xC_{\rm mk}\epsilon(\lambda)/2
\le r_x\bar\theta(\lambda)/2$.
Thus $|b_{k+1}(\lambda)-\hat b_{k+1}|
\le3\bar\theta_\flat\le3/32$;
\cref{C-426-5} gives
$|\hat b_{k+1}|\le B_\sharp-1/2$.
More precisely, (m2) gives
\[
 |s_i(\lambda)|
 \le(1+L^{-(i-t_0)})\bar B_M/\mathsf t_i.
\]
For $j>t_1$, $j-t_0\ge2$, and hence
\[
 |\mu_j(\lambda)|
 \le\bigl(2+(1+L)L^{-(j-t_0)}\bigr)\bar B_M/\mathsf t_j
 \le\tfrac{11}4\tfrac{13}{12}\bar B_M/x_j(\lambda)
 <3\bar B_M/x_j(\lambda).
\]
After $t_1$ there is no mark, so
$|e_j(\lambda)-\hat e_j|\le C_{e,{\rm Lip}}
\bar\theta_\flat\le1$.
The unmarked restart has
\[
 |\hat e_j|
 \le3(L^3-1)\log\mathsf t_{j-1}
       +L^3C_{\rm co}+C_{\mathsf n}+C_F\nu
                   +C_e\sup_{x\ge1}\phi(x).
\]
Use $\log\mathsf t_{j-1}
\le\log x_{j-1}(\lambda)+\log2$ and
$3(L^3-1)(1-\log2)\ge1$ to obtain the
stated $C'_e$ bound.

For a sum over any set of output pointers in an
unmarked step, the insertion argument of
\cref{C-430-3} gives the same ball bound
$(2C_2+4c_sh_F^2A^2)\phi(\mathsf t_k)^2$.
The Schwarz estimate bounds its difference from
the corresponding unmarked-restart sum by
$2C_2\phi(\mathsf t_k)^2C_{\rm Lip}\theta_k
\le2C_2\phi(\mathsf t_k)^2\bar\theta(\lambda)$.
The room estimate proves the required size.
Finally apply the pointed-sum lemma
the pointed-sum lemma of QCD3\_M1, Lemma~8.8,
checking its hypotheses:
the step is unmarked with its ordinary pointing
in the restarted open domain; its coefficient
is real; $|s_k(\lambda)|\le2\bar B_M/\mathsf t_k$;
all earlier fermion activities have size
$C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{i-1})^2$, and those before
$t_0$ vanish.  The step uses these families
through their values on polymers, so their earlier
marks impose no further condition.
The lemma gives $C_2^{\rm pt}=8M^3C_2$ with
the separate suprema at each pointer, as claimed.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Summing the histories after the mark}

\begin{lemma}[The marked flow as a flow with free past]\label{C-430-6}
Under the hypotheses of \cref{C-430-5}, let
$0\le\lambda\le\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{1/2}$.
For $t_0<j\le t_1$, point the fermion part of
$E^{(j)}(\lambda)$ at the centre of the cell
where its polymer is filed, in the same shares
if it is filed at several cells.  Keep its scalar
pointing.  Keep all pointing at levels $j>t_1$,
and set $E^{(j)}=0$ for $j\le t_0$.
These families, the marked-flow numbers at and
above $t_1$, and $E_{t_1}(\lambda)$ form a flow
with free past at $t_1$ in the sense of
\cref{C-418-18}, with $R^{(j)}=E^{(j)}$ and
$D^{(j)}=0$ for $j\le t_1$.

Its initial density is the level-$t_1$ term of
the marked restart.  Write $g_h[\lambda]$ for
the density, against $\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}$,
of its subsequent history $h\in\mathcal H_k^{(t_1)}$.
The history bounds of \cref{C-418-18} hold
with the original constants
$C_5^F,C_E^F,C_\flat^F,c_\star,\mathsf C_{\rm maj}^\dagger$,
with $E_k(\lambda)$ and with scalar history
terms $f_j=0$ for $j\le t_1$.
The action coefficient is
\[
 \beta_h=\beta-\sum_{t_0<j\le k}
                   L^jb_j(\lambda)\varphi_j,\qquad
 \beta=L^K\mathsf b.
\]
Both versions of the bound, with $-\beta A$
and with $-A(\beta_h,\cdot)$, hold.
In particular,
\[
 \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_K^{(t_1)}}
     \int\|g_h[\lambda]\|_{h_F}\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}
 \le\exp[E_K(\lambda)+(C+2)\ell^3].
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
We verify each hypothesis of the free-past
construction.  The constants satisfy its original
ceilings and $(\Gamma^F)$, which belongs to
the assumptions on the two-cutoff data.
Condition (k0) gives $1\le t_0<t_1<K$.

For (F1), \cref{C-430-5} gives local, even,
Borel pointed terms, holomorphic on the regular
complex pairs at fixed radii, joint gauge
invariance, $\mathrm U(N_f)\times\mathrm U(N_f)$
invariance, translation covariance, the pointed
sum rule, zero cell sums on $\mathbb Z^3$, and
the scalar normalization.  Filing the older
fermion terms at their cell centres preserves
all these properties: each new pointed term is
a nonnegative share of the same polymer value,
the shares add to one, the cell sums do not
depend on pointing, and filing commutes with
translations and charts.  The zero earlier
families satisfy these linear conditions.

For (F2), after $t_1$ the step is the ordinary
small-field step with its original pointing.
Repointing the older terms has not changed its
input: the fermion potential and the filing
read their values on polymers.  The extraction
rules therefore give exactly the same numbers
and later families.  Their sizes, arrays,
windows, sums over subsets of pointers and
$\|\cdot\|^{\rm pt}$ bounds, together with
$|b_j|<B_\sharp$ and
$|e_j|\le C'_e(1+\log x_{j-1})$, are all
provided by \cref{C-430-5}.

For (F3), take $R^{(j)}=E^{(j)}$, $D^{(j)}=0$.
On each older polymer, the norms of the
repointed fermion terms add to the norm of
its value, since they are nonnegative shares.
Thus their pointed-sum size is
$C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2$.
The fluctuation families retain size
$C_w\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})$, and the later-level
reading and scalar array bounds are unchanged.
The lag differences vanish.  The initial
density reads the same polymer values and
numbers as before repointing, so is exactly
the marked term at $t_1$.
This proves the asserted applicability of
\cref{C-418-18}.

Its effective coefficient initially reads
$L^{t_1}x_{t_1}(\lambda)$.
The recurrence and
$x_{t_0}(\lambda)=L^s\mathsf b$ give
\[
 \sum_{t_0<j\le t_1}L^jb_j(\lambda)
 =L^{t_1}(\mathsf t_{t_1}-x_{t_1}(\lambda)).
\]
Every history under consideration has
$\varphi_j=1$ for $j\le t_1$.
This converts the free-past action coefficient
to $\beta_h$ above.
The corresponding bound on the absolute
action correction follows because every
plaquette action is nonnegative:
\[
 \left|\sum_{t_0<j\le k}
                 L^jb_j(\lambda)A(\varphi_j,\mathsf U)\right|
 \le L^{t_1}|x_{t_1}(\lambda)-\mathsf t_{t_1}|A(\mathsf U)
       +\sum_{t_1<j\le k}
               |L^jb_j(\lambda)A(\varphi_j,\mathsf U)|.
\]

For the final summation extend to all histories
at level $K$ by putting
\[
 f(h)=
 e^{-E_K(\lambda)+\sum_j\operatorname{Re}f_j(\mathcal S(h))}
       \int\|g_h[\lambda]\|_{h_F}\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}
\]
on $\mathcal H_K^{(t_1)}$, and zero elsewhere.
On labels occurring there put
$\mathsf e(\mathcal S)=-\sum_j\operatorname{Re}f_j(\mathcal S)$,
and put it zero on other labels.
The history and label estimates make
$(f,\mathsf e)$ an admitted pair for the
history summation theorem at
\[
 c=(c_\star+c_\Theta)/2,\qquad
 \mathsf C_{\rm maj}^{\rm th}\ge
                   \mathsf C_{\rm maj}^\dagger,\qquad
 C_\flat^{\rm th}\ge C_\flat^F .
\]
Decreasing the rate and enlarging these
constants weakens the required majorants.
The prescribed floors on $\mathfrak p_0$ and
the corresponding ceilings
$\log\gamma^{-2}\ge\mathsf Y_{\rm f1}$ or
$\mathsf Y_{\rm f2}$ are exactly those of
that summation theorem.
Its nonnegative mark $\Theta^{(K)}$ gives
\[
 \begin{split}
 e^{-E_K(\lambda)}
 \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_K^{(t_1)}}
       \int\|g_h[\lambda]\|_{h_F}\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}
 &=\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_K}
                  f(h)e^{\mathsf e(\mathcal S(h))}\\
 &\le\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_K}
                  f(h)e^{\mathsf e(\mathcal S(h))+\Theta^{(K)}(h)}
 \le\Pi_K(C,c'')\le e^{(C+2)n_K},
 \end{split}
\]
where $c''=(1-\eth)(c_\star-c_\Theta)/2>0$
and $n_K=\ell^3$.
For $c_a>0$, $C$ includes
$\lambda_L=(6L^3+1)\log2$; for $c_a=0$
this addition is unnecessary.
These are the same constants and threshold
choices used in the ordinary history sum.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Recovering the marked total]\label{C-430-7}
With the hypotheses and notation of
\cref{C-430-6},
\[
 Z^\bullet_\lambda
 =\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_K^{(t_1)}}
           \operatorname{Ber}\int g_h[\lambda]\,
                                  d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}
 \le\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_K^{(t_1)}}
                \int\|g_h[\lambda]\|_{h_F}\,
                                  d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The issue is that the coordinate maps are partial.
We show that they lose no marked mass, using the
already established conservation at $\lambda=0$.

On $\mathcal Y=\mathcal V(\Lambda_{s,\ell})$
write $W_j=\mathcal M^{j-t_0}W$.
For $h\in\mathcal H_k^{(t_1)}$ let $\varphi_h$
be $\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet$ times the tests
and gauge-fixing factors of the steps of $h$
above $t_1$, read at these $W_j$.
This is the nonnegative bounded Borel weight
$\mathfrak w_{h/t_0}$ of \cref{C-427-8}.
Let
\[
 \mathsf m_\lambda(W)=
       \prod_{t_0\le k<t_1}\mathsf m_{k,\lambda}^\bullet(W_k).
\]
For the present $\lambda$ it lies in
$[1,(1+\lambda)^{N_{\rm mk}}]$.
The total Berezin mass of the term of $h$ is
\[
       \int_{\mathcal Y}
             \varphi_h\mathsf m_\lambda\hat F_0^\bullet\,dW .
 \tag{*}
\]
To check this identity, first push the restarted
start through the marked steps to $t_1$.
Multiplying a pushforward by a Borel function
of its image is the same as multiplying its
preimage measure by the pullback.
Thus its Berezin integral is
$(\mathcal M^{t_1-t_0})_*
(\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet\mathsf m_\lambda\hat\nu)$.
Use the bounded bare density $\hat\varsigma$
of \cref{C-427-8} and replace it by
\[
 \varsigma_\lambda
   =\hat\varsigma\,(\mathsf m_\lambda\circ\mathcal M^{t_0}).
\]
The identity of that lemma,
$(\mathcal M^{t_0})_*(\mathfrak w_h\hat\varsigma\,dU)
=\mathfrak w_{h/t_0}\hat\nu$,
then holds with the added mark.
The same induction under the partial history
maps, from the one-to-one Borel coordinates
at $t_1$, identifies the subsequent term with
the coordinate image at the density
$\varsigma_\lambda$.
The no-loss property of these coordinates
gives its mass $\int\mathfrak w_h\varsigma_\lambda\,dU$,
which is (*).  This argument uses only bounded
Borel multiplication and the identities for
partial Berezin integrals proved in
\cref{C-427-8}.

Consider now one step $t>t_1$ from a history
$h'$, and a plaquette outcome $\mathsf p$.
Write $P''=P''_t(\mathsf p)$,
$\mathsf N=B(P'')\setminus P''$.
Let $\mathbf1_t^{\rm P}(\mathsf p)$ be its
plaquette test and $\mathbf1^{\rm D}_{h',\mathsf p}$
the indicator that its averaged contours are
defined.  The product form of the history tests
gives
\[
 \sum_{\mathsf o:\,\mathsf p(\mathsf o)=\mathsf p}
        \varphi_{(h',\mathsf o)}
 =\varphi_{h'}\mathbf1_t^{\rm P}(\mathsf p)
                  \mathfrak G_{t-1}(W_{t-1};P''),\qquad
 \sum_{\mathsf p}\mathbf1_t^{\rm P}(\mathsf p)=1.
\]
For $v\in G^{\mathsf N}$ extend $v$ to the
bare lattice constantly on level-$(t-1)$
blocks, and write $s_j$ for its restriction
at level $j$.  Then $s_{t-1}=v$,
$s_t=1$, and at earlier levels the values
are constant on the corresponding blocks.
The substitution $W\mapsto W^{s_{t_0}}$
preserves Haar measure, $W_t$, the earlier
history tests and gauge factors, and the
plaquette test.
It also preserves $\hat F_0^\bullet$:
minimal orbits transform covariantly,
the weighted action and regularity cut are
unchanged, and the effective fermion operator
is conjugated, preserving its determinant.

It preserves the mark as well.
For $k<t_1$, the averaged background transforms
by $s_k$, since $s_k$ is constant on
level-$(k+1)$ blocks.  The intrinsic logarithm
therefore carries the fluctuation to
$\operatorname{Ad}(s_k(b_-))\mathcal A_k^\diamond(b)$.
Its norm, the threshold indicator and every
factor of $\mathsf m_\lambda$ are unchanged.
Average the substitution over $G^{\mathsf N}$.
The normalized gauge-fixing identity is
\[
 \int\mathfrak G_{t-1}(W_{t-1}^v;P'')\,dv
             =\mathbf1^{\rm D}_{h',\mathsf p}.
\]
Fubini then gives
\[
 \int\varphi_{h'}\mathbf1_t^{\rm P}(\mathsf p)
       \mathfrak G_{t-1}\mathsf m_\lambda\hat F_0^\bullet\,dW
 =\int\varphi_{h'}\mathbf1_t^{\rm P}(\mathsf p)
       \mathbf1^{\rm D}_{h',\mathsf p}
                         \mathsf m_\lambda\hat F_0^\bullet\,dW .
\]
Consequently the loss in this step is
\[
 \int\varphi_{h'}\mathsf m_\lambda\hat F_0^\bullet\,dW
 -\sum_{\mathsf o}
       \int\varphi_{(h',\mathsf o)}
                        \mathsf m_\lambda\hat F_0^\bullet\,dW
 =\sum_{\mathsf p}
       \int g_{h',\mathsf p}\mathsf m_\lambda\hat F_0^\bullet\,dW,
\]
where
$g_{h',\mathsf p}=
\varphi_{h'}\mathbf1_t^{\rm P}(\mathsf p)
(1-\mathbf1^{\rm D}_{h',\mathsf p})\ge0$.
Summing over steps and histories telescopes to
\[
 Z^\bullet_\lambda-
 \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_K^{(t_1)}}
       \int\varphi_h\mathsf m_\lambda\hat F_0^\bullet\,dW
 =
 \sum_{t=t_1+1}^K\ 
 \sum_{h'\in\mathcal H_{t-1}^{(t_1)}}\
 \sum_{\mathsf p}
       \int g_{h',\mathsf p}\mathsf m_\lambda\hat F_0^\bullet\,dW.
\]
At zero the left side vanishes by the unmarked
history identity in \cref{C-418-24}.
Every term on the right is nonnegative since
$\hat F_0^\bullet\ge0$.
Thus each $g_{h',\mathsf p}\hat F_0^\bullet$
vanishes almost everywhere, and remains zero
after multiplication by the bounded mark.
This proves the equality for every present
$\lambda$.  Finally
$|\operatorname{Ber}F|\le\|F\|_{h_F}$
because $h_F\ge1$, proving the bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Bound for the marked total]\label{C-430-8}
Under (k0), (k1), and
$K^{\rm A}\ge K_\flat(g,\ell,n)$, the marked
restart exists on
$|\lambda|\le\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{1/2}$
with the form and holomorphy of \cref{C-430-5}.
Moreover
\[
 Z^\bullet_{\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{1/2}}
 \le e\,\mathsf M_{g,\ell}\hat T^\bullet(0),
 \qquad
 \left.\partial_\lambda Z^\bullet_\lambda\right|_{\lambda=0}
 \le e\,\mathsf M_{g,\ell}\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{-1/2}
                                          \hat T^\bullet(0).
\]
The first bound holds also for every
$0\le\lambda\le\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{1/2}$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The preceding two lemmas and
\cref{C-430-5} give
\[
 Z^\bullet_{\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{1/2}}
 \le \exp[\hat E_K+1+(C+2)\ell^3].
\]
The positive unmarked-total estimate
of \cref{C-418-24} applies under (k0), (k1):
$u\ge u_*$, $s\ge s_F$ and
$L^u\gamma^{-2}\ge\Theta_\star$.
It gives
$\hat T^\bullet(0)\ge
\exp[\hat E_K-C_P(1+\log X_g)\ell^3]$.
The quotient is therefore at most
\[
 e\exp[(C+2+C_P(1+\log X_g))\ell^3]
       =e\,\mathsf M_{g,\ell}.
\]
The total is a polynomial in $\lambda$ with
nonnegative coefficients, by its Borel mark
representation and $\hat F_0^\bullet\ge0$.
It is increasing for $\lambda\ge0$, and its
linear coefficient is at most
$\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{-1/2}
Z^\bullet_{\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{1/2}}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The marked restart input]\label{C-426-9}
Let
$K_{\rm mk}(g,\ell,n)=
\max\{K_{\rm rs}(g,\ell,n),K_\flat(g,\ell,n)\}$.
Under (k0)--(k2) and $K^{\rm A}\ge K_{\rm mk}$,
the marked restart through $t_1$ has the
numbers, activities, closed bounds and
level-$k$ measure form of \cref{C-426-6}
for $|\lambda|\le2\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{1/2}$.
Its normalizers and scalar remainders use
the actual pair
$(\mathsf t_{j-1},x_{j-1}(\lambda))$.
It is holomorphic in the open disc, real
at real $\lambda$, and agrees with the
unmarked restart at zero.  Furthermore
\[
 Z^\bullet_{\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{1/2}}
 \le e\,\mathsf M_{g,\ell}\hat T^\bullet(0)
 \le2e\,\mathsf M_{g,\ell}\hat T^\bullet(0).
\]
Thus it supplies the marked input of
\cref{C-418-15}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The threshold lemma \cref{C-426-7} verifies
(Mr1)--(Mr4) at $r=2\Lambda_{\rm mk}^{1/2}$;
apply \cref{C-426-6}.
The smaller-disc scalar bound is
\cref{C-430-8}, proved independently of this
corollary.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The top density test}

The geometric weight $\mathsf k^\bullet$ need not
include the density test at depth $u$.  The
restarted history weight $\hat{\mathsf k}^\bullet$
does.  We estimate the difference by histories
with a large-field region at that level.  A
regularity estimate descending from depth $u$
ensures that the geometric weight also imposes
the density test at the starting depth $s$.

\begin{definition}[Weights and starting test]\label{C-425-2}
Fix one of the two lattices and omit $\bullet$.
Assume (k0) and $L^u\gamma^{-2}\ge\Theta_\star$.
Write $K=K^\bullet$, $t_0=K-s$, $t_1=K-u$,
$\mathsf t_j=L^{K-j}\mathsf b$, and
$W_j=\mathcal M^{j-t_0}W$ for $W\in\mathcal Y$.
In particular $t_0\ge2$.
Let $\mathsf{In}_j$ be the inner ball and
$\mathsf{Cut}_j$ the background cut of radius
$c_\rho\varepsilon(\mathsf t_j)$.
With the fluctuation test $\chi_j^{\rm sf}$
and gauge factor $\mathfrak G_j$,
\[
 \mathsf k(W)=
 \mathbf1_{\mathsf{In}_{t_1}}(W_{t_1})
 \prod_{t_0\le j<t_1}
       [\mathbf1_{\mathsf{Cut}_j}
                       \mathfrak G_j\chi_j^{\rm sf}](W_j).
\]
Write $\chi_j(T_\ell)$ for the density test and
$\mathcal V_j^\chi=\{\chi_j(T_\ell)=1\}$.
The frame assumptions give
$\varpi(V)<2\varepsilon(\mathsf t_j)
\le\varepsilon_{\mathcal W}\alpha_0$ on this set;
hence
$\mathcal V_j^\chi\subset\mathsf{In}_j
\subset\mathsf{Cut}_j$ when $1\le j\le t_1$.

The restart includes $\chi_{t_0}(T_\ell)$ in
its starting density.  Its Berezin integral is
$\hat F_z^\chi(W)\,dW$, where
\[
 \hat F_z^\chi=\chi_{t_0}(T_\ell)\hat F_z.
\]
Where the effective operator is formed, this is
\[
 \chi_{t_0}(T_\ell)(W)
 e^{-\mathsf{wab}(\mathsf c_{w_z},W)}
                      \det\hat{\mathbb D}(W;s(z)).
\]
Set $\hat F_z$ and $\hat F_z^\chi$ to zero
where the operator or its mass kernel is not
formed.  Thus the pointwise identities below
make sense for every $z$; holomorphy and
integral identities are asserted only on their
stated source domains.  Whenever $\hat T(z)$
is used assume $u\ge u_*$ and
$s(z)\in\mathscr O_{t_1}$; whenever
$T^{\rm sf}(z)$ is used assume also $s\ge s_F$
and the source bounds of \cref{C-418-11}.

For $h\in\mathcal H_k^{(t_0)}$ let
$\hat{\mathfrak w}_h$ be the product of its
outcome indicators and gauge factors for
the steps above $t_0$, read on $\mathcal Y$.
Set $\hat{\mathfrak w}_{h_\emptyset^{(t_0)}}=1$.
These are bounded nonnegative Borel functions.
The tests above $t_0$ read no field below
$t_0$: the earlier determining sets are empty
because their regions are the full torus.
For a bounded Borel function $\varsigma\ge0$ put
\[
 \mathsf m_\varsigma(h)
       =\int_{\mathcal Y}\hat{\mathfrak w}_h\varsigma\,dW,
 \qquad
 \mathsf m(h)=\mathsf m_{\hat F_0^\chi}(h).
\]

Use the floor on $A_0$
\[
 (1-L^{-3/2})A_0>2B_3C_HA_1.                 \tag{D}
\]
Here $C_H$ is the constant in the background
descent estimate, namely
$4C_{\rm db}\max\{2,K_{\rm B}^{\rm s}(\rho_{\rm s})\}$.
Put
\[
 \sigma_D=\frac1{2B_3}
       -\frac{C_HA_1}{(1-L^{-3/2})A_0}>0
\]
and let $n_0$ be the least nonnegative integer
with $2B_3L^{-3n_0/2}\le\sigma_D$.
Let $K_{\rm tt}(n)$ be the least integer from
which on $s-u\ge n_0$.  It exists and satisfies
\[
 K_{\rm tt}(n)\le
 \max\left\{2,\
 \left\lceil\frac{2(6n+11)(n_0+1)}{1-c_\#/10}\right\rceil
 \right\}.
\]
Indeed $s-u\ge(1-c_\#/10)\phi_2(n)K^{\rm A}-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[The two weights]\label{C-425-3}
On $\mathcal Y$,
\[
 \hat{\mathsf k}=
 \prod_{t_0\le j<t_1}
   \chi_{j+1}(T_\ell)(W_{j+1})\,
   \mathsf q_{j+1}(W_j)\,
   \mathfrak G_j(W_j)\chi_j^{\rm sf}(W_j)
 =\hat{\mathfrak w}_{h_\emptyset^{(t_1)}}.
\]
Both weights are bounded nonnegative Borel
functions, and
\[
 \hat{\mathsf k}=
      \chi_{t_1}(T_\ell)(W_{t_1})\,\mathsf k,\qquad
 0\le\hat{\mathsf k}\le\mathsf k .
\]
If $\hat{\mathsf k}(W)\ne0$, all $W_j$,
$t_0\le j\le t_1$, pass their density tests
and both weights equal $\prod_j\mathfrak G_j(W_j)$.
Consequently
\[
 \hat{\mathsf k}\hat F_z=
       \hat{\mathsf k}\hat F_z^\chi,\qquad
 \hat T(z)=\int_{\mathcal Y}\hat{\mathsf k}\hat F_z^\chi\,dW
          =\int_{\mathcal Y}\hat{\mathsf k}\hat F_z\,dW
\]
on the asserted source domain.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The small-field history weight of one step has
exactly the factors displayed, together with
$\mathsf q_j^0=1$ for $j\ge1$.
This identity holds for arbitrary consecutive
block fields: the tests and gauge factors are evaluated
from these fields alone, as in the coordinate definitions
of \cite[\S53.1 and Prop.\ 53.14]{YMM1}.
The tests are Borel indicators, the gauge
factors are bounded Borel functions, the cuts
are open, and the block map is Borel.

The density-test implication follows from
\cite[Props.\ 53.13 and 53.14]{YMM1}. Indeed a
passed level-$(j+1)$ density test gives the regular
next datum. The small-field test compares $W$ with
its background on each test cube; the small-bond
argument in the proof of Prop.\ 53.14 makes every
$Q$ test equal to one. The pair then belongs to
$\mathsf{PQ}_{j+1}(T_\ell)$, and Prop.\ 53.13
gives all level-$j$ density tests. Thus
if $\chi_{j+1}(T_\ell)(\mathcal MW)=1$
and $\chi_j^{\rm sf}(W)=1$, then
$\chi_j(T_\ell)(W)=\mathsf q_{j+1}(W)=1$.
If $\hat{\mathsf k}>0$, its factors first
give every density test above $t_0$ and
then this implication gives the one at $t_0$.
All inner-ball and field-cut indicators in
$\mathsf k$ are therefore one, proving
equality on this support.
Conversely, if $\mathsf k>0$ and the density
test at $t_1$ passes, descend successively
from $t_1-1$ to $t_0$ using the same implication.
All the remaining factors of
$\hat{\mathsf k}$ then equal one.
This proves the weight identity everywhere.
It also gives
$\hat{\mathsf k}\chi_{t_0}(T_\ell)=\hat{\mathsf k}$.
Finally the total of the restarted image
is its weight integrated against the
Berezin integral of its start,
$\hat F_z^\chi\,dW$, by \cref{C-418-19}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The starting density]\label{C-425-4}
For $s\ge s_F$, $\hat F_0$ and $\hat F_0^\chi$
are bounded nonnegative Borel functions,
$\hat F_0^\chi\le\hat F_0$, and they are
invariant under all gauge transformations
of the level-$t_0$ lattice.
They vanish off $\mathsf{Cut}_{t_0}$
and $\mathcal V_{t_0}^\chi$, respectively.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
On the open field cut the weighted action is
continuous, real, and has modulus at most
$\frac32(c_\rho\varepsilon(\mathsf t_{t_0}))^2
N_{[s]}L^s\mathsf b$.
The determinant is bounded, Borel and positive
by \cref{C-418-11}.  Multiplication by the
Borel indicators proves the size and support
claims.

A gauge transformation $u$ preserves the
density test and field cut.  Extend it to
the bare lattice by the identity away from
level-$t_0$ sites.  This maps the minimal orbit
over $W$ onto the orbit over $W^u$ and
preserves its weighted action.
The Dirac operator, block averages and
fermion background transform by conjugation
with the restrictions of this extension.
The mass function $F^{\rm UV}/(L^s\mathsf b)$
acts on no colour index.  Therefore
$\hat{\mathbb D}(W^u;0)=
u\hat{\mathbb D}(W;0)u^{-1}$,
so the determinant is unchanged.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Averaging the gauge factors]\label{C-425-5}
If $\varsigma\ge0$ is bounded, Borel and gauge
invariant on $\mathcal Y$, then
\[
 \int\mathsf k\varsigma\,dW
 \le\int\prod_{t_0\le j<t_1}\mathfrak G_j(W_j)
                                      \varsigma(W)\,dW
 \le\int\varsigma\,dW.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The first inequality discards indicators.
Put $J_j=\int\prod_{t_0\le i<j}\mathfrak G_i(W_i)
\varsigma(W)\,dW$.
For the full level-$(j+1)$ site set $P''$
let $\mathsf N=B(P'')\setminus P''$.
Lift $v\in G^{\mathsf N}$ to level $t_0$
constantly on level-$j$ blocks.
The lift changes $W_j$ to $W_j^v$, fixes
$W_{j+1}$, and preserves all earlier gauge
factors, $\varsigma$ and Haar measure.
Averaging over $v$ therefore replaces
$\mathfrak G_j(W_j)$ in $J_{j+1}$ by the
indicator that its averaged contours exist, by
\cite[eq.\ (55)]{YMM1}; the block-constant lift
and its invariance are those used in
\cite[eq.\ (651)]{YMM1}. This indicator is at most one, so
$J_{j+1}\le J_j$.  Iterate.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The starting mass and the history masses}

We first record why the history coordinates can be
read on $\mathcal Y$ without losing mass.  This
also supplies the lifting fact used in the
subsequent gauge average.

\begin{lemma}[Mass of a restarted history]\label{C-425-7}
Assume $u\ge u_*$ and $s\ge s_F$.
For $h\in\mathcal H_k^{(t_0)}$, the Berezin
integral of its restarted term is the image
of $\hat{\mathfrak w}_h\hat F_0^\chi\,dW$
under the free coordinates of $h$ read on
$\mathcal Y$.  Its total mass is $\mathsf m(h)$,
and
\[
 0\le\mathsf m(h)
   =\int\operatorname{Ber}\hat g_h\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}
   \le\int\|\hat g_h\|_{h_F}\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
First consider any $W\in\mathcal V_{t_0}^\chi$.
It admits a bare lift whose small-field history
through $t_0$ has positive weight.
To construct it, set $V_{t_0}=W$ and
$V_j=V_j^{\rm bf}(V_{j+1})$ successively for
$j=t_0-1,\ldots,0$.
If $V_{j+1}$ passes its density test, its
background is defined in the axial gauge,
$\mathcal M(V_j)=V_{j+1}$, and the averaged
background is stably defined by
\cite[Prop.\ 52.3 and Lem.\ 113.10]{YMM1}.
Its fluctuation is zero, so
$\chi_j^{\rm sf}(V_j)=1$.
The density-test descent implication gives
$\chi_j(T_\ell)(V_j)=
\mathsf q_{j+1}(V_j)=\mathsf q_j^0(V_j)=1$.
All averaged contour variables used by the
gauge factor equal the identity, where its
factors are positive.  The bounds needed
here hold at every descended level since
$\mathsf t_j\ge L^u\gamma^{-2}\ge\Theta_\star$.
Thus $U=V_0$ has $\mathcal M^{t_0}U=W$
and $\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset^{(t_0)}}(U)>0$.

The weight factorization
\[
 \mathfrak w_h(U)=
 \mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset^{(t_0)}}(U)\,
          \hat{\mathfrak w}_h(\mathcal M^{t_0}U)
 \tag{*}
\]
follows directly from its product over steps:
the factors through $t_0$ are those of the
empty history, and later tests read only
levels at least $t_0$.

Let $\xi_h$ denote the full history coordinates.
The determining sets below $t_0$ and the
external fluctuation bonds there are empty.
At $h_0=h_\emptyset^{(t_0)}$ the free
coordinate is therefore the entire level-$t_0$
block field, and
\[
 \xi_{h_0}=(\Pi_{h_0}^{\rm le}\times\mathrm{id})
                              \circ\mathcal M^{t_0}.
\]
For each later step let
$\Sigma^{\rm co\prime}_{h|_t}$ be its Borel
partial coordinate map.  The coordinate
composition property, including its domains,
is
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \xi_{h|_t}=
       \Sigma^{\rm co\prime}_{h|_t}\circ\xi_{h|_{t-1}},\\
 \operatorname{dom}\xi_{h|_t}
 =\{U\in\operatorname{dom}\xi_{h|_{t-1}}:
       \xi_{h|_{t-1}}(U)
                    \in\operatorname{dom}\Sigma^{\rm co\prime}_{h|_t}\}.
 \end{gathered}
\]
It applies to the canonical step data at the
calibration frame: these data have the
coordinate properties at every step and
history, by \cite[Prop.\ 53.14 and eq.\ (1357)]{YMM1},
including equality of the new variables on their
precise domains.
Define on $\mathcal Y$
\[
 \hat\xi_{h_0}=\Pi_{h_0}^{\rm le}\times\mathrm{id},
 \qquad
 \hat\xi_{h|_t}=
       \Sigma^{\rm co\prime}_{h|_t}\circ\hat\xi_{h|_{t-1}}
\]
on the inverse image of the domain of the
step map.  These are Borel partial maps.
Induction gives
\[
 \xi_h=\hat\xi_h\circ\mathcal M^{t_0},\qquad
 \operatorname{dom}\xi_h
   =(\mathcal M^{t_0})^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}\hat\xi_h).
\]
Composing with $\operatorname{res}^{\rm le}_h
\times\mathrm{id}$ defines the free map
$\hat{\mathsf v}_h$ on the same domain,
with
$\mathsf v_h=\hat{\mathsf v}_h\circ\mathcal M^{t_0}$.
Completion and restriction have the same domain
by the explicit recursive formulas
\cite[eqs.\ (982)--(984)]{YMM1}: completion retains
the free coordinates and fills each tied bond
with its prescribed average.

The coordinate factor of a step carries
$\hat{\mathfrak w}_{h|_{t-1}}$ to
$\hat{\mathfrak w}_{h|_t}$ on
$\mathcal V_{t_0}^\chi\cap
\operatorname{dom}\hat\xi_{h|_{t-1}}$.
Indeed lift $W$ by the construction above,
apply the coordinate factor identity on
the bare lattice, and cancel the positive
factor $\mathfrak w_{h_0}(U)$ in (*).
The partial fermion kernel has Berezin
integral one over the next-level generators;
stored generators occur in no later kernel.
Consequently induction over the steps,
using these coordinate maps and weight
factors, identifies the Berezin integral
of the restarted term with
$(\hat{\mathsf v}_h)_*
(\hat{\mathfrak w}_h\hat F_0^\chi\,dW)$.

This pushforward loses no mass.
If $W\in\mathcal V_{t_0}^\chi$ and
$\hat{\mathfrak w}_h(W)\ne0$, choose the
positive-weight bare lift $U$ above.
Then (*) gives $\mathfrak w_h(U)\ne0$.
The support of a history weight is in
the domain of its free coordinates, as proved in
\cite[Prop.\ 53.14 and the setting of Prop.\ 66.2]{YMM1};
thus $U\in\operatorname{dom}\mathsf v_h$
and $W\in\operatorname{dom}\hat{\mathsf v}_h$.
The original measure is carried by this set.
Its total mass is therefore $\mathsf m(h)$.
Nonnegativity follows from \cref{C-425-4};
the norm bound follows from
$|\operatorname{Ber}F|\le\|F\|_{h_F}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Summation above the starting level]\label{C-425-6}
Let $\varsigma\ge0$ be bounded, Borel,
gauge invariant, and zero off
$\mathcal V_{t_0}^\chi$.
For $h'\in\mathcal H_{k'}^{(t_0)}$
and $t_0\le k'\le k\le K$,
\[
 \sum_{\substack{h\in\mathcal H_k^{(t_0)}\\h|_{k'}=h'}}
                      \mathsf m_\varsigma(h)
           =\mathsf m_\varsigma(h').
\]
In particular
\[
 \begin{split}
 \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_K^{(t_0)}}\mathsf m_\varsigma(h)
       &=\int_{\mathcal Y}\varsigma\,dW,\\
 \sum_{\substack{h\in\mathcal H_K^{(t_0)}\\
                         h|_{t_1}=h_\emptyset^{(t_1)}}}
                      \mathsf m_\varsigma(h)
       &=\int_{\mathcal Y}\hat{\mathsf k}\varsigma\,dW.
 \end{split}
\]
For these histories,
$h|_{t_1}\ne h_\emptyset^{(t_1)}$
if and only if $Z_{t_1}(h)\ne\varnothing$.
The bare weight factorization (*) in the
proof of \cref{C-425-7} holds for every
$U$ and every history above $t_0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
It suffices to prove the one-step identity.
Let $t_0<q\le K$ and
$h'\in\mathcal H_{q-1}^{(t_0)}$.
All its extensions remain above $t_0$.
For a plaquette outcome $\mathsf p$, put
$P''=P''_q(\mathsf p)$ and
$\mathsf N=B(P'')\setminus P''$.
The partition of the other outcomes gives
\[
 \sum_{\mathsf o:\,\mathsf p(\mathsf o)=\mathsf p}
          \hat{\mathfrak w}_{(h',\mathsf o)}(W)
 =
 \hat{\mathfrak w}_{h'}(W)
 \mathbf1_q^{\rm P}(\mathsf p)(W_q)
                   \mathfrak G_{q-1}(W_{q-1};P'').
\]
Lift $v\in G^{\mathsf N}$ constantly on
level-$(q-1)$ blocks to level $t_0$.
The substitution preserves $W_q$, the
earlier tests and gauge factors, the
plaquette test, $\varsigma$, and Haar measure.
Its average replaces the last factor by
$\mathbf1_{\{W_{q-1}\in\mathcal D(P'')\}}$.
Hence the sum of the masses for this
plaquette outcome is
\[
 \int\hat{\mathfrak w}_{h'}\,
       \mathbf1_q^{\rm P}(\mathsf p)\,
       \mathbf1_{\{W_{q-1}\in\mathcal D(P'')\}}
                                      \varsigma\,dW .
\]

The domain indicator is one on the support
of $\hat{\mathfrak w}_{h'}\varsigma$.
Here is the domain check.
The smallness condition on the frames gives
$\varepsilon(\mathsf t_{q-1})
\le\varepsilon(\gamma^{-2})\le\varepsilon_\flat$.
The contour-domain implication at $q\ge3$
says that the plaquette test of the preceding
outcome implies the present domain condition;
see \cite[\S44.2, proof of eq.\ (651)]{YMM1}.
The proof places each double block in the preceding
passed region, uses its curvature bound
\cite[eq.\ (650)]{YMM1}, and applies the
small-curvature contour estimate
\cite[Lem.\ 4.4]{YMM1}.
It is an implication for bare fields.
For a point in the support under consideration,
$W\in\mathcal V_{t_0}^\chi$; lift it to
$U$ as in \cref{C-425-7}.
If $q\ge t_0+2$, the preceding outcome
indicator is a factor of
$\hat{\mathfrak w}_{h'}(W)$, so its
plaquette test is one.
If $q=t_0+1$, the preceding history is
$h_\emptyset^{(t_0)}$; its plaquette test
is exactly $\chi_{t_0}(T_\ell)(W)=1$,
since its input region and outcome are
empty and its test cubes cover the torus.
In both cases $q-1\ge2$, so that plaquette
test reads only $\mathcal M^{q-1}U=W_{q-1}$.
The contour-domain implication therefore
gives $W_{q-1}\in\mathcal D(P'')$.
Discarding this now redundant indicator and
summing the plaquette tests gives
$\sum_{\mathsf o}\mathsf m_\varsigma(h',\mathsf o)
=\mathsf m_\varsigma(h')$.

Iteration proves the first display.
At $k'=t_0$ its weight is one; at $k'=t_1$
the empty history has weight $\hat{\mathsf k}$.
Finally a history at $t_1$ has full
small-field region if and only if it is
the empty history.  Its regions are
unchanged by restriction from level $K$,
which proves the assertion about $Z_{t_1}$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Descent of the background regularity}

\begin{lemma}[The starting test on the support of the weight]\label{C-425-8}
If $\mathsf k(W)>0$, the background over $W_j$
exists for $t_0\le j\le t_1$.
On its minimal orbit define
\[
 r_j=\frac{\mathsf m_j(U)}{\varepsilon(\mathsf t_j)},
 \qquad
 \mathsf m_j(U)=L^{2j}\max_p|\partial U(p)-1|.
\]
The numerator is constant on the orbit.
Then
\[
 r_j<
 2B_3L^{-3(t_1-j)/2}
       +\frac{C_HA_1}{(1-L^{-3/2})A_0}.
\]
If $s-u\ge n_0$, $W$ passes the density test
at $t_0$.  Consequently, everywhere on
$\mathcal Y$,
\[
 \mathsf k\chi_{t_0}(T_\ell)=\mathsf k,\qquad
                   \mathsf k\hat F_z=\mathsf k\hat F_z^\chi.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
At the top, $W_{t_1}\in\mathsf{In}_{t_1}$,
so $\varpi(W_{t_1})<2\varepsilon(\mathsf t_{t_1})$.
The background estimate
\cite[Prop.\ 52.3]{YMM1} gives $r_{t_1}<2B_3$.
At a lower level, the weight imposes the
field cut for $W_{j+1}$ and
$\chi_j^{\rm sf}(W_j)=1$, with
$\mathcal M(W_j)=W_{j+1}$.
The inverse chart \cite[Prop.\ 52.2]{YMM1} gives
$W_j=V_{W_{j+1}}(B)$ for
$B\in\mathsf{Rg}_{\mathsf t_j}$.
The estimate in the proof of
\cite[Lem.\ 113.10]{YMM1} is
\[
 \mathsf m_j(U)\le
 L^{-2}\mathsf m_{j+1}(U'')
                         +C_H\delta(\mathsf t_j).
\]
Its hypotheses hold because the next field
is in the cut and
$\mathsf t_j\ge L^u\gamma^{-2}\ge\Theta_\star$;
the same chart result puts $W_j$ in its cut.
Use
$\delta(\mathsf t_j)=(A_1/A_0)\varepsilon(\mathsf t_j)$
and
$L^{-2}\varepsilon(\mathsf t_{j+1})
\le L^{-3/2}\varepsilon(\mathsf t_j)$
to obtain
\[
 r_j\le L^{-3/2}r_{j+1}+C_HA_1/A_0.
\]
Its fixed point is
$C_HA_1/((1-L^{-3/2})A_0)$.
Iteration gives the stated bound.

If $t_1-t_0=s-u\ge n_0$, then
$r_{t_0}<1/(2B_3)$ by the definition of
$\sigma_D,n_0$.
Thus
$W\in\mathcal C_{t_0}^\flat
(\varepsilon(\mathsf t_{t_0})/(2B_3))$.
This implies the density test in the
calibration frame.  To check the parameters
of that implication, the radius is in
$(0,1]$. The history ceilings
\(\varepsilon_\gamma\le
\min\{\bar\varepsilon/2,\varepsilon_\flat\}\),
verified in \cite[proof of Lem. 82.5]{YMM1},
and \(B_3\ge1\) give
\[
 \varepsilon(\mathsf t_{t_0})\le\varepsilon_\gamma
       \le B_3\min\{\bar\varepsilon,2c_2^{\rm SO}\},
       \qquad c_2^{\rm SO}=\varepsilon_\flat .
\]
The one-lattice background setting includes
the admitted-constants condition required
by the density-test implication, with its
two specified auxiliary constants
$a_{\mathfrak h},\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}$.
Here is the implication explicitly. The global
background has scaled curvature less than
$\varepsilon(\mathsf t_{t_0})/(2B_3)$.
Curvature averaging gives
$\varpi(W)<\varepsilon(\mathsf t_{t_0})/B_3$.
For every density cube, apply the local background
bound \cite[Prop.\ 44.2]{YMM1} at this radius.
Its defining curvature is strictly less than
$\varepsilon(\mathsf t_{t_0})L^{-2t_0}$, so its
density test equals one. Taking their product
gives $\chi_{t_0}(T_\ell)(W)=1$.
The pointwise identities follow on the
support of $\mathsf k$ and are trivial
elsewhere.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Removing the top test]\label{C-425-9}
Assume (k0), $L^u\gamma^{-2}\ge\Theta_\star$,
$u\ge u_*$ and $s\ge s_F$.
Then
\[
 \begin{split}
 0\le\int_{\mathcal Y}
         |\mathsf k-\hat{\mathsf k}|\hat F_0^\chi\,dW
 &\le e^{-\theta_{\rm dis}A_0^2\mathsf y_{[u]}}
                          \mathsf M_{g,\ell}\hat T(0)\\
 &\le R^F\hat T(0).
 \end{split}
\]
Moreover
$0\le T^{\rm sf}(0)-\hat T(0)
=\int|\mathsf k-\hat{\mathsf k}|\hat F_0\,dW$.
If $s-u\ge n_0$, in particular if
$K^{\rm A}\ge K_{\rm tt}(n)$, then
\[
 \begin{split}
 T^{\rm sf}(z)&=\int_{\mathcal Y}\mathsf k\hat F_z^\chi\,dW,\\
 \int_{\mathcal Y}
          |\mathsf k-\hat{\mathsf k}|\hat F_0\,dW
 &=\int_{\mathcal Y}
          |\mathsf k-\hat{\mathsf k}|\hat F_0^\chi\,dW
 \le R^F\hat T(0)\le\hat R^F\hat T(0).
 \end{split}
\]
The source assertion holds wherever
$T^{\rm sf}(z)$ is defined.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
By \cref{C-425-3,C-425-4},
$|\mathsf k-\hat{\mathsf k}|=\mathsf k-\hat{\mathsf k}$
and
$\hat T(0)=\int\hat{\mathsf k}\hat F_0^\chi\,dW$.
The gauge average \cref{C-425-5}, followed
by \cref{C-425-6,C-425-7}, gives
\[
 \begin{split}
 \int|\mathsf k-\hat{\mathsf k}|\hat F_0^\chi\,dW
 &\le\int\hat F_0^\chi\,dW-\hat T(0)\\
 &=\sum_{\substack{h\in\mathcal H_K^{(t_0)}\\
                              Z_{t_1}(h)\ne\varnothing}}
                                  \mathsf m(h)\\
 &\le\sum_{\substack{h\in\mathcal H_K^{(t_0)}\\
                              Z_{t_1}(h)\ne\varnothing}}
              \int\|\hat g_h\|_{h_F}\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}.
 \end{split}
\]
The discarded-history estimate and positive
total bound of \cref{C-418-24} bound this
last sum by
\[
 e^{-\theta_{\rm dis}p_0(g_{t_1})^2}
       e^{\hat E_K+(C+2)\ell^3}
 \le e^{-\theta_{\rm dis}A_0^2\mathsf y_{[u]}}
                       \mathsf M_{g,\ell}\hat T(0),
\]
where
$p_0(g_{t_1})^2=A_0^2(\log(L^u\mathsf b))^{2\mathfrak p_0}
=A_0^2\mathsf y_{[u]}$.
Since $\mathsf b\ge\gamma^{-2}$,
this is bounded by $R^F\hat T(0)$
with the stated definition of $R^F$.
The difference $T^{\rm sf}(0)-\hat T(0)$
is the integral of the difference of their
weights against $\hat F_0\ge0$.
When $s-u\ge n_0$, \cref{C-425-8} permits
replacement by $\hat F_z^\chi$ for
$\mathsf k$, and \cref{C-425-3} does so
for $\hat{\mathsf k}$.  This proves the
remaining assertions.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Choice of the descent floor.}
The constant $A_0$ is free upward after
$A_1$ in the choice of constants.
The numbers $L,B_3,C_H$ in (D) are already
fixed there: $B_3$ depends on $L$, and
$C_H=4C_{\rm db}\max\{2,K_{\rm B}^{\rm s}(\rho_{\rm s})\}$
is the constant fixed in \cite[\S113, after eq.\ (2131)]{YMM1}.
It depends on the earlier choices
$L,\mathfrak M,R_1$ through $\rho_{\rm s}$.
Thus (D) is a legitimate additional floor.
Indeed, $L\ge13$ gives $L^{-3/2}<1/2$,
so it holds for every $A_0\ge4B_3C_HA_1$.
Intersecting this ray with the finitely many
other floors at $A_0$ leaves an unbounded
ray, and the subsequent choices retain their
admissible order.
This argument uses the actual constant in
the descent estimate; it does not identify
it with a supply-table constant having the
same name.
The quantities $\sigma_D,n_0$ are chosen
after $A_0$, and $K_{\rm tt}(n)$ after
the fixed constants and $n$.
No earlier constant reads these quantities.

Under (k0)--(k2) and
$K^{\rm A}\ge K_{\rm tt}(n)$, all hypotheses
above hold by (k1).  The last display of
\cref{C-425-9} is therefore the top-test
input \cref{C-418-14}, for either lattice.

\section{Histories with prescribed earlier terms}\label{sec:qcdm2-free-histories}

A restart retains functions of earlier block fields. We construct the history expansion with those functions prescribed, first at zero source and then with sources and an interpolation parameter. The coordinate integrals below give a common measure space for the comparison.

\subsection{Source induction with prescribed earlier activities}\label{C-422-1}

The cutoff comparison changes activities that were formed before its
base level. Those activities no longer need to be outputs of the same
flow. They do need the cancellation and locality properties used when
an old activity is read at a later scale. We first specify these
properties, then prove that two weighted sums of their sizes suffice
for the source induction. The parameter disc shrinks at successive
steps to keep the additional mass field inside its coordinate domain.

\begin{definition}[Histories through the base]\label{C-422-2}
Fix an admitted positive-mass datum and $1\le t_1\le K$. The
constants satisfy the additional floor and ceiling in
\cref{C-422-16}. Write
\[
 \mathcal H_k[t_1]=\{h\in\mathcal H_k:h|_{t_1}=h_\emptyset\},
 \qquad t_1\le k\le K.
\]
For such histories, every region before the base is the whole torus,
every early pair is regular, and there is no earlier rim, edge term,
or boundary term. The layers $\mathcal L_n$ with $n<t_1$ are empty.
If $k>t_1$, the first layer is
$\mathcal L_{t_1}=T_\ell\setminus\Omega_{t_1+1}$; if $k=t_1$ it
is the whole torus. The history and the ordinary source chain agree
at every level through $t_1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Free families]\label{C-422-3}
A free family of level $j$ is an even local family
$\Delta=(\Delta(X))_{X\in\mathcal D_j}$ on the fixed pair domains,
with the following form. Its scalar part is pointed:
\[
 \Delta_0(X)=\sum_{z\in X\cap\mathbb T^{(j)}}\Delta_0(X;\cdot;z),
 \qquad
 r^0(\Delta)=\sup_{X,z}e^{(\kappa+1)d_j(X)}
                            \|\Delta_0(X;\cdot;z)\|_X.
\]
Each pointed member is a local term, holomorphic as a function of
the pair, strictly gauge invariant, and zero at the trivial pair.

The part with fermion generators is specified by data $(F,G,\nu)$.
Here $F,G$ are even families of degrees at least two with formal
background fields at levels at most $j$, satisfying the core
holomorphy and joint invariance hypotheses of
\cite[Lem.\ 7.9]{QCDM1}. They are invariant under
$\Psi\mapsto e^{i\alpha}\Psi$,
$\bar\Psi\mapsto e^{-i\alpha}\bar\Psi$; thus their quadratic
parts contain one barred and one unbarred field. The fields in $F$
are read at $m_0-a_K\widehat J$, and those in $G$ at zero source.
Use the pieces and paths of \cite[Prop.\ 10.1 and its proof]{QCDM1}
and set
\[
 a_{X,p}=\operatorname{ord}_0[k_{X,p}(F)]
                      -\operatorname{ord}_0[k_{X,p}(G)].
\]
These matrix moments act trivially on colour, by invariance under
constant colour rotations at the trivial configuration. Define
\begin{align*}
 P_{z;X,p}&=-\mathfrak s_j^{-1}L^{-j}
                  \mathsf S_1(a_{X,p}(z)1_z\psi^{\rm bg}),\\
 l_\square&=L^{-j}\nu\,
                       \mathsf S_1(1_\square\psi^{\rm bg})|_{\mathsf n=0},\\
 P_z^\nu&=L^{-j}\nu\,[\mathsf S_1(1_z\psi^{\rm bg})
                            -\mathsf S_1(1_z\psi^{\rm bg})|_{\mathsf n=0}],\\
 \Delta_{\ge2}(Z)&=F(Z)
       +\sum_{(X,p):Z_p=Z}\sum_zP_{z;X,p}
       +\mathbf1_{\{Z=\square\}}
                                (l_\square+\sum_{z\in\square}P_z^\nu).
\end{align*}
On a torus the piece sum uses only polymers of diameter less than
one quarter of the side, as in the cited extraction rule. The moments
for the omitted pieces are still defined and enter the cell estimates
below. File $F(Z)$ at its polymer's cell, $P_{z;X,p}$ and $P_z^\nu$
at the cell containing $z$, and $l_\square$ at its cube.

Finally, $G$ together with $l_\square$ must be the restriction, on
polymers that do not wrap around the torus, of a family $G^\infty$
on $\mathbb Z^3$. This family has the same holomorphy and symmetry
properties and is covariant, summand by summand, under $M\mathbb Z^3$
translations. With the same lifted paths and moved diagonal terms,
its cell sum vanishes as a matrix in every cell.

Define $r^\psi(\Delta)$ as the maximum of four quantities: the sum
of the norms of the displayed summands of $\Delta_{\ge2}$; the
corresponding sum for $G$ with $l_\square$; that for $G^\infty$;
and $c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2|\nu|$. All three family norms are the
weighted norms for formal backgrounds used in
\cite[\S7, in particular Lem.\ 7.9]{QCDM1}.
Holomorphic dependence on a source means holomorphic dependence of
these data, coefficient by coefficient. The construction is linear
in $(F,G,\nu)$; both sizes are subadditive and absolutely homogeneous.
\end{definition}

The ordinary activity at a source has precisely this form: take its
parts before extraction at the actual coordinates and at zero
coordinates for $F,G$, and its zero-source mass coefficient for
$\nu$. The zero-source cell sum vanishes after extraction.
Consequently differences of two such activities are free families
after their scalar values at the trivial pair have been subtracted.
Those values are added to the scalar normalization.

\begin{definition}[Perturbation at the base]\label{C-422-4}
Let $S$ be an open source set. For $1\le i\le p$ prescribe a
Lipschitz gauge weight $w_i^\Delta$, a colour-scalar matrix field
$\sigma_i^\Delta(s)$, free families $\Delta_i^{(j)}(s)$ for
$j\le t_1$, and a number $e_i^\Delta(s)$. The last three data are
holomorphic in $s\in S$. Write $|\lambda|=\max_i|\lambda^i|$,
$\mathrm P(R)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb C^p:|\lambda|<R\}$, and
\[
 \Delta_i=a_K^{-1}A(w_i^\Delta,\mathsf U)
       -L^{-t_1}\mathsf S_1(\sigma_i^\Delta\psi^{\rm bg})
       +\sum_{j\le t_1}\sum_X\Delta_i^{(j)}(X)+e_i^\Delta.
\]
The fields and formal backgrounds in this formula are read in the
coordinates of the empty history at level $t_1$. Multiply its
ordinary sourced density by $e^{\lambda\cdot\Delta}$ and call
the resulting measure $\rho_{s,\lambda}$. Its gauge weight,
early activities, mass field, and scalar normalization are
\begin{align*}
 w_\lambda&=w+\lambda\cdot w^\Delta,
                   &s_\lambda&=(w_\lambda,J),\\
 E^{(j)}(s,\lambda)&=E^{(j)}(s)+\lambda\cdot\Delta^{(j)}(s),
                   &&j\le t_1,\\
 \sigma_{t_1}(s,\lambda)&=\sigma_{t_1}(s)
                                      +\lambda\cdot\sigma^\Delta(s),\\
 E_{t_1}(s,\lambda)&=E_{t_1}(s)+\lambda\cdot e^\Delta(s).
\end{align*}
The fermion tower retains the fine mass matrix $m_0-a_K\widehat J$.

Put
\[
 r_j^\psi=\sum_i r^\psi(\Delta_i^{(j)}),\quad
 r_j^0=\sum_i r^0(\Delta_i^{(j)}),\quad
 \|\sigma^\Delta\|=\sum_i\sup_x\|\sigma_i^\Delta(x)\|,
 \quad \|w^\Delta\|_\sharp=\sum_i\|w_i^\Delta\|_\sharp.
\]
For $k\ge t_1$ define
\[
 \Sigma_k^\psi=\sum_{j\le t_1}\omega_{k+1-j}r_j^\psi,
 \qquad \omega_l=C_\omega L^{l/4},\qquad
 \Sigma_k^0=\sum_{j\le t_1}L^{-(k-j)}r_j^0.
\]
At radius $R$ we require
\begin{equation}\label{eq:free-family-lags}
 \begin{aligned}
 R\Sigma_k^\psi&\le c_\psi^\Delta\phi_{k-1}
                          &&(t_1\le k\le K),&
 R\Sigma_{t_1}^0&\le c_0^\Delta,\\
 \|w\|_\sharp+R\|w^\Delta\|_\sharp&\le2\varrho,
 &&& R\|\sigma^\Delta\|&\le\tfrac12B_\sigma\phi_{t_1}.
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The constants $c_\psi^\Delta,c_0^\Delta$ are given in
\cref{C-422-16}. Set
\[
 Q_\sigma=2\sqrt L+\tfrac14,\qquad
 R_k=RQ_\sigma^{-(k-t_1)}.
\]
The weight condition ensures $s_\lambda\in\mathcal P$ for
$s\in\mathcal P$ and $\lambda\in\mathrm P(R)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Room in the ordinary source estimates]\label{C-422-5}
At the fixed pair radius $\alpha_0$, the ordinary activities,
their pointed terms, and their zero-source reference families obey
\[
 \epsilon_j^{{\rm s},\psi}\le(2C_w^{\rm s}-C_w)\phi_{j-1}.
\]
The ordinary source chain obeys
\[
 \|\sigma_k(s)\|\le
 (2B_0+C_{\rm var}+4C_{\rm tor}C_{\mathcal L})\phi_k
                  \le\tfrac12(B_\sigma-C_{\rm var})\phi_k.
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The closing estimate in \cite[Prop.\ 10.1, proof]{QCDM1} is
\[
 C_w^\psi\phi_k
 +8\theta_E^{\rm s}(1+c_{\rm cs})C_w^{\rm s}C_{\rm pc}S_{1/4}\phi_k
 +4\sqrt L C_{\rm pc}S_{1/4}\theta_E^{\rm s}c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2
                              (\bar B_M+2B_\sigma)\phi_k.
\]
By the definition of $C_w^{\rm s}$ the first and third terms
sum to at most $(C_w^{\rm s}-C_w)\phi_k$. The middle term is at
most $C_w^{\rm s}\phi_k$ by
$4\theta_E^{\rm s}C_{\rm pc}S_{1/4}(1+c_{\rm cs})\le1/2$.
This includes the reference and the pointed terms; at the first
step the old-activity sums are empty.

For the chain apply \cite[Lem.\ 10.4]{QCDM1}. On $\mathcal P$,
$\|w\|_\infty<2\varrho$ and the local source variation satisfies
$\Xi_k<1/(20M)+1/2<1$. The claimed bound follows from
$|\sigma_k^c(c)|\le B_0\phi_k|c|/\varrho$ and
$B_\sigma\ge4B_0+3C_{\rm var}+8C_{\rm tor}C_{\mathcal L}$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The constants and the count over scales}\label{C-422-16}

We record the constants before applying the history induction.
The additional restriction on the regular sum is a lower bound on
two majorant constants, chosen before the later small-coupling
ceilings. It does not impose a condition depending on the cutoff.

First put
\[
 c_{\rm cs}^\Delta=
       \frac{2C_{\rm hl}M^3C_{\rm bg}^{\rm w}}{Lc_{\mathsf S}\omega_1},
 \qquad
 c_\psi^\Delta=C_w\omega_1
                  \frac{c_{\rm cs}}{c_{\rm cs}+c_{\rm cs}^\Delta},
\]
and
\[
 c_0^\Delta=\min\left\{
 \frac5{12}K_M^\bullet c_{\rm cl},
 \frac{\alpha_0C_w^{\rm s}}
      {16\sqrt2K_M^\bullet K_\Lambda^{\rm s}\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}A_1},
 (\sqrt2-1)E_0^{\rm s},M^{-3}\mathsf B\right\}.
\]
The first two choices preserve the scalar room in
\cref{C-422-8}; the other two will bound the regular scalar sum
and its frame. Define also
\[
 c_\lambda=\min\left\{\tfrac18,c_0^\Delta/E_0^{\rm s},
                         c_\psi^\Delta/(2\sqrt L C_w^{\rm s})\right\}.
\]

The units used below are the quadratic kernels with their diagonal
moments removed, the moved diagonal pieces at their new cells, and
the mass forms in \cref{C-422-3}. Their terms without a difference
belong to the cell sum and are counted separately.
Set $\alpha=3/4$, $c_T=64L^2$, $C_t=9$, and
\begin{align*}
 N_{\rm d}&=2(C(\alpha)+c_T\epsilon_*),\\
 N_{\rm u}&=32C_tMA_\kappa N_{\rm d}
       [(2A_\kappa C_H)^2+\nu C_H^2(2C_{\rm pw}+C_{(N)})],\\
 c_l^{\rm u}&=
 \begin{cases}
 N_{\rm u}L^{9/2}L^{l/4},&l>n_{\rm lag},\\
 N_{\rm u}L^{3l},&0\le l\le n_{\rm lag}.
 \end{cases}
\end{align*}
All constants on the right are the local background, piece, and
path constants in \cite[Lem.\ 7.9 and Prop.\ 10.1]{QCDM1}.
They are fixed before $h_F$. In particular $N_{\rm u}\ge1$.

For a family of size $\varepsilon_{\rm f}$ having the format in
\cref{C-422-3}, its units, apart from their cell sums, contribute
at most $c_{n-j}^{\rm u}\varepsilon_{\rm f}$ to a level-$n$ cube.
For $n-j>n_{\rm lag}$ this statement counts the pieces contained
in $\Omega_{n-1}$; the other pieces have an exponential polymer
tail and will enter the summable kernels below. For
$n-j\le n_{\rm lag}$ it counts the whole units. These statements
also hold along a history: at short lags the needed size is the
sum of the norms of the kernels and forms actually retained by
its regular pointers.

To prove these assertions, fix a level-$j$ cell $c$ with center
$z_c$. At the trivial configuration write each localized leg as
\[
 \Upsilon_\omega(x)\Phi(z_c)+\varrho_\omega(x),\qquad
 \varrho_\omega(x)=\sum_yH_\omega(1)(x,y)
                              [\Phi^{\mathsf u}(y)-\Phi(z_c)].
\]
The term with no $\varrho$ is precisely its cell moment.
The remaining three terms of a quadratic form are bounded by
four times a whole leg times a leg with a difference: the second
difference in the product of two differences costs at most two
whole legs.

Put $l=n-j>n_{\rm lag}$. A whole leg within a piece contained
in $\Omega_{n-1}$ has relative size at most
$2C_Hq_{\rm sup}^{|\omega|}L^{1-l}$.
Transport the difference to $z_c$ along the piece's path. A
neighboring difference of level $j$ is bounded by
\[
 A_\kappa N_{\rm d}L^{2(1+\alpha)}L^{-(1+\alpha)l}.
\]
Indeed the background H\"older estimate contributes
$2A_\kappa C(\alpha)(L^j/\mathsf s_k)^{1+\alpha}$, with
$\mathsf s_k\ge L^{n-2}$ on $\Omega_{n-1}$.
Replacing straight transport by the block field contributes
$2c_T\epsilon_*L^{-2(n-1-j)}$ times a leg of size $L^{1-l}$.
Since $L^{3-3l}\le L^{2(1+\alpha)}L^{-(1+\alpha)l}$, both
contributions have the displayed bound.

If $D'_p=M(1+d_j(X))+9M_w\sum_i(|\omega_i|+1)$ is the
piece diameter, its path length satisfies
\[
 1+C_tD'_p\le8C_tM e^{\kappa d_j(X)}e^{|\omega_1|+|\omega_2|}.
\]
Here $M\ge3M_w$, $1+d\le e^{\kappa d}$, and
$1+|\omega|\le e^{|\omega|}$. The polymer norm pays the first
exponential, and the two localized walk sums pay the others with
$A_\kappa$ each. The ordinary kernel pieces and forms in the cell
therefore contribute at most
\[
 32C_tMA_\kappa N_{\rm d}(2A_\kappa C_H)^2
          L^{1-l}L^{2(1+\alpha)}L^{-(1+\alpha)l}\varepsilon_{\rm f}.
\]
A moved piece has norm at most
$\nu\|a_{X,p}(y)\|C_H^2h_F^2$.
There are two assignments to count: its negative copy in its old
unit and its positive copy at the cell of $y$.
The polymerwise piece bound pays the path length for the first;
the first weighted piece estimate pays the second, whose path
lies within its cell. Each contributes
$C_{\rm pw}h_F^{-2}\varepsilon_{\rm f}$ before the leg factors.
The same difference calculation thus supplies
$\nu C_H^2\,2C_{\rm pw}$ in place of $(2A_\kappa C_H)^2$.
The additional $\nu C_H^2C_{(N)}$ in $N_{\rm u}$ also covers
the alternative count by the old-activity moment bound.

There are $L^{3l}$ cells in the level-$n$ cube. The resulting
scale factor is exactly
\[
 L^{3l}L^{1-l}L^{2(1+\alpha)}L^{-(1+\alpha)l}
                       =L^{9/2}L^{l/4}.
\]
This proves the long-lag count. At short lags no differences are
formed. Each leg has relative size at most one. The kernels and
forms cost $\varepsilon_{\rm f}$ per cell, and the two copies
of moved pieces cost at most
$2\nu C_H^2C_{\rm pw}\varepsilon_{\rm f}$.
Multiplication by $L^{3l}$ proves the short-lag count.

For histories with a rim at level $j$, a piece contained in
$\Omega_{n-1}$ at a long lag lies in $\Lambda_j^{\sim-1}$:
the separation is at least $7ML^{n-1}$ and $n_{\rm lag}\ge1$.
All its pointers and paths therefore agree with the unrestricted
reading; the same cancellation applies. At short lags the retained
kernels and forms have the pointed size bound of the activity.
The retained moved pieces are subsets of the same nonnegative
absolute sums. This proves the asserted count along histories.

For the other contributions define $K_{\rm fin}=\sum_{l\ge0}\mathsf k_l$,
where
\begin{align*}
 \mathsf k_l={}&N_{\rm rd}L^{-l}
   +2C_\omega C_{\rm wr}L^le^{-\kappa(L^{l+1}-2)}\\
 &+\mathbf1_{\{l>n_{\rm lag}\}}
                     N_{\rm wh}L^{3l+2}e^{-\kappa(8L^l-2)}
   +r_l,\\
 r_l={}&
 \begin{cases}
 [C_\omega((1+L^2)C_\omega+2C_{\rm pw})L^l
                  +N_{\rm wh}L^{3l+2}]e^{-\kappa(7L^l-2)},&l>0,\\
 C_\omega((1+L^2)C_\omega+2C_{\rm pw})+N_{\rm wh}L^2,&l=0.
 \end{cases}
\end{align*}
Here $N_{\rm rd}$ is the constant for the higher-degree and
field-dependent quadratic terms in the proof of
\cite[Lem.\ 10.8]{QCDM1}; $N_{\rm wh}$ is the larger constant
for whole pieces outside $\Omega_{n-1}$ and whole rim terms in
that proof. They depend only on the already fixed local geometry,
background and piece constants, and are chosen before the size
of the regular sum. The four kernels have finite sums.
The only terms involving a moved coefficient in $N_{\rm wh}$
have size $\nu\|a_{X,p}(y)\|C_H^2h_F^2L^2$; the weighted
piece bound cancels $h_F^2$, so there is no dependence on a later
choice of $h_F$ in these constants.

Set
\begin{align*}
 S_{\rm lag}&=\frac{L^{3(n_{\rm lag}+1)}-1}{L^3-1},\\
 c_{\rm u}^{\rm leg}&=2C_w^{\rm s}
   \left[\frac{L^{9/2}C_{\rm pc}S_{1/4}}{C_\omega L^{1/4}}
                                                   +S_{\rm lag}\right],\\
 c_{\rm o}^{\rm leg}&=2C_w^{\rm s}K_{\rm fin}
        +C_0^{\rm cs}h_F^2+2c_{\rm cs}C_{\rm pc}S_{1/4}C_w^{\rm s}.
\end{align*}
Choose the two constants in the sourced regular-sum bound so that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:free-history-leg-floor}
 C_{\rm leg}^{\square,\rm s}\ge
                  c_{\rm o}^{\rm leg}+N_{\rm u}c_{\rm u}^{\rm leg},
 \qquad
 C_{\rm leg}^{\rm s}\ge
       \phi(\tfrac12e^{18\mathfrak p_0})C_{\rm leg}^{\square,\rm s}.
\end{equation}
The count just proved shows that these choices also satisfy the
ordinary regular-sum estimate. They are made after $C_w^{\rm s}$
and before the stored-layer constants, majorants, and mass floor.
All constants depending on them are then fixed at these values.

For the additional tail estimate put
\[
 \theta_{\rm tl}=\tfrac14(c_\star-c_\Theta),\qquad
 c_{\rm tl}=\tfrac14(c_\star+3c_\Theta),\qquad
 \mathsf w_{\rm tl}=c_\Theta/c_{\rm tl},\qquad
 c''_{\rm tl}=(1-\eth)\theta_{\rm tl}.
\]
Choose $\gamma$ small enough that the history-summation threshold
of \cite[Prop.\ 67.6(f)]{YMM1} holds at rate $c_{\rm tl}$,
majorant $C$, vacuum-boundary constant $C_\flat^F+C'_{\mathfrak E}$,
and dials $(\mathsf w_{\rm tl},c_a,C_{\rm vol},c_{\rm tl})$.
Explicitly this is
$\log\gamma^{-2}\ge\mathsf Y_{\rm f1}$ if $c_a=0$ and
$\log\gamma^{-2}\ge\mathsf Y_{\rm f2}$ if $c_a>0$, with those
thresholds formed at the displayed arguments and the corresponding
admitted floor on $\mathfrak p_0$.
Both remaining rates, $\eth\theta_{\rm tl}$ and
$(1-\eth)\theta_{\rm tl}$, are positive. Thus the threshold is
finite and depends only on constants fixed before $\gamma$.
This is compatible with all the earlier ceilings, each of which
holds on an interval $(0,\gamma']$.

The constants $c_{\rm cs}^\Delta,c_\psi^\Delta,c_0^\Delta,
Q_\sigma,c_\lambda$ are read after this choice. They place
conditions on the perturbation through \eqref{eq:free-family-lags},
and do not enter the earlier choices. This verifies the order
of constants in \cref{C-422-2}.

\subsection{Perturbations on the base coordinates}

The estimates for prescribed activities must apply to measures,
including complex sources and complex interpolation parameters.
We first define these measures and prove the identities used in
the induction.  The quantitative restrictions on the interpolation
parameter enter only when we estimate their densities.

\begin{lemma}[Coordinates at the base]\label{C-424-17}
Let \(h_\emptyset=h_\emptyset^{(t_1)}\).  Its free coordinates
and its completed coordinates both identify with
\(\mathcal V_{t_1}\).  Their reference measure is Haar probability
measure, and their coordinate map on \(\mathcal V_0\) is
\(\xi=\mathcal M^{t_1}\).
For a gauge transformation \(u\) at level \(t_1\), write
\(\tilde u(x)=u(y)\) on each block \(B^{t_1}(y)\).
Then
\[
 \xi(U^v)=\xi(U)^{v|_{t_1}},\qquad
 \mathsf{Ev}_{h_\emptyset}(V^u)
 =\{\mathsf U^{\tilde u}:\mathsf U\in
                             \mathsf{Ev}_{h_\emptyset}(V)\}.
\]
Here \(\mathsf{Ev}_{h_\emptyset}(V)\) consists of the adapted
elements of the minimal orbit \(U_{t_1}(V)\), and is empty
when that orbit does not exist.  Haar measure on
\(\mathcal V_{t_1}\) is invariant under \(V\mapsto V^u\).

If \(v\) is a gauge transformation at a level \(n\ge t_1\),
its bare lift \(\tilde v\) is also the lift of
\(\tilde v|_{t_1}\).  The map \(U\mapsto U^{\tilde v}\)
preserves Haar measure, the weight \(\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset}\),
and the support of that weight.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Along \(h_\emptyset\), the regions through \(t_1\) are
\(\Omega_j=\Lambda_j=T_\ell\).  All proper bonds, lettered
datum bonds, and external bonds below \(t_1\) are therefore
absent.  At \(t_1\), the proper and lettered datum bonds are
all the bonds, and there are no tied bonds.  Thus restriction
and completion are identities; no fluctuation coordinate remains;
and both coordinate spaces and measures have the stated form.
Gauge covariance of \(\mathcal M\) proves the first identity.

The determining set of this constant sequence consists of all
bonds at level \(t_1\).  Its constraint is
\(\mathcal M^{t_1}U=V\), and its residual gauge group consists
of transformations equal to one at the level-\(t_1\) sites.
A gauge transformation with restriction \(u\) maps this
constraint to the constraint at \(V^u\).  It preserves the
action, constrained criticality, and regularity, and conjugates
the residual gauge group to itself.  It therefore maps the minimal
orbit at \(V\) onto that at \(V^u\), with existence on either
side equivalent to existence on the other.

For the lift \(\tilde u\), the adaptation conditions are also
preserved.  Indeed, the endpoints of each adaptation contour
\((y,a)\), \(a\in B(y)\), have the same value of
\(\tilde u\).  Its contour variable equals one before the
transformation if and only if it equals one after it.  Applying
this observation also to \(u^{-1}\) proves the identity for
\(\mathsf{Ev}\).

The lift from a level \(n\ge t_1\) is constant on every
\(B^{t_1}(y)\).  Each test through \(t_1\) is invariant
under this transformation, as is each gauge-fixing factor.
Their product is \(\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset}\).  Left and
right invariance of Haar measure proves the measure assertion;
invariance of the weight and invertibility of the transformation
prove the assertion about its support.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Holomorphic perturbations]\label{C-424-6}
Let \(\mathcal O\subset\mathbb C^{n_s}\) be open and
\[
 s(z)=s_0+\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}z_i s_i=(w,J)\in\mathcal P.
\]
For \(n_s\ge1\), require \(s(z)\in\mathcal P^\circ\).
For \(n_s=0\), allow any one source in \(\mathcal P\).
Fix \(r_\lambda>0\).  A perturbation consists of
\(w^\Delta(s)\), a complex Lipschitz function on \(T_\ell\);
a field \(\delta\sigma(s)\) in the colour-scalar matrix slot
\(\mathbb M\); a scalar \(\mathfrak n(s)\); and pointed
arrays \(\Delta^{(j)}(s)\), \(1\le j\le t_1\).
All these data are holomorphic in \(z\), pointwise for the
first two and coefficient by coefficient for the arrays.

Each array has the local domains and joint gauge invariance of
\cref{C-422-3}.  Its scalar part vanishes at the trivial pair,
and its part with generators is formed from data
\((F_j(s),G_j(s),\nu_j(s))\) by the extraction rule in that
definition, including its phase invariance, common paths,
infinite-lattice family with zero matrix cell sums, and rules
for assigning terms to cells.  The coefficients are Borel on
the fixed cores \(\mathcal U_j^\circ(X;\alpha_0,\alpha_1)\).
Write
\[
 \rho_j(s)=\|\Delta^{(j)}_0(s)\|_{j,\kappa+1},\qquad
 r_j^\psi(s)=r^\psi(\Delta^{(j)}(s)).
\]
For every \(z\in\mathcal O\) and \(|\lambda|<r_\lambda\),
require
\begin{equation}\label{eq:free-measure-lags}
 \begin{aligned}
 |\lambda|\sum_{j\le t_1}\omega_{k+1-j}r_j^\psi(s)
    &\le c_\psi^\Delta\phi_{k-1}&& (t_1\le k\le K),\\
 |\lambda|\sum_{j\le t_1}L^{-(t_1-j)}\rho_j(s)
    &\le c_0^\Delta,\\
 (w+\lambda w^\Delta(s),J)&\in\mathcal P,&
 |\lambda|\|\delta\sigma(s)\|&\le\tfrac12B_\sigma\phi_{t_1}.
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The constants are those of \cref{C-422-16}; in particular
\(c_0^\Delta\le M^{-3}\mathsf B\) and
\(c_0^\Delta\le(\sqrt2-1)E_0^{\rm s}\).
No geometrical constant denoted by \(c_0\) is being changed.

At an evaluation configuration of the base coordinates, set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:free-measure-exponent}
 \Delta(s)=a_K^{-1}A(w^\Delta(s),\mathsf U)
       -L^{-t_1}\mathsf S_1(\delta\sigma(s)\psi^{\rm bg})
       +\sum_{j\le t_1}\sum_X\sum_{z\in X^{(j)}}
                       \Delta^{(j)}(X;\mathsf U;z;s)
       +\mathfrak n(s).
\end{equation}
The formal backgrounds are evaluated at the fine mass matrix
\(m_0-a_K\widehat J\).  Adding \(\lambda\Delta(s)\) to
the ordinary exponent replaces its gauge weight by
\(\beta_{t_1}-a_K^{-1}(w+\lambda w^\Delta)\), its mass
coefficient by
\(L^{-t_1}(s_{t_1}+\sigma_{t_1}^{h_\emptyset}(s)
+\lambda\delta\sigma)\), and its earlier activities by
\(E^{(j)}(s)+\lambda\Delta^{(j)}(s)\).  It adds
\(\lambda\mathfrak n(s)\) to the scalar normalization.
\end{definition}

The conditions give bounds on each array, uniform on
\(\mathcal O\):
\[
 \rho_j(s)\le\frac{c_0^\Delta L^{t_1-j}}{r_\lambda},
 \qquad
 r_j^\psi(s)\le
 \frac{c_\psi^\Delta\phi_{t_1-1}}
      {r_\lambda\omega_{t_1+1-j}}.
\]
Indeed, let \(|\lambda|\uparrow r_\lambda\) in
\eqref{eq:free-measure-lags}.  Each coefficient is bounded by
its fibre norm times a constant depending only on its finite
Grassmann algebra.  These bounds permit integration in the
parameters on every compact subset of \(\mathcal O\times\mathbb C\).

\subsection{The perturbed measures}

Write
\[
 \mathsf S_\emptyset
 =\{V:\mathsf{Stay}_{h_\emptyset}\mathbf1^{\rm T}_{h_\emptyset}
                    \chi_{t_1}(T_\ell)(V)\ne0\}.
\]
The exponential representation at zero source permits a Borel
Haar-null set \(\mathsf N_0\) such that every point of
\(\mathsf S_\emptyset\setminus\mathsf N_0\) lies in
\(\xi(\{\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset}\ne0\})\), all its
evaluation configurations lie in the required domains, and
\(\Delta(s)\) takes one value there.  We justify these
assertions below.  Define
\[
 g_{s,\lambda}(V)=
 \begin{cases}
  e^{\lambda\Delta(s)(V)},&
           V\in\mathsf S_\emptyset\setminus\mathsf N_0,\\
  1,&\text{otherwise},
 \end{cases}
\]
and let \(G_{s,\lambda}=g_{s,\lambda}\circ\xi\) on the
support of \(\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset}\), with value one
elsewhere.

For \(h\in\mathcal H_k[t_1]\), let
\(T^{\rm F}_{h;(t_1,k]}[U]\) denote the composition of the
normalized fermion kernels and partial Berezin integrals after
level \(t_1\).  Thus
\(T_h^{\rm F}=T^{\rm F}_{h;(t_1,k]}\circ T_{h_\emptyset}^{\rm F}\).
Set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:free-measure-bare-density}
 \begin{split}
 F_s(U)&=T_{h_\emptyset}^{\rm F}[U]
     \bigl(e^{-A(\beta-a_K^{-1}w,U)-S_F(U)+\Phi(J)}\bigr),\\
 \varsigma_h^{s,\lambda}(U)
   &=T^{\rm F}_{h;(t_1,k]}[U]
                     \bigl(G_{s,\lambda}(U)F_s(U)\bigr).
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
