Define \(\check\tau_h^{\rm F}[s,\lambda]\) by pushing
\(\mathfrak w_h\varsigma_h^{s,\lambda}\,dU\) to the free
coordinates, coefficient by coefficient.  Its image on the
completed coordinates is \(\hat\tau_h^{\rm F}[s,\lambda]\).

\begin{lemma}\label{C-424-7}
For the data of \cref{C-424-6}, these definitions have the
following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item The exponent \(\Delta(s)\) is Borel on
\(\mathsf S_\emptyset\setminus\mathsf N_0\), coefficient
by coefficient, holomorphic in \(z\), and bounded there
uniformly for \(z\) in compact subsets of \(\mathcal O\).
The coefficients of \(\varsigma_h^{s,\lambda}\) are bounded
Borel functions of \(U\), holomorphic in \((z,\lambda)\),
and bounded uniformly in \(U\) on compact parameter sets.
Both measures are holomorphic in these parameters when evaluated
on a Borel set.  At \(\lambda=0\), they are the ordinary
sourced measures.
\item At the base,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:free-measure-base-density}
 \begin{split}
 \hat\tau_{h_\emptyset}^{\rm F}[s,\lambda]
 ={}&\mathsf{Stay}_{h_\emptyset}\mathbf1^{\rm T}_{h_\emptyset}
  \chi_{t_1}(T_\ell)e^{\boldsymbol\Phi^w_{h_\emptyset}}\\
 &\quad\cdot
  \exp\bigl[A^{\rm F}_{t_1,h_\emptyset}(s)+\lambda\Delta(s)\bigr]
                    \,\mathscr M_{h_\emptyset}.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
This equality holds coefficient by coefficient off one Borel
null set \(\mathsf N_s\cup\mathsf N_0\), and the exponent
takes one value at the evaluation configurations of every point
of \(\mathsf S_\emptyset\) outside that set.
\item Whenever a later term has an exponential representation
with one null set, the density, support, and admission conclusions
of \cite[Lem.\ 10.7]{QCDM1} apply to that representation.
\item Define the scalar function
\[
 \varsigma^{s,\lambda}(U)
       =\operatorname{Ber}\bigl(G_{s,\lambda}(U)F_s(U)\bigr).
\]
Then, for every \(h\in\mathcal H_k[t_1]\),
\[
 \operatorname{Ber}\check\tau_h^{\rm F}[s,\lambda]
        =\check\tau_h[\varsigma^{s,\lambda}],\qquad
 \operatorname{Ber}\check\tau_h^{\rm F}[s,\lambda]
                    (\mathsf X_h^{\rm fr})
        =\int\mathfrak w_h\varsigma^{s,\lambda}\,dU.
\]
The finite sum of these masses, denoted by \(Z_k(z,\lambda)\),
is holomorphic on \(\mathcal O\times\mathbb C\).  At zero
interpolation parameter,
\[
 \varsigma^{s,0}(U)
  =e^{-A(\beta-a_K^{-1}w,U)}
                         \det(D[U]+m_0-a_K\widehat J).
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
We first choose \(\mathsf N_0\).  The ordinary source
induction and its density lemma
\cite[Lem.\ 10.7 and Prop.\ 10.13]{QCDM1} give the base
density at zero source off one null set.  On
\(\mathsf S_\emptyset\) it has the form \(c e^G\), with
\(c\ne0\), so its scalar coefficient \(c e^{G_0}\) is
nonzero.  The same lemma gives a Borel set
\(S'\subset\xi(\{\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset}\ne0\})\)
outside which the density has integral norm zero.  The two
coordinate measures agree by \cref{C-424-17}.  Hence
\(\mathsf S_\emptyset\setminus S'\) is Haar-null.
Adjoin this set and a Borel null set containing the exceptional
set for the zero-source evaluation domains.  The resulting
\(\mathsf N_0\) has all the required support properties.

At a remaining point, all earlier pairs are regular, since
\(\Lambda_j=T_\ell\) for \(j\le t_1\).  The arrays are
therefore evaluated on their fixed cores.  The sourced fermion
tower also exists, since
\[
 L^{t_1}\|a_KJ\|_\infty
       \le2\varrho_J\le r_J/2\le r_M.
\]
Two evaluation configurations differ by a gauge transformation
equal to one at the retained places.  The action is gauge
invariant plaquette by plaquette.  The matrix
\(\delta\sigma\) commutes with colour, so its mass term
is jointly gauge invariant; the arrays have the same property.
Thus \(\Delta(s)\) is independent of the evaluation
configuration.

The Borel evaluation construction in the ordinary density
induction applies to these terms: the action is continuous in
the configuration, the mass coefficients are fixed functions of
the sites, and the array coefficients are Borel on the same
cores.  At a fixed coordinate point, the background maps are
holomorphic in \(-a_KJ\); every coefficient of the exponent
is a finite sum of products of holomorphic functions of \(z\).
The individual array bounds following \cref{C-424-6}, the
uniform background bounds, and finiteness of the lattice give
uniform coefficient bounds on compact parameter sets.  The
plaquette terms are bounded on the compact configuration space,
and only finitely many values of \(w^\Delta\),
\(\delta\sigma\), and \(\mathfrak n\) occur.

For an even Grassmann element \(H\),
\(e^H=e^{H_0}\sum_{j\ge0}(H-H_0)^j/j!\), with a finite
sum.  This proves the asserted properties of \(g\) and \(G\).
The partial kernels have bounded Borel coefficients, and the
bare sourced density has continuous coefficients on the compact
configuration space.  Products and Berezin integration are
finite operations on coefficients, which proves the bounds for
\(\varsigma_h^{s,\lambda}\).  Integrating over the preimage
of a Borel set preserves holomorphy by these compact-parameter
bounds, Fubini, and Morera's theorem.  At \(\lambda=0\),
\(G=1\), giving the ordinary sourced term.

At the base the partial map in
\eqref{eq:free-measure-bare-density} is the identity.  For
bounded Borel \(g\), pushforward commutes with multiplication
by \(g\circ\xi\), coefficient by coefficient.  Consequently
\(\hat\tau_{h_\emptyset}^{\rm F}[s,\lambda]
=g_{s,\lambda}\hat\tau_{h_\emptyset}^{\rm F}[s]\).
Insert the ordinary exponential representation.  Its density
vanishes off \(\mathsf S_\emptyset\), and the even Grassmann
algebra is commutative.  This gives
\eqref{eq:free-measure-base-density}, after enlarging
\(\mathsf N_s\) by a Borel null set for the ordinary
one-value assertion.  Multiplication by bounded \(g\)
preserves integrability.

For (iii), the proof of the cited density lemma uses of a
coefficient density \(f\) only its boundedness.  Indeed, if
\(\rho'\) is the strictly positive zero-source bare density,
then on a null set \(E\) for its positive history measure,
\[
 |\check\tau_h[f]|(E)
   \le\frac{\sup|f|}{\min\rho'}\check\tau_h[\rho'](E)=0.
\]
The coordinate and history hypotheses are unchanged.  This
proves the same support and admission conclusions for each
bounded coefficient of the perturbed term.

Finally integrate the generators of the highest level first.
Each normalized partial kernel integrates to one; its shifted
generators do not change that integral.  Iterating through the
later levels gives
\(\operatorname{Ber}\varsigma_h^{s,\lambda}
=\varsigma^{s,\lambda}\), independently of \(h\).
Berezin integration commutes with the coefficientwise
pushforward.  This proves (iv), including holomorphy of the
finite sum.  At \(\lambda=0\), the same normalization
reduces the full Berezin integral to the stated determinant.
\end{proof}

The equality \(Z_k=Z_{t_1}\) for every complex
\(\lambda\) requires an additional point: the exceptional
set used to define \(g\) need not itself be gauge invariant.
We prove the required almost-everywhere invariance next.

\subsection{Gauge invariance and the sum over histories}

\begin{lemma}\label{C-424-18}
Use the notation of \cref{C-424-7}.  For a bare gauge
transformation \(v\), let \(\alpha_v\) denote its action
on the Grassmann algebra.  Then
\(F_s(U^v)=\alpha_vF_s(U)\) at every configuration.
If \(V,V^u\in\mathsf S_\emptyset\setminus\mathsf N_0\),
then
\[
 \Delta(s)(V^u)=\alpha_u\Delta(s)(V),\qquad
 g_{s,\lambda}(V^u)=\alpha_u g_{s,\lambda}(V).
\]
The set
\[
 \{U:\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset}(U)\ne0,
                 \ \xi(U)\notin\mathsf S_\emptyset\setminus\mathsf N_0\}
\]
is Haar-null.  Consequently, for every gauge transformation
\(v\) at a level \(n\ge t_1\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:free-measure-ae-invariance}
 \mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset}(U)
 \bigl[\varsigma^{s,\lambda}(U^{\tilde v})
                         -\varsigma^{s,\lambda}(U)\bigr]=0
 \quad\text{for almost every }U.
\end{equation}
This assertion holds for every \((z,\lambda)\in
\mathcal O\times\mathbb C\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The bare Dirac operator transforms by conjugation, and
\(\widehat J\) commutes with colour.  The gauge action is
invariant.  Each partial fermion kernel is jointly gauge
invariant, block by block, because the block average is
covariant.  Berezin integration commutes with the gauge
action: its barred and unbarred changes of variables are
contragredient.  Applying these facts through the base
proves the assertion for \(F_s\).

By \cref{C-424-17}, an evaluation configuration
\(\mathsf U\) at \(V\) gives \(\mathsf U^{\tilde u}\)
at \(V^u\).  The background maps satisfy
\[
 \mathsf H_{i,t_1}[U^v]
      =v|_i\,\mathsf H_{i,t_1}[U](v|_{t_1})^{-1},\qquad
 \bar{\mathsf H}_{t_1,i}[U^v]
      =v|_{t_1}\,\bar{\mathsf H}_{t_1,i}[U](v|_i)^{-1}.
\]
These identities follow along the tower from covariance
of the Dirac operator and the block averages, with the
same fine mass matrix.  If \(\mathsf{sb}_{\mathsf U}\)
substitutes the backgrounds at \(\mathsf U\), they imply
\[
 \mathsf{sb}_{\mathsf U^{\tilde u}}\circ\alpha_{\tilde u}
              =\alpha_u\circ\mathsf{sb}_{\mathsf U}.
\]
Apply this identity to the jointly invariant arrays and
to the mass term, whose matrix commutes with colour.
The action and scalar normalization are invariant separately.
This proves the assertion for \(\Delta\), and hence for
its exponential.

Let \(E=\mathcal V_{t_1}\setminus
(\mathsf S_\emptyset\setminus\mathsf N_0)\).
The base density at zero source vanishes off
\(\mathsf S_\emptyset\), and \(E\cap\mathsf S_\emptyset\)
is Haar-null.  Every coefficient of its measure therefore
vanishes on \(E\).  Taking the full Berezin integral gives
\[
 \int_{\xi^{-1}(E)}\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset}(U)
                           \rho'(U)\,dU=0,
 \qquad
 \rho'(U)=e^{-\beta A(U)}\det(D[U]+m_0).
\]
At positive bare mass, \(\rho'\) has a strictly positive
lower bound on the compact configuration space.  Since
\(\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset}\ge0\), the bad preimage in
the support of that weight is null.

Now fix \(v\).  The map \(U\mapsto U^{\tilde v}\)
preserves Haar measure and the support of the base weight.
Thus almost every \(U\) in this support and its transform
both have coordinates outside the bad set.  At these points
the first two parts of the proof give
\[
 G_{s,\lambda}(U^{\tilde v})F_s(U^{\tilde v})
     =\alpha_{\tilde v|_{t_1}}
                      \bigl(G_{s,\lambda}(U)F_s(U)\bigr).
\]
The full Berezin integral is unchanged by this action.
Off the support the weight is zero.  This proves
\eqref{eq:free-measure-ae-invariance}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[One step under almost-everywhere invariance]
\label{C-424-19}
Let \(t_1<k\le K\), \(h'\in\mathcal H_{k-1}[t_1]\),
and let \(f\) be a bounded complex Borel function on
\(\mathcal V_0\).  Suppose that
\[
 \mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset}(U)
                    [f(U^{\tilde v})-f(U)]=0
 \quad\text{for almost every }U
\]
for every gauge transformation \(v\) at level \(k-1\).
Then the gauge defect vanishes and
\[
 \sum_{h:\,h|_{k-1}=h'}\tau_h[f]=\mathbf T\tau_{h'}[f],
 \qquad \mathbf T=\mathcal M_*.
\]
If the hypothesis holds at each level above \(t_1\), then
\[
 \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_k[t_1]}\tau_h[f]
       =\mathbf T^{k-t_1}\tau_{h_\emptyset}[f],\qquad
 \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_k[t_1]}\int\mathfrak w_hf\,dU
       =\int\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset}f\,dU.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
We check the use of invariance in the history decomposition
of \cite[Prop.\ 44.1 and its proof]{YMM1}.  The calibrated
thresholds obey \(\varepsilon_j\le c_2^{\rm SO}\).
Indeed,
\(\varepsilon(t)=A_0t^{-1/2}(\log t)^{\mathfrak p_0}\)
is decreasing for \(\log t\ge2\mathfrak p_0\), and the
coupling ceilings give
\(\log\gamma^{-2}\ge2\mathfrak p_0\) and
\(\varepsilon(\gamma^{-2})\le c_2^{\rm SO}\).
All calibrations satisfy \(t_j\ge\gamma^{-2}\).
At these thresholds the gauge defect is zero for every
bounded Borel density; it does not require invariance.

Fix a plaquette outcome \(\mathsf p\) in the step.
The factor
\[
 e_{\mathsf p}(U)=\mathfrak w_{h'}(U)
                          \mathbf1_k^{\rm P}(\mathsf p)(\Theta_k(U))
\]
is invariant under the gauge variables integrated in that
outcome.  The earlier weight factors as
\(\mathfrak w_{h'}=\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset}w'\)
with bounded Borel \(w'\).  Hence, for each fixed such
gauge transformation \(v\),
\[
 e_{\mathsf p}(U)[f(U^{\tilde v})-f(U)]=0
 \quad\text{for almost every }U.
\]
In the gauge-averaging proof of the decomposition, make
the Haar-preserving substitution \(U\mapsto U^{\tilde v}\)
for this fixed \(v\).  The displayed equality replaces
the pointwise invariance of the density.  The resulting
integrand is bounded and jointly Borel in \((U,v)\).
Integrate the equality in \(v\) and apply Fubini; no
common exceptional set for all \(v\) is needed.
The normalized gauge-fixing integral and the partition
by the remaining test outcomes now give exactly the
one-step identity.  Summing over all parents and iterating
gives the measure identity.  Pushforward preserves total
mass, which gives its final assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Preservation of the total integral]\label{C-424-20}
For the data of \cref{C-424-6}, every
\((z,\lambda)\in\mathcal O\times\mathbb C\), and every
\(t_1\le k\le K\),
\[
 \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_k[t_1]}\tau_h[\varsigma^{s,\lambda}]
       =\mathbf T^{k-t_1}\tau_{h_\emptyset}[\varsigma^{s,\lambda}].
\]
In particular,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:free-measure-total}
 \begin{split}
 Z_k(z,\lambda)
 &=\int\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset}\varsigma^{s,\lambda}\,dU\\
 &=\operatorname{Ber}\int_{\mathcal V_{t_1}\setminus
                              (\mathsf N_s\cup\mathsf N_0)}
    \mathsf{Stay}_{h_\emptyset}\mathbf1^{\rm T}_{h_\emptyset}
    \chi_{t_1}(T_\ell)e^{\boldsymbol\Phi^w_{h_\emptyset}}\\
 &\hspace{27mm}\cdot
    e^{A^{\rm F}_{t_1,h_\emptyset}(s)+\lambda\Delta(s)}
                    \,d\mathscr M_{h_\emptyset}
  =Z_{t_1}(z,\lambda).
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The scalar density is bounded and Borel by
\cref{C-424-7}, and satisfies the hypothesis of
\cref{C-424-19} at every later level by
\cref{C-424-18}.  Apply the former lemma and then the
base exponential representation
\eqref{eq:free-measure-base-density}.  Berezin integration
commutes with this integrable coefficientwise representation.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Densities holomorphic in both parameters}

Holomorphy of a measure on every Borel set does not yet select
densities holomorphic at every coordinate point.  The positive
zero-source measure provides a common dominating measure and
allows such a selection.

\begin{proposition}\label{C-424-21}
For each \(h\in\mathcal H_k[t_1]\), there is a Borel
function \(g_h(z,\lambda,v)\) on
\(\mathcal O\times\mathbb C\times\mathsf X_h^{\rm fr}\),
with values in the even Grassmann algebra of \(h\), such that
every coefficient is holomorphic in \((z,\lambda)\) at
every \(v\), and
\[
 \check\tau_h^{\rm F}[s(z),\lambda]
           =g_h(z,\lambda,\cdot)\,\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}.
\]
Moreover, \(\int\|g_h\|_{h_F}\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}\)
is bounded on compact parameter sets.  Whenever the term has
an exponential representation with one null set, \(g_h\)
agrees almost everywhere with its density from
\cite[Lem.\ 10.7]{QCDM1}.  For all parameters,
\[
 Z_k(z,\lambda)=\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_k[t_1]}
   \operatorname{Ber}\int g_h(z,\lambda,v)
                                      \,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}(v)
                =Z_{t_1}(z,\lambda).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Let \(\rho'=e^{-\beta A}\det(D+m_0)\ge c'>0\), as in
\cref{C-424-18}.  The finite measure
\(\nu_h=\check\tau_h[\rho']\) is positive.  The ordinary
zero-source density and full Berezin integration give
\[
 \nu_h=f_h^0\,\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr},\qquad
 f_h^0=\operatorname{Ber}g_h^0\ge0.
\]
We choose a Borel version of \(f_h^0\), nonnegative
everywhere, changing it on a null set if necessary.
For a coefficient \(I\), put
\(\mu_{z,\lambda}=\check\tau_h[\varsigma_{h,I}^{s,\lambda}]\).
The definition by pushforward and nonnegativity of the history
weight imply, for every Borel \(E\),
\[
 |\mu_{z,\lambda}(E)|
 \le\frac{\sup_U|\varsigma_{h,I}^{s,\lambda}(U)|}{c'}\nu_h(E).
\]
The factor is bounded on compact parameter sets, and
\(\mu_{z,\lambda}(E)\) is holomorphic by \cref{C-424-7}.

We give the selection argument.  Suppose that \(\nu\) is
a finite positive Borel measure on a separable metrizable
space \(X\), that \(D\subset\mathbb C^m\) is open, and
that complex measures \(\mu_\zeta\) satisfy the two
properties just established: \(\mu_\zeta(E)\) is
holomorphic for every Borel \(E\), and
\(|\mu_\zeta(E)|\le C_Q\nu(E)\) for \(\zeta\in Q\),
for each compact \(Q\subset D\).
Fix a closed polydisc
\(\bar P=\{|\zeta_i-c_i|\le r_i\}\subset D\).
For a multi-index \(\alpha\), Cauchy's formula defines
the complex measure
\[
 a_\alpha(E)=\frac1{(2\pi i)^m}
  \oint_{\partial_0P}\mu_\zeta(E)
                   \prod_i(\zeta_i-c_i)^{-\alpha_i-1}\,d\zeta.
\]
Dominated convergence gives countable additivity, and
\(|a_\alpha|\le C_{\bar P}r^{-\alpha}\nu\).
Radon--Nikodym therefore gives Borel coefficients
\(d_\alpha\), with
\(a_\alpha=d_\alpha\nu\) and
\(|d_\alpha|\le C_{\bar P}r^{-\alpha}\) everywhere after
null-set changes.  There are only countably many coefficients.
The series
\[
 g_P(\zeta,x)=\sum_\alpha d_\alpha(x)(\zeta-c)^\alpha
\]
converges absolutely and uniformly in \(x\) on every
smaller concentric closed polydisc.  It is jointly Borel,
holomorphic in \(\zeta\) at every \(x\), and bounded
there.  Integration term by term gives
\(\int_Eg_P(\zeta,x)\,d\nu(x)=\mu_\zeta(E)\).

Cover \(D\) by countably many polydiscs of half the radii
of polydiscs \(P_i\) whose closures lie in \(D\).
On an overlap \(P_i\cap P_j\), the densities \(g_{P_i}\)
and \(g_{P_j}\) agree \(\nu\)-almost everywhere at each
point of a countable dense subset.  Outside a single Borel
null set for this pair they agree everywhere on the overlap,
by continuity in \(\zeta\).  Take the union of these null
sets over all pairs.  Off this union the functions glue to
\(\hat g\); set \(\hat g=0\) on the union.  This defines
a jointly Borel density, holomorphic at every \(x\).
Every compact subset of \(D\) is covered by finitely many
of the smaller polydiscs, so \(\hat g\) is uniformly
bounded there.

Apply this construction with
\(D=\mathcal O\times\mathbb C\), \(X=\mathsf X_h^{\rm fr}\),
and \(\nu=\nu_h\), separately to each of the finitely
many coefficients.  Set
\((g_h)_I=\hat g_I f_h^0\).
The integral bounds follow from finiteness of \(\nu_h\)
and
\(\|F\|_{h_F}\le\sum_I h_F^{|I|}|F_I|\).
Uniqueness of densities gives agreement with any exponential
representation.  Finally sum the integrals and apply
\cref{C-424-20}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The later steps depend only on the base measure}

The restart comparison identifies two measures at the base.
To propagate that equality, we must check both the later
integrands and the domains of their coordinate maps.

\begin{lemma}\label{C-424-34}
Let \(h\in\mathcal H_k[t_1]\) and \(\xi=\mathcal M^{t_1}\).
For \(V\in\mathcal V_{t_1}\), form \(\Theta_t^\circ(V)\)
by setting its level-\(j\) member equal to
\(\mathcal M^{j-t_1}V\) for \(j\ge t_1\), and to one
for \(j<t_1\).  Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item The history weight factors as
\[
 \mathfrak w_h=\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset}
                                    (\mathfrak w_h^\circ\circ\xi),
 \qquad
 \mathfrak w_h^\circ(V)
 =\prod_{t_1<t\le k}
   \mathbf1_t(\mathsf o_t)(\Theta_t^\circ(V))
   \mathfrak G_{t-1}(\mathcal M^{t-1-t_1}V;P_t''(h)).
\]
The function \(\mathfrak w_h^\circ\) is bounded and Borel.
\item The later fermion integration is
\(T^{\rm F}_{h;(t_1,k]}[U]=T_h^\circ[\xi(U)]\), where
\(T_h^\circ[V]\) is the composition of the same partial
kernels with \(\mathcal M^{n-t_1}V\) in place of
\(\mathcal M^nU\).  Its matrix coefficients
\(T_h^\circ[V]_{II'}\) are bounded Borel functions of \(V\).
\item The free-coordinate map factors, with equality of
domains, as
\begin{equation}\label{eq:free-measure-coordinate-factor}
 \operatorname{dom}\mathsf v_h
       =\xi^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}\mathsf v_h^\circ),
 \qquad \mathsf v_h=\mathsf v_h^\circ\circ\xi,
\end{equation}
where the Borel partial map \(\mathsf v_h^\circ\) is
\[
 V\longmapsto
 \left(
  \bigl((\mathcal M^{l-t_1}V)|_{\Gamma_l^{\rm le}(h)}\bigr)_{t_1\le l\le k},
  \bigl(g_l^{-1}\mathcal A_l^{\prime\diamond}(b)
                (\Theta_{l+1}^\circ(V))\bigr)_{
                   t_1\le l<k,\ b\in\mathfrak X_l^{\rm E+}(h)}
 \right).
\]
Here \(\Gamma_l^{\rm le}(h)\) is the set of lettered datum
bonds, \(\mathfrak X_l^{\rm E+}(h)\) consists of the
positively oriented external bonds, and
\(\mathcal A_l^{\prime\diamond}\) is the new fluctuation
coordinate, scaled by \(g_l\).
\item For a finite Grassmann-valued measure \(\rho\) on
\(\mathcal V_{t_1}\), define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:free-measure-step-map}
 (\mathsf{St}_h\rho)_I(E)
 =\sum_{I'}\int_{(\mathsf v_h^\circ)^{-1}(E)}
     \mathfrak w_h^\circ(V)T_h^\circ[V]_{II'}\,d\rho_{I'}(V).
\end{equation}
If \(\rho=\xi_*\mu\), this is the image under
\(\mathsf v_h\) of
\((\mathfrak w_h^\circ\circ\xi)T_h^\circ[\xi(\cdot)]\mu\).
It is therefore the same for every \(\mu\) with this
pushforward.  In particular,
\[
 \mathsf{St}_h\hat\tau_{h_\emptyset}^{\rm F}[s,\lambda]
                   =\check\tau_h^{\rm F}[s,\lambda]
 \quad((z,\lambda)\in\mathcal O\times\mathbb C).
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The determining bonds at levels \(j<t_1\) are absent:
\(\Omega_{j+1}=T_\ell\).  A later test depends only on
the fields at its two top levels and on the restrictions to
the determining bonds.  The families \(\Theta_t(U)\)
and \(\Theta_t^\circ(\xi(U))\) agree on this data.
Thus they give the same test outcome.  The gauge-fixing
factors after \(t_1\) already depend only on
\(\mathcal M^{t-1}U=\mathcal M^{t-1-t_1}\xi(U)\).
This proves (i); all its factors are bounded and Borel.
The same identity for the averaged configuration proves
(ii), since each partial kernel has bounded Borel
coefficients and each partial Berezin integral is a finite
operation on coefficients.

For (iii), the coordinate factors below \(t_1\) are
one-point spaces: both their datum bonds and their external
bonds are empty.  The retained group coordinates at the
other levels plainly factor through \(\xi\).  We verify
the domains of the fluctuation coordinates.  The completed
collared sequence through the base is constant, so its
datum bonds below \(t_1\) are also absent.  Hence the
completed datum of a later step is the same for
\(\Theta_{l+1}(U)\) and
\(\Theta_{l+1}^\circ(\xi(U))\).

On a strip bond in either shift zone, the new fluctuation
is defined by
\[
 \mathcal A_l^{\prime\diamond}(b)
   =\frac1i\log W_l^{\prime\diamond}(b),\qquad
 W_l^{\prime\diamond}(b)
   =(\Psi_b^\diamond)^{-1}
       \bigl(V_l(b)V_l^{{\rm bg,loc}\diamond}(b)^{-1}\bigr).
\]
Its domain requires the shift to exist, the resulting bond
map \(\Psi_b^\diamond\) to be a bijection, and its inverse
value to differ from \(-1\).  The shift, the bond map,
and the local background, including their domains, depend
only on the completed datum.  Outside these zones, the
coordinate is
\[
 \frac1i\log\bigl(V_l(b)V_l^{{\rm bg}\diamond}(b)^{-1}\bigr),
\]
whose domain requires the stable background to exist and
the logarithm's argument to differ from \(-1\).
Again the background and its domain are determined by the
completed datum.  The two families have this same datum
and the same \(V_l(b)\).  Each fluctuation coordinate
is therefore defined for both or for neither, with the
same value.  This proves
\eqref{eq:free-measure-coordinate-factor}.

Every component is a Borel partial map, being a composition
of the original fluctuation map with the Borel map
\(\Theta_{l+1}^\circ\).  Their finite intersection is a
Borel domain.  Their product is Borel because the
coordinate spaces have countable bases.

For (iv), apply the pushforward identity to the bounded
Borel function
\[
 \mathbf1_{(\mathsf v_h^\circ)^{-1}(E)}
                       \mathfrak w_h^\circ T_h^\circ[\cdot]_{II'}.
\]
Its preimage under \(\xi\) is the corresponding
integrand on \(\mathsf v_h^{-1}(E)\), by (iii).
Sum over \(I'\).  For the final assertion take
\(\mu=\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset}G_{s,\lambda}F_s\,dU\)
and use (i), (ii), and the definitions of the terms.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Reading the early families}

\begin{lemma}[A free family in a later step]\label{C-422-6}
Let $\Delta$ be a free family of level $j\le k<K$, read at a
source of $\mathcal P$ on the fixed pair domains. Its summands
satisfy the old-activity hypotheses of \cite[Lem.\ 7.9]{QCDM1}
with size $r^\psi(\Delta)$, including the moved-diagonal condition
and its torus version with reference $G^\infty$.
Its moved pieces satisfy both weighted piece bounds of
\cite[Prop.\ 10.1, proof]{QCDM1}, with that size.
At lags below $n_{\rm lag}$ it can be counted whole, with weight
$\omega_{k+1-j}$.

More explicitly, its cell sum satisfies
\begin{align*}
 m_c[\Delta]-m_c[G]
 =\sum_{z\in c}\biggl[&\sum_y(A_j^{\mathsf n}-A_j)(y,z)\nu\\
 &+\sum_{X,p}\left(1-\mathfrak s_j^{-1}\sum_yA_j^{\mathsf n}(y,z)\right)
                                                a_{X,p}(z)
   +\sum_{X,p}'a_{X,p}(z)\biggr].
\end{align*}
Here $m_c[G]$ includes $l_\square$, and the last sum consists of
pieces omitted by the torus rule. The cell sum $m_c[G]$ vanishes on
$\mathbb Z^3$; on a torus its remainder is assigned to polymers
that wrap around it. At a level-$k$ cube, the displayed difference
has total norm at most
\[
 (c_{\rm cs}+c_{\rm cs}^\Delta)\omega_{k+1-j}r^\psi(\Delta).
\]
This includes lag zero and remains true when the same members are
counted at a cube of the final level $K$.

The scalar part enters the array of old scalar terms with Wilson
coefficient zero. Its bracket localization at a polymer $Y$ is
bounded by
\[
 K_\Lambda\mathsf s_k(\alpha_0)L^{-(k-j)}r^0(\Delta)
                 e^{-(1-2\delta_{\rm w})\kappa d_k(Y)},
\]
and in the step's polymer norm by
$K_\Lambda^{\rm s}\mathsf s_k(\alpha_0)L^{-(k-j)}r^0(\Delta)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The old-activity argument uses the row-sum bound on a quadratic
kernel, decay of the localized backgrounds and their source
variation, and the piecewise identities
\[
 u_X+\delta_{yy'}a_X(y)=k_X,
 \qquad \sum_y\operatorname{ord}_0[k_{X,p}](y)=m_p(k_{X,p}).
\]
These identities are linear in $(F,G,\nu)$. The definition supplies
their common paths, the reference cell cancellation, the phase
invariance excluding two unbarred or two barred fields, and the
bound $c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2|\nu|\le r^\psi(\Delta)$.
Thus the proof of \cite[Lem.\ 7.9]{QCDM1}, with the source
modifications in \cite[Prop.\ 10.1]{QCDM1}, applies term by term.
In particular, the two weighted piece bounds use only the local
background estimates and the sums of the norms of $F,G$.

To check the cell estimate, add the units, moved pieces, and mass
forms. The result is exactly the displayed identity. The term with
$\nu$ has weighted norm at most
$M^3C_{\rm bg}^{\rm w}L^j\|\mathsf n\||\nu|/r_M$.
Moving its hull to level $k$ costs at most $C_{\rm hl}L^{k-j}h_F^2$.
Since $L^{k+1}\|\mathsf n\|<2r_M$, its contribution is at most
\[
 \frac{2C_{\rm hl}M^3C_{\rm bg}^{\rm w}}{Lc_{\mathsf S}}
                 r^\psi(\Delta)
 =c_{\rm cs}^\Delta\omega_1r^\psi(\Delta).
\]
For the moved pieces the same computation bounds the contribution
by
\[
 C_{\rm hl}C_{\rm pw}
 \left[\eta_{\min}^{-2}
        \left(\tfrac2LC_{\rm bg}^{\rm w}+C_AC_{\rm dx}\right)
                  +\max\{1,C'_{\rm dx}\}\right]r^\psi(\Delta)
 =c_{\rm cs}C_\omega r^\psi(\Delta).
\]
Here $C_{\rm dx},C'_{\rm dx}$ bound
$L^{k-j}e^{-4c_t\ell/\lambda_j}$ and
$L^{k-j}e^{-c_t\ell/\lambda_j}$, respectively. Their bounds
hold through $k=K$, since $\ell/\lambda_j\ge2L^{k+1-j}$.
At lag zero use the second weighted piece estimate; the omitted
pieces are bounded with factor one instead of a tail. The same
constant works because $\max\{1,C'_{\rm dx}\}\ge1$.
This proves the asserted bound at every lag.

Finally the scalar localization is linear in its array.
Apply \cite[Prop.\ 51.16]{YMM1} to the array with the one entry
$\Delta_0$ at level $j$. Its system ratios are one and its scale
factor is at most $\mathsf s_k(\alpha_0)$. The coefficient of the
Wilson action is zero, so the stated estimate follows directly.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The four size bounds]\label{C-422-7}
Suppose the first two conditions in \eqref{eq:free-family-lags}
hold, $|\lambda|<R$, and $t_1\le n\le K$. Let the later sizes
satisfy $\epsilon_j\le(2C_w^{\rm s}-C_w)\phi_{j-1}$ for
$t_1<j\le n$, and put
\[
 \epsilon_j[\lambda]=
 \begin{cases}
  \epsilon_j^{{\rm s},\psi}+|\lambda|r_j^\psi,&j\le t_1,\\
  \epsilon_j,&j>t_1.
 \end{cases}
 \qquad \Phi_n=\sum_{j\le n}\omega_{n+1-j}\phi_{j-1}.
\]
Then
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{j\le n}\omega_{n+1-j}\epsilon_j[\lambda]
       &\le2C_w^{\rm s}\Phi_n
                       \le2C_w^{\rm s}C_{\rm pc}S_{1/4}\phi_n,\\
 c_{\rm cs}\sum_{j\le n}\omega_{n+1-j}\epsilon_j[\lambda]
               +c_{\rm cs}^\Delta|\lambda|\Sigma_n^\psi
       &\le2c_{\rm cs}C_w^{\rm s}\Phi_n,\\
 \epsilon_j[\lambda]&\le2C_w^{\rm s}\phi_{n-1}\quad(j\le t_1),\\
 |\lambda|\Sigma_n^0&\le c_0^\Delta.
\end{align*}
The early size bounds include the pointed terms, the reference,
and the infinite-lattice reference family.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Let $A$ be the weighted sum at $\lambda=0$ and
$X=|\lambda|\Sigma_n^\psi$. By \cref{C-422-5},
$A\le(2C_w^{\rm s}-C_w)\Phi_n$. Since
$\Phi_n\ge\omega_1\phi_{n-1}$ and
$c_\psi^\Delta=C_w\omega_1c_{\rm cs}/(c_{\rm cs}+c_{\rm cs}^\Delta)$,
\[
 X\le C_w\frac{c_{\rm cs}}{c_{\rm cs}+c_{\rm cs}^\Delta}\Phi_n.
\]
This proves the first two bounds, including the cell contribution.
For an individual early level use
$|\lambda|r_j^\psi\le X/\omega_1\le C_w\phi_{n-1}$ and
$\phi_{j-1}\le\phi_{n-1}$. The scalar bound follows from
$\Sigma_n^0=L^{-(n-t_1)}\Sigma_{t_1}^0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The step with early activities]\label{C-422-8}
Assume the first three conditions in \eqref{eq:free-family-lags}
at radius $R$. For $t_1\le k<K$ let
\[
 \mathscr D'_k=\{(\sigma_i)_{t_1\le i\le k}:
                              \|\sigma_i\|<B_\sigma\phi_i\}.
\]
The small-field steps from the base are defined on
$2\mathscr D'_k\times\mathrm P(R)$ and have the same local
form, fixed pair domains, reference at zero sources, and pointed
outputs as \cite[Prop.\ 10.1]{QCDM1}. They are jointly
holomorphic in the coordinates, parameter, and source wherever
the latter varies in an open set satisfying the lag conditions.
They depend only on coordinates in their polymer, are jointly
gauge invariant, and preserve the scalar phase symmetry.

Put $\tau_k^\lambda=
\max\{\tau_k(w;\alpha_0),\tau_k(w_\lambda;\alpha_0)\}$.
The new activities, including their pointed terms, obey
\begin{align*}
 \|\mathcal V_0\|&\le c_{\rm cl}/2,
 &n^{\rm int}+n'&\le w_*/2,
 &\|\mathcal V_\psi\|&\le b_k^{\rm blk,s}\le c_{\rm cl}/8,\\
 \epsilon_{k+1}^{{\rm s},\psi}
   &\le(2C_w^{\rm s}-C_w)\phi_k,
 &\epsilon_{k+1}^{{\rm s},0}
   &\le\tfrac{15}8C_w^{\rm s}\phi_k
                              +\tfrac35C'_{\rm lin}\tau_k^\lambda.
\end{align*}
Their pointed scalar activities have the ordinary bound $E_0^{\rm s}$
at rate $\kappa+1$.
The mass increment is defined by the same moments relative to the
zero-source reference:
\[
 \nu_{k+1}(y;\mathfrak c,\lambda)
   =\mu_{k+1}-\mathfrak s_{k+1}^{-1}\sum_{X,p}a_{X,p}(y).
\]
It takes values in the colour-scalar matrix slot $\mathbb M$ and
satisfies
\[
 |\nu_{k+1}-\mu_{k+1}|\le\tfrac12B_\nu\phi_{k+1},\qquad
 |\nu_{k+1}(y;\mathfrak c,\lambda)-\nu_{k+1}(y;\mathfrak c',\lambda)|
 \le B_\nu\phi_{k+1}\|\mathfrak c-\mathfrak c'\|_{k,y}
\]
for $\mathfrak c\in\mathscr D'_k$ and
$\mathfrak c'\in2\mathscr D'_k$. The first bound and the matrix
slot remain valid when any subset of the pieces is used.
The source energies satisfy
\[
 |e_{k+1}(X;\mathfrak c,\lambda)|
                           \le C_{\mathfrak E}e^{-\kappa d_{k+1}(X)}.
\]
At $\lambda=0$ and the ordinary source coordinates, every output
is the corresponding output of the ordinary flow.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Use the one-step proof of \cite[Prop.\ 10.1]{QCDM1}. We verify
the properties and numerical estimates changed by the early families.
Their pointed scalar terms are local holomorphic functions on the
same cores, while \cref{C-422-6} supplies the precise old-activity
hypotheses for their fermion terms. They are affine in $\lambda$
and independent of the later mass coordinates. Hence the Gaussian
integral, localization, and cluster series remain holomorphic, with
locally uniform convergence once the following bounds are established.

The scalar potential has the ordinary gauge and explicit terms of
size at most $c_{\rm cl}/4$, the linear term of size at most
$c_{\rm cl}/8$, and the old scalar array. The latter has the old
bound $13c_{\rm cl}/144$, plus
\[
 K_\Lambda^{\rm s}\mathsf s_k(\alpha_0)|\lambda|\Sigma_k^0
 \le\frac{c_0^\Delta}{12K_M^\bullet}
 \le\frac5{144}c_{\rm cl}.
\]
Their sum is $c_{\rm cl}/2$ and also proves the Gaussian
admission $n^{\rm int}+n'\le w_*/2$.

For the fermion terms the new cell contribution is
\[
 \Sigma_k^{\rm cs}[\lambda]
 \le C_0^{\rm cs}h_F^2\phi_k
       +c_{\rm cs}\sum_{i\le k}\omega_{k+1-i}\epsilon_i[\lambda]
       +c_{\rm cs}^\Delta|\lambda|\Sigma_k^\psi.
\]
Thus the part of the one-step bound depending on old activities is
controlled by
\[
 C_0^{\rm cs}h_F^2\phi_k
 +(1+c_{\rm cs})\sum_{i\le k}\omega_{k+1-i}\epsilon_i[\lambda]
 +c_{\rm cs}^\Delta|\lambda|\Sigma_k^\psi
 \le[C_0^{\rm cs}h_F^2
       +2(1+c_{\rm cs})C_w^{\rm s}C_{\rm pc}S_{1/4}]\phi_k.
\]
This is the ordinary bound. The new fermion size therefore obeys
\begin{align*}
 \epsilon_{k+1}^{{\rm s},\psi}\le{}&C_w^\psi\phi_k
 +4\theta_E^{\rm s}\sum_{i\le k}\omega_{k+1-i}
       [(1+c_{\rm cs})\epsilon_i[\lambda]
          +c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2(\bar B_M+2B_\sigma)\phi_i]\\
 &+4\theta_E^{\rm s}c_{\rm cs}^\Delta|\lambda|\Sigma_k^\psi.
\end{align*}
Apply \cref{C-422-7} and the calculation in \cref{C-422-5}.
This gives the claimed fermion size and $b_k^{\rm blk,s}$, also
for the reference and pointed terms.

In the new scalar fluctuation family the additional variation has
size at most
\[
 2K_M^\bullet K_\Lambda^{\rm s}\sqrt2\,
       \mathsf C_{\mathcal A}A_1\alpha_0^{-1}\phi_kc_0^\Delta
                         \le\tfrac18C_w^{\rm s}\phi_k.
\]
The other five terms of the ordinary proof retain their estimates.
They give, respectively, a combined $C_w^{\rm s}\phi_k$, the
old-fermion contribution $C_w^{\rm s}\phi_k/2$, and the ordinary
scalar-array contribution $C_w^{\rm s}\phi_k/4$.
The linear terms contribute
$(1/2+1/10)C'_{\rm lin}\tau_k^\lambda$.
Adding these terms gives $15/8$ and $3/5$ as stated. The same
calculation with $K_M^\bullet$ proves the pointed bounds.
The ordinary small-coupling ceiling then bounds each scalar pointer
by $E_0^{\rm s}$.

Every operation commutes with the scalar phase symmetry: the gauge
vertices contain no generators; the fermion Gaussian, its normalized
Berezin integral, the background maps, and all mass forms preserve
the contragredient pair. Pointing counts generators and also commutes
with this symmetry. The new quadratic terms therefore still have
one barred and one unbarred field.
At the trivial configuration, constant colour rotations fix the
pair and commute with the fine mass and background walks. Each
piece's moment commutes with their irreducible action on colour,
so it lies in $\mathbb M$. This proves the assertion even for a
subset of pieces.

The sum of absolute moment bounds gives
$|\nu_{k+1}-\mu_{k+1}|
\le c_{\rm inc}h_F^{-2}2C_w^{\rm s}\phi_k
\le B_\nu\phi_{k+1}/2$.
For locality, a piece bounded by $M_0$ on $2\mathscr D'_k$ reads
only coordinates in its polymer $X$. Put
$T=\max_{i,x\in X}\|\sigma'_i(x)-\sigma_i(x)\|/(B_\sigma\phi_i)$.
Schwarz's lemma on the line from $\mathfrak c$ in the direction
of this restricted difference gives $2M_0T$ if $T\le1$; the
bound $2M_0$ suffices otherwise. Summing the pieces with their
localized walks is exactly the ordinary locality count and yields
the stated $B_\nu$.

Finally the scalar value at the trivial pair is bounded by
$K_Mc_{\rm cl}$, the Gaussian source term by one per pointer,
and the fermion normalizer by its ordinary source bound. Their
difference from the fixed zero-source reference gives
$C_{\mathfrak E}e^{-\kappa d(X)}$.
All properties required at the next level have now been proved.
Induction starts at $k=t_1$, where there are no later activities.
At $\lambda=0$ the input agrees with the ordinary flow, so the
same construction gives identical outputs.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Chains and histories at the parameter}

\begin{lemma}[The shrinking parameter window]\label{C-422-9}
Assume all four conditions in \eqref{eq:free-family-lags}. Starting
with the mass field of \cref{C-422-4}, define
\[
 \sigma_{k+1}(s,\lambda)(x)
 =L\sigma_k(s,\lambda)(x)
   +\nu_{k+1}(y_{k+1}(x);\mathfrak c_k(s,\lambda),\lambda)-\mu_{k+1}.
\]
For $t_1\le k\le K$ this chain is holomorphic on
$\mathrm P(R_k)$ and satisfies
\[
 \|\sigma_k(s,\lambda)-\sigma_k(s)\|
                        \le\tfrac12B_\sigma\phi_k,
 \qquad
 \|\sigma_k(s,\lambda)\|
                   \le(B_\sigma-C_{\rm var}/2)\phi_k.
\]
It equals the ordinary source chain at $\lambda=0$ and is jointly
holomorphic in the source on every open set on which the lag
conditions hold at the same radius.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Set $D_k(\lambda)=\sigma_k(s,\lambda)-\sigma_k(s)$.
The initial bound is the mass condition. If it holds through $k$,
then \cref{C-422-5} puts every preceding coordinate in
$\mathscr D'_k$ on $\mathrm P(R_k)$. The difference of the two
increments is holomorphic there, zero at zero, and bounded by
$B_\nu\phi_{k+1}$, by \cref{C-422-8}.
Schwarz's lemma on each line in the polydisc bounds a holomorphic
norm-valued function that vanishes at zero by its supremum times
$|\lambda|/R_k$. On the smaller disc this gives
\[
 \|D_{k+1}\|
 \le Q_\sigma^{-1}
       (LB_\sigma\phi_k/2+B_\nu\phi_{k+1})
 \le\tfrac12B_\sigma\phi_{k+1},
\]
because $L\phi_k\le2\sqrt L\phi_{k+1}$,
$B_\nu\le B_\sigma/8$, and $Q_\sigma=2\sqrt L+1/4$.
Composition proves holomorphy and closes the induction.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The chain along a history]\label{C-422-10}
For $h\in\mathcal H_k[t_1]$ and $|\lambda|<R_k$, start its
chain at $\sigma_{t_1}(s,\lambda)$. At each later step use only
the pieces whose polymer $Z_p$ lies in $\Lambda_j$ to form
$\nu_j^h$, and set
\[
 \sigma_j^h=L\sigma_{j-1}^h+\nu_j^h-\mu_j\quad\hbox{on }\Omega_j.
\]
Off $\Omega_j$ use the ordinary chain at the parameter.
Let $S_j=\bigcup_{t_1<i\le j}\tilde Z_i(h)$.
With the ordinary constants $R'_\flat,C'_{\mathfrak E}$,
\begin{align*}
 |\sigma_j^h-\sigma_j|(x)
  &\le8B_\nu\phi_j
        e^{-\kappa_\sigma\operatorname{dist}(x,S_j)/(2L^j)}
       &&(\operatorname{dist}(x,S_j)\ge R'_\flat L^j),\\
 \sup_{\Omega_j}|\sigma_j^h-\sigma_j|&\le16B_\nu\phi_j,
 &\sup_{\Omega_j}|\sigma_j^h|&\le2B_\sigma\phi_j,\\
 \sum_{X\subset\Lambda_n}
 |e_n(X;\mathfrak c_{n-1},\lambda)
                 -e_n(X;\mathfrak c^h_{n-1},\lambda)|
  &\le C'_{\mathfrak E}\#_n(\tilde Z_n).
\end{align*}
The coordinates of $h$ are jointly holomorphic and belong to
$2\mathscr D'_j$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The two chains agree at the base. The localized coordinate distance
$a_j(t)$ in the ordinary history-chain proof therefore starts at
zero and satisfies
\begin{align*}
 a_j(t)\le{}&La_{j-1}(t)+B_\nu\phi_j
 \left[C_{\rm loc}e^{-\kappa_\sigma t/L^j}
 +e^{\kappa_\sigma\sqrt3}
    \sup_{v\ge0}e^{-\kappa_\sigma v/L^j}
       \max_{t_1\le i<j}\frac{a_i(t-v)}{B_\sigma\phi_i}\right].
\end{align*}
This follows from the local bound in \cref{C-422-8} and the rule
discarding the pieces outside $\Lambda_j$. The ordinary induction
uses only
$Le^{-\kappa_\sigma R'_\flat}\le1/4$,
$(C_{\rm loc}+3e^{2\kappa_\sigma})e^{-\kappa_\sigma R'_\flat/4}\le2$,
and $B_\nu\le B_\sigma/6$. All remain unchanged. It gives the
first two bounds, and $16B_\nu\le B_\sigma$ keeps the history
coordinates in $2\mathscr D'_j$.
The source-energy estimate follows by the same exponentially
weighted polymer count, using
$|e_n(X)|\le C_{\mathfrak E}e^{-\kappa d_n(X)}$ and the first
bound. These are exactly the inputs of the history-chain proof
in \cite[\S10, following Lem.\ 10.4]{QCDM1}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Regular sums and history frames]\label{C-422-11}
Under these hypotheses the regular activities, including all early
families, have total norm at most
$C_{\rm leg}^{\rm s}\Sigma_{\mathcal L}(h)$.
Their contribution to a cube of a nonempty layer $\mathcal L_n$
is at most $C_{\rm leg}^{\square,\rm s}\phi_n$.
The mass member
\[
 \mathsf M_h(s,\lambda)
 =-\mathsf S_1((s_h+\sigma_h(s,\lambda))\psi^{\rm bg}),\qquad
 \sigma_h=L^{-t_1}\sigma_{t_1}
        +\sum_{t_1<j\le k}L^{-j}(\nu_j^h-\mu_j)\varphi_j
\]
has the same ordinary mass bounds, namely the per-cube bound
$w_0\nu C_H^2h_F^2L(\bar B_M+2B_\sigma)\phi_{n-1}$
and its ordinary sum over layers. The scalar regular sum, together
with the absolute Wilson extraction terms, is at most
$C_5^{\rm s}\Sigma_{\mathcal L}(h)$.

Suppose the history representation through level $k$ has these
bounds and the ordinary bounds on all its later boundary terms
and edge terms. Then its next frame has the same admission bounds
as the ordinary source frame. Its regular scalar class has size
at most $\varepsilon_\flat$. The first seven fermion classes have
total size at most $b_k^{\rm tot,s}$, and the full class obeys
\[
 \mathsf{sz}_{k+1}^\natural
 \le\frac{13}{64}\max\left\{
        \sup_{j\le k}\mathsf{sz}_j^\natural,
        \sup_{j\le k}\bar v_j^{\rm s}\right\}+b_k^{\rm tot,s}.
\]
For $j\le t_1$ the sizes here are those of the original empty
history at the source $s$; for $j>t_1$ they are those of the
new steps. Thus the recursion closes at
\[
 \mathsf{sz}_{k+1}^\natural
        \le\tfrac{64}{51}b^{\rm tot,s}(\gamma)
                       \le\tfrac{16}{17}\varepsilon_\flat,
 \qquad \bar v_{k+1}^{\rm s}\le b^{\rm blk,s}(\gamma)\le c_{\rm cl}/8.
\]
All frame members are Borel, jointly gauge invariant, analytic on
their tiers, and functions of the pair there.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every nonempty layer has $n\ge t_1$, so the four estimates in
\cref{C-422-7} apply at its level. For the terms counted with a
summable lag kernel, their individual size is at most
$2C_w^{\rm s}\phi_{n-1}$. Their sum per cube is therefore at most
$2C_w^{\rm s}K_{\rm fin}\phi_{n-1}$.
The cell terms add at most
\[
 [C_0^{\rm cs}h_F^2+2c_{\rm cs}C_{\rm pc}S_{1/4}C_w^{\rm s}]\phi_n,
\]
by the second estimate of \cref{C-422-7}, including lag zero.
For the units at lags $n-j>n_{\rm lag}$, use the count proved
in \cref{C-422-16} and the whole positive lag sum:
\[
 \sum_{n-j>n_{\rm lag}}c_{n-j}^{\rm u}\epsilon_j[\lambda]
 \le\frac{N_{\rm u}L^{9/2}}{C_\omega L^{1/4}}
                         2C_w^{\rm s}C_{\rm pc}S_{1/4}\phi_n.
\]
At the remaining lags use the individual current-scale bound;
each lag occurs once, giving
$2N_{\rm u}C_w^{\rm s}S_{\rm lag}\phi_{n-1}$.
These terms sum to at most
$(c_{\rm o}^{\rm leg}+N_{\rm u}c_{\rm u}^{\rm leg})\phi_n$.
The floor \eqref{eq:free-history-leg-floor} proves both claims,
since $\phi_n\le\phi(\tfrac12e^{18\mathfrak p_0})$.
The early families have no rim; the later rim estimates are included
in $K_{\rm fin}$ and the history version of the unit count.

For $n>t_1$ the coefficient of the mass member on $\mathcal L_n$
is the ordinary convex combination of the coefficients at levels
$n-1,n$. The bounds of \cref{C-422-10} give
$L^{-(n-1)}(\bar B_M+2B_\sigma)\phi_{n-1}$.
On the first layer the coefficient is simply
$L^{-t_1}(s_{t_1}+\sigma_{t_1}(s,\lambda))$.
Use $L^{-1}\phi_{t_1}\le\phi_{t_1-1}$ to obtain the same bound.
The ordinary background-field count now proves the mass assertions.

For the scalar sum, the contribution of a level-$j$ pointed bound
$g_j$ is, by \cite[Prop.\ 64.2(a.3)]{YMM1}, at most
\[
 C_a^{\rm sc}g_j\sum_{n=j}^kL^{-(n-j)}\#_n(\mathcal L_n).
\]
Here $g_j\le E_0^{\rm s}+|\lambda|r_j^0$ at an early level and
$g_j\le E_0^{\rm s}$ later. Sum in $j$, use
$\sum_{j\le n}L^{-(n-j)}\le13/12$ and
$|\lambda|\Sigma_n^0\le c_0^\Delta\le M^{-3}\mathsf B$.
The Wilson extraction terms cost at most
$13B_\sharp\Sigma_{\mathcal L}(h)/4$, since $|b_j|\le B_\sharp$
and the admitted curvature factor is at most one. Thus the total
is bounded by
$C_m^{\rm sc}(E_0^{\rm s}+B_\sharp+M^{-3}\mathsf B)
\Sigma_{\mathcal L}(h)=C_5^{\rm s}\Sigma_{\mathcal L}(h)$.

We next check the changes in the frame. The scalar list enters
its regular class through
\[
 \mathsf{size}^E
 \le C_{\rm sz}C_{\rm ert}
        (E_0^{\rm s}+|\lambda|\Sigma_k^0+\alpha_0^2B_\sharp).
\]
This follows by summing the coefficient of an old scalar entry,
$C_{\rm ert}L^{-(k-j)}\sum_{i=0}^{k-j}L^i\varpi_i
\le C_{\rm ert}C'_hL^{-(k-j)}$, in
\cite[Prop.\ 58.22]{YMM1}. Since
$c_0^\Delta\le(\sqrt2-1)E_0^{\rm s}$, the ordinary estimate
on the doubled source box bounds this class by
$\varepsilon_\flat/2$. The cubic and higher gauge-weight terms
cost the other half.

The first two fermion classes use the regular sums just proved
and the stored-layer constant. For the third and fourth classes,
the potential bound is that of \cref{C-422-8}. The terms with
stored generators carry $\Theta_k'{}^{\rm s}$ times
\[
 C_0^{\rm cs}h_F^2\phi_k
 +(1+c_{\rm cs})\sum_{i\le k}\omega_{k+1-i}\epsilon_i[\lambda]
             +c_{\rm cs}^\Delta|\lambda|\Sigma_k^\psi.
\]
The first two bounds of \cref{C-422-7} give exactly the ordinary
stored-layer estimate for this expression. All other terms in
these classes have a summable lag kernel or a short-lag count;
the other two bounds of that lemma preserve those estimates.
The fifth and sixth classes use the same lag sum and the per-cube
regular and mass bounds on the stored layers. In particular the
newly stored layer $\Omega_k\setminus\Omega_{k+1}$ is contained
in the old top layer $\Omega_k$, where those bounds have just been
proved. The seventh class contains the mass and rim forms and uses
$|\nu_j^h-\mu_j|\le B_\nu\phi_j/2$.
Thus these seven classes total at most $b_k^{\rm tot,s}$.
The remaining three classes read earlier boundary terms and
insertions. Their ordinary estimate is $13/64$ times the largest
earlier size. Before the base there is no boundary term and the
insertion sizes are those of the original empty history. After
the base the inductive bounds apply. This gives the stated recursion;
$13/51+1=64/51$ closes it.

Finally, the new early members are holomorphic functions of the
pair and jointly invariant on their cores; their mass forms have
coefficients independent of the gauge configuration. Composing
with the Borel evaluation maps gives Borel frame members.
The first seven classes are analytic in the usual field polydisc.
The last three are formed from the later edge and boundary terms
using the same leveling functions and shifts as the ordinary frame;
these functions depend on neither source nor parameter. The
ordinary proof that their sum at each domain depends only on the
pair therefore applies, including the split contributions of each
boundary term through its coefficients and its legs. Their tier
analyticity follows from the same substituted triples and locally
uniform series. This verifies every frame property used by the
next history step, rather than only its numerical size.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The history expansion from the base}

\begin{definition}[Terms and vacuum energy]\label{C-422-12}
For $h\in\mathcal H_k[t_1]$ split the fermion step operator at
the base:
$T_h^{\rm F}=T_{h,>t_1}^{\rm F}\circ T_{h_\emptyset}^{\rm F}$.
Use the Borel representative $G_{s,\lambda}$ constructed in
\cref{C-424-7}: when
$\xi(U)\in\mathsf S_\emptyset\setminus\mathsf N_0$ it is
the pullback of $\exp(\sum_i\lambda_i\Delta_i(s))$,
and it is one elsewhere.
The construction and proof there apply to this finite sum
coefficient by coefficient. Define the perturbed operator by
inserting $G_{s,\lambda}$ between the two factors:
\[
 T_h^{{\rm F},\lambda}[U]
 =T_{h,>t_1}^{\rm F}[U]
 \left(G_{s,\lambda}(U)
       T_{h_\emptyset}^{\rm F}[U]
       (e^{-A(\beta-a_K^{-1}w,U)-S_F(U)+\Phi(J)})\right).
\]
The history term $\hat\tau_h^{\rm F}[s,\lambda]$ is the image
of $\mathfrak w_h(U)T_h^{{\rm F},\lambda}[U]\,dU$ under its
completed coordinates. Its image on free coordinates is denoted
$\check\tau_h^{\rm F}[s,\lambda]$.
At the base this is $\rho_{s,\lambda}$; at $\lambda=0$ it is the
ordinary sourced term.

The coefficients of this operator, set to zero away from the
support of the base history, are bounded Borel functions of $U$.
Indeed, each free-family coefficient is continuous on its pair
domain, and the pair and background evaluation maps are Borel
off the fixed exceptional set, where the representative is used.
The finite fermion kernels are bounded Borel functions. The
Grassmann exponential is its scalar exponential times a finite
polynomial in its nilpotent part. On the support its coefficients
are bounded by the finite norms of the data.

Define the common vacuum energy by
\[
 E_k(s,\lambda)=E_{t_1}(s)+\lambda\cdot e^\Delta(s)
       +(E_k-E_{t_1})
       +\sum_{t_1<n\le k}\sum_X
                    e_n(X;\mathfrak c_{n-1}(s,\lambda),\lambda).
\]
The inductive representation $\mathsf I^{\rm F}(k)[s,\lambda]$
is the ordinary sourced representation of
\cite[Def.\ 10.11]{QCDM1}, with the following explicit changes:
the action has weight $\beta_k-a_K^{-1}w_\lambda$; the early
regular families are $E^{(j)}(s,\lambda)$; the mass member is
$\mathsf M_h(s,\lambda)$ of \cref{C-422-11}; and all formed
factors, edge terms, and boundary terms begin strictly above
$t_1$. Their kept quadratic halves use the same weight $w_\lambda$.
The label-dependent vacuum constant is
\[
 -\mathcal E_{k,\mathcal S}^{\rm F}(s,\lambda)
 =E_k(s,\lambda)-\sum_{t_1<n\le k}f_n(\mathcal S)
                    +\sum_{t_1<n\le k}g_n(\mathcal S;s,\lambda),
\]
where $f_n$ are the ordinary zero-source label constants and
$|g_n|\le C'_{\mathfrak E}\#_n(\tilde Z_n)$.
All operator, stored-layer, regular-sum, frame, and exponent bounds
are the ordinary bounds with the constants of \cref{C-422-11}.
The real action retains at least the fraction $1-\mathsf a$ of
its zero-source weight. The representation is an equality of
measures coefficient by coefficient, and its exponent is independent
of the evaluation representative outside the fixed null set of the
ordinary coordinate construction.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Induction from the base]\label{C-422-13}
Under the four lag conditions,
$\mathsf I^{\rm F}(k)[s,\lambda]$ holds for every
$t_1\le k\le K$ and $\lambda\in\mathrm P(R_k)$.
The numbers $g_n(\mathcal S;s,\lambda)$ are jointly holomorphic
on the corresponding open source sets and parameter discs.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
At the base, adding $\lambda\cdot\Delta$ changes exactly the
four quantities listed in \cref{C-422-4}. The weight condition
and the ordinary ceiling on $\varrho$ preserve the fraction
$1-\mathsf a$ of the action. The mass bound is \cref{C-422-9},
and the regular and exponent bounds are \cref{C-422-7,C-422-11}.
There are no pieces, stored lower layers, or boundary terms.

For the step, use the ordinary sourced history proof in
\cite[Prop.\ 10.13]{QCDM1}. The gauge coordinates and reference
measures are unchanged. The partial fermion kernel, at the fixed
fine mass matrix of $s$, multiplies the old exponent. Its change
to the new background has the same operator bounds. The frame is
admitted by \cref{C-422-11}; in its interior the expansion is
exactly \cref{C-422-8} at the history coordinates, which belong
to $2\mathscr D'_k$ by \cref{C-422-10}.

Extract the local parts using only pieces within $\Lambda_{k+1}$.
The increment enters the mass through its profile; the omitted
profile part enters the edge terms. The zero-source gauge
coefficient shifts the action, the zero-source energy and the
interior source energies enter the vacuum constant. The explicit
weight $a_K^{-1}A(w_\lambda,\mathsf U)$ is carried plaquette by
plaquette through this same identity.

The measure identity is the sourced change-of-coordinates theorem
\cite[Thm.\ AH]{YMM1}, applied separately to each bounded Borel
coefficient described in \cref{C-422-12}. Its source action is
the one Wilson term at weight $w_\lambda$. The frame and the
old representation supply its other hypotheses, just as in the
cited sourced history proof. The new density is Borel because
all evaluation maps are Borel and every new coefficient is a
continuous function on its pair domain. Joint gauge invariance
of the early and later families, and plaquettewise invariance of
the action, give independence of evaluation representatives.

The numerical bounds now close as follows. The mass and regular
sums are \cref{C-422-10,C-422-11}; new activity and pointed sizes
are \cref{C-422-8}; boundary and edge sizes use the frame recursion
in \cref{C-422-11}. The source-dependent label error consists of
source energies outside $\Lambda_{k+1}$, boundary normalizers,
and the difference between ordinary and history coordinates for
the interior source energies. The first is bounded by the polymer
tail, the third by \cref{C-422-10}, and the boundary normalizers
have the ordinary bound. Their sum is at most
$C'_{\mathfrak E}\#_{k+1}(\tilde Z_{k+1})$.

We also check holomorphy of the boundary normalizers, since they
are needed in the vacuum energy. They depend on the gauge source
only through the Gaussian weight, and on the fermion source only
through its fine mass matrix. They do not depend on the added
activities or mass coordinate. If $\mathsf{bn}(w,J)$ denotes
their value in the ordinary step, then
\[
 \mathsf{bn}(w,J)=\mathsf{bn}(w,0)+\mathsf{bn}(0,J)-\mathsf{bn}(0,0).
\]
The ordinary history identity makes $\mathsf{bn}$ the difference
of its holomorphic label energy and two holomorphic source-energy
sums. Thus it is holomorphic on the interior of $\mathcal P$.
At the new step its value is $\mathsf{bn}(w_\lambda,J)$.
The weight condition puts $(w_\lambda,0)$ in that interior, and
on every open source set under consideration $(0,J)$ is also
in the interior. The displayed splitting proves joint holomorphy.
All other source-energy terms are holomorphic by composition.
This proves the new representation and completes the induction.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Histories with perturbed earlier activities]\label{C-422-14}
Suppose the four lag conditions hold at $s$ and radius $R$.
For every $t_1\le k\le K$ and $\lambda\in\mathrm P(R_k)$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(B1)] There are Borel densities $\mathsf g_h[s,\lambda]$
on the free coordinates, with a common parameter-independent
exceptional set, such that
\[
 \operatorname{Ber}\int\rho_{s,\lambda}
  =\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_k[t_1]}
          \operatorname{Ber}\int\mathsf g_h[s,\lambda]
                                             \,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}.
\]
The sum is absolutely convergent. Every density coefficient is
holomorphic at every free-coordinate point on each product
$S'\times\mathrm P(R_k)$, where $S'$ is an open source set on
which the lag conditions hold at $R$.
\item[(B2)] The representation $\mathsf I^{\rm F}(k)[s,\lambda]$
holds with the ordinary constants. In particular its later frames
have size at most $64b^{\rm tot,s}(\gamma)/51$ and the history
coordinates remain in $2\mathscr D'_k$.
\item[(B3)] For the ordinary mark $\Theta^{(k)}$ and majorant $C$,
\[
 \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_k[t_1]}e^{\Theta^{(k)}(h)}
 e^{-\operatorname{Re}E_k(s,\lambda)}
     \int\|\mathsf g_h[s,\lambda]\|_{h_F}\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}
 \le\Pi_k(C,c'')\le e^{(C+2)n_k},
\]
where $c''=(1-\eth)(c_\star-c_\Theta)/2$.
The modulus of the total mass is consequently at most
$e^{\operatorname{Re}E_k(s,\lambda)+(C+2)n_k}$.
\item[(B3$'$)] For $t_1<t''\le k$, the same sum restricted to
$Z_{t''}(h)\ne\varnothing$ is at most
\[
 e^{-\theta_{\rm tl}p_0(g_{t''})^2}\Pi_k(C,c''_{\rm tl})
 \le e^{-\theta_{\rm tl}p_0(g_{t''})^2+(C+2)n_k}.
\]
For $t''\le t_1$ there are no such histories.
\item[(B4)] The vacuum energy is the one in \cref{C-422-12}.
Its source-energy terms obey
$|e_n(X;s,\lambda)|\le C_{\mathfrak E}e^{-\kappa d_n(X)}$.
The vacuum energy, these terms, and the label errors are jointly
holomorphic on $S'\times\mathrm P(R_k)$, and at $\lambda=0$
they equal their ordinary sourced values.
The total mass $\operatorname{Ber}\int\rho_{s,\lambda}$ is
entire in $\lambda$ for each fixed $s$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Integrate the generators above the base in descending order.
Normalization of each partial block kernel removes it, leaving
\[
 \theta_s^\lambda(U)=\operatorname{Ber}
 \left(G_{s,\lambda}(U)
          T_{h_\emptyset}^{\rm F}[U]
          (e^{-A(\beta-a_K^{-1}w,U)-S_F(U)+\Phi(J)})\right).
\]
This bounded Borel function is the same for every history through
the base. Its invariance under lifts from levels $n\ge t_1$
is the weighted almost-everywhere invariance of
\cref{C-424-18}, proved using the positive base density to
transport the exceptional set. That proof applies to
$\exp(\sum_i\lambda_i\Delta_i)$ because each $\Delta_i$ is
jointly invariant on its domain. It does not assert pointwise
invariance of the arbitrarily extended representative.
\Cref{C-424-19} consequently gives the scalar
mass-preserving history identity for $\theta_s^\lambda$.
The history partition and
\cite[Prop.\ 44.1]{YMM1} then give (B1).

We explain the common exceptional set in this identity. The tests,
backgrounds, coordinate maps, and reference measures have no
parameter dependence. Let $\mathsf N_h^0$ be the Borel null set
outside which every member of the ordinary exponent is evaluated
in its domain. On its complement, the early families are evaluated
in the same fixed pair cores, and the new activities are given on
the larger radius-$\alpha_0$ cores. The boundary outputs and
formed factors use the same filing spaces. Hence the new exponent
is defined there at every parameter and has one value by joint
invariance. Set it to zero on $\mathsf N_h^0$.
The free-coordinate construction takes its Borel pullback and
sets it to zero on the preimage of $\mathsf N_h^0$. This is one
null set for all sources and parameters. The coefficientwise
measure identity in \cref{C-422-13} shows that this function is
a density of the history term.

At each point outside that null set, every coefficient is
holomorphic. The action is affine in $w_\lambda$. The kept and
rejected quadratic halves are linear in that weight: their domains,
localization operators, and shifts are fixed. The store depends
holomorphically on $J$ through the fine mass matrix. The mass and
history coordinates are holomorphic by \cref{C-422-9,C-422-10}.
The new regular families are holomorphic by \cref{C-422-8}; the
early ones are affine in $\lambda$. Boundary and edge terms are
locally uniform limits of products of these frame members and the
localized covariances. Their majorants are independent of the
parameter. The vacuum and boundary numbers are holomorphic by
\cref{C-422-13}. Substitution of the finitely many background legs
preserves holomorphy. Finally an even exponential is its scalar
exponential times the finite exponential of its nilpotent part.
On the exceptional set the chosen function is identically zero.
This proves pointwise holomorphy everywhere.

The ordinary one-history majorant, applied to the representation
just proved, is
\begin{align*}
 &e^{-\operatorname{Re}E_k(s,\lambda)+\sum_n\operatorname{Re}f_n(\mathcal S)}
      \int\|\mathsf g_h[s,\lambda]\|_{h_F}\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}\\
 &\quad\le e^{C'_{\mathfrak E}\sum_n\#_n(\tilde Z_n)}
    e^{\mathsf C_{\rm maj}(n_k+\sum_{j\le k}\#_j(Z_j))}
       \prod_t e^{-(1-\mathsf a)c_\star p_0(g_t)^2
                                            \mathsf n_t^{\rm cr}(h)}.
\end{align*}
All its inputs are the bounds in \cref{C-422-11,C-422-13}.
Set the corresponding nonnegative function of histories to zero
outside $\mathcal H_k[t_1]$. It satisfies the ordinary summation
hypothesis with creation rate
$c_{\mathsf a}=(c_\star+c_\Theta)/2$ and boundary constant
$C_\flat^F+C'_{\mathfrak E}$.
Apply \cite[Prop.\ 67.6(f)]{YMM1} with the ordinary dials.
This proves (B3), integrability, and absolute convergence in (B1),
using $|\operatorname{Ber}F|\le\|F\|_{h_F}$ and $h_F\ge1$.

For the tail, multiply this function by
$\exp[\theta_{\rm tl}\sum_tp_0(g_t)^2\mathsf n_t^{\rm cr}(h)]$.
Its remaining creation rate is
$c_{\rm tl}=c_{\mathsf a}-\theta_{\rm tl}$.
If $Z_{t''}\ne\varnothing$, some creation occurred by level
$t''$, and monotonicity gives
$\sum_tp_0(g_t)^2\mathsf n_t^{\rm cr}(h)\ge p_0(g_{t''})^2$.
The same mark is represented by the new dials because
$\mathsf w_{\rm tl}c_{\rm tl}=c_\Theta$.
Its deposit rate equals the available creation rate, as required
by the summation theorem. The extra ceiling in \cref{C-422-16}
therefore gives the sum at rate
$(1-\eth)(c_{\rm tl}-c_\Theta)=c''_{\rm tl}$.
Removing the multiplying factor proves (B3$'$).

The vacuum statement follows from its displayed finite sum and
the already established holomorphy. At fixed source the original
base density times $e^{\lambda\cdot\Delta}$ is entire in
$\lambda$ and bounded on compact parameter sets by the finite
norms of the data on its support. Its integral is therefore entire.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Differences of two flows]\label{C-422-15}
The format is closed under differences. If another activity has
data $(F'_j,G'_j,\nu'_j)$ and reference $G_j'{}^\infty$, its
difference from the ordinary activity, after subtracting scalar
values at the trivial pair, has data
\[
 (F'_j-F_j,G'_j-G_j,\nu'_j-\mu_j),\qquad
                         G_j'{}^\infty-G_j^\infty.
\]
The scalar values are collected in $e^\Delta$. The four entries
of $r^\psi$ must all be estimated, including the reference and
its infinite-lattice family. When the second flow has no activity
at $j$, these data are $(-F_j,-G_j,-\mu_j)$ and $-G_j^\infty$.
Several interpolating directions are allowed by summing their
sizes before imposing \eqref{eq:free-family-lags}.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Application to the restarted flow]\label{C-422-17}
Use the data, formats, and lag estimates of \cref{C-418-4} at
a base $t_0<t_b\le t_1$ and $\Lambda_b\ge1$. Suppose the
scalar difference $d_b(s)$ is a single number $d_b$ on
$\mathcal P$. Let $S_b\supset\mathcal P$ be the open set in
its free-family hypothesis. Set
\[
 S=S_b\cap\mathscr O_{t_b},\qquad R=c_\lambda\Lambda_b,
 \qquad
 \rho_b=\tfrac12(3\sqrt L)^{-(K-t_b)}R.
\]
Apply the preceding construction with base $t_b$, one parameter,
and data
\[
 w^\Delta=\hat w_b,\qquad
 \sigma^\Delta(s)=-\delta_{t_b}(s),\qquad
 \Delta_1^{(j)}(s)=-\Delta^{(j)}(s),\qquad e^\Delta=d_b.
\]
Then its base density is exactly $\rho^{(t_b)}_{s,\lambda}$ of
\cref{C-418-4}. At every source with
$\|w\|_\sharp\le(2-c_\lambda)\varrho$, the four lag conditions
hold at radius $R$, and $\rho_b\le R_K/2<R_K$.
Consequently the history representation and all four bounds of
\cref{C-422-14} hold at every level $t_b\le k\le K$ throughout
the parameter set $\mathcal D_b$ of \cref{C-418-17}.

The history terms are the same measures as the restarted terms
defined from the block field in \cref{C-418-4}. Their densities
agree almost everywhere, coefficient by coefficient, with the
entire-in-$\lambda$ representatives of \cref{C-424-22} wherever
both constructions are defined. For every Borel set $E$, the
integral over $E$ of each coefficient is holomorphic on the
interior of $\mathcal D_b$.
In particular \cref{C-418-17} holds with the explicit $c_\lambda$
of \cref{C-422-16}.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
The negative differences are free families by \cref{C-422-15},
with the same sizes. Their scalar parts have been centered at the
trivial pair, as required. The gauge difference
$\hat w_b=L^{-(K-t_b)}(x_{t_b}-\hat x_{t_b})$ is a real constant,
so $\|w^\Delta\|_\sharp=|\hat w_b|$.

We check holomorphy of the mass field on $S$. The ordinary chain
is holomorphic on $\mathscr O_{t_b}$. The restarted chain is
\[
 \hat\sigma_{t_b}(s)(x)
  =L^{t_b-t_0}\hat\sigma_{t_0}(s)(x)
     +\sum_{t_0<j\le t_b}L^{t_b-j}
                              (\hat\nu_j-\hat\mu_j)(y_j(x)),
\]
where
\[
 \hat\sigma_{t_0}(s)(x)
  =\frac{F^{\rm UV}}{L^{K-t_0}(\mathsf b-w(x))}
      -\frac{F^{\rm UV}}{L^{K-t_0}\mathsf b}.
\]
The denominators do not vanish on $\mathscr O_{t_b}$, since
$\|w\|_\infty<4\varrho<\mathsf b$.
Each later increment is the fixed linear moment extraction from
$\hat F_j(s)$ and $\hat G_j$. The first is holomorphic because
$\hat F_j=F_j-(F_j-\hat F_j)$ and the difference hypothesis
provides the second term on $S_b$; the reference is constant.
The background walk coefficients in these moments are holomorphic
in $\mathsf n=-a_KJ$ and have locally uniform absolute sums,
with the admitted factor $e^{-1/2}$ per walk step. Thus the
increments, restarted chain, and $\delta_{t_b}$ are holomorphic.

The difference-of-exponents identity in \cref{C-418-4} reads
\[
 a_K^{-1}A(\hat w_b,\mathsf U)
 +L^{-t_b}\mathsf S_1(\delta_{t_b}\psi^{\rm bg})
 -\sum_{j\le t_b}\sum_X\Delta^{(j)}(X)+d_b
                      =\hat\Phi_s^{(t_b)}-\Phi_s^{(t_b)}.
\]
Multiplying the ordinary base density by its exponential with
coefficient $\lambda$ proves the claimed base identification.

The hypotheses on the difference sizes give
\begin{align*}
 R\Sigma_k^\psi&\le c_\lambda C_w^{\rm s}\phi_k
           \le2\sqrt L c_\lambda C_w^{\rm s}\phi_{k-1}
           \le c_\psi^\Delta\phi_{k-1},\\
 R\Sigma_{t_b}^0&\le c_\lambda E_0^{\rm s}\le c_0^\Delta,\\
 R\|\sigma^\Delta\|&\le c_\lambda B_\sigma\phi_{t_b}
                                      \le B_\sigma\phi_{t_b}/2,\\
 \|w\|_\sharp+R|\hat w_b|
     &\le(2-c_\lambda)\varrho+c_\lambda\varrho=2\varrho.
\end{align*}
Also $Q_\sigma\le3\sqrt L$, so $\rho_b\le R_K/2$.
Every point of $\mathcal D_b$ therefore belongs to the domains
of the all-level theorem. Its interior lies in
\[
 \{\|w\|_\sharp<(2-c_\lambda)\varrho,
                         \|J\|_\infty<2\varrho_J\}
                                  \times\mathrm P(R_K).
\]

To identify the history measures, put $\xi=\mathcal M^{t_b}$.
The factorization in \cref{C-424-34} gives
\[
 \mathfrak w_h=\mathfrak w_{h_\emptyset}
                              (\mathfrak w_h^\circ\circ\xi),\qquad
 T_{h,>t_b}^{\rm F}[U]=T_h^\circ[\xi(U)],\qquad
 \mathsf v_h=\mathsf v_h^\circ\circ\xi.
\]
Apply this identity coefficientwise to the base measure before
its pushforward under $\xi$. The image of the base density under
the block-field steps is precisely the image of
$\mathfrak w_hT_h^{{\rm F},\lambda}\,dU$ under $\mathsf v_h$.
This is the term defined in \cref{C-422-12}.
Two integrable Borel densities of the same coefficient measure
agree almost everywhere. For example their real difference has
integral zero on its positive and negative sets, so vanishes
almost everywhere; do the same for its imaginary part. Their
integrals, Berezin integrals, and integrals of the fibre norm
therefore agree.

For integrated holomorphy, the pointwise holomorphic density in
\cref{C-422-14} obeys, for every coefficient $I$,
\[
 \int_E|\mathsf g_{h,I}[s,\lambda]|\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}
 \le c_h^{\rm Gr}
          e^{\operatorname{Re}E_k(s,\lambda)+(C+2)n_k}.
\]
On a closed polydisc in any finite-dimensional affine parameter
family inside $\mathcal D_b$, the right side is bounded.
The coefficient is jointly Borel and pointwise holomorphic.
Its Cauchy formula can thus be integrated over $E$ by Fubini,
giving the Cauchy formula for the integral. This proves holomorphy
on each such family, and local boundedness gives the asserted
source holomorphy.

Finally the ordinary bounds in \cref{C-418-17} follow directly
at each level. Because $\hat w_b$ is constant,
$\tau_k(w_\lambda;\alpha_0)=\tau_k(w;\alpha_0)$.
The early scalar excess obeys
\[
 |\lambda|\sum_{j\le t_b}L^{-(n-j)}r_j^0
 \le\tfrac12c_\lambda E_0^{\rm s}\le M^{-3}\mathsf B,
\]
and the corresponding fermion excess is at most
$c_\psi^\Delta\phi_{n-1}/2$. Hence all regular and stored-layer
bounds hold with the stated constants at every level.
At $k=K$, $n_K=\ell^3$ and $\Theta^{(K)}\ge0$ give the total
mass bound. The vacuum identity is
\[
 E_k(s,\lambda)=E_{t_b}(s)+\lambda d_b
     +\sum_{t_b<j\le k}\left[e_jn_j+\sum_Xe_j(X;s,\lambda)\right].
\]
The tail bound at level $t>t_b$ is
\[
 \sum_{h:Z_t(h)\ne\varnothing}
         \int\|\mathsf g_h[s,\lambda]\|_{h_F}\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}
 \le e^{-\theta_{\rm tl}p_0(g_t)^2}
                e^{\operatorname{Re}E_K(s,\lambda)+(C+2)\ell^3}.
\]
These are the remaining clauses of \cref{C-418-17}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Large fields after a prescribed past}\label{C-423-1}

We next allow the activities before a level $t_1$ to be prescribed.
Their individual sizes need not satisfy the induction bounds.
What the later steps require are two sums: the scalar terms are
weighted by $L^{-(k-j)}$, and the terms with fermion legs by
$L^{(k+1-j)/4}$. We prove the induction with these sums as hypotheses.
All histories considered here have no large-field region through
level $t_1$.

Fix the chamber model with $r=1/2$, $N_f\ge1$, and the constants
of \cite[Prop.\ 10.20]{QCDM1}. The datum, calibrations
$\mathsf t_i=L^{K-i}\mathsf b$, tests, tower and background maps
remain fixed. The two geometric conditions of the history induction
in \cite[Prop.\ 9.14]{QCDM1} are assumed. Coefficients of the
action introduced below are real. The gauge step uses such a
coefficient $x'_k$ through
$\tau=x'_k/\mathsf t_k$ and
$|\tau-1|\le\bar B/\mathsf t_k$; its Gaussian and normalization
are those of \cite[Lem.\ 9.4]{QCDM1}.

\begin{definition}[A prescribed past]\label{C-423-2}
Let $1\le t_1<K$ and
\[
 \mathcal H_k^{[t_1]}
 =\{h\in\mathcal H_k:h|_{t_1}=h_\emptyset^{(t_1)}\},
 \qquad t_1\le k\le K.
\]
A free family $F^{(j)}$ is a pointed family on the infinite lattice
and on the torus with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(F1)] Its members are even polynomials in the formal background
generators of levels $\le j$ on their polymer. They are holomorphic
functions of the regular pair on the whole core at
$(\alpha_0,\alpha_1)$, jointly gauge invariant, invariant under
$\mathrm U(N_f)\times\mathrm U(N_f)$, and Borel in the real data.
They depend on no history or label.
\item[(F2)] On the infinite lattice the pointed terms commute with
translations by $M\mathbb Z^3$ in level-$j$ units. On a polymer
that does not wrap around the torus, its torus family is the part
of the infinite-lattice family that fits in the chart, with the
pointers carried by that chart.
\item[(F3)] On the infinite lattice, at the trivial configuration, substitute
$\Psi_n^{\rm bg}=\mathsf H_{n,j}\Phi$ and write the degree-two
part of $\sum_{X\ni z}F^{(j)}(X;z)$ as
$\sum_{y,y'}\bar\Phi(y)K_z(y,y')\Phi(y')$.
Then $q_j(z)=\sum_{y,y'}K_z(y,y')$ commutes with colour,
is periodic under $M\mathbb Z^3$, and
$\sum_{z\in c}q_j(z)=0$ for every cell $c$.
\item[(F4)] The scalar parts form a pointed scalar family on the
same cores and are Borel there.
\end{enumerate}
With $h^{(j)}(n)=C_HL^{-(j-n)}h_F$, define
\begin{align*}
 \epsilon_j^\psi(F)&=\max\sup_\square
   \sum_{X\supset\square}e^{\kappa d_j(X)}
       \sum_z\sup_P\|F_{\ge2}^{(j)}(X;P;z)\|_{h^{(j)}},\\
 \mathsf g_j(F)&=\max\sup_{X,z}
       e^{(\kappa+1)d_j(X)}\sup_P|F_0^{(j)}(X;P;z)|.
\end{align*}
Here the maximum is over the two lattices and $P$ ranges over
the whole open core. A free past $\mathcal F$ at $t_1$ consists
of such families for $1\le j\le t_1$, with finite sizes. Set
\[
 \Lambda_k^\psi(\mathcal F)=\sum_{j\le t_1}
       L^{(k+1-j)/4}\epsilon_j^\psi(F),\qquad
 \Lambda_k^0(\mathcal F)=\sum_{j\le t_1}
       L^{-(k-j)}\mathsf g_j(F).
\]
Thus $\Lambda_k^\psi=L^{(k-t_1)/4}\Lambda_{t_1}^\psi$
and $\Lambda_k^0=L^{-(k-t_1)}\Lambda_{t_1}^0$.

An exponent with this past at $h\in\mathcal H_k^{[t_1]}$
has the history form of \cite[Prop.\ 9.14]{QCDM1}, with
\[
 \beta'_h=L^{t_1}x'_{t_1}
       -\sum_{t_1<j\le k}L^jb'_j\varphi_j,
 \qquad
 s'_h=L^{-t_1}\sigma+\sum_{t_1<j\le k}L^{-j}\mu'_j\varphi_j,
\]
where $x'_i>1$, $|x'_i-\mathsf t_i|\le\bar B$,
$b'_j=L^{-1}x'_{j-1}-x'_j$ is real with $|b'_j|\le B_\sharp$,
and $\sigma,\mu'_j$ may be complex. Its regular sum is
\[
 \mathfrak f'+\sum_{j\le k}\sum_{(z,X)\in\mathsf{Ix}^{\rm rs}_j}
        [F^{(j)}(X;\mathsf U,\bar\Psi^{\rm bg},\Psi^{\rm bg};z)
                                      -F^{(j)}_0(X;\mathbf1;z)].
\]
For $j\le t_1$ use $\mathcal F$; for $j>t_1$ use free families.
The stored quadratic form is the unchanged tower form.
The boundary sum has levels $t_1<j\le k$ only. Its generated
terms are the four kinds of \cite[Prop.\ 9.13]{QCDM1}, with
their strip rows. Their bounds use the size
$\mathsf{sz}_{j-1}^\natural$ of the frame that generated them.
The edge terms are sums of pointed activities outside
$\Lambda_j^{\sim-1}$, with their plaquette shares removed,
together with the action and mass parts left by $1-\varphi_j$.
Their bounds use $\mathsf g_j(F)$, $|b'_j|$, $|\mu'_j|$ and
the insertion size $\bar v_j$, as specified in
\cref{C-423-11}. Their remainders after removing the action
parts obey those bounds on the whole core. A complex vacuum
constant completes the exponent.
\end{definition}

The norm $\epsilon_j^\psi$ bounds every partial sum of pointed
terms on a polymer, including sums with shares of modulus at
most one. Taking the supremum before summing pointers is needed
when different pointers are evaluated at different pairs.
Conditions (F2)--(F3) give the zero cell moment used in
\cite[Lem.\ 7.9]{QCDM1}: translation of each pointer to a fixed
cell preserves its moment and its filing, and the resulting
absolutely convergent sum is $\sum_{z\in c}q_j(z)=0$.
The ordinary activities are free families; their pointed sizes
are finite by \cite[Lem.\ 8.8]{QCDM1}.

\begin{lemma}[Geometry before the first large field]\label{C-423-3}
For $h\in\mathcal H_k^{[t_1]}$, the regions of levels
$j\le t_1$ are the torus and $\varphi_j=1$ there. Every pair
at those levels is regular; their edge and generated-boundary
index sets are empty. Stored layers $\mathcal L_m$ with
$m<t_1$, and pieces and created cells of steps $t\le t_1$,
are absent. Restriction to a level $\ge t_1$ and extension by
one outcome preserve this class of histories. The extracted
vacuum differences $f_n(\mathcal S)$ vanish for $n\le t_1$.
Moreover
\begin{align*}
 \beta'_h&=L^kx'_k+\sum_{t_1<j\le k}L^jb'_j(1-\varphi_j),\\
 w'(\mathsf p)&=\sum_{t_1<j\le k}L^{j-k}b'_j
                \mathbf1\{X(\mathsf p;j)\not\subset\Lambda_j\},
 \qquad |w'|\le\bar B.
\end{align*}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The first $j$ outcomes determine every region at level $j$.
For $j\le t_1$ these outcomes are those of the empty history.
An edge or generated boundary requires a polymer or pointer
outside its region, so none occurs there. Also
$\mathcal L_m=\Omega_m\setminus\Omega_{m+1}$, and pieces
and created cells lie in the new large-field region.
The two histories defining $f_n$ agree through level $n\le t_1$.
Finally telescope
$L^jb'_j=L^{j-1}x'_{j-1}-L^jx'_j$ and use
$\sum_{i\ge0}L^{-i}=L/(L-1)$ and
$\bar B=B_\sharp L/(L-1)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The measure with a prescribed past]\label{C-423-4}
Let $A_{t_1}$ be the ordinary exponent on the empty history and
let $A^{[\mathcal F]}_{t_1}$ be the exponent of
\cref{C-423-2} with initial mass $\sigma$, initial coefficient
$x'_{t_1}$, no boundary sum, $\mathfrak f'=0$, and constant $c$.
Use the fixed exceptional set $\mathsf N_0$ and Borel
representative construction of \cref{C-424-7}.
When $\xi_{t_1}(U)\in\mathsf S_\emptyset\setminus\mathsf N_0$,
define
\[
 R_{\mathcal F}(U)
   =\exp[(A^{[\mathcal F]}_{t_1}-A_{t_1})(\xi_{t_1}(U))],
\]
and give it the value one elsewhere. For
$h\in\mathcal H_k^{[t_1]}$ put
\[
 \varsigma_h^{\mathcal F}(U)
 =e^{-\beta A(U)}T^{\rm F}_{h/t_1}[U]
   \bigl(R_{\mathcal F}(U)T^{\rm F}_{h_\emptyset^{(t_1)}}[U]
                                         e^{-S_F(U)}\bigr).
\]
Each coefficient is bounded and Borel. Let
$\check\tau_h^{[\mathcal F]}$ be the history measure with
these coefficients and $\hat\tau_h^{[\mathcal F]}$ its
coordinate image. Then
\[
 \hat\tau_{h_\emptyset^{(t_1)}}^{[\mathcal F]}
 =\mathsf{Stay}\,\mathbf1^{\rm T}\chi_{t_1}(T_\ell)
       e^{\boldsymbol\Phi}e^{A^{[\mathcal F]}_{t_1}}\mathscr M.
\]
Its exponent has one value at the evaluation configurations
off one null set. For every coefficient $I$ and Borel set $E$,
\[
 |\check\tau_h[\varsigma_{h,I}^{\mathcal F}]|(E)
 \le\frac{\sup|\varsigma_{h,I}^{\mathcal F}|}
             {\min e^{-\beta A}}\check\tau_h(E),
\]
where $\check\tau_h$ is the positive pure-gauge history term.
The exact one-step pushforward identity holds with
$T^{\rm F}_{\mathsf o}$ applied to the density.

If the past, $\sigma$ and $c$ depend holomorphically on a
parameter, with sizes locally bounded, so do all coefficient
functions, locally uniformly in $U$. These conclusions also
hold at an admitted source $(w,J)$, using the same
$R_{\mathcal F}$: the base exponent is then
$A_{t_1}[w,J]+A^{[\mathcal F]}_{t_1}-A_{t_1}$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Outside the fixed exceptional set, every evaluation pair lies in the core at half
the radii. A background leg of level $n\le j\le t_1$ has
column sum at most $C_HL^{-(t_1-n)}$, so its cost at weight
$h_F$ is no larger than $h^{(j)}(n)$. The torus regular sums
and mass term are finite, and the action difference is a bounded
continuous function on the compact link space. Thus
$\sup\|A^{[\mathcal F]}_{t_1}-A_{t_1}\|<\infty$ and
$\|R_{\mathcal F}\|\le\exp(\sup\|A^{[\mathcal F]}_{t_1}-A_{t_1}\|)$.
The coordinate maps and all members are Borel on that set,
and the extension is Borel and bounded. Each partial
Berezin integral is a finite sum of products of bounded Borel
coefficients, which proves the first assertion.

At the base, multiplication by $R_{\mathcal F}$ is multiplication
by a bounded function of the coordinates. Pushforward commutes
with this operation. The even exponents commute, so their
product is $e^{A^{[\mathcal F]}_{t_1}}$. Two evaluation
configurations differ by a gauge transformation fixing the
stored data; joint invariance makes the extra factor the same
at both. The positivity and domination argument in
\cite[Lem.\ 10.7 and its proof]{QCDM1} applies coefficient by
coefficient: $\min e^{-\beta A}>0$, and the pure term supplies
the positive reference measure. In particular every density
obtained in coordinates is integrable in the fibre norm, since
its weighted coefficient variations are finite.

For an extension $(h,\mathsf o)$, the new weight is the old
weight times the step tests and gauge-fixing factor; the new
coordinates are the step map of the old coordinates; and
$T^{\rm F}_{(h,\mathsf o)/t_1}=T^{\rm F}_{\mathsf o}T^{\rm F}_{h/t_1}$.
These facts prove the step identity by pushforward and finite
Berezin integration. For a holomorphic parameter the finite
base sum and its exponential are holomorphic and locally
bounded; subsequent kernels are linear. At a source the bare
scalar density remains continuous and bounded on the compact
link space and the Grassmann coefficients remain bounded.
The sourced base identity follows from
\cite[Prop.\ 10.13]{QCDM1}, with the same multiplication by
$R_{\mathcal F}$. For the ordinary past, $\sigma=s_{t_1}$ and
$c=E_{t_1}+\mathfrak f_{t_1}$, this factor is one on the support
and the original term is recovered.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The contribution of one earlier level}

Put $\delta_k=\delta(\mathsf t_k)$ and
$s_a=c_h\delta_k/a_{\rm an}$. We use the constants in the
proof of \cite[Prop.\ 9.14]{QCDM1} and set
\begin{align*}
 \Theta'_k&=4Lc_\psi+\frac{2C_{\mathcal A}\delta_k}{\beta_0}
