       [9L^4A_\kappa C_H+(2+6L^5A_\kappa)C_{\mathfrak r}\beta_0],\\
 \Theta_k&=c_\psi+C_{\mathcal A}s_a
                         +C_GC_{\mathcal A}\delta_k+\Theta'_k,\\
 \Theta_\circ^{\rm B}&=1+9L^4A_\kappa C_H
                          +(2+6L^5A_\kappa)C_{\mathfrak r}\beta_0,\\
 \Theta_k^{\rm B}&=\frac{2C_{\mathcal A}\delta_k}{\beta_0}
                                      \Theta_\circ^{\rm B},
 \qquad \Theta_k^\sharp=\Theta_k+\Theta_k^{\rm B},\\
 \varkappa_n&=\omega_{n+1}+\frac{12}{11}C_{\rm lay}L^{n/4}
       +C_\omega(c_{\rm rim}+c_{\rm rim}^{\rm pt})
       +c_{\rm geo}+39(1+2\mathsf n_{\rm wk}),\\
 C_{\rm tab}&=C_\omega(1+c_{\rm rim}+c_{\rm rim}^{\rm pt})
       +\frac{12}{11}C_{\rm lay}+c_{\rm geo}
                                  +39(1+2\mathsf n_{\rm wk}).
\end{align*}
Here $\omega_n=C_\omega L^{n/4}$,
$c_{\rm geo}=9\mathsf n_{\rm wk}^2$, and
$\varkappa_n\le C_{\rm tab}L^{(n+1)/4}$.

We retain the following division of the fermion terms in a step.
(B1)--(B2) are the changes with the gauge fluctuation, including
its collar; (B3) is the current mass term; (B4) consists of regular
activities filed in current cells; (B5)--(B6) are their stored-layer
parts and the stored mass term; (B7) contains the mass parts of
edges; and (B8)--(B10) contain the generated boundary terms and
the remaining edges. This is the division used in the proof of
\cite[Prop.\ 9.14]{QCDM1}.

\begin{proposition}[The lag kernels]\label{C-423-5}
Let $t_1\le k<K$, $h\in\mathcal H_k^{[t_1]}$, and
$h'=(h,\mathsf o)$. Form the step from an exponent of
\cref{C-423-2}. All bounds below are per level-$k$ cube on
the admitted tiers, in the summed norm of rate $\kappa-1$
or the polymer norm of rate at least $r_V$, with the step's
external and integrated weights. For $j\le k$ put
$n=k-j$ and $\epsilon_j^\psi=\epsilon_j^\psi(F)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] The activity contributions to (B1), (B2), and
(B4)--(B6) are complex linear in each $F_{\ge2}^{(j)}$.
The level-$j$ contributions satisfy
\begin{align*}
 \mathrm{(B4)}_j&\le
   \Theta_k(\omega_{n+1}+C_\omega c_{\rm rim})\epsilon_j^\psi,\\
 \mathrm{(B5+B6)}_j&\le
   [\tfrac{12}{11}C_{\rm lay}L^{n/4}\Theta'_k
    +(C_\omega c_{\rm rim}^{\rm pt}+c_{\rm geo}
           +39(1+2\mathsf n_{\rm wk}))\Theta_k]\epsilon_j^\psi,\\
 \mathrm{(B1)}_j,\mathrm{(B2)}_j&\le
                         \Theta_k^{\rm B}\varkappa_n\epsilon_j^\psi.
\end{align*}
Their sum is at most
$2\Theta_k^\sharp C_{\rm tab}L^{(k+1-j)/4}\epsilon_j^\psi$.
The levels $j\le t_1$ therefore contribute at most
$2\Theta_k^\sharp C_{\rm tab}\Lambda_k^\psi(\mathcal F)$.
\item[(ii)] On one lattice, or on an interior polymer of a history,
the fermion potential and the insertion size $\bar v_{k+1}$
are bounded by
\begin{align*}
 C_Vh_F^2C_{\mathcal A}\delta_k
 &+(c_\psi+C_GC_{\mathcal A}\delta_k)c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2|s'_k|\\
 &+(c_\psi+C_{\mathcal A}s_a+C_GC_{\mathcal A}\delta_k)
          \sum_{j\le k}\omega_{k+1-j}\|F_{\ge2}^{(j)}\|_j,
\end{align*}
where $s'_k=L^{k-t_1}\sigma+\sum_{t_1<j\le k}L^{k-j}\mu'_j$.
On a torus take the larger of the two activity norms in this
sum. Its early part is at most $C_\omega\Lambda_k^\psi$.
\item[(iii)] Put
$\Sigma_k^{[t_1]}=\sup_{t_1\le j<k}\mathsf{sz}_j^\natural$
and $\bar v_*^{[t_1]}=\sup_{t_1<j\le k}\bar v_j$, with
empty suprema zero. Terms (B8)--(B9) are bounded by
\[
 C_{\rm bd}K_M(1+\bar\eta)
 (c_\psi+2C_{\mathcal A}\delta_k/\beta_0)
                    \max\{\Sigma_k^{[t_1]},\bar v_*^{[t_1]}\},
\]
and (B10) by
\[
 C^{\rm bd}\vartheta_{0,k}
       [\tfrac98K^{\rm lb}\Sigma_k^{[t_1]}
                                  +108M^3K_M\bar v_*^{[t_1]}].
\]
All (B7)--(B10) vanish at $k=t_1$.
\item[(iv)] Terms involving the mass coefficients alone obey
\begin{align*}
 \mathrm{(B3)}&\le(c_\psi+C_GC_{\mathcal A}\delta_k)
                                      c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2|s'_k|,\\
 \mathrm{(B6)}_{\rm mass}&\le\frac L{L-2}C_{\rm lay}\Theta'_k
          w_0\nu C_H^2h_F^2
          \max_{t_1\le m\le k}\max\{|s'_m|,L|s'_{m-1}|\},\\
 \mathrm{(B7)}&\le C_{\rm bd}
       (c_\psi+2C_{\mathcal A}\delta_k/\beta_0)
           M^3w_0\nu C_H^2h_F^2\max_{t_1<j\le k}|\mu'_j|.
\end{align*}
The entry $s'_{m-1}$ occurs only for $m>t_1$. The gauge
variation of the current and stored mass terms has the same
current and stored counts, with factor $\Theta_k^{\rm B}$;
both integrated and collar variations have this bound.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The operations before the cluster expansion are substitution,
filing, taking differences, and extracting specified legs. Each
is linear in an activity. A split leg costs its largest ratio
to the original weight. For a current leg this ratio is
$c_\psi L^{-(k-j)}$; in a layer $\mathcal L_m$ it is
$4Lc_\psi(2L^{-4})^{k-m}$. The gauge response adds the two
ratios
\[
 \frac{2C_{\mathcal A}\delta_k}{\beta_0}
  8L^4A_\kappa C_H(2L^{-4})^{k-m},\qquad
 \frac{2C_{\mathcal A}\delta_k}{\beta_0}
  6L^5A_\kappa C_{\mathfrak r}\beta_0(2L^{-4})^{k-m}.
\]
Cauchy's estimate for an old coefficient adds
$(2C_{\mathcal A}\delta_k/\beta_0)
 L^{-(k+1-m)}L^{-4(k-m)}$ when its bond places lie below
level $m$. It is valid on the shifted core by the domain
calculation in \cite[Prop.\ 9.14, proof]{QCDM1}; (F1)
supplies holomorphy and the norm on that whole core.

For (B4), the difference terms at lags at least $n_{\rm lag}$
and the direct count at smaller lags are exactly the old-activity
estimate \cite[Lem.\ 7.9]{QCDM1}. Its hypotheses are (F1)--(F3)
and the norm; its bound at level $j$ is
$\Theta_k\omega_{n+1}\epsilon_j^\psi$. The zero moment used
there is the cell sum in (F3). On a torus the wrapping and
nonfitting pieces are retained as in that lemma. At levels
$j\le t_1$ every piece is regular, so the history leaves no
additional zero moment. Pieces taken whole near a rim have
the bounds
\begin{gather*}
 C_\omega c_{\rm geo}(L^{3n+2}+L^n)
       e^{-\kappa(1-L^{-1})(8L^{n+1}-2)}\epsilon_j^\psi,\\
 C_\omega c_{\rm geo}(L^{n+2}+L^n)
       e^{-\kappa(1-L^{-1})(8L^n-2)}\epsilon_j^\psi,
\end{gather*}
and the degree-four remainder has
$c_{\rm geo}L^{3n}e^{-\kappa(1-L^{-1})(8L^n-2)}\epsilon_j^\psi$.
These use respectively $L^{-3},L^{-2},L^{-2}$ of the
defining rim sum. Their sum is below
$C_\omega c_{\rm rim}\epsilon_j^\psi$, since
$L^{-3}+2L^{-2}<1$. Multiplying by $\Theta_k$ proves (B4).

For stored layers, before inserting any closed size, the proof
of \cite[Prop.\ 9.14]{QCDM1} gives the following counts.
Whole pointed totals at short lags cost
\[
 4.3(1+2\mathsf n_{\rm wk})L^{3(m'-j)}(2/L)^{k-m'}
                                     \Theta'_k\epsilon_j^\psi.
\]
Long-lag differences cost
$5C_\omega c_{\rm geo}(2A_\kappa C_H)^2
L^{12+3/4}L^{(m-j)/4}(2/L)^{k-m}\Theta'_k\epsilon_j^\psi$.
The regular stored-layer count and the cell-moment count have
the same $L^{(m-j)/4}$ factor. The latter uses
$\|q_j(z)\|_{\rm tr}\le C'^2h_F^{-2}\epsilon_j^\psi$,
the coefficient estimate \cite[Lem.\ 7.8]{QCDM1} applied
pointer by pointer, and $\sum_{z\in c}q_j(z)=0$.
Degree at least four on
$X\subset\Omega_{m-1}\setminus\Omega_{m+2}$ costs
$2(1+4\mathsf n_{\rm wk})L^8L^{-(m-j)}(2/L)^{k-m}
\Theta'_k\epsilon_j^\psi$.
These four groups are covered by the four shares defining
$C_{\rm lay}$. Summing layers gives
\[
 \sum_{m=j}^k L^{(m-j)/4}(2/L)^{k-m}
 \le\frac{L^{n/4}}{1-2L^{-5/4}}
 \le\frac{12}{11}L^{n/4}.
\]

The remaining degree-four polymers span at least
$8L^{m-j}-2$, and also $8L^{m'-j}-2$ if a split leg reaches
$m'\ge m+2$. Their layer count is bounded by
\[
 \sum_{d\ge1}2(d+2)L^{3(d+1)}
             e^{-\kappa(1-L^{-1})(8L^d-2)}\le1,
\]
under $L\ge13$ and $\kappa\ge\log9216$. They cost
$c_{\rm geo}\Theta_k\epsilon_j^\psi$.
Wrapping remainders and whole pointed terms have total cost
at most
\[
 3C_\omega c_{\rm geo}(1+L^2)
 \left(1+\sum_{d\ge1}L^{3d}
                e^{-\kappa(1-L^{-1})(7L^d-2)}\right)
                  \Theta_k\epsilon_j^\psi
 \le C_\omega c_{\rm rim}^{\rm pt}\Theta_k\epsilon_j^\psi.
\]
Here $\sum_{e\ge0}(2L^{-4})^e\le1.0001$ pays repeated
stored layers. Boundary shares add
$39(1+2\mathsf n_{\rm wk})\Theta_k\epsilon_j^\psi$.
All pointer counts use the sum of the separate pointed norms;
partial sums with shares are bounded by the same norm.
This proves the stated (B5)--(B6) estimate.

For (B1)--(B2), replace the old configuration by the new one.
The difference of an activity is linear in it. Cauchy's
estimate contributes $2|B|_Y/\beta_0$; the change of a stored
leg contributes the two response ratios already displayed and
$(2|B|_Y/\beta_0)(3C_{\mathfrak r}\beta_0/2)
(2L^{-4})^{k-m}$. Current legs contribute
$C_G|B|_Y$ and $c_h|B|_Y/a_{\rm an}$, each at most one
quarter of $2|B|_Y/\beta_0$. These factors sum to at most
$(2|B|_Y/\beta_0)\Theta_\circ^{\rm B}
(2L^{-4})^{(k-m)_+}$. The same counts therefore give
$\Theta_k^{\rm B}\varkappa_n\epsilon_j^\psi$ on the tiers,
also for the collar. Adding the three groups proves (i).

The one-lattice estimate is the same substitution estimate
before filing across a boundary. Its three terms are the
vertex, the mass term and the old activities. The original
argument uses only (F1)--(F3), the two-lattice compatibility,
and the real admitted ratio $\tau$; hence it applies with
their actual finite norms. An insertion at specified places
has norm at most the fermion potential, proving (ii).

Boundary terms occur only above $t_1$. Their old reentry
estimate \cite[Prop.\ 9.13, proof]{QCDM1} therefore uses
$\Sigma_k^{[t_1]}$ and $\bar v_*^{[t_1]}$ and gives (iii).
In a stored layer,
\[
 L^ms'_h=(1-\varphi_m)Ls'_{m-1}+\varphi_ms'_m
 \quad(m>t_1),\qquad L^{t_1}s'_h=\sigma.
\]
Thus its modulus is bounded by the maximum in (iv). The
layer sum is $\sum_{m\le k}(2/L)^{k-m}\le L/(L-2)$.
At a rim pointer the mass part retained in the activity and
the part left by the profile combine to
$\varphi_jL^{-j}\mu'_j\bar\psi^{\rm bg}\psi^{\rm bg}$.
The cube count gives $M^3w_0\nu C_H^2h_F^2|\mu'_j|$.
The current mass estimate and its gauge variation use the
same legs and coefficients. This proves (iv).
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The scalar contribution]\label{C-423-6}
In the setting of \cref{C-423-5}, form the scalar list of
\cite[Def.\ 9.5]{QCDM1} with entries $F_0^{(j)}$, zero
counterterms, the generated boundary entries of the exponent,
and the canonical remaining entries. Use $\tau=x'_k/\mathsf t_k$
and $w'$ of \cref{C-423-3}. Put
$\mathsf g_j=\|F_0^{(j)}\|_{j,\kappa}\le\mathsf g_j(F)$.
The scalar identities, measurability and covariance of
\cite[Lem.\ 9.6]{QCDM1} hold for this list. Its regular
potential is complex linear in the entries. With
\[
 C_\varpi=\sum_{q\ge0}(L^5/2)^qv_q,\qquad
 v_q=\begin{cases}1&q\le3,\\e^ae^{-aL^{q-3}}&q\ge4,
                \end{cases}\qquad a=2\delta\kappa,
\]
the wide and octet parts satisfy
\[
 |\mathbb V^{\rm E,wd}(Y)+\mathbb V^{\rm E,oc}(Y)|
 \le C_{\rm V}C_{\mathcal A}s_k^{\rm fx}C_{\rm ert}C_\varpi
     \frac L{L-2}\sum_{j\le k}L^{-(k-j)}
          (\mathsf g_j+\alpha_0^2B_\sharp)e^{-r_Vd_k(Y)}.
\]
Here $s_k^{\rm fx}=\delta_k/\alpha_0$. A part made by
specified scalar entries $G^{(j)}$, $j\in J$, with sizes
$\mathsf g_j^G$, has the same bound with sum
$\sum_{j\in J}L^{-(k-j)}\mathsf g_j^G$ and no
$\alpha_0^2B_\sharp$ term. The edge-tent potential is zero.
On one lattice the old scalar variation is bracket localization
of the array with entries $F_0^{(j)}$ and zero counterterms,
and
\[
 |\mathcal V_0^{\rm old}(Y)|
 \le K_\Lambda(1+\beta_s)\frac{\delta_k}{\alpha_0}
       \sum_{j\le k}L^{-(k-j)}\mathsf g_j
                       e^{-(1-2\delta_{\rm w})\kappa d_k(Y)}.
\]
In both bounds the early entries enter through
$\Lambda_k^0(\mathcal F)$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Condition (F4) supplies a pointed scalar family on each core.
The generated entries are holomorphic on their slices, Borel,
gauge invariant, and functions of the pair. Their old bound
is $\mathsf B e^{-\kappa d}$. Edge entries at level $j>t_1$
have bound $8M^3\mathsf g_j(F)e^{-\kappa d}$; there are none
at earlier levels. Thus the scalar-list hypotheses used in
\cite[Lem.\ 9.6]{QCDM1} hold with
$\mathsf B'=\max\{\mathsf B,8M^3\max_{j>t_1}\mathsf g_j(F)\}$.
The remaining hypotheses concern the step geometry and the
fixed constants. The list identities therefore apply. In
particular the action terms left on the rims combine with
$-A(\beta'_h,\mathsf U)$ to give
\[
 -L^{t_1}x'_{t_1}A(\mathsf U)
 +\sum_{t_1<j\le k}L^jb'_j
       \sum_{\mathsf p:X(\mathsf p;j)\subset\Lambda_j}
                                              a_{\mathsf p}(\mathsf U)
 =-L^kx'_kA(\mathsf U)-L^kA(w';\mathsf U).
\]
This follows plaquette by plaquette from the pointed shares
and the telescoping identity in \cref{C-423-3}.

The regular-frame estimate
\cite[Prop.\ 58.22 and its proof]{YMM1} uses
\[
 \mathsf{size}^{\rm E}
 =C_{\rm ert}\sum_{m\le k}\varpi_{k-m}
    \left(\mathsf g'_m+\sum_{j<m}L^{-(m-j)}\mathsf g'_j\right),
 \qquad \mathsf g'_j=\mathsf g_j+\alpha_0^2B_\sharp.
\]
Its weights are $\varpi_i=L^{3i}\sum_{p+q=i}u_pv_q$.
The levelling floor $\delta_\star^{\rm pc}L\ge10\log L$
gives $u_p=2^pe^{-\delta_\star^{\rm pc}Lp/2}\le2^pL^{-5p}$,
and hence $\varpi_i\le C_\varpi(2L^{-2})^i$.
Interchanging the finite sums now gives
\[
 \mathsf{size}^{\rm E}
 \le C_{\rm ert}C_\varpi\sum_{j\le k}
   L^{-(k-j)}\mathsf g'_j\sum_{m=j}^k(2/L)^{k-m}
 \le C_{\rm ert}C_\varpi\frac L{L-2}
                    \sum_{j\le k}L^{-(k-j)}\mathsf g'_j.
\]
The defining series for $C_\varpi$ converges because $v_q$
decays exponentially in $L^q$.

To isolate specified entries, apply this bound to $tG$ for
$t>0$. Linearity multiplies the potential by $t$; the
additive $\alpha_0^2B_\sharp$ bound stays fixed. Divide by
$t$ and let $t\to\infty$. This removes that additive term.
Zero counterterms make the edge-tent part vanish. Finally
\cite[Prop.\ 51.16]{YMM1} gives the bracket localization
bound on the absolute system, with factor
$(1+\beta_s)\delta_k/\alpha_0$ and array size
$\sum_jL^{-(k-j)}\mathsf g_j$. Its linearity also gives
the stated bound for the early part.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[One step with a prescribed past]\label{C-423-7}
Let $t_1\le k<K$, $h\in\mathcal H_k^{[t_1]}$, and
$h'=(h,\mathsf o)$. Suppose its term has the measure identity
\[
 (\mathrm I_k)\qquad
 \hat\tau_h^{[\mathcal F]}
 =\mathsf{Stay}_h\mathbf1_h^{\rm T}\chi_k(\Omega_k)
    e^{\boldsymbol\Phi_h}e^{A_{k,h}^{[\mathcal F]}}\mathscr M_h,
\]
with an exponent of \cref{C-423-2}, independent of the
evaluation configuration off one null set. Assume also:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(Fr)] Each of the four frame classes, the fermion class,
the scalar classes $\mathrm{rg},\mathrm{bd}$, and
$\mathcal V^{\rm q}$, has size at most $\varepsilon_\flat$
on the tiers at rate $r_V$.
\item[(Sm)] The sum
\begin{align*}
 \tfrac72K_P\delta_k
 &+K_\Lambda(1+\beta_s)\frac{\delta_k}{\alpha_0}
                         \sum_{j\le k}L^{-(k-j)}\mathsf g_j(F)\\
 &+C_Vh_F^2C_{\mathcal A}\delta_k
 +(c_\psi+C_GC_{\mathcal A}\delta_k)c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2|s'_k|\\
 &+(c_\psi+C_{\mathcal A}s_a+C_GC_{\mathcal A}\delta_k)
                    \sum_{j\le k}\omega_{k+1-j}\|F_{\ge2}^{(j)}\|_j
\end{align*}
is at most $c_{\rm cl}/4$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the step is defined. On an interior polymer its output
equals the one-lattice output with the same families, coefficient
$x'_k$, and mass coefficient $L^{-k}s'_k$. If
$\widetilde E^{(k+1)}(X;z)$ is its pointed output, subtract
local parts at arbitrary numbers $e',b',\mu'$:
\begin{align*}
 F^{(k+1)}(X;z)={}&\widetilde E^{(k+1)}(X;z)
  -\mathbf1_{X=\{z\}}
       \left(e'-L^{-(k+1)}\mu'\sum_v
                       \bar\psi^{\rm bg}(v)\psi^{\rm bg}(v)\right)\\
 &-L^{k+1}b'\sum_{\mathsf p:X(\mathsf p)=X}
                       \upsilon_z(\mathsf p)a_{\mathsf p}(\mathsf U).
\end{align*}
It has (F1), (F2), and (F4), and finite sizes. The new
coefficients are $x'_{k+1}=L^{-1}x'_k-b'$ and
$s'_{k+1}=Ls'_k+\mu'$. The action and mass parts left by
$1-\varphi_{k+1}$ are placed in the edge terms. The extracted
numbers enter the regular constant and vacuum constant by
the rule of \cite[Lem.\ 9.15]{QCDM1}.
The resulting exponent $A_{k+1,h'}^{[\mathcal F]}$ satisfies
$(\mathrm I_{k+1})$, with one value at the evaluation
configurations, and the domination of \cref{C-423-4} holds.
If also (F3) holds for the new family and the new real
coefficients are in their windows, the new exponent has the
format of \cref{C-423-2}.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Since $k\ge t_1\ge1$, the first small-field region is the
whole torus. The old configuration at the chain point is the
shifted configuration of the usual step. The gauge objects,
tests, coordinates and Gaussian are unchanged except for
their admitted ratio $\tau=x'_k/\mathsf t_k$. Every evaluation
pair lies in its core at half the radii. Thus (F1) and the
boundary assumptions define every old member at the places
where the step evaluates it.

Complete the fermion square at the new background. The
Schur identity concerns only the tower. Substitution into
each old member and changing the background are linear in
that member. Consequently the exact algebra of
\cite[Prop.\ 9.11]{QCDM1} applies. The estimates for its
activity and mass variations are those of \cref{C-423-5};
the scalar variations and the action-profile identity are
those of \cref{C-423-6}. No assertion about the birth sizes
of early families enters this algebra.

On $\Lambda_{k+1}$ all profiles are one, so the two
coefficients are $L^kx'_k$ and $L^{-k}s'_k$. By (Sm), the
scalar and fermion potential sizes add to at most
$c_{\rm cl}/4$. The test tail is at most $c_{\rm cl}$.
The expansion \cite[Lem.\ 7.5]{QCDM1} therefore applies on
both lattices, with its bounds and first variations. Its
inputs are holomorphic in the pair, jointly invariant and
flavour invariant. Substitution, integration and pointing
preserve these properties. Translation covariance and
compatibility on polymers that fit follow term by term from
the same properties of the inputs. The scalar bracket
localization is defined on the whole core by
\cite[Prop.\ 51.16]{YMM1}; hence the scalar output is a
pointed family there. Local extraction preserves these
properties. The output has decay $e^{-\kappa_+d}$, and the
local parts have size-zero support. Since
$\kappa_+\ge\kappa+1$, the polymer and pointer counts give
finite sizes. These statements prove (F1), (F2), and (F4);
they do not assert (F3) for arbitrary extraction numbers.

On an interior domain, the two frames have the same
potential values, covariances and cluster operations.
The interior agreement argument of
\cite[Lem.\ 9.10]{QCDM1} therefore identifies their outputs
and pointed terms. The extraction identity is linear in
$e',b',\mu'$, so its signs give precisely the new
coefficients displayed above. Generated boundary terms and
edge terms have the properties proved in \cref{C-423-11}.

It remains to justify the measure identity for complex
coefficients. The coefficient functions of
\cref{C-423-4} are bounded Borel functions. Both the old
term and the coefficientwise measure carried through the
next step are dominated by a constant times a positive
pure-gauge term. Their variations are therefore integrable.
Each change of variables in the exact history identity
can be applied to the four positive parts of each complex
coefficient. Null sets are carried by the same coordinate
maps: absolute continuity with respect to the pure term
replaces any use of positivity of the fermion coefficient.
The finite Berezin integral then commutes with these
operations. This proves $(\mathrm I_{k+1})$ as a measure
identity, not only as an equality of formal integrands.

Two evaluation configurations differ by a gauge
transformation fixing all stored generators. The new
regular members and boundary terms are jointly invariant,
and the tower and mass term are covariant. Thus the new
exponent has one value off the coordinate null set. Its
old boundary terms retain their levels and its new ones
have level $k+1>t_1$. With the extra moment and window
assumptions it has all clauses of the required format.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Closing the bounds}

\begin{remark}[Constants for the prescribed past]\label{C-423-8}
Let $b_k^{\rm blk},b_k^{\rm lay},b_k^{\rm ms}$ be the three
bounds in the proof of \cite[Prop.\ 9.14]{QCDM1}. Define
\begin{gather*}
 m_\omega=\min\{1,S_\omega\},\qquad
 \lambda_0=m_\omega/34,\\
 \lambda'_0=\min\left\{1,
 \frac{K_\Lambda(1+\beta_s)(L-2)\varepsilon_\flat}
 {LC_{\rm V}C_{\mathcal A}C_{\rm ert}C_\varpi c_{\rm cl}}\right\},\\
 K_0^{\rm F}=\tfrac72K_P+
  \frac{K_\Lambda(1+\beta_s)}{\alpha_0}
           \left(\frac L{L-1}E_0+1+E_0\right),\\
 C_2^{\rm pt}=8M^3C_2,\qquad
 b_k^{\rm pt}=2\Theta_k^\sharp C_{\rm tab}S_\omega
                         C_2^{\rm pt}\phi(\mathsf t_k)^2.
\end{gather*}
The pointed constant is that of \cite[Lem.\ 8.8]{QCDM1};
in particular its use precedes the constants that count
stored pointers. A function of $\gamma$, such as
$b^{\rm pt}(\gamma)$ or $\Theta^\sharp(\gamma)$, means
the corresponding expression evaluated at
$\delta(\gamma^{-2})$, $\phi(\gamma^{-2})$, and $\gamma^2$.
Impose the additional ceiling
\[
 (\Gamma^{\rm F})\qquad
 K_0^{\rm F}\delta(\gamma^{-2})+b^{\rm blk}(\gamma)
       \le\tfrac14c_{\rm cl},\quad
 b^{\rm ms}(\gamma)\le\tfrac3{16}\varepsilon_\flat,\quad
 b^{\rm lay}(\gamma)+b^{\rm pt}(\gamma)
       \le\tfrac14\varepsilon_\flat .
\]
Each left side tends to zero with $\gamma$. Its constants
have already been fixed: $C_\varpi,\Theta_\circ^{\rm B},
\lambda_0,\lambda'_0,K_0^{\rm F}$ precede $h_F$;
$C_{\rm tab}$ and $C_2^{\rm pt}$ use constants through
$h_F$; and $\gamma$ is chosen last. The bound
$2C_{\mathcal A}\delta(\gamma^{-2})\le\beta_0$ gives
$\Theta_k^{\rm B}\le\Theta_\circ^{\rm B}$.

For the variation of the outputs put
\begin{align*}
 K_{\rm num}&=\max\{1,c_b^{-2}C^\psi_{am}(\nu h_F^2)^{-1},
                                      2+C_{am}r_\alpha^{-2}\},\\
 K_{\rm lin}&=32K_M(1+K_\mu)(1+K_{\rm num})
                       +C_EK_{\mathbf M}^{\rm v}K_\Lambda^{-1},\\
 C_\Sigma&=K_{\rm lin}\max\{2\Theta^\sharp(\gamma)C_{\rm tab},
   (c_\psi+C_{\mathcal A}s_a(\gamma)
                   +C_GC_{\mathcal A}\delta(\gamma^{-2}))C_\omega\},\\
 C'_\Sigma&=K_{\rm lin}\max\left\{
  C_{\rm V}C_{\mathcal A}\frac{\delta(\gamma^{-2})}{\alpha_0}
                  C_{\rm ert}C_\varpi\frac L{L-2},
  K_\Lambda(1+\beta_s)\frac{\delta(\gamma^{-2})}{\alpha_0}
                                  \right\}.
\end{align*}
Here $K_{\mathbf M}^{\rm v}$ is the scalar-system variation
constant of \cite[Lem.\ 7.4]{QCDM1}. The first two constants
are fixed at $h_F$; the last two after $\gamma$. None is used
to choose an earlier constant.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[A flow above the prescribed past]\label{C-423-9}
A flow above $t_1$ consists of families $E^{(j)}$ on both
lattices, real $x_i$ for $t_1\le i\le K$, complex initial
$s_{t_1},E_{t_1}$, and numbers $e_j,b_j,\mu_j$ for
$t_1<j\le K$, with the unchanged tower, tests and backgrounds.
Assume:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(G1)] Every family has (F1)--(F4) and the pointed sum
rule. Its scalar part has no extracted action multiple;
its infinite-lattice pointed values at the trivial pair
have zero mean over a cell; and on the torus those values
are field-independent numbers.
\item[(G2)] For $j>t_1$, the family and numbers are those
produced by the one-lattice step and its extraction rules.
Thus $x_j=L^{-1}x_{j-1}-b_j$ and $s_j=Ls_{j-1}+\mu_j$.
The windows are
$x_i>1$, $|x_i-\mathsf t_i|\le\bar B$, and
$|s_i|\le2\bar B_M/\mathsf t_i$.
Also $|b_j|\le B_\sharp$ and
$|e_j|\le C'_e(1+\log x_{j-1})$.
The scalar size is at most $E_0$.
The usual activity norm, including each pointed term and
every partial sum of pointed terms on one polymer, is at
most $C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2$, on both lattices.
The stronger pointed size satisfies
\[
 \epsilon_j^\psi(E)\le C_2^{\rm pt}\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2.
\]
\item[(G3)] For $j\le t_1$ write
$E^{(j)}=R^{(j)}+D^{(j)}$, with both summands satisfying
(G1), and $D_0^{(j)}$ zero at the trivial pair. Require
\[
 \epsilon_j^\psi(R)\le C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2,\qquad
 \mathsf g_j(R)\le E_0,
\]
and, for every $t_1\le k\le K$,
\[
 \Lambda_k^\psi(D)\le\lambda_0C_2\phi(\mathsf t_k)^2,
 \qquad
 \Lambda_k^0(D)\le\lambda'_0(1+E_0).
\]
\end{enumerate}
The flow's free past is $(E^{(j)})_{j\le t_1}$.
Write $\mathfrak f_k$ for the torus sum of all scalar
values at the trivial pair through level $k$, and set
\[
 E_k=E_{t_1}+\sum_{t_1<j\le k}e_jn_j,\quad
 \mathfrak d^0=\max_{t_1\le k\le K}\Lambda_k^0(D),\quad
 \mathfrak d^\psi=\max_{t_1\le k\le K}\Lambda_k^\psi(D).
\]
Its term is that of \cref{C-423-4} with
$\sigma=s_{t_1}$ and $c=E_{t_1}+\mathfrak f_{t_1}$.
The windows give
$|\mu_j|\le4\bar B_M/\mathsf t_j$.
At a step satisfying (G1), the extracted mean quadratic
moment is a scalar matrix; the mass rule is its negative
scalar coefficient divided by $\eta_j^2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Which assumptions are used]\label{C-423-15}
The whole-core holomorphy and invariance define the shifted
members and their common value in coordinates. Translation
covariance and (F3) give the cell cancellations; (F4)
gives the scalar list. The ordinary norm in (G2) controls
the one-lattice potential. Its pointed norm is used when
stored pointers have different evaluation pairs. In (G3)
the pointed norm of $R^{(j)}$ has the smaller constant
$C_2$, so its stored contribution lies inside the old
bound; the contribution above $t_1$ is instead paid by
$b_k^{\rm pt}$. The real coefficient window admits the
Gaussian. The mass window gives the factor $4$, rather
than $3$, in the edge mass bound. Finally the vanishing
scalar value of $D^{(j)}$ keeps the wrapping constant
unchanged. These conditions are separate hypotheses;
one does not infer them merely from finite sizes.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[The frame closes]\label{C-423-10}
Let a flow of \cref{C-423-9} be given. Suppose its term at
$h\in\mathcal H_k^{[t_1]}$, $k<K$, has the format and identity
$(\mathrm I_k)$, with its actual families and coefficients,
and its boundary terms have the properties of
\cref{C-423-11}. Suppose earlier frame sizes are at most
$\varepsilon_\flat$ and $\bar v_j\le b_{j-1}^{\rm blk}$.
Then (Sm) and (Fr) hold at every extension $h'$.
More precisely,
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] On one lattice,
$\varepsilon_{\rm V}\le K_0^{\rm F}\delta_k$,
$\varepsilon_\natural\le b_k^{\rm blk}$ and
$\bar v_{k+1}\le b_k^{\rm blk}$.
The potential part linear in $D$ has size at most
\[
 s_D=(c_\psi+C_{\mathcal A}s_a+C_GC_{\mathcal A}\delta_k)
                 C_\omega\Lambda_k^\psi(D)
      +K_\Lambda(1+\beta_s)\frac{\delta_k}{\alpha_0}
                                      \Lambda_k^0(D)
 \le\tfrac14c_{\rm cl}.
\]
The potential with $D$ removed also has size at most
$c_{\rm cl}/4$.
\item[(ii)] With $b_k^{\rm tot}=b_k^{\rm blk}
+b_k^{\rm lay}+b_k^{\rm ms}$, the fermion class satisfies
\begin{align*}
 \mathsf{sz}_k^\natural
 &\le\tfrac{13}{64}\max\{\Sigma_k^{[t_1]},\bar v_*^{[t_1]}\}
            +b_k^{\rm tot}+\tfrac13b_k^{\rm ms}
                         +b_k^{\rm pt}+P_D,\\
 P_D&\le\min\left\{2\Theta_k^\sharp C_{\rm tab}\Lambda_k^\psi(D),
   \frac{\lambda_0}{m_\omega}
             (b_k^{\rm blk}+\tfrac{59}{11}b_k^{\rm lay})\right\}
 \le\tfrac{35}{748}\varepsilon_\flat.
\end{align*}
In particular $\mathsf{sz}_k^\natural\le\varepsilon_\flat$.
\item[(iii)] The sizes of $\mathrm{rg},\mathrm{bd}$ and
$\mathcal V^{\rm q}$ are at most
$3\varepsilon_\flat/4$, $2\varepsilon_\flat/5$, and
$\varepsilon_\flat$, respectively. The part of
$\mathrm{rg}$ linear in $D$ is at most
$C_{\rm V}C_{\mathcal A}s_k^{\rm fx}C_{\rm ert}C_\varpi
 L\Lambda_k^0(D)/(L-2)\le\varepsilon_\flat/4$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For the ordinary families in (G2) and $R$ in (G3), put
$n=k+1-j$. The scale fall gives
\[
 \phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2
 \le L^{-n}(1+n\log L)^{2\mathfrak p_0}\phi(\mathsf t_k)^2.
\]
After multiplication by $L^{n/4}$ their sum is at most
$L^{-1/2}S_\omega\phi(\mathsf t_k)^2$. The $D$ terms
contribute at most $\lambda_0\phi(\mathsf t_k)^2$, and
$\lambda_0\le(1-L^{-1/2})S_\omega$. Thus the old-activity
sum fits in the third term of $b_k^{\rm blk}$.
The mass window gives its second term. For scalars,
\[
 \sum_{j\le k}L^{-(k-j)}\mathsf g_j(E)
 \le\frac L{L-1}E_0+\Lambda_k^0(D)
 \le\frac L{L-1}E_0+1+E_0.
\]
Apply \cref{C-423-5,C-423-6} and $(\Gamma^{\rm F})$.
The same estimates with $D=0$ apply after its removal.
Each of the two summands of $s_D$ is covered by the
corresponding bound just used. An insertion costs no more
than the fermion potential. This proves (i).

For (ii), split each member into three parts: the one
formed with $R$ below $t_1$ and zero families above it,
including its vertex, mass and boundary terms; the terms
from $E^{(j)}$ above $t_1$; and the terms from $D$.
The first part has the closed bounds of
\cite[Prop.\ 9.14, proof]{QCDM1}. Its regular pointed
sizes are at most $C_2\phi^2\le C_2^{\rm pt}\phi^2$.
Stored mass coefficients obey
$L^m|s_h|\le\max\{|s_m|,L|s_{m-1}|\}
\le2\bar B_M/\mathsf t_m$.
The boundary terms have their induction bounds. The
only changed bound is $|\mu_j|\le4\bar B_M/\mathsf t_j$:
it replaces the edge contribution $b_k^{\rm ms}$ by
$4b_k^{\rm ms}/3$. Thus the first part is at most
the first three terms in the displayed recurrence.

For the second part use the pointed bound of (G2) in
\cref{C-423-5}(i). Its sum is at most
$2\Theta_k^\sharp C_{\rm tab}S_\omega C_2^{\rm pt}
\phi(\mathsf t_k)^2=b_k^{\rm pt}$.
For the third part the same proposition gives the first
bound for $P_D$. To obtain the second, write
$\Phi=C_2\phi(\mathsf t_k)^2$, $\Lambda=\Lambda_k^\psi(D)$
and $\theta_1=c_\psi+C_{\mathcal A}s_a+C_GC_{\mathcal A}\delta_k$.
Since $\Theta_k^{\rm B}\le2\Theta'_k$, the separate
kernels give
\begin{align*}
 P_D\le{}&(\theta_1+5\Theta'_k)C_\omega\Lambda
       +\tfrac{60}{11}C_{\rm lay}\Theta'_kL^{-1/4}\Lambda\\
 &+5\Theta_k[C_\omega(c_{\rm rim}+c_{\rm rim}^{\rm pt})
            +c_{\rm geo}+39(1+2\mathsf n_{\rm wk})]
                                      L^{-1/4}\Lambda.
\end{align*}
Here we used
$\sum_jL^{(k-j)/4}\epsilon_j^\psi(D)=L^{-1/4}\Lambda$
and $\sum_j\epsilon_j^\psi(D)\le L^{-1/4}\Lambda$.
The first $\theta_1$ term is at most
$(\lambda_0/S_\omega)$ times the third term of
$b_k^{\rm blk}$. The remaining terms are paid by
$b_k^{\rm lay}$: its stored-layer and interface factors
satisfy $C_{\rm lay}\Theta'_k\Phi\le b_k^{\rm sl}$ and
$39(1+2\mathsf n_{\rm wk})\Theta_k\Phi\le b_k^{\rm if}$;
also $c_{\rm geo}\le C_\omega c_{\rm rim}^{\rm pt}$.
Their largest multiplier is
\[
 \lambda_0\max\{5/S_\omega,10L^{-1/4},
                         (60/11)L^{-1/4}\}
 \le(59/11)\lambda_0/m_\omega .
\]
This uses $L\ge13$. Consequently
$P_D\le(1/34)(70/11)(1/4)\varepsilon_\flat
=35\varepsilon_\flat/748<3\varepsilon_\flat/64$.
The new ceiling gives
$b_k^{\rm blk}+(b_k^{\rm lay}+b_k^{\rm pt})
+4b_k^{\rm ms}/3\le3\varepsilon_\flat/4$.
Since the earlier maximum is at most $\varepsilon_\flat$,
the recurrence closes with
$13/64+3/4+3/64=1$.

Finally split the scalar list into its closed entries
and the entries $D_0^{(j)}$. The first list satisfies the
ordinary scalar bounds and contributes at most
$\varepsilon_\flat/2$ to $\mathrm{rg}$.
\Cref{C-423-6} and the definition of $\lambda'_0$ bound
the second by
$K_0^{\rm F}\delta_k\varepsilon_\flat/c_{\rm cl}
\le\varepsilon_\flat/4$. The boundary scalar class reads
only later generated terms and edges, so its ordinary
$2\varepsilon_\flat/5$ bound persists. The quadratic
gauge class reads only the configuration, tests and real
$\tau$, and retains its bound. The four sizes give the
frame amplitude condition of \cite[Lem.\ 9.9]{QCDM1}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The new boundary terms]\label{C-423-11}
Assume $(\mathrm I_k)$, (Fr), and (Sm) in
\cref{C-423-7}, and the stated boundary properties at
earlier levels. The generated boundary term of level
$k+1$ is the sum of the four kinds in
\cite[Prop.\ 9.13]{QCDM1}: the cluster remainder, the
gauge and fermion normalizers, and the rejected forms,
with their strip rows. It is holomorphic in the pair
on its slices, jointly invariant, Borel, and depends
only on the pair and stored data. It vanishes on the
interior in the same cases as those four kinds. Its
scalar and full bounds are those of that proposition;
the part with fermion legs is bounded by
\[
 (1+\eta_{k+1}^{\rm sr})K^{\rm lb}
             \mathsf{sz}_k^\natural e^{-\kappa_+d_{k+1}(X)}.
\]
For an edge domain, the new edge term has norm at most
\[
 M^3\bigl(8\mathsf g_{k+1}(F)+108K_M\bar v_{k+1}
       +3\bar C_{\rm reg}^2|b'|
       +w_0\nu C_H^2h_F^2|\mu'|\bigr)e^{-\kappa d_{k+1}(X)}.
\]
Its scalar bound omits the insertion and mass terms.
Its part with fermion legs is bounded more precisely by
\[
 4M^3(d_{k+1}(X)+3)^3K_M\bar v_{k+1}
                        e^{-\kappa_+d_{k+1}(X)},
\]
plus $M^3w_0\nu C_H^2h_F^2|\mu'|$ on one-cube domains.
Here $\bar v_{k+1}\le c_{\rm cl}/4$ and
$\sum_{X\in\mathsf{Ix}^{\rm ed}_{k+1}}e^{-\kappa d_{k+1}(X)}
\le C_{\mathsf B}\#_{k+1}(Z_{k+1}^{\sim})$.

After the action parts left on the rim are removed, the
edge term depends on the configuration on $\operatorname{Bd}(X)$
alone and obeys its bounds on the whole core. Its scalar
part there is the scalar edge family with bound
$8M^3\mathsf g_{k+1}(F)e^{-\kappa d_{k+1}(X)}$.
The removed action parts combine with the action profile
to give $-L^{k+1}A(w';\mathsf U)$, even for complex $b'$.
When $b'$ is real with $|b'|\le B_\sharp$,
$w'$ is real and $|w'|\le\bar B$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The four kinds are built from the step's potential,
background maps, decoupled covariance and normalizers.
The latter three use only the tower and regions. The
potential inputs have the required properties by (F1),
the previous boundary hypotheses and
\cref{C-423-6,C-423-7}. For the stored form and mass term,
gauge covariance of the tower and background maps gives
\[
 \langle\bar\Psi u^{-1},\mathbb D_h[U^u]u\Psi\rangle
     =\langle\bar\Psi,\mathbb D_h[U]\Psi\rangle.
\]
The mass coefficient is scalar at every place, so the
same statement holds for it. The scalar list gives
the regular and boundary scalar potentials as functions
of the pair; the quadratic gauge class has that property
by \cite[Lem.\ 9.4]{QCDM1}. Boundary levelling uses only
their slice bounds and their whole-core edge remainders,
as in \cite[Lem.\ 9.7]{QCDM1}.

The expansion under (Fr) preserves holomorphy,
measurability and invariance. Its cluster bound is
$\mathsf b_{\rm cs}^{\mathfrak F}e^{-\kappa''d}$,
with $\mathsf b_{\rm cs}^{\mathfrak F}\le3/16$, and
its fermion part is at most
$K^{\rm lb}\mathsf{sz}_k^\natural e^{-\kappa''d}$.
The strip row multiplies these bounds by
$\eta_{k+1}^{\rm sr}$ and uses rate $\kappa_+$.
The normalizer amplitudes are
$24(LM)^3E_{\rm nf}$ and $C_NN_f$; the rejected forms
and quadratic correction have the original unit bounds.
All their rates are at least $\kappa$. Thus their sum
is at most
$\mathsf B^{\rm F}e^{-\kappa d}\le\mathsf Be^{-\kappa d}$,
where $\mathsf B^{\rm F}=24(LM)^3E_{\rm nf}+C_NN_f+3$.
On an interior polymer the cluster remainder vanishes
by \cref{C-423-7}; the other vanishing assertions concern
only the regions. This proves the generated-term claims.

An edge domain lies inside $\Lambda_{k+1}$, so its
pointed terms are outputs of the one-lattice step.
Their insertion part costs
$4K_M\bar v_{k+1}e^{-\kappa_+d}$ per pointer, and there
are at most $M^3(d+3)^3$ pointers. Since
$(d+3)^3e^{-(\kappa_+-\kappa)d}\le27$, this gives
the coefficient $108M^3K_M\bar v_{k+1}$.
The scalar edge bound is the pointed scalar count of
\cite[Prop.\ 9.13, proof]{QCDM1}, applied with its actual
size $\mathsf g_{k+1}(F)$.

The action remainder has size-zero support. On such a
domain at most $3M^3L^{3(k+1)}$ fine plaquettes contribute,
each at most $\bar C_{\rm reg}^2L^{-4(k+1)}$.
Their coefficient is $L^{k+1}b'$ and their shares sum to
one, giving $3M^3\bar C_{\rm reg}^2|b'|$.
At a rim pointer the mass part in the pointed activity
and the part left by the profile add to
$\varphi_{k+1}L^{-(k+1)}\mu'
\sum_v\bar\psi^{\rm bg}(v)\psi^{\rm bg}(v)$.
There are $M^3L^{3(k+1)}$ fine sites per cube and each
leg costs $C_HL^{-(k+1)}h_F$. Hence its bound is
$M^3w_0\nu C_H^2h_F^2|\mu'|$.

The insertion and scalar bounds hold uniformly on the
whole core: the one-lattice expansion is defined there,
and $\mathsf g_{k+1}(F)$ is a supremum over that core.
The mass bound is independent of the configuration.
Only the removed action terms used regular evaluation
configurations; subsequent steps place them with the
action profile, whose exact plaquette identity is
\cref{C-423-6}. The edge-domain count depends only on
the label. These observations prove every stated
domain and norm assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Agreement for equal history excerpts]\label{C-423-16}
Let two histories $h',h'_1\in\mathcal H_{k+1}^{[t_1]}$
use the same free past, coefficients, mass numbers and
later free families. Assume their steps through level
$k+1$ satisfy \cref{C-423-11}. Suppose the torus has
the chart floor $(\mathrm{Tor}^{\rm c})_{k+1}$.
If their excerpts, including label bonds, agree at a
generated domain $X$, then $X$ is generated for both
histories and their boundary terms at $X$ are the same
function on the same space, including their strip rows.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Use the identity chart on the vicinity of $X$.
The chart correspondence in \cite[Prop.\ 9.13, proof]{QCDM1}
descends to every earlier level: the keys and records
of a restricted history are the same earlier keys and
records of the whole history. It also restricts to each
subdomain $Y\subset X$, since its vicinities are nested
and its label bonds are the corresponding subset.
The chart floor descends to those levels. Thus the
triples, graded spaces, stored data spaces and boxes
on every such $Y$ agree.

Induct on the level $m>t_1$ of a generated term in $X$.
At the base there are no generated or edge terms.
At a later step, the frame on a subdomain $Y$ uses:
the prescribed regular families, evaluated at pairs
selected by the regions; the coefficients and profiles;
the generated terms at earlier levels; the edge terms;
and the tower, shifts and Gaussian objects.
The regular families are the same functions. Regularity
of a pair reads its polymer and the nearby region,
and the background walks read only their recorded
vicinities. The coefficients are the same; the profile
$\varphi_j(y)$ reads $Z_j$ within
$|x-y|_\infty<3\mathsf s_j/4$, a subset of its recorded
vicinity. The action weight reads whether a plaquette
corner lies in $Z_j$. Earlier generated terms agree
by induction. An edge term reads its family, the
coefficients, its rim pointers and its profile, so it
also agrees. Finally the tower and its decoupled
covariances are carried by the same chart.

Consequently the fermion class agrees, term by term.
The two scalar lists have the same regular entries,
earlier generated entries and canonical factors on $Y$;
the scalar localization and bracket construction
therefore give the same regular and boundary potentials.
The weight potential agrees plaquette by plaquette.
The quadratic class reads the pair, $\tau$ and whether
its cube belongs to $\Lambda_m$, all fixed by the
excerpt. The Gaussian and fermion integration families
also agree. The local cluster operations thus produce
the same output on every subdomain of $Y$.

The cluster kind is this output at the stored field
minus its interior one-lattice output. The strip row
is the same finite integer combination of output
values at the same external fields. The normalizer
kinds use the tower and regions; the rejected forms
and quadratic correction use those data and the same
$\tau$. Each of the four kinds therefore agrees.
This closes the induction and proves the claim at $X$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Dependence on the early error]\label{C-423-12}
Under the hypotheses of \cref{C-423-10}, put
\[
 \mathfrak d_k(D)=C_\Sigma\Lambda_k^\psi(D)
                              +C'_\Sigma\Lambda_k^0(D).
\]
With the later families, coefficients and boundary terms
fixed, every frame member and every one-lattice potential
member is affine in $D$. Its linear part has norm at most
$\mathfrak d_k(D)$ in the norm used by the step.
The output activity, its pointed terms and the extracted
numbers are holomorphic functions of the input members.
Their differences from the outputs with $D$ removed are
at most $\mathfrak d_k(D)$, in the ordinary activity and
scalar array norms and in modulus for the numbers.

At the step with $D$ removed, extraction uses the same
bounded linear functionals of the new infinite-lattice
activity. It removes the trace of the mean quadratic
moment. Without an additional symmetry assumption this
asserts trace zero, not that the entire matrix moment
vanishes.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The linearity and the four relevant bounds are
\[
 2\Theta_k^\sharp C_{\rm tab}\Lambda_k^\psi(D),\quad
 C_{\rm V}C_{\mathcal A}s_k^{\rm fx}C_{\rm ert}C_\varpi
                  \frac L{L-2}\Lambda_k^0(D),
\]
and the two summands of $s_D$ in \cref{C-423-10}.
The other members read no early family. These estimates
give the first assertion and, by the definition of the
constants, $K_{\rm lin}s_D\le\mathfrak d_k(D)$.

Replace the early family by $R+\zeta D$ and keep all
other data fixed. If $s_D=0$ the outputs do not change.
Otherwise set $\rho=c_{\rm cl}/(4s_D)\ge1$.
The potential has size at most $c_{\rm cl}/2$ on
$|\zeta|\le\rho$ and less than $3c_{\rm cl}/4$ on
$|\zeta|<2\rho$. The expansion
\cite[Lem.\ 7.5]{QCDM1} is holomorphic on the latter disc.
On the former disc its outputs are bounded by
$K'_M(3c_{\rm cl}/2)e^{-\kappa_+d}$, including the
test tail of size at most $c_{\rm cl}$.

At a potential of size at most $c_{\rm cl}/2$, perturb
in an even direction $f$ by
$\lambda c_{\rm cl}f/(4\|f\|)$. On $|\lambda|=1$
the potential has size at most $3c_{\rm cl}/4$.
Cauchy's estimate and the test tail give the variation
bound $7K'_M\|f\|e^{-\kappa_+d}$.
The insertion at a pointer costs at most the fermion
potential, hence at most $c_{\rm cl}/2$, so its pointed
output is bounded by
$(7/2)K'_Mc_{\rm cl}e^{-\kappa_+d}$.
It is holomorphic in $\zeta$: the joint family consisting
of the pointing path plus $\lambda$ times its insertion
has potential size below $c_{\rm cl}$ for
$|\zeta|<2\rho$ and $|\lambda|<1/3$.
Differentiate in $\lambda$ and integrate the pointing
path. Uniform Cauchy bounds justify that integral.
Summing polymers through a cube gives the bound
$4K_Mc_{\rm cl}$ for the output and each pointed output
in both norms under consideration.

The extraction functionals require no linear symmetry
of the families. If $\mathsf m_\zeta$ is the cell mean
of the row sums of the quadratic kernel, they give
\[
 \mu(\zeta)=-(\nu\eta_{k+1}^2)^{-1}
                    \operatorname{tr}\mathsf m_\zeta,\quad
 b(\zeta)=b^\circ+\mathsf{cf}^{\sharp}[\widetilde E_{\zeta,0}],
 \quad e(\zeta)=e^\circ+\widetilde e(\zeta).
\]
The constants $b^\circ,e^\circ$ use only the normalizers,
the fixed coefficient and fine mass. The coefficient
bound \cite[Lem.\ 7.8]{QCDM1} gives
$\|\mathsf m_\zeta\|_{\rm tr}\le C^\psi_{am}h_F^{-2}
\|\widetilde E_{\zeta,\ge2}\|$ and
$|\eta_{k+1}|\ge c_b$. Thus the mass extraction multiplies
the activity bound by at most
$K_\mu=1+c_{\mathsf S}C^\psi_{am}c_b^{-2}/\nu$.
The action functional has bound $C_{am}r_\alpha^{-2}$.
Translation covariance gives
$|\widetilde e|\le M^{-3}\|\widetilde E_{\zeta,0}\|$:
the cell sum of its pointed totals is the sum over
polymers through the cell divided by their number of
cubes. Scalar extraction consequently has factor
at most $2+C_{am}r_\alpha^{-2}$.
All three functionals are bounded and linear.

The extracted outputs, pointed terms and numbers,
after their constant contributions are removed, are
therefore holomorphic and bounded by
$M_{\rm out}=4K_Mc_{\rm cl}(1+K_\mu)(1+K_{\rm num})$.
The remaining scalar bond terms need separate mention.
Only the fourth scalar-system entry changes with $D$;
it is the bracket localization of its scalar array.
The two scalar potentials have size at most
$c_{\rm cl}/4=w_*/4$, and their difference has size
at most $s_D\le w_*/4$. The variation estimate
\cite[Lem.\ 7.4]{QCDM1} therefore gives a pointed
bond difference at most
$K_{\mathbf M}^{\rm v}K_\Lambda^{-1}s_De^{-\kappa_+d}$,
and after summation at most
$C_EK_{\mathbf M}^{\rm v}K_\Lambda^{-1}s_D$.

For a normed-space holomorphic function on $|\zeta|<2\rho$
bounded by $M_{\rm out}$ on $|\zeta|\le\rho$, Schwarz's
lemma applied to $g-g(0)$ and norm-one functionals gives
$\|g(1)-g(0)\|\le2M_{\rm out}/\rho$.
This equals
$32K_M(1+K_\mu)(1+K_{\rm num})s_D$.
Add the scalar bond contribution to obtain
$K_{\rm lin}s_D\le\mathfrak d_k(D)$.
At $\zeta=0$ the remaining mean moment is
$\mathsf m_0+\mu(0)\eta_{k+1}^2\mathbf1$, whose trace is
zero by the displayed extraction formula. This proves
the final qualification as well.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Summation over the layers]\label{C-423-13}
Let a flow of \cref{C-423-9} have the identities and
step bounds of \cref{C-423-10,C-423-11} through level $k$.
In the constants of the upper history bound
\cite[Thm.\ D]{QCDM1}, replace
\[
 E_0\ \hbox{by}\ E_0+\mathfrak d^0,\qquad
 C_{\rm leg}\ \hbox{by}\
          C_{\rm leg}+C_{\rm leg}^{\square}\mathfrak d^\psi .
\]
Here $C_{\rm leg}^{\square}$ is the per-cube constant in
its regular-leg proof. With these constants, the scalar
and fermion sums obey the same layer bounds. The action
shift to be included in the scalar bound is
\[
 L^{t_1}|x_{t_1}-\mathsf t_{t_1}|A(\mathsf U)
       +\sum_{t_1<j\le k}|L^jb_jA(\varphi_j,\mathsf U)|.
\]
Moreover $|\mathfrak f_k|\le C_{\rm fs}$,
$f_n(\mathcal S)=0$ for $n\le t_1$, and
\[
 |f_n(\mathcal S)|\le
 C_\flat^{\rm F}(1+\log\mathsf t_{n-1})
                         \#_n(Z_n^\sim)\quad(n>t_1).
\]
The last constant can already be taken at the original
$E_0$.

The pointwise and integrated bounds of that upper
history theorem hold with $\operatorname{Re}E_k$ in
place of $E_k$ and with the present action profile.
In particular, for the free-coordinate density $g_h$,
\begin{align*}
 \|g_h\|&\le
 e^{-\beta A(\mathsf U)+C_E^{\rm F}\Sigma'(h)
       +\operatorname{Re}E_k-\operatorname{Re}\sum_nf_n}
             \prod_{(t,D)}|\mathsf u_{t,D}[\mathscr Q_{t,D}]|,\\
 e^{-\operatorname{Re}E_k+\operatorname{Re}\sum_nf_n}
       \int\|g_h\|\,d\mathscr M_h^{\rm fr}
 &\le e^{C_{\rm maj}^{\dagger}(n_k+\Sigma_Z(h))}
            \prod_t e^{-c_\star p_0(g_t)^2n_t^{\rm cr}(h)},
 \qquad C_{\rm maj}^{\dagger}=48L^3C_E^{\rm F}+C'_\star .
\end{align*}
The pointwise bound also holds with the actual action
profile, or with $L^{t_1}x_{t_1}A$, in place of $\beta A$.
These bounds hold for every $x_{t_1}$ in its window.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Apply the scalar sum estimate
\cite[Prop.\ 64.2]{YMM1} to one level at a time, putting
zero families at the other levels. This is permitted
because its size parameter is free and (F4) supplies
each family's hypotheses. On a layer $\mathcal L_n$,
$n\ge t_1$, the sum of the resulting sizes is bounded by
\[
 \sum_{j\le n}L^{-(n-j)}\mathsf g_j(E)
 \le\frac L{L-1}E_0+\Lambda_n^0(D)
 \le\frac L{L-1}(E_0+\mathfrak d^0).
\]
There are no earlier layers. For the action profiles
the same per-level plaquette count gives
$L^jA(\varphi_j,\mathsf U)
\le3\sum_{n\ge j}L^{-(n-j)}
(C_{\rm reg}\varepsilon_n)^2\#_n(\mathcal L_n)$.
At $j=t_1$ its profile is one. The coefficient at
each layer is therefore at most
\[
 3\left[\bar BL^{-(n-t_1)}
      +B_\sharp\sum_{t_1<j\le n}L^{-(n-j)}\right]
 =3\bar B\le\tfrac{13}4B_\sharp.
\]
This is precisely the profile share of the old scalar
bound, including the initial coefficient displacement.

The regular-leg proof of \cite[Thm.\ D]{QCDM1} bounds
the level-$j$ contribution per cube in $\mathcal L_n$
by $C_{\rm leg}^{\square}L^{(n-j)/4}$ times its
pointed norm at a pointer. It uses the zero cell
moment, covariance, the whole-core invariance and
the coefficient estimate for $q_j(z)$, all supplied
by (G1). The families $R^{(j)}$ and the later families
have the usual size $C_2\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2$ at
each pointer. Their sum is the one included in
$C_{\rm leg}$, since
\[
 \sum_{j\le n}L^{(n-j)/4}\phi(\mathsf t_{j-1})^2
 \le\phi(\mathsf t_{n-1})^2
       \sum_{d\ge0}L^{-3d/4}(1+d\log L)^{2\mathfrak p_0}.
\]
The extra family contributes at most
$C_{\rm leg}^{\square}L^{-1/4}\Lambda_n^\psi(D)
\le C_{\rm leg}^{\square}\mathfrak d^\psi$ per cube.
The mass term has the old bound because
$L^n|s_h|\le\max\{|s_n|,L|s_{n-1}|\}\le L\bar B_M$.
Summing cubes proves the claimed replacements.

The scalar values of $D^{(j)}$ vanish at the trivial
pair. Those of $R^{(j)}$ and later families have zero
infinite-lattice cell mean. Their torus discrepancy
is the difference of wrapping and nonfitting polymers,
with decay at rate $\kappa+1$ and size $E_0$.
The wrapping estimate of \cite[Lem.\ 9.15]{QCDM1}
therefore gives $|\mathfrak f_k|\le C_{\rm fs}$.
For $n>t_1$, its bound on $f_n$ uses only that step:
the vacuum increment, $|e_n|\le C'_e(1+\log x_{n-1})$,
the new scalar size $E_0$, the collar and normalizer,
and $|\log(x_{n-1}/\mathsf t_{n-1})|\le
2\bar B/\mathsf t_{n-1}$. These are unchanged.

The boundary sum is bounded by \cref{C-423-11},
$\mathsf g_j\le E_0$, $|b_j|\le B_\sharp$,
$|\mu_j|\le4\bar B_M/\mathsf t_j\le(1+L)\bar B_M$
and $\bar v_j\le c_{\rm cl}/4$. Its domain count is
unchanged. Adding the stored-factor bound gives
$C_E^{\rm F}\Sigma'(h)$ with the two replacements above.
All its defining terms are affine with nonnegative
coefficients in $E_0$ and $C_{\rm leg}$.

For the measure estimate use the bounded Borel
coefficients and domination in \cref{C-423-4}.
The coordinate-density construction of
\cite[Lem.\ 10.7]{QCDM1} applies coefficient by
coefficient. The even exponentials commute and
$\|e^G\|\le e^{\|G\|}$. In the action write
\[
 -A(\beta_h,\mathsf U)
 =-\beta A(\mathsf U)
   +L^{t_1}(\mathsf t_{t_1}-x_{t_1})A(\mathsf U)
   +\sum_{t_1<j\le k}L^jb_jA(\varphi_j,\mathsf U).
\]
The last terms are bounded by the profile sum already
proved, with no sign restriction on the displacement.
The same argument keeps either the actual profile or
$L^{t_1}x_{t_1}$ as reference coefficient.
Finally the pure-gauge piece estimate used in
\cite[Thm.\ D, proof]{QCDM1} depends only on the
history's canonical background data. It supplies
$e^{-c_\star\sum_tp_0(g_t)^2n_t^{\rm cr}}$ and the
integrable piece majorants. The inequalities
$\Sigma'(h)\le48\Sigma_{\mathcal L}(h)$ and
$\Sigma_{\mathcal L}(h)\le n_k+L^3\Sigma_Z(h)$
then give the integrated bound. No positivity of
the perturbed fermion term has been used.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The induction above the base]\label{C-423-14}
Assume the constants of \cite[Thm.\ D]{QCDM1} and
$(\Gamma^{\rm F})$ in \cref{C-423-8}. Let a flow of
\cref{C-423-9} be given. For every $t_1\le k\le K$
and $h\in\mathcal H_k^{[t_1]}$, its term has identity
$(\mathrm I_k)$ with its actual families, coefficient
$\beta_h=L^{t_1}x_{t_1}
-\sum_{t_1<j\le k}L^jb_j\varphi_j$, stored tower form,
mass profile, and regular constant $\mathfrak f_k$.
Its boundary terms have levels above $t_1$ only and
satisfy \cref{C-423-11}. Its vacuum constant is
\[
 -\mathcal E_{k,\mathcal S}=E_k-\sum_{n\le k}f_n(\mathcal S),
 \qquad f_n=0\quad(n\le t_1).
\]
The exponent is defined and has one value at evaluation
configurations off one null set. Every coefficient of
the measure is dominated by a constant times the pure
history term.

Every next step satisfies (Sm), (Fr),
$\mathsf{sz}_k^\natural\le\varepsilon_\flat$ and
$\bar v_{k+1}\le b_k^{\rm blk}$, as well as the variation
estimate of \cref{C-423-12}. The boundary terms agree
for equal excerpts under the torus floor of
\cref{C-423-16}. All the bounds of \cref{C-423-13} hold.

If the families and numbers depend holomorphically on
a parameter on a domain where (G1)--(G3) hold, the
frame members, outputs, extracted numbers and bounded
Borel coefficient functions are holomorphic there.
The real $x_i$, and hence $b_i$, $\tau$ and the action
weights, are constant on each connected component.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
At $k=t_1$ there is one history. Its identity is
\cref{C-423-4} with
$c=E_{t_1}+\mathfrak f_{t_1}$ and $\sigma=s_{t_1}$.
There is no boundary term, and all earlier frame
hypotheses are empty. The exponent has precisely the
claimed regular and vacuum constants.

Assume the identity at level $k$ and the step bounds
at earlier levels. \Cref{C-423-10} gives (Sm), (Fr)
and the new size bounds. The one-lattice step in
\cref{C-423-7} is the step required by (G2), on the
torus and on the infinite lattice with the same
families and coefficients. Its extraction numbers
are read from the infinite-lattice activity, as in
the definition of the flow. Thus its new family is
$E^{(k+1)}$, and its numbers are
$e_{k+1},b_{k+1},\mu_{k+1}$. These have (F3) and the
required windows by (G1)--(G2). Interior agreement
identifies the same output at every history.
\Cref{C-423-11} supplies the new boundary terms, and
\cref{C-423-7} gives the measure identity at level
$k+1$. The extraction rule adds the new trivial
values to $\mathfrak f_k$ and
$e_{k+1}n_{k+1}$ to $E_k$; its history difference is
$f_{k+1}$. This proves the asserted constants.

The induction gives the hypotheses of
\cref{C-423-16} simultaneously for both histories
being compared, since the flow's families and
numbers are common to all histories. It gives those
of \cref{C-423-12} at every step and
\cref{C-423-13} at every level. The definedness,
common value and domination follow from
\cref{C-423-4,C-423-7}.

For the last assertion, a real-valued holomorphic
coefficient is constant on each connected component.
Thus the Gaussian, quadratic correction, tower and
fermion integration family have no parameter
dependence. The remaining frame members are formed
by linear operations, background substitutions and
earlier boundary terms. The expansion and pointing
are holomorphic in their input potentials, and
extraction is bounded and linear. The cluster part
of a generated boundary term is an output
difference; its strip row is a finite integer
combination of output values. Its other kinds
have no parameter dependence. Edges are formed
from pointed outputs and the holomorphic mass
numbers. Induction therefore proves their
holomorphy. Finally \cref{C-423-4} gives the bounded
Borel coefficient functions, locally uniformly;
the early sizes are bounded by (G3).
\end{proof}

To apply this theorem to \cref{C-418-18}, take $t_1=t_b$.
The norms of \cref{C-418-4} are exactly the two sizes
in \cref{C-423-2}, with the maximum over both lattices.
The zero cell moments, joint invariance and translation
covariance in the hypotheses of \cref{C-418-18} give
(F3): the zeroth moment commutes with colour by
constant gauge invariance, is periodic by covariance,
and its cell sum is the stipulated zero moment.
The other structural hypotheses give (F1), (F2),
and (F4), and the pointed sum rule and scalar
normalization give (G1). The post-base step and
pointed-size hypotheses are (G2); its split into
$R+D$ and the lag sums are (G3). Its history measures
are the measures in \cref{C-423-9}, since both start
with the same density and apply the same subsequent
weights and partial kernels.

The linear-entry assertion of \cref{C-418-18} is
\cref{C-423-12}; its history induction and locality
are \cref{C-423-14}; its scalar, leg and integrated
estimates are \cref{C-423-13}. Per layer cube the
additional leg contribution is
$C_{\rm leg}^{\square}L^{-1/4}\Lambda_m^\psi(D)$.
When $D=0$ both replacements vanish, so the constants
reduce to the original upper-history constants.
The parameter assertion includes the necessary
constancy of the real action coefficients.

\subsection{Scalar estimates with a prescribed past}\label{C-424-1}

The scalar estimates retain the size of each early level.
This is needed because an interpolation may have large individual
early terms while its weighted sum at the base is small.

\begin{definition}[Levels and histories]\label{C-424-2}
Fix \(1\le u<s<K\), and put \(t_1=K-u\), \(t_0=K-s\).
We use \(\mathcal H_k[t_1]\) from \cref{C-422-2}:
its histories agree with \(h_\emptyset^{(t_1)}\) through \(t_1\).
For numbers \(a_j\ge0\), \(j\le t_1\), write
\[
 \Lambda_n^0[a]=\sum_{j\le t_1}L^{-(n-j)}a_j,\qquad n\ge t_1.
\]
Thus \(\Lambda_n^0[a]=L^{-(n-t_1)}\Lambda_{t_1}^0[a]\).
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[The early regions]\label{C-424-3}
For \(h\in\mathcal H_k[t_1]\), the regions through \(t_1\)
are the torus. All early pairs are regular, the layers below
\(t_1\) are empty, and no boundary or edge term is generated
through \(t_1\). Boundary terms and the corresponding vacuum
corrections therefore have levels strictly greater than \(t_1\).
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
These are the geometric statements of \cref{C-423-3}.
They depend on the regions of the history and not on the
activities inserted in its exponent.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Scalar sums by level]\label{C-424-4}
Assume the geometric, regularity, and domain hypotheses for
the scalar sums in \cite[Prop.\ 64.2]{YMM1}.
At level \(j\), let
\(e_j\) bound the pointed scalar terms at rate \(\kappa+1\);
let \(B_j e^{-\kappa d(X)}\) bound each generated boundary
term. Let \(C_{\rm ly}\ge1\) be the regular-field constant.
For a history evaluation these hypotheses are applied to
the glued field, with \(C_{\rm ly}=C_{\rm reg}\).
Write
\[
 N_n=\#_n(\mathcal L_n),\qquad
 A_n=\sum_{j\le n}L^{-(n-j)}e_j.
\]
For a level-\(j\) pointer \(z\) lying in \(\mathcal L_n\),
\[
 \sum_{X:\,z\in X\subset\Lambda_j}
 |E_j(X,U,z)-E_j(X,1,z)|
 \le e_jL^{-4(n-j)}
   \min\{C_a^{\rm sc},
          C_a'{}^{\rm sc}(C_{\rm ly}\epsilon_n/\alpha_0)^2\}.
\]
The regular sum of level \(j\) is consequently at most
\[
 C_a^{\rm sc}e_j\sum_{n\ge j}L^{-(n-j)}N_n,
\]
with the corresponding curvature factor available term by term.
The profile term satisfies
\[
 L^jA_{\varphi_j}\le
 3\sum_{n\ge j}L^{-(n-j)}(C_{\rm ly}\epsilon_n)^2N_n.
\]
The boundary and edge terms of level \(j\) have total norm at most
\[
 C_f' (B_j+8M^3e_j)M^{-3}\#_j(\widetilde Z_j)
 \le27C_f'(M^{-3}B_j+8e_j)\#_j(Z_j).
\]
In particular, if \(|b'_j|\le B_\sharp\), then
\begin{align*}
 |\text{regular sum}|+|\text{boundary sum}|
 \le{}&\sum_n
 \left[C_a^{\rm sc}A_n+
       \tfrac{13}4 B_\sharp(C_{\rm ly}\epsilon_n)^2\right]N_n\\
 &+27C_f'\sum_j(M^{-3}B_j+8e_j)\#_j(Z_j).
\end{align*}
The increments \(b'_j\) may be complex.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Apply the scalar estimate of \cite[Prop.\ 64.2]{YMM1}
to the array with its sole nonzero entry at level \(j\).
Zero entries satisfy the local-term conditions, so this gives
the first estimate with \(e_j\) in place of its common bound.
Counting the level-\(j\) pointers in a level-\(n\) cube costs
\(L^{3(n-j)}\); the factor \(L^{-4(n-j)}\) therefore leaves
\(L^{-(n-j)}\). This proves the regular estimate.
The profile estimate in that proof is geometric and does not use
the increments. Multiplication by \(|b'_j|\) thus permits complex
increments. The boundary count uses the generated terms through
\(B_j\), and the edge terms through \(8M^3e_j\).
At an evaluation configuration the same scalar proof applies to
the glued field, with \(C_{\rm ly}=C_{\rm reg}\);
the bounds on generated terms are coefficient bounds there.

Finally interchange the finite sums over \(j,n\).
For the profiles use
\(3\sum_{j\le n}L^{-(n-j)}\le3L/(L-1)\le13/4\).
The other two terms are exactly the displayed sums.
No sign of an activity or increment enters these estimates.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The early scalar sum]\label{C-424-5}
Suppose \(\Lambda_j=\mathbb T_\ell\) for every \(1\le j\le t\).
Then the layers below \(t\) are empty, and the contribution of
levels \(j\le t\) to the regular sum is at most
\[
 C_a^{\rm sc}A_t\sum_{n\ge t}L^{-(n-t)}N_n.
\]
The curvature version of \cref{C-424-4} holds as well.
There is no early boundary contribution.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
For \(n\ge t\),
\(\sum_{j\le t}L^{-(n-j)}e_j=L^{-(n-t)}A_t\).
The boundary sets of those levels are empty by
\cref{C-424-3}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The steps at the interpolation parameter}

\begin{definition}[The interpolated flow]\label{C-424-8}
Let the data be as in \cref{C-424-6}, and put
\(w_\lambda=w+\lambda w^\Delta(s)\).
For the step estimates below, take \(z\in\mathcal O\), \(s=s(z)\), and
\(|\lambda|<r_\lambda\).
The early arrays are \(E^{(j)}(s)+\lambda\Delta^{(j)}(s)\).
Above \(t_1\) use the small-field step with these earlier
arrays, the fine mass \(m_0-a_K\widehat J\), and the
zero-source reference. Extract the ordinary numbers
\(e_j,b_j,\mu_j\); form the mass increment from the moments
relative to that reference. The scalar source energy is
\[
 e_j(X;\mathfrak c)=
       \mathfrak E_j(X;\mathfrak c)-\mathfrak E_j(X;0).
\]
Start with
\(\sigma_{t_1}(s,\lambda)=\sigma_{t_1}(s)+\lambda\delta\sigma(s)\);
below \(t_1\) keep the source chain. Above it set
\[
 \sigma_{j+1}(s,\lambda)(x)=L\sigma_j(s,\lambda)(x)
     +\nu_{j+1}(y_{j+1}(x);\mathfrak c_j(s,\lambda))
     -\mu_{j+1}.
\]
The vacuum energy is
\[
 E_k(s,\lambda)=E_{t_1}(s)+\lambda\mathfrak n(s)
       +\sum_{t_1<j\le k}
          \left[e_jn_j+\sum_Xe_j(X;\mathfrak c_{j-1}(s,\lambda))\right].
\]
For a history use the same start and only the pieces with
polymer inside \(\Lambda_j\) in its increment \(\nu_j^h\).
Its coordinates use \(\sigma_j^h\) on \(\Omega_j\) and
\(\sigma_j\) off \(\Omega_j\). All these rules are applied
only while the indicated steps are defined.

We use three induction conditions.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \((\mathrm{Int}_i)[s,\lambda;h]\) means that the step
from \(i\) at the history coordinates belongs to the fixed
pair domain \(2\mathscr D_i(\alpha_0)\), has
\(\|\mathcal V_0\|\le c_{\rm cl}/2\) and
\(\|\mathcal V_\psi\|\le b^{\rm blk,s}(\gamma)\), and produces
the local, Borel, holomorphic pointed activities of
\cref{C-422-8}. Their scalar pointer bound is \(E_0^{\rm s}\)
at rate \(\kappa+1\). The scalar fluctuation norm uses
\(\tau_i^\lambda=\max\{\tau_i(w;\alpha_0),\tau_i(w_\lambda;\alpha_0)\}\).
\item \((\mathrm{Sh}_k)[s,\lambda;h']\) means that the first
seven fermion classes of the step along \(h'\) have total
size at most \(b^{\rm tot,s}(\gamma)\), on every tier at
rate \(r_V\) and every external-field box.
\item \(\mathsf I^{\rm F}(k)[s,\lambda]\) is the representation
and the eight bounds of \cref{C-422-12}, now for the measures
of \cref{C-424-7}. Its gauge weight is
\(\beta_k-a_K^{-1}w_\lambda\), its mass field is
\[
 s_h+\sigma_h(s,\lambda),\qquad
 \sigma_h=L^{-t_1}\sigma_{t_1}(s,\lambda)
             +\sum_{t_1<j\le k}L^{-j}(\nu_j^h-\mu_j)\varphi_j,
\]
and its early arrays are those above. All generated boundary
terms have levels greater than \(t_1\).
The frame bound is \(64b^{\rm tot,s}(\gamma)/51\).
Its vacuum label is
\[
 -\mathcal E_h=E_k(s,\lambda)-\sum_{t_1<n\le k}f_n(h)
                                  +\sum_{t_1<n\le k}g_n(h;s,\lambda),
 \qquad |g_n|\le C'_{\mathfrak E}\#_n(\widetilde Z_n).
\]
The other bounds are the ordinary sourced bounds, including
the kept halves, the loss in the gauge action, the stored
factors, and the coefficientwise norm of the exponent.
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[The scalar regular sum]\label{C-424-9}
Suppose \((\mathrm{Int}_i)[s,\lambda;h]\) holds for
\(t_1\le i<k\). At every evaluation configuration of
\(h\in\mathcal H_k[t_1]\), the scalar regular sum and
the absolute profile terms are together at most
\[
 \left[\tfrac{13}{12}C_a^{\rm sc}E_0^{\rm s}
       +C_a^{\rm sc}|\lambda|\Lambda_{t_1}^0[\rho(s)]
       +\tfrac{13}4B_\sharp\right]\Sigma_{\mathcal L}(h)
 \le C_5^{\rm s}\Sigma_{\mathcal L}(h).
\]
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Apply \cref{C-424-4,C-424-5} with
\(e_j=E_0^{\rm s}+|\lambda|\rho_j\) for \(j\le t_1\)
and \(e_j=E_0^{\rm s}\) otherwise.
The ordinary part sums to at most \(13E_0^{\rm s}/12\).
The extra part is at most \(c_0^\Delta\le M^{-3}\mathsf B\).
The admitted curvature factor is at most one.
Since
\[
 C_m^{\rm sc}=\tfrac{13}{12}C_a^{\rm sc}+432C_f'+\tfrac{13}4,
 \qquad
 C_5^{\rm s}=C_m^{\rm sc}(E_0^{\rm s}+B_\sharp+M^{-3}\mathsf B),
\]
the stated bound follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The scalar class]\label{C-424-10}
Under the interior and boundary hypotheses of
\cref{C-424-8}, form the scalar list from the early arrays,
the later activities, and the boundary terms already generated.
The counterterm at the early levels is zero.
Then its class \({\rm rg}\), including the gauge-weight
terms of order at least three, has size at most
\(\varepsilon_\flat\).
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The coefficient of a scalar entry from level \(j\), in the
regular-frame bound of \cite[Prop.\ 58.22]{YMM1}, is
\[
 C_{\rm ert}L^{-(k-j)}
                   \sum_{i=0}^{k-j}L^i\varpi_i.
\]
Writing \(C'_h=\sum_{i\ge0}(i+1)L^i\varpi_i\) and
\(C_{\rm sz}=LC'_h/(L-1)\), its total gives
\[
 \mathsf{size}^E
 \le C_{\rm sz}C_{\rm ert}
 \left[E_0^{\rm s}+\alpha_0^2B_\sharp
       +(1-L^{-1})L^{-(k-t_1)}
                        |\lambda|\Lambda_{t_1}^0[\rho(s)]\right].
\]
Hence this is at most
\(C_{\rm sz}C_{\rm ert}(E_0^{\rm s}+c_0^\Delta+
\alpha_0^2B_\sharp)\). The regular-frame estimate proved in
\cref{C-422-11} applies, because
\(E_0^{\rm s}+c_0^\Delta\le\sqrt2E_0^{\rm s}\).
The doubled source ceiling leaves \(\varepsilon_\flat/2\)
for these terms. The terms of order at least three cost the
remaining \(\varepsilon_\flat/2\), since
\((w_\lambda,J)\in\mathcal P\).
Empty edge and counterterm lists are allowed; generated terms
enter only above the base. Thus the scalar-list hypotheses
used in that estimate are unchanged.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The fermion frame recursion]\label{C-424-11}
Assume \((\mathrm{Sh}_k)\), the preceding interior conditions,
and the boundary clause of \(\mathsf I^{\rm F}(k)\).
Let \(\Sigma^\natural_k\) and \(v_k\) be the largest frame
and insertion sizes of levels \(t_1<j\le k\), with value
zero if there are no such levels. Then
\[
 \mathsf{sz}_{k+1}^\natural
 \le\tfrac{13}{64}\max\{\Sigma^\natural_k,v_k\}
                                      +b^{\rm tot,s}(\gamma)
 \le\tfrac{64}{51}b^{\rm tot,s}(\gamma)
 \le\tfrac{16}{17}\varepsilon_\flat.
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The first seven classes are bounded by \((\mathrm{Sh}_k)\).
The eighth and ninth read the previously generated terms with
factor \((1/8)(9/8)\); the tenth has factor \(1/16\).
Their sum is \(13/64\), as in \cref{C-422-11}.
There is no generated term below the base, and
\(v_k\le b^{\rm blk,s}(\gamma)\le b^{\rm tot,s}(\gamma)\).
The inequality \(13/51+1=64/51\) closes the recursion.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Agreement in the interior]\label{C-424-12}
Suppose the conditions in \cref{C-424-8} hold through the
step from \(k\) to \(t=k+1\). For \(X\subset\Lambda_t\),
the terms, activities, and cluster sums of the history step
are those of the small-field step at its history coordinates.
The cluster sum is
\[
 E^{\rm lab}(X)=\mathbf G^v(X)+\widetilde E(X).
\]
The pointed outputs are the pointed activities of that step,
with the bounds in \((\mathrm{Int}_k)\).
In a frame without a centered origin, with at most four classes
each of size at most \(\epsilon_\flat\), the first variation
of an even analytic insertion \(W\) on the tiers has bound
\[
 K^{\rm lb}\|W\|_{r_V}e^{-\kappa''d_t(X)}.
\]
In the small-field polymer norm the corresponding bound is
\(4K_M\|W\|\).
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Inside \(\Lambda_t\) all profiles equal one, the decoupled
mean vanishes, and there is no edge or boundary term.
Both steps use the same gauge covariance, fermion covariance,
fine mass, scalar list, and background maps. Their mass member
is \(-L^{-k}\mathsf S_1((s_k+\sigma_k^h)\psi^{\rm bg})\).
Every early array is read at all its regular pointers.

At center zero the two centered terms satisfy
\(\mathbb W^{\rm q}+\mathbb W^{\rm l}
=\mathcal V^v+\mathcal V^{\rm lin}\), and
\(\mathbb W^\times=0\). Merge their origins in the multilinear
cluster series. This gives the same terms as the small-field
series. The Gaussian origin is
\(\mathcal V^{\rm q}+\mathcal V^v\), so its contribution is
\(\mathbf G^v\). The linear term remains in the scalar potential.
Pointing and differentiation of a finite insertion commute
with the locally uniformly convergent series.
This proves the identities, including their normalization,
by the argument of \cite[Lem.\ 9.10 and Prop.\ 10.14]{QCDM1}.

For the norm estimate, the potential on the interpolation path
has size at most \((1/2+1/8)c_{\rm cl}\).
Add \(\zeta c_{\rm cl}W/(4\|W\|)\).
For \(|\zeta|<3/2\) it remains below \(c_{\rm cl}\);
on \(|\zeta|=1\) it is at most \(7c_{\rm cl}/8\).
The test tail costs at most \(c_{\rm cl}/16\).
Cauchy's estimate therefore gives
\((15/4)K'_M\|W\|\le4K_M\|W\|\).
Under the stated restrictions on the frame and insertion,
the same insertion in the joined frame gives the stated
\(K^{\rm lb}\) bound and its exponential polymer factor.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The centered history frame]\label{C-424-13}
Assume \(\mathsf I^{\rm F}(k)[s,\lambda]\),
\((\mathrm{Int}_i)[s,\lambda;h]\) for \(t_1\le i\le k\),
and \((\mathrm{Sh}_k)[s,\lambda;h']\), where
\(h'=(h,\mathsf o)\in\mathcal H_{k+1}[t_1]\).
The step has a centered frame, with the constants of
\cite[Lem.\ 10.12]{QCDM1}.
For \(v'=-w_\lambda/\mathsf b\), its centered members satisfy
\[
 \|\mathbb W^{\rm q}+\mathbb W^{\rm l}\|_{{\rm I}\star,r_V}^{\rm rad}
 \le\mathsf k_\odot(\sigma_s+\varrho_s'g_k)
 \le\tfrac12\mathsf m_\odot,\qquad
 \|\mathbb W^\times\|_{{\rm I}\star,r_V}^{\rm rad}
 \le C_{\rm cr}^{V}\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}A_1\varrho\,
       \mathsf t_k^{-1}(\log\mathsf t_k)^{\mathfrak p_0}
 \le\tfrac14c_M^{\rm O}.
\]
The centered class has size at most \(c_M^{\rm O}\).
The other four classes have sizes
\[
 \mathsf{sz}^{\rm rg}\le\varepsilon_\flat,\quad
 \mathsf{sz}^{\rm bd}\le\tfrac12\varepsilon_\flat,\quad
 \mathsf{sz}^{\rm q}\le\varepsilon_\flat,\quad
 \mathsf{sz}^\natural\le\tfrac{16}{17}\varepsilon_\flat.
\]
Their amplitude obeys
\[
 \varepsilon_{\mathsf w}^{\mathfrak F+}L^3
       \le\frac5{32\mathsf K_{\rm ap}^{+}},\qquad
 \mathsf b_{\rm cs}^{\mathfrak F+}\le\tfrac9{32}.
\]
The cluster sums are Borel coefficientwise, analytic, local,
jointly gauge invariant, and functions of the pair.
For \(X\not\subset\Lambda_{k+1}\), the full cluster sum
and its Gaussian part each have bound
\(9e^{-\kappa''d_{k+1}(X)}/32\). Their difference has bound
\(9e^{-\kappa''d_{k+1}(X)}/16\), and its part with generators
has bound
\[
 K^{\rm lb}\mathsf{sz}_{k+1}^{\natural}
                                    e^{-\kappa''d_{k+1}(X)}.
\]
For \(X\subset\Lambda_{k+1}\), \cref{C-424-12} applies.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The centered terms read the source only through its weight.
Here
\[
 \sup|v'|\le2\varrho/\mathsf b\le\sigma_s,\qquad
 \mathsf t_k|v'(p)-v'(p')|
       \le\sqrt3M\operatorname{Lip}(w_\lambda)\le\varrho_s'
\]
for the neighboring plaquettes in the centered-frame proof.
These follow from \(\|w_\lambda\|_\sharp\le2\varrho\).
The proof of \cite[Lem.\ 10.12]{QCDM1} therefore gives the
centered estimates on exactly the same tiers.

The regular class is \cref{C-424-10}. The boundary class
uses the generated-term bound \(\mathsf B_\natural\),
the formed-factor bound \(\mathsf B_{\rm fr}^{\flat}+1\),
and \(8M^3E_0^{\rm s}\le\mathsf B_\natural\) for its edges.
These are clauses of \(\mathsf I^{\rm F}(k)\); no early
edge occurs. The quadratic class is the source-independent
class of \(\mathcal V^{\rm q}\). The fermion class is
\cref{C-424-11}.

Analyticity on the tiers follows as in the last paragraph of
the proof of \cref{C-422-11}. In the first seven classes,
the old arrays are holomorphic on the fixed cores and the
mass coefficient is independent of the configuration.
The last three classes use later boundary coefficients,
their background legs, the fixed leveling functions and shifts,
and the same substituted triples as the ordinary frame.
These operations preserve the pair dependence and give locally
uniform series. They also preserve the Borel and invariance
properties. The source-dependent normalizer is the one at
the fine mass \(m_0-a_K\widehat J\).

The four sizes sum to less than \(6\varepsilon_\flat\).
The choices of the ordinary frame constants give
\[
 6e\varepsilon_\flat L^3=\frac3{32\mathsf K_{\rm ap}^{\max}}
       \le\frac3{32\mathsf K_{\rm ap}^{+}},\qquad
 e(w_0^{\rm O})^{-1}c_M^{\rm O}L^3
       =\frac1{16\mathsf K_{\rm ap}^{+}}.
\]
Thus the amplitude is at most \(5/(32\mathsf K_{\rm ap}^{+})\);
adding the centered contribution \(1/8\) gives \(9/32\).
The joined expansion in \cite[Lem.\ 9.1]{QCDM1} uses only
these sizes and the ordinary fermion Gaussian properties.
It proves the stated bounds, also for the Gaussian subframe
and for the marked class with generators.
Its termwise operations give all the stated regularity properties.
The interior identity is \cref{C-424-12}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The step as an identity of measures]\label{C-424-14}
Under the hypotheses of \cref{C-424-13}, the term of \(h'\)
has, coefficientwise off one null set, the representation
\[
 \widehat\tau_{h'}^{\rm F}[s,\lambda]
 =\mathsf{Stay}_{h'}\mathbf1_{h'}^{\rm T}
   \chi_{k+1}(\Omega_{k+1})e^{\boldsymbol\Phi^w_{h'}}
   \exp[A_{k+1,h'}^{\rm F}(s,\lambda)]\,\mathscr M_{h'}.
\]
The exponent is the one produced by the step in
\cref{C-424-8}, with action weight
\(\beta_{k+1}-a_K^{-1}w_\lambda\), the updated mass field,
the new pointed activities in the regular region, and the
generated boundary terms elsewhere. Its density is Borel
and integrable in the fibre norm, and the exponent takes
one value on each evaluation set off the null set.
The free-coordinate density properties of
\cite[Lem.\ 10.7]{QCDM1} hold.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Apply the exact coordinate identity of
\cite[Thm.\ AH]{YMM1} coefficientwise, as in
\cite[Prop.\ 10.14]{QCDM1}. Its geometric chain and
change-of-variables conditions are independent of the parameters.
The Gaussian normalizers use the fine mass of \(s\).
The weighted Wilson identity holds for every plaquette weight,
here \(w_\lambda\). All arrays are jointly gauge invariant;
the added mass matrices commute with colour.
Thus the source and the exponent take one value on evaluation
sets. The expansion condition is \cref{C-424-13}.

The terms themselves have the required transport identity by
\cref{C-424-7}: the next partial Berezin kernel acts on the
preceding transported density, and the new scalar tests multiply
its weight. The representation at level \(k\) supplies the
remaining hypothesis of the coordinate identity.
Inside \(\Lambda_{k+1}\), extraction removes \(e_{k+1},b_{k+1}\),
the source energies, and the restricted moment
\(-L^{-(k+1)}\mathsf S_1(\nu_{k+1}^{h'}\psi^{\rm bg})\).
The profiles return the mass increment and \(b_{k+1}\)
to the mass field and action. Their residual terms are precisely
the edge terms. This gives the displayed exponent.

For integrability first apply Tonelli to its fibre norm and
then Fubini to each coefficient. Every coefficient measure
in \cref{C-424-7} is dominated by the positive scalar reference
measure. Its null sets therefore suffice for the complex
parameters as well. The finite Grassmann exponential is invertible,
so the algebraic identities pass to the exponential representation.
All new coefficients are finite products or locally uniform limits
of Borel coefficients; the source exponent is continuous in the
gauge field. This proves Borel measurability.
The one-value property just checked and the free-coordinate
change of variables prove the last assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[A history step at the parameter]\label{C-424-15}
If \(\mathsf I^{\rm F}(k)[s,\lambda]\) holds and every
prolongation \(h'\) satisfies the interior and share conditions
of \cref{C-424-13}, then its next term has the representation
of \cref{C-424-14}, the frame and output bounds of
\cref{C-424-13}, and the scalar regular-sum bound of
\cref{C-424-9}. Its measure is holomorphic in the source
parameters and \(\lambda\). The total integral satisfies
\(Z_{k+1}(z,\lambda')=Z_{t_1}(z,\lambda')\) for every
\(\lambda'\in\mathbb C\).
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The first assertions have just been proved.
The regular activities through level \(k+1\) are produced
by the same steps along \(h\) and \(h'\), since their regions
through \(k\) agree. Thus \cref{C-424-9} applies at the next
level. Holomorphy of the coefficient measures follows from
\cref{C-424-7}; preservation of the scalar integral follows
from \cref{C-424-20}. Neither of these measure assertions
requires the small parameter disc used for the RG bounds.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Closing the induction}

\begin{remark}[The scalar allowance]\label{C-424-16}
All constants used here were fixed in \cref{C-422-16}.
In particular \(c_0^\Delta\) satisfies four inequalities:
\[
 c_0^\Delta\le M^{-3}\mathsf B,\quad
 c_0^\Delta\le(\sqrt2-1)E_0^{\rm s},\quad
 c_0^\Delta\le\tfrac5{12}K_M^\bullet c_{\rm cl},\quad
 c_0^\Delta\le
 \frac{\alpha_0 C_w^{\rm s}}
 {16\sqrt2K_M^\bullet K_\Lambda^{\rm s}\mathsf C_{\mathcal A}A_1}.
\]
The first bounds the scalar regular sum; the second admits
its regular frame. The last two leave room for the extra
scalar array in the one-step potential and its new activity.
They impose no later restriction on previously chosen constants.
The only additional lower bounds on the ordinary constants
are the two regular-sum bounds in
\eqref{eq:free-history-leg-floor}.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[A closed datum]\label{C-424-23}
Let \(R>0\), and set
\[
 \mathrm P(R)=\{|\lambda|<R\},\qquad
 R_k=R Q_\sigma^{-(k-t_1)},\qquad Q_\sigma=2\sqrt L+\tfrac14.
\]
A closed datum over \(\mathcal O\) consists of the objects
of \cref{C-424-6}, with the following requirements at every
\(s=s(z)\).
The extraction data \(F_j(s),G_j(s),\nu_j(s)\) and the
infinite-lattice reference \(G_j^\infty(s)\) of
\cref{C-422-3} are holomorphic in \(z\), coefficientwise
at every pair, with locally uniform bounds.
Their quadratic terms have one barred and one unbarred field.
The matrix cell sums of \(G_j^\infty\), including its mass
forms, vanish. The same walks are used in \(F_j,G_j\);
on a torus the moved moments use only the permitted polymers
of diameter less than a quarter of the side.
The size \(r_j^\psi(s)\) bounds the sums of summand norms
at the point, the reference, and the infinite-lattice reference,
and \(c_{\mathsf S}h_F^2|\nu_j(s)|\), as in \cref{C-422-3}.
Finally require
\begin{equation}\label{eq:closed-datum-lags}
\begin{aligned}
 R\Sigma_k^\psi(s)&\le c_\psi^\Delta\phi_{k-1},
 &\Sigma_k^\psi(s)&=\sum_{j\le t_1}\omega_{k+1-j}r_j^\psi(s)
                                      &&(t_1\le k\le K),\\
 R\Lambda_{t_1}^0[\rho(s)]&\le c_0^\Delta,
 &R\|\delta\sigma(s)\|&\le\tfrac12B_\sigma\phi_{t_1},\\
 (w+\lambda w^\Delta(s),J)&\in\mathcal P
                                      &&(|\lambda|<R).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
These imply the conditions of \cref{C-424-6} at every
radius \(r_\lambda\le R\).
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Sizes of the early arrays]\label{C-424-24}
Let a closed datum be given. For \(t_1\le n\le K\),
put
\[
 \epsilon_j[\lambda]=
 \begin{cases}
 \epsilon_j^{{\rm s},\psi}(\alpha_0)+|\lambda|r_j^\psi(s),
                                                      &j\le t_1,\\
 \epsilon_j,&t_1<j\le n,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 \Phi_n=\sum_{j\le n}\omega_{n+1-j}\phi_{j-1},
\]
where \(\epsilon_j\le(2C_w^{\rm s}-C_w)\phi_{j-1}\).
The early array \(E^{(j)}(s)+\lambda\Delta^{(j)}(s)\)
is formed by the extraction rule from
\[
 \bigl(\widetilde E_{\ge2}^{(j)}(\mathfrak c_{j-1}(s))+\lambda F_j(s),
       \widetilde E_{\ge2}^{(j)}(0)+\lambda G_j(s),
       \mu_j+\lambda\nu_j(s)\bigr).
\]
Its infinite-lattice reference has zero matrix cell sums.
Its summand norms, including both reference families, are
