The proof is the Gaussian-part comparison in
\cite[Prop. 124.5]{YMM1}, with the two potential
origins zero. It applies to the present quadratic
system: \(3/4\le\tau_i\le4/3\), its precision has
the stated uniform gap, and it is the admitted
Gaussian system at scale zero in \cref{C-350-7}.
Cauchy's formula and the sum over polymers anchored
at one insertion give the claimed \(\epsilon_i\).
Odd moments vanish by symmetry.

In an orthonormal colour basis put
\[
 F_i^\alpha(p)=x_i^{-1/2}(\mathsf T_iB_i)^\alpha(p),
 \quad c_i^{\alpha\beta}(p,q)
       =\langle F_i^\alpha(p)F_i^\beta(q)\rangle,
 \quad
 \kappa_i^{\alpha\beta}(p,q)
       =\kappa(F_i^\alpha(p),F_i^\alpha(p),
                    F_i^\beta(q),F_i^\beta(q)).
\]
Independence across levels and the moment--cumulant
identity give
\[
 \langle q_1;q_2\rangle
 =\tfrac14a_K^{-2}\sum_{p,q}w_1(p)w_2(q)
  \sum_{\alpha,\beta}
   \left\{2\left(\sum_i c_i^{\alpha\beta}(p,q)\right)^2
                       +\sum_i\kappa_i^{\alpha\beta}(p,q)\right\}.
\]
The slice identity \cite[Prop. 120.3]{YMM1} is
\[
 \mathsf T_i\mathsf M_i^{-1}\mathsf T_i^{\mathsf T}
       =L^{-i}\tau_i^{-1}\mathcal C_{(i+1)}.
\]
Since \(x_i^{-1}L^{-i}\tau_i^{-1}=\beta^{-1}\),
the Gaussian covariance in the last formula is
\(\delta_{\alpha\beta}\beta^{-1}\mathcal C_{(i+1)}\).
Its Gaussian value is therefore
\[
 \tfrac32b^{-2}\sum_{p,q}w_1(p)w_2(q)\Sigma(p,q)^2,
 \qquad
 \Sigma=\sum_{1\le i<n}\mathcal C_{(i+1)}
                 =C^{\rm fl}_{K,K-n}-\mathcal C_{(1)}.
\]

Let \(C_{\rm row}\) be the row-sum constant of
\cite[Prop. 120.6]{YMM1}:
\(\sup_p\sum_b|\mathsf T_i(p,b)|\le C_{\rm row}L^{-2i}\).
Multilinearity gives
\[
 |c_i^{\alpha\beta}
       -\delta_{\alpha\beta}\beta^{-1}\mathcal C_{(i+1)}|
       \le\tfrac43C_{\rm row}^2\beta^{-1}L^{-3i}\epsilon_i,
 \qquad
 |\kappa_i^{\alpha\beta}|
       \le\tfrac{16}9C_{\rm row}^4\beta^{-2}L^{-6i}\epsilon_i.
\]
There are at most \(35^2(d/a_K)^6\) contributing
plaquette pairs. Put \(u_i=d/D_i\),
\(E_k=\sum_{1\le i<n}u_i^k\epsilon_i\), and
\[
 S_\Sigma=\sup_{u>0}\sum_{s\in\mathbb Z}
                  (uL^s)^3e^{-\delta_{\rm tp}uL^s/\sqrt3}<\infty.
\]
On those pairs the slice bound gives
\((d/a_K)^3(|\Sigma|+|\mathcal C_{(1)}|)
 \le C_{\rm tp}S_\Sigma\).
Expanding the square now bounds the test-removal
error by
\[
 \frac{35^2}{4}b^{-2}
 \{16C_{\rm tp}S_\Sigma C_{\rm row}^2E_3
         +32C_{\rm row}^4E_3^2+16C_{\rm row}^4E_6\}\eta.
\]

For \(D_i<d\), write
\(\log(3b/(4D_i))=\Lambda_b+\log u_i\),
where \(\Lambda_b=\log(3b/(4d))\).
Then \((\Lambda_b+t)^2\ge\Lambda_b^2+t^2\), and
the \(\log u_i\) are spaced by \(\log L\).
The sum is bounded using the finite number
\[
 S_\chi=\sup_{t_0\ge0}\sum_{s\ge0}
       e^{6(t_0+s\log L)-c_\chi(t_0+s\log L)^2}.
\]
For \(d\le D_i\le d^{1/2}\), use
\(\sum u_i^3\le2\) and
\(\epsilon_i\le C_\chi
 e^{-c_\chi\{\log(3b/(4d^{1/2}))\}^2}\).
For \(D_i>d^{1/2}\), use
\(\sum u_i^3\le2d^{3/2}\).
Thus, for \(k=3,6\),
\[
 E_k\le C_\chi(S_\chi+2)
       \left[d^{3/2}
          +e^{-c_\chi\{\log(3b/(4d^{1/2}))\}^2}\right].
\]
This proves the term with \(C_{\rm Bx}\).
The omitted first slice has
\[
 (d/a_K)^3|\mathcal C_{(1)}(p,q)|
 \le C_{\rm tp}(d/a_K)^3
                     e^{-\delta_{\rm tp}d/(\sqrt3a_K)}.
\]
Together with \eqref{eq:pure-fourth-gaussian-reduction}
it gives the term with \(C_{\rm Bt}\).

Finally the squared-template estimate
\cite[Prop. 121.2]{YMM1}, including its slice-tail
bound, gives
\[
 \left|\sum_{p,q}w_1(p)w_2(q)
          (C^{\rm fl}_{K,K-n}(p,q))^2
          -\frac3{8\pi^2}\mathcal K_6(f,h)\right|
 \le C_{\rm tm}
       \left[\frac{a_K}{\vartheta d}
                  +(d/\ell)^3+(d/D_n)^3\right]\eta.
\]
Take \(n=K\), so \(D_n=1\).
The colour factor is
\(\tfrac32\cdot3/(8\pi^2)=c_2\).
Use \(d/a_K\ge L(\log(1/d))^2\), and write
\(b^{-2}=(b/d)b^{-3}d\); this gives the stated
\(\bar\epsilon_4\).
Its Gaussian-logarithmic exponentials decrease
faster than any power of \(d\), uniformly for
\(g^{-2}<b'\le b_+(g)\). The slowest remaining
term is \(b'd^{1/2}\), proving
\(\bar\epsilon_4(g,d)\le C_4(g)d^{1/2}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:pure-total-taylor-remainder}
In the setting of \cref{C-350-7}, write
\(\mathsf J_2=\sum_{j=1}^K\mathsf n_j^1\) and
\(\mathsf h_{2m}=\mathsf h_{2m}^{(K)}\).
There is a constant \(C_E\), depending only on the
construction constants, such that
\[
 |\mathsf h_{2m}|\le C_Eb^{-m}d^{m-2}l^{2mp_0}\eta
       \quad(m=2,3),\qquad
 |\mathsf J_2-\mathsf h_4-\mathsf h_6|
       \le C_Eb^{-4}d^2l^{8p_0}\eta.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
If an even holomorphic function \(H\) is bounded by
\(B\) on \(|\lambda|<R\), then
\[
 |H_{[2m]}|\le BR^{-2m},\qquad
 \left|H(1)-\sum_{m=0}^pH_{[2m]}\right|
       \le\frac{BR^{-2p-2}}{1-R^{-2}}.
\]
Apply these inequalities to \(\mathsf n_{j+1}^\lambda\)
on the disc of radius \(\rho R_j\). Its squared radius
is at least two. The bound in \cref{C-350-7}, evaluated
on that disc, therefore gives
\[
 c\,b^{-m}(\log x_j)^{2mp_0}
          D_j^{m-2}\chi_j\Pi_{j+1}\eta
\]
for its coefficient of order \(2m\), and the same
expression with \(m=4\) for its remainder after
order six. The coefficients of orders zero and two
vanish.

For \(D_j\ge d\), one has \(\Pi_{j+1}=1\),
\(\log x_j\le l\), and
\[
 D_j^{m-2}\chi_j
       =d^{m-2}(d/D_j)^{5/2-(m-2)}.
\]
The exponents are \(5/2,3/2,1/2\) for \(m=2,3,4\);
each gives a convergent geometric sum. For \(D_j<d\),
write \(D_j/d\) as a power of \(L^{-1}\), up to a
factor in \([1,L]\). The factor \(\Pi_{j+1}\) decays
exponentially in \(d/D_j\), whereas the other factors
grow by powers of \(d/D_j\) and \(\log(d/D_j)\).
Their sum is bounded by a constant times
\(d^{m-2}l^{2mp_0}\). Summing the two ranges proves
both claims.
\end{proof}

\subsection{A cutoff sufficient for the pure-gauge limit}

\begin{proposition}\label{C-350-16}
Fix \(0<g\le\gamma\) and \(\ell\in\mathfrak L(g)\).
There are \(K_0,K_\flat\in\mathbb N\),
\(C_\diamond<\infty\), and \(d_{\rm K}>0\),
depending only on \(g,\ell\) and the fixed constants,
such that
\[
 K_\sharp(d)=\max\{K_0,K_\flat,
                   \lceil3600\log_L(\sqrt3M/d)\rceil\}
\]
has the following property. For \(0<d\le1\),
\(20d\le\ell\), \(b\in[\gamma^{-2},L^2(g^{-2}+\bar B)]\),
\((f,h)\in\mathfrak T_{T_\ell}(d;\vartheta)\), and
\(K'\ge K\ge K_\sharp(d)\),
\[
 |S^T_{2;K',\ell,L^{K'}b}
                  -S^T_{2;K,\ell,L^Kb}|(f,h)
       \le C_\diamond\vartheta^{-2}d^{178}\eta.
\]
The same bound holds with the full cutoff limit
\(S_2^{(\ell,b)}\) in the first term.
For \(d\le d_{\rm K}\),
\[
 s(d)<K_\sharp(d),\qquad
       (\sqrt3M/d)^{3600}
             \le L^{K_\sharp(d)}\le d^{-3601}.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The displayed label interval is an admitted compact
interval for the fixed-torus cutoff theorem
\cite[Cor. 117.1 and Thm. AS]{YMM1}. At order two
that result gives, uniformly in this interval,
\[
 |S^T_{2;K'}-S^T_{2;K}|(f,h)
 \le C'\ell^9K^{6p_0+1/2}L^{-K/10}
                       \|f\|_\sharp\|h\|_\sharp,
 \qquad
 \|f\|_\sharp=\max\{\|f\|_\infty,40M\operatorname{Lip}f\}.
\]
It applies above \(K_0\) once, with
\(u=\lceil K/1800\rceil\) and support sup-distance
\(d_\infty\ge d/\sqrt3\),
\[
 d_\infty L^u\ge6M,\qquad
 c_9\ell^3L^{3u}e^{-d_\infty L^u/M}
       \le\tfrac12 C\ell^9K^{6p_0+1/2}L^{-K/10}.
\]
All constants here are those of that theorem on
the indicated compact interval; in particular \(C>0\).
Put \(y=K/1800\) and
\(c_{10}=\max\{0,\log(2c_9/C)\}\).
Choose \(K_\flat=\lceil1800y_0\rceil\) so that
\[
 L^{y/2}\ge c_{10}+3\log L+200y\log L
                         \quad(y\ge y_0).
\]
The other defining bound for \(K_\sharp\) gives
\(L^{y/2}\ge\sqrt3M/d\).
Their product proves both required inequalities,
after increasing \(K_\flat\) to make the first
right side at least six. Also
\[
 K^{6p_0+1/2}L^{-K/10}
       \le cL^{-K/20}
       \le c(d/(\sqrt3M))^{180},\qquad
 \|f\|_\sharp\|h\|_\sharp
       \le(40M)^2(\vartheta d)^{-2}\eta.
\]
These give the claimed \(d^{178}\) bound.
The fixed-torus theorem gives the full cutoff
limit and permits \(K'\to\infty\) in it.

Minimality of \(s(d)\) gives
\[
 L^{s(d)}d
 <LC_{W,0}A_0^2
       \{\log L^{s(d)}+\log b_+(g)\}^{2p_0}.
\]
For small \(d\) this implies \(L^{s(d)}\le d^{-2}\).
Once the logarithmic term in \(K_\sharp\) exceeds
the two fixed thresholds,
\[
 (\sqrt3M/d)^{3600}
 \le L^{K_\sharp(d)}
 <L(\sqrt3M/d)^{3600}\le d^{-3601}.
\]
Decreasing \(d_{\rm K}\) proves both final assertions.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Comparison with the least pure-gauge torus}

We require the following comparison only for torus
measures. Write \(\widetilde\mu_{K,\ell,\beta}\) for
their periodic extension to the infinite lattice.

\begin{proposition}\label{C-350-21}
Let \(g\le\gamma_W^{\rm sd}\), where this ceiling
ensures the source and history hypotheses of
\cref{IV-141-3,IV-141-4,IV-142-1}.
We include \((\gamma_W^{\rm sd})^{-2}\ge4\bar B\)
in this choice.
Let \((K,\beta)\) be a first-passage datum at \(g\),
\(K\ge3\), and \(a_K\le9d\le1/20\).
Suppose real Lipschitz functions \(\tilde f,\tilde h\)
have disjoint nonzero sets, each vanishes outside
a ball of radius \(d\), both vanish outside one
ball of radius \(9d\), and
\[
 \operatorname{Lip}\tilde f\le
       \|\tilde f\|_\infty/(\vartheta d),\qquad
 \operatorname{Lip}\tilde h\le
       \|\tilde h\|_\infty/(\vartheta d).
\]
They need not be nonnegative or satisfy integral
lower bounds. There are \(Q_2^{\rm T}(g)\ge1\)
and \(C_2^{\rm T}(g)<\infty\), independent of
the cutoff, datum, side, pair, and position, such that
for every \(\ell'\in\mathfrak L(g)\),
\[
 |S_2^T[\widetilde\mu_{K,\ell',\beta}]
       -S_2^T[\widetilde\mu_{K,\ell_g,\beta}]|
                    (\tilde f,\tilde h)
 \le(30d)^3\,2Q_2^{\rm T}(g)^2A_\star(d)^{-2}\eta .
\]
Here \(A_\star\) is the amplitude in
\eqref{IV-140-18}. In particular, if also
\[
 d\le d_\star(g,\vartheta)
       =4\sqrt3M\vartheta^{-1}
                (K_{\rm L}^\vee/K_{\rm Q}^\vee)^2g^{-2},
\]
then
\begin{equation}\label{C-350-17}
 |S_2^T[\widetilde\mu_{K,\ell',\beta}]
       -S_2^T[\widetilde\mu_{K,\ell_g,\beta}]|
                 (\tilde f,\tilde h)
       \le C_2^{\rm T}(g)\vartheta^{-1}d^2b^{-2}\eta .
\end{equation}
These constants may depend on the fixed source
radius and on the stability assignment.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Put \(\mu'=\widetilde\mu_{K,\ell_g,\beta}\) and
\(l=\ell_g/2=L^m\). Choose \(o\in a_K\mathbb Z^3\)
within coordinate distance \(a_K/2\) of the centre
\(x_1\) of the ball of radius \(9d\).
The eight cells
\[
 Q_{\mathbf k}=o+l\mathbf k+[-l/2,l/2]^3,
                  \qquad\mathbf k\in\{0,1\}^3,
\]
form a board on the least torus. Reflection in
each plane \(x_\mu=o_\mu\pm l/2\) preserves
the lattice. The unit ball about \(x_1\) lies
strictly inside \(Q_0\). Its reflected copies
have centres at sup-distance at least \(l-a_K\).

For a function \(F\) of the bonds inside \(Q_0\),
the pure-gauge chessboard comparison
\cite[Cor. 86.6]{YMM1} gives
\[
 |\widetilde\mu_{K,\ell',\beta}(F)|
       \le Q_0\|F\|_{\rm ch},\qquad
 \|F\|_{\rm ch}^8
       =\mu'\left(\prod_{\mathbf k}F^{[\mathbf k]}\right)\ge0.
\]
Its pressure factor is at most
\(\exp\{l^3(p_{\ell_g}-p_{\ell'})\}\).
The zero-source upper and lower partition bounds
of \cite[Thm. AD]{YMM1}, including their vacuum-energy
comparison, bound this difference by \(C_{\rm pr}(g)\).
Thus \(Q_0=e^{l^3C_{\rm pr}(g)}\) works for every side.
This is the sole use here of the source radius
in the stability theorem.

For functions \(F_1,F_2\) in the unit ball, write
\[
 X_a=\mathcal O(F_a),\quad P_a=X_a-\mu'(X_a),\quad
 P_{12}=P_1P_2-S_2^T[\mu'](F_1,F_2).
\]
For \(\mu=\widetilde\mu_{K,\ell',\beta}\),
\[
 (S_2^T[\mu]-S_2^T[\mu'])(F_1,F_2)
                 =\mu(P_{12})-\mu(P_1)\mu(P_2).
\]
In the joint-cumulant expansion of the chessboard
product of the eight \(P_{12}\)'s, singleton blocks
cancel by centering, and a two-entry block contained
in one cell cancels with its subtracted covariance.
Every remaining block therefore meets at least two
cells. The analogous assertion for a product of
the \(P_a\)'s follows from centering.

We bound these linking cumulants on the least
torus. Assign one variable to each of the at most
sixteen reflected observables, and let \(W_z\) be
their summed source. By \eqref{eq:pure-packed-source},
\(\|W_z\|_{\rm lw}\le\max_i|z_i|u_i\), where the
\(u_i\)'s are the corresponding suprema divided
by \(A_\star(d)\). Decompose its logarithm as
\[
 \log\frac{Z[W_z]}Z
 =\log\Phi(z)
  +\left\{\mathcal E(W_z)
                  -\sum_{\mathbf k}\mathcal E(w^{[\mathbf k]})\right\}
  +\sum_{\mathbf k}\mathcal E(w^{[\mathbf k]}).
\]
All derivatives used here are at zero, where
\(\Phi(0)=1\). A linking derivative kills the
last sum. By \cref{IV-142-1}, with eight balls
and sixteen variables, the squarefree derivatives
of \(\Phi\) are bounded by \(Q_{\rm D}u^B\).
The finite moment--cumulant formula bounds those
of \(\log\Phi\) by
\(\mathrm{cu}_{16}Q_{\rm D}^{16}u^B\).

Locality cancels from the bracket every domain
meeting at most one reflected ball. Any remaining
level-\(j\) domain contains two points at sup-distance
at least \(l-3\). A nonwrapping domain fits in a
cuboid of lengths at most \(MD_j(d_j(X)+2)\);
a wrapping domain has
\(M(d_j(X)+2)\ge l/D_j\). In either case
\[
 d_j(X)\ge(l-3)/(MD_j)-2.
\]
Use \eqref{eq:pure-lw-energy} and sum domains
anchored at a source ball. Retaining half of the
exponential for this size lower bound leaves a
summable rooted-domain count, since
\(\kappa>2(\kappa_{\mathcal D}+2)\).
The remaining sum over levels is bounded by a
constant times
\[
 \sum_{r\ge0}L^{3r}
       \exp\{-\tfrac12\kappa[(l-3)L^r/M-2]\}<\infty.
\]
Thus the bracket is bounded on the unit source
polydisc by \(C_\Delta\max_i|z_i|u_i\).
Cauchy's estimate bounds its linking derivatives
by \(C_\Delta u^B\).
Enlarge
\(C_{\rm LK}=\mathrm{cu}_{16}Q_{\rm D}^{16}+C_\Delta\)
to be at least one.

There are at most \(\mathrm{Bl}_{16}\) relevant
partitions. Every block has size at least two,
so taking the eighth root costs at most one
factor \(C_{\rm LK}\) per pair of entries.
The chessboard estimate and the preceding
cancellation give
\[
 |S_2^T[\mu]-S_2^T[\mu']|(F_1,F_2)
       \le2Q_1^2u_1u_2,\qquad
 Q_1=Q_0\mathrm{Bl}_{16}^{1/8}C_{\rm LK}.
\]

Apply this to the signed packed sums of
\(\tilde f,\tilde h\). The grid
\(\delta=a_K\lceil18d/a_K\rceil\le27d\)
packs at least \((30d)^{-3}\) translates of their
radius-\(9d\) carrier inside the unit ball for
\(d\le1/180\). Averaging the signs removes cross
translates, and lattice translation invariance
makes the surviving terms equal. This proves
the first estimate with \(Q_2^{\rm T}=Q_1\).

Finally \(x_K>g^{-2}\), and
\(\sigma_{\rm src}=\mu_\star/K_{\rm Q}^\vee\).
The square-root entry of \(A_\star\) is the
smaller one whenever
\(\vartheta d\le4\sqrt3M(K_{\rm L}^\vee/K_{\rm Q}^\vee)^2b_+\).
The stated \(d_\star\) ensures this. Hence
\[
 A_\star^{-2}
  =(K_{\rm L}^\vee/\mu_\star)^2
       \frac{b_+}{b_-^2}\frac{4\sqrt3M}{\vartheta d},
 \qquad
 \frac{b_+}{b_-^2}
       \le b^{-2}
          \frac{(X_g+\bar B)^3}{(g^{-2}-\bar B)^2}.
\]
Inserting this into the first bound proves
\eqref{C-350-17}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The pure-gauge short-distance law}

The preceding estimates identify the first two
terms of the covariance. The remaining issue is
uniformity in the ultraviolet cutoff. We first
compare the sixth-order coefficient with its
infinite-lattice value at cutoffs of polynomial
size in \(d^{-1}\). The fixed-torus cutoff estimate
then removes this restriction for a common interval
of labels. Finally, comparison of two torus sizes
covers the other labels of a first-passage datum.

Put
\[
 c_2=\frac9{16\pi^2},\qquad
 c_1=\frac8{3\pi},\qquad
 \varkappa=c_1c_2=\frac3{2\pi^3},\qquad
 L_b^+(f,h)=c_2b^{-2}
       \{\mathcal K_6(f,h)+c_1b^{-1}\mathcal K_5(f,h)\}.
\]
All constants and auxiliary data used to define
the pure-gauge progression are fixed once, before
choosing \(g\). In particular, when a pair
\((K,\beta)\) is admitted at two coupling thresholds,
it defines the same progression and the same
torus measure at either threshold.
The interval
\[
 I(g)=(g^{-2}+\bar B,L(g^{-2}+B_\sharp)-\bar B]
\]
has the useful property that every \((K,L^Kb)\),
\(b\in I(g)\), is a first-passage datum at \(g\),
for every \(K\ge1\); see \cite[Cor. 74.2]{YMM1}.

\begin{proposition}\label{C-350-3}
There is a threshold \(\gamma_{\rm e}>0\), depending
only on the construction constants, with the following
properties. Fix \(0<g\le\gamma_{\rm e}\),
\(\vartheta\in(0,1)\), \(P\ge3601\), and
\(\ell=\ell_g\). Set
\(C_{\rm lat}=\frac32C_{\rm tm}\vartheta^{-1}\),
where \(C_{\rm tm}\) is the constant of
\cite[Prop. 121.2]{YMM1}.
There are \(d_{\rm e}>0\), \(c_{1/2}<\infty\),
and a nondecreasing function
\(\bar\varepsilon:(0,d_{\rm e}]\to[0,\infty)\)
tending to zero at zero such that, for
\((f,h)\in\mathfrak T_{T_\ell}(d;\vartheta)\)
and \(d\le d_{\rm e}\), the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)]
For a first-passage datum \((K,\beta)\) at \(g\)
with \(s(d)<K\) and \(L^K\le d^{-P}\), set
\(b=a_K\beta\). Then
\begin{equation}\label{C-350-4}
 |S^T_{2;K,\ell,\beta}-L_b^+|(f,h)
 \le\{\bar\varepsilon(d)b^{-3}d+
                         C_{\rm lat}b^{-2}a_K/d\}\eta.
\end{equation}
\item[(b)]
For every \(b\in I(g)\), \eqref{C-350-4} holds
at \((K,L^Kb)\) for every \(K>s(d)\). Its full
fixed-torus cutoff limit satisfies
\[
 |S_2^{(\ell,b)}-L_b^+|(f,h)
 \le\min\{\bar\varepsilon(d),c_{1/2}d^{1/2}\}
                                  b^{-3}d\,\eta.
\]
\item[(c)]
Suppose also that
\[
 g\le L^{-1/4}
          \min\{\gamma_{\rm e},\gamma_W^{\rm sd}\},
\]
where \(\gamma_W^{\rm sd}\) is the threshold in
\cref{C-350-21}. There are \(d'_{\rm e}>0\) and
\(\bar\varepsilon'(d)\to0\) such that
\eqref{C-350-4}, with \(\bar\varepsilon'\) in place
of \(\bar\varepsilon\), holds for every first-passage
datum at \(g\) with \(K>s(d)\) and every
\(d\le d'_{\rm e}\), without a restriction on \(L^K\).
\end{enumerate}
These constants and functions depend only on
\(g,\vartheta,P\) and the fixed construction data.
In (c) this includes the source radius and the
choice of constants used in the source progression.
They are independent of the cutoff, label, pair,
and position of its supports.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Take \(\gamma_{\rm e}=\min\{\gamma_s,\gamma_{\rm C}\}\).
All the smallness requirements on \(d\) below involve
only the permitted dependencies. Their minimum will
define \(d_{\rm e}\).

\emph{Reduction to the sixth-order coefficient.}
Let \(D=(K,\beta)\) be as in (a), and put
\[
 r=d/a_K,\qquad l=\max\{1,\log(2b/d)\},\qquad
 b_+=L(g^{-2}+\bar B).
\]
The witness-depth bounds give \(K\ge3\),
\(8a_K\le d\), and
\(r\ge(\log(1/d))^2\ge8\), after restricting \(d\).
Apply \cref{C-350-8,lem:pure-total-taylor-remainder,C-350-9}
at every translate in \(\mathsf{Pk}\).
Since \(L_b^+\) is invariant under translations,
\begin{equation}\label{C-350-18}
\begin{split}
 |S^T_{2;K,\ell,\beta}-L_b^+|(f,h)
 &\le\left[(E_1+E_2+E_3)b^{-3}d+
                     C_{\rm lat}b^{-2}\frac{a_K}{d}\right]\eta\\
 &\quad+b^{-3}a_K
       \max_{v\in\mathsf{Pk}}
       \left|\mathsf H^{(K)}[D]
                    -\varkappa\mathcal K_5/a_K\right|
                                      (\tau_vf,\tau_vh),
\end{split}
\end{equation}
where
\[
 E_1=C_{\rm A}(g)\vartheta^{-1}bd,\qquad
 E_2=C_Eb^{-1}dl^{8p_0},\qquad
 E_3=\bar\epsilon_4(g,d).
\]
Here \(\mathsf h_6=b^{-3}a_K\mathsf H^{(K)}[D]\).
It remains to bound the last absolute value by
\(r\eta\) times a function tending to zero.
We work at any one translate and suppress it
from the notation. If one sampled source vanishes, every source jet and the
lattice coefficient \(\mathsf P_1^{\rm lat}\) vanish.
The last comparison below, \cref{IV-73-73}, still bounds
their difference from \(\varkappa\mathcal K_5(f,h)\);
only that last comparison is needed in this case.

\emph{Depths for the comparison.}
Set
\[
 K'=\max\{K,\lceil24\log_Lr\rceil\},\qquad
 N_0=\ell L^K,\qquad N'=\ell L^{K'},\qquad
 n_1=K'-\lceil K'/78\rceil.
\]
Then
\[
 r^{24}\le L^{K'}\le
              \max\{d^{-P},Lr^{24}\}\le Ld^{-24P}.
\]
First suppose \(K'>K\). Then
\(r^{24}>r/d\), so \(r>d^{-1/23}\).
The following auxiliary datum and estimates are used only in this case.
Fix \(b_*\in I(g)\), and set
\(D'=(K',L^{K'}b_*)\); this is a datum by
\cite[Cor. 74.2]{YMM1}. Choose \(n_0\) so that
\[
 D_{n_0}\in[d^{1/2},Ld^{1/2}),\qquad
 L^{n_0}\in[rd^{-1/2},Lrd^{-1/2}).
\]
For small \(d\), \(2\le n_0\le K\) and
\[
 L^{n_0}<Lr^{12.5},\qquad
 L^{n_1}\ge L^{77K'/78-1}\ge r^{23.6}/L,
\]
so \(n_0<n_1\). The bare plaquette base points
lie within \(12r+2\) of one another, and
\(12r+2\le N_0/8\). Their lifts to \(\Lambda_{N'}\)
are sources \(\breve w_a\) with the same supremum
norms and lattice support size. In the physical
units of \(D'\) their support radius and separation
are \(d'=ra_{K'}\), with \(8a_{K'}\le d'\).
Thus \cref{C-350-6,C-350-7} apply at \(D'\).
These propositions require neither the witness-depth
condition nor Lipschitz estimates for the lifted
sources. The unit \(r\eta\) is unchanged.

\emph{Comparison of the coefficients.}
When \(K'>K\), the sequence is
\begin{equation}\label{C-350-19}
\begin{aligned}
 \mathsf H^{(K)}[D]
 &\longrightarrow\mathsf H^{(n_0)}[D]
 \longrightarrow\mathsf T[N_0,n_0](w)
 \longrightarrow\mathsf T[N',n_0](\breve w)\\
 &\longrightarrow\mathsf H^{(n_0)}[D']
 \longrightarrow\mathsf H^{(n_1)}[D']
 \longrightarrow\mathsf T[N',n_1](\breve w)\\
 &\longrightarrow
       a_K^{-1}\mathsf P_1^{\rm lat}(\tilde f,\tilde h;a_K)
 \longrightarrow\varkappa\mathcal K_5(f,h)/a_K .
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
We justify each step, including its domain conditions.
The first and fifth arrows use the coefficient
tail \eqref{eq:pure-running-coefficient-tail}.
The second, fourth, and sixth use
\cref{C-350-11,C-350-13,C-350-23}. Specifically,
\(\mathsf h_6^{(n)}=\gamma_2^{\rm r}\),
\(\beta^3a_K^2\gamma_2^\circ=\mathsf T[N,n](w)\),
and their difference is at most
\[
 \mathcal U(x_{n-1},\mathsf N)\eta,\qquad
 \mathcal U(x,\mathsf N)=C_X\mathsf N^{36}
       \exp[-\gamma^{\rm tr}A_1^2(\log x)^{2p_0}/8],
 \quad \mathsf N=N+\beta.
\]
This removal of the Gaussian windows requires
\[
 \gamma^{\rm tr}A_1^2(\log x_{n-1})^{2p_0}\ge80,\qquad
 10240N^3e^{-\gamma^{\rm tr}A_1^2(\log x_{n-1})^{2p_0}/8}
       \le1.
\]
Their uniform validity is checked below.
The two occurrences of
\(\mathsf T[N',n_0](\breve w)\) represent the same
number: this coefficient depends on no running
coupling or counterterm.

For the third arrow use \cref{C-350-14} with
\[
 \nu=\ell/D_{n_0}>\ell d^{-1/2}/L\ge\nu_W.
\]
The last condition follows from
\(d\le(\ell/(L\nu_W))^2\); the required separation
from the boundary follows from \(12r+2\le N_0/8\).
For the seventh arrow apply \cref{C-350-15} to
the lattice with top side
\(\ell'=N'/L^{n_1}=\ell L^{\lceil K'/78\rceil}\).
The size conditions \(\ell'\ge N_{\mathsf H}\)
and \(\ell'L\ge C_LM\) follow from
\cref{C-350-6}. For small \(d\), the plaquette
base points also lie within \(N'/8-1\) of one
another. There are at most \(900r^6\) pairs.
The bound \(3C_*\ell'^{19}n_1L^{-n_1/2}\)
in that proposition, and
\[
 \frac{19}{78}+\frac1{156}-\frac12=-\frac14,
       \qquad r^5\le L^{5K'/24},
\]
give the error \(E_{10}\) below. The remaining
rescaling identity is
\(a_K\mathsf T^{\rm lat}(\tilde w)
 =\mathsf P_1^{\rm lat}(\tilde f,\tilde h;a_K)\).

Finally, \cref{IV-73-73,IV-73-98,IV-73-100} give
\[
 |\mathsf P_1^{\rm lat}(\tilde f,\tilde h;a_K)
                  -\varkappa\mathcal K_5(f,h)|
 \le C_T\vartheta^{-1}a_K\lg(r)\eta .
\]
The lifted pair belongs to
\(\mathfrak T_{\mathbb R^3}(d;\vartheta)\).
Here the computed continuum coefficient is
\(\varkappa=3/(2\pi^3)\).

In units of \(r\eta\), the successive errors are
\begin{equation}\label{C-350-20}
\begin{aligned}
 E_4&=C_Rl^{6p_0}d^{3/4},&
 E_5&=\mathcal U(x_{n_0-1},\mathsf N_0)/r,\\
 E_6&=900r^5C'_WN'^{237}
                         e^{-\delta_{\rm tp}\ell d^{-1/2}/48},&
 E_7&=\mathcal U(x'_{n_0-1},\mathsf N')/r,\\
 E_8&=C_R(l')^{6p_0}d^{3/4},&
 E_9&=\mathcal U(x'_{n_1-1},\mathsf N')/r,\\
 E_{10}&=2700C_*\ell^{19}L^{20}K'L^{-K'/24},&
 E_{11}&=C_T\vartheta^{-1}\lg(r)/r .
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The notation \(x'\) refers to \(D'\);
\(\mathsf N_0=N_0+\beta\) and
\(\mathsf N'=N'+L^{K'}b_*\).
The parameter bounds give
\[
\begin{gathered}
 \mathsf N_0\le(\ell+b_+)d^{-P},\qquad
 \mathsf N'\le(\ell+b_+)Lr^{24},\\
 x_{n_0-1}\ge\tfrac34d^{-1/2},\qquad
 x'_{n_0-1}\ge\tfrac34r^{23}d^{1/2}
                 \ge\tfrac34\max\{r^{11.5},d^{-1/2}\},\\
 x'_{n_1-1}\ge L^{K'/78},\qquad
 l'\le\log(2b_+)+K'\log L .
\end{gathered}
\]
For \(E_4,E_8\) we used
\((r/L^{n_0})^{3/2}\le d^{3/4}\).
When \(K'=K\), set \(D'=D\) and
\(\mathsf N'=\mathsf N_0=N_0+\beta\). Use only
\[
 \mathsf H^{(K)}[D]\longrightarrow
 \mathsf H^{(n_1)}[D]\longrightarrow
 \mathsf T[N_0,n_1](w)\longrightarrow
 a_K^{-1}\mathsf P_1^{\rm lat}
 \longrightarrow\varkappa\mathcal K_5/a_K .
\]
The first error, divided by \(r\eta\), is at most
\(C_Rl^{6p_0}L^{3(1-0.94K)/2}\), since
\(r/L^{n_1}\le L^{1-0.94K}\); the other errors
are \(E_9,E_{10},E_{11}\), with
\(x_{n_1-1}\ge L^{K/78}\) and
\(\mathsf N'\le(\ell+b_+)L^K\).

\emph{Uniform control for (a).}
At each removal of Gaussian windows, write
\(x_\flat\) for the preceding lower bound on
the relevant running coupling. The two required
conditions hold if
\[
 \tfrac18\gamma^{\rm tr}A_1^2(\log x_\flat)^{2p_0}
       \ge10+\log(10240\mathsf N^3).
\]
Indeed, we may use
\[
 \log\mathsf N\le C_1+C_2\log x_\flat,\qquad
 C_1=\log((\ell+b_+)L)+P ,
\]
with \(C_2=2P,3,78\) at the first, second, and
third such comparison. The first bound uses
\(\log(1/d)\le2\log x_\flat+0.6\); the second
uses \(\log x_\flat\ge11\log r\), and the third
uses \(\log x_\flat\ge K'\log L/78\).
When \(K'=K\), only the third bound is needed, with
\(x_\flat=L^{K/78}\) and \(\mathsf N'=N_0+\beta\).
Every \(x_\flat\) used here tends uniformly to infinity
as \(d\to0\). Since \(2p_0\ge2\),
\[
 \mathcal U(x_\flat,\mathsf N)
 \le C_X\exp\!\left[
       36C_1+36C_2\log x_\flat
       -\tfrac18\gamma^{\rm tr}A_1^2
                                  (\log x_\flat)^{2p_0}\right]
\]
tends to zero faster than every negative power
of \(x_\flat\).

The remaining errors have uniform bounds
\[
\begin{split}
 E_6&\le900C'_W(\ell L)^{237}
         d^{-5693P}e^{-\delta_{\rm tp}\ell d^{-1/2}/48},\\
 E_4+E_8&\le2C_R
       [\log(2b_+L)+24P\log(1/d)]^{6p_0}d^{3/4},\\
 E_{11}&\le C_T\vartheta^{-1}
       \sup_{\rho\ge(\log(1/d))^2}\lg(\rho)/\rho .
\end{split}
\]
The error \(E_{10}\), and the first error in the
case \(K'=K\), tend to zero since
\(K'\ge K>s(d)\to\infty\).
The same is true of \(E_1,E_2,E_3\), uniformly
for \(g^{-2}\le b\le b_+\).
Taking the supremum of the sum of these bounds
over all smaller positive \(d\) defines a
nondecreasing function \(\bar\varepsilon_{\rm a}(d)\)
tending to zero. Inserting it into
\eqref{C-350-18} proves (a).

\emph{Arbitrary cutoffs for \(b\in I(g)\).}
Every \((K,L^Kb)\), \(b\in I(g)\), is a datum
at \(g\). For \(s(d)<K\le K_\sharp(d)\), (a)
applies because \cref{C-350-16} gives
\(L^K\le d^{-3601}\le d^{-P}\).
For \(K>K_\sharp(d)\), compare with \(K_\sharp\)
using that proposition and then apply (a).
Since \(a_{K_\sharp}\le(d/(\sqrt3M))^{3600}\),
\[
 |S^T_{2;K,\ell,L^Kb}-L_b^+|(f,h)
 \le\left[\bar\varepsilon_{\rm a}(d)
     +C_\diamond\vartheta^{-2}b_+^3d^{177}
     +C_{\rm lat}b_+d^{3598}\right]b^{-3}d\,\eta .
\]
The same estimate holds for the full cutoff
limit. Add the nondecreasing envelope of the
two last errors to \(\bar\varepsilon_{\rm a}\)
to obtain \(\bar\varepsilon\).

For the stated rate in the limit, use just the
cutoff \(K_\sharp\), where \(r\ge d^{-3599}\)
and \(K'>K\). The errors \(E_5,E_6,E_7,E_9\)
are smaller than every power of \(d\);
\(E_{10}+E_{11}\le Cd^{3598}\log(1/d)\);
\(E_1+E_2\le Cd(\log(1/d))^{8p_0}\);
and \(E_4+E_8\le Cd^{3/4}(\log(1/d))^{6p_0}\).
By \cref{C-350-9}, \(E_3\le C_4(g)d^{1/2}\).
The cutoff comparison errors also decay faster
than \(d^{1/2}\). Enlarging a constant therefore
gives the claimed \(c_{1/2}d^{1/2}\) bound.

\emph{All first-passage labels.}
Assume the additional smallness condition in (c).
Set
\[
 g_{\rm a}=L^{1/4}g,\qquad
 g_{\rm b}=L^{-1/4}g,\qquad x=g^{-2}.
\]
Each of \(g,g_{\rm a},g_{\rm b}\) is at most
\(\min\{\gamma_{\rm e},\gamma_W^{\rm sd}\}\).
The choice of \(\gamma_W^{\rm sd}\) gives
\(x\ge4L^{1/2}\bar B\ge5\bar B\).
At the fixed construction data the flow is a
function of \((K,\beta)\), independently of which
of these thresholds admits the datum. The
source progression and its torus measures in
(a), (b), and \cref{C-350-21} consequently agree
whenever both are defined.

The labels at \(g\) lie in
\([x,L(x+\bar B)]\), while
\[
 I(g)=(x+\bar B,L(x+B_\sharp)-\bar B].
\]
The omitted lower interval is contained in
\(I(g_{\rm a})\), and the omitted upper interval
is contained in \(I(g_{\rm b})\). To check the
endpoints, use \(x\ge5\bar B\) and \(L\ge13\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
 L^{-1/2}x+\bar B&<x,&
 x+\bar B&\le L^{1/2}x+LB_\sharp-\bar B,\\
 L^{1/2}x+\bar B&\le L(x+B_\sharp)-\bar B,&
 L(x+\bar B)&\le L(L^{1/2}x+B_\sharp)-\bar B .
\end{aligned}
\]

For each of the three thresholds put
\(C_w(g'')=\sup_{s\ge0}C_W(s)L^{-s/2}\),
with \(C_W\) evaluated at that threshold.
Choose \(d'_{\rm e}\) below the minimum, over
the three thresholds, of
\[
 1/180,\quad L^{-2},\quad d_{\rm e}(g''),\quad
 d_\star(g'',\vartheta),\quad (LC_w(g''))^{-2}.
\]
The witness depth at any of them then satisfies
\(L^{s(d)}\le d^{-3}\). Indeed, its minimality
gives \(L^{s-1}d<C_wL^{(s-1)/2}\).

Now let \((K,\beta)\) be any datum at \(g\)
with \(K>s_g(d)\). If \(L^K\le d^{-P}\),
use (a). If \(b\in I(g)\), use (b). In the
remaining case \(b\in I(g_\bullet)\), with
\(g_\bullet=g_{\rm a}\) or \(g_{\rm b}\).
The same pair \((K,L^Kb)\) is a datum at
\(g_\bullet\), and \(K>s_{g_\bullet}(d)\)
because \(L^K>d^{-P}\ge d^{-3}\).
Part (b) gives the asserted law on
\(T_{\ell_{g_\bullet}}\) for the pair with
the same lift. This lift preserves
\(\eta,\mathcal K_5,\mathcal K_6\).

Both \(\ell_g\) and \(\ell_{g_\bullet}\) are
of the form \(2L^m\). Let \(g_\circ\) correspond
to the smaller side. The larger side is admitted
at \(g_\circ\), the datum is admitted at both
thresholds, and one torus is the least torus at
\(g_\circ\). Thus \eqref{C-350-17} gives the
difference of their covariances as at most
\[
 C_2^T(g_\circ)\vartheta^{-1}d^2b^{-2}\eta
 \le C_2^T(g_\circ)\vartheta^{-1}b_+d
                                      \,b^{-3}d\,\eta .
\]
The lattice error \(C_{\rm lat}b^{-2}a_K/d\)
is unchanged. Hence (c) holds with
\[
 \bar\varepsilon'(d)=
       \max_{g''\in\{g,g_{\rm a},g_{\rm b}\}}
                                   \bar\varepsilon_{g''}(d)
       +\max_{g''\in\{g,g_{\rm a},g_{\rm b}\}}
                       C_2^T(g'')\vartheta^{-1}b_+d .
\]
This completes the proof.
\end{proof}

\section{Index of notation and conventions}
\label{app:qcdm2-notation}

The table lists the principal notation in the order in which it
is used. A cited result includes the definitions immediately
preceding it.

\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.1}
\begin{longtable}{@{}p{0.24\textwidth}@{\hspace{0.025\textwidth}}p{0.735\textwidth}@{}}
\textbf{Notation} & \textbf{Meaning and location}\\
\hline
\endfirsthead
\textbf{Notation} & \textbf{Meaning and location (continued)}\\
\hline
\endhead
\endfoot
\endlastfoot
$a=L^{-K}$, $\lambda_j$, $\beta$, $m_0$
& The fine spacing, the level spacing $\lambda_j=L^{j-K}$,
and the bare parameters $\beta=\mathsf b/a$, $m_0=a\mathsf m$;
\cref{sec:qcdm2-setting}.\\
$I_g$, $\mathfrak L(g)$, $T_\ell$
& The admitted interval for $\mathsf b$, the admitted torus
sides, and $(\mathbb R/\ell\mathbb Z)^3$;
\cref{sec:qcdm2-setting}.\\
$D[U]$, $D_\pm$, $e_\pm$, $\mathsf G_\pm$
& The massless chamber operator, its two internal blocks,
their projections $(1\pm\tau_3)/2$, and the physical
resolvents $a(D_\pm+m_0)^{-1}$;
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-Dirac}.\\
$\mathfrak B$, $O_K(w)$, $\Phi_K(J)$
& The reflection-real meson basis, the action insertion,
and the site bilinear insertion;
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-action}--\eqref{eq:qcdm2-meson}.
The label $0$ denotes the action density.\\
$\|f\|_\alpha$, $\|f\|_\sharp$
& $\|f\|_0=\|f\|_\sharp
=\max(\|f\|_\infty,40M\operatorname{Lip}f)$ and
$\|f\|_\Gamma=\|f\|_\infty$ for $\Gamma\in\mathfrak B$;
\cref{sec:qcdm2-setting}.\\
$\nu_K$, $\mathcal G^{\rm tor}_{K,\beta,m_0}$
& The finite-torus gauge law and the set of its infinite-lattice
torus limits; \cref{sec:qcdm2-circle}.\\
$\mathsf L(f)$, $\Xi_\nu^f(z)$
& The loop $\operatorname{Tr}(\mathsf G_+\hat f)$ and its
determinant moment; \eqref{eq:qcdm2-Xi}.
The hat denotes multiplication by the test function.\\
$D^{\rm mix}$, $E_K^{\rm mix}$, $h_K$
& Mixed extraction by inclusion--exclusion, the resulting
energy in \eqref{C-415-2}, and the holomorphic
normalization in the circle bound
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-pure-energy}.\\
$F_s$, $Z_K(s)$, $\nu_{K,s}$, $\mathfrak l_s$
& The determinant at physical mass $s$, its partition function,
its gauge law, and
$\mathfrak l_s=\partial_s\log|F_s|^2$;
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-mass-partition}--\eqref{eq:qcdm2-mass-loop}.\\
$R_b$, $R^{\rm mix}$, $P_{\rm col}$
& Deletion of species $b$, the mixed projection
$(1-R_1)(1-R_2)$, and independent constant colour averaging
in the two species at the trivial pair; \cref{C-415-6}.\\
$\mathsf t_j$, $x_j$, $\phi_j$, $\delta_j$, $\mathfrak l_j$
& The calibration coefficient $\lambda_j^{-1}\mathsf b$,
the running coefficient, $\phi(x_j)$, and the gauge fluctuation
radius; \cref{sec:qcdm2-mixed-proof}. The additional scale weight is
$\mathfrak l_j=\mathsf t_j^{-1/2}(\log\mathsf t_j)^{-p_0}$;
\cref{C-415-5}.\\
$\mathfrak c$, $\mathscr D_k^\circ$, $\sigma_i$
& The free coordinates $\mathfrak c=(0,\mathsf n,(\sigma_i)_{i\le k})$,
their domain at zero gauge source,
and the extracted mass-source corrections;
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-zero-source-domain}.\\
$H_k$, $\bar H_k$, $\Gamma_k^{-1}$, $W$
& The unbarred background map, its row twin, the fermion
fluctuation covariance and the fermion fluctuation;
\cref{sec:qcdm2-mixed-proof}. The gauge fluctuation is $B$.\\
$\epsilon_F$, $\|m_c^{\rm tor}\|_{\rm nat}$
& The weighted norm of the chosen local decomposition of $F$,
and the norm of its grouped cell zeroth moments;
\cref{C-415-9}.\\
$\mathscr S$, $M^*$, $\mathscr S_{\mathbb R}$
& The enlarged bilinear label space, the involution
$M^*=\tau_3M^\dagger\tau_3$, and its real form;
\eqref{C-401-2}. The insertion with label $M$ is $\Phi[M](f)$.\\
$G_{\mathbb C}$, $G$, $V(S)$
& $\mathrm{Sp}(2N_f,\mathbb C)^2$, its compact form
$\mathrm{USp}(2N_f)^2$, and the unitary action of $S\in G$;
\eqref{C-401-3} and \cref{C-401-46}.\\
$S^{\rm ext}$, $\sigma^{\rm ext}$, $\mathcal H^{\rm ext}$,
$H$, $P_1,P_2$
& The extended truncated functions, their centered functional,
the reflection Hilbert space, and its time and spatial
translation generators; \cref{C-401-49}.\\
$n$, $Q$, $\mathcal H_n^{\rm ext}$, $\mathcal H_\pi^{\rm ext}$
& A species weight, the quark-number operator $Q$ with eigenvalue
$q=\sum_fn_f$,
the corresponding weight space, and the $\pi$-isotypic space.
Here $|\pi|$ is the largest $\ell^1$ norm of a weight of $\pi$;
\cref{C-401-46,C-400-34}.\\
$\mathsf j^T$, $j_\mu^T$, $J^T(f)$
& The chamber-link current, its sum across a site bond,
and its smeared physical insertion, including its factor $i$;
\eqref{C-402-3}.\\
$\mathcal M$, $\mathsf n$, $\mathscr O_k^{\mathcal M}$,
$\mathcal P^{\mathcal M}$, $\mathcal O_j^{{\rm lev},\mathcal M}$
& The matrices acting on spin, internal and flavour indices
and trivially on colour; the bare source $\mathsf n=-aJ$;
and the chain, physical and level source domains;
the definitions preceding \cref{C-417-7}.\\
$\mathcal D_j$, $d_j(Y)$, $E_K(s)$, $e_j(Y;s)$, $W_K[s]$
& The polymers and their block-tree lengths, the extracted
energy, its local increments, and the remaining factor in
$Z_K[s]=e^{E_K(s)}W_K[s]$;
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-energy-decomposition}.\\
$\mathcal P$, $\rho_b$, $\rho_m$, $W_{\mathbb C}$
& The physical source ball and the complex coupling--mass
neighbourhood of the real parameter window;
\cref{sec:analytic-labels} and
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-analytic-radii}.\\
$d_\cap(S_1,\ldots,S_n)$
& $\min_{x\in T_\ell}\max_i\operatorname{dist}(x,S_i)$.
It is positive exactly when the closed supports have empty
total intersection; the definition preceding \cref{C-412-53}.\\
$I$, $U_r$, $\mathcal E_K(z)$, $h_K(z)$
& The mass interval, its complex $r$-neighbourhood, the common
vacuum normalization, and $h_K(z)=Z_K(z)e^{-\mathcal E_K(z)}$;
\cref{sec:qcdm2-mass-continuation,C-404-67}.\\
$I_\epsilon$, $\rho_\ell$, $w_\ell$, $\Omega_\epsilon$
& The longer real mass interval, the radius used in its
zero-free estimate, and its complex neighbourhood of width
$w_\ell=\rho_\ell/[2(e+1)]$;
\eqref{eq:qcdm2-mass-width} and \cref{C-404-72}.\\
$h$, $\mathcal Z$, $\mathcal S_n(z;X)$
& A subsequential limit of the normalized partition functions,
its zero set, and the common meromorphic continuation of the
separated cumulants; \cref{C-404-60}.\\
$s,u,t_0,t_1$, $\phi_1,\phi_2$
& The comparison depths for adjacent cutoffs and their fixed
fractions of $K$; \eqref{eq:qcdm2-comparison-depths}.\\
$\mathcal M$, $\mathcal V_{[d]}$, $\mu_d^{F,K}$, $\mu_d^F$
& The block map, the configuration space at physical depth $d$,
the pushed-forward finite-cutoff law and its total-variation limit;
\eqref{C-406-60} and \cref{C-406-68}.\\
$\mathcal V_{\rm thr}$, $\mu_{\rm thr}^F$
& The product of the block configuration spaces and the probability
law supported on compatible block fields; \cref{C-406-68}.\\
$K_d^\sharp$, $T_d^\sharp$, $m_d^\sharp$, $\pi_d$
& The cutoff chosen for parameter recovery, the action statistic,
its pure-gauge mean and the projection onto the mean's range;
\cref{C-406-72}.\\
$\hat b_d$, $\hat b$, $\Delta_d$, $\hat N$
& The coupling estimators, the rescaled mean shift and the flavour
estimator; \cref{C-406-72}.\\
$\mathfrak T_E(d;\vartheta)$, $\mathcal K_q$, $\mathfrak f$
& The separated nonnegative test pairs, their kernel integrals,
and $\mathfrak f=\|f\|_\infty\|h\|_\infty$;
\cref{def:pure-test-pairs,C-403-3}.\\
$s(d)$, $c_2$, $\mathfrak c_1(N_f)$
& The witness depth and the coefficients $9/(16\pi^2)$ and
$(8-2N_f)/(3\pi)$; \cref{C-403-3}.\\
$\lambda$, $\xi_j(\lambda)$, $\bar\lambda_j$
& The complex field scale, the interpolated gauge coefficient
and the radii for its holomorphic flow; \cref{C-403-33}.\\
$\mathsf n_j^\lambda$, $\mathsf n_{j,[2m]}$
& The mixed source derivative of the level-$j$ energy and its
Taylor coefficients in the common field scale;
\cref{C-403-33}.\\
$\mathsf h_{2m}^{(n)}$, $\mathsf D^\lambda$
& The sums of the pure-gauge coefficients through level $n$ and
the weight in their constrained covariance formula;
\cref{C-350-11}.\\
\end{longtable}

\subsection*{Conventions}

The barred and unbarred variables are independent Grassmann
generators. Haar measure has mass one, and the Berezin integral
of $e^{-\bar\psi A\psi}$ is $\det A$. The traces defining
$\mathsf L$ and $\mathfrak l_s$ include position, spin and colour
but no flavour; when a source acts on flavour, the propagator
is extended by the identity on that factor.

Operator formulas use lattice coordinates; supports and distances
are physical unless stated otherwise. Links on $T_\ell$ are
periodic and spinors are antiperiodic. The volume-first and
growing-torus limits have the meanings given in
\cref{sec:qcdm2-setting}; each theorem specifies the limits it uses.
The complex parameter results keep $T_\ell$ fixed.

The symbol $M^*$ on $\mathscr S$ denotes the displayed reflection
involution. Elsewhere $*$ on an operator denotes its Hilbert-space
adjoint. The functions called $h_K$ in the circle bound and in
mass continuation have the separate definitions listed above.
The former subtracts a one-species energy; the latter is a
normalized partition function.
Likewise $\mathfrak l_s$ in \cref{sec:qcdm2-mass-comparison}
is a random loop at physical mass $s$, whereas $\mathfrak l_j$
in the scale estimates is the deterministic weight listed above.
In \cref{sec:qcdm2-currents},
$G_U=(D_+[U]+m_0)^{-1}=a^{-1}\mathsf G_+$ denotes the
lattice propagator; $\mathsf G_+$ includes the physical factor $a$.
